- guardrail.rs:562-572 and 695-701: the 64 MiB guard uses metadata().len(), which follows the link and is 0 for a character device or FIFO. guardrail.gate is a locked Engine::register handler (handlers/guardrail.rs:304), so there the endless read would hold the store mutex.

findings.title: git.commit (commit phase), git.branch.create, git.stage/unstage, git.branch.delete, clean_merged and worktree.remove run checkouts, filters, signing, history walks and tree deletion under the store mutex
findings.symbol: CommitOp finish, BranchCreate, Stage, Unstage, BranchDelete, CleanMerged, WorktreeRemove
findings.evidence:
These run inside the transaction (registered with e.register, or in a staged op's finish) through worktree::git_mutate, which has no timeout:
- CommitOp finish: `git_mutate(&root, &["commit","--no-verify","-m",..])` (571). --no-verify skips only pre-commit and commit-msg; commit.gpgsign (gpg/pinentry), prepare-commit-msg and post-commit still run.
- BranchCreate: `git switch -c name [start]` (366-374) is a full checkout with smudge filters and post-checkout hooks.
- Stage `git add -- paths` (501-503) and Unstage `git reset HEAD -- paths` (521-527) run clean filters and hash large files.
- BranchDelete (455-485) and CleanMerged (695-713) call branches_for. Its merged_tips walks the base's whole history whenever any branch is unmerged, and upstream_metrics adds two rev-walks per branch. Both then call list_with_dirty (opens every worktree) and run one `git branch -d` per branch.
- WorktreeRemove (129-144): dir_size over the whole checkout, then purge_build, then `git worktree remove --force`. workspace.rs:320-324 explicitly moves this same work off the bus as 'seconds of disk work per agent'.
- guardrail.confirm of a held commit replays the whole prepare phase inside the open transaction (engine.rs:325-351): git add -A, plus the user's pre-commit hook, which hooks.rs:210 runs with no timeout.
The desktop calls git.commit, git.stage, git.unstage, git.branch.create and git.branch.delete in normal use.
findings.impact:
Each of these stalls every request that needs the store: all mutations, the opening ctx.read of every unlocked query, and all agent MCP calls. Keystrokes are spared (D148). Concrete stalls:
- A user with commit.gpgsign=true commits from Relay, and the bus waits until they type the passphrase into pinentry.
- Staging a large Unreal/Blender asset hashes it under the lock.
- 'Create and switch' to a start point other than HEAD checks out and LFS-smudges the tree under the lock.
- Deleting one branch in a long history walks the whole history under the lock.
- Removing a worktree with a multi-GB target/ holds the bus for the entire deletion.
findings.fix: Convert these ops to register_staged, as BranchSwitch and Push already are: do the git work in prepare, and keep finish to events and audit. For commit, decide the gate first (a short read, or a finish that only records a hold/refusal), run `git commit` outside the transaction, then record the result. Make guardrail.confirm run a replayed staged op's prepare before it opens the transaction. Give every one of these subprocesses a timeout (see the timeout finding).

v1.reason: engine.rs register (around line 480) runs the closure inside the request transaction with the store held. git.rs:129 WorktreeRemove, 345 BranchCreate, 445 BranchDelete, 490 Stage, 507 Unstage and 693 CleanMerged are all registered with e.register. Each of them does subprocess or tree work through worktree::git_mutate, and worktree.rs:27-36 shows that is a bare Command::output() with no timeout, which also breaks the output_with_timeout rule. In detail: WorktreeRemove calls worktree::remove (worktree.rs:352-369), which runs purge_build (one dir_size plus remove_dir_all per build dir), then dir_size over the whole checkout, then `git worktree remove --force`, then prune, all under the lock. workspace.rs:320-324 calls exactly this work 'seconds of disk work per agent' and moves it after the commit there. BranchDelete and CleanMerged call branches_for(ctx.tx(), ..) (git.rs:1445), which runs the merged_tips rev-walk under the lock, then list_with_dirty, then `git branch -d`. CommitOp is staged, but its finish (git.rs:571) runs `git commit --no-verify` inside the transaction. With commit.gpgsign that waits on pinentry, and post-commit hooks still run. engine.rs:325-351 confirms that invoke_registered (the guardrail.confirm replay) runs a staged op's prepare against the open transaction: `git add -A`, hooks::refresh_git, and run_user_pre_commit (hooks.rs:210, a bare Command::output()). The desktop calls git.commit, git.stage, git.unstage, git.branch.create and git.branch.delete (code_git.rs:280/392/470-474/904-908/1035/1136).
v1.correction: In the common case stage, unstage and branch -d are quick. The stalls that actually happen are worktree.remove on a checkout with large build output, gpg-signed or hook-heavy commits, the guardrail.confirm replay of a held commit (pre-commit hook under the lock), and checkouts with LFS or filters. Keystrokes are spared (D148). Only agents' MCP calls and UI mutations and queries stall, so this is high, not critical. Fix: split each op into prepare/finish as BranchSwitch is. For WorktreeRemove, check ownership in a short read, then do the removal in prepare (or after the commit, as workspace.rs does). Run CommitOp's `git commit` in prepare after a gate pre-check, or have finish record the hold and run the commit after the commit point. Route git_mutate and run_user_pre_commit through proc::output_with_timeout.

v2.correction:
1. Reach. Nothing in the desktop or the CLI's own subcommands calls worktree.remove, git.branch.clean_merged or integration.discard. They are reachable only through `relay cmd`, tests and perf. Their lock holds are real but rarely triggered, so they should not drive the severity.

2. BranchCreate. With no start point, `git switch -c` only creates a ref and moves HEAD, which is cheap. It is not a full checkout. The checkout cost appears only when the start point differs from HEAD, and then only for the files that differ. BranchSwitch already runs that same `git switch` as a staged op with a 120 s timeout (git.rs:384-437), so the inconsistency is explicit.

3. Commit hooks. prepare-commit-msg and post-commit do not run in Relay session worktrees: their per-worktree core.hooksPath directory holds only pre-commit. They do run in checkouts without Relay's hooksPath, such as the primary checkout. The signing-prompt stall applies everywhere.

4. WorktreeRemove order. worktree::remove runs purge_build first, then dir_size, then `git worktree remove --force`, then prune.

5. Missing instance. git.pr.open (git.rs:666-692) runs `gh pr create`, a network call, with a bare `.output()` inside the transaction. The desktop calls it (code_git.rs:662), and agents can call it too (Actors::All). It is the same root cause and the worst routine instance, so add it to related unless another finding already reports it.

6. The replay path. D149 and engine.rs:325-327 document it as an accepted cost. That makes it intended, not harmless: it is reached for every over-cap or protected-path user commit.

7. Fix for commit. As written ("decide the gate first with a short read, run git commit outside, record after"), it opens a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race on GrantScope::Once grants: two concurrent commits could both pass the gate on one grant, and one of them would escape the guardrail. The gate and the grant consumption must stay atomic with publishing the commit. Two ways to do that:
- Build the commit object unlocked in prepare (`git write-tree` plus `git commit-tree`; any signing happens here). Then in finish, run the gate and a compare-and-swap `git update-ref`.
- Reserve the grant in a first short transaction.

8. Fix for guardrail.confirm. Make it staged: read the hold and the frozen op briefly, run the op's prepare unlocked, and in finish check again that the hold is still open before running the op's finish.

findings.title: git.pr.open runs `gh pr create` (network) with plain Command::output() while holding the store mutex
findings.evidence: `e.register::<PrOpen>(|ctx: &mut Ctx, p| { ... let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(gh); cmd.current_dir(&root).args(["pr","create"]); ... let out = cmd.output()`. Because it is registered with Engine::register, it runs inside the request transaction with the single store connection locked. The subprocess is not bounded by proc::output_with_timeout. `gh pr create --fill` makes several GitHub API round trips. This breaks two CLAUDE.md rules: no slow work under register, and every handler subprocess goes through output_with_timeout. The desktop offers it as 'Open PR' (code_git.rs:662).
findings.impact: While GitHub is slow, or forever if the connection stalls, every store-backed request waits: all mutations, the short read every unlocked query starts with (git.status, file.tree, session.list), and every agent's MCP call. The UI and all agents stall.
findings.fix: Register it with register_staged. In prepare, run gh through proc::output_with_timeout (about 60 s) with GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1. Only emit git.changed in finish.

v1.reason: git.rs:666 is `e.register::<PrOpen>` and does `std::process::Command::new(gh)...args(["pr","create"])...output()` inside the transaction, with no timeout and no GH_PROMPT_DISABLED. Neighbouring gh calls already avoid this: PrList is unlocked and uses output_with_timeout (git.rs:1094), and branch_cleanup.rs:171-172 sets GH_PROMPT_DISABLED and bounds its call. `gh pr create` makes several GitHub API round trips, and a stalled connection holds the single store mutex indefinitely. Every mutation, the opening ctx.read of every unlocked query, and every agent MCP call waits behind it. The desktop exposes it as 'Open PR' (code_git.rs:662, after a confirm dialog at 1240-1241).
v1.correction: Convert it to register_staged. In prepare, resolve the root with resolve_root_unlocked and run gh with output_with_timeout (about 60 s) plus GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1 and stdin set to null. finish only calls changed(). github.rs:45 (github.status, also a bare `gh api user`) is worth checking for the same pattern.

v2.correction:
1. "Forever" overstates the stall. stdin is already null under .output(), and stdout is a pipe, so gh cannot prompt. The OS TCP timeouts eventually fail a dead connection. A realistic statement is "a few seconds normally, tens of seconds to minutes on a degraded network, with no overall bound from gh".

2. The impact should be narrowed. Terminals keep typing and rendering (D148 fast path). The desktop's main connection would be blocked by this request even without the lock, because socket.rs handle_conn (335-744) handles each connection's requests one at a time. What the lock adds is the stall of every agent (the PreToolUse guardrail.gate call plus MCP calls), the other desktop connections, the phone door and background writes.

3. Refinements to the fix:
- Map Ok(None) from output_with_timeout to a typed timeout error that says the outcome is unknown. The createPullRequest mutation may already have landed. A retry is safe, because gh refuses when a PR for the branch already exists.
- The 60 s engine deadline is longer than the desktop's 30 s request timeout (client.rs:65-71). Either lower the deadline below 30 s or add git.pr.open to the client's long-timeout list. Otherwise the UI reports "timed out" while the PR may still be created.
- Consider sending the request on a dedicated connection, as lifecycle_request does, so the main socket does not queue behind it for up to the deadline.
- "stdin set to null" adds nothing: output_with_timeout already forces it (proc.rs:36).

4. The first verifier's side note about github.rs:45 (github.status) is a different and lesser issue. That op is registered unlocked (provider.rs:247), so its bare `gh api user` call does not hold the store lock. It can only hang its own request and connection.

5. Lock line references: the lock is taken at engine.rs:954-956 and the handler is called at 980. The subprocess runs at git.rs:669-681.

findings.title: Commit gate ignores the source path of a staged rename: protected files can be moved out unchallenged, and renames count as whole-file additions
findings.evidence: parse_status records renamed_from (worktree.rs:109-111). staged_numstat ignores it: per entry it does `let old = revision_text(root, "HEAD", &s.path)?; let new = index_text(root, &s.path)?; ... push_str(format!("{a}\t{r}\t{}\n", s.path))`. Verified: `git mv secrets/config.yml moved.yml` gives porcelain `R  moved.yml\0secrets/config.yml`, so the numstat line is `50\t0\tmoved.yml`. The old path never appears, and because HEAD has nothing at the new path, the whole file counts as added. evaluate_commit (guardrail.rs:765-781) matches protected_paths only against the paths in this numstat. The Diff handler looks up the old side by the new path in the same way (207).
findings.impact: When protected paths are configured, an agent refactor that moves a protected file elsewhere commits through git.commit with no protected-path refusal or hold. A deliberate `git mv protected/x x` does the same. The file leaves its protected location without a grant. Conversely, moving any file longer than the line cap (default 2000) counts as that many added lines and triggers a false guardrail.cap hold. git.diff shows renamed files as entirely new.
findings.fix: Treat a rename as touching both paths: add renamed_from to the touched list and read the old text from renamed_from. Simpler: feed the gate from `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M`, which reports both paths and handles binaries.

v1.reason: `parse_status` (worktree.rs:109-111) records `renamed_from` for R/C records. `staged_numstat` (git.rs:861-872) emits only `s.path`, and reads the old text with `revision_text(root,"HEAD",&s.path)`, i.e. by the new path. So a staged `git mv secrets/x moved` produces the line `N\t0\tmoved`. `evaluate_commit` (guardrail.rs:757-781) is fed that string as `request.diff` (git.rs:560-569) and matches protected_paths only against the paths in it. The source path never appears, so no protected_path refusal or hold is raised. The agent exec gate does not check shell commands against protected paths; `evaluate_write` (512) covers writes only. So an agent can `git mv` a protected file in its shell and commit it through the git.commit MCP op unchallenged. A plain `git rm` of the same file would be caught as a deletion. Moving any file longer than caps.lines counts its whole length as added lines and raises a false guardrail.cap hold. The Diff handler (207) shows renamed files as entirely new in the same way.
v1.correction: The bypass is specific to the in-process git.commit op (MCP git_commit and the desktop Commit button). A shell `git commit` goes through the pre-commit hook, where `request.diff` is None and evaluate_commit falls back to `git diff --cached --numstat`. That output reports a rename as `old => new`, so prefix or `**` patterns still match the old path. Fix: add `renamed_from` to the touched paths and read the old side from `renamed_from` (in staged_numstat and in Diff at 207). Alternatively, have both paths use `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M`, parse its separate old and new path fields, and feed both to the protected-path check.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. I reproduced it with git 2.55. After `git mv secrets/config.yml moved.yml`, `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` prints `R  moved.yml\0secrets/config.yml\0`. `staged_numstat` (git.rs:861-872) reads the old side with `revision_text(root,"HEAD",&s.path)`, which looks up the new path in HEAD and gets "". It writes only `50\t0\tmoved.yml`. The commit op passes that string as `Some(&numstat)` (git.rs:557-569). `evaluate_commit` then checks protected_paths only against those paths (guardrail.rs:765-781). A port of `path_matches` matches nothing for `moved.yml`. The design says a move should be caught: file.rename and file.move both guard the source path (file.rs:180, 209), and BUS.md §9.2 says git.commit refuses commits touching protected paths.

(b) Reachability. Three conditions are needed:
- protected_paths must be configured. The default is `[]` (settings.rs:31).
- An agent must move a protected file. Nothing stops the move itself: Bash `git mv`/`mv` goes through evaluate_exec, which only checks denied commands (guardrail.rs:811-847), and git.stage has no gate (git.rs:490-506).
- The commit must go through the in-process git.commit. Agents can only call it with the per-session `bus_writes` option, which is off by default (guardrail.rs:363-366). The desktop Commit button calls it as the user (code_git.rs:280/392). For the user, the only loss is a user_bypass confirmation prompt (guardrail.rs:1028).

Moving a protected file is rare.

(c) When it fires, the commit lands on the session branch with the protected file relocated. The content is kept, and it can even be edited up to git's 50% similarity threshold and still count as a rename. There is no refusal, hold, notification or grant request, and nothing later re-checks: integration.rs has no guardrail check. It is recoverable through git and shows in the diff and status ("Renamed from"). There is no data loss.

Secondary effect, verified: `git mv big.rs src/big.rs` on a 2500-line file gives `2500\t0\tsrc/big.rs` in-process but `0\t0` from git. That exceeds the default caps.lines of 2000, and a directory move totalling more than 2000 lines does the same. git.diff (git.rs:207) also reports renamed files as +N/-0.

(d) This should be medium, not high:
- It needs opt-in configuration and an uncommon action.
- The outcome is reversible and visible on review.
- It gives a deliberate agent nothing new. `git commit --no-verify` is not in the default denied_commands and nothing parses it. Bash writes are never checked against protected paths. So the commit gate is a safety net against accidents, not a boundary (BUS.md §9.5 calls agent guardrails best effort).

It is a real gap in that net in an edge-case path.

(e) The fix direction is right, but it needs the caveats in the correction.
v2.correction:
1. Severity: medium, not high (see reason).

2. Agents can reach git.commit only when the session has `bus_writes` (off by default). The finding's impact statement leaves this out. From the desktop Commit button, the user loses only a confirmation prompt.

3. The first verifier said the shell `git commit` route still catches renames with prefix or `**` patterns. That is only partly true. With default git config, `git diff --cached --numstat` (guardrail.rs:760) compacts paths. Verified outputs:
- `0 0 secrets/config.yml => moved.yml`
- `0 0 {secrets => lib}/config.yml`
- `0 0 config/{secrets => }/prod.yml`

A port of `path_matches` gives these results:
- `secrets` and `secrets/**` match only the first form.
- An exact-file pattern such as `secrets/config.yml` never matches.
- The brace forms match neither. They are the usual output when a file moves to another directory under the same name, so `migrations/**` misses `{migrations => db/migrations}/x.sql`.

So the default agent route, the pre-commit hook, has the same blind spot for most renames. The root cause is `evaluate_commit`'s input in both routes. The broader reach is still bounded by protected_paths being opt-in.

4. The cap symptom is a refusal for an agent: `refused` with code `guardrail.cap` and an exception hint. Only the user gets a hold (`guardrail.user_bypass`). It also fires for directory moves whose files total more than 2000 lines, not only for one large file.

5. Fix caveats:
- Do not add the rename source to staged_numstat as an extra numstat line. `evaluate_commit` counts files per line, so every rename would count twice against caps.files: a 25-file directory move would count as 50, over the default 40. The source path must be matched against protected patterns but counted once.
- Preferred fix: produce both inputs, staged_numstat's replacement and the `None` fallback at guardrail.rs:760, from `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M`. Give `evaluate_commit` a `-z` parser. Verified format: `a\tr\tpath\0`, and for renames `a\tr\t\0old\0new\0`. `-M` forces rename detection whatever `diff.renames` says. Match protected patterns against both old and new paths. This also yields real counts (0/0 for a pure rename), which removes the false cap.
- In git.diff (git.rs:207), read the old side from `renamed_from` when it is present.
- Add a regression test covering an exact-file pattern, a directory pattern, a same-name move out of the protected directory, and both commit routes.

findings.title: A submodule bump or a nested repository makes git.commit and git.diff fail outright
findings.evidence: revision_text does `let object = entry.object().map_err(gix_err("git.object"))?;` and index_text does `repo.find_object(entry.id).map_err(gix_err("git.object"))?` (836). Neither checks the entry mode. For a gitlink (mode 160000) the id is a commit in the submodule's repository, not in the superproject's object store (verified: `git cat-file -t <gitlink oid>` reports 'could not get object info'), so both return Err. staged_numstat (861-872) calls both for every staged path. The Diff handler (203-213) calls revision_text and working_text for every status path. Verified porcelain output: a staged submodule bump is `M  lib`, an untracked nested repository is `?? nested/`. working_text(root, "nested/") calls fs::read on a directory; the IsADirectory error is not NotFound, so it returns git.read_failed (844-847). tree_diff_files survives the same input only because it uses .ok().
findings.impact: Any commit through Relay that includes a submodule pointer update is refused in prepare with a cryptic git.object error. The desktop smart commit (all:true runs `git add -A`) in a worktree where an agent cloned a reference repo stages it as an embedded gitlink and then fails the same way. git.diff fails for the whole worktree whenever a submodule is modified or a nested repository is untracked.
findings.fix: Check the entry mode before loading. For gitlinks, return git's own text (`Subproject commit <oid>\n`) built from the entry id. Treat a missing object as empty via .ok(). In working_text, return empty for directories and other non-regular files.

v1.reason: revision_text (git.rs:802-827) calls entry.object()? and index_text (829-840) calls repo.find_object(entry.id)?. Neither checks the mode, so a gitlink (mode 160000) id, which is absent from the superproject's object store, yields Err(git.object). staged_numstat (857-869) runs in CommitOp prepare for every staged path, so a staged submodule bump makes git.commit fail. I reproduced the nested-repo case: `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` prints `?? nested/`, and `git add -A` (which the commit path runs when all:true) stages it as `160000 <oid> nested`, so index_text then fails on that oid. working_text("nested/") does fs::read on a directory, gets an EISDIR error that is not NotFound, and returns git.read_failed, so git.diff fails for the whole worktree. My repro also found a second trigger the finding missed: an untracked symlink to a directory is listed as `?? dl`, and working_text follows it into the same EISDIR failure.
v1.correction: Lowered to medium. Submodules and embedded clones are less common in this user's flows. The desktop does not call git.diff (only git.diff.file), so the visible failure is git.commit refusing a commit with a cryptic git.object error, plus agents' and the phone's git.diff. Fix: in revision_text and index_text, treat EntryKind::Commit as the text `Subproject commit <oid>\n` and map a missing object to empty. In working_text, use symlink_metadata and return empty, or the link target, for anything that is not a regular file. That overlaps with core-git#2's fix.

findings.title: git.diff, git.show and the commit gate reopen the repo and reload the index per file, then run an unbounded Myers diff on whole file contents, binaries included
findings.evidence: counts is `TextDiff::from_lines(old,new)`. similar's default config has no deadline, and its own docs (algorithms/myers.rs:12-18) say large distinct inputs 'will make it spin without making reasonable progress'. It runs on whole files before any binary check: `binary: old.contains('\0')||...` is computed afterwards (224, 1246). The inputs are `String::from_utf8_lossy(..).to_string()` copies, which expand each invalid byte to a 3-byte U+FFFD. Each revision_text call does gix::open + rev-parse + tree peel (803-815). Each index_text call does gix::open + index_or_empty() (831-832), i.e. a full index decode per file. staged_numstat (861-872) and the Diff loop (203-231, which also does an O(n*m) `files.iter_mut().find`) call these for every changed path. tree_diff_files diffs every blob of a commit (1239). The desktop guards only images, by extension, before calling git.diff.file (code_git.rs:1325).
findings.impact: Committing modified non-LFS binary assets (.uasset/.umap/.blend, MBs to hundreds of MBs) via git.commit spins a worker in prepare for minutes or longer before the gate even runs. The client gives up after 30 s while the engine keeps working. Clicking such a file in the git panel, or opening a commit that changed one, does the same and allocates several times the file size. For LFS files the comparison is pointer vs smudged binary, so every modified LFS asset shows as a huge bogus diff. Staging thousands of files in a repo with a large index re-decodes that index thousands of times.
findings.fix: Open the repository and the index once per request and pass them down. Check size and binary-ness (NUL in the first 8 KiB) before reading whole files, and skip the text diff for binaries. Set a timeout with `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`. For the commit gate, run `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M` once; it handles binaries, renames and filters, and evaluate_commit already falls back to it.

v1.reason: `counts` (git.rs:850-860) is `TextDiff::from_lines(old,new)`. Through `TextDiff::configure()` that uses similar 2.7.0's default config, which sets no deadline, and similar's own myers.rs:12-18 says two large, distinct inputs make it spin. Nothing checks for binary content before this: `binary: old.contains('\0')||...` is computed after the diff (git.rs:224 and 1246). `revision_text` (803) calls gix::open, rev_parse and peels the tree on every call. `index_text` (831-832) calls gix::open and `index_or_empty()` on every call. `staged_numstat` (861-872) calls all three for every staged path, inside git.commit's prepare (557). `tree_diff_files` (1239) runs `counts` on every blob of a commit for git.show. DiffFileOp (237-253) runs `from_lines(...).unified_diff()` with no deadline and also returns both full lossy texts in its response. The desktop routes only images around git.diff.file (code_git.rs:1325). A modified multi-MB binary (.uasset/.umap/.blend not tracked by LFS) has hundreds of thousands of NL-separated 'lines' with large edit distance. Myers is O((N+M)D), so prepare, the diff-file pane or git.show spins for minutes and allocates several times the file size.
v1.correction: Three corrections. (1) Severity is medium, not high. Every affected handler is register_unlocked or register_staged, so the store mutex is not held and the bus does not freeze. One blocking-pool thread burns a core and the calling client times out. (2) The LFS claim is wrong for the commit gate: HEAD and the index both hold LFS pointers, so staged_numstat compares pointer to pointer, which is cheap. It holds only for unstaged git.diff and git.diff.file, where working_text reads the smudged binary and compares it with the HEAD pointer. (3) The desktop never calls the list-form git.diff; only MCP agents do. The fix is right: open the repo and index once per request, check for NUL in the first 8 KiB and for size before decoding and diffing, and set `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`. For the gate, use `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M` through proc::output_with_timeout.

findings.title: Session checkouts lose every git hook except pre-commit, so pushes from them never run git-lfs's pre-push upload
findings.evidence: install_git writes only `hook_dir.join("pre-commit")` (hooks.rs:103-139), then sets `git config --worktree core.hooksPath <.relay/hooks/<session>>` (151-154). With a per-worktree hooksPath, git looks for hooks only in that directory. The shared .git/hooks pre-push, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge (where `git lfs install` puts its hooks) therefore stop running in that checkout. Verified with a stand-in hook: a shared .git/hooks/pre-push ran for a push from a linked worktree, stopped running once that worktree had Relay's per-worktree hooksPath, and still ran from the primary. session.create installs this for every checkout kind, including the primary (session.rs:890-893), which the Unreal plugin makes the default (plugin.json:18). git.push (git.rs:617) and the agent's own `git push` run in these checkouts. The code is outside this chunk; the consequence shows in git.push.
findings.impact: In an LFS repository, pushing agent commits that add or change LFS assets uploads the pointer files but not the objects. GitHub rejects such a push (GH008 unknown Git LFS objects). Hosts that do not check accept it, leaving teammates with pointers that cannot be smudged. For Unreal projects this also affects the primary checkout for as long as a session runs there.
findings.fix: Chain every hook, not just pre-commit: for each executable standard hook in the previous hooks dir, write a wrapper in the session dir that execs it. Keep the guardrail step in pre-commit.

v1.reason: install_git (hooks.rs:100-154) writes only <.relay/hooks/<session>>/pre-commit, chaining just the previous pre-commit (hooks.rs:103-109). It then sets `git config --worktree core.hooksPath <that dir>`. Git looks for every hook in core.hooksPath only, so pre-push, commit-msg, prepare-commit-msg, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge from the previous hooks dir stop running in that checkout. Nothing chains them or calls `git lfs push`: no matches for lfs, pre-push, commit-msg or post-checkout in hooks.rs, worktree.rs or handlers/git.rs. git-lfs uploads objects only from its pre-push hook. A git.push from such a checkout (git.rs:617, via worktree::git_mutate), or an agent's own `git push`, sends pointers without objects. GitHub then rejects the push with GH008; other hosts accept it and leave teammates with pointers they cannot smudge. session.create calls install_git for every checkout kind (session.rs:890-893), and the unreal-engine plugin sets default_checkout to primary (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18). So the user's own primary checkout is affected through its per-worktree config while a session runs there. Repos without LFS also lose commit-msg hooks (commitlint, husky).
v1.correction: The pre-push loss is certain from git semantics; the confidence can be raised. For worktrees created by Relay, LFS smudge on checkout still works, because `git worktree add` runs before install_git and smudge is a filter, not a hook. The lost post-checkout and post-merge hooks mainly affect LFS lockable read-only handling. Fix: for each standard hook that exists and is executable in previous_dir (other than pre-commit), write a wrapper in the session dir that execs it with "$@" and passes stdin through. Keep the guardrail chain in pre-commit.

v2.reason:
(a) The mechanism is real. install_git writes only `<.relay/hooks/<session>>/pre-commit`, chaining just the previous pre-commit (hooks.rs:103-139). It then runs `git config --worktree core.hooksPath <that dir>` (hooks.rs:150-154). From then on git ignores .git/hooks, and any shared core.hooksPath such as husky's, for every other hook. D23 and D93 promise only pre-commit chaining. Nothing documents the loss of the other hooks as intended. Cited lines check out: session.rs:892 (every checkout kind), session.rs:481 (launch), git.rs:617 (push via git_mutate), plugin.json:18 (default_checkout primary).

(b) The trigger the finding names does NOT produce the claimed result. I reproduced install_git's exact layout with real git 2.55 and git-lfs 3.8.0 (isolated HOME, local bare remote, scripts in the scratchpad: lfs_hook_exp*.sh). This covered a pooled linked worktree and the primary checkout. The first `git add` of an LFS-tracked file in the session checkout made git-lfs's filter process write pre-push, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge into the active core.hooksPath, which is `.relay/hooks/<session>/`. The later push uploaded the object. git-lfs installs its hooks lazily into whatever core.hooksPath resolves to, whenever its clean or smudge filter runs. That is how fresh clones get their hooks.

Any agent commit that adds or changes an LFS asset has to pass through the clean filter (git add, commit -a, Relay git.commit's `add -A`). Merges, rebases and checkouts that bring LFS files in run smudge. So "agent commits that add or change LFS assets" repair the hook dir before they can be pushed. Relay's own `git status` refresh (worktree::status_files, worktree.rs:86) re-cleans touched LFS files, which repairs it too. The finder's stand-in hook does not model any of this.

What does reproduce, with a settled index so no racy-git re-clean happens:
- An unpushed LFS commit made before the hooksPath switch, for example assets committed earlier in the primary checkout, which the Unreal plugin makes the session default.
- That commit is pushed from the session checkout (git.push, or `git push` by the agent or user).
- No LFS file has been staged, checked out or re-cleaned there since the switch, for example an agent that only edits C++.

In that case the dir held only pre-commit, the pointer was pushed, and the remote got no LFS object. The override lasts until the last session on that checkout is closed (session.rs:1513-1520), so it also catches the user's own terminal pushes from the primary.

Separately, and every time: non-LFS client hooks silently stop running for commits and pushes made in session checkouts. Examples are husky's commit-msg and pre-push, commitlint, Gerrit's Change-Id commit-msg, the pre-commit framework's pre-push stage, and post-checkout or post-merge hooks.

(c) In the LFS residual case, GitHub (GH008) and GitLab reject the push and tell the user to run `git lfs push --all`. That is a visible failure the user can recover from. Lenient hosts accept pointers without objects, and teammates' smudge then fails until someone runs `git lfs push --all`. The objects stay in the local .git/lfs/objects, so nothing is lost locally. For the other hooks, the user's own client-side checks are skipped without notice; CI or Gerrit usually catches the result.

(d) High is too strong. The normal flow the finding describes (agent commits LFS assets, then pushes) works. The real failure needs a specific order of events, and on the major hosts it shows up as a rejected push, not as corruption. The silent loss of other hooks is a real bug in a less common setup. Both fit medium.

(e) I tested the proposed fix and it works. With wrappers that `exec .git/hooks/<hook> "$@"` for pre-push, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge, git-lfs printed nothing and left the wrappers in place. The push uploaded both the earlier object and the new one.
v2.correction:
Rewrite the title and impact. Suggested title: "A session checkout's per-worktree core.hooksPath hides every user git hook except pre-commit."

Drop "never run git-lfs's pre-push" and "pushing agent commits that add or change LFS assets uploads pointers only". Both are wrong. git-lfs re-installs its hooks into Relay's session dir the first time its clean or smudge filter runs in that checkout, and staging an LFS asset always runs that filter. This is verified with git-lfs 3.8.0. The first verifier's claim that "the pre-push loss is certain from git semantics" is wrong for the same reason.

The real LFS impact is narrower. An unpushed LFS commit that predates the session, for example assets committed earlier in the primary checkout (the Unreal default), is pushed without its objects when no LFS file has been staged, checked out or re-cleaned in that checkout since the session started. GitHub (GH008) and GitLab reject such a push; lenient hosts accept the pointers. Add the deterministic impact the finding underplays: commit-msg, pre-push and post-* hooks from husky, commitlint, Gerrit or the pre-commit framework are silently skipped in session checkouts until the last session there is closed. Severity: high → medium.

Fix caveats:
- Write a wrapper only for a hook that exists and is executable in previous_dir at install time. An unconditional pre-push wrapper, or one that checks for the hook at run time, would stop git-lfs from installing itself, because it refuses to overwrite a foreign hook. That breaks the self-repair whenever .git/hooks has no LFS hook.
- Guard against a wrapper pointing at itself, as pre-commit already does.
- Rewrite the wrappers idempotently from refresh_git and launch.
- A hook added to previous_dir after the session starts is still missed. git-lfs's self-install covers the LFS case.

findings.title: task.dispatch with `create` runs session.create's git fetch and `git worktree add` inside its transaction
findings.impact: Dispatching a task to a new agent freezes every store-backed request for a network fetch plus a full checkout, which is tens of seconds to minutes on an Unreal-sized repo, and N times that with fanout. This path is reached from the CLI, the user-level MCP server and the phone; the desktop dispatch dialog targets an existing session instead.
findings.fix: Make task.dispatch staged: run the session creations (their prepare phases) before opening the transaction, and link tasks to sessions in finish. Alternatively, create the sessions after commit and report them by event.

v1.reason: task.dispatch is registered with e.register (task.rs:1049), so its handler runs in the transaction with the store mutex held. With `create`, dispatch_task calls ctx.invoke_registered("session.create", ..) (task.rs:683). For an op that has a prepare phase, invoke_registered (engine.rs:325-351) runs that prepare with `held: Some(self.tx)`, which is still under the mutex. Its comment calls this acceptable only for the guardrail.confirm replay path. session.create's prepare (session.rs:855-893) does the slow work in the default "new" case (plugins.rs:210-215 returns "new" unless a plugin pins primary): refresh_new_worktree -> fetch_remote (bounded at 20 s), new_worktree_base, worktree::create (`git worktree add` with checkout and LFS smudge, bounded at 120 s) and install_git. Its own comment says none of this belongs under the global store mutex. With fanout:true, dispatch_task runs once per not-done descendant in the same transaction (task.rs:1067-1075). The path is reachable through `relay cmd task.dispatch` (relay-cli main.rs:36) and the user-level MCP server. The desktop dispatch dialog sends `session` (task_pages.rs:652), and launch.rs:810 stages with `session` too, so the desktop UI does not trigger it today.
v1.correction: No current desktop flow reaches this; the triggers are the CLI or MCP (and the remote client if it forwards the op). It stays high because one call freezes every store-backed request for up to about 140 s per task, multiplied by N with fanout. Fix: make task.dispatch staged. Create the sessions (their prepare phases) in the unlocked phase and do the task and session linking in finish, or refuse create inside invoke_registered and require two calls.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims; I traced it myself. task.dispatch is a plain `e.register::<Dispatch>` (task.rs:1049). The pipeline takes the single `Mutex<Connection>` and opens the transaction at engine.rs:953-956, and releases it only at commit (engine.rs:1024-1025). With `create`, dispatch_task calls `ctx.invoke_registered("session.create", ..)` (task.rs:683). Because session.create is `register_staged` (session.rs:833), invoke_registered runs its prepare with `held: Some(self.tx)` (engine.rs:328-342), so the prepare runs under the lock. In the "new" arm (session.rs:865-877) that means:
- `refresh_new_worktree`, which runs `git fetch --all --prune` with a 20 s cap whenever the branch is new, which is the default (git.rs:945, 969-974);
- `new_worktree_base`;
- `worktree::create`, a `git worktree add` with checkout, capped at 120 s (worktree.rs:214);
- `install_git` (session.rs:890-893).

The code's own comment at session.rs:854-856 says none of this belongs under the store mutex. With the default `start: true`, the nested `session.spawn` prepare also runs under the lock (task.rs:710-713 into stage_launch/prepare_launch, which install hooks, copy skill folders and write brief files). The fanout loop (task.rs:1067-1075) repeats all of it for each not-done descendant. Nothing documents this as intended. D149 (DECISIONS.md, the "Two constraints bind" paragraph) and the engine.rs:325-327 comment both say the nested-prepare cost applies to `guardrail.confirm` replay "and only that path". session.create became staged later (6e7b044, 2026-09-09) than the nested call (fcbdbce), and the nested call never followed.

(b) The trigger is reachable in normal use from the phone. Both phone dispatch flows (RequestSheet "New request" on-board, and Board dispatch) always send `create` with `start: true`. relay-remote/tests/remote.rs:305-315 calls these "exactly the payloads the app sends". The door forwards any `actor:"user"` line unchanged (relay-remote/src/wire.rs:95-103). The trigger is also reachable from `relay cmd task.dispatch`, whose actor defaults to User (relay-cli main.rs:118-129). It is reachable from the user-level MCP server too, which exposes the op for a User actor (mcp.rs:91-103, 159-163). Fanout comes only from the CLI or MCP. The desktop does not reach it: task_pages.rs:652 sends `session`, and launch.rs:810 dispatches with `session` after a separate, properly staged session.create. Agents cannot call the op (UserOnly).

(c) While the lock is held, every store-backed request waits:
- Any agent-actor request waits at authorization (engine.rs:870-872). That includes each running agent's PreToolUse `guardrail.gate` hook, which has no client-side timeout (main.rs:465-471), and the PostToolUse `session.report`. Every agent therefore stalls on its next Bash, Edit or Write.
- Desktop queries and mutations queue behind it, and those beyond 30 s fail with "Request timed out" (relay-native client.rs:65-71).
- Keystrokes still work, because the D148 fast path at engine.rs:891-897 skips the store.

The duration is typically a few seconds on an ordinary repo (a fetch round trip plus a checkout). The worst case is about 140 s or more per task, and N+1 times that with fanout. There is no data loss.

(d) "A freeze of the bus" is listed under high, and this happens on every phone dispatch. It also breaks the first invariant in CLAUDE.md, which the authors explicitly fixed for the direct session.create path. High stands, with the impact corrections listed below.

(e) The fix is directionally right but incomplete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
Impact overstated for Unreal. The finding's example of minutes-long freezes on an Unreal-sized repo is wrong when the Unreal plugin is on. plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18 sets `default_checkout: "primary"` (D160; plugins.rs:210-214). The phone, CLI and MCP payloads omit `worktree`, so session.create takes the "primary" arm (session.rs:860-864). That arm runs only `git worktree list`, with no fetch and no `git worktree add`, so the freeze is short. The long freeze applies to projects without a primary-pinning plugin: ordinary code repos, or an Unreal repo with the plugin off. There it costs one fetch (up to 20 s) plus one full checkout (up to 120 s) per task.

Triggers stated precisely. The remote door does forward the op (wire.rs:95-103), and it is the phone's normal dispatch path, not a hypothetical one. Fanout comes only from the CLI or the user-level MCP server.

Additional locked work. With the default `start: true`, the nested `session.spawn`, `session.wake` or `session.resume` prepare also runs under the lock (task.rs:710-713). It is short, but a fix has to cover it.

Docs drift. The engine.rs:325-327 comment and D149's "and only that path" should name task.dispatch as a second nested path, or be made true.

Fix completeness:
1. A staged task.dispatch cannot simply run the spawn prepare before the transaction. stage_launch reads the session row by name (session.rs:604-608), and that row only exists after finish_create. So either commit create+link first and spawn in a second staged request (the desktop's session.create, then dispatch{session, start:false}, then spawn flow), or document the short launch staging that stays under the lock.
2. The finish phase must re-validate what prepare read: the task's column, its project, and for fanout the descendants. On refusal it must undo each prepared checkout's hook the way session.create's finish does (session.rs:900-911). Today, a dispatch that fails after a nested create (for example a spawn refused with provider.not_installed from plan_launch, or a later fanout child failing) rolls back the rows. It leaves behind the worktree, its new branch, and the hook installed for a session that never exists, because PreparedCreate's Drop (session.rs:729-735) only releases the name.
3. The first verifier's alternative, refusing `create` inside invoke_registered, would break both phone dispatch flows unless those are changed too.

Not verified: Relay installs the Claude PreToolUse gate with a 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:351). What Claude Code does when a freeze outlasts that and the gate hook is killed, block or proceed, lies outside this repo and was not established.

findings.title: Background git status runs with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1, so Relay's polling makes concurrent git commands in the same checkout fail on index.lock
findings.evidence: status_files runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` with `.env("GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS","1")`. This is deliberate (comment 83-85): it persists refreshed stat data. The cost is that git status holds index.lock through its collect phase (untracked scan, submodule status). Verified: while such a status was running (slowed via a submodule), a concurrent `git add` failed immediately with "Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists". Relay runs this status for git.status, every file.tree listing (status_badges, file.rs:31), dirty flags, git.diff, suggest_message, branch switch and commit prepare. The desktop re-runs git.status and file.tree on every file.changed / git.changed event (app.rs:1232-1240 -> editor.rs:508-524, 1 s debounce).
findings.impact: While an agent edits files, the panel keeps re-running status on the checkout it is showing. The agent's or the user's own git add / commit / switch in that checkout then fails intermittently with 'Another git process seems to be running'. The window grows with status time (large trees, many untracked files, submodules), which are exactly the repos the setting was meant to help.
findings.fix: Use GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 on polling paths (panel refresh, badges, dirty flags). Persist stat data separately with an occasional `git update-index -q --refresh`, run when no session is live in the checkout or on an explicit refresh.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:86-91 runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1. In git's cmd_status, the index lock is taken before refresh and released only after wt_status_collect (repo_update_index_if_able), so it is held through the untracked scan. A concurrent `git add`, `commit` or `switch` in the same checkout fails immediately on index.lock, because the index lock has no retry. The callers are real and frequent. file.tree badges (file.rs:31) and git.status (git.rs:178) run as register_unlocked queries, so they run concurrently with other work. The desktop re-runs file.tree and git.status 1 s after any file.changed or git.changed event (app.rs:1232-1240 -> editor.rs:508-524). `worktree.list` with include_dirty runs status in every linked checkout. An agent's edit, then a 1 s debounce, then a status refresh lines up with the agent's next `git add` or `git commit`. The intent comment (83-85) and the LFS test at :399 explain why the lock is wanted (persisting stat data so LFS assets are not rehashed). They do not make the side effect harmless.
v1.correction: GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1 is git's own default, so the explicit env is not what introduces the lock. What does is running background polling with the default lock behaviour; VS Code sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for exactly this reason. The explicit "1" also overrides a user or agent environment that set 0. The fix stands: use 0 on the polling paths (badges, panel refresh, dirty flags) and keep 1, or an occasional `git update-index -q --refresh`, for explicit or idle refreshes so the LFS-rehash concern stays addressed.

findings.title: Timed-out git switch / worktree add / status are SIGKILLed, leaving a stale index.lock that blocks every later git command
findings.evidence: Budgets: run_switch bounds git switch with output_with_timeout(.., 120s); worktree::create does the same for git worktree add (worktree.rs:214); status_files uses 10 s (worktree.rs:91); fetch uses 20 s (945). At the deadline, proc.rs:55 sends SIGKILL to the process group, and git cannot remove its lock files on SIGKILL. Verified: a git switch killed during a slow smudge left .git/index.lock behind, and the next `git switch` failed "Unable to create '.../index.lock': File exists". With SIGTERM instead, git removed the lock. run_switch's doc comment ('every refusal leaves the checkout as it was', 1345-1346) is false on this path. The client gives these ops 30 s (client.rs:65-70). Its table entry `git.worktree.create` names no op (the op is `worktree.create`). So the UI reports failure while the engine keeps switching for up to 120 s, and a retry collides with the first run's lock.
findings.impact: A switch or worktree creation that overruns its budget leaves the checkout half-updated and locked; this is plausible with LFS smudge of large Unreal assets. Every later git command there fails, for the user and for agents, until someone deletes index.lock by hand. A killed `git worktree add` also leaves a registered half-checkout plus the new branch, so the retry fails with worktree.exists.
findings.fix: In output_with_timeout, send SIGTERM to the group, wait a short grace period (1-2 s), then SIGKILL. When a mutating git command times out, say so and check for a leftover lock. Align the client's per-op timeouts with the engine's budgets and fix the op name in the client table.

v1.reason: proc.rs:53-58: when the deadline passes, output_with_timeout sends kill(-pid, SIGKILL) to the process group. SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's lockfile cleanup (its atexit and signal handlers) never runs, and an index.lock held at that moment stays behind. Nothing in relay-core removes a stale index.lock; the only reference is a test path in watch.rs:284. Callers that hold the index lock for most of their run: run_switch (git.rs:1347-1351, 120 s; its doc comment says every refusal leaves the checkout as it was) and worktree::create's `git worktree add` (worktree.rs:212-215, 120 s; its own message admits partial files are kept). status_files (worktree.rs:86-91, 10 s) sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1, so `git status` holds index.lock while it refreshes, and the comment there names slow LFS rehashing as a reason a run can be long. The client timeouts do not match: git.branch.switch gets the default 30 s, and the table lists "git.worktree.create" (client.rs:69), while the real op is "worktree.create" (relay-bus ops/git.rs:11), so that op also falls back to 30 s. The UI can therefore report a timeout while the engine keeps switching.
v1.correction: session.create already gets 180 s on the client, which covers the 20 s fetch plus the 120 s add. The client-mismatch part applies only to git.branch.switch and worktree.create. status_files is a real trigger too, because of GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1. Fix: in output_with_timeout, send SIGTERM to the group, wait 1-2 s, then send SIGKILL (pty.rs:342-349 already does this). Fix the client op name and give git.branch.switch more than 120 s.

findings.title: Concurrent worktree/session creations run parallel `git fetch --all --prune` in one repository; one fails on ref locks and its launch is aborted
findings.evidence: refresh_new_worktree (969-974) calls fetch_remote (`git fetch --all --prune`, 938-960) for every new branch. It is reached from WorktreeCreate (113-114) and session.create's prepare (session.rs:866); git.fetch calls fetch_remote too (583). These prepare phases now run concurrently (they are off the store mutex), and nothing serializes fetches per repository. Verified: two concurrent `git fetch --all --prune` into one clone while the remote had new commits; in 5 of 5 rounds one exited 1 with "cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/main': is at X but expected Y". Any fetch error is a refusal by design ('A failed fetch must never silently launch from stale refs').
findings.impact: Starting two agents at nearly the same time while origin has new commits makes one launch fail with git.fetch_failed. Ways this happens: two clicks, desktop plus phone, or pressing Fetch during a launch.
findings.fix: Serialize fetches per repository with a mutex keyed by the common dir. A caller that arrives while a fetch is in flight waits and reuses its result, or treats a fetch completed within the last few seconds as fresh.

v1.reason: `fetch_remote` (git.rs:938-960) runs `git fetch --all --prune` with no per-repository serialization. It is reached from refresh_new_worktree (969-974) via WorktreeCreate's prepare (113-114) and session.create's prepare (session.rs:866), and from git.fetch's prepare (583). All three run off the store mutex, so they can overlap. Two overlapping fetches that update the same remote-tracking ref fail in git's ref locking ('cannot lock ref ... is at X but expected Y' or an existing .lock). Any non-zero exit becomes git.fetch_failed and aborts the launch by design. The trigger is narrower than claimed. The desktop launch sheet sends its multi-agent session.create calls one at a time (launch.rs:799-805, each awaited) and disables itself on click. task.dispatch reaches session.create through invoke_registered, which runs the prepare inside the open transaction, so those calls are serialized by the store mutex. A race therefore needs two independent clients (desktop plus phone, an MCP agent creating sessions, or Fetch pressed during a launch) inside one fetch window, while origin has moved. The result is a refusal the user can retry; nothing is lost.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low: rare trigger, and the failure is retryable with no data harm. The suggested fix (a per-common-dir mutex, plus reusing a fetch that completed seconds ago) is fine. Related problem outside this finding: because task.dispatch runs session.create's prepare under the held transaction (engine.rs:325-341), a dispatch that creates a session runs the network fetch (up to 20 s) and the worktree checkout while holding the store mutex. That freezes the bus, which is a CLAUDE.md invariant issue worth its own finding.

findings.title: `.relay/` is only excluded when Relay creates a pooled worktree; primary-checkout sessions get Relay's files committed
findings.evidence:
ensure_excluded (39-41) adds .relay/, .claude/settings.local.json and .codex/hooks.json to .git/info/exclude. Its only caller is worktree::create (199). A session on the primary checkout never triggers it, yet:
- install_git writes .relay/hooks/<session>/pre-commit into the repo (session.rs:890-893, hooks.rs:100-139);
- the provider install writes .relay/agent-statusline.sh, .relay/relay.settings.json, .relay/relay.mcp.json (with the absolute relay binary path) and .claude/settings.local.json (hooks.rs:386-411).
The Unreal plugin makes primary the default (plugin.json:18, D160). The desktop smart commit sends all:true when nothing is staged (code_git.rs:277-281), which runs `git add -A` (git.rs:544-546). Status-cleanliness tests cover only pooled worktrees (tests/sessions.rs:768-770). Separately, exclude_paths is an unlocked read-modify-write of the exclude file (49-65), raced by skills::apply (skills.rs:247-249). This is recorded as an unfixed flake in docs/upstream-v3/READINESS.md:86-91.
findings.impact: On a project whose sessions run in the main checkout (every Unreal project with the plugin on), Relay's generated hook scripts, its MCP/status-line config with machine-specific absolute paths, and .claude/settings.local.json appear as changes. The first smart commit commits them and they get pushed to the team. Teammates' Claude sessions then pick up hook commands that point at a relay binary they do not have. The race can also drop .relay/ from the exclude file in pooled setups.
findings.fix: Call ensure_excluded wherever Relay first writes into a repo or checkout: session.create's prepare for every checkout kind, and project.add. Make exclude_paths take hooks::writes() and write via a temp file plus rename.

v1.reason: `ensure_excluded` has exactly one production caller, worktree::create (worktree.rs:199); the rg search shows only that and a test. session.create's prepare for `"primary"` (session.rs:860-865) and for an explicit existing path (877-888) never calls it, but it still runs `hooks::install_git`, which writes `<repo>/.relay/hooks/<session>/pre-commit` (hooks.rs:100-139). The Claude install writes `.relay/agent-statusline.sh`, `.relay/relay.settings.json` and `.relay/relay.mcp.json` (with the absolute relay binary path) plus `.claude/settings.local.json` into the worktree (hooks.rs:378-411). plugins.rs:208-214 together with plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18 (D160) makes primary the default for Unreal projects, so a project that has never had a pooled worktree gets these files with no exclude entry. The desktop's smart commit sends `all: true` when nothing is staged (code_git.rs:277-278), which runs `git add -A` (git.rs:544-546) and commits them. The exclude_paths read-modify-write race with skills.rs:247-249 is real and documented as an unfixed flake at READINESS.md:86-91.
v1.correction: A project that has ever created a pooled worktree is already protected, because the exclude file persists. The exposure is primary-only projects, chiefly Unreal ones. For the fix, calling ensure_excluded from session.create's prepare (every checkout kind) and from project.add is right. For the race, serialise with a lock or use temp file plus rename; rename alone does not prevent lost updates between two read-modify-write writers.

findings.title: git.pr.list downloads every PR of the repository (all states, every page) on each git-panel refresh
findings.evidence: The command is `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100&sort=updated&direction=desc`, with a 10 s budget (PR_LIST_TIMEOUT). The desktop's refresh_git calls git.pr.list alongside git.branches and git.log (code_git.rs:578-583). refresh_git runs on every file.changed / git.changed / worktree.changed event (app.rs:1232-1240, editor.rs:508-524). The panel only uses PRs whose head is the current branch (code_git.rs:592-604). BUS.md:828 still documents the op as returning open PRs only.
findings.impact: Each refresh costs ceil(total PRs / 100) GitHub API calls, and the panel refreshes back to back while agents edit files. A repo with about 500 PRs exhausts GitHub's 5,000 requests per hour within the hour; after that every gh call on the user's account is rate-limited. A repo with a few thousand PRs needs more than 10 s, so git.pr.list always times out: the panel never shows PR state, and the merged-PR branch cleanup it drives never runs.
findings.fix: For the panel, query only the current branch (`gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --json ..` or `pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>&state=all`) and cache the result per project with a TTL/ETag. Run the full scan used for cleanup rarely and incrementally: sort by updated and stop at the last updated_at already seen. Update BUS.md.

v1.reason: git.rs:1083-1091: list_pull_requests runs `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100...`, so it fetches every page of every PR in every state, with PR_LIST_TIMEOUT = 10 s (git.rs:83). The handler (git.rs:625) is register_unlocked, so it does not hold the store mutex, but it has no cache. The desktop calls git.pr.list from refresh_git on each refresh (code_git.rs:578-583) and uses only PRs whose head is the current branch (code_git.rs:592-604). refresh_git runs from Editor::invalidate, which is debounced to 1 s on the code/agents pages (editor.rs:508-524). invalidate fires on every file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed and integration.* event (app.rs:1232-1240). GitRefreshGuard keeps at most one refresh in flight and queues one more. While agents keep editing files, refreshes therefore run back to back, each costing ceil(N/100) API calls. On a repo with several hundred PRs that exceeds 5,000 calls an hour. On a repo with thousands of PRs the 10 s budget runs out, so the panel shows 'GitHub unavailable' and the merged-branch cleanup hook (git.rs:629-641) never runs from this path. BUS.md:828 still says the op returns open PRs with fields { number, branch, draft, url, title }, so the doc has drifted from the code.
v1.correction: No bus freeze: the op is register_unlocked. Cost per refresh is about one call per 100 PRs, so small repos stay under the rate limit. The impact is real only for repos with a few hundred PRs or more. Refresh is coalesced by the 1 s debounce plus a single in-flight guard, not run per event. Fix: query only the current head branch for the panel (pulls?head=owner:branch&state=all), cache per project with a TTL, and keep the full scan for the cleanup sweep. Update BUS.md:828.

findings.title: git.branches still runs a merge-base walk per branch with no object cache; the PERF §1.3 fix went only into the duplicate branches_for
findings.evidence: The git.branches handler computes merged per branch with `head.as_ref().and_then(|h| repo.merge_base(*h, id.detach()).ok())` (324-328), on a repo opened without object_cache_size_if_unset. branches_for (1445-1513) builds the same Branch rows with a single merged_tips walk and a 16 MiB object cache. Commit f2789df changed only branches_for: the handler is identical in f2789df~1 and f2789df. Yet FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24 credits git.branches with '§1.3: one walk decides merged for every branch; object cache on'. The owners SQL is also duplicated: worktree_owners_by_branch (18-32) vs an inline copy (1463-1474).
findings.impact: git.branches runs on every git-panel refresh, i.e. continuously while agents work. PERF §1.3 measured this algorithm at 520 ms CPU and 545 MB allocated for about 150 branches and 65 commits. That cost repeats on every refresh in a busy repo, and the two copies will keep drifting apart.
findings.fix: Keep one function that builds Branch rows (merged_tips, object cache, owners map). Call it from git.branches and from the delete/clean paths, running it unlocked. Correct the FIXES table.

v1.reason: The git.branches handler (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:290-343, registered with register_unlocked) still opens the repo with no object cache. For every local branch it computes `repo.merge_base(*h, id.detach())` (lines 324-328). branches_for (1445-1513) sets `repo.object_cache_size_if_unset(16 * 1024 * 1024)` and calls merged_tips (1289), which decides `merged` for every branch in one walk. At both f2789df~1 and f2789df the handler starts with the same code (`register_unlocked::<Branches>` ... `worktree_owners_by_branch`), so the perf commit changed only branches_for. Its message says "branches_for decides merged with one walk ... git.branches 10 ms to 0.9 ms". FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24 credits git.branches with the §1.3 fix, but the handler never received it. BASELINE §1.3 itself says git.branches varied between 0.6 ms and 10 ms depending on how much history the fixture had, so the claimed 11x is fixture variance. The owners SQL is also duplicated: worktree_owners_by_branch (18-32) and the inline loop in branches_for (1463-1474). The desktop client calls git.branches on every git panel render (code_git.rs:579) and from project_files.rs:194.
v1.correction: Calibrate the impact. The handler runs unlocked, so it never blocks the bus. The cost is CPU, allocation and Code-page latency, scaling as branches × distance to the base. The 520 ms / 545 MB figure was measured on clean_merged, not on git.branches, whose baseline was 10 ms on the perf fixture; on a large real repo with old branches it can reach hundreds of ms or more. The primary category is performance (an unapplied perf fix), with duplication and docs drift (the FIXES table row) as secondary. Fix: build the Branch rows in one helper that takes the owners map as a parameter, so it runs unlocked for git.branches and from ctx.tx() for the delete and clean paths. Have git.branches call it and add remote_branches. Correct FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24.

findings.title: tree_diff_files reports directories as changed files in git.show and git.diff {base}
findings.evidence: The callback matches Addition, Deletion, Modification and Rewrite and pushes a DiffFile for every non-empty location; it never checks entry_mode. gix-diff 0.66 emits changes for tree entries: a (tree, tree) pair with different ids is visited as Change::Modification before it recurses (gix-diff tree/function.rs:301-320); whole subtrees are visited as Addition/Deletion (131-191); and the rewrite tracker passes tree modifications straight through (rewrites/tracker.rs:171-184). For a tree, find_object(..).try_into_blob() fails, so the entry gets empty text and 0/0 counts. The desktop commit panel prints files.len() as 'N FILES CHANGED' (code_git.rs:1462-1468).
findings.impact: A commit touching crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs shows 5 changed 'files': four directories with +0 -0, plus the file. Every count and list built on git.show or git.diff {base}, including what agents read, is inflated the same way.
findings.fix: Skip entries whose entry_mode is a tree (and, for modifications, previous_entry_mode). While there, report Rewrite{copy:true} as "C" rather than "R".

v1.reason: tree_diff_files (git.rs:1161-1255) pushes a DiffFile for every Addition, Deletion, Modification and Rewrite with a non-empty location and never checks entry_mode. In gix-diff 0.66, tree/function.rs handle_lhs_and_rhs_with_equal_filenames visits Change::Modification for a (tree, tree) pair with different oids before it queues recursion. add_entry_schedule_recursion and delete_entry_schedule_recursion visit tree entries too. Rewrite tracking is on by default (gix Tree::changes uses Options::from_configuration). Tracker::try_push_change passes modifications through, and tree additions and deletions are emitted later when nothing matches them. location defaults to Location::Path (gix diff.rs:30), so a directory's path is non-empty. For a tree id, try_into_blob fails, so the row has empty text and +0 -0. git.show (git.rs:1158) and git.diff {base} (git.rs:199) both use this function. The desktop commit panel prints files.len() as 'N FILES CHANGED' (code_git.rs:1462-1468). The only test (tests/phase8.rs:248-256) commits a root-level file and checks files[0], so it cannot catch the bug.
v1.correction: Skip a change when entry_mode.is_tree() (and, for Modification, previous_entry_mode.is_tree() with entry_mode.is_tree()). Optionally map Rewrite{copy:true} to "C". Add a test that commits a file in a nested directory and asserts files.len() == 1.

findings.title: git.branch.create checks out the new branch in a live session's checkout, bypassing the guard that git.branch.switch enforces
findings.evidence: checkout defaults to true, and the handler runs `git switch -c <name> [start]` (366-374) in whatever root resolve_root returns, with no session-ownership check. BranchSwitch refuses the same move with git.checkout_session_owned ('This checkout belongs to the live session ..; its agent decides its branch', 389-401). The desktop branch picker always offers 'Create and switch' and sends checkout:true with the selected checkout (code_git.rs:974-1037), including an agent's worktree.
findings.impact: Creating a branch while viewing an agent's checkout moves that agent onto the new branch mid-task. Its later commits land on a branch that no session row records (sessions.branch goes stale), so branch-ownership checks and closed-session cleanup reason about the wrong branch.
findings.fix: When checkout is true, apply BranchSwitch's live-session owner check. Alternatively, offer only checkout:false for checkouts owned by a session.

v1.reason: BranchCreate (git.rs:345-385) defaults `checkout` to true and runs `git switch -c <name> [start]` in the root that resolve_root picks. It never checks whether that checkout belongs to a live session. BranchSwitch (387-401) runs `SELECT name FROM sessions WHERE project_id=?1 AND worktree=?2 AND state!='closed'` and refuses with git.checkout_session_owned. In the desktop picker (apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:991-1037), 'Create and switch' always sends `"checkout":true` through git_action. That calls self.payload, which adds the currently viewed worktree (editor.rs:890-895). Nothing on the client side hides the button for a session-owned checkout. So creating a branch while viewing an agent's worktree moves that agent's checkout to the new branch, which is exactly the move BranchSwitch refuses. sessions.branch then still names the old branch.
v1.correction: The user explicitly chose 'Create and switch', so this is an inconsistency between the two guards rather than a silent action. Impact is a stale sessions.branch and an agent whose branch changes mid-task. Severity is medium at most. Separately, BranchCreate is registered with Engine::register, so the `git switch` (worktree::git_mutate, a plain Command::output() with no timeout) and the `git worktree list` inside root_verify both run while the store mutex is held. The same applies to Stage and Unstage. That breaks the CLAUDE.md invariants and is worth its own finding if no other auditor reported it.

findings.title: worktree::git / git_mutate and the GitHub helpers run subprocesses with no timeout and no prompt suppression
findings.evidence: git() is `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()`. It does not use proc::output_with_timeout, does not set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and does not use ssh BatchMode. Through git_mutate it runs git push (git.rs:617), add -A (545), commit (571), stage/unstage, branch create/delete, and the git calls inside worktree::remove, create and rename_branch. The same pattern appears in validate_branch_name (git.rs:1269-1274), git.pr.open (679-681), hooks::run_user_pre_commit (hooks.rs:210-213), github::status (`gh api user`, github.rs:45), github::repositories (paginated, 68-71), download_skills (`git clone --depth 1 <url>`, 106-110) and collect_skills (155-157). CLAUDE.md requires every handler subprocess to go through proc::output_with_timeout.
findings.impact: A push over a stalled connection, or one waiting on an SSH host-key or passphrase prompt (git and ssh prompt on /dev/tty when the engine has a terminal, e.g. a dev instance started from a shell, or via a GUI askpass), never returns. The engine thread and the git process stay stuck. The desktop gives up after 30 s and re-enables the panel, and each retry adds another stuck push. skill.install of a private or misspelled github.com repo makes git clone wait for credentials in the same way. In the locked callers covered by the locked-mutations finding, the same hang freezes the bus indefinitely.
findings.fix: Route git() and the github.rs/hooks.rs calls through proc::output_with_timeout with per-call budgets: about 30 s for local ops, longer for push/fetch/clone. Set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes' and GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1. Make this change together with SIGTERM-first in proc.rs, otherwise timed-out mutations will leave stale locks.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:26-33 `git()` is a bare `Command::new("git")...output()`, and `git_mutate` (line 36) just forwards to it. It sets no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT and no timeout. The codebase is inconsistent with itself here. `fetch_remote` (git.rs:938-960), `run_switch` (git.rs:1347-1351), the `worktree add` inside `worktree::create` (worktree.rs:212-215), branch_cleanup.rs:114 and branch_cleanup.rs:171 (GH_PROMPT_DISABLED) all use `proc::output_with_timeout` with prompts disabled. Push (git.rs:600-618, `register_staged`, prepare phase) goes through the unbounded `git_mutate`, so a stalled push or one waiting on a prompt keeps a worker thread and the git child alive indefinitely. Most of these calls are in unlocked or staged-prepare phases, so in the common case the bus stays up and only a worker thread is held: Push, CommitOp `add -A`, SkillInstall `download_skills` (provider.rs:211-216, staged), GitHubStatusOp and GitHubRepoList (register_unlocked). The listed locations are accurate: github.rs:44, :68-70, :109, :155; hooks.rs:210-213; git.rs:1269-1274.
v1.correction: The case most worth fixing is one the finding only covers by reference. `git.pr.open` (git.rs:666-690) is registered with plain `Engine::register`, so `gh pr create` (a network call, with no timeout and no GH_PROMPT_DISABLED) runs while the store mutex is held, which freezes every request including keystrokes. Stage, Unstage, BranchCreate, BranchDelete and CleanMerged likewise run unbounded local git (`add` can run LFS clean filters) under the mutex. Pre-commit (hooks.rs:210) is a user hook that legitimately runs a long time; it runs in the staged prepare phase, so give it a generous budget instead of a short one. Rust's `output()` already sets stdin to null, so a prompt only blocks through /dev/tty or askpass; that trigger is less frequent than the finding implies. A stalled network push remains a realistic trigger.

findings.title: Paths are passed to git as pathspecs, so a bracketed filename also stages (or, via file.restore_head, discards) its glob matches
findings.evidence: Stage builds `vec!["add","--"]` plus the caller's paths (501-503). Unstage uses `reset HEAD --` or `rm --cached --` (521-527). file.restore_head runs `git_mutate(&root, &["checkout","--",&p.path])` (file.rs:256). A `--` separator does not disable pathspec magic. Verified: `git add -- "src/[id].tsx"` also staged src/i.tsx and src/d.tsx. validate_path only rejects `..` and absolute paths.
findings.impact: Bracketed names are routine in Next.js, SvelteKit and Nuxt (pages/[id].tsx, [slug]/page.tsx). Staging or unstaging one such file also stages or unstages any sibling whose name matches the character class. file.restore_head on such a file throws away uncommitted edits in those siblings. Names containing * or ? behave the same way.
findings.fix: Pass --literal-pathspecs (a global option placed before the subcommand), or set GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, for these commands.

v1.reason: Stage builds `vec!["add", "--"]` plus the caller's paths (git.rs:501-503). Unstage uses `reset HEAD --` or `rm --cached --` (520-526). file.restore_head runs `git_mutate(&root, &["checkout", "--", &p.path])` (file.rs:256). None of them sets --literal-pathspecs or GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS; rg finds neither anywhere in crates. validate_path (git.rs:780) rejects only absolute paths and `..`. I reproduced this in a scratch repo: `git add -- 'src/[id].tsx'` also staged src/i.tsx and src/d.tsx. `git reset HEAD -- 'src/[id].tsx'` also unstaged src/i.tsx. `git checkout -- 'src/[id].tsx'` silently discarded uncommitted edits in src/i.tsx. Pathspec magic prefixes such as `:(glob)` and `:!` also pass validation.
v1.correction: The trigger is rarer than the finding implies. The bracket class must match a real sibling, e.g. `[id].tsx` against `i.tsx` or `d.tsx`, or `app/[slug]/page.tsx` against `app/s/page.tsx`. Ordinary Next.js trees seldom have such siblings, and names containing `*` or `?` are rare. The consequence on file.restore_head is silent loss of uncommitted edits, so this is rated medium as data-loss in an uncommon edge case. Fix: pass `--literal-pathspecs` before the subcommand, or set GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, in these three call sites. The simplest place is git_mutate's callers for path-taking ops.

findings.title: The commit gate judges a numstat taken before the lock, then `git commit` commits whatever the index holds at that later moment
findings.evidence: prepare computes staged_numstat(&root) (557) with nothing locked. finish later passes it to `guardrail::enforce(.. Some(&numstat) ..)` and runs `git commit --no-verify` (561-572). That commits the index as it stands at that moment and skips the per-session pre-commit gate hook. Nothing ties the commit to the tree that was evaluated.
findings.impact: Anything staged between prepare and finish is committed without being checked against protected paths or caps: the agent's own `git add` in its shell, or another tool. An agent can simply retry until the race lands. Separately, outside this chunk: the default denied_commands (settings.rs:33) do not include `git commit --no-verify`, so an agent with a shell can skip the hook-based gate entirely.
findings.fix: Gate a snapshot. In prepare, run `git write-tree` and compute the numstat for that tree. In finish, commit exactly that tree: `git commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD -m ..`, then `git update-ref HEAD <new> <old>` as a compare-and-swap. Alternatively, recompute the numstat inside finish and refuse if it changed.

v1.reason: CommitOp's prepare stage (git.rs:536-559) runs unlocked. It stages (`add -A` if all), refreshes hooks, runs the user's pre-commit hook and computes `staged_numstat(&root)`. finish (560-576) passes that stale numstat to guardrail::enforce(GateKind::Commit) and then runs `git commit --no-verify -m`, which commits whatever the index holds at that moment and skips the gate hook. Nothing ties the committed tree to the evaluated numstat. Anything staged between prepare and the lock is committed without being checked against protected paths and caps, and the user's pre-commit hook also judged a different index. The related claim holds as well. Shell commits are gated only by the per-worktree core.hooksPath pre-commit hook (hooks.rs:111, 153). The default denied_commands (settings.rs:33) are ["rm -rf", "git reset --hard", "git clean -fd", "git push --force"], and nothing else in crates/relay-core matches `--no-verify` or `core.hooksPath` overrides on agent commands.
v1.correction: Calibration: the race on the bus path is the weaker part of this. Agents can call git.commit only with session.bus_writes (guardrail.rs:363-366; agent_surface.rs:111 asserts that a builder cannot by default). Every agent has a shell, and from there `git commit --no-verify` (or `-c core.hooksPath=...`) skips the commit gate outright, so the race adds little for an adversarial agent. On its own the race is low: the window is short and it needs concurrent staging, e.g. an agent staging in a checkout the user is committing from the desktop. The --no-verify shell bypass is the real guardrail escape (medium to high). It is arguably its own root cause and should be reported separately if no other auditor has.
