findings.evidence: `e.register::<ProjectClone>` runs `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()` inside the request transaction with the store mutex held. It does not go through proc::output_with_timeout, sets no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and does not null stdin. The registry describes the op as "(async; project.changed when done)" (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:37-38), and the native client allows it 1800 s (client.rs:65-67). By contrast git.rs fetch_remote (L937-952) uses a timeout, a null stdin and runs outside the transaction.
findings.impact: Every clone freezes the whole bus (UI queries, agent MCP calls, every lock-taking op) for its full duration: seconds to tens of minutes for large or LFS-heavy repositories. A clone that waits on a credential prompt or helper blocks it indefinitely.
findings.fix: Make it register_staged: clone in the prepare phase via proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and stdin null, then run project.add in the short finish phase. Alternatively run it as a background job that emits project.changed, as the op description already claims.

v1.reason: workspace.rs ~L228-247 registers ProjectClone with plain `e.register`, so the handler runs inside the transaction with the store mutex held. It calls `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()`. That is a raw `.output()`, not proc::output_with_timeout, and it has no deadline. proc.rs's module doc says every subprocess forked from a handler goes through output_with_timeout and that long work belongs after commit. The op is advertised as "(async; project.changed when done)" (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:37-38) but is fully synchronous. The native client gives it a 1800 s request timeout (client.rs:67) and calls it from onboarding (onboarding.rs:527). For the whole clone, every other locked request (UI queries, agent MCP calls, mutations) waits on the mutex. A clone stuck on authentication never returns. The cleanup `fs::remove_dir_all` on failure also runs under the lock.
v1.correction: One claim is wrong: Rust's `Command::output()` already defaults stdin to null, so "does not null stdin" is not accurate. The hang risk comes instead from the missing GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and the missing deadline. git prompts on /dev/tty when the engine has a controlling terminal, and it may run a GUI askpass or credential helper that waits for input. session.input does not touch SQLite (D148), so raw keystrokes may still flow, but everything else that takes the lock freezes. Fix: register_staged. Clone in prepare via proc::output_with_timeout (long deadline) with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (and GIT_ASKPASS unset or `true`). Then invoke project.add in the short finish phase and delete the destination on finish failure. Alternatively make it truly async, with a worker thread and a project.changed emit, as the op description already claims.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what is claimed. crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:228 uses plain `e.register::<ProjectClone>`. For such handlers, dispatch_inner takes `self.store.lock()` and opens the transaction (engine.rs:953-956), then calls the handler (engine.rs:980). Line 234 runs a raw `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()`: no deadline, and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, which every other git call that can reach a remote sets (git.rs:943 and 1349, worktree.rs:213, branch_cleanup.rs:114). D144 and D149 forbid exactly this, and so does proc.rs's module doc ("Long-running work belongs on a worker thread after commit"). D149's list of converted ops includes git.fetch and skill.install but not project.clone.

(b) Reachability. The op is UserOnly, so agents cannot call it. It is reached three ways: desktop onboarding "clone from GitHub" (onboarding.rs:527, which passes GitHub's HTTPS clone_url); `relay cmd`; and any paired phone (relay-remote wire::gate forwards every actor=user line). It runs once per project added from GitHub. That is an occasional but normal flow, and it hurts when other agent sessions are running, which is the app's normal state. The project's own perf baseline put a LOCAL 1,500-file clone at 263 ms p50 and 694 ms p95 (BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:210). Network clones take seconds to minutes. With git-lfs installed, checkout also downloads every LFS object, which is many minutes for game-asset repositories.

(c) Consequence. The store mutex is held for the whole clone.
- Agents: every agent request blocks, even unlocked queries, because token auth locks the store (engine.rs:1377-1378).
- Agent tool use: every Claude/Codex PreToolUse hook calls guardrail.gate, a locked handler (guardrail.rs:304). The CLI has no client timeout, and Relay installs these hooks with timeout 30 (hooks.rs:351, 521).
- Other blocked ops: every UI and phone mutation, session.create and session.close (180 s client timeout), and new terminal attaches.
- Still working: PTY output (pty.rs never touches the store) and keystrokes (D148 fast path; each GUI terminal has its own connection, terminal.rs:476).
- Desktop UI, independent of the mutex: the clone is sent on the main control connection (app.rs:1111-1116; it is not in is_lifecycle_request). The engine serves each connection strictly in order (socket.rs handle_conn awaits every dispatch before reading the next line). So all other UI calls queue behind the clone and fail at 30 s with "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown", and their engine-side effects still land later.
- Indefinite hang: git with prompts enabled opens /dev/tty. An engine launched from a terminal (the documented `relay serve` usage) has one. A clone that needs credentials with no helper configured, or an SSH URL with an unknown host key or a locked key, then waits on that tty, or is stopped by SIGTTIN if the engine was backgrounded. The bus stays frozen until the git child is killed. Under the systemd unit there is no tty and git fails fast, unless a GUI askpass or credential helper waits.
- No data loss: the transaction holds only reads until project.add.

(d) Severity: high is right. This is literally "a freeze of the bus or the UI" in a normal flow. It is not critical: the clone is user-initiated and occasional, the bus recovers when git exits, and the unbounded case needs a waiting prompt.

(e) The proposed fix is directionally right but incomplete; see correction. One possible amplifier is unverified: if Claude Code lets a tool call proceed when its PreToolUse hook times out, any lock hold over 30 s would let agent Bash/Edit/Write run without a guardrail verdict. That is provider behaviour I could not check from this repo, and it deserves its own finding.
v2.correction:
1. "does not null stdin" is wrong. Command::output() already defaults stdin to Stdio::null, and git reads credentials from /dev/tty, not stdin. The hang comes from prompts being left enabled plus the missing deadline.

2. "freezes the whole bus" needs two qualifications. PTY output and keystrokes keep flowing. Unlocked queries from other user connections (the CLI, the phone) still run. The desktop UI, however, is frozen even apart from the mutex, because it sends project.clone on its main connection, which the engine serves serially.

3. "blocks indefinitely" is conditional. It needs git to reach a prompt that waits: an engine with a controlling tty, or a GUI askpass or credential helper. A systemd-launched engine fails fast instead.

4. The fix is incomplete, in four ways.
   (i) register_staged alone does not unfreeze the UI. Either also route project.clone over a dedicated connection on the client (add it to is_lifecycle_request at client.rs:50-62, as session.create already is), or make the op truly async: return at once, clone on a worker via after_commit, emit project.changed, and write the project.clone.completed audit row that BUS.md §5.1 (:247) and the registry text at relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38 already promise. Async also removes that docs drift.
   (ii) Prompt suppression: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 alone still lets askpass helpers and ssh prompt. Also set GIT_ASKPASS to an empty string (this skips core.askPass and SSH_ASKPASS) and use ssh -o BatchMode=yes when the user has no GIT_SSH_COMMAND. Add -c http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime so a stalled transfer fails, and run it through proc::output_with_timeout with a long deadline; its process-group kill also reaps git-remote-https and git-lfs.
   (iii) Once the existence check moves outside the lock, it can race a concurrent clone, and the failure cleanup `fs::remove_dir_all(&destination)` could delete the other clone. Clone into a unique temp directory inside the workspace, rename it into place in the short finish phase, and only ever delete the temp directory.
   (iv) Sibling to fix in the same change: crates/relay-core/src/github.rs:105-110 (skill.install's `git clone --depth 1`) is also a raw .output() with no deadline and no prompt suppression. It is staged and unlocked, so it does not hold the mutex, but it can hang its request forever.

Related additions: apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1111; apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:50; crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:332; docs/engine/BUS.md:247; crates/relay-core/src/github.rs:105.

findings.title: file.write diffs the whole old file with quadratic Myers (no deadline) while holding the store mutex
findings.evidence: The locked Write handler reads the old file with no size cap (`let old = fs::read_to_string(&path);` L76) and calls `line_counts(&old, &p.text)` (L103), which runs `TextDiff::from_lines(old, new)` (L602). similar 2.7's TextDiffConfig defaults to `deadline: None`, so Myers costs O((N+M)·D). guardrail.rs:1096-1099 documents a linear multiset counter written to "deliberately avoid quadratic LCS work on large generated files". evaluate_write already reads the same file and computes counts with it (guardrail.rs:562-583).
findings.impact: Saving a large file whose content mostly changed (a regenerated lockfile or JSON fixture, or an agent rewrite with no 1 MiB editor cap) holds the single store lock for seconds to much longer. That stalls every agent and UI request, and the file is read and counted twice.
findings.fix: Drop `similar` here. Make guardrail::changed_line_counts pub(crate) and reuse it, or have enforce return the counts it already computed. Cap or stream the old-file read.

v1.reason: Write is registered with e.register (file.rs:72), so the store mutex is held. It reads the old file with no cap (L76), then guardrail::enforce reads and line-counts the same file again (guardrail.rs:562-575, linear multiset). After that, line_counts (L599-610) runs `TextDiff::from_lines(old, new)`. In similar 2.7.0, TextDiffConfig.deadline defaults to None (text/mod.rs:45), and myers::diff_deadline has no heuristic cutoff, so the cost grows as O((N+M)*D). guardrail.rs:1096-1099 says explicitly that the linear counter exists to avoid this quadratic LCS work. Reachability: the 64 MiB hold (which, per #6, can never be lifted) keeps old files at or under 64 MiB. Within that range, a write that changes most of a large file is allowed outright when allow_if_recoverable sees the file as recoverable from git, or after the user confirms, and then the Myers diff runs under the lock.
v1.correction: Rated medium rather than high. The native editor loads at most 1 MiB (editor.rs:637), and ordinary saves change few lines, so D stays small and the diff is cheap. The bad case needs a large rewrite through file.write, mostly from an agent using MCP file_write or a whole-buffer replace in the editor. Fix as proposed: have enforce return its counts, or reuse changed_line_counts (pub(crate)), and drop `similar` from this handler. Note that this changes the meaning of the returned removed/added counts from LCS to multiset; alternatively set a deadline on TextDiff::configure().

findings.title: file.search reads every entry whole with no size cap, opens non-regular files through symlinks, and walks generated trees
findings.evidence: Only `e.file_type()...is_dir()` is tested (L323). Everything else (symlinks, FIFOs, sockets, device nodes) reaches `fs::File::open(&path).and_then(|mut file| read_to_end(&mut file, &mut buffer))` (L335-336). open follows symlinks, there is no size limit, and text detection happens only after the full read (L341). skip_dir skips only `.git .relay node_modules target` (L629-636), so build/, dist/, .gradle, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache and Binaries are read in full. The editor re-runs the search on every debounced invalidation while a query is present (editor.rs:508-523). The socket door processes one request per connection at a time (socket.rs:335-746). overlap.rs:246 `std::fs::read(worktree.join(path))` reads the same way before its 2 MB check.
findings.impact: A FIFO in the tree blocks open() forever, which pins a blocking-pool thread and stalls every later request on that client connection. A symlink to a device or a multi-GB asset makes the engine allocate without bound, and an OOM abort kills every session. In Unreal or Android projects, ordinary searches re-read gigabytes of build output every second while agents work.
findings.fix: Use symlink_metadata and search only regular files. Check md.len() against a cap before reading. Sniff the first few KB for NUL before reading the rest. Reuse a single generated-dir predicate (or git-ignore status) for the walk. Apply the same rules in overlap::changed_symbols.

v1.reason: In the Search handler (file.rs:303-379, register_unlocked) the only type check is `e.file_type().map(|t| t.is_dir())` (L323). DirEntry::file_type does not follow symlinks, so symlinks, FIFOs, sockets and devices all reach `fs::File::open(&path).and_then(|mut file| read_to_end(...))` (L335-336). That open follows symlinks, the read has no size cap, and the UTF-8 test runs only after the whole file is read (L341). skip_dir (L629-636) skips only .git/.relay/node_modules/target. Yet watch::is_generated_path (watch.rs:158-188), which list_dir already uses for file.tree (L527), also skips build, .gradle, dist, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache and Binaries. Search and tree have already diverged. The editor re-runs file.search after a 1 s debounce on every invalidation while a query is present and the page is code or agents (editor.rs:508-523). The native client sends almost every call over one socket connection (client.rs; only lifecycle ops and image_read use separate connections). The socket door awaits each request before reading the next (socket.rs:335-746). So one slow or blocked search stalls every later UI request on that connection, keystrokes included, even after the client's 30 s timeout gives up on it. A FIFO in the tree blocks open() indefinitely, and a symlink to /dev/zero makes read_to_end grow without bound. The common trigger is ordinary: a UE or Android project with GB of Intermediate/Binaries/build output gets that output re-read in full on rare-hit queries while agents work.
v1.correction: The usual trigger is generated trees and large binaries. FIFOs and device symlinks are rare edge cases that make it worse, not the main path. The searcher stops at `limit` hits (100 from the editor), so common queries end early; the cost falls on queries with few or no hits. Fix: reuse watch::is_generated_path, the predicate list_dir already uses, instead of skip_dir. Take symlink_metadata and search only regular files. Cap md.len() and sniff the first few KB for NUL before reading the rest. The overlap.rs:246 read was not independently verified here.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says, as of 361c6f9. The Search handler (file.rs:299, register_unlocked) checks only `e.file_type().map(|t| t.is_dir())` (L323). DirEntry::file_type does not follow symlinks, so symlinks, FIFOs and devices all fall through to `fs::File::open(&path).and_then(|mut file| read_to_end(..))` (L335-336). That open follows symlinks, nothing caps the size, and the UTF-8 test runs only after the whole file is read (L341). skip_dir (L629-636) skips only .git/.relay/node_modules/target. watch::is_generated_path (watch.rs:158-188) also skips build, .gradle, dist, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache and Binaries, and file.tree already uses it (list_dir, L518). So search walks output that the tree hides. I checked in a scratch test that an O_RDONLY open of a FIFO blocks (killed by timeout, exit 124), and that reading a directory fails with EISDIR, so symlinked directories are harmless.

(b) Reachable in normal use. The editor is the default "agents" page (app.rs:618, 747). Pressing Enter in its search box runs file.search with limit 100 (editor.rs:952-954, 1110). Queries with fewer than 100 hits, the usual case for a specific identifier, walk the whole tree. While a query stays in the box, every file/git/worktree/integration event for the project re-runs the search after 1 s (editor.rs:508-523). invalidate clears its pending flag before calling run_search, and run_search has no in-flight guard. Unreal and Android projects are first-class here (relay-cli/src/unreal.rs; watch.rs names their build directories). In those projects each search reads GBs: Intermediate, Binaries, Saved, build, .gradle, and also the version-controlled Content/*.uasset files. The repo's own measurement is 60 ms for 1,500 small files (docs/perf), and these trees hold tens of thousands of files and GBs, so a search takes seconds. Plain code repos see little effect: this repo walks about 160 MB.

(c) Consequence. All UI calls share one connection (app.rs:1111-1117), and the socket door awaits each request before reading the next (socket.rs:335-746). A slow search therefore holds back every UI request: tree, git, session and task refreshes, and button mutations. When searches take longer than events arrive, they stack up. Requests time out at the client after 30 s and show "Request timed out", but the engine still runs each one, so the backlog clears only after agents go quiet. A FIFO in the tree wedges that connection for good, until the user clicks Reconnect, which tears down the panes. Hits from build output pollute the results.

(d) High fits the rubric: a UI freeze in a normal flow for the app's main project types. It is not critical: the store lock is not held, other connections keep working, and the OOM and FIFO cases need unusual files.

(e) The proposed fix is right but incomplete (see correction).
v2.correction:
1. Keystrokes are NOT stalled, contrary to the first verifier. Each terminal pane opens its own connection (terminal.rs:476) and sends session.input on it (terminal.rs:234-241), as client.rs:1-2 states. Only the main UI connection stalls.
2. OOM is overstated. For regular files the buffer is sized to the largest file read and freed when the search ends. Growth is unbounded only with an endless source such as a symlink to /dev/zero, or a file close to free RAM such as a staged .pak. Treat the OOM and FIFO cases as edge cases. The main trigger is large trees plus the editor re-running the search.
3. overlap.rs:246 is a separate, low-severity site. It only reads .rs/.ts/.tsx/.svelte/.kt/.kts paths that git status reports as changed (overlap.rs:115-127, 241-246), and git never reports a FIFO, so it needs a deliberately planted symlink.
4. Fix, in file.rs:
   - Search only entries whose DirEntry type `is_file()`.
   - Open with O_NONBLOCK, or fstat after opening, so a file swapped between the check and the open cannot hang the search.
   - Skip files over a size cap, using e.metadata().len().
   - Read the first few KB and stop if it contains a NUL or invalid UTF-8 (allowing a truncated multi-byte character at the end); only then read the rest. This, not skipping generated directories, is what stops UE Content/*.uasset files being read in full.
   - Reuse watch::is_generated_path for directories, as file.tree does.
   - Make a read_dir failure on a subdirectory non-fatal. Today the `?` at file.rs:316-318 fails the whole search on one unreadable directory.
   - Side benefit: searching only regular files stops search from reading through symlinks that leave the worktree, matching file.read's safe_join rule (file.rs:489-503).
5. Fix, in the native client: add an in-flight or coalescing guard to editor::run_search (editor.rs:1100) so re-searches cannot pile up on the shared connection. This change is under apps/relay-native and cannot be compiled in CI, which must be stated.

findings.title: Rename/move/delete are gated as a write of the file's current content: full read under lock, and >64 MiB files always held
findings.evidence: `let text = fs::read_to_string(content).unwrap_or_default();` reads the entire file being renamed, moved or deleted and passes it as `new_text`. Rename and Move call it twice (L180-181, L209-210) and Delete once (L224). evaluate_write then stats the same path and, when `meta.len() > 64 * 1024 * 1024`, returns `hold("destructive_write", ... "larger than the 64 MiB comparison cap")` regardless of actor (guardrail.rs:563-571).
findings.impact: Every rename, move or delete of a file over 64 MiB (videos, Unreal assets, APKs) is held as a "destructive write" that the user or agent must get confirmed. Before that, the whole file (multiple GB) is read into memory, once or twice, while the store mutex is held.
findings.fix: Give moves and deletes their own gate: a protected-path and ownership check on source and destination with no content. Never read file contents for these ops.

v1.reason: guard_path_mutation (file.rs:571-588) does `fs::read_to_string(content).unwrap_or_default()`. std's read_to_string reads every byte before it checks UTF-8, so a multi-GB binary is read in full and then thrown away. This runs inside handlers registered with Engine::register (Rename L162, Move L189, Delete L220), so the store mutex is held throughout. Rename and Move call it twice, both times reading `from` (L180-181, L209-210). The result goes to guardrail::enforce as Write with path = the source path. evaluate_write (guardrail.rs:562-571) then stats that path and, for files over 64 MiB, returns `hold("destructive_write", ...)` for every actor. The finding missed something worse. That cap check never looks at `request.skip_policy` or at grants. guardrail.confirm replays the frozen op with skip_policy="destructive_write" (handlers/guardrail.rs:583 -> engine.rs:364-376), the replay reaches the same check, and enforce creates a fresh hold. Confirming therefore never succeeds. Rename, move or delete of any file over 64 MiB through file.* (and file.write to one) can never complete; each confirm just produces another hold.
v1.correction: Also add a skip_policy/grant check to the 64 MiB branch at guardrail.rs:564 (or skip it when the content is unchanged), so a confirm can actually lift the hold. Related: Import (file.rs:286) reads each external source file in full under the lock the same way, though there the cap does not trigger because the destination does not exist yet. Fix as proposed: give path-only mutations a protected-path and ownership check on source and destination with no content read.

v2.reason:
(a) Confirmed at 361c6f9. `guard_path_mutation` (file.rs:571-589) runs `fs::read_to_string(content).unwrap_or_default()` on the source and passes the result as `new_text` to `enforce(GateKind::Write, path=<source rel>)`. Rename (file.rs:180-181) and Move (209-210) pass `&from` as the content on both calls; Delete (224) calls it once. std's `read_to_string` reserves `metadata.len()` and reads to EOF before it checks UTF-8, so a binary file is read in full and then thrown away. All three handlers are registered with `e.register` (file.rs:164/192/221), so this runs with the store mutex held (engine.rs:954). `evaluate_write` then stats the source and, above 64 MiB, returns `hold("destructive_write", …)` (guardrail.rs:562-571) for every actor, before any `skip_policy` or `granted_path` check.

The first verifier's escalation holds. `guardrail.confirm` is user-only and replays the held op with skip_policy="destructive_write" (handlers/guardrail.rs:583, engine.rs:364-376). The replay hits the same branch, and `enforce` inserts a fresh hold (handlers/guardrail.rs:690-703). Confirm itself returns Ok, so the pipeline commits that new hold along with marking the old one confirmed (engine.rs:997-1037). The native client then shows "Allowed, but the action then failed: … larger than the 64 MiB comparison cap" and refreshes into a new open hold (guardrail_pages.rs:299-305). A grant cannot lift the hold either. No test covers this path; the only confirm test (tests/phase8.rs:159-175) covers a protected path.

(b) Who can trigger it:
- The user, from the native file tree: right-click Rename or Move to trash (project_files.rs:298-302, then editor.rs:1262-1266), or drag-and-drop move (project_files.rs:371-378).
- Agents, through file.rename/move/delete (`Actors::All`).

It fires every time on a file over 64 MiB. The tree hides build folders (watch.rs:169-186), so the realistic triggers are visible source assets: Content/*.uasset/.umap, .blend, .fbx, .psd, video. Those are routine in the Unreal/Blender projects Relay ships tooling for, and rare in a code-only repository.

(c) What happens: that file can never be renamed, moved or trashed through Relay. Every attempt and every "Allow once" adds another open hold and notification, and reads the whole file into memory again with the store mutex held. For a multi-GB file that stalls every locked bus op for seconds and raises memory use by the size of the file. No data is lost; the workaround is the OS file manager or a shell. BUS.md §9.2 applies destructive_write only to `gate{write}` and `file.write`, and only protected paths to rename/move/delete, and it promises for a user "you confirm, it proceeds". So the behaviour contradicts the documented contract.

(d) High is right, at the low end of it. This is a deterministic, total failure of a normal file-tree flow for a whole class of files, the designed escape hatch loops forever, and large files stall the bus. If confirm worked, this would be medium.

(e) The proposed fix (a path-only gate: protected-path check with grants and the user-hold behaviour on source and destination, no content read, no destructive-write or shape checks) is exactly what BUS.md §9.2 specifies. It needs its own evaluator entry, because `evaluate_write` called with new_text=None and diff=None returns "kind=write requires new_text or diff" and holds on shape gates.
v2.correction:
1. For a file over 64 MiB the source is read once per attempt, not "once or twice": the hold from the first `guard_path_mutation` call returns through `?` before the second call runs. Each confirm repeats that read. For a source of 64 MiB or less, rename and move read it three times (twice in `guard_path_mutation`, once more as `old` at guardrail.rs:572) and delete reads it twice.

2. The handler registrations are at file.rs:164 (Rename), 192 (Move) and 221 (Delete), not L162/189/220 as the first verifier wrote.

3. Add BUS.md §9.2 as evidence. Its policy table applies only protected paths to file.rename/move/delete, and destructive_write only to `gate{write}` and `file.write`.

4. The fix is incomplete without the verifier's addition. The 64 MiB branch (guardrail.rs:563-571) must also honour `skip_policy == "destructive_write"` and `granted_path`. Otherwise `file.write` or `file.create` aimed at an existing file over 64 MiB still loops on every confirm.

5. Caveat for that addition. `confirm` replays with the confirming user's session, which is None, because `ctx.set_session(hold.session_id)` runs only after `replay_registered` (handlers/guardrail.rs:583 vs 593). An agent's held `file.*` op whose payload omitted `worktree` therefore replays against the project root (file.rs:401-407), not the agent's worktree. Set the hold's session, or freeze the resolved worktree into the held payload, before making these confirms succeed.

6. Related: Import (file.rs:286) reads each external source in full with the lock held, but it is user-only and never hits the cap.

findings.title: project.remove fails with a foreign-key error for any project that has labels
findings.evidence: The ordered delete list (L354-375) clears tasks, modules, notes and so on but never `labels`. v16 created `labels (... project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ...)` with no ON DELETE CASCADE (store.rs:315-320), and foreign_keys is ON (store.rs:397). L380 `DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1` therefore violates the FK. Labels are created by task.label.add (task.rs:137). A throwaway SQLite run of this schema gave `IntegrityError FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. registry_remove.rs tests never create labels.
findings.impact: A project whose tasks were ever labelled cannot be removed: the user gets an internal error. workspace.remove with force fails the same way, because it calls project.remove for each project.
findings.fix: Add `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1` after the tasks delete (task_labels cascades), or add ON DELETE CASCADE in a migration. Add a regression test that labels a task and then removes the project.

v1.reason: store.rs:315-319 (v16) creates `labels(... project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ...)` with no ON DELETE CASCADE, and no later migration changes it. foreign_keys is ON (store.rs:397, 414). The delete list in ProjectRemove (workspace.rs:354-375) never touches `labels`, and workspace.rs:380 runs `DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1`. Labels are inserted by task.rs:137 (via task.create's `labels` or task.label.add) and are never deleted, even after every task is untagged: task.rs:1219 deletes only task_labels rows. So any project that has ever had a label can never be removed, and there is no workaround op. I reproduced this in a throwaway SQLite run of that schema shape: `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. Every other table that references projects/tasks is either in the delete list or cascades (skill_projects, plugin_projects; task_labels and task_relations cascade from tasks; tasks.parent_id self-refs are deleted in one statement). The failure rolls back the whole transaction, so nothing is lost or half-removed.
v1.correction: Insert `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1` after the tasks delete. task_labels cascades from both tasks and labels, so order is not critical once tasks are gone. Add a regression test in tests/registry_remove.rs that labels a task and then removes the project. workspace.remove with force fails the same way through workspace.rs:173. Impact is a hard, permanent failure of a cleanup flow with no data loss. High is right because there is no workaround.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. store.rs:315-319 (v16) creates `labels(project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ...)` with no ON DELETE action. No later migration (up to v20) and no trigger changes that. foreign_keys is ON for the engine connection (store.rs:397). Fifteen tables reference projects(id). `labels` is the only one that neither cascades nor appears in the delete list at workspace.rs:354-375. So `DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1` at workspace.rs:380 fails. Label rows are only ever inserted: task.rs:137, through task.create's `labels` (task.rs:745) and task.label.add (task.rs:1191). Nothing deletes them: task.label.remove (task.rs:1219) deletes only task_labels rows, and the bus has no label-delete op.

I reproduced it with the real schema. A throwaway script parsed all 20 MIGRATIONS from store.rs and the 20 statements of the delete list from workspace.rs, then ran them on SQLite with foreign_keys=ON:
- With no labels, project removal succeeds.
- With one labelled task it fails with `IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, and the project and task remain.
- After the label is removed from every task it still fails.
- With `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1` inserted after the tasks delete, it succeeds and leaves labels and task_labels empty.

(b) Reachable in the normal desktop flow. The GTK sidebar and settings offer "Remove project…" and "Remove workspace…" (apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:475, 484, 809). Both send the op with `payload["force"] = json!(true)` every time (registry.rs:626). Labels are created from the GTK task form (task_pages.rs:495) and the label chips (task_pages.rs:689, 707), and by agents through task.create or task.label.add. Any project that has ever had a label can never be removed. Its workspace cannot be removed either, because workspace.rs:173 propagates the error with `?`. Every retry fails the same way. The only way out is hand-editing store.db.

(c) The dialog shows an internal "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed" error and the project stays. That is worse than a clean rollback, because the GTK path always uses force. Before the failing DELETE, project.remove runs session.close for every open session (workspace.rs:328) and device.run.stop for every live run (workspace.rs:349). Their effects outside SQLite are not rolled back:
- session.close's staged prepare phase runs inside the open transaction (engine.rs:328-348). It uninstalls the agent's git, Claude and Codex hooks (session.rs:1575, run_teardown) and deletes `.relay/hooks/<name>` (session.rs:1596).
- Its finish phase removes the PTY from the engine maps (session.rs:1602, engine.rs:616) and moves it into an after_commit closure (session.rs:1606).
- On the error path the pipeline rolls back (engine.rs:1074) and drops after_commit without running it. That drops the last Arc<Pty>, and Pty::drop SIGKILLs the agent's process group with no grace period (pty.rs:381-388).
- The on_exit callback was not silenced (session.rs:646-676), so it then marks the session 'exited' and a builder's active task 'failed'.
- device.run.stop has already removed and stopped the run's runtime (device.rs:265-267), but the run's row goes back to building/running.

End state: the user's agents for that project are killed, and the project and its records stay. No repository data is lost.

(d) High is correct. This is a deterministic, permanent failure of a normal UI flow with no in-app workaround, and the forced path leaves wrong state behind. It is not critical: project removal is not a frequent flow, and no repository data is lost.

(e) The proposed fix is correct, and the run above confirms it. Order is not critical because task_labels cascades from both tasks and labels.
v2.correction:
The first verifier wrote: "The failure rolls back the whole transaction, so nothing is lost or half-removed." That is wrong for the force path, and force is the only path the GTK dialog uses (registry.rs:626). By the time the FK check fails, the nested session.close calls have already:
- uninstalled each agent's hooks and deleted its `.relay/hooks/<name>` directory (session.rs:1575, 1596);
- removed each agent's PTY from the engine map (session.rs:1602).

When the transaction rolls back, the dropped after_commit closure SIGKILLs every agent through Pty::drop (pty.rs:381-388). on_exit then marks those sessions 'exited' and active builder tasks 'failed' (session.rs:646-676). device.run.stop has already stopped the runtimes (device.rs:265-267), while the run rows return to running.

Complete fix:
1. Add `"DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1"` right after `"DELETE FROM tasks WHERE project_id=?1"` (workspace.rs:364).
2. Add a regression test to tests/registry_remove.rs: label a task, open a session, call project.remove with force:true, and assert it succeeds and the labels table is empty.
3. Add a schema-driven test that walks pragma_foreign_key_list for every table and asserts each FK to projects(id) either has ON DELETE CASCADE or is covered by the delete list. The list is maintained by hand: plugin_projects was added to it in 9b4a327, but labels, which arrived in fcbdbce, was missed.
4. Optional: before the forced, side-effecting nested closes run, check that the project can actually be deleted, for example by trying the deletes inside a SAVEPOINT and rolling them back, so that a late failure cannot leave agents killed while the project remains.

findings.title: Relay trash is never purged although BUS.md promises a grace-window hard delete
findings.evidence: Delete moves the path to `root/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` (L230-232) and records a file_trash row. No code deletes payload dirs or rows, except that project.remove drops the rows and leaves the payloads (workspace.rs:369). `undo.grace_days` (settings.rs:42) is never read anywhere. BUS.md §5.4 says trashed files are "hard-deleted by the reconcile pass" after the grace window. The UI tells the user "The file can be restored from Relay trash" (editor.rs:1225) and offers no way to empty it.
findings.impact: Disk usage grows forever by everything deleted through Relay, and the project-root trash is never reclaimed. Trash inside a session worktree disappears when that worktree is removed, while its rows stay open and file.restore then fails.
findings.fix: Add a reconcile step that removes rows older than undo.grace_days along with their payload dirs, and drops rows whose worktree no longer exists. Delete payloads on project.remove.

v1.reason: Delete inserts a file_trash row and renames the path to root/.relay/trash/<id>/payload (file.rs:225-233). Nothing under crates/ deletes trash payloads or rows on age. Searching for 'trash' finds only the store schema, file.rs and project.remove's `DELETE FROM file_trash WHERE project_id=?1` (workspace.rs:369), which leaves the payload directories on disk. undo.grace_days is defined (settings.rs:42) and read only by a settings test. Recovery's reconcile pass prunes audit rows but not trash. That contradicts BUS.md §5.4 (docs/engine/BUS.md:288-292): 'hard-deleted by the reconcile pass'. The editor tells the user the file 'can be restored from Relay trash' (editor.rs:1225), and no UI empties the trash. When a session worktree is removed, its .relay/trash goes with it while the rows stay open, so file.restore then fails with an I/O error.
v1.correction: Growth is proportional to what the user deletes through Relay's editor or bus. Agents mostly delete through their own shells, and deleted source files are usually small. That is unbounded over time but not fast in normal use, so medium fits better than high. This is also docs drift against BUS.md §5.4. Fix: add a recovery/reconcile step that hard-deletes rows (and their payload directories) older than undo.grace_days, drops rows whose worktree is gone, and removes payloads on project.remove.

findings.title: Directory-level rename/move/delete bypass protected paths of the files inside the directory
findings.evidence: Rename checks only `from_rel` and `into_rel` (L180-181), Move does the same (L209-210), Delete checks only the named path (L224), and Import only the top-level `dest_rel` (L286). path_matches matches a path inside a protected pattern but never an ancestor of one (guardrail.rs:1164). The port confirms that pattern `config/*.json` against the operand `config` returns false.
findings.impact: A bus_writes session can rename, move or trash the parent directory of protected files, which moves the protected content out from under its pattern without any refusal. BUS.md §9.2 says protected paths apply to rename/move/delete "touching them".
findings.fix: When the operand is a directory, refuse if any protected pattern could match beneath it (pattern starts with `<dir>/`, or a glob whose literal prefix overlaps), or walk the directory and check each descendant.

v1.reason: Rename, Move and Delete call guard_path_mutation only with the operand path(s) (file.rs:180-181, 209-210, 224), and Import only with the top-level dest_rel (file.rs:286). The write-gate protected check is `cfg.protected_paths.iter().find(|p| path_matches(p, &path))` (guardrail.rs:512). path_matches returns true when the path equals the pattern, lies under it, or matches its glob (guardrail.rs:1161-1168), never when the operand is an ancestor of the pattern. Example: with protected 'config/secrets.json', file.rename of path 'config' to 'cfg' checks 'config' and 'cfg', both of which pass, and the protected file moves out from under its pattern. file.delete of 'config' trashes it, recoverably. This contradicts BUS.md:494, which says protected paths apply to rename/move/delete 'touching them'. The commit-time protected check (guardrail.rs:776-786) may still refuse a later commit that touches the old path, but the working-tree change has already happened.
v1.correction: For a directory operand, refuse when any protected pattern lies under it: the pattern starts with '<dir>/', or the glob's literal prefix is the dir or overlaps it. Alternatively, walk the subtree and check each descendant. Note that the commit gate is a partial downstream catch.

findings.title: file.create follows a dangling symlink at the final component, creating the file outside the worktree
findings.evidence: `if path.exists()` (L131) follows symlinks, so a dangling link looks absent. safe_join then canonicalizes only the parent (L491-494), and `fs::write(&path, text)` (L154) opens with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, which follows the link and creates its target. Import's copy() → `fs::copy(from, to)` (L624) behaves the same for a destination link.
findings.impact: The "path escapes the worktree through a symlink" protection does not hold for file.create: a session with bus_writes can create files outside its worktree root, past the write-root policy.
findings.fix: Create with `OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true)`; O_EXCL refuses any existing directory entry, including a link, and also closes the exists()-then-write race. In safe_join, judge the final component with symlink_metadata.

v1.reason: For a dangling symlink, path.exists() (file.rs:131) follows the link and returns false. safe_join then canonicalizes only the parent directory (file.rs:491-495), which is inside the root, so the check passes. guardrail::enforce is given the worktree-relative p.path, so write roots and protected paths judge the link's name rather than its target. fs::write(&path, text) (file.rs:154) opens with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, which follows the dangling link and creates the target outside the worktree with content the caller chose. file.write is not affected: it renames a temp file over the link, replacing the link itself. file.restore also uses rename. For a dir-kind create, create_dir_all fails on the link. Import's fs::copy follows the link the same way (file.rs:624), but file.import is UserOnly. Preconditions: a dangling link must already exist in the worktree (committed in the repo, or made by an agent's shell), and the caller needs bus_writes. An agent with a native shell usually has easier ways out, which is why this is medium rather than critical.
v1.correction: Create the file with OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true). O_EXCL refuses any existing directory entry, a dangling link included, and also closes the race between the exists() check and the write. In safe_join, judge the final component with symlink_metadata. Use the same create_new destination in import's copy() for files.

findings.title: safe_join requires the parent to exist, so nested creates, writes and restores fail and the create_dir_all calls are dead
findings.evidence: For a path that does not exist, `fs::canonicalize(path.parent().unwrap_or(root))` (L494) returns ENOENT whenever the parent is also missing, which becomes `file.not_found`. So `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` in Write (L105), Create (L151) and Restore (L247) never creates anything, and Create kind=dir only works one level deep. The UI's create dialog suggests `relative/path.rs` (editor.rs:1203). For existing paths, canonicalize(path) follows the final symlink (L492, L496), so links that point outside the worktree, or dangle, cannot be deleted, renamed or moved.
findings.impact: Common flows fail: creating `newdir/file.rs` from the UI, an agent writing a file in a new module directory, restoring a trashed file whose folder was trashed too. The user also cannot remove an outward or broken symlink from the Code page.
findings.fix: Canonicalize the deepest existing ancestor and check containment there. Treat the final component with symlink_metadata, so ops act on the link itself rather than its target.

v1.reason: file.rs:488-504 safe_join: when `path` does not exist and may_not_exist is true, it runs `fs::canonicalize(path.parent().unwrap_or(root))`, which returns ENOENT when the parent is also missing. That error is mapped to `file.not_found` at L497. Write (L74), Create (L130) and Restore (L245) all call safe_join(.., true) before their `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` calls at L105, L151-152 and L247. Those calls therefore only ever run on a parent that already exists, so they never create anything. Create kind=dir with `a/b` fails the same way. The only test (tests/phase8.rs:65-72) creates `src` first and then `src/main.rs`, so the nested case is never exercised. The native create dialog (editor.rs:1203) offers a free-form `relative/path.rs`, so typing `newdir/x.rs` fails with file.not_found. The symlink half also holds. `path.exists()` follows links, so a dangling link takes the canonicalize(path) branch and fails with not_found (Delete, Rename and Move pass may_not_exist=false). A link pointing outside the worktree canonicalizes outside the root and is refused as 'escapes the worktree', even though fs::rename would act on the link itself.
v1.correction: Restore only fails when the file's parent directory is itself gone, for example when a file is trashed and then its folder is trashed separately. Trashing a folder moves its children with it, so that case is narrower than the finding suggests. Agents mostly write through their own harness tools, so the main exposure is the Code-page create dialog and MCP file_write/file_create. Fix: walk up to the deepest existing ancestor, canonicalize it and check starts_with(root). Every remaining component is a plain Normal component, guaranteed by rel(). For Delete, Rename and Move, canonicalize only the parent and use symlink_metadata on the final component.

findings.title: file.write replaces a symlinked file with a regular file and leaks temp files on failure
findings.evidence: The temp file is written to `root/.relay/tmp/<uuid>.tmp` (L107-110) and then `fs::rename(&temp, &path)` (L115). rename replaces the directory entry, so when `path` is a symlink inside the worktree (which safe_join accepts) the link becomes a regular file and its target is not updated. Any error after L110 (set_permissions, rename, including EXDEV when the target directory is another mount) returns with `?` and leaves the temp file behind.
findings.impact: Saving a symlinked file in the editor (for example a doc that is a symlink to a shared file) silently breaks the link, leaves the real file stale and shows a typechange in git. Failed saves accumulate stray temp files.
findings.fix: Resolve the final symlink first (canonicalize when symlink_metadata says link). Create the temp next to the real target (tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent) then persist), and remove it on every error path.

v1.reason: When `path` is an existing symlink, safe_join(root, rel, true) canonicalizes it. The link is accepted only if its target is inside the root (file.rs:489-504), so only in-worktree links reach the write. The handler reads the target's content through the link, then runs fs::rename(&temp, &path) (file.rs:115). rename(2) replaces the link entry itself, so the link turns into a regular file and its target is never updated, which git reports as a typechange. Any failure after fs::write(&temp) (file.rs:110), whether set_permissions or rename, returns with `?` and leaves `<uuid>.tmp` behind in root/.relay/tmp. Nothing ever cleans that directory up. EXDEV needs a mount point inside the worktree, which is very rare.
v1.correction: Rare edge case (symlinked files edited through Relay) with no content lost, so low rather than medium. Fix: when symlink_metadata(path) reports a link, resolve it with canonicalize (already proven inside the root), write the temp file next to the resolved target and rename onto that. Remove the temp file on every error path.

findings.title: file.import does all of its copying and whole-file reads under the store lock, is not atomic, and cannot be replayed after a hold
findings.evidence: `e.register::<Import>` is locked. For each source, guard_path_mutation reads the source fully (L286, L578), then the recursive `copy(source, &dest)` (L293, L612-627) copies whole trees. Sources are processed one at a time, so an error, refusal or user-bypass hold on source N leaves sources 1..N-1 on disk while the transaction rolls back (or commits only the hold). Replaying a confirmed hold reruns the whole op, which then fails at `dest.exists()` (L287) for the files already copied. Nothing refuses a source directory that contains the destination, so that copy recurses into its own output until path limits.
findings.impact: Dragging a large folder in freezes every bus request for the length of the copy. Failed or held imports leave partial copies behind and cannot complete through confirmation.
findings.fix: Stage the op: check every destination and gate first, copy without the lock into a temp dir inside the worktree, then rename the results in. Refuse sources that are ancestors of the destination, and drop the content read for directory sources.

v1.reason: Import is registered locked (file.rs:265). It loops over the sources. For each, guard_path_mutation calls fs::read_to_string(source) (file.rs ~578), which reads a whole file into memory and fails cheaply on a directory. Then the recursive copy() (file.rs ~612-627) copies whole trees while the store mutex is held, which is the slow-work-under-lock pattern CLAUDE.md forbids. Sources are handled one at a time. A refusal, a hold or an IO error on source N leaves sources 1..N-1 on disk, and enforce's commit_error persists only the hold. guardrail.confirm replays the frozen request, which then fails with file.exists at the dest.exists() check for the files already copied. A source directory that contains `into` makes copy() recurse into its own output. Impact is far below the finding's claim: the op is UserOnly and nothing calls file.import (rg finds no reference in apps/relay-native, relay-remote or relay-cli). No drag-in UI exists, so 'dragging a large folder in freezes every bus request' is not a current flow.
v1.correction: Severity drops to low because the op has no caller in any client; only a manual `relay q file.import` reaches it. The 'drop the content read for directory sources' part is moot, since read_to_string on a directory errors immediately and yields an empty string. Fix as proposed (validate every destination and gate first, copy off the lock, refuse a source that is an ancestor of the destination), or remove the op until a client needs it.

findings.title: file.restore_head runs `git checkout` under the store lock without a timeout
findings.evidence: `crate::worktree::git_mutate(&root, &["checkout", "--", &p.path])` goes to worktree.rs:26-33 `Command::new("git")...output()`, with no proc::output_with_timeout, inside `e.register::<RestoreHead>`. A checkout runs smudge filters (LFS) and post-checkout hooks.
findings.impact: Breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every handler subprocess goes through output_with_timeout. A slow or hung filter or hook freezes the whole bus while the user restores one file.
findings.fix: Register it staged: run git in prepare through proc::output_with_timeout, and keep finish to the event emission.

v1.reason: RestoreHead is registered with e.register (file.rs:253), so it holds the store mutex and the transaction. It calls worktree::git_mutate, which is git(), which runs Command::new("git")...output() (worktree.rs:26-36) with no proc::output_with_timeout. That breaks the CLAUDE.md subprocess rule. `git checkout -- <path>` runs smudge filters, for example an LFS download when the object is not cached, and in the primary checkout it also runs the user's post-checkout hook. In session worktrees core.hooksPath points at Relay's directory, which holds only pre-commit. A hung filter therefore freezes the whole bus. Reachability is lower than the finding implies. The op is UserOnly, and rg finds no caller in apps/relay-native, relay-remote or relay-cli; it is reachable only through a generic `relay q file.restore_head`. The 'one-click answer' in BUS.md §9.3 is not wired to any UI.
v1.correction: Severity drops to low because no client flow calls this op today, so it is a latent invariant breach rather than a freeze in normal use. Fix: register it unlocked or staged, run git through proc::output_with_timeout with nothing held, and only emit file.changed under the lock. git_mutate itself has no timeout, so audit its other locked callers as well.

findings.title: project.remove/workspace.remove force-close sessions with their teardown subprocesses running under the held lock
findings.evidence: `ctx.invoke_registered("session.close", ...)` runs once per open session. invoke_registered runs a staged op's prepare with `held: Some(self.tx)` (engine.rs:325-351). session.close's prepare (session.rs:1547-1596) runs run_teardown, which is documented as "Subprocesses and file rewrites, so it runs with the store unlocked" (session.rs:350-362) and spawns git config calls with 10 s timeouts (hooks.rs:233-281). The comment at L320-326 claims the slow work is moved after the commit, but only worktree deletion is.
findings.impact: Removing a project with many live sessions holds the store for dozens of git invocations; a slow git holds it for up to 10 s per call. All of that time is felt by every other request.
findings.fix: Collect the teardown work and run it in after_commit like the worktree removal, or make project.remove itself staged and run the closes' external phases before opening the transaction.

v1.reason: ProjectRemove is registered with plain `e.register` (workspace.rs:300). With force it loops `ctx.invoke_registered("session.close", {remove_worktree:false})` (workspace.rs:327-329). invoke_registered (engine.rs:309-361) runs a staged op's prepare in place with `held: Some(self.tx)`, i.e. under the open transaction and store mutex. session.close's prepare (session.rs register_staged::<Close>) calls run_teardown, whose own doc says "Subprocesses and file rewrites, so it runs with the store unlocked" (session.rs ~350-352). run_teardown -> hooks::uninstall_git_any (hooks.rs:233-281) runs `git config --worktree --get core.hooksPath` and then a set or `--unset`, each bounded by GIT_TIMEOUT = 10 s (hooks.rs:581), plus uninstall_claude/codex file rewrites and remove_hook_dir. So every open session costs about 2 git spawns plus file I/O with the lock held. workspace.remove (workspace.rs:172-176) nests this across every project.
v1.correction: The comment at workspace.rs:320-326 does not actually claim the hook teardown is deferred. It defers only the PTY kills and the worktree deletion, and lists "hooks uninstalled" as one of the rules close keeps. The real cost is about 2 git invocations per open session, roughly 10-20 ms each normally and up to 10 s each if git hangs. That is noticeable but bounded, so medium is right for a rare, user-initiated op. Fix: make project.remove/workspace.remove staged and run each close's teardown in the external phase, or collect the (repo, worktree, Teardown) tuples and run them in after_commit next to the worktree removal. Out of scope for this finding but nearby in the same file: WsDiscover (workspace.rs:114) does a depth-4 directory walk, and ProjectClone (workspace.rs:233) runs `git clone` through Command::output with no timeout. Both are registered with plain `e.register` and so hold the store mutex, a larger instance of the same invariant breach.

findings.title: workspace.discover walks the filesystem while holding the store mutex although it never touches the store
findings.evidence: `e.register::<WsDiscover>(|_, p| {` ignores ctx, yet `register` holds the store lock for the whole handler. discover_repositories (L393-413) does read_dir up to four levels deep. The op is a query (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:12-13), and onboarding calls it with a user-chosen folder such as $HOME (onboarding.rs:336).
findings.impact: A tree walk under the global lock, which CLAUDE.md names explicitly. On a big home directory or a network mount, every agent and UI request stalls for the duration.
findings.fix: Change it to `register_unlocked`; nothing else needs to change.

v1.reason: workspace.rs:114 registers WsDiscover with `e.register::<WsDiscover>(|_, p| ...)`. Plain `register` runs the handler inside the store transaction with the mutex held (engine.rs register vs register_unlocked/register_staged). The handler never uses ctx. discover_repositories (~L393-413) recursively read_dirs up to depth 4 and stats `.git` in every directory. The op is OpMeta::query (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:12-13), so register_unlocked accepts it. Onboarding calls it on a user-typed or chosen folder (onboarding.rs:336) and re-runs it as the path changes. A big $HOME, or a network or FUSE mount, holds the global lock for the whole walk. CLAUDE.md names this case ("a tree walk") explicitly.
v1.correction: Fix: switch to `e.register_unlocked::<WsDiscover>(|_, p| ...)`. Nothing else is needed. A second bug in the same walk: `for entry in fs::read_dir(path)?` and `entry.file_type()?` propagate the first EACCES or ENOENT from any subdirectory. One unreadable directory under the chosen root (for example a root-owned docker or lost+found dir in $HOME) makes the whole discovery fail with workspace.discover_failed instead of skipping that entry. The walk should skip unreadable subdirectories and fail only on the root.

findings.title: awareness::brief runs git history walks while its callers hold the store connection
findings.evidence: brief() calls `crate::handlers::git::briefing_state(...)` (L211-215), which opens the repo with gix, runs upstream_metrics twice and divergence once (git.rs:1018-1058): up to six rev walks. Its callers hold the store: `e.register::<Brief>` (session.rs:1124-1129) and plan_launch inside `ctx.read(|conn| ...)` (session.rs:603-609), whose own doc says to keep that closure to plain queries (engine.rs:171-172).
findings.impact: Each spawn, resume and session.brief walks history under the global lock. On large repos with a far-behind base or upstream, every request waits on these walks.
findings.fix: Compute the git section outside the lock and pass it into brief() as a parameter; brief() should stay pure SQL.

v1.reason: awareness::brief (awareness.rs:211-215) calls git::briefing_state (git.rs:1018-1058). That function does gix::open on the worktree, then calls upstream_metrics for the branch and for the base, each of which may run divergence(): two rev_walks with a hidden set. A third divergence of branch vs base follows, so up to 6 history walks plus a FETCH_HEAD stat. This runs with the store held in two places. (1) `e.register::<Brief>` (session.rs:1124-1129) is a normal locked handler inside the transaction. (2) stage_launch (session.rs:603-609) runs plan_launch inside `ctx.read(|conn| ...)`, and plan_launch calls awareness::brief at session.rs:451. The doc on Unlocked::read (engine.rs:171-172) says to keep that closure to plain queries because it is back on the global lock. CLAUDE.md names tree walks as work that must not run under the mutex, and history walks are the same class. In typical linear histories with small divergence each walk takes milliseconds, so the usual cost is modest. But a base far behind its upstream, unrelated histories, or a large repo on slow disk puts the whole walk on the lock, during every spawn, resume and session.brief.
v1.correction: The lines are correct. Cost is usually small and grows with how far branch, base and upstream have diverged, so this is a latency spike rather than a constant freeze. Fix: compute briefing_state before taking the lock. For staged launches, call it in the unlocked phase from the session row's worktree, branch and base, then pass the string into brief(). For session.brief, register it with register_unlocked and do the git part outside ctx.read.

findings.title: Project/workspace ids are recycled while removal leaves id-keyed state that the next project or workspace inherits
findings.evidence: workspaces and projects use `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` without AUTOINCREMENT (store.rs:46-57), although the v2 comment cites D85: "a bare rowid recycles a deleted id" (store.rs:60-62). A SQLite run confirmed the max id is reused. WsRemove deletes only the workspaces row (L178) and never `guardrails.workspaces.{id}.*`, which guardrail::layers reads by id (guardrail.rs:107,129-131). ProjectRemove deletes exactly `layout.current.{id}` (L378-379), but settings are stored as flattened leaves (settings.rs:68-78) and the client writes `native.layout.current.{id}` (shell.rs:308). Open holds and audit rows keep the old id.
findings.impact: A newly added workspace silently inherits the removed one's guardrail layer, which may be looser. A new project inherits pending holds, layout state and audit/undo history that belong to a different repository.
findings.fix: Migrate both tables to AUTOINCREMENT (table rebuild). On workspace.remove, delete settings under `guardrails.workspaces.{id}`. On project.remove, delete `native.layout.current.{id}%` and resolve or delete open holds.

v1.reason: store.rs:46-57 declares workspaces and projects with `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` and no AUTOINCREMENT. The v2 comment (store.rs:60-62) states this lesson: "a bare rowid recycles a deleted id into the next insert". Without AUTOINCREMENT, SQLite assigns max(rowid)+1, so removing the newest workspace or project and then adding another reuses its id. WsRemove (workspace.rs ~L150-180) deletes only the workspaces row and never deletes settings under `guardrails.workspaces.{id}`. guardrail.config.set writes exactly that prefix for ConfigScope::Workspace (handlers/guardrail.rs:69). guardrail::layers (guardrail.rs:107-131) reads the workspace layer by id and merge_value()s it over the global layer, so it can loosen as well as tighten. A workspace added after removing the last one silently inherits a guardrail layer the user configured for a different directory. ProjectRemove deletes settings `path = 'layout.current.{id}'` exactly (workspace.rs:378-379). Settings are stored as flattened leaves (settings.rs flatten; tests/bus.rs:769/783 sets layout.current.7 and reads layout.current.7.page), so the exact match misses every leaf. The native client's key `native.layout.current.{id}` (shell.rs:308) is never deleted at all. Project-scoped guardrails ARE cleaned (`guardrails.projects.{id}.%`).
v1.correction: The holds and audit part is weak. Audit rows are kept on purpose (comment at workspace.rs ~L349). Open holds of the project's sessions are expired by session.close, which project.remove invokes for every open session. Only session-less holds could survive, and I did not establish that any exist. The real consequences are the workspace guardrail layer (main issue) and layout state carried over to an unrelated project (cosmetic). Trigger needs the removed workspace/project to have the highest id, which is common when a just-added wrong folder is removed and the right one added. Fix: in WsRemove, delete `guardrails.workspaces.{id}` and `guardrails.workspaces.{id}.%`. In ProjectRemove, use `path = 'layout.current.{id}' OR path LIKE 'layout.current.{id}.%' OR path LIKE 'native.layout.current.{id}%'`. Optionally migrate both tables to AUTOINCREMENT via a table-rebuild migration appended to MIGRATIONS.

findings.title: File/symbol overlap scans only run when an agent calls overlap.flag, so overlap.list is empty or stale in practice
findings.evidence: apply_scan is reached only from Flag (L455-482) and Scan (L531-545). `overlap.scan` has no caller outside tests and perf examples. Role instructions tell agents to declare files with session.claim (providers.rs:42), which inserts claims but writes no overlaps rows and triggers no scan (session.rs:1296-1306). The UI's "Shared file activity" list reads overlap.list (pages.rs:161-175). SPEC §15 describes a debounced overlap scan.
findings.impact: Two agents editing the same file or symbol are never flagged in normal use. Rows produced by an occasional flag stay `active=1` until the next flag, so the list can also be stale.
findings.fix: Trigger a debounced staged scan after file.changed or session.claim events, or have session.claim reuse the Flag scan.

v1.reason: Nothing schedules a scan. The only code that writes `overlaps` rows is apply_scan (overlap.rs ~L317-440). It is reached only from the overlap.flag finish (~L466-481) and the overlap.scan finish (~L531-545). rg finds no non-test caller of overlap.scan in relay-core, relay-native or relay-cli. Its own OpMeta reads "Force a scan now (tests / reconcile)" (relay-bus ops/overlap.rs:15), but no reconcile path exists. COMMON_INSTRUCTIONS in providers.rs tells agents to declare files with session.claim. That handler (session.rs ~L1294-1306) inserts claims and emits overlap.changed, but writes no overlaps row and triggers no scan. No file.changed or worktree watcher calls the scan. The native Guardrails page reads only overlap.list (pages.rs:161) for "Shared file activity". In normal use (agents editing files and using session.claim), two sessions changing the same file or symbol therefore never produce a File or Symbol overlap. SPEC §15 ("Overlap scan: linear per file, debounced") describes a scan that does not exist.
v1.correction: The staleness part is overstated. Closing a session deactivates every overlap row that names it (session.rs:251-255), and recovery.rs:169 does the same, so rows do not survive their sessions. They only go stale while both sessions stay open. The impact is partly reduced because session.claim still returns `collisions` for claim-vs-claim conflicts directly to the agent. What is missing is detection of actual edits and the UI view. Related UI bug: pages.rs:173 prints `text(&overlap, "note")`, but the Overlap type has no `note` field (overlap_row builds id/project_id/sessions/path/symbol/kind/acked_by/first_seen/last_seen), so the second line of every entry is always empty. Fix as proposed: run a debounced register_staged-style scan after commit on file.changed or session.claim, off the store lock (collect_changes already runs unlocked).

findings.title: Sessions sharing one worktree (PAIR/review) are scanned separately and reported as overlapping on every changed file
findings.evidence: scan_targets returns one (name, worktree) per live session (L284-295). PAIR sessions must share one worktree (session.rs:800), and review groups share a checkout (workspace.rs:325-326). apply_scan pairs every two names (L321-347), so identical change sets intersect completely. Claim-vs-change also flags a partner's claim against the shared checkout.
findings.impact: The overlap list fills with false collisions for every file and symbol a pair or group touches. Each shared checkout is also status-scanned and parsed once per member.
findings.fix: Group targets by worktree, scan each checkout once, and never pair sessions that share a worktree.

v1.reason: scan_targets (overlap.rs:284-295) returns one (name, worktree) row per non-closed session. A PAIR create is refused unless it reuses the partner's worktree (session.rs:800). D32 calls PAIR two identities over one checkout. Review groups put up to two builders and a reviewer on one worktree (session.rs:760-772, workspace.rs:325). collect_changes runs gix status and the tree-sitter parse once per session (L302-312), so members of a group get identical change sets. apply_scan pairs every two names (L321-347), so every changed file and symbol in a shared checkout becomes a File/Symbol overlap between partners. In the claim loop (L370-385), one partner's claim is matched against the other partner's identical file set, so each partner claim also yields a Claim overlap. Nothing filters same-worktree pairs, either here or in the overlap consumers. The result is a list full of false collisions on every scan or flag in projects that use PAIR or review groups, and the redundant status and parse work multiplies.
v1.correction: Fix: key collect_changes by worktree, scanning each checkout once. Carry worktree identity into apply_scan and skip any pair, for both change-vs-change and claim-vs-change, whose sessions share a worktree. Claim-vs-claim between partners can stay if wanted, since that one is explicit intent.

findings.title: Symbol overlaps key symbols by bare name, so same-named items in a file overwrite each other
findings.evidence: node_name returns a bare identifier (L180-195). impl_item has no `name` field, so the first type identifier is used, which is the trait for `impl Trait for X`. symbols() does `out.insert(name, hash_hex(bytes))` into a BTreeMap (L214), so every `fn new`, every `impl Display for ...` and so on share one key, and the last inserted (first in file) wins.
findings.impact: An edit to one same-named method can be masked by another's unchanged hash (false negative), and edits to different items with the same name are reported as one shared symbol (false positive). Symbol-level detection, the precision D28 promises, is unreliable.
findings.fix: Key symbols by a qualified path (enclosing symbol names plus kind), or append an ordinal for duplicates.

v1.reason: symbols() (overlap.rs:202-220) inserts `out.insert(name, hash_hex(bytes))` into a BTreeMap keyed only by node_name's bare identifier. In tree-sitter-rust 0.24.2, node-types.json shows that impl_item has fields body/trait/type/type_parameters and no `name`. node_name (L180-195) therefore falls back to the first identifier/type_identifier child. For `impl Display for Foo` that is `Display`, and for plain `impl Foo` it is `Foo`, which collides with `struct Foo`. For `impl<T> Foo<T>` it finds no identifier at all (the type is a generic_type), so the block is skipped. Every `fn new`/`fn fmt`/`fn default` in a file shares one key, and whichever node is popped last from the DFS stack wins. changed_symbols compares those single hashes. As a result, two agents editing different `new` methods are reported as a shared Symbol overlap (false positive), and an edit to a losing duplicate never registers as a changed symbol (false negative). File-level overlaps are still emitted for the same pair (L327-333), so collisions are not hidden entirely, but the symbol-level precision D28 offers is wrong in ordinary Rust files.
v1.correction: Mechanism detail: the false negative only affects symbol granularity, because the file-level finding is always recorded alongside it, and an edit inside an impl usually also changes the enclosing impl_item's hash. Fix: key symbols by a qualified path (enclosing impl/mod/class names plus kind, using the impl's `type` field and, where present, its `trait` field) rather than the bare identifier. Fall back to an ordinal suffix for remaining duplicates.

findings.title: Claim path normalization differs between overlap.flag and session.claim (and five validators exist), so equivalent claims never collide
findings.evidence: overlap.rs relative_path rejects any non-Normal component and does not trim (L82-96). session.rs claim_path trims, rejects only absolute paths and `..`, and stores `path.display()`, keeping `./` or `//` (session.rs:223-237). gix status reports `src/a.rs`, and apply_scan compares strings (`files.contains(path)`, `a.1 != b.1`). session.claim's own collision query uses `path=?2`. Separate validators also live in file.rs:470, git.rs:780 and guardrail.rs:1135.
findings.impact: A claim recorded as `./src/a.rs` never matches a peer's change or a claim on `src/a.rs`, so collisions go unreported. Each validator applies different rules (see the protected-path finding).
findings.fix: Write one normalize_relative(path) -> String (Normal components only, `/` separators, trimmed) and use it in all five places and when storing claims.

v1.reason: session.rs:223-237 claim_path trims and rejects only absolute paths and `..`, then stores `path.display()`, which keeps the caller's spelling (`./src/a.rs`, `src//a.rs`). overlap.rs:82-96 relative_path rejects every non-Normal component, so `./src/a.rs` is refused there, and it does not trim. Both paths write into the same `claims` table (session.rs:1298 and overlap.rs:470). Every comparison is an exact string match: session.claim's collision query uses `path=?2` (session.rs:1271), and apply_scan uses `files.contains(path)` against gix status locations, which come out as `src/a.rs`, plus `a.1 != b.1` between claims (overlap.rs:375, 389). So if an agent calls session.claim with `./src/a.rs`, that claim never collides with a peer's `src/a.rs` claim or with a peer's change to that file. Nothing upstream normalizes the path. The trigger needs an agent to spell the path unusually, and the cost is a missed advisory collision (claims are advisory under D116), so low.
v1.correction: The real bug is that claim paths are stored without normalization in session.claim/session.release (session.rs:223, used at 1263 and 1327) and that the two claim entry points apply different rules. The 'five validators' framing is overstated. file.rs:470 `rel`, git.rs:780 `validate_path` and guardrail.rs:1135 `relative_path` are near-identical guards that reject `..`/root/prefix before a filesystem join. They never key a string comparison, so normalizing them adds little. Fix: have claim_path keep only Normal components and join them with '/' (or reuse overlap::relative_path after a trim), so stored claims and overlap.flag agree. Folding the three FS guards into one helper is optional cleanup.

findings.title: Overlap rows are never pruned, and each scan rewrites every historical row under the lock
findings.evidence: `UPDATE overlaps SET active=0 WHERE project_id=?1` has no `AND active=1` (L424-428). New fingerprints, which include session names, are upserted (L429-437). Nothing deletes rows except project.remove (workspace.rs:368); session close and recovery only deactivate them (session.rs:251-252, recovery.rs:166-172).
findings.impact: The table grows with every new session pairing. Each flag or scan touches all rows and their `(project_id, active, last_seen)` index entries inside the transaction, so it gets slower over time.
findings.fix: Add `AND active=1` to the deactivate statement, and prune inactive rows older than N days in reconcile.

v1.reason: apply_scan runs `UPDATE overlaps SET active=0 WHERE project_id=?1` (overlap.rs:424-428) with no `AND active=1`, so every scan or flag rewrites every historical row of the project, including the `(project_id, active, last_seen)` index entries (store.rs:185). Fingerprints hash the session names (L267-276), so each new session pairing creates fresh rows. The only DELETE is in project.remove (workspace.rs:368). Session close (session.rs:249-252) and recovery (recovery.rs:166-172) only deactivate rows. D28 deliberately keeps inactive rows so that acks survive rescans. Rows whose sessions have all closed can never be reactivated, though, so they are pure accumulation.
v1.correction: Growth is real but slow. Rows appear only when an overlap or claim exists, and scans happen only on overlap.flag or overlap.scan, never on a timer. A long-lived project reaches perhaps thousands of rows, so the extra per-scan UPDATE costs milliseconds under the lock rather than anything user-visible. Low. Fix: add `AND active=1` to the deactivate statement, and in recovery/reconcile delete inactive rows that reference no live session, or are older than N days.

findings.title: The compact brief carries unbounded task bodies and notes into one Codex argv string
findings.evidence: state_public includes every assigned task's full body and changelog (L224-242). compact adds the standing note, the full adjacent-task list and peers' claims (L389-392). providers.rs:81-94 packs role text and the brief into a single `developer_instructions=<json>` argument (L220). Linux caps one argv string at 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN). The comment at L246-248 keeps the launch assignment out because argv is readable by other local users, yet task bodies and notes go in anyway.
findings.impact: A Codex spawn fails with E2BIG once assigned task text (pasted logs or specs) plus notes exceed about 128 KiB. Task and note text is also exposed in the process command line, which defeats the comment's stated intent.
findings.fix: Point Codex at the brief file already written to session_brief_path and keep argv to a short pointer, or cap each section and say where the full text is.

v1.reason: The compact brief (awareness.rs:385-388) is built from state_public. For every assigned non-done task that includes the full title, body and changelog (L232-238), plus standing notes, the full adjacent-task list, the peer table with claims, and plugin sections. No size cap exists: task create and update (task.rs:740, 887) and the changelog write store body and changelog unbounded. Only Codex consumes it in argv. Codex::args (providers.rs:213-228) puts codex_developer_instructions (providers.rs:81-94) into a single `--config developer_instructions=<json>` argument on both fresh and resume launches. prepare_launch (session.rs:527-540) passes `Some(&brief_compact)`. Claude's driver ignores the brief (providers.rs:172). Linux caps one argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (32 pages, 128 KiB), and JSON escaping inflates text further. A Codex session with several queued tasks carrying pasted logs or specs, or a long changelog that agents keep appending to, will fail exec with E2BIG on every start and resume. The privacy point also stands. The comments at awareness.rs:246-248 and session.rs:515-516 keep the launch assignment out of argv because `ps` shows it to other local users, yet task bodies, changelogs, notes and peer claims go into the same argv. Without hidepid, /proc/<pid>/cmdline is readable by any local user for the life of the Codex process.
v1.correction: This affects Codex only. The overflow needs about 128 KiB of brief text, so it is uncommon. But it is a hard, repeatable launch failure once reached, and the exposure applies to every Codex session. Fix: keep argv to role instructions plus a pointer to the brief file prepare_launch already writes (session_brief_path / $RELAY_BRIEF) or the role-instructions file, or use a Codex config option that reads instructions from a file. At least drop task bodies, changelogs and notes from the argv copy, and cap the remainder.

findings.title: file.tree/read/search register a recursive watcher per root that is never released
findings.evidence: Tree, Read and Search call `crate::watch::ensure_after_commit(ctx, root.clone(), project.id)` (L21, L41, L301) for whatever root the caller named, including every agent worktree. ensure() creates a RecursiveMode::Recursive notify watcher, which has its own thread and one inotify watch per subdirectory including target/ and node_modules, and inserts it into engine.watchers (watch.rs:132-140). No code ever removes entries from that map.
findings.impact: Watcher threads and inotify watches pile up for the engine's lifetime, one set per worktree ever browsed or read. They can exhaust the user's inotify watch limit, after which new watchers fail silently and the Code page stops refreshing.
findings.fix: Drop the watcher when a session closes, a worktree is removed or a project is removed. Optionally bound the map with an LRU.

v1.reason: file.tree, file.read and file.search are all register_unlocked handlers (file.rs:19-21, 39-41, 299-301).
