They call watch::ensure_after_commit for whatever worktree the caller names. ensure (watch.rs:76-151) creates a notify RecommendedWatcher and watches it with RecursiveMode::Recursive. On Linux that is a separate inotify instance and event thread per watcher, with one watch per subdirectory; is_generated_path filters target/ and node_modules events only after they arrive, so those directories are still watched. The watcher is then inserted into engine.watchers (watch.rs:134-139). A search for `watchers` finds only the field (engine.rs:420), its init (engine.rs:457) and the inserts and contains_key checks in watch.rs. Nothing ever removes an entry: not on session close, not on worktree removal, not on project removal. Each worktree that is browsed, read or searched keeps an inotify instance and a thread until the engine exits. Agent sessions each have their own worktree and the Code page browses them, so the count grows in normal use. The tighter limit is usually fs.inotify.max_user_instances (often 128, shared with the user's IDEs and other tools) rather than watch count. Once it is reached, recommended_watcher fails, ensure silently registers nothing (watch.rs:132-145), and Code-page refresh stops for new worktrees. For a deleted worktree the kernel drops its watches but the instance and thread stay.
v1.correction: The resource that runs out first is the per-user inotify instance count (one per watcher), not just the watch count. Fix: remove the map entry when a worktree is removed or its session closes, and when a project is removed (worktree and session teardown paths). Optionally cap the map with LRU eviction.

findings.title: Every file.write audit row stores the whole file text (up to 64 KB) for 180 days
findings.evidence: file.write is a mutation audited Always (relay-bus ops/file.rs:14-15, engine.rs:1394-1398). audit::append stores the full payload JSON whenever it is ≤ STORE_LIMIT (64 KB) (audit.rs:14, 22-27, 88-93), and that payload includes `text`. Retention defaults to 180 days (settings.rs:43), and backups copy the store.
findings.impact: Each editor save and each agent write appends the file's contents to store.db. That grows the single locked database (hundreds of MB at steady state with frequent saves) and keeps edited content, including secrets, in plain text in the store and its backups.
findings.fix: Audit file.write/create with a hash and byte count instead of `text` (an op-specific limit like CHATTY_STORE_LIMIT, or redact the field).

v1.reason: file.write is OpMeta::mutation, which defaults to Audit::Always (relay-bus/src/registry.rs:114-117), so every call is audited. audit::append keeps the full payload JSON, `text` included, whenever it is at most store_limit(op), and store_limit returns STORE_LIMIT = 64 KB for every op except session.report and usage.report (audit.rs:14, 22-27, 88-93). Launch recovery prunes rows only after audit.retention_days, default 180 (recovery.rs:182-200). file.write has no undo, so the stored text is not needed to reverse anything. The finding overstates the impact, though. The editor calls file.write only on an explicit save, with no autosave (editor.rs:677-704). Agents reach file.write only through bus_writes and normally edit files with their own tools. A file over 64 KB is replaced by a truncation marker. The 'hundreds of MB' figure is a guess. The point about secrets is weak: the same text already sits in plain text in the worktree, and the store is local to the user.
v1.correction: Calling this a design oversight is fair: CHATTY_STORE_LIMIT already exists for exactly this problem and could cover file.write and file.create. Alternatively, store a hash and byte count in place of `text`. Expected growth is about (saves per day) x (file size) over 180 days, which is a few tens of MB for a typical user. That makes this low, not medium.

findings.title: restore_head restores from the index rather than HEAD, treats the name as a pathspec, and validates after git runs
findings.evidence: `git checkout -- <path>` copies the index version, so a staged change survives "restore head". The argument is a pathspec: glob characters in real file names (e.g. `[id].tsx` routes), `.` (allowed by rel()) and pathspec magic widen the revert. safe_join is called at L258, after git has already run.
findings.impact: The one-click answer to a guardrail.violation leaves a staged destructive change in place. A file name containing glob characters can also revert uncommitted work in sibling files.
findings.fix: Run `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- :(literal)<normalized path>` after safe_join, and refuse `.` or empty paths.

v1.reason: `git checkout -- <path>` (file.rs:256) copies from the index, not HEAD. A change the agent already staged survives an op named restore_head that BUS.md describes as the restore for a post-hoc violation. p.path goes to git raw as a pathspec. Arguments after `--` still get pathspec magic and glob matching, so `[id].tsx` also matches `i.tsx` and `d.tsx`. rel(".") is accepted, because Component::CurDir is not rejected, and `git checkout -- .` reverts every unstaged change in the worktree. safe_join runs only after git (file.rs:258). That ordering matters little, because git itself refuses paths beyond a symlink. All of this is limited by the op being UserOnly and having no UI caller (rg: no client references), so only a user typing `relay q` reaches it.
v1.correction: The symlink and ordering point is cosmetic, since git rejects paths beyond a symlink. The real issues are the source (index instead of HEAD) and the pathspec interpretation, including `.`. Fix: validate with safe_join first, reject empty and `.`, and run `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- :(literal)<path>` through proc::output_with_timeout off the lock.

findings.title: assigned_tasks ignores per-participant completion and labels every non-active task "IN REVIEW"
findings.evidence: The query filters only `t.col!='done'` (L30-35), with no `ts.completed_at IS NULL`, whereas next_queued_task requires `t.col='active' AND ts.completed_at IS NULL` (session.rs:28-43). queue_state (L225-231) labels anything that is neither current nor active as "IN REVIEW", including backlog and ready tasks. task_sessions rows are not removed when a user moves a task back.
findings.impact: A group builder that already reported done still sees the task as CURRENT/QUEUED on resume and may redo it. Deprioritized tasks are announced to agents as in review.
findings.fix: Exclude or explicitly mark completed assignments, and label from the actual column.

v1.reason: Only the labelling half holds up. In awareness.rs:225-231, queue_state is CURRENT when the task is session.task_id, QUEUED when col=='active', and "IN REVIEW" for everything else. assigned_tasks (L28-36) filters only `t.col!='done'`, so it also returns backlog and ready tasks. task.move (task.rs:903) changes only `tasks.col`. Nothing outside workspace removal (workspace.rs:359) deletes task_sessions rows. So when a user moves an assigned task back to backlog or ready, the brief announces it as "Task #n [IN REVIEW]". The impact is small because the next line of the brief prints the real `column: backlog`. The "redo" half is wrong. When a builder in a group calls session.done, complete_group_assignment (session.rs:96-99) sets completed_at and returns while other builders are still working. sessions.task_id and the task's 'active' column are left unchanged on purpose, so CURRENT is the accurate state until the group advances. Once it advances, the task becomes in_review (shown correctly) and task_id moves on. No path shows a finished, already-advanced task as CURRENT or QUEUED.
v1.correction: Narrow this to the label. Derive queue_state from the column ("IN REVIEW" only for in_review; otherwise something like "BACKLOG"/"READY" or "PARKED"). If you want the brief to say so, also note `ts.completed_at IS NOT NULL` as "done, waiting for group". Drop the claim that agents redo finished work: a builder whose task_id still points at the task has not been advanced, and CURRENT is correct for it.

findings.title: One unreadable peer worktree aborts the whole overlap scan, so overlap.flag fails
findings.evidence: `let files = changed_files(path)?;` in collect_changes. changed_files maps any gix open or status error to an internal error (L99-110). Only a missing directory is skipped (L305).
findings.impact: A half-removed, pruned or permission-broken checkout of any session makes every overlap.flag and overlap.scan in the project fail, so no agent can flag.
findings.fix: Log and skip a checkout that fails to open or scan, and continue with the rest.

v1.reason: collect_changes (overlap.rs:302-312) skips only `!path.is_dir()` and then does `let files = changed_files(path)?;`. changed_files maps every gix error to an internal error: open, status, into_iter and each item (L99-110). Both overlap.flag (prepare at L457-463) and overlap.scan (L516-519) run collect_changes before anything else. A single live session whose directory exists but cannot be opened or walked therefore fails the whole op for every agent in the project. Examples: its `.git` gitdir file points at a pruned admin dir, a permission error, or a status item error while an agent is rewriting files. The claim that overlap.flag would have recorded is not written either. In contrast, changed_symbols already degrades gracefully with `let Ok(repo) = gix::open(..) else { return .. }`.
v1.correction: Reaching it needs a broken checkout behind a still-open session, or a transient status error, so low is right. Fix: on a changed_files error, log a warning and skip that session (or record it as unscanned), then continue.

findings.title: file.restore writes without any guardrail check and trusts the stored root
findings.evidence: Restore (L238-252) takes root from the file_trash row (L245), never calls root_verify or guardrail::enforce, and renames the payload into place (L248). Every other file mutation calls guardrail::enforce, either directly or through guard_path_mutation.
findings.impact: A bus_writes session can put back any trashed file, including one at a protected path and in a checkout that is not its own (for example something the user deleted from the primary checkout).
findings.fix: Re-verify the root, and run guardrail::enforce (protected path plus ownership) for the restored path.

v1.reason: Restore (file.rs:238-252) reads root, original_path and trash_path from the file_trash row. It does safe_join and an exists check, then fs::rename, with no guardrail::enforce. Every other file.* mutation calls enforce, directly or through guard_path_mutation. file.restore is not UserOnly (relay-bus ops/file.rs:30), and agents with bus_writes are admitted to every `file.*` op (guardrail.rs:363-366). The MCP tool list exposes file_restore. Scenario: the user deletes a file at a protected path after confirming the hold; an agent with bus_writes calls file.restore with that trash_id and puts it back, which file.write would refuse with guardrail.protected_path. The impact is small. The agent can only restore content that already existed, it needs the bus_writes opt-in, and the trash ids are sequential and scoped to the project.
v1.correction: The claim that it can restore into 'a checkout that is not its own' is not a separate hole. Under D111 every file.* op already accepts any worktree of the project, including `worktree: "@project"`. root_verify only checks that the path is a worktree of this project, and no op checks which session owns a worktree. The real gap is the missing protected-path and shape-gate check on the restored path. Fix: run guardrail::enforce(GateKind::Write, original_path, content of the payload) before the rename. Optionally re-run root_verify on the stored root.

findings.title: `.relay/` is only git-excluded once an agent worktree exists, but file ops create it in the project root earlier
findings.evidence: worktree::ensure_excluded is called only from worktree::create (worktree.rs:199). project.add (workspace.rs:183-227) does not call it. file.delete creates `<root>/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` (L230-232) and file.write creates `<root>/.relay/tmp` (L107).
findings.impact: In a newly added project, a file deleted from the Code page shows up as an untracked `.relay/trash/...` file, and a `git add -A` commits the content the user meant to delete.
findings.fix: Call worktree::ensure_excluded in project.add, or before the first `.relay` write in file ops.

v1.reason: worktree::ensure_excluded (worktree.rs:39) has one production caller, worktree::create (worktree.rs:199). ProjectAdd (workspace.rs:183-227) never calls it. Skills only add their own folder entries through exclude_paths (skills.rs:249). A user's file op with no session resolves to the project root (default_worktree_in returns `repo` when session_id is None, file.rs ~402). file.delete then renames the file to `<root>/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` (file.rs:230-232). Until the first agent worktree is created, nothing excludes that path. status_files runs `git status --untracked-files=all` (worktree.rs:86-96), so the deleted content shows up as untracked in Relay's own git view, makes is_dirty true, and a `git add -A` or stage-all commits it. file.write's `.relay/tmp` stays empty after the rename, so git does not list it. Only the trash payload is visible.
v1.correction: Only file.delete leaves visible content; file.write's `.relay/tmp` is an empty directory, which git never shows. The window lasts from project.add until the first worktree::create, which in normal agent use comes soon. Fix: call ensure_excluded in project.add after commit, or before the first `.relay` write in file ops.

findings.title: Three hard-coded skip lists have diverged: the tree hides build/dist dirs that search descends into
findings.evidence: list_dir filters with watch::is_generated_path, which hides build, dist, coverage, Saved, Binaries, Intermediate, .next and others by name at any depth (L519; watch.rs:158-188). Search's skip_dir has only `.git .relay node_modules target` (L629-636). discover_repositories has its own list (workspace.rs:404).
findings.impact: Tracked source under a directory named build/ or dist/ (e.g. a committed dist/ in a JS action) is invisible in the tree, yet search reads and returns hits from such directories, including large generated ones.
findings.fix: Use one shared predicate, preferably based on git-ignore status (the tree already fetches status badges).

v1.reason: list_dir (file.rs:516-520) filters entries with watch::is_generated_path. That function (watch.rs:158-188) was written to decide which watcher events to ignore. It hides any component named build, dist, coverage, .next, .svelte-kit, .gradle, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache or Binaries, at any depth. Search's skip_dir (file.rs:629-636) skips only .git, .relay, node_modules and target. discover_repositories (workspace.rs:404) has a third list. Result: tracked source under a directory named `build/` or `dist/` cannot be seen or opened from the tree, while file.search reads it and returns hits there. Search also walks into Unreal Intermediate, Saved and DerivedDataCache, reading every file in full, which is large in exactly the Unreal projects this app targets. Search is register_unlocked, so this is wasted work for the caller only and does not stall the bus.
v1.correction: The user-visible part is a behaviour bug: tracked files are hidden in the tree. It comes from reusing a watcher-noise filter as a tree filter. The fix is one shared 'generated directory' predicate used by tree, search and discover. Ideally the tree should show git-tracked paths even when their names match the list.

findings.title: discover_repositories aborts the whole discovery on the first unreadable directory
findings.evidence: `for entry in fs::read_dir(path)? {` and `entry.file_type()?` propagate the first EACCES, and L410 maps it to workspace.discover_failed.
findings.impact: A workspace folder containing one root-owned directory (a container volume, lost+found) returns no repositories at all during onboarding.
findings.fix: Skip directories that cannot be read, with a debug log, and continue the walk.

v1.reason: In discover_repositories::walk (workspace.rs:393-413), `fs::read_dir(path)?`, `entry?` and `entry.file_type()?` propagate the first io error, and workspace.rs:410 maps it to BusError::unavailable("workspace.discover_failed"). The only caller is WsDiscover (workspace.rs:130), so a single unreadable subdirectory at depth < 4 (for example a root-owned docker volume or a mode-700 dir owned by another user) makes the whole discovery return an error instead of the readable repos. The top-level path itself is checked with is_dir but not for readability.
v1.correction: Skip unreadable entries (log at debug) and continue. Only the root read_dir failing should be an error. Separately, WsDiscover is registered with plain `e.register` (workspace.rs:114) although it walks a tree up to depth 4. It should be `register_unlocked`, since it does not touch the store. That is a distinct, more serious invariant finding.

findings.title: overlap.flag returns and emits the first claim row for the path, ignoring the symbol
findings.evidence: `.find(|overlap| overlap.kind == OverlapKind::Claim && overlap.path == path && overlap.sessions.contains(&own.session.name))` does not compare symbols, and list() orders by path then symbol, NULL first (L52-53).
findings.impact: Flagging `a.rs#foo` while already holding `a.rs` (or `a.rs#bar`) returns and broadcasts the other claim, so the agent misreads what it holds.
findings.fix: Also match `overlap.symbol == (!symbol.is_empty()).then(...)`, preferring the own-claim row.

v1.reason: In the overlap.flag finish (overlap.rs ~L476), the result is `overlaps.into_iter().find(|o| o.kind == Claim && o.path == path && o.sessions.contains(&own.session.name))`, and the symbol is never compared. list() orders by `path, symbol, kind, id`, and SQLite sorts NULL first. Take a session that holds claim (a.rs, "") and then flags (a.rs, "foo"). apply_scan writes own rows {[me], a.rs, None} and {[me], a.rs, Some(foo)}, and find() returns the None row. If a peer holds a conflicting claim on a.rs, the pair row [me, peer] can also come first, depending on id order. The wrong row is both returned to the agent and broadcast in overlap.changed.
v1.correction: The fix should also match `o.symbol.as_deref() == (!symbol.is_empty()).then_some(symbol.as_str())`. Among the matches, prefer the row whose sessions == [own name], so the agent gets its own claim rather than a pair row. Impact is cosmetic or misleading only: the claims table itself is written correctly.

findings.title: file.read truncation can split a UTF-8 character, which turns a text file into base64
findings.evidence: The bytes are cut to exactly `limit` (L54-55), and then `String::from_utf8(bytes.clone())` (L57) fails if the cut falls inside a multi-byte character, so the whole result is returned as `bytes_b64`. The clone also copies up to 32 MiB.
findings.impact: Agents reading large non-ASCII text files with max_bytes get base64 they cannot use, and every read does a needless allocation.
findings.fix: When truncated, back off to `Utf8Error::valid_up_to()` if `error_len()` is None. Use from_utf8(bytes) and recover the buffer with into_bytes() on error.

v1.reason: The Read handler (file.rs:47-62) reads limit+1 bytes, then `bytes.truncate(limit as usize)` cuts at an arbitrary byte. `String::from_utf8(bytes.clone())` then fails whenever the cut lands inside a multi-byte character, and the whole result goes to the base64 branch with text=None. max_bytes is caller-controlled (relay-bus ops/file.rs:9) and the default cap is 4 MiB. An agent reading a non-ASCII text file with a small max_bytes gets base64 back at random, depending on where the cut falls. This codebase's own docs, full of em dashes, would trigger it. The clone is a real but minor extra copy of up to 32 MiB.
v1.correction: When truncated and the error's error_len() is None (an incomplete trailing sequence), truncate to utf8_error().valid_up_to() and keep the text. Use String::from_utf8(bytes) and recover the buffer with FromUtf8Error::into_bytes() to avoid the clone.

findings.title: file.tree fails entirely when one entry vanishes between read_dir and stat
findings.evidence: `.map(|e| entry(root, &e.path(), ...)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?` together with entry's `fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(...)?` (L533).
findings.impact: While agents create and delete temp files, the Code page's tree refresh (rerun on every invalidation) fails intermittently with file.stat_failed.
findings.fix: Skip entries whose stat returns NotFound.

v1.reason: list_dir (file.rs:513-522) uses `.flatten()`, which drops iteration errors from read_dir, but then `.map(|e| entry(..)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?`. entry() calls `fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(..)?` (L533) and recurses into list_dir for subdirectories (L546), whose `fs::read_dir(dir).map_err(..)?` (L514) also propagates. When an entry is removed between read_dir and the stat, or when a nested directory vanishes before it is read, the whole file.tree request fails. The tree is unlocked, so nothing else is blocked; the refresh simply errors.
v1.correction: There is also a deterministic trigger besides the race: a subdirectory that cannot be read (for example a root-owned directory created by a Docker bind mount) fails read_dir with EACCES. Any file.tree with depth > 1 then errors permanently, not intermittently. Fix: skip entries whose stat fails with NotFound, and for unreadable subdirectories return the directory entry with children: None instead of failing the whole tree.

findings.title: file.search glob uses the guardrail matcher, so `*.rs` matches only root-level files
findings.evidence: `crate::guardrail::path_matches(glob, relp)`: in that matcher `*` stays within one path segment (guardrail.rs:1158-1160).
findings.impact: Agents passing ripgrep-style globs get silently incomplete results with no error.
findings.fix: Match the basename when the glob contains no `/`, or use globset with ripgrep semantics.

v1.reason: file.rs:329-333 filters with `crate::guardrail::path_matches(glob, relp)`, where relp is the worktree-relative path. path_matches (guardrail.rs:1161-1168) first tries exact equality or directory prefix, then glob_match. In glob_match a single `*` may not consume `/` (guardrail.rs:1180-1181 for a trailing star, 1195-1196 on retry). So `*.rs` against `src/main.rs` returns false, and only top-level .rs files match. SearchIn.glob (relay-bus ops/file.rs:38) has no documented semantics, and nothing reports an error. A caller using ripgrep or gitignore conventions silently gets incomplete hits.
v1.correction: Workaround: `**/*.rs` matches files at depth. A pattern with no `/` also matches a whole directory subtree through the prefix rule (`src` matches everything under src/), which ripgrep's glob does not do. Fix: when the glob has no `/`, match it against the basename, and document the semantics in the op schema.

findings.title: Stale comments say root verification spawns `git worktree list`; BUS.md describes the old worktree default; root resolution is duplicated in git.rs
findings.evidence: file.rs:389-390, 425-426 and 457, and git.rs:767, all say verification runs a `git worktree list` subprocess and must stay off the lock. worktree::contains now just reads the `.git` pointer (worktree.rs:157-171), and locked handlers call root() anyway. BUS.md §10.13 says `worktree` defaults to the primary checkout, which D111 changed for agents. root/root_unlocked are duplicated as git.rs resolve_root/resolve_root_unlocked (git.rs:751-778), differing only in the error code.
findings.impact: Readers are misled about which calls are slow and about agents' default tree. There are two copies of the resolution logic to keep in step.
findings.fix: Update the comments and §10.13, and use one helper parameterized by the error code.

v1.reason: The comments on default_worktree_in (file.rs:388-389), root_verify (L430-431) and root_unlocked (L455), and on git.rs resolve_root_unlocked (git.rs:766-767), all say verification runs a `git worktree list` subprocess. worktree::contains (worktree.rs:157-171) now reads the `.git` pointer file and does no subprocess, and its own doc comment says so. BUS.md §10.13 says '`worktree` defaults to the project's primary checkout'. D111 (DECISIONS.md:523-529) and default_worktree_in (L401-407) default an agent to its own worktree. The BUS.md drift matters because BUS.md is the contract agents and tool descriptions are written against.
v1.correction: The duplication part is overstated. git.rs resolve_root and resolve_root_unlocked are 8-line wrappers that already call file::root_choice and file::root_verify, differing only in the error code. That is negligible and not a second copy of the logic. The real fix is to update the comments and BUS.md §10.13; folding the wrappers is optional.

results.coverage:
I read every line of hooks.rs, skills.rs, plugins.rs, watch.rs and branch_cleanup.rs. To trace callers and context I read: handlers/session.rs (launch/create/close/teardown, roughly lines 300-660, 760-960 and 1540-1640), handlers/git.rs (commit, pr.list, branch.cleanup, clean_merged), handlers/provider.rs (skill and plugin handlers), handlers/file.rs (watcher triggers, list_dir), recovery.rs (hook sweep), serve.rs, engine.rs (Unlocked/Ctx/register* and the watchers map), socket.rs (per-connection dispatch), worktree.rs (create/remove/status/exclude), github.rs (skill staging), usage.rs, sessions.rs (new_name), and relay-cli main.rs, blender.rs and unreal.rs (hook adapters and the python tools). From the native client I read only the call sites that bear on these findings: code_git.rs, shell.rs, agent_menu.rs, client.rs, tools_skills.rs and app.rs. I also read the notify 8.2 inotify backend in ~/.cargo/registry and the D147/D153/D159/D160 entries in DECISIONS.md and §9.3 in BUS.md.

Throwaway experiments, all in the scratchpad: git `--git-path hooks` versus worktree/repo-level core.hooksPath, a dangling hooksPath skipping all hooks, `git config` rewriting the config file and failing on config.lock, the restored explicit hooksPath shadowing a later repo-level one, and SQLite AUTOINCREMENT id reuse after a rollback. I also did read-only listings of ~/.claude/skills, ~/.codex/skills and this worktree's .claude/skills, plus directory counts for the primary checkout.

Not verified by execution, per the rules (no cargo, no app, no mcp__relay__): Claude Code treating exit 127 and hook timeouts as non-blocking (taken from its documented hook semantics); Codex hook trust and failure semantics; whether the native Code view hides .relay entries in its change list (it does not matter for `git add -A`). Severity of the inotify-limit consequences depends on the distro's sysctl defaults; this machine has max_user_watches=524288 and max_user_instances=1024. I ran no tests. Pedantic clippy output for these files contained only one cast (plugins.rs:246, a usize→u32 skill file count), which is harmless.

findings.title: Plugin MCP tools that execute arbitrary Python (blender_python, ue_python, ue_console, ue_call) are wired into agents but never reach a guardrail gate
findings.evidence: The only PreToolUse gate Relay installs for Claude is `"matcher": "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash"` (hooks.rs:350); Codex gets `"Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write"` (hooks.rs:517). `add_claude_mcp_servers` (hooks.rs:417-443) writes every enabled plugin's MCP server into `.relay/relay.mcp.json`, and Codex gets them through `codex_mcp_config` (session.rs:546-548). The bundled manifests expose `blender_python` and `ue_python`, `ue_console` and `ue_call`. `blender_python` runs the caller's `code` through `run(PY_RUN, ...)` in a Blender process (relay-cli/src/blender.rs:197-206). `ue_python` runs `python(code, ...)` in the editor (relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:340-343). Neither calls `guardrail.gate`. Their tool names (`mcp__blender__blender_python`, `mcp__unreal__ue_python`) match none of the matcher's alternatives, so `claude_pre_tool` (which fails closed on unknown tools, main.rs:462) never runs for them.
findings.impact: With the Blender or Unreal plugin on, an agent can run `import subprocess; subprocess.run([...])` through blender_python or ue_python. That covers anything the command deny list refuses for Bash (for example `rm -rf`), writes to protected paths, and rewrites past the caps, with no hold, no refusal and no Relay audit row. This defeats the enforcement doors described in BUS.md §9.3 for plugin projects.
findings.fix: Extend the PreToolUse matcher to `mcp__.*`, or at least to the plugin servers' code-executing tools, and teach `claude_pre_tool`/`codex_pre_tool` to map them to `kind: "exec"`, with the code (or console command) as the command text. The CLI already fails closed on tools it does not know. Alternatively, have `relay blender-mcp`/`unreal-mcp` call `guardrail.gate` with the session's identity before executing code.

v1.reason: The Claude PreToolUse matcher is exactly `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash` (hooks.rs:350), and the Codex matcher is `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write` (hooks.rs:517). Plugin MCP servers are merged into relay.mcp.json (add_claude_mcp_servers, 417-443) and into the Codex config overrides. The plugin manifests expose blender_python, ue_python, ue_call and ue_console. blender.rs `call` runs `run(PY_RUN, ...)` on agent-supplied code, and unreal.rs runs `python(code, ...)`. rg finds no `guardrail` reference in either file, so these arbitrary-code tools never reach guardrail.gate and leave no audit row. An agent that is refused a protected-path write or a denied command through Edit or Bash can do the same thing through ue_python or blender_python.
v1.correction: Calibrate down to medium. BUS.md principle 6 says guardrails are 'seatbelts, not sandboxes' (they stop mistakes, not hostile agents), and the exec gate is already a shell-word pattern match that `python3 -c ...` through Bash also gets past. Claude is launched without a permission-skip flag (providers.rs:172-191), so Claude Code's own permission prompt still applies to MCP tools unless the user has allowed them. The real gap is that a plugin project's code-execution and asset-writing tools sit entirely outside Relay's gate and audit trail, which matters most for protected paths and write caps that an agent can route around once it has been refused. The fix as proposed (match `mcp__.*` and map the code tools to exec/write kinds, or have the plugin MCP servers call guardrail.gate) is reasonable.

findings.title: remove_hook_dir deletes the hook directory a shared checkout's core.hooksPath still points at, silently disabling the commit gate and the user's own pre-commit hook
findings.evidence: The doc comment says "a hook directory that is still wired into a live worktree is left alone by [`uninstall_git`] before this runs", but nothing checks that. In `session.close`, `let teardown = if others == 0 { Some(read_teardown(..)) } else { None };` (session.rs:1559) skips the uninstall whenever another live session shares the worktree. It then unconditionally calls `crate::hooks::remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name)` (session.rs:1596). In a shared checkout (a PAIR, or the primary checkout that D160 gives every agent of an Unreal project), `core.hooksPath` is the directory of whichever session installed last. Verified in a scratch repo: with `core.hooksPath` pointing at a deleted directory, `git commit` runs no pre-commit hook and succeeds.
findings.impact: The trigger is closing the last-launched session of a shared checkout with remove_worktree:false. That is what the shell's "Discard session" sends, and the only option allowed while a partner is live. Afterwards every remaining agent's shell `git commit` in that checkout is ungated, and the user's chained pre-commit hook (husky, lint) stops running there too, until some session relaunches. The fsck `sweep_hook_dirs` (recovery.rs:138, live = open sessions only) and the refused-create path (session.rs:906, which restores the pre-Relay path past other live sessions) un-wire live checkouts the same way.
findings.fix: Before deleting a session's hook directory, read `core.hooksPath` of its worktree. If it still points at that directory and other sessions are live, first re-run `install_git` for a live session of that worktree, which re-records the same pre-Relay path. Make `sweep_hook_dirs` skip directories referenced by any worktree's `core.hooksPath`, and make the refused-create rollback hand ownership to a live session instead of restoring the pre-Relay path.

v1.reason: `install_git` (hooks.rs:68-155) always points `core.hooksPath --worktree` at `.relay/hooks/<this session>`, and it runs on every launch (session.rs:481). In a shared checkout (a PAIR, or a D160 primary checkout for Unreal-plugin projects), the hook path therefore belongs to whichever session launched last. In session.close, `teardown` is `None` whenever `others > 0` (session.rs:1559), so `uninstall_git_any` is skipped. Even so, `remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name)` runs unconditionally (session.rs:1596). The doc comment on remove_hook_dir (hooks.rs:283-284) claims a protection that does not exist. Once the directory is gone, git finds no pre-commit at the configured path and commits with no hook. That removes both the Relay commit gate and the chained user hook (husky, lint) for every remaining agent's shell commit, and for the user's own commits in the primary checkout. Nothing fixes this until some session of that worktree launches again. The refused-create rollback (session.rs:898-911) restores the pre-Relay path even when other live sessions share the checkout: it only checks `pair_with.is_none()`, and a D160 primary-checkout create has no pair_with.
v1.correction: The commit gate was never a hard boundary, since an agent can run `git commit --no-verify`. The concrete harm is that a normal multi-agent Unreal flow silently disables the gate and the user's own pre-commit hook. The sweep_hook_dirs part (recovery.rs:138) only matters after one of the two paths above has already left a dangling reference, so it is secondary. Fix: before removing a session's hook directory, check whether the worktree's core.hooksPath points at it. If it does and other sessions are live, run `install_git` again for one live session, which chains to the same recorded previous path. Apply the same handover in the create rollback.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what is claimed. `install_git` runs on every create (session.rs:892) and every launch (session.rs:481). Each time, it points the worktree's `core.hooksPath` at `.relay/hooks/<that session>` (hooks.rs:150-154). In a shared checkout, the active directory therefore belongs to whichever session was created or launched last.
- In `session.close`, `teardown` is `None` whenever `others > 0` (session.rs:1559), so no uninstall runs.
- `remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name)` then runs unconditionally (session.rs:1596).
- The protection the doc comment at hooks.rs:283-284 describes does not exist.
- This predates 853e635: the earlier close handler had the same `other_sessions == 0` guard followed by an unconditional `remove_hook_dir`.
- Reproduced on git 2.55: with the active hook directory gone, `git commit` runs neither the gate nor the chained user hook, and the commit succeeds.

(b) Reachability. Shared checkouts are a normal part of the app:
- PAIR groups: a reviewer and up to two builders share one worktree.
- D160: every session of a project with the Unreal plugin enabled defaults to the primary checkout (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18). This is a flow the author uses.
- An explicit `worktree: "primary"` or a path to another session's worktree.

The trigger is closing the most recently created or launched session while any other session on that checkout is not yet closed, in any state. Nothing blocks it:
- The agent menu's "Close session…" defaults to `remove_worktree:false` (agent_menu.rs:612, checkbox unchecked).
- "Discard session" always sends `remove_worktree:false` (shell.rs:734).
- `remove:true` is refused with `session.pair_live` in this situation, so `remove_worktree:false` is the only way to close here.

In D160 this happens on any close that is not in strict launch order, for example closing the newest helper agent first, or creating an agent and discarding it before launch. The repo's own test avoids the case on purpose: sessions.rs:1364-1366 closes "oldest first, so the newest session's hook stays active".

(c) What happens:
- **Immediately, and silently:** every hook-path commit in that checkout skips Relay's commit gate (protected paths, file and line caps, user holds). That covers agents' shell `git commit` and the user's own terminal or IDE commits in the primary checkout. The user's own pre-commit hook (husky, lint, tests) is skipped too. For Codex this is the gate D132 calls "the final write-set enforcement boundary", because Codex's PreToolUse sends every tool call as `exec`.
- **After a later create or launch in that checkout:** the gate comes back, but the user's hook does not. `install_git` cannot read the dead directory's previous-path file and falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (hooks.rs:98). That returns the dead Relay directory (verified), so the new hook records it as the pre-Relay path. The user's hook stays out of the chain until the last session on that checkout closes.
- **After a bus `git.commit` during the window:** `refresh_git` (git.rs:548) reinstalls under the dead session's name. That recreates its directory with a `.relay-previous-hooks-path` pointing at itself. When the last session closes, `uninstall_git_any` follows that self-reference and leaves `core.hooksPath` on Relay's directory, which breaks D23's restore. The user's commits then call `relay … guardrail.gate`, which fails with "no engine" while Relay is not running. At the next engine start, the fsck sweep (recovery.rs:138) deletes the directory. The user's checkout is then left with no hooks at all until a manual `git config` fix or another full Relay cycle there. I confirmed this whole sequence by simulation.

No data is lost or corrupted.

(d) High is correct. The rubric's high band includes "a safety check that can be silently bypassed" and "likely user-visible wrong behavior in a normal flow". It is not critical for three reasons:
- An agent can always run `git commit --no-verify`; the default `denied_commands` (settings.rs:33) does not include it.
- The bus `git.commit` op enforces the gate in-process regardless (git.rs:561).
- Nothing is lost.

(e) The fix is right in direction. It is incomplete in the points listed under corrections.
v2.correction:
Impact correction: the finding says hooks are off only "until some session relaunches". That is wrong. A relaunch or create restores the gate but not the user's own hook, because `install_git` falls back to `rev-parse --git-path hooks` (hooks.rs:98), which returns the dead Relay directory and records it as the pre-Relay path. A bus `git.commit` during the window is worse: `refresh_git` (git.rs:548) recreates the dead directory with a previous-path file pointing at itself. After the last close, Relay's hook then stays wired into the user's checkout. Once the next fsck sweep deletes that directory, the checkout runs no hooks at all.

Related locations to add:
- `session.discard_restorable` (session.rs:1505-1525) has the same `others > 0` guard. It never removes the closing directory, so that directory stays active and the next sweep deletes it.
- The refused-create rollback is guarded only by `pair_with.is_none()` (session.rs:900), so a D160 primary-checkout create that is refused un-wires the live sessions. This trigger is rare.

Fix additions:
1. Before removing a session's hook directory, hold `hooks::writes()` and check whether the worktree's `core.hooksPath` still points at it. If it does and other sessions on the worktree are not closed, either re-run `install_git` for the newest of them before deleting (it reads the closing directory's previous-path file and re-chains the user hook), or leave the directory in place.
2. Apply the same handover in `session.discard_restorable` and in the refused-create rollback, or skip their uninstall when other non-closed sessions share the checkout.
3. Make `sweep_hook_dirs` skip any directory that a worktree's `core.hooksPath` references.
4. Harden `install_git`: never record a path under `.relay/hooks` as the previous path. When the configured Relay directory's previous-path file is missing, fall back to the default or local hooks directory instead of `rev-parse --git-path hooks`. Without this, checkouts already in the broken state, and anything `refresh_git` recreates, keep the user's hook out of the chain.
5. Add a test that closes the newest session first in a shared checkout.

findings.title: install_claude/install_codex never rewrite an existing Relay handler, so a stale relay path or instance persists and the guardrail fails open with exit 127
findings.evidence: `let already_installed = pre.iter().any(|group| ... command.contains(CLAUDE_PRE_TOOL))`, then `if !already_installed { pre.push(...) }`. An existing handler is kept verbatim, including the absolute `relay` path and `--instance` captured at the first launch. The report hooks (364-367) and Codex (512-515, 530-532) use the same pattern. The integration test confirms it: a second `install_claude(.., Path::new("relay"))` after a spawn still yields exactly one Relay group with the old command (tests/guardrails.rs:426-433). Git hooks have `refresh_git` precisely because "Existing worktrees can outlive the Relay process that created them" (hooks.rs:158-159); the provider adapters do not. `claude_pre_tool` fails closed (exit 2) only when the binary actually runs (main.rs:348-356). A missing binary makes the shell exit 127, which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking hook error and then runs the tool.
findings.impact: run.sh launches `$PWD/target/debug/relay` (run.sh:25), so the hook path depends on which checkout the engine was built in. After the binary moves (Relay run from another checkout or a since-removed worktree, a moved repository, a packaged install), every resumed session's worktree and every shared primary checkout keeps calling the dead path. Edit, Write and Bash then run ungated. A handler edited to, say, `true # hook claude-pre-tool` also still matches the substring and is never repaired on relaunch.
findings.fix: On every install, drop every handler carrying Relay's exact generated prefix (the same filter `uninstall_claude`/`uninstall_codex` use, tightened to the generated command shape), then append freshly generated handlers for the current binary and instance. This is in effect uninstall + install, done for PreToolUse, the report hooks and Codex alike.

v1.reason: install_claude (hooks.rs:333-353) and the report loop (364-375), together with install_codex (512-546), skip insertion whenever any handler command merely contains the marker substring, so a handler from an earlier launch is kept verbatim. That includes its absolute relay path and its instance. `.relay/relay.mcp.json` and the git hook are rewritten on every launch: install_claude rewrites the MCP file each time, and refresh_git repairs the git hook. `.claude/settings.local.json` is not, and it survives across restorable sessions because it is only removed by teardown when the last session closes. relay_bin() resolves to `RELAY_BIN` or the current exe's sibling, and run.sh uses `$PWD/target/debug/relay`, so the path depends on the checkout the engine was started from. If that binary is moved or deleted (for example, Relay run from a worktree that is later removed) and a session is resumed, the PreToolUse handler exec's a missing file. The shell returns 127, which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking hook error, so Edit, Write and Bash run ungated. The CLI's fail-closed exit 2 (main.rs:348-356) never gets a chance to run.
v1.correction: Severity is medium, not high. The trigger is the engine binary changing location while sessions are restorable or live, which is a less common path, although this developer's workflow of running Relay from checkouts makes it realistic. Fix: on every install, drop the handlers whose command contains the Relay marker (the same filter as uninstall_claude/uninstall_codex), then append freshly generated ones. The test at guardrails.rs:426 would need updating to expect the refreshed command.

findings.title: Branch cleanup targets every closed session's branch, not only Relay's relay/<name> branches, and can delete long-lived user branches locally and on GitHub
findings.evidence: The candidate SQL is `WHERE s.state = 'closed' AND s.branch != '' AND s.branch != p.base_branch AND NOT EXISTS (...)`; the base branch is the only exclusion. `session.create` records `primary.branch` for primary checkouts (session.rs:860-864) and any existing branch passed as `branch` (session.rs:867, where worktree::create checks out an existing branch instead of creating one). `evaluate` then deletes locally when the tip is an ancestor of `<base>`/`origin/<base>`, runs `config --remove-section branch.<b>`, and, when `gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged` returns a PR whose head equals or contains the tip and `ls-remote` still shows that head, runs `git push <remote> --delete <branch>` (322-337). The module header says the feature exists for `relay/<name>` branches.
findings.impact: Take git-flow with base main. A session is created on `develop` or `release/x`, or runs in a primary checkout that is on develop, and is closed. After the next release PR develop→main merges, the sweep (at most 20 minutes later) does two things whenever no checkout has develop: it deletes local develop with its upstream config, and, because origin/develop still equals the merged PR's head, it deletes develop on GitHub, which closes every open PR targeting it. The UI meanwhile says "The branch is kept" (agent_menu.rs:606).
findings.fix: Only consider branches Relay created for the session. Either record a `created_branch` flag at session.create, or require `s.branch == worktree::branch_for(&s.name)`. Never delete a remote branch Relay did not create. Add a protected-branch list (base plus main/master/develop/release/*) that both branch_cleanup and git.clean_merged honour.

v1.reason: The candidate query at branch_cleanup.rs:76-78 only excludes `s.branch = p.base_branch` and branches held by open sessions. Nothing restricts it to branches Relay created. session.rs:859-863 records `primary.branch` for primary checkouts, and the Unreal plugin makes primary the default (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18, plugins.rs:210). session.rs:865-873 records any `p.branch` the caller passes; worktree.rs:198-206 checks out an existing branch instead of creating one. The `other` path (session.rs:875-884) records whatever branch an existing worktree is on. Once that branch is no longer checked out in the primary (the `checkouts` early-return at 225-226 no longer applies), `evaluate` deletes it locally when its tip is an ancestor of base, and wipes its config section. When `gh pr list --head <b> --state merged` returns a PR whose headRefOid equals the tip and ls-remote still shows that sha, it runs `git push <remote> --delete <b>` (322-329). Example: a git-flow release PR develop->main, with develop recorded by an earlier closed session. Afterwards both the local and the GitHub `develop` are deleted, which closes the PRs that target it. A main->develop back-merge does the same to a non-default `main` when base is develop; GitHub refuses only the repository's default branch. The module header (lines 3-5) describes the feature as cleaning up `relay/<name>` branches, so this is not the intended scope. The commits are not lost (they are merged), and GitHub can restore the branch, so high fits better than critical.
v1.correction: The decisive lines are 76-78 (the query) and 329 (the remote delete). Simplest fix: only consider `s.branch == worktree::branch_for(&s.name)`, or record at session.create whether Relay created the branch (worktree::create already knows: `exists` at worktree.rs:198). Never push --delete a branch Relay did not create.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. The `candidates()` query (branch_cleanup.rs:76-78) excludes only the base branch and branches that open sessions use. session.create records whatever branch the checkout holds: the primary's branch (session.rs:860-863), a caller-supplied existing branch, which worktree.rs:204-206 checks out instead of creating (session.rs:867), or an existing worktree's branch (session.rs:878-887). `evaluate` then runs `update-ref -d` (314), `config --remove-section` (319), and `push --delete` (329) when gh shows a merged PR whose head contains the tip and the live remote sha matches. The module header (3-5) scopes the feature to `relay/<name>` branches, and no test covers any other branch.

(b) Only the user can trigger it, because session.create and session.close are user_only (BUS.md §9.1). The default UI path never records a non-Relay branch: the launch dialog always sends `worktree`, defaulting to "new" (launch.rs:260, 346). A non-Relay branch is recorded only in these cases:
- the user types "primary" or a path in the collapsed expander;
- a create omits `worktree` on an Unreal-plugin project (D160, plugins.rs:210-215). The phone, `relay q`, and the `create` form of task.dispatch do this;
- the request passes an explicit `branch`.

When the primary is on the base branch, which is the usual case, the base exclusion applies. Once a branch is recorded, it is re-judged every 20 minutes indefinitely, and immediately when git.pr.list sees its PR merged (git.rs:627-641). The module landed on 2026-10-05 (2d38f75), so every historical closed session's branch is judged in the first sweep, 90 s after start.

(c) No commits can be lost: deletion needs the tip in the base or inside a merged PR, and the delete is compare-and-delete. What is lost is the local ref and its `branch.<b>` config. A pooled checkout holding the branch is also removed if it is clean.
- Feature branch merged by PR: this mirrors GitHub's auto-delete. It is surprising, and the close dialog says "The branch is kept." (agent_menu.rs:609, not 606), but it is mostly harmless.
- Long-lived branch: consider develop, with main as the GitHub default branch, merged via a PR from develop and then left unchecked-out. Develop is deleted locally, on GitHub, and from refs/remotes. GitHub refuses the delete for the default branch or a protected one.
- Open PRs based on the deleted branch: the claim that this "closes every open PR targeting it" is not established. GitHub's docs say open PRs are retargeted to the merged PR's base, although some users report that GitHub closed them instead. Either outcome is harmful.
- Recovery: use "Restore branch" on the merged PR, or push the sha back.

(d) High overstates it. The harmful case needs a session that was deliberately or plugin-defaulted onto a non-base long-lived branch, plus a PR that merges that branch, a remote branch that is neither protected nor the default, and the branch checked out nowhere at sweep time. That is a real bug in a less common path, so medium. The category stays data-loss because Relay deletes user refs, config and a GitHub branch without being asked.

(e) The proposed fix is correct. Adding `AND s.branch = 'relay/' || s.name` to `candidates()` covers all four callers. PAIR joiners drop out, but the creating session's row still yields the branch.
v2.correction:
The decisive lines are branch_cleanup.rs:76-78 and 329. The UI string is at agent_menu.rs:609. The PR consequence should read: open PRs based on the deleted branch are retargeted to the merged PR's base, per GitHub's docs, or closed according to some user reports. Not simply "closes". Reachability should say that the native launch default ("new") never records a non-Relay branch. Exposure comes from typing "primary" or a path, from creates without `worktree` on Unreal-plugin projects (D160: phone, `relay q`, task.dispatch `create`), or from an explicit `branch`.

Notes on the fix:
1. The name filter leaves branches renamed by session.update before spawn uncleaned (session.rs:1452-1455). That is safe. A `created_branch` column needs a MIGRATIONS entry, a SCHEMA_VERSION bump, and a backfill of `branch = 'relay/' || name`.
2. The name filter does not protect a session branch that has been promoted to a long-lived branch. This repo is an example: origin/HEAD is relay/proud-otter, and the primary checkout is on main. So the fix should also skip the remote's default branch (refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD) and any branch that is the base of an open PR.
3. Extending a protected list to git.branch.clean_merged is optional. It is an explicit user op whose documented purpose is deleting merged branches (BUS.md:830).
4. Reword the close dialog. This is an apps/relay-native change that cannot be compiled here.

findings.title: Relay writes .relay/ and .claude/settings.local.json into primary checkouts without excluding them, so a smart commit commits hook scripts, MCP config and session briefs
findings.evidence: `.relay/`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` reach `.git/info/exclude` only through `worktree::ensure_excluded`, whose sole caller is `worktree::create` (worktree.rs:199). The primary and explicit-worktree branches of session.create (session.rs:860-864, 878-887) never call it. Yet `install_git` does `fs::create_dir_all(&hook_dir)` under `<repo>/.relay/hooks/<session>/` (hooks.rs:100-102). `install_claude` writes `<checkout>/.relay/relay.mcp.json`, `.relay/relay.settings.json`, `.relay/agent-statusline.sh` and `.claude/settings.local.json`, and prepare_launch writes `.relay/sessions/<name>/session-brief.md` containing "Launch assignment" (session.rs:505-509).
findings.impact: With the Unreal plugin on, D160 makes the primary checkout the default, so such a project may never create a pooled worktree and never gets the excludes. git status then lists Relay's files. The Code view's commit with nothing staged sends `all:true` (code_git.rs:276-282), which makes git.commit run `git add -A` (git.rs:544-546). That commits the hook scripts, absolute binary paths and session briefs, including the user's launch prompts, into the repository, and the next push publishes them. Agents running `git add -A` do the same. For a tracked `.codex/hooks.json`, an exclude cannot help at all: Relay modifies a tracked file in place.
findings.fix: Call `worktree::ensure_excluded(repo)` at the start of install_git, install_claude and install_codex (or once in session.create for every checkout kind). It is idempotent and cheap. For a tracked `.codex/hooks.json`, prefer Codex's per-launch `--config` overrides over editing the project file.

v1.reason: The only non-test caller of worktree::ensure_excluded is worktree::create (worktree.rs:199), and skills::apply excludes only skill folders (skills.rs:247-250). The "primary" and explicit-path branches of session.create (session.rs:860-887) never call it, yet they then run install_git, which creates <project>/.relay/hooks/<session>/ (hooks.rs:100-102). prepare_launch also runs install_claude (.claude/settings.local.json, .relay/relay.mcp.json, .relay/relay.settings.json, .relay/agent-statusline.sh) and writes .relay/sessions/<name>/session-brief.md including "Launch assignment:" plus the user's prompt (session.rs:497-509). The Unreal plugin sets default_checkout "primary" (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18, D160), so such a project can go its whole life without a pooled worktree. The native Code view commits with `all = !has-staged` (code_git.rs:276-282), and git.commit then runs `git add -A` (git.rs:544-546). This stages and commits Relay's hook scripts, absolute binary paths and session briefs with launch prompts, and a push publishes them. Agents running `git add -A` do the same.
v1.correction: Scope: .git/info/exclude lives in the common git dir, so a repository where any pooled ('new') worktree was ever created via worktree::create is already covered, primary checkout included. The bug hits projects used only through primary or explicit checkouts, which is the default flow for Unreal projects. The tracked `.codex/hooks.json` case is a separate, deliberate design choice (install_codex documents merging into the project hook layer) and should not be folded into this fix. Fix: call worktree::ensure_excluded(repo) in session.create for every checkout kind (or at the top of install_git), which is idempotent and cheap.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. The only non-test caller of `worktree::ensure_excluded` is `worktree::create` (worktree.rs:199). Its other callers, session.create "new", worktree.create (git.rs:119) and integration runs (integration.rs:101), all go through `create`. The "primary" and explicit-path branches of session.create (session.rs:860-887) never call it. They then run `install_git`, whose `fs::create_dir_all(&hook_dir)` (hooks.rs:101) creates `<project>/.relay/hooks/<session>/`, holding `pre-commit` (with the absolute relay path) and `.relay-previous-hooks-path`. `prepare_launch` then:
- runs `install_claude`, which writes `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.relay/agent-statusline.sh`, `.relay/relay.settings.json` and `.relay/relay.mcp.json`;
- writes `.relay/session-skills.md`;
- writes `.relay/sessions/<name>/session-brief.md`, which includes "Launch assignment:" and the prompt (session.rs:497-509);
- writes `role-instructions.md`.

A scratch-repo test confirms that without the exclude these files show as `??` and `git add -A` stages them. Once the common-dir `info/exclude` lists them, the primary checkout is clean.

(b) The trigger is reachable but narrower than both earlier write-ups claim. The exclude goes into the common git dir, so a single Relay-created worktree or integration in the repository covers it permanently. The bug needs a repository where that never happened, plus sessions in the primary checkout or at an explicit path. The native launch dialog's Worktree field defaults to the text "new" (launch.rs:259-262), and `payload` always sends it (launch.rs:346). So a native launch with default settings creates a pooled worktree and fixes the exclude. That dialog also never applies the D160 default. The real paths are:
1. Phone-door or CLI `session.create` / `task.dispatch {create}` with no `worktree`, for a project with the Unreal plugin on (plugins.rs:210-215; session.rs:858; the payload shape is in remote.rs:311-321).
2. A user who types "primary" or a path in the dialog from the first launch onward.

When those conditions hold, the bug fires every time. In the user's own long-used projects, it is unlikely to have fired.

(c) After the first launch, the main checkout shows about 9 untracked Relay files. The per-session brief and role files are never removed for a checkout that is not pooled, so the list grows by 2 files per session ever launched. The Code view lists all of them, and the commit button reads "Commit all N" with the tooltip "Nothing is staged, so every change is committed" (code_git.rs:330-348). That sends `all:true`, and git.commit runs `git add -A` (git.rs:544-546). Agents' `git add -A` does the same. A push then publishes launch prompts, briefs and home-directory paths. A committed `.claude/settings.local.json` makes collaborators' Claude call an absolute relay path that does not exist on their machines. Default guardrails do not stop it: `protected_paths` is empty, and the cap is only a confirmable hold for the user. A secondary effect is that `is_dirty` counts untracked files, so a device run with primary sync refuses with `device.sync_dirty` (device.rs:1566). This is not silent, since the files and the count are visible before the commit. There is no data loss, and it is recoverable with `git rm --cached` unless already pushed publicly.

(d) Medium, not high. It is a real bug in a less common path that needs specific preconditions, and it is visible before it does harm.

(e) The fix is sound. `ensure_excluded` is idempotent and resolves the common dir through gix, so it also works when called with a linked worktree path. It runs in unlocked phases under `hooks::writes()`.
v2.correction:
Severity high -> medium.

Two scope corrections:
1. The native launch dialog sends worktree:"new" by default (apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:259-262, 346). So in the native app, primary-checkout sessions are not "the default flow for Unreal projects". The D160 default only applies to the phone door and to CLI/bus `session.create` / `task.dispatch {create}` without `worktree`, or when the user types "primary" or a path.
2. Any earlier `worktree::create` in the repository (pooled session, worktree.create, or an integration run) writes the shared common-dir exclude and protects the primary checkout permanently.

Added impact: `.relay/sessions/<name>/{session-brief,role-instructions}.md` are never cleaned up for a checkout that is not pooled, so untracked files accumulate per session. The smart commit is labelled "Commit all N", so the user can see the files are included.

Drop the tracked `.codex/hooks.json` sub-claim. That file is the deliberate project hook layer and a separate root cause.

Fix placement: call `worktree::ensure_excluded(repo)` in `install_git` or at the top of `prepare_launch`, rather than only in session.create. That way sessions already created in a primary checkout get the exclude on their next spawn, resume or wake. The exclude does not untrack files already committed, so affected repos need a one-time `git rm --cached`.

findings.title: File watchers are never removed: one thread, one inotify instance and three fds leak per worktree, and a reused pooled path is never watched again
findings.evidence: `watchers.insert(key.clone(), watcher)` is the only mutation of `engine.watchers` besides its declaration (engine.rs:420). No close, remove or delete path ever drops an entry. Each notify 8.2 inotify `RecommendedWatcher` owns an inotify instance, a mio epoll fd and a waker eventfd, plus a dedicated "notify-rs inotify loop" thread (notify inotify.rs:90-125). `ensure_after_commit` returns early when `engine.watchers.lock().unwrap().contains_key(&key)` (watch.rs:53). It is triggered by file.tree, file.read and file.search (file.rs:21,41,301) and by git.status (git.rs:164), so every session worktree an agent or the Code view touches gets a watcher.
findings.impact: Over the engine's lifetime (it outlives the window), every session worktree ever browsed keeps a thread and an inotify instance alive. With the common `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` default of 128, after roughly a hundred worktrees inotify_init fails for Relay and for the user's other apps. Session names are unique only among non-closed sessions (sessions.rs:80; 36×36 combinations). A reused name recreates `.relay/worktrees/<name>`, the dead watcher's key blocks re-registration, and that session's Code view never live-refreshes.
findings.fix: Drop the watcher keyed by the canonical path when a worktree is removed (session.close, worktree.remove, branch_cleanup's removal). Also, when the callback sees its root removed (DELETE_SELF / IN_IGNORED), remove its own entry through the weak engine.

v1.reason: engine.watchers is mutated only by the insert at watch.rs:138. rg finds no remove or clear anywhere, and engine.rs:420 is only the declaration. ensure_after_commit is called from file.tree/read/search (file.rs:21,41,301) and git.status (git.rs:164) with the resolved worktree root, so every worktree that is browsed, read through MCP, or status-checked gets a RecommendedWatcher. In notify 8.2 each one owns an inotify fd, a mio Poll, a Waker, and a 'notify-rs inotify loop' thread (inotify.rs:90-125), all kept until the engine exits. worktree::remove callers (session.rs:1522/1578, git.rs:139, branch_cleanup.rs:307, workspace.rs:340, integration.rs:62/120) never touch watchers. Reuse is real: session.create only rejects a name if `pooled_path(...).exists()` (session.rs:840), and new_name only checks non-closed sessions (sessions.rs:73-89). Once an old worktree is removed, its name can be drawn again and the same canonical path recreated. watch.rs:53 then sees the stale key and returns, and the dead watcher's kernel watches were already dropped when the old directory was deleted (IN_IGNORED). So the new worktree never emits file.changed of its own.
v1.correction: Downgraded from high. When the directory is deleted the kernel drops its watches, so max_user_watches is not leaked; the leak is one inotify instance, an epoll fd, an eventfd and one mostly idle thread per worktree touched during the engine's lifetime. Running out needs on the order of 100+ distinct worktrees in one engine run under the kernel default max_user_instances=128 (this machine has 1024). The reuse bug is milder in the native client, because editor.invalidate runs on file.changed from any watcher. That session's own edits still never trigger a refresh. Fix as proposed: remove the canonical-path entry from engine.watchers wherever worktree::remove succeeds, and/or have the callback remove its own entry through the weak engine when it sees the root's Remove/DELETE_SELF.

findings.title: Skill materializer prefers the library's original SKILL.md over the stored body, so skill.update edits never reach agents' skill folders
findings.evidence: For library skills, `copy_bounded(&library_dir(store, *id), dest)?` copies the folder that skill.install staged from the clone, and that folder includes its SKILL.md (github.rs:180-182 copies `path.parent()`). Then `if !instructions.is_file() { fs::write(&instructions, &row.body) }`, so `row.body` is written only when no SKILL.md was copied. `skill.update` (provider.rs:155-173), exposed by the skill editor (tools_skills.rs:468-471), changes only the DB body and `updated_at`, which changes the stamp and forces a re-copy of the stale file.
findings.impact: A user edits an installed GitHub skill's instructions in the skill editor. `.relay/session-skills.md` shows the new text, but `.claude/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/...` and the machine-wide homes keep the original. Those folders are the delivery path D147 points agents at, so agents keep following the old instructions. The same happens when skill.create reclaims a soft-deleted name whose old library folder still exists.
findings.fix: For `Source::Library`, always write `row.body` to SKILL.md after copying (the row is the source of truth), or skip SKILL.md when copying the library folder.

v1.reason: GitHub install stages the whole skill folder, SKILL.md included (github.rs:178-181 copies `path.parent()`; the test at github.rs:256 asserts `assets.join("SKILL.md")`). That folder is adopted into `library_dir(id)` (provider.rs:505). In `fill` (skills.rs:328), `copy_bounded(&library_dir(..), dest)` copies that original SKILL.md, and lines 340-343 write `row.body` only `if !instructions.is_file()`, so the stored body never reaches the folder. `skill.update` (provider.rs:155-173) changes only `name`, `body` and `updated_at` and never touches the library folder. The native editor sends `skill.update` with the edited body (tools_skills.rs:467-471). The stamp changes, so the folder is re-copied, but from the stale library SKILL.md. The same happens on `skill.create` reclaiming a soft-deleted name (provider.rs:115-120): `skill.delete` leaves the library dir in place, so the old SKILL.md comes back.
v1.correction: Downgraded to medium: only installed GitHub skills with a library folder are affected; skills made in the editor have no library dir and are written from `row.body`. The agent also sees the new text in `.relay/session-skills.md`, so it gets contradictory instructions rather than only the old ones. Fix: for `Source::Library`, always write `row.body` to SKILL.md after the copy, or skip SKILL.md in the copy. Optionally remove the library dir on skill.delete, or on a reclaiming skill.create.

findings.title: install_git records the effective hooks dir as the worktree's previous core.hooksPath, so uninstall pins an explicit value (or a self-referencing Relay dir)
findings.evidence: `previous_dir` falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` in two cases: when nothing is configured at worktree level, and when the active Relay dir has no `.relay-previous-hooks-path`. Verified: `--git-path hooks` honours core.hooksPath. It returns `.git/hooks` when unset and returns the worktree-level Relay dir when that is configured. The value is persisted (140-145), and `uninstall_git_any` writes it back with `git config --worktree core.hooksPath <previous>` (256-262), never restoring "unset".
findings.impact: (a) A primary checkout that had no worktree-level hooksPath ends up with an explicit `core.hooksPath=.git/hooks` after its last session closes. Verified: a later repo-level `core.hooksPath=.husky/_` (husky, lefthook) is then shadowed, and the user's new hooks silently never run there. (b) When the active Relay dir lost its record (the remove_hook_dir finding, followed by refresh_git on a bus commit), the record becomes the Relay dir itself. uninstall_git_any then re-sets it on every iteration and returns with hooksPath on a Relay dir that is later swept, which permanently disables the user's hooks in that checkout. In that state run_user_pre_commit also skips the user's hook.
findings.fix: Persist the worktree-level configured value separately, with an explicit 'unset' sentinel, from the effective directory used for chaining. Restore with `--unset` when it was unset. Never record a path under `.relay/hooks/` as the previous value.

v1.reason: previous_dir falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (hooks.rs:98), which returns the effective hooks dir, not "unset". install_git persists it to .relay-previous-hooks-path (hooks.rs:140-145). uninstall_git_any restores it with `git config --worktree core.hooksPath <previous>` (hooks.rs:256-262) and only unsets when the file is missing or empty. I reproduced the consequence: with `core.hooksPath=.git/hooks` in .git/config.worktree, a later repo-level `git config core.hooksPath .husky/_` is shadowed (`rev-parse --git-path hooks` still prints .git/hooks). This hits primary checkouts and explicit worktrees, which are not deleted on close, after their last session closes. Husky or lefthook installed afterwards then silently never runs there. The same happens in reverse when husky was active at install time and later removed. I also observed that `git worktree add` copied the main worktree's config.worktree into the new linked worktree, so the pinned value spreads. Scenario (b) is reachable: Close with a live partner on the same worktree computes teardown=None but still calls remove_hook_dir (session.rs:1596), which may delete the active hook dir. The next bus commit's refresh_git then reinstalls it, reads no record, and records the Relay dir itself as previous.
v1.correction: In scenario (b), run_user_pre_commit does not skip a hook. user_dir resolves to the Relay dir itself, so it runs Relay's own generated pre-commit (an extra guardrail.gate) instead of the user's hook. The user's hook is skipped only in the sense that it is lost. The fix is right: record the worktree-level configured value with an explicit 'unset' sentinel, restore with --unset, and never record a path under .relay/hooks/. Separately, remove_hook_dir at session.rs:1596 should be skipped when that dir is still the active hooksPath.

findings.title: run_user_pre_commit runs the user's hook with Command::output() and no timeout, breaking the subprocess invariant
findings.evidence: `let output = Command::new(&hook).current_dir(worktree).output()` is the only subprocess in this module not run through `proc::output_with_timeout`. It runs in git.commit's prepare phase (git.rs:555). The comment at 187-189 ("would wait on that same transaction forever") is stale, because the hook now runs before any transaction opens. The socket door handles one connection's requests sequentially (`spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(..)).await` inside the read loop, socket.rs:742), and the native app sends git.commit on its main connection (code_git.rs:1723 → `ui.call`).
findings.impact: A pre-commit hook that never exits (for example one waiting on /dev/tty, a lock or the network) leaves git.commit pending forever. Every later request on that connection (the UI's main socket, or an agent's MCP connection) stops being answered, and the blocking-pool thread and the child leak. CLAUDE.md: "Every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout."
findings.fix: Run the hook through `proc::output_with_timeout` with a generous, configurable bound (for example 10 minutes), report a timeout as `git.pre_commit_failed`, and update the comment.

v1.reason: hooks.rs:210-213 runs the user's pre-commit with `Command::new(&hook).current_dir(worktree).output()`, with no timeout. Every other subprocess in hooks.rs goes through `git()` -> `proc::output_with_timeout` (hooks.rs:583-588). The only caller is git.commit's staged prepare phase (git.rs:555), so the store mutex is not held. The harm is therefore not a bus-wide freeze. It is per connection: socket.rs handles one connection's requests in sequence (`spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(..)).await` inside the read loop). The native app sends git.commit through `Ui::call` -> `client.request` on its shared main connection, because only lifecycle ops get their own connection (client.rs:50-63). A hung hook therefore stalls every later UI request on that connection. Each one times out after the client's 30 s request_timeout, and a blocking-pool thread and the child process leak. The comment at 187-189 ('while its transaction is open ... wait on that same transaction forever') is stale: D144 moved the hook ahead of the transaction.
v1.correction: Severity is medium, not higher: the store is not locked, so other connections such as agents' MCP sessions keep working. A timeout alone also does not fix the UI stall. An ordinary pre-commit that runs longer than 30 s, such as a test suite, already makes the UI's commit time out ('outcome unknown') and blocks the main connection while it runs. The fix needs both a bounded `proc::output_with_timeout` and sending git.commit on its own connection, the way lifecycle requests are sent. Related, same class, should be tracked separately: `worktree::git` (worktree.rs:26-33), used by git_mutate for `add -A`, `commit` and `push` (network), also calls `.output()` with no timeout.

findings.title: Bus commits skip the user's commit-msg hook: git.commit uses --no-verify and only pre-commit is emulated
findings.evidence: git.commit runs `git_mutate(&root, &["commit", "--no-verify", "-m", &p.message])` (git.rs:568) so Relay's generated hook is not re-entered. `--no-verify` bypasses both pre-commit and commit-msg, but `run_user_pre_commit` only looks up `user_dir.join("pre-commit")` (hooks.rs:208).
findings.impact: Every commit made through Relay (the Code view's commit button, MCP git_commit) silently bypasses commitlint, Gerrit Change-Id insertion and ticket-number checks implemented as commit-msg hooks. The result is non-conforming commits, and pushes that Gerrit rejects.
findings.fix: Also run the user's commit-msg hook in the prepare phase on a temp file holding the message (honouring its rewrite or refusal), and pass the result with `-F <file>`; or generalise run_user_pre_commit to `run_user_hook(name, args)`.

v1.reason: git.commit does use `commit --no-verify` (git.rs:568), and only pre-commit is emulated (run_user_pre_commit, hooks.rs:208). That bypasses commit-msg, as claimed. But the root cause is broader. install_git points the worktree's core.hooksPath at .relay/hooks/<session>/ (hooks.rs:149-153), and that directory contains only `pre-commit` (hooks.rs:103, 138). Only the user's pre-commit is chained (hooks.rs:104-121). Every other user hook in the previous dir (commit-msg, prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge) stops running for every commit and push in a hooked checkout, including agents' and the user's plain `git commit`/`git push`. I reproduced it: an executable .git/hooks/commit-msg runs on a normal commit, but not with core.hooksPath set to a dir holding only pre-commit. Nothing in relay-core handles LFS or other hooks (rg for lfs/commit-msg/pre-push found nothing relevant).
v1.correction: Re-scope the root cause from the --no-verify flag to install_git's hook directory holding only pre-commit. Impact is wider than commitlint and Gerrit Change-Id: git-lfs installs pre-push, post-commit, post-checkout and post-merge hooks in .git/hooks, and these no longer run. Pushes from an LFS repository (likely for the Unreal projects this app targets) do not upload LFS objects. GitHub rejects such a push (GH008, unknown LFS objects); other hosts accept pointers to missing objects. Fix: in install_git, write a pass-through shim into the Relay hook dir for every standard hook name that execs `$previous_dir/<name> "$@"` when present (pre-commit keeps its gate). For bus commits, also run the user's commit-msg hook on a message file in the prepare phase and commit with -F, or drop --no-verify once the generated hook can no longer deadlock (it runs in the unlocked phase now).

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. git.commit's locked `finish` phase runs `git_mutate(&root, &["commit", "--no-verify", "-m", &p.message])` (git.rs:571). Its unlocked prepare phase emulates only one hook: run_user_pre_commit looks up `user_dir.join("pre-commit")` (hooks.rs:208). `--no-verify` skips both pre-commit and commit-msg, so a user's commit-msg hook never runs for a bus commit, whether or not the checkout is hooked.

The first verifier's broader root cause is also real. install_git sets the checkout's per-worktree core.hooksPath to .relay/hooks/<session> (hooks.rs:150-154). That directory holds only the generated pre-commit (hooks.rs:103), and the generated hook chains only the previous pre-commit (hooks.rs:104-121). D23 and D96 only describe chaining pre-commit. Nothing there says dropping the other hooks is intended.

I reproduced it in an isolated scratch repo (git 2.55). An executable .git/hooks/commit-msg ran for a commit in the main checkout. It did not run for a commit in a linked worktree whose per-worktree core.hooksPath pointed at a directory holding only pre-commit.

(b) Who hits it, and when:
- Every bus commit: the Code view's commit button (code_git.rs:280/392) and MCP git_commit.
- Every terminal commit or push in a hooked checkout. That covers agents' pooled worktrees. It also covers the user's own main checkout when a session runs in "primary" mode, which is the Unreal plugin's default (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18, session.rs:858). The hooks stay replaced until the session closes.
- It only matters in repositories that have hooks other than pre-commit: husky/commitlint, Gerrit Change-Id, pre-commit-framework commit-msg or pre-push stages, or test-before-push hooks.
- The author's own RelayV4 repo has none. Its .git/hooks holds only samples, and .relay/hooks/*/ holds only pre-commit. So whether it bites depends on the project's setup.

(c) The LFS consequence the first verifier added does not happen in practice. With git-lfs 3.8.0 (installed on this machine), any LFS filter call inside the hooked checkout writes pre-push, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge into whatever core.hooksPath is active, which here is the Relay directory. I saw this happen in three cases:
