- after one `git lfs clean`;
- after the first ordinary `git commit -am` in a fresh hooked worktree, where racily-clean LFS entries are cleaned again;
- in a worktree on a branch carrying an LFS object that was committed elsewhere and never pushed.

In every case the next `git push` uploaded the LFS objects to the remote.

The LFS case that remains needs a hooked checkout that pushes LFS objects created before the hook was installed, with no LFS filter run since. That is rare, and GitHub then rejects the push loudly (GH008), which `git lfs push` fixes.

What is real:
- commit-msg checks and rewrites are silently skipped: commitlint, Change-Id insertion, ticket checks. Gerrit then rejects the push, loudly.
- The user's pre-push hooks (tests, branch protection) are skipped, and Relay has no push gate of its own (GateKind is only Write/Commit/Exec).
- post-checkout and post-merge automation does not run.

There is no data loss and no way for an agent to get past the guardrails.

(d) Medium is right, and high is not. This is a real, silent bug, but it depends on the project's hook setup. The case for high rested on rejected LFS pushes, and git-lfs reinstalling its own hooks prevents those.

(e) The original fix is correct for bus commits: run the user's commit-msg hook in the prepare phase on a temp file, honour its rewrite or refusal, then commit with `--no-verify -F`. It is incomplete, though, because it leaves terminal commits and pushes in hooked checkouts untouched. The first verifier's alternative, "drop --no-verify ... it runs in the unlocked phase now", is wrong. The commit runs in `finish`, inside the transaction with the store mutex held (engine.rs:522-554; git.rs:560-572). Without --no-verify, git would run the generated pre-commit, which calls `relay cmd guardrail.gate` over the socket and waits on the store this very request holds. That is the D96 deadlock. It would also run user hooks under the store mutex, which breaks a CLAUDE.md invariant.
v2.correction:
Line: the `commit --no-verify` call is git.rs:571, not 568 (568 is `Some(&numstat)` in the enforce call).

Root cause: keep the first verifier's broader scope. install_git (hooks.rs:100-109 and 150-154) replaces the checkout's whole hooks directory with one that holds only pre-commit. On top of that, git.commit's `--no-verify` skips commit-msg even in checkouts Relay has not hooked. Note that "primary" mode, the Unreal plugin's default, hooks the user's own main checkout for as long as the session lives.

Impact: drop the LFS claim. git-lfs 3.8.0 writes its pre-push, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge hooks into the active core.hooksPath (the Relay directory) on its first filter call there, and pushes then upload LFS objects. I verified this with `git lfs clean`, with a first commit in a fresh worktree, and with a branch carrying an LFS object that had not been pushed. The impact that remains is skipped commit-msg, prepare-commit-msg, pre-push and post-* hooks of other tools.

Fix:
- Drop the "drop --no-verify" alternative. The commit runs in the locked `finish` phase, so it would reintroduce the D96 self-deadlock and run user hooks under the store mutex.
- For bus commits: in prepare, run the user's commit-msg hook (and optionally prepare-commit-msg) from the previous hooks directory on a temp message file, then commit with `--no-verify -F <file>`.
- For terminal commits and pushes: in install_git, write a pass-through shim that does `exec "$previous_dir/<name>" "$@"` (stdin is inherited) for each hook name actually present in the previous directory. refresh_git re-runs install_git on every launch and bus commit, so the shims stay current. Do not shim every standard name: that would fork sh on high-frequency hooks such as reference-transaction and post-index-change.
- Caveat for the shims: a shim named pre-push stops git-lfs from installing any of its hooks into the Relay directory. It refuses to overwrite a foreign hook, and the filter ignores that error and installs nothing. I confirmed this. So shims must reliably chain to wherever LFS's own hooks live.

findings.title: adopt() replaces the skill library folder inside the install transaction; a rollback leaves an orphan that the next skill reusing the rolled-back id materializes
findings.evidence: `adopt` does `fs::remove_dir_all(to)` and `fs::rename(from, to)` on `<store>/skills/<id>`. It is called from install_downloaded_skill inside skill.install's finish transaction (provider.rs:504-508). When a later item in the same install fails (`skill.name_exists`, provider.rs:228-240), the transaction rolls back but the folder move stays. The skills id is `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` (store.rs:259), and the sqlite_sequence bump rolls back too. Verified: after a rolled-back insert the next INSERT receives the same id.
findings.impact: Installing a repository whose second skill conflicts by name leaves `<store>/skills/N` holding skill #1's folder. The next `skill.create` gets id N, and because fill prefers a copied SKILL.md (see the related finding), that new skill materializes into every checkout and home with skill #1's instructions and assets. For an existing id, the library now holds the new files while the row keeps the old body, revision and stamp, so checkouts disagree.
findings.fix: Adopt after commit: stage to `<id>.pending` inside the transaction and rename it in `after_commit`, or adopt entirely in `after_commit`. Also remove any pre-existing library dir when a row is created fresh (skill.create / INSERT).

v1.reason: install_downloaded_skill (handlers/provider.rs:416-509) INSERTs or UPDATEs the row and then calls skills::adopt (provider.rs:504-507). adopt (skills.rs:51-66) calls remove_dir_all on `<store>/skills/<id>` and renames the staged folder into it. All of this runs in the finish closure of register_staged, inside the store transaction. If a later item in the loop (provider.rs:229-240) returns an error, for example the `skill.name_exists` conflict with an already-installed skill at 455-487 or `valid_skill_name`, the handler returns Err and the transaction rolls back. The filesystem move is not undone. deduplicate_downloaded_skills only removes duplicates within the download, not conflicts with existing rows, so the trigger is a normal flow: install a multi-skill repo where a later skill (BTreeMap order) has the name of one already installed. skills.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT (store.rs:259), and the sqlite_sequence update rolls back with the transaction, so the next INSERT reuses the id. skill.create (provider.rs:136-140) does not clear any library dir. fill (skills.rs:320-342) then copies library_dir(id), including the orphan's SKILL.md, and writes row.body only when SKILL.md is missing. The new hand-made skill therefore materializes with the other skill's instructions and assets. For an UPDATE target the library holds the new files while the row (body, revision, updated_at stamp) is rolled back, so checkouts already stamped keep the old content and fresh ones get the new files.
v1.correction: Fix as proposed: either collect the (assets, id) pairs and adopt them in ctx.after_commit, or stage under `<id>.pending` and rename after commit. Defensively, also have skill.create's INSERT path remove any existing library_dir for the new id. Medium is right: real wrong content in an install-with-conflict path, and no data loss.

findings.title: folder_name maps distinct skill names to the same folder, so two skills overwrite each other on every apply
findings.evidence: `folder_name` lowercases, turns every non-[a-z0-9] run into '-', truncates to 64 chars and falls back to "skill". Skill names are unique only case-insensitively (`name=?1 COLLATE NOCASE`, provider.rs:160, 434), so "Code Review" and "code-review", or any two non-ASCII names, coexist. `apply` writes each row to `base.join(&row.dir)`. `write_skill` is fresh only if the marker equals this row's stamp, which the other row just overwrote. `with_plugins` (135) guards only plugin-vs-installed collisions.
findings.impact: Each launch or refresh rewrites the shared folder twice (remove_dir_all plus a copy of up to 64 MiB each) and only the last row survives, so one installed skill is invisible to agents. The brief (awareness.rs:356) still advertises both names at the same folder.
findings.fix: Assign folder names once per plan and disambiguate collisions (for example append `-<id>`), or reject install/rename when folder_name collides with another live skill.

v1.reason: folder_name (skills.rs:106-118) lowercases the name, collapses every non-ASCII-alphanumeric run to '-', truncates to 64 characters and falls back to "skill". Names are unique only case-insensitively (store.rs:260 `name TEXT NOT NULL COLLATE NOCASE UNIQUE`). valid_skill_name (provider.rs:572) only checks length. So "Code Review" and "code-review", any two all-non-ASCII names, or names that share their first 64 characters can coexist. row_of sets dir = folder_name(name). apply (skills.rs:229-246) writes each row to base.join(&row.dir). write_skill's freshness check compares the marker with this row's stamp, which the other row just overwrote, so on every apply (every launch, every refresh_all) both rows rewrite the folder with remove_dir_all plus a copy, and the last row wins. with_plugins (skills.rs:131-147) dedupes only plugin rows against installed rows, not installed rows against each other. The brief (awareness.rs:353-361) lists both names at the same path.
v1.correction: Disambiguate when building the plan, for example by appending `-<id>` on collision (the brief would need the same mapping, since awareness.rs computes folder_name independently), or reject create, update and install when folder_name collides with another live skill. Medium: a real but uncommon edge case.

findings.title: Plugin skills are materialized into the machine-wide ~/.claude/skills and $CODEX_HOME/skills, reaching every project although the plugin is off there
findings.evidence: `Ok(with_plugins(rows, &crate::plugins::enabled_anywhere(conn)?))`. The user-scope plan includes every skill of every plugin enabled in any project, and plan_user writes it to `~/.claude/skills` and `$CODEX_HOME/skills`. plugins.rs:9 promises "Nothing is written for a project that has it off." Live state (read-only listing): ~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills hold 27 unreal-*/blender-* folders stamped `plugin unreal-engine ...`, while this RelayV4 worktree's .claude/skills holds only audit and impeccable (the plugin is off here), and this audit session itself was offered those 27 skills.
findings.impact: Switching a plugin on for one project injects its skills, and their descriptions in every session's context, into every Claude and Codex session on the machine: other projects and the user's non-Relay sessions included. Agents in unrelated repositories can load Unreal or Blender instructions.
findings.fix: Leave plugin skills out of the Claude user base, since Claude already reads the enabled projects' checkout folders. For Codex, either give Relay's Codex sessions a per-launch CODEX_HOME overlay, or accept the global reach explicitly and fix the module doc.

v1.reason: skills.rs:172 builds the user-scope plan with `with_plugins(rows, &plugins::enabled_anywhere(conn)?)`. plan_user writes it to `~/.claude/skills` and `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (user_bases, skills.rs:178-197), and refresh_all applies it on every skill change and at engine start. The plugins.rs:9 module doc says "Nothing is written for a project that has it off", and D159 justifies off-by-default because plugins "change how every agent in a project works". Read-only check: ~/.claude/skills holds unreal-* and blender-* folders whose marker reads `plugin unreal-engine 0668aa7957a39104 unreal-ai`, while this worktree's .claude/skills holds only audit and impeccable. This very session was offered those Unreal and Blender skills. The machine-wide union is a deliberate choice for installed skills (D147, the enabled_anywhere doc comments), but for plugins it contradicts the per-project promise. For Claude it is pure leakage, because Claude already reads the enabled projects' checkout copies.
v1.correction: This is intentional in code (plugins::enabled_anywhere's doc says "what the machine-wide skill folders carry"), so it is a policy and docs contradiction rather than an accident. The impact is context noise and possibly misapplied skills in unrelated Claude and Codex sessions, not corruption. Simplest fix: leave Source::Plugin rows out of the ~/.claude/skills base. Keep or explicitly document them for $CODEX_HOME, which has no per-project alternative, and correct plugins.rs:9 and D159 accordingly.

findings.title: Dev and stable instances share the user-scope skill folders and .relay/hooks namespace, so each instance's cleanup prunes the other's live state
findings.evidence: `user_bases` ignores the instance except Test and returns the same `~/.claude/skills` and `$CODEX_HOME/skills` for Dev and Stable. `prune` removes every folder carrying `.relay-skill` that is not in this instance's rows (350-361), and the stamps embed per-store ids. Every engine start runs `refresh_all` (serve.rs:29-33), and run.sh defaults to the dev instance. Likewise `sweep_hook_dirs` (hooks.rs:291) deletes every `.relay/hooks/<name>` not open in this instance's store (recovery.rs:124-139).
findings.impact: Starting a dev engine whose store has different skills removes or rewrites the stable instance's user-scope skill folders, and the stable instance does the same on each of its launches. Codex sessions of the other instance lose their skills. When both instances list the same repository, each fsck deletes the other's live hook directories, leaving dangling core.hooksPath values: commits go ungated and the user's hooks are skipped.
findings.fix: Namespace by instance: record the instance in the marker and prune only your own folders, and use `.relay/hooks/<instance>/<session>` (or pass every instance's live set to the sweep).

v1.reason: Each instance has its own store (paths.rs:51-58: `<data_local>/relay-v4/<instance>/store.db`), but `user_bases` (skills.rs:179-197) returns the same `~/.claude/skills` and `$CODEX_HOME/skills` for Dev and Stable; only Test returns empty. `prune` (skills.rs:350-361) deletes every folder carrying `.relay-skill` whose name is not in this instance's rows, and `refresh_all` runs on every engine start (serve.rs:29-33) and after every skill change (provider.rs:532-538), and `plan_launch` adds the user plan to every launch (session.rs:445). So whichever instance ran last decides the machine-wide skill set; the other's skills that it lacks are deleted, and because stamps embed per-store ids (skills.rs:157) even identical skill sets rewrite each other's folders. Hook half is also real: recovery step 5 (recovery.rs:124-139) lists only this store's non-closed sessions per project and `sweep_hook_dirs` (hooks.rs:291-308) removes every other dir under `<repo>/.relay/hooks/`. `install_git` writes the pre-commit guardrail gate into `<repo>/.relay/hooks/<session>` (hooks.rs:100-128) and points the worktree's core.hooksPath at it. If both instances have the same project (likely for someone developing Relay with Relay; run.sh defaults to dev), starting the dev engine deletes the stable instance's live hook dirs. Git then finds no hooks at that path, so commits skip both the Relay commit gate and the user's chained pre-commit, with no error until the session is relaunched.
v1.correction: The trigger needs both instances in use at once with overlapping projects or different skill sets, which is why this stays medium even though the hook half is a silent bypass of the commit gate. The hook sweep only runs at engine start (recovery), not on every launch. Fix: put the instance in the skill marker and in the hook path (`.relay/hooks/<instance>/<session>`, or prune/sweep only entries whose marker or script names this instance). Codex-home pruning should likewise skip folders stamped by another instance.

findings.title: Branch cleanup's checked-out check fails open on a git error and deletes with update-ref, which ignores worktree, rebase and bisect protections
findings.evidence: `let Ok(ran) = git.run(&["worktree", "list", "--porcelain"], GIT_TIMEOUT) else { return Vec::new() };`, and `ran.out` is parsed without checking `ran.ok`. A timeout or failure therefore reads as "checked out nowhere". Deletion is `update-ref -d refs/heads/<b> <tip>` (314), plumbing that does not refuse a branch checked out in a worktree or being rebased or bisected; a branch being rebased shows as `detached` in the listing. `live` is snapshotted once at the start of `run` (356-359), which may be minutes before a candidate is evaluated. By contrast, git.clean_merged fails closed when the listing fails and uses `git branch -d` (git.rs:696-713).
findings.impact: If `git worktree list` times out (20 s) or errors, a branch checked out in the primary checkout or in a live agent's worktree is deleted. That checkout's HEAD then names a missing branch: git shows "No commits yet" and the next commit starts a new root history. A user mid-rebase on such a branch has the rebase's final ref update fail.
findings.fix: Treat a failed or empty listing as 'keep' (fail closed), re-list immediately before deleting, and refuse when any worktree is rebasing or bisecting that branch, or delete with `git branch -D` after re-verifying the tip.

v1.reason: `checkouts` (branch_cleanup.rs:139-152) returns an empty Vec when `git.run` errs or times out, and parses `ran.out` without checking `ran.ok`. A failed listing therefore reads as 'checked out nowhere', so the primary-checkout and live-worktree guards at 223-235 are skipped. The delete at 314 is `update-ref -d refs/heads/<b> <tip>`, which, unlike `git branch -d`, does not refuse a branch checked out in a worktree. git.clean_merged (git.rs:696-697) fails closed on a listing error, so the two paths are inconsistent. The trigger is rare: `git worktree list --porcelain` is cheap and robust, so it would need a 20 s timeout or a broken repository. There is also a small race: between the listing and the delete come cherry and a gh call of up to 30 s, and a checkout made in that window is not seen. The consequence is bounded. The branch is merged (deletion requires that), so no commits are lost and uncommitted files stay. The affected checkout's HEAD points at a missing branch until the user recreates it.
v1.correction: The listing is not a snapshot taken at the start of `run`: `checkouts` runs fresh for each candidate. Only the open-session `live` list (356-359) is snapshotted. The fix is to fail closed: return Err or a 'keep' verdict when `run` errs or `!ran.ok`, and re-list just before the update-ref.

findings.title: After-close cleanup removes the worktree the user just chose to keep, including git-ignored files, contradicting the UI's "worktree and branch are kept"
findings.evidence: "Discard session" sends `{"remove_worktree":false,"purge_build":false}` with the tooltip "its worktree and branch are kept" (shell.rs:724,734), and the close dialog says "The branch is kept" (agent_menu.rs:606). `after_close` then runs `evaluate`, which treats that kept pooled worktree as removable once the branch is merged and `worktree::status_files` is empty. That status uses `--untracked-files=all` without `--ignored` (worktree.rs:89). It then calls `worktree::remove(&candidate.repo, path, true)`, which purges build dirs and runs `git worktree remove --force`, falling back to remove_dir_all.
findings.impact: Closing an agent tile with 'keep' right after its PR merged deletes the worktree seconds later. Ignored files the dirty check never sees go with it (.env, local configs, the build caches the user explicitly asked to keep), and the branch is deleted too.
findings.fix: Pass the close's remove_worktree choice into after_close and never remove a worktree the user kept, or at minimum require `git status --ignored` to be clean apart from BUILD_DIRS. Then align the UI copy with the cleanup policy.

v1.reason: The close dialog's 'Also remove the worktree' box is unchecked by default (agent_menu.rs:593), and its copy says 'the worktree and branch are kept unless you choose otherwise' and 'The branch is kept.' (589, 609). 'Discard session' sends remove_worktree:false with the tooltip 'its worktree and branch are kept' (shell.rs:724,734). session.close (session.rs:1630-1635) always schedules `after_close`, which does not know the user's choice. The closed session's worktree is no longer in `live`, it is under the pool, so `evaluate` sets `removable` (231-234). When the branch is merged and `worktree::status_files` is empty, `worktree::remove(&repo, path, true)` runs at line 307. That status uses `--untracked-files=all` without `--ignored` (worktree.rs:89). `remove` purges BUILD_DIRS and runs `git worktree remove --force`, falling back to remove_dir_all (worktree.rs:359-366), so gitignored files (.env, local config, build caches the user left unpurged) are deleted. The 20-minute sweep would do the same later. The module header (lines 13-15) documents this removal as intended, so the engine and the UI copy disagree: in practice 'kept' means 'kept until merged'. The loss of ignored files is not harmless.
v1.correction: The main mechanism is the after-close path for a merged branch, plus the sweep later on. Either honour remove_worktree:false by passing it to after_close and not removing a kept worktree in that run, or require `git status --ignored` to be clean apart from BUILD_DIRS before removing. In either case, fix the UI copy so it states the real policy.

findings.title: Recursive watch registration covers every session worktree and build tree under the root, follows symlinks, and on failure silently re-walks on every request
findings.evidence: `watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive)` registers an inotify watch for every directory; `is_generated_path` filters events only. Session worktrees live inside the primary root (`.relay/worktrees`). Here the primary checkout has 24,602 directories, 19,878 of them under .relay/worktrees (5 worktrees). notify 8.2's recursive add walks with `follow_links` (Config::default `follow_symlinks: true`), and its `?` aborts the whole watch on the first directory that vanishes mid-walk (PathNotFound) or on ENOSPC (inotify.rs:400-415). `ensure` drops the error without logging and clears the registration key, so the next file.tree, file.read, file.search or git.status starts another full walk.
findings.impact: About 80% of the primary checkout's inotify watches sit on trees whose events are discarded, and each worktree's build dirs are watched twice. While agents build, target/ directories churn: registering the primary checkout can keep failing, the Code view gets no live refresh, and every request spawns another ~25k-directory walk. When max_user_watches is lower, the limit is exhausted silently.
findings.fix: Watch the root non-recursively and each top-level entry recursively unless it is generated, `.relay` or `.git` (adding new top-level directories on Create). Set `Config::default().with_follow_symlinks(false)`, log registration errors, and back off retries per root.

v1.reason: watch.rs:133 calls `watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive)` on the primary checkout, and pooled worktrees live under `<repo>/.relay/worktrees` (worktree.rs:14-19). is_generated_path drops every `.relay` event (watch.rs:173) but only after delivery. I measured this checkout: 24,634 directories, 19,910 of them under .relay/worktrees. In notify 8.2, add_watch walks with `WalkDir::follow_links(self.follow_links)`; Config::default sets `follow_symlinks: true` (config.rs:122). The mask includes OPEN, MODIFY, CREATE and others (inotify.rs add_single_watch), so every file an agent's build opens in its worktree's target/ is delivered to the primary's loop thread, and also to that worktree's own watcher if it has been touched. Any add_single_watch error is propagated with `?` (PathNotFound on ENOENT, MaxFilesWatch on ENOSPC, and the post-add `metadata(...).map_err(Error::io)?`), which fails the whole watch() call. ensure() then drops the watcher without logging (watch.rs:141-147) and clears the registration key, so the next file.tree/read/search or git.status starts a new full walk. watcher_registrations allows at most one walk per root at a time, and the walk runs on a separate thread, not under the store lock.
v1.correction: The claim that registration 'can keep failing' while agents build is overstated. filter_dir already drops entries whose stat fails, so a directory that vanishes only aborts the walk if it disappears in the tiny window between that stat and inotify_add_watch, or right after the add. That can happen with cargo incremental session dirs, but rarely. The confirmed, ongoing cost is about 20k redundant watches with pinned inodes plus duplicated OPEN/MODIFY event traffic during worktree builds, all off the bus, together with silent, unlogged failures and an immediate re-walk with no backoff. ENOSPC is unlikely in practice: this machine's max_user_watches is 524288. Fix as proposed: do not descend into `.relay`, `.git` or generated dirs (e.g. watch the root non-recursively and its non-generated top-level entries recursively), turn off follow_symlinks, log the error, and back off retries per root.

findings.title: install_git rewrites the shared .git/config on every launch/create/commit, and refresh_git does it without hooks::writes(), so lock contention fails the operation
findings.evidence: `git(repo, &["config", "extensions.worktreeConfig", "true"])` runs unconditionally. Verified: git rewrites .git/config (new inode) even when the value is unchanged, and fails with "could not lock config file .git/config: File exists" (exit 255) while another writer holds config.lock. `refresh_git` is called on every git.commit (git.rs:548-553) without taking `hooks::writes()`. Other writers of .git/config include agents' `git push -u`, `branch_cleanup`'s `config --remove-section` (branch_cleanup.rs:319) and `git branch -m`.
findings.impact: An agent pushing with -u at the same moment as a launch, create or bus commit makes it fail (`session.spawn` errors, or git.commit returns `git.hook_refresh_failed`). Every bus commit also spawns 4-5 git processes and rewrites the shared config for nothing.
findings.fix: Read `git config --get extensions.worktreeConfig` and set it only when missing; take `hooks::writes()` in refresh_git; skip the rewrite when the hook script and hooksPath are already current.

v1.reason: install_git always runs `git(repo, &["config", "extensions.worktreeConfig", "true"])` (hooks.rs:75). I checked in the scratchpad with git 2.55: rewriting an unchanged value replaces the inode of .git/config, and a pre-existing config.lock makes it fail immediately with "could not lock config file .git/config: File exists" (exit 255), with no retry. refresh_git (hooks.rs:159-181) calls install_git and is invoked in the unlocked prepare phase of every git.commit (git.rs:548-553) without taking hooks::writes(). A failure maps to `git.hook_refresh_failed`. It can therefore race a concurrent launch, create or close holding writes(), another bus commit, or any agent's own .git/config writer (`git push -u`, `git branch -m`, etc.), and fail spuriously. Each git config write takes about a millisecond, so collisions are rare, which keeps this low.
v1.correction: The impact is an occasional spurious failure, not a frequent one. The fix is as proposed: read before setting extensions.worktreeConfig, take hooks::writes() in refresh_git, and skip the rewrite when the script and hooksPath are already current (this also removes about 4 git subprocesses per bus commit). Lock contention with agents' own git commands cannot be fully removed; a short retry on "could not lock config file" would cover it.

findings.title: Skill materialization is unsynchronized: concurrent refresh_all threads and launches race, so stale plans win and fill's error path deletes another writer's folder
findings.evidence: Every skill or plugin change spawns a new `skill-materialize` thread running refresh_all (provider.rs:532-538), and so does engine start. refresh_all plans under the store lock and then applies with no lock. prepare_launch applies under `hooks::writes()`, which refresh_all never takes. `fill` starts with `fs::remove_dir_all(dest)`, and on any error `write_skill` runs `fs::remove_dir_all(dest)` (318-320).
findings.impact: Two quick toggles produce two threads whose plans were read at different times. Whichever finishes a root last decides it, so a disabled skill can linger or an enabled one be pruned until the next refresh. Two writers filling the same folder can each delete the other's finished copy, leaving the skill missing for sessions started meanwhile.
findings.fix: Funnel all materialization through one worker: a mutex plus a dirty flag, re-planning after acquiring it. Have prepare_launch use the same lock instead of `hooks::writes()`.

v1.reason: Every skill.create/update/delete/enable/install spawns a new `skill-materialize` thread running `refresh_all` after commit (provider.rs:532-538), and so do engine start (serve.rs:29-33) and project add (workspace.rs:214). Each thread plans under the store lock and then applies with no lock (skills.rs:267-306). `prepare_launch` applies under `hooks::writes()` (session.rs:478-495), which refresh_all never takes. `fill` begins with `remove_dir_all(dest)` and then copies (skills.rs:325-347), and `write_skill` removes `dest` on any error (skills.rs:318-320). Two quick toggles therefore produce two unsynchronized appliers whose plans were read at different times. The one that finishes a base last wins, so a stale plan can re-add a disabled skill or prune an enabled one, and two fills of the same folder can delete each other's files mid-copy, so the error path removes the folder.
v1.correction: The windows are milliseconds, except for large library folders. The state heals on the next refresh or launch, and the worst case is a skill folder missing or stale until then, so low is right. Fix: one materializer guarded by a mutex with a generation/dirty counter, re-planning after it acquires the lock and coalescing queued refreshes; have the launch path take the same lock.

findings.title: Remote branch deletion is check-then-act without a lease, and uses an unqualified refspec
findings.evidence: After `ls-remote --heads` shows `sha == pr.head || sha == tip`, Relay runs `git push <remote> --delete <branch>`. Nothing ties the push to the observed sha, and `--delete relay/x` is ambiguous if a tag of that name exists.
findings.impact: Commits pushed to the branch between the check and the delete (a collaborator, or CI pushing a fix-up) are dropped from the remote, contrary to the comment "only if nobody pushed to it since".
findings.fix: Use `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<sha> <remote> :refs/heads/<b>`, which deletes only while the remote still points at the sha that was checked.

v1.reason: Lines 324-329 run `ls-remote --heads`, compare the sha, then run a separate `git push <remote> --delete <branch>` with no lease. A push to the remote branch between those two network calls (a collaborator or CI) is deleted along with the branch. The pusher still has the commits locally, and the window is a few seconds, so in a mostly single-user app the impact is small. The '--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<sha>' fix is a one-line improvement. The 'unqualified refspec' half of the finding is wrong: if both a head and a tag named <b> exist on the remote, git refuses with 'dst refspec matches more than one'. If only a tag exists, ls-remote --heads shows nothing and the push is never attempted. So the ambiguity fails safe.
v1.correction: Drop the refspec-ambiguity claim. The race alone is the finding: use `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<sha> <remote> :refs/heads/<b>` with the sha that was checked.

findings.title: Each 20-minute sweep re-evaluates every leftover closed-session branch from scratch with ~10 git processes, including git cherry
findings.evidence: Every closed-session branch still present is evaluated on every sweep. That means rev-parse; `worktree list --porcelain` per candidate (139-140); config --get twice; resolving 2-3 refs; merge-base; `git cherry base tip`, which patch-ids every base commit since the fork; and `rev-list --count`. GH_CACHE (185-194) skips only the network call. Unmerged branches are kept forever, so the set only grows.
findings.impact: Background CPU and process churn grows with every abandoned session: hundreds of git processes and potentially seconds of patch-id work every 20 minutes. Meanwhile the SWEEPING mutex makes `git.branch.cleanup` and after-close cleanups wait for the whole sweep.
findings.fix: Cache the local verdict keyed by (tip, base tip, remote base tip) and skip unchanged branches; list worktrees once per repository per run.

v1.reason: `spawn_sweeper` (429-455) calls `run(engine, None, None, ...)` every 20 minutes. Every closed session whose branch still exists is a candidate (76-79). For each candidate, `evaluate` runs about 8-10 git processes: rev-parse of the tip, `worktree list` once per candidate, two `config --get`, resolves of the remote and base refs, `merge-base --is-ancestor` and `git cherry` for each base, and `rev-list --count`. GH_CACHE (185-194) skips only the gh call. An unmerged or abandoned branch is kept and re-evaluated forever, and `git cherry base tip` patch-ids every base commit since the fork point, so it gets costlier as the branch ages. SWEEPING (183, 355) serializes the sweep with the user-invoked `git.branch.cleanup` (git.rs:646-655) and with after_close cleanups. The work runs at background priority off the store lock, so the real impact is modest background churn plus an occasional wait on the on-demand op.
v1.correction: Cache the local verdict keyed by (tip, base tip, remote-base tip) so an unchanged branch is skipped without spawning git. List worktrees once per repo per run.

findings.title: Watcher's git-metadata handling assumes .git is a directory; in pooled worktrees index/HEAD live outside the watched root, so staging never refreshes
findings.evidence: `let index_path = root.join(".git/index")` and the `.git/` rules in is_generated_path (162-168) only work for the primary checkout. In a linked worktree `.git` is a file, and the index and HEAD are in `<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>/`, outside the watched root. The primary's watcher classifies `.git/worktrees/...` paths as generated.
findings.impact: `git add`/`git reset` run by an agent in its own worktree never produce `file.changed`, so staged badges in the Code view stay stale until some unrelated event invalidates it.
findings.fix: Resolve the worktree's git dir (gix `repo.git_dir()`), watch it non-recursively for index and HEAD, and compare against that index path.

v1.reason: Pooled worktrees come from `git worktree add` (worktree.rs:206-208), so `.git` is a gitdir file; this worktree's own `.git` reads `gitdir: /home/anthony/dev3/RelayV4/.git/worktrees/spry-newt`. In watch.rs:89, `index_path = root.join(".git/index")` points at a path that does not exist for a linked worktree, and the per-worktree recursive watch (watch.rs:133) never sees `<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>/index` or that worktree's HEAD. The primary checkout's watcher does see that file, but is_generated_path (watch.rs:162-167) only lets through `.git/index`, `HEAD`, `packed-refs`, `config` and `refs/**`, so `.git/worktrees/<name>/index` counts as generated and is dropped. So when an agent runs `git add`/`git reset` from its shell in its worktree, no file.changed is emitted. Bus git.stage/unstage still emit git.changed. The native client calls editor.invalidate on any file.changed from any watcher (app.rs:1232-1240, editor.rs:508), so the stale state lasts only until some other event arrives.
v1.correction: The impact is narrower than stated. A commit in a linked worktree updates `<repo>/.git/refs/heads/relay/<name>`. If the primary checkout's watcher is registered, it passes that change through as a refs change and emits file.changed, which the native client applies to the whole view. So only staging-only (and HEAD-only, e.g. a checkout of the same tree) operations made from a shell go unseen, and only until the next unrelated event. Fix: resolve `repo.git_dir()` with gix, compare against `git_dir/index`, and add a non-recursive watch on the git dir, or let `.git/worktrees/*/index|HEAD` through in the primary watcher and map them to the owning worktree.

findings.title: is_generated_path treats any build/dist/target/coverage/Saved/Binaries component at any depth as generated, hiding tracked source directories
findings.evidence: `relative.components().any(|component| matches!(value, ".relay" | "node_modules" | "target" | "build" | ... | "dist" | "coverage" ...))`. file.rs list_dir uses the same predicate to drop entries from the tree (file.rs:519).
findings.impact: Tracked directories with those names (the committed `dist/` of a JavaScript GitHub Action, `scripts/build/`, a `src/target/` module) are invisible in the Code view's tree, and edits under them never trigger a refresh.
findings.fix: Decide by git ignore rules (gix exclude stack, `git check-ignore`) or by root-level build directories, not by name at any depth.

v1.reason: is_generated_path (watch.rs:169-187) treats a path as generated if any component, at any depth, is one of target/build/dist/coverage/Saved/Binaries/Intermediate and the rest of the list. list_dir (file.rs:518-519) filters tree entries with this same predicate, so a tracked `scripts/build/`, a committed `dist/` of a JS action, or a `src/target/` module never appears in the Code view tree, and edits under them never trigger a refresh. The nested matching is partly deliberate: the test asserts that `/repo/app/build/generated/source.kt` is generated, to catch Android `app/build`. But the cost of hiding tracked source is not handled anywhere: the tree has no tracked-file check.
v1.correction: There is also a divergence: file.search uses a separate, narrower list, `skip_dir` (file.rs:629-636), with only .git/.relay/node_modules/target. So search finds and opens files under `build/`, `dist/`, `Saved/` and similar directories that the tree hides, which makes the behaviour inconsistent. Fix: decide with the gix exclude stack (ignored and untracked) for the tree listing, or at least exempt directories that contain tracked entries. Keep the cheap name list only as a watcher event filter.

findings.title: Claude status-line adapter: the command path is unquoted and the shared usage file is rewritten non-atomically by every session
findings.evidence: `"statusLine": {"type":"command", "command":statusline_path, ...}` passes a raw absolute path that Claude runs through a shell; the hook commands, by contrast, go through shell_quote_path. The script does `printf '%s\n' "$input" > "$out"` (577) into one shared `relay-usage.json` from every concurrent Claude session, and usage.rs:39-43 parses that file.
findings.impact: A project under a path with spaces (e.g. "~/Unreal Projects/Game") makes the status line fail, so usage is never captured. When sessions write concurrently, readers can see truncated JSON and report no usage intermittently.
findings.fix: Quote the path with `shell_quote_path`, and write to `$out.$$` followed by `mv -f` in the script.

v1.reason: hooks.rs:394-396 writes `"statusLine": {"type":"command", "command": statusline_path}` with a raw absolute path, while every hook command goes through shell_quote_path. Claude Code runs statusLine commands through a shell, so a repository path containing whitespace or shell metacharacters (worktrees live under `<repo>/.relay/worktrees/...`) breaks the status line and usage capture silently. The script (claude_statusline_script, about hooks.rs:577) writes `> "$out"` with truncate-then-write into one shared `~/.claude/relay-usage.json` from every Claude session. read_claude_file (usage.rs:39-52) returns None when parsing fails, so a read that lands mid-write briefly reports no usage.
v1.correction: The impact is small. The torn-read window is tiny and recovers on the next report; the unquoted path only matters for repositories under paths with spaces. Fix: shell-quote the statusLine command, and have the script write to a temp file and then `mv -f` it into place.

findings.title: hooks::writes() is documented as held for milliseconds, but launches hold it across skill folder copying, serializing every create/launch/close
findings.evidence: Doc: "Held for milliseconds, never across a network call." prepare_launch takes `let writes = crate::hooks::writes();` (session.rs:480) and drops it only at 560. In between it runs `skills::apply` for both plans, copying every enabled skill folder (up to 64 MiB each) into two bases and the user homes, plus three brief writes.
findings.impact: A first launch in a fresh worktree with many or large skills blocks every other launch, create and close, across all repositories, for the duration of the copy.
findings.fix: Drop the guard right after the adapter writes, before skills::apply. Skill writes need their own serialization (the materializer lock), not the git-config lock.

v1.reason: hooks.rs:57-63 says the guard is "Held for milliseconds, never across a network call". prepare_launch takes `let writes = crate::hooks::writes();` at session.rs:480 and only drops it at session.rs:560. In between it runs `crate::skills::apply` for the project plan and the user plan (session.rs:491-495). apply -> write_skill -> fill -> copy_bounded copies the library folder, which can be up to 64 MiB / 4000 files per skill (skills.rs:24-25). It also writes the brief and role files and may create_dir_all the write roots. While that happens, every other create (session.rs:891), launch, and close/teardown (session.rs:353), across all repositories, blocks on this global mutex. The impact is limited: write_skill returns early when the marker stamp matches (skills.rs:304-306), so the long hold only happens on the first launch after a skill is added or changed in a checkout or user home. The store mutex is not held, so the bus is not frozen.
v1.correction: There is no existing "materializer lock" to fall back on, so the suggested fix needs a new one. skills::apply also does a read-modify-write of the shared `.git/info/exclude` (skills.rs:247-250 -> worktree.rs:44-66) and rewrites the shared user-home skill folders (remove_dir_all then copy). Moving it out of the guard therefore needs its own serialization. Note that skills::refresh_all (skills.rs:264-301) already calls apply with no lock at all, so skill writes are not serialized by this guard today anyway. Either fix the doc comment, or move apply after `drop(writes)` behind a dedicated skills mutex.

findings.title: uninstall_claude repeats the same file removals three times, and its loose marker can strip user handlers
findings.evidence: The three `fs::remove_file` calls at 448-450 are repeated verbatim in the NotFound arm (456-458), and the MCP config is removed again at 488. Handlers are dropped when `command.contains("hook claude-")` (475), which also matches a user command such as `~/bin/notify-hook claude-done`.
findings.impact: Dead duplicate code obscures the actual flow, and a user's own handler whose command happens to contain the marker is deleted on close.
findings.fix: Remove the files once at the top and match handlers by Relay's exact generated prefix (the same predicate the install path should use).

v1.reason: hooks.rs:447-489 (uninstall_claude). Lines 448-450 remove MCP_CONFIG_RELATIVE, CLAUDE_SETTINGS_RELATIVE and CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_RELATIVE unconditionally. The NotFound arm (455-459) removes the same three files again, and line 488 removes MCP_CONFIG_RELATIVE a third time, all after the first removals already ran. Those repeats do nothing. CLAUDE_HOOK_MARKER is "hook claude-" (line 13) and is matched with `contains` (line 475), so a command such as `notify-hook claude-done` would also be stripped. The only caller is session close (handlers/session.rs:356), and it runs on `.claude/settings.local.json` in the session worktree.
v1.correction: The duplicated removals are real but cause no harm. The marker collision is theoretical: the file is a gitignored local settings file in a Relay-made worktree, and a user command would need to contain the exact substring "hook claude-". Treat this as cleanup. Delete lines 456-458 and 488. Optionally match on the generated form "--instance <x> hook claude-" or on the relay binary path. Low.

findings.title: skills::materialize is dead and materialize_user is test-only; both copy under the store lock, contrary to D147/D149
findings.evidence: `materialize` has no callers anywhere, and `materialize_user` is called only by this file's unit test. Their doc ("for callers already holding the transaction that launched") describes planning and copying with the connection held, which D147 forbids ("The copying never runs under the store mutex").
findings.impact: A public API that invites the exact pattern the design bans, kept alive only by one test.
findings.fix: Delete both and have the test call `apply(&plan_user(&conn, ..)?, &store)` after dropping the lock.

v1.reason: rg finds no caller of `skills::materialize` (skills.rs:255) anywhere, examples included. `materialize_user` (skills.rs:261) is called only by the unit test at skills.rs:402/411. All production paths use `plan`/`plan_user` under the lock and then `apply` after releasing it (refresh_all skills.rs:267-306, workspace.rs:214-217, session.rs:441-493). The doc comment ('for callers already holding the transaction that launched') describes copying with the connection held, which D144/D147 avoid.
v1.correction: Delete both functions. Have the test call `let plan = plan_user(&store.lock(), Instance::Test)?; apply(&plan, &store)` so it no longer holds the lock while it copies. This is a small cleanup.

findings.title: watch::Defer trait abstracts two contexts but only Unlocked ever uses it
findings.evidence: Both `impl Defer for Ctx` and `impl Defer for Unlocked` exist, but all four callers of `ensure_after_commit` are `register_unlocked` handlers (file.rs:21,41,301; git.rs:164), so the Ctx impl is unused.
findings.impact: An extra trait, two impls and a boxed closure exist for a single concrete use.
findings.fix: Take `&mut Unlocked` directly and delete the trait and both impls.

v1.reason: `trait Defer` with impls for `Ctx` and `Unlocked` (watch.rs:29-41) exists only for `ensure_after_commit` (watch.rs:45). All four callers are `register_unlocked` handlers: file.rs:19-21 (Tree), file.rs:39-41 (Read), file.rs:299-301 (Search), git.rs:162-164 (Status). So the `Ctx` impl is never used.
v1.correction: The payoff is tiny: about ten lines, and the boxed closure stays unless `Unlocked::after_commit` is generic. It is really an unused impl (dead code) rather than meaningful overengineering. Taking `&mut Unlocked<'_>` directly and deleting the trait is fine but optional.

findings.title: Two SKILL.md front-matter parsers (plugins::frontmatter and github::frontmatter_name) have already diverged
findings.evidence: plugins.rs:162-178 requires keys at column 0 and returns `Some("")` for an empty value. github.rs:218-229 trims leading whitespace (so it matches an indented nested `name:`), skips empty values and caps the result at 120 characters. Both parse the same SKILL.md format.
findings.impact: Installed and bundled skills read their names differently, so a SKILL.md with a nested `name:` key, or an empty top-level one, gets a different name depending on the path it came in by.
findings.fix: Keep one parser (plugins::frontmatter, or a shared helper in skills.rs) and call it from github.rs.

v1.reason: In production, plugins::frontmatter only reads `description` of bundled plugin SKILL.md files (plugins.rs:151). A bundled skill's name and folder come from its directory name (plugins.rs:139-145, `dir`), never from front matter. The only `frontmatter(.., "name")` calls are in tests (plugins.rs:356, 378), which assert that name equals the dir. So the claimed impact, that installed and bundled skills read their names differently and get different names depending on the path they came in by, does not exist. The two parsers read different keys from different inputs: repo-authored files fixed at build time versus downloaded files. Merging two 12-line functions with different contracts (generic key versus name with a fallback and a 120-character cap) has little payoff.
v1.correction: The real defect is narrower and lives only in github.rs:224. frontmatter_name uses `line.trim().strip_prefix("name:")`, so an indented nested key (for example `metadata:\n  name: x`) placed before the top-level `name:` is taken as the skill name. That would be a separate low-severity finding on github.rs, not a duplication finding.

results.coverage: Read every line of all six assigned files (app.rs, import_v3.rs, integration.rs, notify.rs, settings.rs, ui.rs). Traced into: engine.rs (pipeline, register/register_unlocked/register_staged, after_commit, system_write, fill_identity), relay-bus registry + ops metadata for app/notify/ui/git, guardrail.rs (authorize, config/typed/validate_config, put_raw, inverse_patch), handlers/guardrail.rs, worktree.rs, proc.rs, store.rs (backup_to, schemas), recovery.rs, workspace.rs (project.remove / integrations_live), device.rs (device.run, run_command, stream_command), device_lease.rs, task.rs (safe_name, attach_bytes, next_position), audit.rs (undo replay), socket.rs (watch leases), relay-remote bridge/wire gate (phone acts as user), tests (store.rs v3 fixture, phase8 integration, registry_remove, bus.rs D150), and native call sites (status.rs, code_git.rs, shell.rs, tools_settings.rs, onboarding.rs, board_view.rs). Experiments: Python model of flatten/set_at/merge_value reproduced the notify-settings undo and dotted-key bugs; sqlite3 confirmed case-insensitive LIKE deletion and that the prefix query scans. Nothing compiled or run. Not established: real v3 sessions.json cap conventions (0/negative), hence medium confidence on the caps finding; whether gix rev_parse_single resolves refs whose names start with '-' (possible option injection into `git merge` via agent-supplied branches; not reported, low impact since agents already run git); actual freeze durations. Checked and dismissed: app.status providers::list (PATH lookup only), BackupNow under lock (inherent per D15), resources.watch lease handling (socket door releases on disconnect), cast warnings in these files (benign), first_run.state provider count (no native consumer, intent ambiguous). Observed outside this chunk, not reported here: git.rs:129 worktree.remove has the same locked-removal problem (listed as related); relay-bus app.rs gives app.resources.watch Actors::All although BUS.md §9.1 lists app.* mutations as user_only; jiff Timestamp Display trims fractional digits so same-second text ORDER BY can misorder. Skipped as trivia: query_row vs prepare_cached, hand-written enum/string maps duplicating serde derives, dead `_ctx` fn at app.rs:287. apps/relay-mobile out of scope, not reviewed.

findings.title: v3 import copies attachments to dest_dir.join(original_name) and reads v3 `path` unchecked: path traversal, arbitrary file write/read, silent overwrite
findings.evidence: Lines 243-266: `let candidates = if Path::new(&path).is_absolute() { vec![PathBuf::from(&path)] } else { vec![dir.join(&path), repo.join(&path)] }; ... let dest_dir = attach_root.join(new_id.to_string()); std::fs::create_dir_all(&dest_dir).bus()?; let dest = dest_dir.join(&name); std::fs::copy(&src, &dest).bus()?;` where `name` = v3 `attachments.original_name` and `path` = v3 `attachments.path`, both straight from the untrusted relay.db. Path::join with an absolute `name` replaces the base and `../` climbs out of `<store dir>/attachments/<id>/`. v4's own attach path (task.rs:490 `safe_name` keeps only file_name() and rejects ./..; task.rs:523 writes `{id}-{name}`) does neither of these things for the importer.
findings.impact: Importing a crafted v3 store (a repo that committed `.relay/relay.db`, or one an agent wrote into a checkout the user then types into the onboarding import field) with original_name `../../../../.local/bin/git` copies attacker bytes, exec bits preserved by fs::copy, to an arbitrary path (PATH dir, ~/.bashrc, or `<store dir>/store.db`, corrupting the live store); an absolute `path` such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa is copied into Relay's attachment store and served by task views. Benign data breaks too: two attachments of one task named `image.png` (clipboard pastes) land on one file, so the second silently overwrites the first while both rows point at it; a name containing '/' or equal to '' / '..' makes fs::copy fail and `?` aborts the whole import.
findings.fix: Reuse task.rs `safe_name` and the `{attachment_id}-{name}` naming (insert the row first, as attach_bytes does); canonicalize each source candidate and require it to stay under the v3 .relay dir/repo; downgrade per-attachment failures to warnings instead of aborting the import.

v1.reason: In the attachments loop of import_v3.rs (~243-266), `name` (v3 attachments.original_name) and `path` come straight from the imported relay.db. `let dest = dest_dir.join(&name); std::fs::copy(&src, &dest)` escapes `<store dir>/attachments/<id>/` when name is absolute or contains `..`. An absolute `path` is read from anywhere. task.rs attach_bytes, by contrast, applies safe_name (file_name only, rejects ./..) and names the file `{id}-{name}`. There is also a benign-data bug: two attachments of one task with the same original_name copy to the same dest, so the second overwrites the first and both rows point at one file. In addition, any copy error aborts the whole import through `?`. The transaction rolls back, so nothing is half-written, but the entire import fails.
v1.correction: Downgraded from high. app.import.v3 is `Actors::UserOnly` (relay-bus ops/app.rs), so no agent can call it with a crafted source. The exploit needs the user to type the path of an attacker-crafted v3 store into onboarding or the CLI. The importer exists to migrate the user's own v3 data, so that is unlikely. The duplicate-name overwrite is the more realistic harm. The fix stands: insert the row first and write to `{attachment_id}-{safe_name(name)}`, require each canonicalized source to stay under the v3 .relay dir or repo, and turn per-attachment failures into warnings.

findings.title: integration.discard removes the worktree (tree walks, rm -rf, untimed git) inside a locked `register` handler
findings.evidence: `e.register::<IntegrationDiscard>(...)` runs in the request transaction with the store mutex held and calls `worktree::remove(Path::new(&project.path), Path::new(path), true)` then `worktree::git_mutate(..., &["branch", "-D", ...])`. worktree::remove (worktree.rs:352-370) does purge_build (dir_size walk + remove_dir_all per build dir), a second dir_size over the whole checkout whose result this handler discards, then `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune` via worktree::git, a bare `Command::output()` with no timeout (worktree.rs:26-33). D149 converted session.close/discard_restorable to register_staged for exactly this work (session.rs:1505, 1547); this op was missed. integration.request likewise runs gix::open + rev_parse_single per branch under the lock (lines 28-29), the gix work D149 moved out of transactions.
findings.impact: Discarding an integration that built (a Rust/Gradle/Unreal target tree of several GB, 100k+ files) holds the global store mutex for seconds to minutes; every other request queues behind it, including agents' guardrail.gate hooks on each tool call, session.report and the UI's ctx.read bursts. A git that hangs (hook, LFS, index lock) holds it forever. Breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout.
findings.fix: Register with register_staged: prepare reads the row via ctx.read and removes worktree + branch unlocked (git through output_with_timeout); finish only sets state='discarded'. Skip the size walk when the freed bytes are unused. Move integration.request's gix validation into a staged prepare as well. git.rs:129 worktree.remove needs the same change.

v1.reason: IntegrationDiscard is registered with plain e.register (integration.rs:58) and calls worktree::remove(..., true) at line 62. That function (worktree.rs:352-370) runs purge_build (a dir_size walk plus remove_dir_all on build dirs), then a second dir_size over the whole checkout whose result the handler drops, then `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune`. It then runs `git branch -D` via git_mutate. All of these go through worktree::git, a bare Command::output() with no timeout (worktree.rs:26-33), and all run with the store mutex held. This breaks both CLAUDE.md rules (slow work under the lock; subprocesses through proc::output_with_timeout). The same holds for worktree.remove (git.rs:129).
v1.correction: Downgraded from high to medium. Both integration.discard and worktree.remove are Actors::UserOnly, and neither has a caller in apps/relay-native, so they are reached only through a generic bus or CLI call. A real stall can happen but rarely does in normal use. The gix::open + rev_parse_single in integration.request (lines 28-29) costs milliseconds and is minor. Fix: register_staged, with prepare reading the row and doing the removal and branch delete unlocked (git through output_with_timeout) and finish setting state='discarded'. Skip the second dir_size when the freed byte count is not used.

findings.title: Integration worktrees, branches and build output are never removed: unbounded disk growth from the normal 'Test together' flow
findings.evidence: Every request creates `<repo>/.relay/integrations/<id>` on branch `relay/integration-<id>` (lines 86-101) and run() returns after Passed/Failed/Conflict leaving both; the only cleanup is UserOnly integration.discard and the discarded-before-merge path (119-122). The native Code page always sends `"build":true` (code_git.rs:738) and lists integrations as plain labels with no discard action (code_git.rs:752-770); recovery.rs, branch_cleanup and worktree GC never touch .relay/integrations. Each request also spawns an unbounded std::thread (line 40). SPEC §8 specifies '→ discard' and 'The 73GB problem, closed'; the module doc calls them throwaway. app.resources measures only session worktrees, so this disk is invisible in the resources panel.
findings.impact: Each integration leaves a full checkout (plus LFS content) and its build tree (often GBs) on disk and a relay/integration-N branch in the user's repo and branch picker, forever. A builder agent (integration.request is in its default allowlist, settings.rs:36) can loop requests, each spawning a thread, a checkout and a concurrent build with no cap; the `queued` state is never actually used.
findings.fix: Purge build dirs and remove the worktree when a run ends failed/conflict, and after a short retention for passed ones (keep the latest N per project); cap concurrent integrations per project and really queue the rest; add a discard action in the Code page; have recovery GC directories under .relay/integrations with no live row.

v1.reason: integration.rs:86-101 creates <repo>/.relay/integrations/<id> on branch relay/integration-<id> via worktree::create; run() ends at Passed (216-225), Failed/Conflict (fail(), 103-111/128-142/167-170) with no removal. The only removal paths are IntegrationDiscard (58-69, Actors::UserOnly per relay-bus ops/git.rs:145) and the discarded-before-merge check (113-123). rg finds no caller of integration.discard in apps/relay-native (code_git.rs:738 sends {sessions, build:true}; 753-770 renders up to three plain labels with no action), and recovery.rs / git.branch.cleanup / workspace.rs never touch .relay/integrations or relay/integration-* branches. SPEC §8 promises '→ discard' and 'The 73GB problem, closed'. integration.request is not UserOnly and is in the builder default allowlist (settings.rs:36), and each request spawns an unbounded std::thread (line 40) with no per-project cap; 'queued' is set at insert and immediately overtaken by Merging.
v1.correction: Additional related defects worth folding in: (1) nothing resets integrations left in queued/merging/building/deploying after an engine restart (recovery.rs:114 and engine.rs:645 reset device_runs only), and workspace.rs:166/304 integrations_live() then refuses project.remove / workspace.remove forever for that project unless the user finds integration.discard outside the native UI. (2) IntegrationDiscard is registered with Engine::register and calls worktree::remove(..., purge=true), which walks and rm -rf's the build dirs and runs dir_size over the whole checkout while holding the store mutex (CLAUDE.md invariant: slow tree walk in a locked handler) — once a discard UI exists, discarding a multi-GB build freezes the bus. Fix should register discard with register_staged and do the removal outside the lock, plus a restart sweep that marks stale live integrations failed and GCs orphan directories.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. run() (integration.rs:85-101) creates `<repo>/.relay/integrations/<id>` from base on `relay/integration-<id>`. Every terminal path returns without removing the directory or the branch: Failed at create (102-111), Conflict (128-142), build Failed (167-170), deploy Failed (186-195, 209-212) and Passed (216-225). Only two paths remove anything: integration.discard (58-69, Actors::UserOnly per relay-bus ops/git.rs:145-146) and the discarded-before-merge check (113-123). Nothing else touches them:
- recovery.rs steps 1-7 never read `integrations`.
- Engine::shutdown (engine.rs:633-659) only closes device_runs.
- branch_cleanup candidates are closed sessions' branches only (branch_cleanup.rs:74-104).
- project.remove deletes the integration rows (workspace.rs:370), but `remove_worktrees` only covers session pool dirs (330-347). After a project removal the trees are orphaned with no row left to discard.
- app.resources measures only open sessions' worktrees (app.rs:182-190).

(b) Who can trigger it:
- The user, from the native Code page MERGE TEST section (code_git.rs:666-750). Its copy promises "a disposable worktree" (677), and it always sends build:true (739).
- Builder agents: integration.request is in the default builder allowlist (settings.rs:36), with Actors::All.

Every use leaks, and nothing reclaims it. The desktop client has no discard: apps/relay-native never calls integration.discard or worktree.remove, and runs are rendered as plain labels (753-774). The user can't delete the branch from the branch picker either: git.branch.delete refuses because the branch is unmerged and checked out (git.rs:469-480). The only ways out are `relay cmd integration.discard` or manual git. On this machine there is no `.relay/integrations` directory and no `relay/integration-*` branch, so the leak is latent until the feature is first used.

(c) What each run leaves behind:
- A full working-tree checkout, with LFS files materialized.
- A `.git/worktrees` admin dir.
- A permanent branch.
- Build output, but only when the project has a build_cmd and the merge passed. build_cmd is NULL by default (store.rs:54). For scale, this repo's worktree holds a 24 MB checkout but a 13 GB `target/`.

The trees and branches pile up in the editor's CHECKOUTS & BRANCHES picker (project_files.rs:147-178), in LOCAL BRANCHES and in the device worktree picker. They are invisible in the resources panel. The primary checkout's recursive watcher (watch.rs:133; notify 8.2 inotify walks every directory, and `.relay` is filtered only at event time, watch.rs:173) also walks and watches every leaked tree. Each request gets its own thread (line 40) and starts work at once, because 'queued' is overwritten by Merging immediately. N clicks therefore mean N concurrent builds; the button is re-enabled as soon as the row commits (745).

(d) High is right: disk grows without bound through normal use of a first-class flow, there is no in-app recovery, and the disk panel doesn't show it. It is not critical: no data is lost, growth is human-paced, and manual git can recover the space. D38 (DECISIONS.md:138-141) deliberately keeps the worktree "for inspection until explicit discard". That keep is by design, but it is not harmless, because the desktop client never got the explicit discard.

(e) The fix direction is right, with the caveats listed under correction.
v2.correction:
Corrections to the finding:
- "The 73GB problem, closed" (SPEC.md:216-219) belongs to the session worktree-lifecycle bullet, not the integration one. The integration bullet (212-216) only ends "→ discard". The finding should cite D38 (DECISIONS.md:138-141), which makes keep-until-explicit-discard the design. So the defect is the missing discard affordance plus the missing retention policy, not the fact that the tree is kept.
- Build output accrues only when project.build_cmd is set (NULL by default) and the merge passed. Otherwise each run costs a checkout (plus LFS files) and a branch.
- The builder-agent loop is speculative. The realistic case is repeated clicks, each starting another concurrent build.

Fix caveats:
1. integration.discard runs under the store mutex (registered with `register` at integration.rs:58). worktree::remove does dir_size walks and remove_dir_all, and runs `git worktree remove --force`, `git worktree prune` and `git branch -D` with no timeout. Wiring a Code-page button to the handler as it stands turns a multi-GB discard into a one-click bus freeze. Move it to register_staged, as session.close does (session.rs:1547-1582), or to after_commit. git.rs:129 (worktree.remove) has the same pattern; that is a separate invariant finding.
2. Removing failed or conflict trees immediately contradicts D38's inspection intent. Prefer purging build output on failure plus retention by age or count.
3. A retention GC must:
   - skip trees that a live device_run uses (device_runs.worktree). device.run and device.build with integration_id run Gradle inside a passed tree (device.rs:983-1016).
   - delete the `relay/integration-<id>` branch too, because worktree::remove keeps branches.
4. A startup GC must do its disk work outside the recovery transaction, which holds the store lock across steps 2-7.

On the first verifier's extra items:
- Item (1) is real but has a different root cause: nothing reconciles integrations after a restart. Rows stuck live permanently block project.remove and workspace.remove even with force (workspace.rs:166-169, 303-307). Report it separately as medium and cross-reference the shared startup sweep.
- Item (2) is a separate invariant finding, but fixing it is required before adding the discard button (caveat 1).

A rare extra consequence: worktree::create (worktree.rs:204-211) checks out an existing branch instead of branching from base. With a fresh store against the same repo (ids restart at 1), a leaked `relay/integration-1` either fails the new run (the path or branch is already checked out) or, if its directory was pruned, gets merged onto a stale integration commit.

findings.title: Integrations interrupted by quit or crash stay merging/building/deploying forever and permanently block project and workspace removal
findings.evidence: The run is a detached `std::thread::spawn(move || run(engine, id, parent))` with no registry. recovery::run_with (recovery.rs:53-213) resets sessions and device_runs but never integrations; Engine::shutdown ignores them; app.quit checks only `live_pty_count()` (app.rs:39-41). project.remove refuses 'force or not' while any row is in ('queued','merging','building','deploying') (workspace.rs:304-307, integrations_live at 387-391) with hint 'wait for the integration to finish'; registry_remove.rs:150 inserts exactly such a 'merging' row.
findings.impact: Quitting (no warning) or crashing during a multi-minute build leaves '#N · building' in the Code page forever after restart; project.remove and workspace.remove are refused forever with a hint that can never be satisfied, and the only escape (integration.discard) has no UI. The `fish -lc` build child keeps running as an orphan after the engine exits.
findings.fix: In recovery, mark rows in queued/merging/building/deploying as failed with finished_at and a 'interrupted by restart' log note; have app.quit without force report running integrations; keep a child handle so shutdown can kill it (see the untimed-children finding).

v1.reason: The run is a detached thread (integration.rs:39-41), and shell() uses Command::output() (integration.rs:216-223) with no handle and no parent-death signal. Searching relay-core/src for `integrations` finds no reset in recovery or shutdown: the only writers are integration.rs and workspace.rs deletions. app.quit checks only live_pty_count (app.rs:38-41). integrations_live counts queued/merging/building/deploying (workspace.rs:387-391) and blocks project.remove (304-307, 'force or not') and workspace removal (166). integration.discard is UserOnly with no native-UI caller (apps/relay-native only uses integration.list/request). So a quit or crash mid-run leaves the row stuck in a live state permanently, blocks removal with an unsatisfiable hint, and leaves the fish child running as an orphan.
v1.correction: Downgraded from high to medium. The trigger is quitting or crashing during an integration run, which is a less common path. An escape exists, though not in the UI: a generic bus or CLI call of integration.discard. Fix: in recovery, mark queued/merging/building/deploying rows failed with finished_at and an 'interrupted by restart' log line, have app.quit without force report running integrations, and keep the child handle so shutdown can kill it.

findings.title: Integration deploy re-implements device.run without the device lease, ANDROID_SERIAL or the default Gradle install
findings.evidence: Deploy runs `shell(&path, command, Some(&device))` whose only device plumbing is `cmd.env("RELAY_DEVICE", device)` (lines 185-215, 228-234), and requires project.run_cmd (186-195: 'Deploy requested but no run command is configured.'). device.run first does `device_lease::check(ctx, &p.device, &holder)` and `device_lease::acquire(...)` (device.rs:150, 177), checks the device is ready, sets both RELAY_DEVICE and ANDROID_SERIAL (device.rs:1673) plus ANDROID_HOME, and with an empty run_cmd falls back to `./gradlew install<Variant>` (device.rs:1037-1055; the native project form labels an empty run command 'Gradle wrapper install task'). A run_cmd stored as "" makes integration deploy run `fish -lc ""` and report passed.
findings.impact: A builder agent can call integration.request with deploy (default allowlist): the install bypasses the lease that device_lease.rs exists to enforce, silently clobbering an APK another session is testing. Without ANDROID_SERIAL a configured `./gradlew installDebug` installs on every connected device (device_lease.rs:28 says exactly this) and adb fails with more than one device; projects relying on the default Gradle install can never deploy an integration.
findings.fix: Drop the bespoke deploy: once the build passes, start the existing device.run path with integration_id (resolve_run_root at device.rs:984 already accepts a passed integration's worktree), or at minimum share run_command/stream_command and take the lease with the requesting session as holder.

v1.reason: run() deploy (185-215) calls shell(&path, run_cmd, Some(device)) which only sets RELAY_DEVICE (231-233). device.run (device.rs:140-185) checks and acquires the device lease, requires the device to be ready, sets RELAY_DEVICE and ANDROID_SERIAL (device.rs:1673) and falls back to `./gradlew install<Variant>` when run_cmd is empty (run_command, device.rs:1037-1055). So an integration deploy takes no lease (device_lease.rs:1-18 exists precisely to stop installs clobbering another session's APK), a configured `./gradlew installDebug` installs on every connected device without ANDROID_SERIAL, and projects using the default Gradle install fail with 'Deploy requested but no run command is configured.' integration.request (with deploy) is in the builder default allowlist (settings.rs:36) while device.run is not, so this is the path an agent would use.
v1.correction: Downgrade to medium/bug: the native UI never sends deploy (code_git.rs:738), so only an agent via MCP/CLI reaches it, and the lease is a coordination mechanism rather than a security boundary. The run_cmd "" case is only reachable via a raw bus call: the native project form sends null for an empty field (registry.rs:926-931). Fix as proposed: after a passed build, start device.run with integration_id (resolve_run_root at device.rs:975 already accepts a passed integration) and the requesting session as lease holder.

findings.title: integration.request lets an agent act on any project_id, unlike handlers that refuse not_own("project")
findings.evidence: `let project = get_project(ctx.tx(), p.project_id)?;` and nothing compares it with the caller's session. guardrail::authorize only scopes payload fields named `session`/`task_id` (guardrail.rs:328-349) and fill_identity fills project_id only when omitted (engine.rs:1150-1165). notes::assert_actor_project (notes.rs:47-55), overlap.rs:68-79 and session.rs:195-204 all refuse a foreign project for agents; BUS.md §9.1 draws the agent boundary at the caller's own project.
findings.impact: A builder agent in project A passing project B's id creates worktrees and relay/integration-N branches in B's repository, runs B's build_cmd on B's branches and, with deploy, installs on a device, all audited as A's agent. integration.get/list return other projects' build log tails to agents, and ui.layout.save/delete (allow_ui) accept any project_id the same way.
findings.fix: Apply the notes::assert_actor_project check at the top of integration.request (and integration.get/list, ui.layout.*); better, enforce project_id scope once in guardrail::authorize for agent callers.

v1.reason: The default builder allowlist includes integration.request (settings.rs:36). The handler takes p.project_id at face value (integration.rs:17). fill_identity (engine.rs:1150-1169) fills project_id only when it is absent. guardrail::authorize (guardrail.rs:328-349) scopes only the `session` and `task_id` fields, then accepts any allowlisted op. So a builder in project A that passes B's id gets an integration worktree and branch in B's repo, B's build_cmd run, and optionally B's run_cmd with RELAY_DEVICE set. The run is audited under A's agent. Arbitrary revspecs are accepted via `branches` (rev_parse_single). integration.get/list are queries with no project check, so agents can read other projects' build log tails. notes.rs:47-55 shows the intended boundary (not_own("project")) and is enforced elsewhere.
v1.correction: Real-world impact is bounded. The agent cannot inject code into B through this path: it only merges B's existing refs and runs B's user-configured commands. Agents usually also have a shell as the same OS user, so this mainly gives cross-project build/deploy and log reads through the bus with mis-attributed audit, not a new code-execution primitive. Fix: enforce project_id scope for agent callers once in guardrail::authorize (compare payload project_id with session.project_id), or apply assert_actor_project in integration.request/get/list and ui.layout.*.

findings.title: Every merge failure is reported as a 'conflict' between the first two alphabetically sorted branches
findings.evidence: `branches.sort(); branches.dedup();` (line 26) discards the caller's order; then `if let Err(error) = worktree::git_mutate(&path, &merge_args) { let pair = integration.branches.first().cloned().zip(integration.branches.get(1).cloned()); fail(..., IntegrationState::Conflict, &format!("merge: {error}"), pair) }` (128-141). Octopus refusal, a branch deleted after validation, a failing pre-merge-commit hook and unrelated histories all become Conflict, and the pair is whatever sorts first. SPEC §8: 'Conflicts abort with the pair named.'
findings.impact: With three or more agents selected, the Code page (`#id · conflict · a, b`, code_git.rs:752-766) tells the user two agents conflict when the conflict is between others; non-conflict failures send the user to resolve a conflict that does not exist.
findings.fix: Keep the caller's order; distinguish conflicts (unmerged paths / CONFLICT in output) from other failures (state failed); to name the pair, merge the branches one at a time with --no-commit and record which branch failed against which, or test pairwise after an octopus failure.

v1.reason: integration.rs:26 sorts/dedups the branch list; 124-127 runs a single `git merge --no-ff --no-edit b1 b2 ...` (octopus onto base HEAD); on any Err (128) the pair is unconditionally branches[0], branches[1] and state is Conflict. With three or more branches the octopus strategy cannot tell which pair conflicted, so the named pair is merely the alphabetically first two; with two branches the conflict may be between the base and one branch. Any non-conflict merge failure (e.g. a branch ref deleted between validation at line 29 and the merge, a failing hook) is also labelled Conflict with a pair. The native Code page renders exactly '#id · conflict · a, b' (code_git.rs:753-766) and does not show log_tail, so the user sees only the wrong pair.
v1.correction: Sorting itself is harmless for octopus correctness; the defect is that the pair is fabricated. Fix: detect real conflicts (unmerged paths / CONFLICT lines) vs other errors (state failed), and find the pair by merging sequentially (or pairwise after an octopus failure) and recording which branch failed against which; show log_tail in the UI.

findings.title: Integration merge/build/deploy children are untimed, uncancellable, fully buffered, and survive discard
findings.evidence: `let out = cmd.output().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;` for `fish -lc <cmd>` (229-234); the merge goes through worktree::git_mutate, also a bare `.output()` (worktree.rs:27). No deadline, no process group, no handle kept; integration.discard has nothing to kill, and after a discard set_state returns Ok(()) silently (266-270) so run() proceeds to the next step. output() buffers the child's whole stdout+stderr before tail() keeps 12 KB.
findings.impact: A build or hook that hangs (waiting on a lock, device or prompt) leaves the integration building/deploying and its thread parked forever. Discarding a running build deletes the directory under cargo/gradle, which keep writing and recreate `.relay/integrations/<id>/target/...` outside any registered worktree, where nothing will ever remove it. A chatty long-running command grows engine memory without bound.
findings.fix: Model integrations like device runs: keep the Child (own process group) in a runtime map, stream output into a bounded ring buffer, enforce a configurable deadline, and have discard/shutdown kill the group before removing the worktree; make set_state signal 'discarded' so run() stops.

v1.reason: shell() (228-242) runs `fish -lc <cmd>` with bare Command::output(): no deadline, no process group, no stored handle; the merge goes through worktree::git (worktree.rs:26-33), also bare .output(). integration.discard (58-69) has nothing to kill and only removes the directory; set_state returns Ok(()) on discarded (266-270), so run() continues to the next step.
