I checked that the rebuild happens in normal use. render_projects (registry.rs:126-137) folds every session's (project_id, state) into the signature. apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:101-131) runs on every `session.changed`, updates sidebar_sessions and calls render_projects. The engine emits `session.changed` on every state change (session.rs:1424-1426, `if state_changed || provider_ref_changed { emit_session }`). So each agent state transition throws away every row and leaks one popover subtree per workspace header and per visible project row. The same file already shows the safe pattern at pages.rs:229 (`let pop = popover.downgrade();`). The registry_editor part also holds up. check (registry.rs:826-828) holds `save` strongly. save's clicked closure (912) holds name/branch/build/run/pinned strongly. Each entry's connect_changed handler (871-875) and pinned's notify handler (880-883) hold `check`. That makes save -> handler -> name -> handler -> check -> save, a cycle of GObjects that survives the panel being torn down. That leak is one per open of the settings sheet, so it is minor next to the sidebar one.
v1.correction: The rate is not measured. The per-popover cost is probably modest because the leaked popovers are never realized or measured, but the growth is unbounded and scales with (rows x agent state transitions), which fits the 'unbounded growth in normal use' rule for high. Fix: capture `popover.downgrade()` in the entry closures, as pages.rs:229 does, or build the popover lazily with MenuButton::set_create_popup_func. In registry_editor, capture `save` weakly inside `check`, or capture the inputs weakly in save's clicked closure. Not compiled or run: the leak follows from reading the code and from GTK4 dispose semantics.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. In registry.rs:505-512 every menu entry's clicked closure owns `pop = popover.clone()`, a strong reference. `key` is appended to `body` (504), and `popover.set_child(Some(&body))` (514) makes body the popover's child. That is a cycle: popover → body → key → closure → popover. `clear()` (app.rs:64-68) only calls `container.remove`, nothing calls run_dispose or disconnects these handlers, and registry_drag (shell.rs:38) and the row's other closures all hold weak references, so only the popover subtree survives. I checked the GTK side directly. A throwaway C program against the installed GTK 4.22.5 (the pinned version) builds the same structure: MenuButton → Popover → Box → 2 labels + 5 × (Button → Box → Image + Label), with a strong ref in each entry's clicked closure, then removes the row as clear() does. The MenuButton is finalized, but the popover (refcount 5, one per closure), its body and its buttons all survive: 2000 of 2000 leaked, about 76 KiB of heap each. The weak-ref version frees everything, with about 0.5 KiB per rebuild of noise.

(b) It fires in ordinary use. render_projects puts every session's (project_id, state) in the signature (127-132) and rebuilds the whole tree when it changes (133-137). apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:99-131) runs on every session.changed, and app.rs:1212-1229 does not filter out other projects' session events. The engine emits session.changed on every state change: report hooks (session.rs:1357-1426: tool_use/session_start → running, stop → idle, permission notification → blocked), and also typed input to an idle agent (engine.rs:1317-1343, mark_session_running). So every prompt and every turn end of any agent, in any project, leaks one popover subtree per workspace header (366) and per visible project row (439).

(c) Memory in the relay-native process grows without bound and is reclaimed only by a restart. The leaked widgets are detached, so they cost no CPU, and there is no functional error. In the model, a 10-row sidebar loses about 0.75 MB per agent state change. At an illustrative 100 transitions an hour (a few agents) that is about 75 MB an hour, or hundreds of MB to GBs over a long session. The engine is a separate process (relay-native does not depend on relay-core), so agents and data survive if the client is eventually killed.

(d) High is right: this is unbounded growth in normal use, and the magnitude is material. It is not critical: there is no data loss and the engine is unaffected.

(e) The weak capture (`popover.downgrade()` or `glib::clone!(#[weak] popover)`) is correct and complete for registry_menu, and the experiment confirms the weak variant frees the whole subtree. The Action closures hold only JSON, the id and a Weak<Ui>. The registry_editor part also holds: save's clicked closure (912-913) holds name/branch/build/run/pinned strongly, their changed/notify handlers (873, 885) hold `check`, and `check` holds `save` strongly (828). That cycle outlives Panel::close's clear(body); the Panel itself is dropped because every closure holds it weakly. It leaks about a dozen widgets per open of the settings sheet. Making `save` weak inside `check` is enough to break it.
v2.correction:
Details:
- The safe example is at pages.rs:228, not 229.
- The workspace menu holds 3 JSON clones (470) and the project menu 2 (478).
- Another source of session.changed: engine.rs:1317-1343, where input to an idle agent marks it running.

Impact, measured rather than guessed: in a C reproduction on GTK 4.22.5, each leaked menu subtree costs about 76 KiB of heap. Each rebuild loses about 75 KiB × (workspace headers + visible project rows); the Rust closures and JSON clones come on top of that. This is still a model of the app, not a measurement of the app.

Fix: `set_create_popup_func` is an optimisation, not a substitute for the weak capture. GTK calls it on every activation, so it must build only when `menu.popover().is_none()`, and the popover it builds still needs weak captures in its entry closures.

Related sites with the same root cause, not listed in the finding: agent_menu.rs agent_settings_body captures `popover.clone()` strongly in closures on its own children. These are brief (451), save (541), start-fresh confirm (578) and close confirm (608). The closed handler (370-373) unparents that popover, but the cycle keeps the whole subtree alive, so every open and close of an agent's settings leaks it. That happens once per user click, which is less often, and the same fix applies.

Separate issue, not counted here: the rebuild disposes the MenuButton of an open ⋯ menu, so the menu disappears under the user whenever any agent changes state. Building the menu lazily does not fix this; only avoiding the full rebuild does.

findings.title: Switching project with an explicit page (Files and Git, dashboard rows, notifications) is undone by the per-project layout restore
findings.evidence: open_project (24-36) sets restored_project=0, spawns refresh(), and then calls navigate(page). navigate's save_layout bumps layout_revision (app.rs:1358 → shell.rs:287-288). The refresh future only runs later, and captures the revision at that point (app.rs:1371). So restore_layout's guard `if self.layout_revision.get() != revision` (327, 338) never sees that explicit navigation. After session.list and settings.get, apply_layout ends with `self.navigate(page)` to the saved page (398-402). The saved page cannot express Files: self.page is "agents" for both views, and editor.layout_state (project_files.rs:38-41) stores only pane visibility and widths. navigate("agents") always calls editor.show_agents() (app.rs:1350-1356), and navigate also runs dismiss_panels().
findings.impact: In project A, choosing "Files and Git" from project B's ⋯ menu (registry.rs:481) shows Files, then flips back to B's agent wall a couple of round trips later. These all land on the project's last saved page instead of the requested one: dashboard hold rows (tools.rs:373, "guardrails"), review rows (tools.rs:412, "board" + open_task), and notification clicks (notification_center.rs:310). A task panel opened in that window is either closed by dismiss_panels or ends up over the wrong page. The editor tree and git status are also loaded twice. This is exactly what the comment at 337 says must not happen. No test covers it: roadmap_smoke.rs:239 passes "files", which navigate silently ignores.
findings.fix: Make an explicit destination win over the restore. One option: read the revision in open_project before calling navigate and store it as the restore baseline, so restore_layout applies `page` only if nothing navigated since the switch. Another: pass the requested page into restore_layout/apply_layout and apply only mode, columns, order, split and project_tools. Also persist Files vs Agents in the layout, so restoring "agents" does not force show_agents().

v1.reason: Traced it. In shell.rs:24-35, open_project sets project=B and restored_project=0, then calls self.refresh(). That refresh() is glib::spawn_future_local, which is deferred to the main loop, not polled synchronously. Next, navigate(page) runs at shell.rs:36. Its save_layout (app.rs:1358 -> shell.rs:287-288) bumps layout_revision and then returns early because restored_project (0) != B. The refresh future only reads layout_revision when it runs (app.rs:1371), which is after that bump. It awaits session.list and calls restore_layout(revision) (app.rs:1439). In restore_layout, restored_project != B, and the revision check at shell.rs:327 passes because nothing has changed since the capture. It awaits settings.get, and the guard at shell.rs:338 passes too. Then apply_layout (shell.rs:349) ends with navigate(saved page) at shell.rs:402, with applying_ui set. The saved page cannot say "code": layout_state stores self.page, which is "agents" for both views, and editor.layout_state (project_files.rs:38-41) stores only pane visibility and widths. So navigate("agents") takes files=false and calls editor.show_agents() (app.rs:1350-1356). When the saved page differs from the requested one, navigate also calls dismiss_panels(), which closes the task panel opened by tools.rs:412-416 or the notification task.get path. Callers that pass an explicit page are registry.rs:481 ("code"), tools.rs:373 ("guardrails"), tools.rs:412 ("board"), tools.rs:534, tools.rs:640, notification_center.rs:310 and pages.rs:238. Each saved state comes from the last navigation in that project, so a project you have used before almost always has a saved page, usually "agents". The comment at shell.rs:337 states the opposite intent. The test at roadmap_smoke.rs:239 passes "files", which navigate drops because no content child has that name (app.rs:1317), so the Files path is never exercised.
v1.correction: Mechanism as stated. The fix should make the requested destination survive. One option: in open_project, after navigate, set a 'restore baseline' that makes restore_layout skip the saved page. Another: pass the requested page through and apply only mode, columns, order, split, sidebar and project_tools. In both cases, persist Files vs Agents in the layout. Finding #5 is the opposite race: when a refresh is already in flight during the switch, the explicit page wins but B's layout is overwritten. Both should be fixed together around one 'restore pending for project X, baseline revision R' state.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. I traced it at 361c6f9. In shell.rs:24-34, open_project sets project=B and restored_project=0, then calls refresh(). refresh() goes through glib::spawn_future_local (app.rs:1368). In glib 0.22.9 that attaches a TaskSource whose first poll happens on a later main-loop dispatch (main_context_futures.rs:230-233 sets ready_time 0), not synchronously. navigate(page) at shell.rs:36 then runs save_layout (app.rs:1358). save_layout bumps layout_revision unconditionally (shell.rs:287-288) and returns early because restored_project != B. The future reads the already-bumped revision at app.rs:1371. Between that read and the checks at 327/338, nothing bumps it again: every save_layout caller is a click, a key or navigate, and render_projects, reconcile, layout, update_attachments and refresh_page never call it. So restore_layout passes both guards, and apply_layout runs navigate(saved page) at shell.rs:402. The saved page can never be "code", because navigate rewrites it to "agents" before storing (app.rs:1315, and 1348 is the only writer of page). The project_tools state holds only pane visibility and widths (project_files.rs:38-41). navigate("agents") therefore calls show_agents() (app.rs:1355), and on a page change it also calls dismiss_panels() (app.rs:1316). Layouts do persist: native.layout.current.N passes valid_path, and settings.set accepts any path (settings.rs:58-66, 216-224).

(b) The trigger fires whenever the user switches to another project with an explicit destination, and that project already has a saved layout. Any earlier navigation in that project saves one, and every restore saves it again. In normal use that means:
- The board's own project picker (board_view.rs:513 -> pages.rs:238, open_project(B,"board")). This is the most common case: picking another project while on the Board bounces the user to B's agents wall when B was last left on agents.
- "Files and Git" in the ⋯ menu (registry.rs:481). This always fails for a project with a saved layout.
- Dashboard hold rows (tools.rs:373) and review rows (tools.rs:412).
- Portfolio cards (tools.rs:534).
- The notifications page (tools.rs:640) and the notification window (notification_center.rs:310).
Normally no refresh is already in flight, because session.changed events are applied in place (agent_menu.rs:99-137). The in-flight case is the opposite race, #5.

(c) The requested page shows for about two bus round trips, then flips to the saved page. A task panel opened by a review row or notification is either closed by dismiss_panels or lands over the wrong page, because task_pages::open makes three calls before showing it. The notification window's set_mode("focus") on the notified session (notification_center.rs:321-326) is also undone, because apply_layout overwrites mode and focused. The restore navigates with applying_ui set, so sync_navigation does not run, and the engine's recorded page stays at the requested one while the window shows another. No data is lost. A second click works, because it is then a same-project navigate.

(d) Under the rubric this is "likely user-visible wrong behavior in a normal flow" and fits high. It sits at the low end of high: there is no data, safety or hang impact. The comment at shell.rs:337 shows the intent was that a restore must never undo navigation. roadmap_smoke.rs:239 passes "files", which returns at app.rs:1319-1320, so the Files path is never exercised.

(e) The proposed fix direction is right but needs care; see the correction.
v2.correction:
Add the board's project picker (board_view.rs:513 -> pages.rs:238) to the triggers. It is the most frequent one. Also add the facets from (c): the notification focus mode is lost, and the engine's page state diverges from what the window shows.

Fix option 1 is wrong as written. If open_project captures a pre-navigate baseline, the existing guard at shell.rs:327-329 returns before anything is applied and calls save_layout(). That would overwrite B's saved mode, columns, order and split with A's on every switch, because open_project always navigates. The baseline must gate only the page field. In practice that makes option 2 the correct shape: restore mode, columns, focused, order, split and project_tools, and skip the page when an explicit destination was requested.

Two further points for the fix:
- editor.apply_layout can hide the file sidebar that show_files just revealed (project_files.rs:43-45 vs 21). For an explicit "code", call show_files again after applying, or keep the tree visible.
- The sidebar rows and "Open agents" also pass "agents" explicitly (registry.rs:283, 416, 480). The API needs an Option<page>, so that a plain switch can still restore the saved page.

Persisting Files vs Agents is an optional improvement, not needed to fix this bug. Fix it together with #5 through one "restore pending for project X" state.

findings.title: Agent-skills switch: reverting it re-fires state-set, which hides errors and loops skill.enable forever on a persistent failure
findings.evidence: 873-888: `toggle.connect_state_set(move |key,on| { ... key.set_sensitive(false); spawn(async { match ui.call("skill.enable", json!({.."enabled":on})).await { Ok(_) => feedback.set_visible(false), Err(error) => { key.set_active(!on); feedback.set_text(..); feedback.set_visible(true); } } key.set_sensitive(true); }); Proceed })`. GtkSwitch::set_active emits state-set again. Both other copies of this switch guard against exactly that, with the comment "A rejected write restores the switch while it is disabled" and `if !key.is_sensitive() { return Proceed; }` (tools_plugins.rs:122-125, tools_market.rs:717-720). This copy has no guard, so the revert re-enters the handler and sends skill.enable with enabled:!on. Persistent failures exist: skill.enable returns not_found for both values when the project or skill is gone (provider.rs:193-194), and ui.call fails immediately with Disconnected while the engine is down (app.rs:1112). skill.enable is a Mutation with Audit::Always (registry.rs:117 in relay-bus), and a refused non-Invalid mutation gets its own audit transaction (engine.rs:1073-1075).
findings.impact: (1) After any one-off failure, such as the 30 s Timeout, the revert's own request succeeds and its Ok branch hides the error just shown. The switch snaps back with no explanation. (2) On a persistent failure the handler and the error branch call each other forever. Triggers: toggling while the engine is disconnected, or after another client removed the project or skill. The switch flickers and the GTK thread spins. With an engine connected, every iteration is a refused, audited write, so audit rows grow without bound and the store mutex stays busy. The in-flight futures own the switch, so the loop survives closing the panel. After a disconnect, the first call that succeeds on reconnect persists whichever value the loop happened to be on, not the user's choice.
findings.fix: Reuse the guarded helper (tools_market.rs's switch is already generic over enable_op and id_key), or add the same `if !key.is_sensitive() { return Proceed }` guard. Cleaner: return Propagation::Stop from state-set and call `key.set_state(on)` only once the engine answers, so a failure never writes `active` back.

v1.reason: apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:873-887: the skills switch's state-set handler disables the key, spawns skill.enable with `enabled:on`, and in the Err arm calls `key.set_active(!on)` while the key is still insensitive. gtk_switch_set_active emits state-set, and the handler has no guard, so it re-enters and sends skill.enable with the reverted value. The two sibling copies have exactly the guard this one lacks: `if !key.is_sensitive() { return Proceed }`, with the comment "A rejected write restores the switch while it is disabled" (tools_plugins.rs:122-125, tools_market.rs:717-720). That shows the author knew about the re-emission. Consequences: (1) after a one-off failure, the revert's own request usually succeeds, and its Ok arm hides the error that was just shown. (2) On a persistent failure, the Err arm and the handler keep calling each other. ui.call returns Error::Disconnected at once when there is no client (app.rs:1112), and SkillEnable returns not_found for a missing project or skill whatever the value of `enabled` (provider.rs:193-194). A not_found refusal is not ErrorKind::Invalid, so engine.rs:1072-1075 writes an audit row in its own transaction for every iteration. The spawned futures hold clones of the switch, so the loop outlives the panel.
v1.correction: Calibrated down from high. The infinite loop needs an uncommon trigger: toggling while the engine is down or reconnecting, or after the skill or project was deleted while the sheet is open. It is not a UI freeze. Each iteration yields to the main loop, so the result is one core spinning and a flickering switch (Disconnected case), or audit rows growing without bound until the app exits (not_found case). The hidden error after a transient failure is the common, milder symptom. Fix: use crate::tools::plugins::switch-style guarding (`if !key.is_sensitive() { return Proceed }`), or better, return Propagation::Stop and call key.set_state(on) only on Ok.

findings.title: Sidebar stores its rebuild key as the projects_box widget name; GTK interns each key as a permanent GQuark, and any agent state change rebuilds the whole tree
findings.evidence: 127-137: `let signature = format!("{active}:{}:{}:{:?}:{collapsed:?}:{expanded:?}:{query}", serde_json::to_string(&projects).., serde_json::to_string(&workspaces).., sessions.iter().map(|s| (s["project_id"].as_i64(), text(s, "state")..)).collect::<Vec<_>>()); if self.projects_box.widget_name() == signature { return; } self.projects_box.set_widget_name(&signature); clear(&self.projects_box);`. gtk_widget_set_name interns the name as a GQuark (the CSS node id), and quarks are never freed. I verified this with a scratch PyGObject experiment against the installed GTK 4.22.5: after set_name, GLib.quark_try_string(name) is non-zero, and it stays non-zero after renaming and dropping the widget. The key embeds every project row (including updated_at, protected_paths and critical_files) and the state of every session in every project. render_projects runs on every session.changed (agent_menu.rs:131), which the engine emits on each running/idle/blocked transition (session.rs:1424-1426).
findings.impact: Each distinct sidebar state leaks a full copy of the serialized registry (several KB) into the process-wide quark table for the life of the app. Growth slows down only while projects and session lists stay unchanged. Each state change also rebuilds every row: an open ⋯ menu disappears under the cursor, keyboard focus in the sidebar is dropped, hover tools flicker, and every row's popover is rebuilt (and leaked, per the registry_menu finding). The full registry is also re-serialized on the GTK thread for every session event.
findings.fix: Keep the cache key in the `Sidebar` thread-local (or as a u64 hash) instead of the widget name. Derive it from what is actually rendered: ids, names, pinned, order, and per-project open/held/running. Then a running/idle change that does not change a lamp does nothing. Update lamps on existing rows instead of rebuilding them.

v1.reason: shell/registry.rs:127-137 builds a signature string from the serialized projects and workspaces plus the (project_id, state) of every sidebar session, and stores it with projects_box.set_widget_name. I reproduced the interning against the installed GTK 4.22.5 with PyGObject. After Box.set_name(s), set_name('other') and dropping the widget, GLib.quark_try_string(s) is non-zero, so the full string is interned for the life of the process. render_projects runs on every session.changed (agent_menu.rs:131). Any change in the signature calls clear(&self.projects_box) and rebuilds every row, including each row's MenuButton and Popover (registry.rs:449-515). An open project menu therefore vanishes whenever any agent in any project changes state, which happens on every turn with many agents running.
v1.correction: The memory growth is slower than implied. A new quark is created only for a never-before-seen signature, and repeated running/idle flips of the same session set reuse existing quarks. New strings come from session create/close, active-project changes, fold changes and each keystroke in the sidebar filter (the query is in the key). Project updated_at changes only on project.update (workspace.rs:276). The leak itself is low severity. The more user-visible cost is the full rebuild on every state flip, which dismisses open menus and drops focus; that is what justifies medium. Fix: keep a u64 hash in the Sidebar thread-local instead of the widget name, and update the per-project lamps in place instead of rebuilding the tree.

findings.title: A refresh in flight across a project switch saves the old layout over the new project's saved layout, which is then never restored
findings.evidence: refresh captures layout_revision at the top of each iteration (app.rs:1371). It calls restore_layout(revision) only after awaiting project.list/workspace.list and session.list (app.rs:1373-1439). restore_layout reads self.project only when it starts (322). Suppose the user switches to P2 during those awaits. open_project has set restored_project=0 (33), and its navigate has bumped the revision. The stale iteration then calls restored_project.set(P2) (326), sees `layout_revision != revision`, and calls save_layout() (327-329). save_layout now passes its restored_project == P2 check and persists the current state as native.layout.current.P2. The next iteration returns early at 323 because restored_project == P2. The same happens when settings.get fails (341): restored_project is already set, so the next save overwrites a layout that was never applied.
findings.impact: Clicking project A then project B quickly permanently replaces B's remembered mode, columns, focused agent, split and page with A's (or the startup defaults). Clicking a project during the startup refresh does the same, and it is more likely when the store mutex is busy with many agents. B's real saved layout is never read.
findings.fix: Pass the iteration's project into restore_layout, and return without touching restored_project when it differs from self.project. On a failed read, reset restored_project so the next refresh retries. If the user edited the layout during the read, merge that edit into the stored layout instead of overwriting all of it.

v1.reason: Reproduced by reading the code. A refresh iteration captures layout_revision r (app.rs:1371) and awaits session.list. During that await, open_project(B) sets project=B and restored_project=0 (shell.rs:24,33). Its refresh() call only sets dirty, because refresh_pending is already true, and its navigate bumps the revision. The stale iteration resumes. The session.list result is discarded by the project check at app.rs:1427 (`Ok(_) => {}`), but restore_layout(r) still runs at app.rs:1439. restore_layout reads project=B at shell.rs:322, sets restored_project=B at 326, sees the revision mismatch at 327 and calls save_layout(). save_layout now passes its check at shell.rs:290 and queues settings.set native.layout.current.B with the current layout_state. That state is still A's mode, columns, split, focused agent and sidebar, plus the new page; nothing has applied B's saved state. The next iteration returns at shell.rs:323 because restored_project == B, so B's real layout is never read. The startup case happens the same way if the user clicks a project during the first project.list/session.list. The settings.get failure path is also as described: restored_project is set at 326 before the read, and an Err leaves it set with nothing applied (shell.rs:341). That path needs an engine error, so it is rare. The window is one or two bus round trips. That makes it reachable but not frequent, and what is lost is a UI preference, not user data.
v1.correction: Primary site: the stale-iteration path is shell.rs:322-329 together with app.rs:1439, which calls restore_layout without checking that the iteration's project is still current. Fix: capture the project with the revision at the top of the iteration and pass both in. If self.project differs, return without touching restored_project. Reset restored_project to 0 when settings.get fails. A layout edit made before the restore should apply on top of the stored layout rather than replace it.

findings.title: Focus-mode tabs show stale agent lamps: they are rebuilt only by layout(), which a state change does not call
findings.evidence: The tab strip and its lamps are built only inside layout() (162-203): `match text(session, "state") { "running" | "spawning" => lamp.add_css_class("live"), "blocked" => ..("held"), "restorable" => ..("waiting"), _ => () }`. reconcile (app.rs:1508-1513) calls layout() only when the order changed or a pane was created (`if *self.ordered.borrow() != names || created { ..layout() } else { self.update_attachments() }`). So a session.changed event that only changes state never updates the tabs.
findings.impact: In focus mode, when another agent goes from running to blocked ("NEEDS YOU") or finishes, its tab keeps the old lamp. It updates only when something else calls layout(): a navigation, a mode change, or a new pane. The tabs are the only per-agent status visible in focus mode, so an agent waiting on the user is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Move the tab strip into its own function and call it from reconcile whenever a rendered session signature changed, or update the lamp classes of the existing tabs in place. This also splits up the 129-line layout().

v1.reason: The focus tabs and their lamps are built only in layout() (shell.rs:162-203). A session.changed event goes through apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:99-137) and then reconcile (app.rs:1448). For a state-only change the names are the same and no pane is created, so reconcile calls update_attachments (app.rs:1567-1584), which only toggles set_active. layout() is not called, and a tab's lamp keeps its old state class until something else calls layout().
v1.correction: Downgraded from medium. The tabs are not the only place this status shows in focus mode. render_status_counts (status.rs:9-30) runs on every reconcile and shows a 'needs you' count of blocked sessions. agent_blocked notifications also flag a blocked agent (notification_center.rs:210). Tabs exist only in focus mode with more than one agent, which narrows it further. Fix: in reconcile, rebuild the tabs (or update their lamp classes in place) when a session's rendered signature changes.

findings.title: Window shortcuts run in the Capture phase, so Ctrl+K and Ctrl+N never reach agent terminals
findings.evidence: `keys.set_propagation_phase(gtk::PropagationPhase::Capture)` is set on the window. The handler returns Stop for any DEFAULTS chord (shortcuts.rs:3-11: Ctrl+K palette, Ctrl+1/2/3, Ctrl+N new session, Ctrl+,). Capture handlers on the window run before the focused vte4::Terminal sees the key. The only exemption is that no panel is open (1073).
findings.impact: With the cursor in an agent's terminal, Ctrl+K opens the command palette instead of reaching the terminal (readline/emacs kill-to-end-of-line, nano cut). Ctrl+N opens the launch sheet instead (readline next-history, vim completion). Neither control byte can be sent to the PTY while the default bindings are in place. Only Ctrl+Shift+B is terminal-safe, matching the terminal's own Ctrl+Shift+C/V (terminal.rs:263-276).
findings.fix: When the focus widget is a vte4::Terminal, skip chords that are valid terminal input. Alternatively, move the controller to the Bubble phase so the terminal handles keys first, or change the defaults to Ctrl+Shift chords.

v1.reason: shell.rs:1065-1100 adds an EventControllerKey to the main window in PropagationPhase::Capture. It returns Stop for any chord in shortcuts::DEFAULTS (shortcuts.rs:3-11: Ctrl+K palette, Ctrl+N new_session, Ctrl+1/2/3, Ctrl+,). The only exemption is an open panel (1073). Capture handlers run from the window down before the focused widget, so the vte4::Terminal in an agent pane never receives Ctrl+K or Ctrl+N. Its own controller (terminal.rs:261-279) only claims Ctrl+Shift+C/V. No DECISIONS or docs entry says this is intended. The Notes window installs its own controller on a separate window (notes_window.rs:40), so it is not affected.
v1.correction: Mitigation: the chords can be rebound or emptied in Settings > Keyboard (tools_settings.rs keybindings.*), so the user can work around it. The same capture also steals these chords from the Code page's GtkSourceView, which is arguably desired there. Fix: skip the global chords when the focus widget is a vte4::Terminal, unless the chord is Ctrl+Shift. Alternatively, default to Ctrl+Shift chords.

findings.title: load_appearance re-fetches and re-decodes the wallpaper on the GTK thread for every appearance setting change, and one Settings save runs it 5-7 times
findings.evidence: Each call does all of this: reads six settings; calls wallpaper_rotation::refresh, which fetches appearance.wallpapers (up to 1.5 MB) and runs `library.to_string()` plus a hash on the GTK thread (wallpaper_rotation.rs:59-64, 92-104); base64-decodes the wallpaper and decodes it with gdk::Texture::from_bytes on the GTK thread (1219-1237); reloads the app-wide CSS provider (1212); and reapplies every pane's appearance (1241-1244). app.rs:1257-1262 calls it for every settings.changed whose path starts with "appearance." or is terminal.font_size. settings.set always emits settings.changed (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:217-224). The Settings page's Save writes every control, changed or not (tools_settings.rs:606 collect_settings). There is no coalescing and no revision check (only generation), so overlapping runs can apply out of order.
findings.impact: One Save on the Settings page triggers about 5-7 full appearance reloads. Each one re-downloads the unchanged wallpaper and library, re-decodes the wallpaper on the main thread, and restyles the whole window, which shows up as visible jank. It also adds 5-7 rounds of large library and wallpaper reads on the engine's single store connection, delaying other requests.
findings.fix: Coalesce runs the way refresh() does (pending/dirty flags). Use the value carried in the settings.changed payload for the path that changed. Remember the applied wallpaper string (or its hash) and skip decoding when it is unchanged. Decode off the main thread (rt.spawn_blocking; gdk::Texture can be created off-thread). Share one decoder with tools_settings.rs:1022 wallpaper_texture, which duplicates this decode.

v1.reason: load_appearance (shell.rs:1116-1246) calls wallpaper_rotation::refresh, which issues two settings.get calls, one of them for the whole appearance.wallpapers library. It then runs six settings.gets and, on the GTK thread, base64-decodes the wallpaper and runs gdk::Texture::from_bytes. It also reloads the app-wide CSS provider and reapplies every pane's appearance. app.rs:1257-1262 calls it for every settings.changed whose path starts with appearance. or is terminal.font_size, and SettingsSet always emits settings.changed (settings.rs:218-224). The Settings Save button (tools_settings.rs:115-150) sends one settings.set per control, sequentially and whether or not it changed: appearance.mode, panel_alpha, wallpaper_dim, content_contrast, wallpaper_rotation.enabled, wallpaper_rotation.interval_minutes and terminal.font_size. That is about 7 full reloads, each decoding the same wallpaper on the main thread and restyling the window. Only refresh() has a revision check. load_appearance itself checks only generation.
v1.correction: Calibrated down to low. The trigger is a Settings Save, an infrequent deliberate action, and the cost is a one-off stall of a few hundred ms, not ongoing jank. The sliders do not write live (value-changed only updates the label). The engine-side cost is a handful of small settings reads, not meaningful store contention. Out-of-order application is unlikely, because each run starts after its own set and the last run reads the final state. Fix: coalesce runs with a pending/dirty flag or a revision like refresh(), and skip the texture decode when the wallpaper string is unchanged.

findings.title: The native layout key native.layout.current.{id} differs from the engine's layout.current.{id}, so it is never cleaned up and a reused project id inherits it
findings.evidence: save_layout and restore_layout use `native.layout.current.{project}` (308, 334). The engine deletes `layout.current.{id}` on project.remove (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:378-379), and ui.layout.save's fallback reads `layout.current.{id}` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:32-40). DECISIONS D150 also says a page switch persists `layout.current.<id>`. projects.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT (crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:51-52), so removing the newest project frees its id for the next project added.
findings.impact: Removed projects leave their layout rows behind. A project added after removing the newest one inherits that project's page, mode, columns, split and sidebar. ui.layout.save without a state (from the phone or CLI) saves the engine default instead of the desktop's current layout.
findings.fix: Use one key everywhere. Either have the client write layout.current.{id} (the engine already deletes it and reads it in fallback_state), or have project.remove also delete native.layout.current.{id}.

v1.reason: The client reads and writes `native.layout.current.{project}` (shell.rs:308, 334). project.remove deletes only `layout.current.{id}` (workspace.rs:378-379), and ui.rs:32-40 fallback_state reads `layout.current.{id}`. projects.id is `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` without AUTOINCREMENT (store.rs:51), so removing the newest project frees its id. A project added next gets that id, and restore_layout then reads the removed project's page, mode, columns, split and project_tools. The native rows are also never cleaned up.
v1.correction: The engine side is broken too. settings.set stores leaf rows (settings.rs:203-213 flatten), so a layout object lives at `layout.current.N.page` and similar paths. project.remove deletes only `path = 'layout.current.N'`, without the LIKE subtree that it uses for guardrails, so it would miss those rows even if the client used that key. Also, nothing in the source writes `layout.current.*`: only tests/bus.rs does, and the PageSwitch handler in ui.rs does not persist it. That contradicts D150 ('A page switch persists layout.current.<id>'), and fallback_state always returns its default. Fix: have project.remove delete the subtree of both keys (or of one shared key), and align D150 with the code.

findings.title: Sidebar drag reorder rewrites every sibling's order with N sequential updates; a mid-way failure leaves the order half-applied
findings.evidence: 105-126: `for (order, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() { ... ui.call(if workspace {"workspace.update"} else {"project.update"}, payload).await ... Err(e) => { ui.show_error(..); break; } }`. Every item in the group is sent, including those whose order did not change. Each update emits project.changed or workspace.changed, and each event sets registry_dirty and calls refresh (app.rs:1223-1225). Each update also records its own undo entry (workspace.rs:281-285).
findings.impact: Dragging within a workspace of N projects means N round trips with the sidebar insensitive, N events, several full re-lists, and repeated tree rebuilds (each of which leaks, per the other findings). If a call fails part-way, some items are renumbered and others are not, which leaves duplicate order values and an order scrambled by id tie-breaks.
findings.fix: Send only the items whose order changed (usually a contiguous range). Better: add a single reorder op that writes all orders in one transaction and emits one event.

v1.reason: shell.rs:105-126 loops over every item in the group and awaits one workspace.update/project.update per item, sending unchanged orders too, and stops with `break` on the first error. ProjectUpdate (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:265-288) is a separate transaction each time. Each call writes its own set_undo entry and emits project.changed, and app.rs:1223-1225 sets registry_dirty and calls refresh() for every project./workspace. event. A failure part-way leaves some items renumbered and others not, and the `ORDER BY pinned DESC, ord, id` tie-break then decides the order. With the usual small N the cost is modest, and a mid-loop failure needs an engine error or a lost connection, so this stays low.
v1.correction: There is also a user-visible cost the finding leaves out. One drag records N undo entries, so undoing a drag takes N undos, each one restoring a single item. The claim that each tree rebuild leaks rests on other findings and was not checked here. Fix: send only the items whose order changed. Better, add one reorder op that writes all orders in a single transaction with one undo entry and one event.

findings.title: sheet() ignores its height argument, and one commit's "taller popover" change edited only that dead argument
findings.evidence: 135-144: `pub(super) fn sheet(&self, title: &str, width: i32, _height: i32) -> Option<(Rc<Panel>, gtk::Box)> { let panel = Panel::toggle(self, title, width)?; let body = panel.body.clone(); Some((panel, body)) }`. All six callers pass a height that is discarded: shell.rs:465, 782, 904, 1004, registry.rs:702 and agent_menu.rs:459. Commit 304ab0f ("a taller popover") changed project_plugins' call from 560 to 640, which did nothing; the real height comes from panel.top/min_height.
findings.impact: The parameter misleads readers, and has already wasted one fix. The wrapper adds indirection over Panel::toggle, whose body field is already pub.
findings.fix: Delete the wrapper and call Panel::toggle directly (or at least drop the unused parameter), and set heights through compact/top/min_height as the callers already do.

v1.reason: shell.rs:135-144: `sheet(&self, title, width, _height)` passes only title and width to Panel::toggle and discards the height. All six callers pass a height (shell.rs:465, 782, 904, 1004; registry.rs:702 passes 0; agent_menu.rs:459). The parameter misleads readers.
v1.correction: The claim that commit 304ab0f's taller-popover fix did nothing is wrong. That commit changed `panel.top(560)` to `panel.top(640)` as well as the sheet() argument, so the popover did get taller. Changing the sheet() argument was only redundant. Fix: drop the unused parameter, or inline Panel::toggle.

findings.title: project_skills and project_plugins duplicate the same sheet scaffolding, the copies have diverged, and the plugins doc comment is stale
findings.evidence: 780-901 and 903-1002 repeat about 50 lines: the project-name lookup (787-793 / 911-917), the uppercase section label, the intro, the "Loading…" list, the feedback label, a footer whose manage key closes the panel and navigates, present(), and a spawned list call with clear/rows/error handling. The copies have already diverged: skills calls fit() while plugins sets min_height(460), and skills builds its own unguarded switch while plugins uses tools::plugins::switch. The doc comment at 902 says the plugins sheet is "opened from its row in the sidebar", but commit 304ab0f removed that row key; the only caller (app.rs:855) passes the current project.
findings.impact: Fixes land in one copy only. The unguarded skills switch (reported separately) is a direct result. The stale comment and the now-unneeded `project` parameter mislead readers.
findings.fix: Extract one helper parameterized by title, intro, list op, row builder and manage page, and build both rows with the shared switch helper. Correct the doc comment.

v1.reason: shell.rs:780-901 (project_skills) and 903-1002 (project_plugins) repeat the same scaffolding: the project-name lookup, the uppercased section label, the intro, the Loading list, the feedback label, the footer with a manage key that closes the panel and navigates, present(), and a spawned list call. The doc comment at 902 still says the sheet is "opened from its row in the sidebar". Commit 304ab0f removed that call site (`-ui.project_plugins(id)`) and moved the key to the top bar, so the only caller is app.rs:855 `ui.project_plugins(ui.project.get())`. The real harm from the divergence is the unguarded skills switch, reported as native-shell#3.
v1.correction: One listed divergence is deliberate, not drift. Commit 304ab0f's message explains that plugins uses min_height(460) because its list arrives after the panel opens. Do not cite that as an example of the copies diverging. The worthwhile part is to build the skills row with a shared guarded switch helper and to correct the doc comment. A full shared sheet helper has a modest payoff.

findings.title: Window presets for focus, review and mosaic overwrite the grid column count
findings.evidence: The presets include ("focus", "Focus + tabs", 1), ("review", ..., 2) and ("mosaic", ..., 2) (479-486). Every preset's click handler runs `ui.columns.set(columns); ui.set_mode(mode);` (543-544). columns only affects grid mode (layout() 221-234), and it is persisted in layout_state (319).
findings.impact: Choosing "Focus + tabs" sets the grid to one column. Leaving focus with a pane's zoom key (agent_menu.rs:328 switches to "grid") then gives a vertical stack instead of the user's two- or three-column grid. Review and mosaic reset a three-column grid to two.
findings.fix: Set columns only for the grid presets.

v1.reason: Confirmed at shell.rs:541-544: every preset's handler runs `ui.columns.set(columns); ui.set_mode(mode);`. The focus preset sets columns=1, and review and mosaic set 2. columns is read only for grid mode (shell.rs:220-233); focus forces cols=1 and review/mosaic use fixed 1/2 columns in wall_right. So the write only matters after a later switch to grid. The pane zoom key (agent_menu.rs:328) switches back to "grid" without touching columns, and the result is a 1-column stack after the Focus preset was used. columns is also persisted by save_layout. The preset's selected-state check (shell.rs:532) already ignores columns for non-grid modes, which shows columns is meant to be grid-only.
v1.correction: Only set columns when mode == "grid". The impact is cosmetic: the grid can be restored with one click on a grid preset.

findings.title: A deleted window preset stays in the open presets list, and delete has no confirmation
findings.evidence: The saved-preset rows are built once from ui.layout.list (605-633). The delete key calls `ui.mutate("ui.layout.delete", ..)`, whose success path only calls ui.refresh() and refresh_page() (app.rs:1118-1129). The layout.changed "deleted" event falls through to refresh_page and never touches the sheet. Unlike other destructive keys, delete is not wrapped in confirm_inline.
findings.impact: After a delete, the preset still appears in the list. Clicking it, or deleting it again, shows a "no layout" error banner. One misclick deletes a preset with no confirmation.
findings.fix: Remove the row (or rebuild the list) when the delete succeeds, and wrap the delete key in confirm_inline.

v1.reason: The saved rows are built once from ui.layout.list (shell.rs:605-633). The delete key calls ui.mutate (app.rs:1118-1129), whose success path only calls refresh() and refresh_page(). The layout.changed event is acted on only when action=="applied" (app.rs:1241-1244). So the row of a deleted preset stays in the open sheet, and clicking it calls ui.layout.apply, which returns ui.layout_not_found (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:240) and shows an error banner. The missing confirmation is accurate. The engine does record an undo for ui.layout.delete (ui.rs:257), but the native client exposes undo only on the board (board_view.rs:872), so the user cannot recover a deleted preset from the UI.
v1.correction: Remove the row in mutate's success path, or use a custom future that removes the row on success. A confirm step is optional for a low-stakes preset. Wiring the engine's existing undo record (ui.rs:257) to a toast would also work.

findings.title: The notification badge fetches up to 100 full rows for every notify event, with no coalescing
findings.evidence: 749-779: each call sends `notify.list {unread_only:true, limit:100}` and discards all but the newest answer using the revision check. Unlike refresh(), there are no pending/dirty flags, so nothing is coalesced. It is called on every notify.* event (app.rs:1197-1200), and full rows (title, body, link) are fetched only to count them and check two categories.
findings.impact: A burst of N notifications (several agents finishing or blocking) issues N concurrent list queries on the shared control socket and N store reads, of which only the last result is used.
findings.fix: Coalesce with pending/dirty flags the way refresh() does. Ideally, use a count/flag query instead of listing rows.

v1.reason: shell.rs:749-779 is accurate. Each call spawns a separate notify.list {unread_only:true, limit:100}; a revision counter discards all answers except the last; and nothing coalesces the requests. It is triggered on every notify.* event (app.rs:1197-1199) and also directly after acks in notification_center.rs:267/285, so one ack produces two queries: the direct call and the event. The engine's list (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:51-82) builds dynamic SQL with prepare rather than prepare_cached, and it runs under Engine::register while holding the store mutex. The real cost is small. Bursts are a few events, and AckAll emits a single event. The per-row emits in session.rs:269 are the largest source. Each query is a LIMIT 100 indexed read. The payoff is modest, but the cleanup is clear.
v1.correction: Coalesce with pending/dirty flags as refresh() does, and drop the redundant direct calls in notification_center.rs that the notify.changed event already covers. A dedicated count/has-held query would avoid fetching rows altogether. The impact is negligible bus load, not a user-visible problem.

findings.title: Project settings report unsaved changes, and refuse to close, when a stored value has leading or trailing spaces
findings.evidence: `original` keeps name, base_branch, build_cmd and run_cmd untrimmed (815-821), but check() compares trimmed input against them: `n.trim() != original.0` (847) and `build.text().trim() != original.2 || run.text().trim() != original.3` (861-862). So a stored " make" reads as dirty before any edit. The close guard (891-898) calls check() and refuses with "Save or cancel your changes first."; dismiss_panels refuses navigation the same way. project.update stores values as given, without trimming (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:265-278).
findings.impact: Rare: for a project whose name or commands were set with surrounding spaces (e.g. via the CLI), the untouched settings sheet cannot be closed with X, Escape or the scrim, and it blocks navigation until the user presses Cancel.
findings.fix: Trim the values when building `original`. The save path already trims what it sends.

v1.reason: `original` is built from the raw stored values (registry.rs:815-821), and the entries start from the same raw text (744-750). check() compares `n.trim() != original.0` (847) and `build.text().trim() != original.2 || run.text().trim() != original.3` (861-862). So a stored value with surrounding whitespace counts as dirty before any edit. The guard installed with panel.set_guard (890-898) returns false when check() is true and shows 'Save or cancel your changes first.' That means X, Escape and the scrim all refuse to close the sheet. project.update (workspace.rs:265-278) writes name/build_cmd/run_cmd exactly as given, without trimming. project.add trims a requested name (workspace.rs:416), but nothing trims on update, so a CLI, MCP or agent call such as `build_cmd: "make "` produces this state. The native editor's own save trims, so the GUI never creates it.
v1.correction: The trigger is rare: only values written outside the native editor (CLI, MCP or an agent calling project.update or workspace.update). Impact is minor. The sheet shows 'Unsaved changes', and the user can press Cancel, or Save, which stores the trimmed value and clears the state. Fix: trim name/build_cmd/run_cmd when building `original`, or have project.update/workspace.update trim on the engine side so the stored values are always normalized.

findings.title: Review and mosaic layouts show an empty right column when only one agent is open
findings.evidence: 158-161: `self.wall_right.set_visible(matches!(mode.as_str(), "review" | "mosaic") || (mode == "grid" && self.columns.get() == 2 && names.len() > 1))`. The review/mosaic placement branch, however, requires `names.len() > 1` (210). With one session the pane goes to `wall`, while wall_right (minimum width 280, app.rs:569) stays visible and empty.
findings.impact: With a single agent in "Focus + stack" or "Focus + grid", part of the wall is an empty column next to a narrowed terminal.
findings.fix: Add the same `&& names.len() > 1` condition for review and mosaic.

v1.reason: shell.rs:158-161 makes wall_right visible for every review/mosaic layout, whatever the pane count. The placement branch at shell.rs:210 requires `names.len() > 1`, so a single pane goes to `wall` at 0,0. wall_right is the Paned end child (app.rs:564) with set_shrink_end_child(false) and size_request(280,-1) (app.rs:567-569). With one agent in review or mosaic layout, an empty column of at least 280px therefore sits beside a narrowed terminal. The `names.len() > 1` guard on placement was already there before commit 2ee0e091; the visibility expression simply never got the same guard.
v1.correction: Fix: add `&& names.len() > 1` to the review/mosaic visibility condition.

results.coverage:
I read every line of apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs (1-2540). I traced the callers and callees it depends on:
- pages.rs: refresh, workspace_picker, task_mark, board_switcher, widgets.
- app.rs: helpers, Ui::call, refresh/refresh_page, event routing at 1180-1265, show_error, confirm_inline.
- client.rs: requests are async on tokio, not blocking.
- shell.rs: open_project and the window shortcut controller.
- panel.rs: the panel host is outside the board page.
- icons.rs (cached), task_pages.rs (compose, approve, COLUMNS) and note_pages.rs (picker rebuild).
- Engine handlers for task.list/move/update/approve/parent.set/delete and audit.list/undo, the engine's audit and undo recording, bus task types, the usage/statusLine path, and CI config.
I also grepped the pedantic clippy output for this file. The usize/i64/u32/f64 casts are all on small lane or index values that are guarded (`next >= 0`, clamp, min), so none is a real truncation bug.

Nothing was compiled or run: there is no GTK 4.22 here, and the instructions rule out cargo. These GTK runtime behaviours are reasoned from GTK docs and GIR rather than observed:
- whether key events inside popovers propagate through the popover's parent chain (this is why finding 4 is medium confidence);
- where focus goes when the focused widget is unparented;
- whether drag-end fires when a re-render destroys the drag source mid-drag (not reported);
- Caps Lock keyval translation.
The performance impact in finding 1 is not measured.

Checked and found clean in this file:
- No RefCell double-borrow paths: every borrow is dropped before grab_focus or render.
- No Rc cycles: all closures use Weak<Board> or Weak<Ui>.
- No glib timeouts are left running; the idle callbacks are one-shot.
- No signal handlers accumulate across renders: changed handlers sit on fresh adjustments.
- No synchronous bus, file or subprocess work on the main thread.
- No Pango markup injection: every label and tooltip is plain text.

Out of scope and only cited in "related": app.rs routes every unclassified event to refresh_page, and pages.rs makes two sequential round-trips per board refresh.

findings.title: Every refresh rebuilds all cards, Done included, with O(n²) lookups on the GTK main thread
findings.evidence: show() always ends with `*board.tasks.borrow_mut() = tasks; board.render();` (502-503), even when the task list is unchanged. render() does `clear(&self.content)` (1188) and deep-clones every task (`let tasks = self.tasks.borrow().clone();`, 1191). render_columns and render_list then walk every non-hidden column, `done` included, and call `self.card(task, tasks)` / `self.row(task, tasks)` for each visible task (1619-1653, 1859-1889). Nothing caps Done: task.list returns every non-deleted task with no limit (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:831-863). Each card is at least 17 widgets (card, top, tools and foot boxes; 3 icon Buttons with Images; 2 DrawingAreas; 4 labels; 2 spacers) plus 4 controllers from wire() (1972-2087). Per card, `all.iter().find(|t| t["id"] == task["duplicate_of"])` (1796) scans the whole list, because a null duplicate_of never matches, and blocked_by scans again for each edge (1773-1779, 1937-1939). A render is therefore O(n²) JSON index lookups. The copy button captures a fresh title+body String per card (1717), render_peek deep-clones all tasks again (2299), and filter_menu is O(n²) (1416). Triggers: app.rs:1264 sends every unclassified event (task.changed, task.deleted, notify.*, mailbox.*, guardrail.*, overlap.changed, module.changed, ...) to refresh_page, and search (709-713) and filter toggles render directly.
findings.impact: Done only grows. In a long-lived project with a few hundred to a few thousand tasks, every agent event and every search keystroke rebuilds roughly 20·N widgets and does O(N²) lookups on the main thread. With several agents working, the board stutters or freezes continuously. I could not measure how long this takes: there is no GTK 4.22 build here.
findings.fix: Skip render() in show() when the (id, updated_at) list is unchanged. Build one HashMap<i64,&Value> per render for the blocked_by, duplicate_of and parent lookups, and use task["children"] in filter_menu and render_peek. Cap Done (for example the 50 most recent with a 'show all' toggle, or collapsed by default), or move lanes to gtk::ListView so only visible rows are realized. Capture the id in the copy closure and build the text on click. Hold the tasks as Rc<Vec<Value>> instead of deep-cloning them in render, render_peek and filter_menu. Use sort_by_cached_key in sorted().

v1.reason: Confirmed mechanism: show() always sets tasks and calls render() (board_view.rs:502-503). render() clears and rebuilds every card (1181-1222), the Done lane included unless the user hides it (render_columns 1619-1656). task.list has no limit or column cap (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:831-863). Each card builds roughly 15-20 widgets. `all.iter().find(|t| t["id"] == task["duplicate_of"])` (~1796) scans the whole list for every card, so a render does O(N²) comparisons. Unclassified events reach refresh_page (app.rs ~1263). Overstated: refresh_page coalesces bursts into one in-flight refresh with a dirty flag (app.rs:1662-1686), so events do not each trigger a render. The O(N²) part is cheap Value comparisons (about 1M for N=1000, a few ms). The real cost is rebuilding N×~20 GTK widgets on every refresh while the board is the visible page. Nothing measured how long that takes, and it cannot be built here. The stall grows with Done and recurs while agents generate events, but 'freezes continuously' is not established.
v1.correction: Severity is medium, not high: the cost of each render is unmeasured, and refresh_page already coalesces refreshes. The highest-payoff fixes are to skip render() when the (id, updated_at) set is unchanged and to cap or collapse Done by default. An id→task HashMap per render is a minor cleanup.

findings.title: Each refresh closes an open card menu or peek picker and resets the peek's scroll and focus
findings.evidence: render() always ends with `self.render_peek();` (1247). That does `clear(&self.peek);` (2289) and appends a brand-new `crate::app::scrolled(&body)` (2457-2459) whose adjustment is never pushed to `self.scrolls`, so its position is never restored. The card context menu is parented to the card (`pop.set_parent(anchor);`, 2095), and render() destroys every card (`clear(&self.content)`, 1188). The peek's Status/Priority/Type/Size pickers are MenuButtons inside the cleared peek (2350-2381), and the strip is cleared too (1281). Focus is restored only when it was inside `self.content` (1182-1186). The peek close button and the peek task links rebuild the peek under the focused widget and never restore focus (2318-2323, 2477-2482). show() renders even when no task changed (502-503), and app.rs:1264 refreshes the page on every unclassified event.
findings.impact: While agents work, any event for the project (an agent's task.update, notify.new, mailbox.new, guardrail.held...) has these effects: a right-click menu or a peek picker vanishes under the pointer; a long description being read in the peek jumps back to the top; text selected in the peek is dropped; and keyboard focus on a strip chip or a peek control is lost.
findings.fix: Skip render when the task list is unchanged (compare ids and updated_at). In render_peek, rebuild only when the peeked task's updated_at has changed; otherwise keep the panel, or keep the scroller and save/restore its vadjustment. Defer re-render while a card menu or a peek picker popover is open, and re-render on its `closed` signal. Restore focus (focus_board) after the peek close and task-link handlers.

v1.reason: Board::render (apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1180-1247) starts with clear(&self.content), clears self.layout and self.scrolls, rebuilds every card, and always ends with self.render_peek(). render_peek (2288) begins with clear(&self.peek) and appends a fresh crate::app::scrolled(&body) (2457-2459). That adjustment is never pushed to self.scrolls, so the peek's scroll position is never restored. The card context menu is a Popover parented to the card with pop.set_parent(anchor) (2095). When the card is removed from the content box it is unmapped, and the popover goes with it. The Status, Priority, Type and Size pickers are MenuButtons inside the cleared peek. Focus is restored only when it was inside self.content (1181-1186, 1227-1238). The peek close button (2318-2323) and task_link (2477-2482) call render_peek, which destroys the focused button, and nothing re-grabs focus. Reachability: show() (478-503) calls render() every time with no change check. In app.rs the event loop's final else branch (around 1263) calls ui.refresh_page() for every subscribed event tagged with the current project that is not handled earlier. Those events include task.changed, mailbox.new, guardrail.held, notify.new and, most often, usage.changed. UsageReport (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:75-83) tags the event with the session's project, and audit.rs:15-16 says provider hooks call usage.report on every window refresh. So while any agent works in the open project, the board and peek are torn down and rebuilt repeatedly in an ordinary flow, which warrants high.
v1.correction: The most frequent trigger is usage.changed (provider.rs:83), which falls through to refresh_page in app.rs even though the board shows nothing from it; device.changed and run.changed fall through the same way. The cheapest first fix is in app.rs: route usage.changed, device.changed and run.changed away from refresh_page, as is already done for settings.changed. Then skip Board::render when the task list's ids and updated_at values are unchanged, and rebuild the peek only when the peeked task changed. Defer a re-render while a card menu or picker popover is open. The auditor's line numbers are close: render_peek starts at 2288 and the pickers are at about 2330-2370. Note that apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in this environment.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. show() stores the tasks and always calls render() (board_view.rs:502-503). render() (from 1181) clears self.content (1188) and the strip (1281). It always ends in render_peek() (1247), which runs clear(&self.peek) (2289) and appends a new ScrolledWindow (2457-2459). Scroll positions are saved and restored only for self.scrolls (1187-1234), which holds the lane and board scrollers but never the peek's. Focus is restored only when it was inside self.content (1182-1186, 1235-1246). The card menu is a Popover set_parent to the card (2095). The peek pickers are MenuButton popovers (2258-2284) inside the cleared peek. Unparenting an ancestor unrealizes these popovers, so they close.

(b) The trigger fires whenever the Board page is open while agents work, and often. The busiest path is one neither earlier pass named. The project filter in app.rs:1213-1216 lets `session.*` events from any project through. apply_session_event then calls refresh_page whenever the page is board or dashboard (agent_menu.rs:133-135). session.report emits session.changed on every running/idle/blocked transition (session.rs:1424-1427), and a keystroke into an idle pane does the same (engine.rs:1318-1341). So any agent in any project starting or ending a turn rebuilds the board. In the current project, each turn end also emits notify.changed, or notify.new plus mailbox.new (session.rs:261-299 and 1415-1423), and agents' task moves and updates emit task.changed. All of these fall through to app.rs:1264. refresh_page only merges requests that arrive while one is already running (app.rs:1662-1685). With a few active agents, the board is rebuilt several times a minute.

The first verifier's "most frequent trigger is usage.changed" is wrong. The statusLine script installed at hooks.rs:384-399 only writes ~/.claude/relay-usage.json (hooks.rs:576-577), which usage.get reads (usage.rs:36). Nothing in relay-cli calls usage.report. The audit.rs:16 and D151 wording about it is stale. device.changed is emitted only while the device watch is running (device.rs:365-377).

(c) When a rebuild happens:
- An open right-click or "." card menu, or a Status/Priority/Type/Size picker, vanishes under the pointer.
- A long peek description jumps back to the top.
- Selected text in the selectable title, description or commit labels is dropped.
- Focus on a strip chip or a peek control is lost.
- The peek close button and the task links (2318-2323, 2477-2482) also destroy the focused button and never re-grab focus.
No task data changes and no stale action is applied: the damage is lost UI state, over and over, in the board's core flow.

(d) This meets the rubric's "likely user-visible wrong behavior in a normal flow", now based on a trigger frequency shown from the code. It is UI-state only, which keeps it at high rather than critical.

(e) The direction of the fix is right, but its change test is incomplete. Task rows carry derived fields that change without bumping tasks.updated_at: sessions, commits, labels, children, rollup and blocked_by/blocks (task.rs:229-341), plus the client-added _module_name and _parent_title. For example, session.update inserts task_sessions rows without touching tasks (session.rs:1463-1478). Comparing only ids and updated_at would leave the board stale.
v2.correction:
Trigger: replace usage.changed with session.changed from any project, which goes through apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:133-135) because the project filter at app.rs:1213-1216 exempts session.* events. Add the notify.changed / notify.new / mailbox.new events emitted at each agent turn end in the current project (session.rs:1415-1423, 261-299), and task.changed from agents. These fall to app.rs:1264. usage.report is not called by any hook: the statusLine script only writes relay-usage.json (hooks.rs:576-577). The audit.rs:16 and D151 comments saying it is called on every window refresh are stale.

Lines: render starts at 1181, not 1180. The auditor's picker lines (2350-2381) are right; the verifier's "about 2330-2370" is not.

Fix:
1. Skip render when the whole decorated task list (Vec<Value>) is equal to the last one, not just ids and updated_at, because derived fields (sessions, commits, labels, rollup, relations, _module_name) change without bumping updated_at.
2. Build a key for the peek from the peeked task and the tasks it links to (parent, sub-tasks, blocked-by/blocks), and rebuild the peek only when that key changes. Otherwise keep the scroller, or save and restore its vadjustment the way the lanes do (1222-1234).
3. Defer the render while a board popover is open, and run it on the popover's `closed` signal.
4. Call focus_board after the peek close button and the task-link handlers.
5. Routing: limiting the board refresh in apply_session_event to the current project's sessions is a bigger win than moving usage/device/run.changed out of the fallback refresh, since session.changed is the busiest trigger. Keep the refresh for the current project, because task assignment reaches the board only through session.changed.

apps/relay-native cannot be compiled here, so this is verified by reading the code only.

findings.title: Board undo retries the same stale row forever, so older changes, including a deleted task, become unrecoverable
findings.evidence: undo_last lists the 50 newest user task.* audit rows (882). It always picks the newest row that has an inverse and is not yet undone: `rows(&history, "rows").iter().find(|r| !r["undo_op"].is_null() && r["undone_by"].is_null())` (885-888). It then calls `ui.call("audit.undo", json!({"audit_id":row["id"]})).await?` (890). audit.undo refuses with `audit.stale` when the entity's updated_at has moved since the op (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:58-63), and it leaves undone_by NULL. The next Ctrl+Z therefore selects the same row and fails again. Nothing skips the row, and `force` is never offered. The context menu's Delete runs without confirmation and says `"Ctrl+Z on the board restores it"` (2218-2226). The native client has no other task.restore or include_deleted path. A successful undo does not say what it undid.
findings.impact: Example: delete task A, then drag task B to Ready. An agent dispatched to B, or any agent task.update or link_commit on B, bumps B's updated_at. From then on every Ctrl+Z fails with 'the entity changed after the audited operation', and A cannot be restored from the app. Rows older than the 50 most recent task ops are also out of reach. A successful Ctrl+Z can silently revert an editor change made hours earlier.
findings.fix: When audit.undo fails with audit.stale or not_undoable, tell the user which task and op are blocked, and offer 'undo anyway' (force) or 'skip' (remember the skipped audit ids and move to the next candidate). On success, show 'Undid <op> on #id <title>'. Put Delete behind crate::app::confirm_inline, which already exists for destructive keys, or add a restore path for deleted tasks (task.list include_deleted plus task.restore).

v1.reason: undo_last (board_view.rs:872-902) lists audit rows with actor=user, op_prefix=task., limit 50. audit.rs:218 orders them `ORDER BY id DESC`. It then always takes the first row where undo_op is set and undone_by is null. Every inverse for task.move, task.update and task.delete carries an expect of {updated_at} (task.rs:890, 905, 918-922). audit.undo (handlers/audit.rs:57-65) returns audit.stale when updated_at differs and force is not set. On that error undone_by is never written: only a successful undo sets it, through mark_undone in engine.rs:1016-1021. Agent and session paths do bump task updated_at outside the user's audit rows, for example session.rs:104, 662, 1177 and 1394, and agent task.update/move calls. So once the newest user row goes stale, every Ctrl+Z picks that row and fails, and every older row, including a task.delete, is shadowed for good. A new user op only adds a row that is undone first, after which the stale row blocks again. The native client never sends force on audit.undo and never calls task.restore or include_deleted (rg finds no such call in apps/relay-native/src). Delete (2218-2226) has no confirmation and its tooltip says "Ctrl+Z on the board restores it".
v1.correction: This is not permanent data loss: task.delete is a soft delete (deleted_at), and task.restore can still be reached through the CLI or MCP, just not from the app. A deleted task's own delete row rarely goes stale, because the session updates guard on `deleted_at IS NULL`. The failure is that the deleted task gets shadowed by a newer stale row. Fix as proposed: on audit.stale, offer 'undo anyway' (force) or 'skip' (remember skipped ids and try the next candidate), and say what was undone on success. Also add a confirmation or a restore path for Delete.

findings.title: Capture-phase board keys steal Enter, Space and arrows from card buttons and from popovers inside the page
findings.evidence: The page's key controller runs in the capture phase (646). It steps aside only for `widget.is::<gtk::Editable>() || widget.is::<gtk::TextView>()` (995-1002). current() treats any focus inside a card as the card itself: `.position(|(_, card)| focus == *card || focus.is_ancestor(card))` (972). With focus on a card's Copy, Peek or Open button (1714-1738), Enter is claimed by `Key::Return ... => task_pages::open` (1088-1092) and Space by `toggle_peek` (1093-1097). Both return Stop before the button sees the key. The card's context menu is parented to the card (2095), so the same applies to its items. Arrow keys are handled whatever has focus (1053-1075, falling back to focus_board()). Escape closes the quick bar and clears its title (1038-1041), or closes the peek.
findings.impact: Certain: Tab to a card's Copy button and press Enter or Space. The editor opens or the peek toggles, and nothing is copied. Not established, because it needs GTK4 to propagate popover key events through the popover's parent chain to the page, which I could not run: (1) in the menu opened with '.', Enter on 'Delete task' or on a MOVE TO key opens the full editor instead; (2) Down in that menu, in a quick-bar DropDown list or in the workspace/filter popovers moves focus to a card; (3) Escape to dismiss a quick-bar DropDown list closes the bar and throws away the typed title. This breaks keyboard use of a board designed to be keyboard-first.
findings.fix: In key(), return Proceed when any focus ancestor is a gtk::Popover, or is a Button, DropDown or MenuButton other than the card itself. Make current() match only `focus == *card`, or count a descendant as the card only when it is not interactive. Alternatively, attach the controller to `content` in the bubble phase so focused widgets handle their keys first.

v1.reason: The page's EventControllerKey is in the Capture phase (board_view.rs:645-646, attached at 795). key() (994-1002) steps aside only when focus is in an Editable or TextView. current() (968-975) treats any descendant of a card as the card (`focus.is_ancestor(card)`). Each card holds focusable Copy, Peek and Open gtk::Buttons (1714-1738). board.css:73 shows them on :focus-within, so keyboard focus is expected to land on them. With focus on Copy, Enter matches Key::Return (1088-1092), opens the task, and returns Stop before the button's own activate binding runs. Space toggles peek instead of copying. So keyboard activation of the Copy button never works, and Enter on Peek opens the editor rather than peeking.
v1.correction: The popover cases are not established. The '.' menu (2094-2095) and DropDown lists are popovers parented to the card or the bar, and whether their key events pass through the page's capture controller depends on whether GTK puts a grab on autohide popovers, which would stop propagation at the popover. I could not verify that without the GTK C sources or a build. The author tests the keyboard-first menu, which also argues against that part. The confirmed part only affects Tab-focused card tool buttons, mostly Copy, since Open and Peek have key equivalents, so it rates low. Fix: in key(), return Proceed when focus is a Button, DropDown or MenuButton, or sits inside a Popover, rather than on the card itself. Or make current() match only `focus == *card`.

findings.title: Shift+J/K reorders against the unfiltered, ungrouped column, so it often does nothing visible
findings.evidence: nudge finds the neighbour with `let order = self.column_order(&column);` (1163). column_order sorts every task in the column by (position, id) and ignores search, filters and grouping (811-821). nudge then sends `self.move_to(task, &column, Some(next as usize))` with `next = at ± 1` (1167-1172). The lane on screen, by contrast, comes from sorted() (1515-1529), which applies filters and orders by group_of first.
findings.impact: Filter type=bug on a column ordered bug1, chore1, bug2. Shift+J on bug1 moves it to index 1, after the hidden chore1, so the visible order stays bug1, bug2 and a second press is needed. With 'group by priority' the visible order is by group first. Shift+J then swaps a card with a card in another group, again with no visible change. Shift+K on the first card of a lower group does nothing. Whenever a filter, search or grouping is active, the doc comment's promise ('swaps places with its neighbour') does not hold.
findings.fix: Take the neighbour from the rendered lane (self.layout, which already reflects filters and grouping), then send `drop_index(&self.column_order(&column), id, neighbour, delta > 0)`. While grouping is active, refuse a move across groups, or tell the user why nothing moved.

v1.reason: nudge (board_view.rs:1157-1173) finds the neighbour with column_order (811-821). The doc comment says column_order covers every live task in the column with filters ignored, sorted by (position, id). It sends task.move with position at±1. The lane on screen comes from sorted() (1515-1528): filtered by task_matches (render 1194-1197) and ordered by group_of first. With a filter or search hiding the card between two visible cards, Shift+J moves the card past the hidden one and the visible order does not change. With grouping active, the position neighbour can sit in another group, so nothing visible moves. Shift+K on the first card of a group can likewise do nothing visible. In both cases the hidden ordering is still changed. Drag-and-drop does not have this problem: drop_on calls drop_index with the visible target card.
v1.correction: Take the neighbour from the rendered lane (self.layout for this column), then compute the index with drop_index(&self.column_order(&column), id, neighbour, delta > 0), as drop_on already does. Under grouping, refuse moves across group boundaries.

findings.title: Repeated P, Shift+J/K or [ ] presses are computed from the stale task list and collapse into one step
findings.evidence: Keyboard commands read `self.tasks`, which changes only when a refresh round-trip lands in show() (502). `p` sends `order[(at + 1) % 4]`, with `at` taken from `text(&task, "priority")` (1136-1141). `[` and `]` take the target from the task's current column (1121-1131). nudge takes `next` from column_order (1163-1172). act() is fire-and-forget with no local update: it spawns the request and calls `ui.refresh_page()` (823-831). Nothing records the pending change.
findings.impact: Press P three times, or Shift+J three times, or hold Shift+J with key repeat, before task.list, module.list and a full render have come back. Every press sends the same payload ('high', or position at+1), so the card moves one step instead of three and the other presses are lost. On a large board, where the render alone is slow, normal typing speed is enough to hit this.
findings.fix: Apply the change to self.tasks optimistically (priority, column, position) and re-render before sending the request; the server's refresh then confirms or corrects it. Alternatively keep a per-task pending value that later presses build on.

v1.reason: Every keyboard command builds its payload from self.tasks, which is replaced only in show() (board_view.rs:502) after a refresh round-trip. act() (823-831) spawns the call and then ui.refresh_page(), with no optimistic update. refresh_page (app.rs:1662-1686) coalesces, so the new task list arrives only after the call, task.list and a full render. Until then, every `p` press computes order[(at+1)%4] from the same old priority (1135-1142). Every `[`/`]` press computes the same target column (1121-1132).
