Every Shift+J/K press computes the same index from column_order (nudge 1157-1173). All of them send identical payloads. Example: `p p` on a medium task leaves it at high, not urgent, and holding Shift+J moves the card one place. Nothing is lost beyond the extra steps, and the card shows the result, so the user can press again.
v1.correction: Severity is medium at most, because the result is visible and self-correcting. The suggested fix is fine: apply the priority, column or position change to self.tasks and re-render before sending, then let the refresh reconcile.

findings.title: Picking the current Status in the peek moves the card to the bottom of its column; the other pickers write no-op updates
findings.evidence: picker() wires every value, the current one included: `key.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... pick(&board, value); })` (2273-2280). The current value is only styled (`key.add_css_class("selected")`, 2267-2269). Picking a Status calls `board.move_to(&moving, c, None)` (2356). For a non-done column, move_to sends `task.move` with no position (845-849), and the engine then appends the card at the end: `None => next_position(...)` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:901). The context menu disables only its current column (2158-2161); its Priority and Type keys stay clickable (2173-2199), and so do the peek's. task.update always rewrites updated_at (task.rs:887).
findings.impact: Open the peek on the second card in Ready and pick Status → Ready, which is a natural way to dismiss the picker. The card silently drops to the bottom of Ready, and an undo row is recorded. Re-picking the current priority, type or size writes a no-op task.update that bumps updated_at, which makes earlier undo rows for that task stale (see the undo finding).
findings.fix: In picker(), skip pick() when `value == current`, or make that key insensitive the way the context menu does for its current column. Apply the same rule to the context menu's priority and type keys.

v1.reason: Board::picker (apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs ~2264-2280) styles the current value with the `selected` class and still wires every key, the current one included, to `pick(&board, value)`. Nothing skips the current value. The peek's Status picker calls `board.move_to(&moving, c, None)` (~2356). For a column other than done, move_to (834-850) sends `task.move` with no position. The engine's Move handler (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:901) then computes `next_position` = `COALESCE(MAX(position),-1)+1` over the column (452-453). That MAX includes the task itself, so the card always lands after every other card, and the handler records an undo row (905) and rewrites updated_at. The board orders cards by group, then position (sorted(), 1515-1529), so the card visibly drops to the bottom of its group. Picking Done while already in Done does nothing because of the `from != "done"` guard. The context menu disables only its current column (`key.set_sensitive(false)`, ~2158-2161). Its Priority and Type keys (~2167-2199) stay live, as do the peek's Priority, Type and Size pickers. Each of those sends a task.update that rewrites every field unchanged plus `updated_at=ctx.now` (task.rs:885-887) and records an undo row.
v1.correction: Main harm: the card moves to the end of its column and the user can undo it with Ctrl+Z. The no-op updates are harmless apart from adding undo rows and bumping updated_at. Medium (a real bug on a less common path) is the right rating; it is not high. Fix: in picker(), make the current value's key insensitive or return early when `value == current`; do the same for the context menu's Priority and Type keys. Alternatively, have the engine's Move handler keep the task's position when `p.column == before.column && p.position.is_none()`.

findings.title: Quick-create's 'More fields…' throws away the typed title, type, priority and column
findings.evidence: `more.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... board.close_quick(); task_pages::compose(&ui, board.project); })` (770-775). close_quick does `self.quick.title.set_text("")` (914). compose(ui, project) takes no initial values (task_pages.rs:335), so the full editor opens empty.
findings.impact: Type a title in the quick-create bar, choose Bug / Urgent / Ready, then click 'More fields…' to add a description. The editor opens blank and the bar has already been cleared, so everything has to be typed again.
findings.fix: Pass the quick bar's title, type, priority and column to compose (add a prefill argument or a Draft). Clear the bar only once the editor has the values.

v1.reason: board_view.rs:770-775: the 'More fields…' handler calls board.close_quick() and then task_pages::compose(&ui, board.project). close_quick (911-915) hides the bar and runs quick.title.set_text(""). compose (task_pages.rs:335) takes only (ui, project) and builds a blank title Entry with kind defaulting to "task" and priority to "medium" (343-353). Nothing passes the bar's title, column, type or priority across, so whatever was typed or chosen is lost.
v1.correction: The impact is retyping one title and re-picking up to three dropdowns, in a flow that is meant to escalate a quick create to the full editor. That is an annoyance, not a failure, so it rates low rather than medium. Fix: give compose an optional prefill (title, type, priority, column) and clear the bar only after the editor has been built from it.

findings.title: Ctrl+Z bypasses the undo button's in-flight guard, so key repeat fires overlapping undos
findings.evidence: undo_last disables the button while it runs (`key.set_sensitive(false)`, 875). Ctrl+Z, however, calls `self.undo.emit_clicked()` (1003-1005), and emitting the signal runs the handler whether or not the button is sensitive. Each call spawns its own audit.list followed by audit.undo (877-902).
findings.impact: Holding Ctrl+Z, or pressing it twice quickly, starts several undo_last tasks at once. Every list answered before the first undo commits picks the same row; the extra undos fail with 'audit row N was already undone' in the banner, and later ones undo further rows. How many steps get undone is unpredictable.
findings.fix: Return early from the Ctrl+Z branch when `!self.undo.is_sensitive()`, or keep an `undoing: Cell<bool>` on Board that undo_last checks and sets.

v1.reason: undo_last makes the button insensitive (board_view.rs:875). Ctrl+Z in key() calls self.undo.emit_clicked() (1003-1005). That emits the 'clicked' signal directly, and the handler (737-742) runs whatever the button's sensitivity. Each run spawns its own audit.list followed by audit.undo. A second press made before the first undo commits lists the same newest row. Its audit.undo then fails in the transaction with "audit row N was already undone" (handlers/audit.rs:54-56), which surfaces as an error banner. Presses whose list arrives after the commit undo further rows.
v1.correction: The practical effect is a spurious error banner on a quick double press, or a varying number of steps undone under key repeat. Nothing is corrupted, because the already-undone check runs inside the transaction. Fix: check `self.undo.is_sensitive()` in the Ctrl+Z branch, or call activate() / use an `undoing: Cell<bool>` guard.

findings.title: Create stays clickable while task.create is in flight, so a double click can create two tasks
findings.evidence: quick_create disables only the entry: `self.quick.title.set_sensitive(false);` (934). The Create button (758-762) stays sensitive. An insensitive entry still returns its text, so a second click passes the `title.is_empty()` check (920) and sends a second, identical task.create. The title is cleared only when the first reply arrives (939-941).
findings.impact: When the engine is slow, for example while the store is busy under many agents, a double click on Create makes two identical tasks.
findings.fix: Make the whole bar, or at least the Create button, insensitive for the duration of the request, or guard quick_create with a `creating: Cell<bool>`.

v1.reason: quick_create (board_view.rs:917-950) makes only quick.title insensitive (934). The Create button's clicked handler (758-762) calls quick_create again unconditionally. title.text() still returns the text while the entry is insensitive, so the empty-title guard (920) passes, and a second task.create with an identical payload goes out. The title is cleared only when the first reply arrives (939-941), and even then only if it still matches.
v1.correction: This needs a click during the round trip, which is usually only milliseconds unless the store mutex is contended, so the impact is a duplicate task now and then. Fix: make the Create button (or the whole bar) insensitive while the request is in flight, or guard with a Cell<bool>.

findings.title: The header 'New task' button always opens quick-create on Backlog; its focused-card lookup can never succeed
findings.evidence: `add.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... let column = board.current().map(|(column, _)| column); board.open_quick(column.as_deref().unwrap_or("backlog")); })` (745-750). current() reads the window's live focus (968). By the time `clicked` fires, a mouse press has already moved focus to the button: GtkButton focus-on-click is on by default and button() does not change it. Activating the button from the keyboard also needs focus on it. current() therefore always returns None.
findings.impact: With a card focused in Ready, clicking 'New task' preselects Backlog, not Ready as the code intends. Only the C key preselects the column correctly.
findings.fix: Use the remembered card instead: `board.focused.get().and_then(|id| board.task(id)).map(|t| text(&t, "column").to_string())`.

v1.reason: add.connect_clicked (board_view.rs:744-750) calls board.current(), which looks up the root's live focus among the cards (967-975). `add` comes from app::button (app.rs:34-45), which does not turn off focus-on-click. GTK4's GtkButton grabs focus in its click-pressed handler when focus_on_click is true, so by the time `clicked` fires, focus is on the button. Keyboard activation also requires focus on the button. current() therefore returns None, and the button always opens on Backlog. The C key (1098-1100) uses `here`, computed while focus is still on a card, so it works.
v1.correction: This depends on GTK's focus-on-click behaviour, which was not checked against 4.22 in a running build. Note that the remembered `focused` id may belong to a Done card. "done" is not in QUICK_COLUMNS, so open_quick still falls back to index 0, which is harmless.

findings.title: Scroll positions are restored by index, so V or hiding a column applies offsets to the wrong scroller
findings.evidence: `let saved: Vec<f64> = self.scrolls.borrow().iter().map(|a| a.value()).collect();` (1187) is zipped onto the new scrollers by position (1223-1234). The scroller list differs by view: the board pushes its horizontal adjustment first, then one vertical adjustment per visible lane (1610, 1634); the list pushes a single vertical adjustment (1855). The restore handler stays connected until the saved offset becomes reachable.
findings.impact: Switching from board to list applies the board's horizontal offset to the list's vertical scroll, and switching back does the reverse. Hiding Backlog gives Ready the old Backlog offset, Active the old Ready offset, and so on. When a saved offset cannot be reached immediately, the armed handler can jump the lane later (for example on a window resize), after the user has scrolled.
findings.fix: Key the saved values by role ("board-h", "lane:<column>", "list") in a map and restore only matching keys. Disconnect the handler once it has fired, or after the first allocation.

v1.reason: render() saves the scroll offsets as a Vec in index order (board_view.rs:1187) and zips them onto the new scrollers by index (1223-1234). render_columns pushes the board's horizontal adjustment first and then one vertical adjustment per visible lane (1610, 1634). render_list pushes a single vertical adjustment (1855). Switching views through V (1111-1114) or the view toggles re-renders. Board to list applies the board's horizontal offset to the list's vertical scroll. List to board applies the list's vertical offset to the board's horizontal scroll. Hiding a column (1296-1301, 1559) shifts each later lane's offset onto its neighbour. The `done` guard makes each restore handler fire only once. It fires late only if the content grows before the next render replaces the scrollers, which is a narrow window.
v1.correction: The 'jumps later after the user has scrolled' part is minor: the handler fires once, and the next render (on any event) discards the adjustment. The main bug is the index-based mapping. Key the saved offsets by role (board-h, lane:<column>, list).

findings.title: The peek shows 'Updated Aug 27 ago' or ' ago' for old or missing timestamps
findings.evidence: `prop("Updated", &value(&format!("{} ago", ago(text(&task, "updated_at"))).replace("now ago", "just now")));` (2397); 'Created' on 2398 is built the same way. ago_between returns a calendar date once the age reaches 35 days (`_ => then.format("%b %-d")`, 157), and an empty string for a missing or unparseable timestamp (144-148).
findings.impact: Any task older than five weeks reads 'Updated Aug 27 ago' in the peek. A missing created_at reads ' ago'.
findings.fix: Give the peek its own formatter: 'just now', '5m ago', 'on Aug 27', or '—' when there is no timestamp.

v1.reason: render_peek builds both lines as `format!("{} ago", ago(...)).replace("now ago", "just now")` (apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs ~2397-2398). ago_between (143-158) returns `then.format("%b %-d")` once the age reaches 3,024,000 s (35 days), and the in-file test confirms it returns "Mar 1". So any task untouched for five weeks or more reads "Updated Mar 1 ago" / "Created Mar 1 ago". That is a common case for backlog items.
v1.correction: The " ago" result for a missing timestamp is nearly unreachable: the engine always sets created_at and updated_at. The real trigger is the over-35-days date case. Fix: format the date branch as "on Mar 1" (or drop the "ago" suffix when ago() returns a date), and keep 'just now' for the 'now' case.

findings.title: Grouping by size orders the groups L, M, None, S, and the fallback groups sort among the real ones
findings.evidence: For size and type, group_of falls back to `key => task[key].as_str().unwrap_or("None").to_string()` (131), and sorted() orders by that raw string (1522-1524). Only priority gets an ordinal prefix (127-130). The fallbacks 'Top level', 'No module' and 'Unassigned' (118-125) also sort by spelling; 'Unassigned' sorts ahead of every lowercase session name because 'U' < 'a'.
findings.impact: With 'group by size', the groups appear as L, M, None, S, which is not size order. The fallback groups land in arbitrary positions among the real ones.
findings.fix: Prefix size with an ordinal as priority already does ("0 S", "1 M", "2 L", "9 None") and strip it in group_title. Force the fallback groups to sort last.

v1.reason: group_of (board_view.rs:116-132) gives priority an ordinal prefix (127-130) and falls through to `key => task[key].as_str().unwrap_or("None")` (131) for size and type. sorted() (1515-1528) orders by that raw string, and render emits a heading each time the group changes (1643-1648, 1879-1882). The engine stores size as Option (handlers/task.rs:325), so a task with no size gets "None". Lexical order is then L < M < None < S. The fallbacks "Top level", "No module" and "Unassigned" also sort by spelling among the real names.
v1.correction: Purely cosmetic. Type is in the same position but has no natural order, so only size is clearly wrong. The fix as proposed is right: give size an ordinal prefix through SIZES and strip it in group_title (134), and push the fallback groups to the end.

findings.title: The board header's workspace picker is built once per mount and goes stale when projects are added, renamed or deleted
findings.evidence: Board::mount appends `workspace_picker(ui, project, "board")` (513). workspace_picker reads ui.projects and ui.workspaces when it is built (pages.rs:187-249). The header is not rebuilt until the project changes (show, 479-490). The Notes workspace, by contrast, rebuilds its picker on every refresh: `clear(&shell.picker); shell.picker.append(&super::workspace_picker(ui, project, "notes"));` (note_pages.rs:1121-1122).
findings.impact: While the board stays open: a renamed project keeps its old name in the header; a newly added project is missing from the menu; a deleted project is still listed, and choosing it switches to an id that the next refresh() rejects.
findings.fix: Keep a slot Box in the header and rebuild the picker in render() or show(), the way note_pages::workspace does.

v1.reason: Board::mount appends workspace_picker(ui, project, "board") once (board_view.rs:513). workspace_picker reads ui.projects and ui.workspaces when it is built (pages.rs:187-250). A project.* or workspace.* event sets registry_dirty and calls refresh() (app.rs:1223-1225). refresh() reloads ui.projects (app.rs:1373-1384) and then calls board_view::show with the same project id (pages.rs:86-88). That takes the no-remount branch (board_view.rs:479-480), so the header picker is never rebuilt. Notes, by contrast, rebuilds its picker on refresh (note_pages.rs:1121-1122).
v1.correction: If the open project itself is deleted, refresh() switches ui.project, and the next show() remounts with a fresh picker. The stale state therefore only affects other projects: renamed, added or deleted ones. Picking a stale deleted id leads to an open_project on a missing row, which the next refresh resolves by falling back to the first project.

findings.title: Showing the drop rail at drag start pushes the whole board down under the pointer
findings.evidence: The rail is an ordinary child of the page's vertical Box, placed between the quick bar and `main` (603-608, 610-622). drag_begin calls `board.rail.set_visible(true)` (2027), and drag_end hides it again (2043). board.css:37 gives it a 10px margin, 5px padding, 22px buttons and a border: about 40px of new height above the lanes.
findings.impact: As soon as a drag starts, every lane and card moves down by about 40px, so the card under the pointer is no longer the one the user aimed at. Short reorder drags land a slot off unless the user re-aims, and the board jumps back when the drag ends.
findings.fix: Reserve the rail's space permanently and toggle its opacity and sensitivity instead, or float it in a gtk::Overlay above the lanes, so starting a drag does not reflow the content.

v1.reason: The rail is a plain child of the vertical page Box, appended after the quick bar and before main (apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:603-608, then main at 610-622). drag_begin calls board.rail.set_visible(true) (2027), and drag_end hides it again (2043). board.css:37-38 gives it a 10px top margin, 5px padding, a 1px border and 22px buttons, so roughly 40px of new height appears above main. main is the vexpand child, so every lane and card shifts down by that amount once the drag threshold is crossed. Drop targets under the pointer move relative to where the user aimed, and the board jumps back when the drag ends. Nothing documents this as intended.
v1.correction: Keep the rail permanently allocated and toggle its opacity and sensitivity, or place it in a gtk::Overlay above main. Note that apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in this environment.

findings.title: Board shortcuts compare raw keyvals, so they stop working while Caps Lock is on
findings.evidence: key() matches lowercase keyvals directly (`Key::j | Key::k`, `Key::c`, `Key::n`, `Key::f`, `Key::v`, `Key::g`, `Key::p`; 1053-1134). It treats an uppercase J/K as Shift+J/K only when `shift` is set (1014, 1049), and Ctrl+Z requires `key == Key::z` (1003). With Caps Lock on, GDK delivers the uppercase keyval without SHIFT_MASK, so `Key::J` fails the `if shift` guard and no other arm matches.
findings.impact: With Caps Lock on, j/k/h/l navigation, C, N, F, V, G, P and Ctrl+Z all silently do nothing on the board.
findings.fix: Match on `key.to_lower()` for letters, and take the reorder intent from SHIFT_MASK alone.

v1.reason: board_view.rs:993-1170 Board::key matches raw keyvals from EventControllerKey::key-pressed (wired at 790-795, no normalisation). With Caps Lock on, GTK4 sends the uppercase keyval with LOCK_MASK and no SHIFT_MASK. `Key::J | Key::K if shift` (1049) fails the guard. `Key::j | Key::k | Key::Down | Key::Up` (1053) does not match J or K. The letter arms c/n/f/v/g/p (1100-1134) only match lowercase. So these keys reach `_ => Proceed` and nothing happens. Ctrl+Z (1003) needs `key == Key::z`. The reverse also goes wrong: Shift+j with Caps Lock gives a lowercase j with SHIFT set, so the user gets navigation instead of a reorder. The arrow keys and Enter/Space still work, so the board stays usable.
v1.correction: Normalise once at the top with `let key = key.to_lower();` and take the reorder intent from SHIFT_MASK alone (Shift+j/k and Shift+Up/Down). Ctrl+Z is covered by the same normalisation.

findings.title: render_columns/render_list and card/row duplicate the per-task logic and have already diverged
findings.impact: Every board change has to be made twice, and the two views already disagree: the list view has no all-hidden message and does not show duplicate_of. Further drift will follow.
findings.fix: Write one render_sections(list: bool) loop that calls card() or row() and shares the all-hidden message. Build one per-task summary (blockers, duplicate, agents) once from an id index and use it in both views.

v1.reason: render_list (1850-1893) repeats the per-column loop of render_columns (1599-1656) almost line for line: the hidden skip, the total count, sorted(), lane_head, lane_drop, the group headings tracked through previous, the placed list and the layout push. They have already diverged in one place: only render_columns shows the 'Every column is hidden' message (1614-1618), so list view shows a blank page in that state. The rest of the claimed divergence is overstated. row() is a deliberately compact one-line view; leaving out duplicate_of, the rollup meter and the full agent list there is a design choice, not drift. The two blocked checks (1773-1779 and 1937-1939) compute the same predicate. Moving the clipboard text to task.copy_text would not be simpler: it adds an async bus round-trip for a local string, and task.copy_text uses a different format ("#id title\n\nbody", crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1308-1315), so switching would change behavior.
v1.correction: Limit the finding to the duplicated section loop and the missing all-hidden message in list view. A shared render_sections(list) loop that calls card() or row() is the reasonable fix. Drop the card/row and task.copy_text parts of the suggested fix: row is meant to be compact, and the two copy strings at 1717 and 2203 are identical one-liners.

findings.title: The task vocabulary (columns, types, priorities, sizes) is written out about ten times across board_view and task_pages
findings.evidence: board_view defines COLUMNS (13), TYPES (20), PRIORITIES urgent→low (21), SIZES (22), QUICK_COLUMNS (445) and QUICK_PRIORITIES low→urgent (446). It also has literal copies: `["low", "medium", "high", "urgent"]` (682, 1136) and `["S", "M", "L"]` (683, 1401). task_pages keeps its own `COLUMNS` (task_pages.rs:5) and further literal type, priority and size lists (task_pages.rs:352-354, 361).
findings.impact: Adding a column, type or size to the bus enums means hunting down every copy. Any copy that is missed silently leaves the new value out of a picker, a filter or the rail.
findings.fix: Create one shared vocabulary module under pages/ (column names and titles, types, priorities in one order, sizes) and derive the quick-create, rail and cycle orders from it.

v1.reason: Confirmed copies: board_view.rs:13 COLUMNS, :20 TYPES, :21 PRIORITIES (urgent first), :22 SIZES, :445 QUICK_COLUMNS, :446 QUICK_PRIORITIES (low first). Literal copies sit at :682-683, :1136 and :1401, and `.clamp(0, 4)` at :1125 hard-codes the column count. task_pages.rs repeats them at :5 (COLUMNS), :352-354, :361, :382, :389, :547, :551 and :554. Every copy agrees today, so nothing has diverged in behaviour yet. The cost is the future one the finding describes.
v1.correction: Add task_pages.rs:382/389/547/551/554 and board_view.rs:1125 (`clamp(0, 4)`) to the related locations. Since nothing has diverged yet, low is the right severity.

findings.title: The board's pure logic is tested only inside the GTK crate, which CI never builds
findings.evidence: The tests at 2488-2540 cover task_matches, drop_index, zone and ago_between. They live in relay-native, which is not a default member (Cargo.toml:5, `default-members` excludes apps/relay-native) and which ci.yml:69-82 deliberately does not build. Of these functions, only ago_between needs glib. Nothing tests group_of or sorted() ordering, nudge, scroll restore or undo row selection.
findings.impact: Regressions in the board's ordering, filtering and drop-index logic (see the nudge and size-grouping findings) reach users without ever running a test: the existing tests never run in CI.
findings.fix: Move task_matches, haystack, group_of, drop_index, zone and a jiff-based age formatter into a GTK-free module that a headless crate compiles and tests (a small crate, or a #[path] include from a default member). Add cases for grouped and filtered reorders.

v1.reason: These facts check out. The tests (~2488-2540) live in relay-native. Cargo.toml:5 default-members excludes relay-native. ci.yml:69-84 explains that CI leaves it out on purpose (the GTK 4.22 / pango 1.56 pins are not available on ubuntu-latest). Nothing tests sorted()/group_of ordering. task_matches, drop_index and zone are pure and need no GTK; ago_between uses glib::DateTime. However, the stated impact ("reach users without ever running a test") is overstated. README.md:62 makes `cargo test --workspace` part of the developer verification list, so these tests run on the author's GTK machine, which also hosts the agent sessions. What is missing is CI enforcement, which is a documented and deliberate trade-off, plus coverage of sorted()/group_of.
v1.correction: Restate the impact: the tests run locally (README.md:62) but CI does not enforce them, and the grouped-sort ordering has no tests. Extracting the pure helpers (task_matches, haystack, group_of, drop_index, zone) into a GTK-free module compiled by a default member would put them under CI cheaply. The ago formatter would need a non-glib time source to move with them. Modest payoff; low.

findings.title: The board says approval links the project HEAD; the engine links the last agent's branch tip
findings.evidence: The MOVE TO Done tooltip reads `"Done · approves the task and links the project HEAD"` (2157), and move_to's doc comment says approval 'links the project checkout's HEAD' (832-833). task.approve actually resolves `refs/heads/{session.branch}` for the most recently dispatched session, and falls back to the checkout HEAD only for a task that was never dispatched (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1094-1126). The 'Ctrl+Z undoes it' notice (839) also overpromises: the inverse is only a task.move, and the linked commit stays.
findings.impact: For the usual case, a task an agent was dispatched to, the user is told the wrong commit will be recorded as the task's delivery.
findings.fix: Reword to 'approves the task and links its agent branch tip (the project HEAD if it was never dispatched)'. Drop the undo promise or qualify it.

v1.reason: The move_to doc comment (apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:832-833) and the Done menu tooltip (around 2157) say approval links the project HEAD. The task.approve handler (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1086-1127) takes the latest task_sessions row for the task, resolves refs/heads/{session.branch} in the project repository and records that branch. It falls back to the checkout HEAD only when the task was never dispatched. Approve records undo as a task.move back to the previous column and position (1141-1145), and undo_last replays that row. The 'Ctrl+Z undoes it' notice at 839 therefore restores the column, but the commit linked by link_commit stays on the task.
v1.correction: Reword the tooltip and comment to 'links the last agent's branch tip (the project HEAD if never dispatched)'. Qualify the undo notice: undo restores the column, but the linked commit remains.

findings.title: Dropping a card into empty space in its own lane does nothing
findings.evidence: The lane and section drop handler returns early for a same-column drop: `if text(&task, "column") == column { return false; }` (1589-1591). Only the per-card drop targets handle reordering (drop_on, 851-870).
findings.impact: Dragging a card into the empty area below the last card of its own lane (the natural way to send it to the bottom), or onto the section header, is silently rejected. The user has to hit the bottom 30% of the last card exactly.
findings.fix: On a same-column lane drop, move the card to the end (`task.move` with position = the number of other tasks in the column), or work out the slot from the drop y against the lane's cards.

v1.reason: In lane_drop (apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1567-1597), the drop handler returns false when text(&task, "column") == column (1589-1591). Only the per-card DropTargets (wire, about 2047-2086, then drop_on at 851) compute a slot with drop_index. A same-lane drop onto the empty area below the last card, onto the 6px gaps between cards, or onto the lane or section header is therefore rejected, and the card snaps back. connect_enter still adds the drop-lane highlight for a same-lane drag, so the target looks as though it will accept the drop. Keyboard reorder and card-zone drops still work, so this is a UX gap with low impact.
v1.correction: Possible fix: on a same-column lane drop, call move_to(&task, column, Some(column_order(column).len() - 1)) to send the card to the end. Alternatively, do not add the drop-lane class (or return an empty action from enter) for a same-column drag, so the target does not look as though it accepts the drop.

findings.title: Switching project discards the board's view settings and the quick-create draft
findings.evidence: show() mounts a new Board whenever the project differs (479-490). mount() initialises `list: Cell::new(false)`, empty `hidden`, `group` and filters, and calls `views[0].set_active(true)` (542, 669-678). Nothing keeps these settings per project or globally. The old board's quick-create title is dropped along with its widgets (`clear(page)`, 485).
findings.impact: A user who prefers List view, or who hides Done, has to set it up again after every project switch, including on returning to the same project. A half-typed quick-create title silently disappears when the project changes.
findings.fix: Keep the view mode, hidden columns and grouping in a per-project (or global) map outside Board, or in the ui settings, and re-apply them in mount(). Reset only the project-specific filters.

v1.reason: show() (board_view.rs:477-491) mounts a fresh Board whenever page_projects["board"] differs from the project. mount() starts with list=false, empty hidden, an empty group, fresh Filters, and views[0] active (542, 668-678). The only writes to list, hidden and group are in-memory (733, 1299-1301, 1346, 1383, 1501, 1559). There is no persistence in ui settings or a per-project map, so every project switch, including a return to the same project, resets them. clear(page) drops the quick-create entry along with its text.
v1.correction: This is UX state loss, not data loss. Resetting filters per project is arguably correct. Keeping the view mode, hidden columns and grouping is the meaningful part.

results.coverage:
I read every line of apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs (2037 lines) and apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs (502 lines).

**Context I read to trace callers, callees and data:**
- editor.rs (all)
- project_files.rs (all)
- client.rs (all)
- app.rs: helpers, Ui::call, show_error, event routing at 1178-1286, refresh, navigate
- panel.rs: response and close
- shell.rs: open_project and key controllers
- engine handlers/git.rs: status, diff.file, log, show, branches, branch create/switch/delete, stage/unstage, commit, fetch, push, pr.list/open, suggest_message, upstream_metrics, list_pull_requests
- worktree.rs: status_files, parse_status, the git helper
- watch.rs
- socket.rs: handle_conn dispatch loop
- handlers/file.rs: file.read and list_dir
- relay-bus FileStatus/Entry/DiffFileIn
- similar 2.7.0 udiff.rs, tokenizer and TextDiffConfig
- Cargo.toml and ci.yml

**Experiments, all in the scratchpad:**
- PyGObject with the system gdk-pixbuf 2.44.7 (glycin): size-prepared fires only at close(); set_size still scales; a 110 MP PNG decodes past the guard at 393 MB RSS.
- Scratch git repos: a both-added conflict shows as `AA`; a UU conflict followed by `git add -A` and `git commit` commits the markers.
- I used new directory names because the Relay guardrail denies `rm -rf`.

**Not done:** I did not compile or run relay-native: the hard rules forbid cargo here, and CLAUDE.md notes it cannot be built on standard images anyway. GTK behaviour behind the rebuild and leak findings is inferred from GTK4/GObject semantics, not observed in the running app: unparenting the focused widget's ancestor clears window focus, signal closures are freed only at dispose, and a MenuButton's dispose unparents its popover. The rates of GitHub requests and memory growth depend on how often file/git events arrive and how many PRs and branches the repo has.

**Out of scope (engine code seen while tracing, for the owning chunks):**
- handlers/git.rs:666-692: git.pr.open runs `gh pr create` through Command::output() inside Engine::register, so the store mutex is held with no timeout.
- BranchCreate, Stage, Unstage, BranchDelete and CleanMerged run git subprocesses through worktree::git (Command::output(), no timeout) inside Engine::register.
- hooks.rs:210-213: the user's pre-commit hook has no timeout.
- git push has no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
- CommitOp runs `git add -A` in its unlocked phase, before the guardrail gate, so a held or refused commit has already changed the index.
- git.diff.file has no size or binary limit, uses no diff deadline, and does not apply git filters (LFS pointers, eol).
- socket.rs reads request lines with an unbounded lines() and dispatches each connection's requests sequentially.
- project_files.rs refresh_scopes and update_scope_label never reset a selected worktree that has disappeared.

findings.title: Branch picker and merge-test widgets leak on every Git refresh through strong signal-closure cycles
findings.evidence: render_branch_picker: `let query = search.clone(); ... create_key.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... query ... })` (997-999), `let filter = entries.clone(); search.connect_search_changed(...)` (1179-1181) and `let first = entries.clone(); let create = create_key.clone(); search.connect_activate(move |_| { ... create.emit_clicked() })` (1194-1196). The search entry's handlers own create_key and every branch row (`entries`), and create_key's handler owns the search entry. refresh_git's merge test: `let test = test.clone(); pick.connect_toggled(...)` (700-701) and `test.connect_clicked(move |key| { let selected: Vec<_> = picks ... })` (719-723), so each check button owns `test` and `test` owns every check button. GObject drops signal closures only at dispose, which needs the refcount to reach zero, but `clear(&e.git)` (170) only unparents the old tree. The popover itself is freed because rows hold it through `downgrade()`, but these pairs keep each other alive. Both are rebuilt on every successful refresh (render_branch_picker at 779; the merge test at 682-750 whenever at least one session is live).
findings.impact: editor.rs invalidate() runs refresh_git for every file.changed/git.changed/worktree.changed/integration.* event in the project, up to once a second while agents work and even with the Git panel hidden. Each refresh orphans one SearchEntry, the create key and form, every branch row and each live session's check button. That is roughly 200+ GObjects per refresh in this repo (21 local + 12 remote branches). The GTK client's memory grows steadily for as long as the project is busy and is only reclaimed on restart.
findings.fix: Capture widgets weakly in these handlers (glib::clone! with #[weak] search, create_key and test, or `downgrade()`). Keep the row list as weak refs. Better: build the picker and merge-test widgets once and update them in place (see the rebuild finding).

v1.reason: render_branch_picker sets up two cycles. create_key's clicked closure captures `query = search.clone()` (code_git.rs ~997-1008). search's activate closure captures `create = create_key.clone()` and `first = entries` (~1194-1201), and its search_changed closure captures `filter = entries`, which holds strong refs to every row widget and key button. That gives the cycle SearchEntry -> closure -> create_key -> closure -> SearchEntry. In the merge test, each CheckButton's toggled closure captures `test` (700-701), and test's clicked closure captures `picks` (the Vec of CheckButtons, 719-723), another cycle. app.rs:64 `clear` only calls Box::remove (unparent). GObject removes signal handlers in dispose, and dispose runs only when the last ref drops, so these cycles are never collected. Each successful refresh_git rebuilds both: render_branch_picker at 779, and the merge test whenever live sessions exist. Refreshes come from invalidate (editor.rs:508-528), at up to one a second while agents generate file and git events and the code or agents page is open. The popover itself is freed, as the finding says (rows hold it weakly), and its show-handler ref to search dies with it, but the search/create_key/entries and test/picks groups survive.
v1.correction: The merge-test cycle exists only when at least one live session gives a CheckButton. With none, `picks` is empty and `test` is freed. The leak happens only on the code and agents pages (editor.rs:509). The object count per refresh depends on the number of branches; the 200+ figure is plausible but not measured. The fix stands: capture `search`, `create_key` and `test` weakly (glib::clone! #[weak] or downgrade()), keep `entries` and `picks` as weak refs, or build the widgets once and update them in place.

v2.correction:
The refresh frequency is understated. Watcher file.changed events have no envelope project_id (watch.rs:128 goes through emit_system, engine.rs:567-569, and Event::new leaves project_id as None). app.rs:1213 therefore lets them through from every project. Any watched root in any project, plus agent commits through .git/refs under the project root, refreshes the current project's Git panel. This happens at most once a second, on page "agents", which also covers the Code view. The missing scoping is a separate amplifier and deserves its own finding; the fix there is `.in_project(project_id)` on the watcher event.

The picker cycle leaks on every refresh that renders the picker, even with zero branches. The merge cycle needs at least one non-closed session in the current project.

"200+ GObjects" counts widgets only. Adding CSS nodes and gestures gives a few hundred GObjects, about 100 KB per refresh. That figure is an estimate, not a measurement, and it grows with the branch count.

A minimal fix needs only one weak edge per cycle:
- `search.downgrade()` in create_key's handler, or a weak create_key in search's activate handler;
- `test.downgrade()` in each toggled handler, or `Vec<WeakRef<CheckButton>>` in test's handler.

Weak row lists are optional. The change is under apps/relay-native, which cannot be compiled in the agent image (CLAUDE.md), so it ships without a build check.

findings.title: The Git panel is destroyed and rebuilt on every file/git event, dropping focus, open popovers and view state
findings.evidence: refresh_git does `clear(&e.git);` (170) and then rebuilds everything: the header and the branch-picker MenuButton, a Paned with a recomputed `panes.set_position(...)` (250), and the commit form, re-parenting the persistent commit TextView through `detach(&message)` (297/311). It also rebuilds every section, the history (`graph_key.set_active(true)`, 552) and the merge-test check buttons. It is triggered from editor.rs invalidate(), which app.rs:1232-1240 calls for every file.changed/git.changed/worktree.changed/integration.* event in the project, debounced to 1 s. It runs without checking `self.git.is_visible()` and without looking at which worktree the event came from (invalidate takes no payload). Removing the focused TextView's ancestor makes GTK unset the window focus, and removing the MenuButton disposes its popover. The function is about 700 lines (clippy too_many_lines 696/100). Because nothing survives a refresh, state lives in widget names and CSS classes (`widget_name() != "commit-message"`, the `has-staged` class).
findings.impact: While an agent edits files in the project, someone typing a commit message loses keyboard focus on every refresh and the following keystrokes are dropped. The branch picker or commit-options popover closes under the pointer, the History split jumps back to its computed position, the Graph toggle turns back on, merge-test ticks clear and scroll positions reset, about once a second. All of this work (5 bus requests and hundreds of widgets) is also done while the panel is hidden.
findings.fix: Build the panel skeleton once and update its parts in place: labels, counts, and row lists keyed by path. That keeps focus, popovers and user state. Skip refresh_git while the panel is hidden and refresh when toggle_git or apply_layout shows it. Ignore file.changed events whose payload worktree is not the shown checkout. Split refresh_git into per-section builders.

v1.reason: refresh_git calls `clear(&e.git)` (code_git.rs:170), which removes the whole old tree, including the overlay holding the persistent commit TextView. It then rebuilds the header and MenuButton with its popover, the Paned with a recomputed set_position (250), the commit form (via `detach(&message)`, 297), every section, and the Graph toggle with `set_active(true)` (552). Nothing records or restores focus: the only grab_focus in the function is on the empty-message error path (387). In GTK4, unrooting the focus widget unsets the window focus, and removing a MenuButton drops its popover. The triggers: app.rs:~1232-1240 sends file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed, integration.changed and integration.result for the current project to editor.invalidate. invalidate (editor.rs:508-528) debounces for 1 s and then calls refresh_git whenever the page is code or agents. It takes no payload, does not check which worktree the event came from, and refresh_git never checks `self.git.is_visible()` (toggle_git and apply_layout only flip visibility). The watcher (watch.rs) filters .relay/ and build directories but keeps .git/refs changes, so agent commits and any git.* bus mutation in the project produce events. With agents active, a person typing a commit message loses focus mid-typing, and open popovers and the pane split are reset.
v1.correction: The refresh is not once a second without pause. It happens at most once per second, and only while project events keep arriving, which is common with active agents (refs updates, git.changed, integration events). Agent file edits inside .relay/worktrees are filtered for the primary checkout's watcher. Fix as proposed: build once and update in place, or at minimum save and restore focus and popover state, and skip the work while the panel is hidden. Category bug (UX). The 700-line function is a secondary maintainability point.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. Every git.status that completes reaches `clear(&e.git)` (code_git.rs:170), and nothing compares it with the previous render. The function then rebuilds:
- the branch MenuButton and its popover (182-241);
- a new Paned, with a position computed from the window height (243-250);
- the persistent commit TextView, moved into a new Overlay (297, 311);
- every section, including a Graph toggle forced back on (552) and new merge-test CheckButtons (683-693).

`clear` calls gtk_box_remove, which unparents the widget, so GTK unsets the window focus when the removed subtree holds it. Nothing restores focus: the only grab_focus is on the empty-message path (387). The window key controllers (app.rs:989-1009, shell.rs:1066-1095) handle only Escape and shortcuts, so later keys reach no widget.

(b) The trigger is reachable in normal use. app.rs:1232-1240 calls editor.rs:508-528, which acts whenever ui.page is "agents". navigate() maps "code" to "agents" (app.rs:1314-1315), so this is the main page, and the Git panel sits beside the agent terminals there (app.rs:611-618, editor.rs:276-283). Refreshes run at most about once a second, and only while events keep arriving. If events land during a refresh, GitRefreshGuard runs the next one straight away.

Sources of those events in multi-agent use:
- Each agent commit or fetch rewrites .git/refs/** in the shared git directory. The primary-root watcher keeps those paths (watch.rs:162-167).
- git.* bus mutations emit git.changed.
- Starting or closing a session emits worktree.changed.

The trigger is also wider than the finding says. Watcher events go out through emit_system, and Event::new leaves project_id as None (engine.rs:567-569, envelope.rs:234-245). The project filter at app.rs:1213 therefore never drops them. The watched checkouts of any project fire, and so does any agent worktree once it has been opened in the scope picker: git.status and file.tree register a watcher there (git.rs:164, file.rs:21). Watchers are only ever added, never removed (watch.rs:138). While such a watcher sits on an active agent's worktree, the panel rebuilds about once a second.

(c) What the person sees while typing a commit message:
- Focus disappears mid-word and the following keystrokes are lost. Text already typed survives, because the TextView and its buffer persist.
- An open branch picker or commit-options popover closes.
- The History split snaps back, Graph turns back on, merge-test ticks clear, and both scroll views jump to the top.
- History stays empty and the MERGE TEST section is missing until all four joined requests return (578-583, 673-675), so the panel visibly blanks on every refresh.

Fold state is kept. No data is lost. When the panel is hidden (its initial state, editor.rs:300), the same work still runs, including git.pr.list. That call runs `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all` with no cache (git.rs:625-628, 1083-1092), so every refresh is a GitHub round-trip.

(d) High is right. This is wrong behaviour you can see (lost input, popovers closing) in the main commit flow, caused by the app's core activity of running agents side by side. It is not critical: no data is lost and a click recovers focus.

- The rebuild is not unconditional once a second. It happens at most once per second, and only while events arrive.
- "Events in the project" understates the trigger. Watcher file.changed events and system worktree.changed events carry no envelope project_id, so app.rs:1213 lets them through from every watched root in every project, for the life of the engine.

Gaps in the proposed fix:
1. The git.status fetched in refresh_git also feeds note_changes (code_git.rs:172 calls project_files.rs:549-586), which tints Explorer folders. Skipping refresh_git while the panel is hidden would leave those tints stale. Keep fetching status and calling note_changes, and skip only the rebuild and the other four requests. toggle_git and apply_layout take &self and get no ui, so they need some other way to start a refresh when the panel is shown.
2. Filtering file.changed by the payload's worktree needs care:
   - Compare canonical paths: watch.rs canonicalizes the root, while Editor.worktree is "" for the primary checkout.
   - Keep events from the primary root even when a linked worktree is shown. A commit there changes only the shared .git/refs under the primary root.
   - Also filter on payload project_id, or set the event's project with .in_project() in watch.rs.
3. A cheap first step removes most spurious rebuilds: skip the clear and rebuild when the fetched payloads match the last render. Otherwise, save and restore focus and cursor, the Paned position, the Graph state, the merge selections and the scroll positions. Or defer the rebuild while the commit field has focus or a popover is open.

Related, worth checking as a separate finding: with live sessions, each rebuild probably leaks the merge-test widgets. The Test button's clicked closure owns the CheckButtons (719-727), and each CheckButton's toggled closure holds a strong clone of the Test button (698-714). This is a gtk-rs reference cycle that dispose never breaks.

findings.title: Every Git refresh pages the project's entire GitHub PR history through gh, and history, branches and status wait on it
findings.evidence: `let results = tokio::join!(ui.call("git.branches", ..), ui.call("git.log", ..), ui.call("integration.list", ..), ui.call("git.pr.list", json!({"project_id":project})));` (578-583). The engine answers git.pr.list with `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100`, under a 10 s timeout and with no cache (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:1083-1112). GitRefreshGuard (4-12) keeps git_refresh_pending set until the whole future, including this join, has finished; any refresh_git call in the meantime only sets git_refresh_dirty (146-149). Opening a project calls refresh_git twice: prepare_project calls it through load_tree (editor.rs:564-567) and again directly (project_files.rs:63-67). The dirty flag therefore forces a second full refresh, with a second gh call.
findings.impact: (a) GitHub quota: each refresh costs ceil(PRs/100) REST requests. That can happen about once a second while agents work, even with the panel hidden, against a 5000/h budget shared with the agents' own `gh` token. Once the budget is exhausted, Relay's PR features and the agents' gh commands fail for up to an hour. (b) History, the branch list and the merge test show placeholders until gh answers, up to 10 s, on every refresh. (c) The refresh after a stage, commit or checkout switch waits behind any gh call already in flight, so the panel shows the pre-action state for up to 10 s. (d) After a project switch, the new project's panel stays blank until the previous project's gh call returns.
findings.fix: Take the PR lookup out of the per-event refresh. Fetch it on explicit refresh, fetch, push or branch change, or cache it per (project, branch) with a TTL. Ask only for the current branch (`pulls?head=owner:branch`). Render each phase-2 result as it arrives, and release git_refresh_pending once the status phase is done.

v1.reason: refresh_git (code_git.rs:578-583) uses tokio::join! to wait on git.branches, git.log, integration.list and git.pr.list together, and renders history, branches and the merge test only after all four return. git.pr.list is register_unlocked (handlers/git.rs:625) and calls list_pull_requests (1083-1112) on every request: `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100...` under PR_LIST_TIMEOUT, with no cache anywhere. GitRefreshGuard (code_git.rs:4-12) holds git_refresh_pending until the whole future finishes, so a refresh_git call made in the meantime only sets the dirty flag (146-149) and runs again after the join. editor.rs invalidate debounces to one refresh per second for file, git, worktree and integration events while the code or agents page is open. That is roughly one gh pagination per refresh cycle while agents write files, which can use up a 5000/h REST budget the agents' own gh calls share. Points (b), (c) and (d) follow from the join plus the pending guard. On a project switch the old future waits out its join before it returns and lets the dirty refresh run.
v1.correction: The refresh runs only while the code or agents page is visible (editor.rs:509), not in every situation the finding implies. The cost per refresh is ceil(PRs/100) requests, and how close it comes to the rate limit depends on how fast gh answers and how busy the agents are. The fix stands: take git.pr.list out of the per-event join, or cache it per project with a TTL and ask for `head=` the current branch. Render each result as it arrives.

The panel is cleared and rebuilt on every refresh (clear(&e.git), line 170). git.pr.list (handlers/git.rs:625) runs `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100...` on every call (1083-1112). The only bound is PR_LIST_TIMEOUT = 10 s (line 83); there is no cache anywhere. The coalescing works as described: GitRefreshGuard (4-12) holds pending, and a call made meanwhile only sets dirty (146-149). prepare_project calls refresh_git twice on a project open (editor.rs:564-567, project_files.rs:66). The design record says the opposite should happen. D130 (DECISIONS.md:637-640) says the Code surface asks git.pr.list once when the project opens and "File-watch refreshes do not repeat the network request". The native client breaks that.

(b) How often it fires. Editor::invalidate (editor.rs:508-528) calls refresh_git for every file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed and integration.* event (app.rs:1233-1240), at most once a second. It runs whenever ui.page is "agents". navigate() maps "code" to "agents" (app.rs:1314-1315), and "agents" is the startup and home page (app.rs:747). So the refresh runs on the terminal wall too, and nothing checks whether the Git panel is shown. Watcher events are sent through emit_system without an envelope project_id (engine.rs:567-569). The project filter at app.rs:1213 therefore never drops them, so a ref update from an agent's commit or fetch in any watched project refreshes the current project. In the default setup the primary-checkout watcher ignores `.relay/` worktree edits (watch.rs is_generated_path) but sees .git/refs updates. Agents' own worktrees are watched once someone calls file.read or git.status on them; root_choice defaults to the caller's worktree. (d) High is right. Main-window bus stalls and panel blanking happen in a normal flow, and the work is paid even with the panel hidden. It is not critical: each call is capped at 10 s, and no data or sessions are lost.

Only the other pages (board, dashboard, settings and so on) skip the refresh. It runs whether or not the Git panel is visible.

"About once a second" is an upper bound. In the default setup most triggers are ref updates from agent commits and fetches, Relay git and file ops, and worktree and integration events. Edits inside agents' worktrees count only once those worktrees are watched.

1. Keep git.pr.list's documented contract ("all states, every page"). MCP agents call it, and it triggers the merged-PR branch cleanup. Add an optional branch filter or a new op instead.
2. Better still, add a per-project TTL cache in the engine, cleared on git.push, git.pr.open and git.fetch. That protects every client.

findings.title: Push, fetch, commit hooks and GitHub calls run on the UI's single, serialized control connection
findings.evidence: git_action sends every op through `guarded(&ui,op,payload)` (1244), which calls `ui.call(op, payload.clone())` (1723). refresh_git sends git.pr.list the same way (582). Ui::call uses the one shared Client for everything except session lifecycle ops (app.rs:1111-1117, client.rs:50-63). The engine handles one connection's requests one at a time: it awaits `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(req, Door::Socket)).await?` before reading the next line (crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:739-742). git.push runs `git push` through worktree::git, a plain `Command::output()` with no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (worktree.rs:26-27, handlers/git.rs:600-618). The user's pre-commit hook also has no timeout (hooks.rs:210-213). The client gives up after 30 s (client.rs:65-71).
findings.impact: While a push, a fetch (up to 20 s), a slow pre-commit hook or a gh call is running, every other request the window makes waits behind it: save, open file, session list, guardrail approvals. Pushes with LFS objects in a game repo easily take longer than 30 s. Past 30 s the push is reported as "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown" while it keeps going, and requests queued behind it time out as well. A push stalled on the network wedges the control connection until the user clicks Reconnect, which also tears down and re-creates every terminal pane.
findings.fix: Send long-running git ops (git.push, git.fetch, git.commit, git.pr.open, git.pr.list, git.diff.file) over a dedicated connection, the way lifecycle ops already are: extend is_lifecycle_request, or call Client::lifecycle_request from git_action. Give them timeouts that match the engine's. Separately, give `git push` an engine-side timeout and set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.

v1.reason: The engine processes one connection's requests one at a time. handle_conn loops `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line()` (socket.rs:335) and awaits `spawn_blocking(... dispatch ...)` for each request before reading the next (socket.rs:740-741). The client sends every non-lifecycle op on the one shared Client (app.rs:1111-1117; is_lifecycle_request at client.rs:50-62 lists only session and task.dispatch ops). guarded() (code_git.rs:1722-1723) uses ui.call. git.push runs through worktree::git_mutate, which is a plain `Command::new("git")...output()` (worktree.rs:26-36) with no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (git.rs:617). run_user_pre_commit also calls a plain `.output()` (hooks.rs:210-212). The client's request timeout is 30 s for these ops (client.rs:65-71). So a push stalled on the network, or a slow hook, blocks every later request from the window (save, open, guardrail hold inspection, refresh), and anything past 30 s is reported as an unknown outcome.
v1.correction: Terminal keystrokes are not affected, because each terminal has its own connection (terminal.rs:476). git.fetch already uses output_with_timeout(20 s) with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (git.rs:943-949), and git.pr.list has PR_LIST_TIMEOUT (git.rs:1094), so neither can hang indefinitely; they can only delay other requests. The ops that can hang without limit are git.push, the commit path (`git add -A`, the user's pre-commit hook, `git commit`) and any other git_mutate caller. Those calls also break the CLAUDE.md invariant that every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout. The fix has two halves: run git_mutate and the hook through output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and send long git ops from the client over a separate connection.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. guarded() sends the op with `ui.call(op, payload.clone())` (code_git.rs:1723), and git_action reaches it at line 1244. refresh_git sends git.pr.list on the same path (code_git.rs:578-583). Ui::call (app.rs:1111-1117) uses the one shared Client for every op except those in is_lifecycle_request (client.rs:50-62), which lists only session and task.dispatch ops. The engine works through one connection's requests one at a time: handle_conn reads a line, awaits `spawn_blocking(... e.dispatch ...)` (socket.rs:741-742), writes the response, and only then reads the next line. BUS.md §6.2 allows a client to pipeline requests, but it says nothing about running them in parallel. git.push runs through worktree::git, a plain `Command::output()` (worktree.rs:26-27, git.rs:617): no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. run_user_pre_commit also uses a plain `.output()` (hooks.rs:210-213). Every one of these ops gets the default 30 s client timeout (client.rs:65-71). The author already moved session lifecycle ops onto their own connection because they "must not sit behind slow reads on the UI socket" (client.rs:131), so leaving the git ops on the shared socket is an oversight, not a decision.

(b) This is reachable in normal use by the person at the desktop. Push and commit in the Source Control panel trigger it. LFS is in use here (worktree.rs:84, session.rs:855, client.rs:68). So pushing new binary assets, or a commit whose `git add -A` cleans large LFS files or runs a slow user pre-commit hook, can take more than 30 s. A trigger that fires more often is git.pr.list. Each file.changed or git.changed event while the Code or Agents page is open calls editor.invalidate (app.rs:1232-1240), which waits 1 s and then calls refresh_git (editor.rs:508-524). refresh_git runs `gh api --paginate` (git.rs:1083-1094, up to 10 s). With agents editing files, these network calls keep occupying the control connection. Terminals are not affected because each has its own connection (terminal.rs:476). Agents and other clients are not affected either: Push and Commit are register_staged, so their slow phase runs without the store lock.

(c) While one of these ops runs, every other request the window sends waits behind it: file.read and file.write, session and page refreshes, notification counts, and guardrail.confirm and guardrail.reject (guardrail_pages.rs:299/380/477). That last one means agents whose actions are held cannot be approved until the op finishes. After 30 s the push is reported as "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown" even though it keeps running and usually succeeds. Requests queued behind it time out the same way, and mutations among them, such as a save or an approval, are still applied later. A push stalled on the network ties up the connection until git dies. A credential prompt does the same: run.sh:32 starts the engine with `nohup ... &`, which keeps the launching terminal as its controlling terminal, so git's prompt there blocks indefinitely. Reconnect (app.rs:1131) stops and clears every terminal pane. Nothing is lost or corrupted.

(d) High is right under the rubric: a likely user-visible wrong result in a normal flow (a long LFS push or commit reported as an unknown outcome), plus a freeze of the window's whole control plane, approvals included, for as long as the op runs. It is not critical: there is no data loss, and terminals and agents keep running.

(e) The direction of the fix is right but it is incomplete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
1. Bounded vs unbounded ops. git.fetch is bounded: it uses output_with_timeout(20 s) with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (git.rs:938-949). git.pr.list is bounded by PR_LIST_TIMEOUT of 10 s (git.rs:83, 1094). Both can only delay other requests. The ops with no limit at all are git.push (git.rs:617) and the commit prepare phase: `git add -A` plus run_user_pre_commit.

2. The most frequent trigger is git.pr.list, not push. Every debounced Source Control refresh runs it (code_git.rs:578-583, editor.rs:508-524, app.rs:1232-1240). It should get the dedicated connection too, or the engine should cache its result.

3. git.pr.open is worse than this finding says, and it is a separate root cause. It is registered with Engine::register (git.rs:666), so `gh pr create` runs through a plain `.output()` (git.rs:679-681) while the store mutex is held. That blocks bus requests from every client, not just the window. It should be reported separately as an invariant break.

4. The fix must cover guarded()'s follow-up calls. guarded() also sends guardrail.hold.get and guardrail.confirm, and guardrail.confirm replays the held op synchronously. For a staged op such as git.commit, invoke_registered runs the prepare phase (`git add -A` and the pre-commit hook) inside the open transaction (engine.rs:325-342). So the whole guarded() flow needs the dedicated connection. The locked replay is its own invariant problem.

5. A dedicated connection alone does not fix the misreported push. Client::lifecycle_request still uses request_timeout, which gives git.push and git.commit 30 s. Add explicit client timeouts for them that match a new engine-side limit.
   - Run `git push`, `git add -A` and the user's pre-commit hook through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, as fetch already does.
   - The push limit has to be generous, minutes rather than 20 s, because LFS uploads can legitimately take that long.
   - Ideally worktree::git itself should use output_with_timeout, since stage, unstage and the in-transaction `git commit` share it.

6. Alternative fix: let the engine dispatch one connection's requests concurrently, since responses are already matched by id. This would fix every client at once, but code that relies on per-connection ordering (subscribe, attach, device.run streaming) would need review.

findings.title: Opening the diff of a large text file or any non-image binary disconnects the window from the engine
findings.evidence: open_diff only diverts files that pass `is_image(&path)` (1325); for everything else it sends `ui.call("git.diff.file", payload)` on the shared control connection (1338). The engine returns the whole HEAD blob and the whole working file, lossy-decoded, plus a unified diff, with no size or binary check (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:235-255, 842-849). The diff is computed by similar's `TextDiff::from_lines` (Myers, no deadline by default in similar 2.7). The client's reader ends the whole connection when a line exceeds MAX_LINE = 2 MiB (client.rs:48, 200-205), and app.rs:1267-1275 turns that into "Engine disconnected". The client's own `old.len() + new.len() > 1048576` check (1350) only runs after a response small enough to arrive.
findings.impact: Clicking a changed package-lock.json over about 1 MiB disconnects the window from the engine. So does a modified .uasset, .blend, .pdf or LFS-tracked asset of a few hundred KB: lossy UTF-8 plus JSON escaping inflates binaries about 2.5x, and old, new and diff are all sent. For multi-MB rewritten binaries the engine first spends minutes in the unbounded diff while the serialized connection waits. Binary assets are routine in the Unreal/Blender projects Relay targets.
findings.fix: Check size and binary status before fetching (git.diff returns `binary` and line counts; the tree has sizes). Add `max_bytes`, binary detection and a similar deadline to git.diff.file. Fetch diffs over a bounded side connection like Client::image_read, and show "binary or too large" instead of fetching.

v1.reason: open_diff (apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:1319-1365) skips only paths that pass is_image, then sends `ui.call("git.diff.file", payload)` (1338). That call goes through the shared control Client (app.rs:1111-1117). The engine's DiffFileOp handler (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:234-253) returns the whole HEAD blob and the whole working file. Both are decoded with from_utf8_lossy (git.rs:826, 845), and the handler adds a full TextDiff::from_lines unified diff. It checks neither size nor binary content, unlike git.diff, which computes `binary` (git.rs:224). The client's reader rejects any line longer than MAX_LINE = 2 MiB with Error::Protocol (client.rs:48, 200-205). The reader task then fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected (client.rs:257-263). app.rs:1267-1275 handles that by dropping the client and showing "Engine disconnected". The client's 1 MiB check (code_git.rs:1350) runs only after a response that was small enough to arrive. The row button that calls open_diff (code_git.rs:896-899) never looks at the `binary` flag; that flag is only drawn as a tag at 1508. So clicking a changed lockfile over about 1 MiB, or a binary of a few hundred KB, disconnects the window.
v1.correction: Terminal panes keep working because they use their own connections (terminal.rs:476). What drops is the window's control connection, and with it every request in flight. The 'minutes in an unbounded diff' cost is mostly theoretical: binaries have few newlines, so line tokens are few. A large text file with many edits is the real slow case, and it runs under register_unlocked, so the store mutex is not held. Fix: have the client check `binary` and the file size before fetching. Give git.diff.file a byte cap and a binary flag (the engine can return `binary: true` without the text), and set a deadline on the TextDiff config.

I measured the JSON inflation of lossy-decoded content with Python, whose escaping rules match serde_json's:

| Content | Inflation |
|---|---|
| Compressed binary (scrcpy-server jar) | 2.35x |
| Binary with many zero bytes (ELF, gguf) | 3.35x |
| JSON text | 1.1x |

| Change | Text file | Binary file |
|---|---|---|
| Small edit, new file or deleted file | about 0.9 MiB | about 310-450 KB |
| Full rewrite | about 0.45 MiB | about 150-220 KB |
