Fix: in refresh_scopes' Ok branch, if worktree is non-empty and missing from the list, fall back to the primary checkout (select_checkout("") when not dirty) and tell the user. A dirty buffer should keep its text, with a notice.

findings.title: Add/add, both-deleted and one-sided merge conflicts are shown as Added/Deleted, not as conflicts
findings.evidence: Conflict detection only looks for a U. note_changes uses `let code = if text(file, "index") == "U" { "U" } else { code };` (559), and status_letter maps only `"U" => ("!", "git-conflict", "Conflict")` (497). The explorer's file badge is the engine's single collapsed code, `if !s.worktree.is_empty() { s.worktree } else { s.index }` (git.rs:737-741). code_git's is_conflict is `index == "U" || worktree == "U"` (code_git.rs:118-120). Git's unmerged codes include AA and DD, which contain no U. A scratch repo confirmed that an add/add merge conflict prints `AA new.txt`. For UA/UD the collapsed badge is A or D.
findings.impact: Suppose two agents add the same file and their branches are merged (AA). The explorer shows a green 'A Added' badge and a 'modified' folder tint, and the Git panel lists it as an ordinary change. A file full of conflict markers can then be staged and committed without the UI ever saying 'Conflict'.
findings.fix: Add one shared helper that treats (index, worktree) in {DD, AU, UD, UA, DU, AA, UU} as a conflict, and use it in note_changes, the badge rendering and is_conflict. Have file.tree badges carry both codes, or colour file rows from CHANGED.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:106-124 parses `git status --porcelain=v1` into single-character index and worktree codes. Every conflict test looks only for 'U': code_git.rs:118-120 has `text(file, "index") == "U" || text(file, "worktree") == "U"`, project_files.rs:559 overrides only when index == "U", status_letter maps only "U" to Conflict (project_files.rs:497), and folder_status checks only for "U" (533). Git also reports unmerged paths as AA (both added) and DD (both deleted), which contain no U. An AA path has index A and worktree A. The Git panel (code_git.rs:256-260) therefore lists it under both Staged and Changes with a green 'A Added' letter instead of the Conflicts group. The explorer badge comes from status_badges (git.rs:733-743), which collapses to worktree-or-index, so it shows 'A'. For UA and UD the collapsed badge is A or D; note_changes catches those only through its index == "U" override, while the file-row badge does not. A user who stages the file through the UI resolves the conflict in git's eyes, and can then commit a file full of conflict markers without the UI ever showing 'Conflict'. AA is a realistic result when two agents in parallel worktrees create the same new file and their branches are merged.
v1.correction: Add the engine check at crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:415 (git.checkout_unmerged in git.branch.switch) to related: it has the same U-only test. Because AA and DD are tracked changes, that path still fails later as checkout_dirty, or inside git itself, with a less accurate message. DD is mostly harmless; AA is the case that matters. Fix: share one is_unmerged(index, worktree) helper covering {DD, AU, UD, UA, DU, AA, UU}, ideally computed in the engine (a `conflict: bool` on FileStatus and the badge), so that native and engine cannot diverge.

findings.title: The explorer renders every entry of a directory eagerly (about 15 widgets and controllers per row) with no cap or virtualization
findings.evidence: `for entry in entries { ... let row = button("", "tree-row"); ...}` (746-885). Each row gets a content box, chevron box, glyph box, label, badge, DrawingArea guides and an icons::image with two signal handlers. bind_tree_row adds two GestureClicks and a DragSource, plus a DropTarget for folders (project_files.rs:263-337). file.tree returns the whole directory (file.rs:508-525) over the control connection, which is capped at 2 MiB per line (client.rs:48).
findings.impact: Opening, or keeping expanded, a folder with thousands of entries (assets, fixtures, generated docs) blocks the GTK main thread on each render. Because the tree is rebuilt on every refresh, the stall repeats about once a second during agent activity. A directory of roughly 10k entries produces a file.tree response over 2 MiB, which disconnects the UI (client.rs:200-205).
findings.fix: Use gtk::ListView with a TreeListModel, which creates and recycles rows on demand. At minimum, page large directories (first N entries plus 'Show more') and ask the engine for a bounded listing.

v1.reason: render_tree (apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:735-885) builds every entry eagerly and has no cap. Each row gets a Button, a content Box, indent guides, chevron and glyph Boxes, a name Label, an optional badge Label and icon images. bind_tree_row (project_files.rs:263-337) adds two GestureClicks and a DragSource, plus a DropTarget on folders, and file rows also get bind_image_hover. The engine's list_dir (file.rs:508-525) returns the whole directory with no limit. The rebuild repeats: app.rs:1232-1239 sends every file.changed/git.changed/worktree.changed to Editor::invalidate (editor.rs:507-531). That debounces for 1 s, then calls load_tree, which clears and re-renders the root. Every expanded folder then calls toggle(true) again with loaded=false (editor.rs:851-853), so it re-fetches over file.tree and rebuilds its rows too. So an expanded large folder is rebuilt about once a second while agents edit files. The client reader rejects any frame over MAX_LINE = 2 MiB (client.rs:48, 200-205) and tears down the connection. An Entry is roughly 150-250 bytes of JSON, so a single directory of around 10k entries would exceed that.
v1.correction: The trigger is narrower than the finding implies. list_dir already drops .git, .relay and every is_generated_path directory (node_modules, target, build, dist, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache, Binaries, ...), so it takes a large hand-kept folder (icon sets, fixtures, asset dumps) to hit the stall. The repeat comes from invalidate's 1 s debounce re-fetching every expanded folder, not from a generic refresh. Cheapest useful fix: cap entries per file.tree response with a `truncated` flag plus a 'Show more' row, and refresh only changed folders rather than rebuilding every expanded one. ListView with TreeListModel is the full fix.

findings.title: The scope picker lists the primary checkout twice
findings.evidence: `let mut choices = vec![(String::new(), String::from("Primary checkout"))]; choices.extend(self.worktrees.borrow().iter().map(...))` (148-158). worktree.list always includes the primary first (`out.push(Worktree { path: canon(&primary), .. session: None .. })`, worktree.rs:139-141), and the handler returns it unchanged (git.rs:86-98).
findings.impact: The menu shows both 'Primary checkout' and '<branch> · Checkout' for the same tree. Picking the second sets `worktree` to the absolute primary path, a second identity for the same checkout: branch_holder normalizes the primary to "" and then compares it with that path (code_git.rs:946-950). It also closes the document and reloads for nothing.
findings.fix: When building choices, skip the first worktree.list row, or any row whose canonical path equals the project path.

v1.reason: scope_picker seeds `choices` with `(String::new(), "Primary checkout")` and then extends it with every worktrees row (project_files.rs:148-158). worktree.list always pushes the primary first with session None (worktree.rs:139), and worktrees_owned_by passes that row through unchanged (git.rs:55-69). The menu therefore shows "Primary checkout" and "<branch> · Checkout" for the same tree. Picking the second calls select_checkout with the absolute primary path. That clears the document, reloads, and sets a second identity for the primary that `matches()` and branch_holder (code_git.rs:932-950, which maps the primary to "" before comparing it with current) do not treat as the same.
v1.correction: The practical consequences are a confusing duplicate entry and a pointless reload. No wrong git operation was established. Fix: skip the first worktree.list row, or any row whose path equals the project path, when building choices. Alternatively, normalise the primary's path to "" in select_checkout.

findings.title: The scope picker drops its local-branch list whenever any refresh bumps scope_revision
findings.evidence: The picker captures `let revision = self.scope_revision.get();` (186) and discards the git.branches result with `if !ed.matches(&ui, project, &worktree) || ed.scope_revision.get() != revision { return; }` (195). refresh_scopes bumps scope_revision (editor.rs:916) and runs on every invalidate (editor.rs:525).
findings.impact: Opening the scope menu while agents are writing files often leaves 'LOCAL BRANCHES' empty with no error. Invalidate fires about once a second, and git.branches waits behind the refresh on the sequential connection.
findings.fix: Drop the scope_revision comparison, since matches() already guards project and checkout, or check that the popover is still alive.

v1.reason: project_files.rs:186 captures `let revision = self.scope_revision.get();` and line 195 drops the git.branches result when `ed.scope_revision.get() != revision`. refresh_scopes (editor.rs:914-917) bumps scope_revision synchronously each time it runs. invalidate (editor.rs:508-528) calls it from a 1 s debounced timer whenever the engine emits file.changed, git.changed or worktree.changed (app.rs:1232-1240) and the page is code or agents, which is where the picker lives. The engine handles one connection's requests one after another (socket.rs:335-743, each dispatch awaited before the next line is read). git.branches therefore waits behind the load_tree, refresh_git and worktree.list calls the same invalidate queued. If the timer fires at any point between opening the popover and the reply, the LOCAL BRANCHES section stays empty and shows no error. The check protects nothing the code needs: the popover is rebuilt on every open through set_create_popup_func (editor.rs:941), and matches() already guards project and checkout. The worst a late result can do is append rows to a popover that is already closed.
v1.correction: Impact is limited to the picker. Reopening it retries, so nothing is lost; it is a nuisance during heavy agent activity. The fix stands: drop the scope_revision comparison and keep matches(), or check that `pop.upgrade()` is still mapped.

findings.title: Drag-move marks the editor busy without set_busy and applies the result without a scope or dirty recheck
findings.evidence: `ed.busy.set(true);` (376) is used instead of set_busy, so the view stays editable during the move. After the await, `ed.busy.set(false)`; then, if the moved path contains the open document, it runs `ed.clear_document(); ed.open(&ui, new_path);` (379-389). is_dirty() was checked only at drop time (361), and there is no `matches(&ui, project, &worktree)` check, which every other async editor path performs.
findings.impact: Text typed into the open file while the move is queued is wiped by clear_document without a prompt. The UI connection is sequential, so the queue can last seconds when it is backlogged.
findings.fix: Use set_busy(true)/set_busy(false), and recheck matches() and is_dirty() before clear_document; reuse the shared post-move helper from the file_action finding.

v1.reason: bind_tree_drop sets `ed.busy.set(true)` directly at project_files.rs:376. set_busy (editor.rs:454-471) is the only place that sets view.set_editable(false) and turns Save and Discard off, so the source view stays editable during file.move. Save sensitivity keys on `view.is_editable()` (editor.rs:373-374), so Save stays clickable too, although save_file refuses while busy. When the move succeeds and the open document lies under the moved path, the code runs `ed.clear_document(); ed.open(&ui, new_path);` (379-389). clear_document does buffer.set_text("") and set_modified(false) with no dirty check, so anything typed during the move is discarded silently. is_dirty() was checked only at drop time (line 361). There is also no matches(&ui, project, &worktree) recheck, unlike the other async editor paths. If the user switches project while the move is pending (reset does not consult is_dirty), the callback opens the remapped path in the new project's scope.
v1.correction: The window is usually short: file.move is a rename, and it only lengthens when the sequential connection is backlogged. Losing text needs the user to type into the open file during that window, and only when the file is under the dragged path. Low severity is right. The fix is set_busy(true)/set_busy(false) (which also disables editing), plus a matches() recheck before clear_document/open.

findings.title: Opening a file leaves the cursor at the end of the buffer
findings.evidence: read_file does `e.buffer.set_text(content); e.buffer.set_modified(false);` (660-661) and never places the cursor. GTK's insert mark has right gravity: 'The standard left-to-right cursor is a mark with right gravity' (Gtk-4.0 GIR, gtk_text_buffer_create_mark), so after set_text it sits after the inserted text. rerender_diff explicitly calls `self.buffer.place_cursor(&self.buffer.start_iter())` (code_git.rs:1417).
findings.impact: The status bar reads 'Ln <last line>' for a freshly opened file. Discard (reload) jumps the caret to EOF, and keystrokes before a click land at the end of the file.
findings.fix: After set_text, place the cursor at the start, or at the requested line for search hits, and scroll_to_mark.

v1.reason: read_file calls `e.buffer.set_text(content); e.buffer.set_modified(false);` (editor.rs:660-661) and never places the cursor or scrolls. gtk_text_buffer_set_text deletes the whole buffer and inserts at the start iter. The 'insert' mark has right gravity, so it ends up after the inserted text, at EOF. The cursor-position handler (editor.rs:388-400) then shows the last line in 'Ln N, Col M'. Discard also goes through read_file (editor.rs:558-566), so it moves the caret to EOF too. rerender_diff explicitly calls place_cursor(start_iter) (code_git.rs:1417), which shows the author knew this behavior and handled it only on that path.

findings.title: Dead generality: load_tree's directory argument and open_path's worktree switch are never used
findings.evidence: Every external caller passes `load_tree(ui, None)`. The only `Some` comes from the editor's own `directory`, which is always "" after a load (518-520), and from the guard (`Some(directory.unwrap_or_default())`, 540). So `Editor::directory` (66), tree_load_next's String (37) and the parameter always carry "". open_path (898-913) is called only from the tree, with `None` (880). Its doc comment says 'Used by session file rails and task links', but commit 54e6bbc removed the last external caller (`ui.editor.open_path(&ui, path.clone(), Some(String::new()))`). That leaves the worktree-switch branch (903-911) dead. It has also already diverged from select_checkout: it does not reset expanded, selected_path, search text or the commit message.
findings.impact: Readers have to reason about a directory scope and a worktree switch that cannot happen, and the stale comment points them at callers that no longer exist. Reviving the branch would bring back stale per-checkout state.
findings.fix: Make it `load_tree(&self, ui)` with a `Cell<bool>` reload-queued flag and delete `directory`. Reduce open_path to the dirty check plus open (or call select_checkout if that feature returns), and fix the comment.

v1.reason: Editor::directory is written only at editor.rs:502 (clear) and 588 (`= directory.clone()` from load_tree's argument). Every caller passes None (editor.rs:909,962,989,1002,1103,1295,1324; code_git.rs:1278; project_files.rs:64,104,390), and the only Some values come from e.directory itself (518-520) or the guard's `Some(directory.unwrap_or_default())` (540, re-fed at 79). So the value is always "". open_path's only caller is the tree row click with `None` (editor.rs:880). Commit 54e6bbc removed `ui.editor.open_path(&ui, path.clone(), Some(String::new()))`, which leaves the worktree-switch branch (903-911) unreachable. The doc comment 'Used by session file rails and task links' is stale. The branch has also drifted from select_checkout (project_files.rs:87-110): it does not reset expanded, selected_path, the search text or the commit/branch fields.
v1.correction: No functional change. Collapse load_tree's argument and tree_load_next to a bool reload flag, delete `directory`, reduce open_path to the dirty check plus open (or route to select_checkout), and fix the comment.

findings.title: Symlinked directories are shown as files and fail to open
findings.evidence: `let directory = text(&entry, "kind") == "dir";` (748). The engine reports links as "symlink" (types.rs:870-873, file.rs:539-540), so a link to a folder gets a file row whose click calls read_file. The engine follows the link and rejects it: `if !md.is_file() { return Err(BusError::invalid("file.type", "path is not a file")) }` (file.rs:44-46).
findings.impact: Symlinked folders, common in monorepos and shared-config setups, cannot be browsed, and clicking one shows 'path is not a file'.
findings.fix: Have the engine report the link target's kind, or let the client treat a symlink to a directory as a folder row. At minimum give symlinks their own glyph and don't try to open them as text.

v1.reason: entry() (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:533-545) uses symlink_metadata, so every link is reported as EntryKind::Symlink, which serializes as "symlink" (relay-bus/src/types.rs:868-874). render_tree checks only `text(&entry, "kind") == "dir"` (editor.rs:748), so a link to a folder becomes a file row. Clicking it goes through open_path -> open -> read_file -> file.read (editor.rs:861-868, 596-637). That handler calls fs::metadata, which follows the link, and returns `BusError::invalid("file.type", "path is not a file")` (file.rs:44-46). Symlinks to files still open correctly.
v1.correction: The click path is open_path -> open -> read_file (editor.rs:868), not read_file directly. A link that points outside the worktree is rejected earlier by safe_join ('path escapes the worktree through a symlink'), so the 'not a file' error only affects in-worktree directory links. Fix: report the target kind for in-root links (or add a `target_kind` field) and render those as folder rows.

findings.title: verify_save assumes the README read finishes within 500 ms and panics otherwise
findings.evidence: smoke.rs:709-714 runs verify_open and then `glib::timeout_add_local_once(Duration::from_millis(500), move || ui.editor.verify_save(&ui))`. verify_save begins with `assert!(!self.busy.get()); assert_eq!(self.path.borrow().as_str(), "README.md");` (607-608).
findings.impact: On a loaded runner, or while the engine is still registering watchers, the read can take longer than 500 ms. The fixture smoke then aborts inside a glib callback, a flaky failure unrelated to the code under test. smoke_project_files already uses wait_for for the same wait.
findings.fix: Make verify_save async and wait with `wait_for(|| !busy && path == "README.md")`, as smoke_project_files does.

v1.reason: smoke.rs:709-714 calls verify_open, which asserts busy, and then schedules verify_save after a fixed 500 ms. verify_save then asserts `!self.busy.get()` and path == "README.md" (editor.rs:607-608). If the file.read round trip takes longer than 500 ms, or the engine is busy with watcher registration, the assert panics inside a glib callback and aborts the smoke run. smoke_project_files.rs:29 already has an async wait_for helper that it uses for the same wait (line 105).
v1.correction: Impact is small. relay-native does not build in CI, so this is a flaky local smoke run, not flaky CI. The settings smoke (smoke.rs:718-720, 700 ms) and the burst check (smoke.rs:705) use the same fixed-delay pattern.

findings.title: Icons repaint only on map and state-flag changes, so CSS class and palette changes leave them the wrong colour
findings.evidence: `image.connect_map(paint); image.connect_state_flags_changed(move |image, _| paint(image));` (231-232). paint bakes `image.color()` and `lookup_color("console")` into the SVG document (214-227). track_navigation toggles `key.add_css_class("selected")` and remove_css_class (app.rs:209-216), which switches between `button.nav { color: @secondary }` and `button.nav.selected { color: @ink }` (theme.css:31, 39) without any state-flag change. load_appearance's `ui.appearance.load_from_string(&css)` (shell.rs:1212) redefines @secondary and @console the same way.
findings.impact: After each navigation, the previously selected nav button keeps a bright icon beside a dimmed label until it is hovered. Keyboard- or engine-driven navigation leaves the new one dim. After a palette or contrast change, the settings/sliders icons keep the old console colour in their knobs.
findings.fix: Install the glyphs as symbolic icons in an icon-theme search path (as install_app_icon already does, named *-symbolic.svg) so GTK recolours them on every style change. That removes the RENDERED cache, the per-image paint closure and both handlers. Alternatively, repaint on the parent's css-classes notify and on appearance reload.

v1.reason: image_with_stroke bakes `image.color()` and the @console colour into an SVG document (icons.rs:212-228). It repaints only from connect_map and connect_state_flags_changed (icons.rs:231-232). nav_button puts such an image inside each nav button (app.rs:55-62). track_navigation toggles the button's `selected` CSS class (app.rs:204-217), and that flips the inherited colour between `button.nav` @secondary and `button.nav.selected` @ink (theme.css). A parent's CSS class change neither re-maps the child image nor changes its state flags, so the baked colour goes stale. When the user clicks X, the previously selected button Y loses `selected` and its label dims, but Y's icon keeps the @ink it was last painted with, until Y is hovered. Reloading the appearance CSS (shell.rs) has the same problem for both colours.
v1.correction: Window focus changes mitigate it: BACKDROP propagates to children and triggers state-flags-changed, so the stale colours fix themselves on the next focus-out/focus-in. The effect is purely cosmetic and transient, so low. Two fixes are reasonable: repaint when the button's css-classes change and after an appearance reload, or install the glyphs as *-symbolic icons in a theme search path so GTK recolours them.

findings.title: is_dirty() treats an in-flight read as unsaved changes, so closing the window and switching projects are refused with a misleading message
findings.evidence: `self.buffer.is_modified() || self.busy.get() || self.git_busy.get()` (452). `busy` is also set while merely reading a file (read_file, 627), an image (open_image) or a diff (open_diff). The close handler refuses with 'Save or discard your editor changes before closing.' (app.rs:1046-1049). open_project refuses with 'Save or discard editor changes before switching projects.' (shell.rs:15-18). refresh() stops at app.rs:1397-1400.
findings.impact: Closing the window or switching project while a file is still loading is refused with a message about unsaved changes that do not exist. The load can take up to the 30 s request timeout when the UI connection is backlogged.
findings.fix: Split is_dirty into has_unsaved_edits() (modified, or a write in flight) and is_loading(). Let navigation and close cancel loads by bumping the revision instead of refusing.

v1.reason: editor.rs:451-453 `is_dirty()` returns `buffer.is_modified() || busy.get() || git_busy.get()`. `busy` is set by read_file (set_busy(true) at ~627), open_image and open_diff (code_git.rs ~1334), not only by save_file. The close handler (app.rs:1046-1048), open_project (shell.rs:15-17), open_repository_in (app.rs:1691) and the removed-project path (app.rs:1397) all refuse on is_dirty() and show 'Save or discard ... changes'. While a read is in flight, closing or switching projects is refused with a message about edits that do not exist. The window is short in normal use: file.read is register_unlocked and capped at 1 MiB here. It grows only when the UI's sequential connection is backlogged (30 s client timeout).
v1.correction: Also affects app.rs:1691 (adding a project). A write or git op in flight should still block close. Only the read, image and diff loads should be cancellable by bumping `revision`. A simple fix is to have is_dirty() check modified || git_busy || a separate `writing` flag.

findings.title: Editing a CRLF file inserts LF-only lines, so the saved file has mixed line endings
findings.evidence: read_file loads the raw text with `e.buffer.set_text(content)` (660), and save_file writes `self.buffer.text(&start, &end, false)` back verbatim (689-692). There is no newline-type detection (GtkSourceFile/FileLoader is not used), and GtkTextView/GtkSourceView insert "\n" for Enter.
findings.impact: Saving a Windows-origin file (.bat, .sln, an Unreal .ini) after adding lines leaves CRLF and LF lines mixed. This shows up as diff noise and can break tools that expect one convention.
findings.fix: Detect the dominant newline on load (count "\r\n" against bare "\n") and normalize newlines to it on save or in an insert-text handler.

v1.reason: read_file puts the raw text into the GtkSourceBuffer (editor.rs:660). save_file reads `buffer.text(start, end, false)` (editor.rs:689-692) and sends it to file.write, and the handler writes p.text verbatim (fs::write of p.text.as_bytes(), file.rs ~110). Nowhere in this path is the newline convention detected or normalized; GtkSourceFile/FileLoader is not used. GtkTextView inserts "\n" for Enter. So any line added to a CRLF file is saved with a bare LF, and the file ends up with mixed line endings.
v1.correction: Pasted text keeps whatever line endings it carries, which also contributes. The fix can live in the editor (detect on load, normalize on save) without touching the engine.

results.coverage:
Read every line of all five assigned files: mirror.rs (1245), mirror/decode.rs (311), mirror/input.rs (219), mirror/glyphs.rs (68) and tools_devices.rs (893).

Supporting code traced:
- relay-native: client.rs in full; panel.rs in full; app.rs helpers, main event loop (1131-1286), main-window close handler (1032-1072), navigate/refresh/refresh_page/mutate/dismiss_panels; tools.rs helpers; icons.rs painter; main.rs; css/mirror.css.
- relay-core: handlers/device.rs (device.list, watch, mirror start/stop/input, mirror_worker, send_input, AVD handlers, run logcat, fail/advance_run); device.rs (MirrorRuntime, RunRuntime); socket.rs (mirror and run stream forwarding, per-connection WatchLease and MirrorAttachment); mirror.rs (InputMsg and encoders); device_lease.rs (lease JSON); audit.rs.
- Dependency and toolkit sources: glib-0.22.9 JoinHandle::abort / TaskSource (self-abort from inside the session task is safe); system Gtk-4.0.gir (4.22.5) DropDown docs.

Checked and found OK, not reported:
- every input `type` the client sends is a valid `InputMsg` variant;
- all `failure_title` codes and `device.none` exist in the engine;
- device.watch leases are connection-owned, so `wait_for_device` does not leak one;
- status frames carry seq 0 and bypass the Gate;
- frames can precede the device.mirror.start response, but only the status frame plus an empty history, so the 64-slot notices queue cannot deadlock;
- `device.signing.create` is `Audit::Never`, so the password is not persisted;
- no RefCell double-borrows, no Rc cycles (the run_window/open task↔panel cycle breaks on close or completion), no duplicate signal connections.
- Pedantic clippy casts in these files are bounded: dimensions ≤ 4096, clamped before `as`, u16-safe.

Not verifiable here:
- relay-native cannot be built or run in this environment, and cargo was off-limits anyway.
- GTK C behaviour was confirmed only from docs and knowledge of the source: GtkButton focus-on-click and Space/Enter activation bindings, fullscreen state updated asynchronously, DropDown filtering without an expression.
- FFmpeg's behaviour on a mid-stream resolution change (rotation) was not checked.

Out-of-chunk observations, not reported as findings:
- socket.rs:323/335 reads request lines with unbounded `BufReader::lines()`.
- MirrorRuntime::send_control (device.rs:279-283) does a blocking `write_all` with no write timeout, and device.mirror.input is answered on the connection's async task (socket.rs:735-739); not traced further.
- app.rs:1263-1265 refreshes the current page on nearly every event, which is the root of the Devices-page refresh load.

findings.title: avd.create and avd.boot run avdmanager, emulator and adb inside locked handlers with no timeout (reached from the Devices AVD form)
findings.evidence: `e.register::<AvdCreate>` (321) spawns `avdmanager create avd` and blocks on `child.wait_with_output()` (335), then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339). `e.register::<AvdBoot>` (344) calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (346). `list_avds` → `list_avds_with` runs `Command::new(emulator).arg("-list-avds").output()` (478), and `running_avds_with` runs `adb devices` plus `adb -s X emu avd name` with a bare `.output()` (505). The doc on `list_avds_with` says these calls "happen with nothing locked (D144)", which holds only for the unlocked `avd.list`. Callers in this chunk: tools_devices.rs avd_form "Create AVD" (418-422) and the Boot/Cold boot actions (106-119, 652-665). Outside the assigned chunk, reported because this chunk's UI drives it.
findings.impact: "Create AVD" holds the store mutex and the SQLite transaction for the whole avdmanager JVM run (seconds). "Boot"/"Cold boot" hold them for `emulator -list-avds` plus one `adb emu` per running emulator. Every store-touching request waits meanwhile: UI refreshes, agents' guardrail checks, MCP calls. Nothing has a timeout, so a wedged emulator console or a hung avdmanager holds the mutex indefinitely and stalls every session's bus traffic; the client's 30 s request timeout then reports an unknown outcome while the engine is still blocked.
findings.fix: Register both as `Engine::register_staged`: read the tool paths in the locked phase, and run avdmanager and `list_avds_with` in the unlocked phase. Route every one of these subprocesses through `proc::output_with_timeout`, including those in `avd.list` (478/505) and `avd.catalog` (314).

v1.reason: `e.register::<AvdCreate>` (device.rs:321) is a plain locked handler: engine.rs:478 `register` runs inside the transaction with the store mutex held (D3/D144). It spawns avdmanager and blocks on `child.wait_with_output()` (335) with no timeout. It then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339), which runs `Command::new(emulator).arg("-list-avds").output()` (478). Through `running_avds_with`, it also runs one `adb -s X emu avd name` per running emulator with bare `.output()` (505). `e.register::<AvdBoot>` (344) calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` at 346 the same way, still under the lock. The doc comment on `list_avds_with` ("happen with nothing locked (D144)") is true only for the `register_unlocked` `AvdList` (301). avdmanager is a JVM tool that takes seconds even when healthy, and `adb emu` talks to the emulator console, which can stall. Neither has a bound, so every store-touching request waits behind them, including agents' guardrail checks and UI refreshes. That breaks the CLAUDE.md rules on slow work in locked handlers and on subprocesses going through `proc::output_with_timeout` (proc.rs:28). Only `list_with_adb` (582) uses the timeout helper. Reached from the Devices page and panel (avd_form "Create AVD", Boot/Cold buttons).
v1.correction: Also affected but not in a locked handler: `AvdCatalog` (314, unlocked, `avdmanager list device -c` with bare `.output()`) and `AvdList` (unlocked) only break the timeout rule. There they hang the caller's request, not the bus. Fix: register `AvdCreate` and `AvdBoot` with `register_staged`. Read `sdk_tool`/`adb_path` under the lock, then run avdmanager and `list_avds_with` in the unlocked phase. Wrap `emulator -list-avds`, `adb emu avd name` and both avdmanager calls in `proc::output_with_timeout`. For avdmanager create, write "no\n" to stdin first, or pass `echo no |` semantics via a stdin pipe the helper supports.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims, at 361c6f9.
- `e.register::<AvdCreate>` (device.rs:321) and `e.register::<AvdBoot>` (344) are plain locked handlers. In `dispatch_inner`, engine.rs:953-980 takes `self.store.lock()`, opens the transaction, and only then calls `(h.call)`.
- AvdCreate spawns avdmanager and blocks on `child.wait_with_output()` (335) with no deadline. It then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339). AvdBoot calls the same function at 346.
- `list_avds_with` runs `emulator -list-avds` with bare `.output()` (478). Through `running_avds_with` it also runs `adb devices -l` (bounded at 2 s by `list_with_adb`, 582) and then one `adb -s X emu avd name` per running emulator with bare `.output()` (505).
- The doc comment at 475-476 ("nothing locked") holds only for `register_unlocked::<AvdList>` (301). D149's list of converted ops names `avd.list` and `avd.catalog` but not `avd.create` or `avd.boot`. There is no special routing for `avd.*` in engine.rs or socket.rs, and no DECISIONS entry accepts this.

(b) Who can trigger it and how often.
- Both ops are `Actors::UserOnly` (relay-bus ops/device.rs:55-59), so only the user can trigger them; an agent cannot.
- Reached from the native Devices page: "Create AVD" calls `ui.mutate("avd.create")` (tools_devices.rs:419). Boot and Cold boot use `tools.rs` `action`, which calls `ui.mutate` (tools_devices.rs:106-119 and 652-665).
- Create AVD is a normal but infrequent flow. Boot is common for an Android developer.

(c) What happens when it fires.
- Create AVD: the store mutex and transaction are held for the whole avdmanager JVM run plus the list probe, which is seconds.
- During that time every store-touching request on every connection waits. That includes each agent's PreToolUse hook: `guardrail.gate` goes through `check_session_token`, which locks the store (engine.rs:1373). It also includes agents' MCP calls, the phone door and the CLI.
- Not affected: keystrokes (no lock for the User actor; per-pane connection, terminal.rs:476) and PTY output (the reader takes no store lock).
- Boot: the hold is normally sub-second (up to about 2 s if the adb server is cold-starting).
- The unbounded part is `adb emu`. It reads the emulator console until EOF with no deadline. An emulator that `adb devices` still lists as "device" but whose console does not answer (stopped or frozen, or busy saving a snapshot on exit) keeps the mutex held until that emulator dies. The whole bus is frozen for every session for that time, and the UI's 30 s timeout (client.rs:70) then reports "outcome unknown".
- A hung avdmanager is less likely than the finding implies. `wait_with_output` closes stdin after the "no\n" answer, so any further prompt gets EOF.

(d) Severity: high is right. The rubric lists "a freeze of the bus" as high. Create AVD always causes a global stall of several seconds, and an uncommon emulator state makes the hang unbounded. The rare trigger and the unaffected keystrokes keep it out of critical.

(e) The fix direction is right but incomplete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
1. Make the Boot description complete. It should also mention `adb devices -l`, which is the only call on this path that is already bounded (2 s, device.rs:577-582). The unbounded calls are `emulator -list-avds` (478) and `adb emu avd name` (505). Drop "hung avdmanager" as a likely trigger, since stdin is closed after "no\n"; avdmanager's real cost is its multi-second run.

2. `register_staged` alone does not fully fix it. The socket door serves one request at a time per connection: socket.rs:334 is the `while let Some(line)` loop, and it awaits `spawn_blocking(...dispatch)` at 742 before reading the next line. The native client sends avd.create and avd.boot on its single control connection; only `is_lifecycle_request` ops get their own connection (app.rs:1111-1117).
   - After the staged change the mutex is free for everyone else, but every UI page load and refresh still queues behind the avdmanager run.
   - A run longer than 30 s still trips the client timeout.
   - To fix that too, run avdmanager on a worker after commit and report through the existing `avd.changed` event. This is D144's rule for genuinely long work, and AvdBoot already does it for the emulator launch. Alternatively, add "avd.create" to `is_lifecycle_request`.

3. `proc::output_with_timeout` forces `Stdio::null()` stdin (proc.rs:35). Moving avdmanager create onto it drops the "no\n" answer. That needs either a helper variant that takes stdin bytes, or proof that avdmanager treats EOF as the default "no"; I could not establish which holds.

4. AvdBoot's existence check needs only `emulator -list-avds` (or `<name>.ini`), not the adb probes. The staged prepare can skip `running_avds_with`.

5. Related unlocked cases are worse for the UI than the first verifier says. `avd.list` runs on every Devices page and panel refresh (tools_devices.rs:92 and 643), and `avd.catalog` runs on "Load installed images" (377). With per-connection serial dispatch, a wedged emulator console (avd.list) or a slow avdmanager (avd.catalog) stalls the native UI's whole control connection, not just one request. They do not stall the global bus.

findings.title: Devices page rebuilds the Release signing form on every engine event, discarding the alias and passwords being typed
findings.evidence: Only the header, build_form and avd_form are built once per project (23-54). Everything below is rebuilt on each call: `let list = page.last_child()...; clear(&list);` (55-56), then the "Release signing" section calls `signing_form(ui, &row, project)` (161), which creates new Entry/PasswordEntry widgets. `refresh` runs from `Ui::refresh_page`, and the main event loop calls that for nearly every event (app.rs:1263-1265 else branch). That includes `usage.changed`, which provider hooks send "on every window refresh" (audit.rs:16-17), and `device.changed`, which this page subscribes to via `device.watch` (app.rs:1339-1346). tools.rs:1 states "Forms stay mounted across engine events."
findings.impact: While an agent works in the current project (usage.changed every few seconds), or on any device, lease, run or task event, the "Create Relay signing key" expander collapses and the alias, password and confirmation being typed are thrown away. Creating a key from the page is unreliable. Each rebuild also re-runs device.list, avd.list, device.signing.get and device.run.list, spawning `adb` and `emulator -list-avds` for events unrelated to devices. Because the list is rebuilt across three awaits (92, 131, 164), a user scrolled down to "Build and run history" is pulled back up as the half-built list shrinks the scroll range.
findings.fix: Build the signing form in the stable part of the page, next to build_form/avd_form, and only update its status line on refresh. Alternatively, skip rebuilding that section while its fields have focus or content. Separately, rebuild the device sections only for device, lease, run and avd events.

v1.reason: In tools_devices.rs, only the header, build_form and avd_form sit inside the `page_projects != project` branch (23-54). Every refresh runs clear(&list) on the last child (55-56) and rebuilds the sections. When signing is not configured, that includes signing_form(ui,&row,project) (161), which creates a new Expander with fresh Entry/PasswordEntry widgets (486-500). refresh_page (app.rs:1662-1686) dispatches 'devices' to tools::refresh. The main event loop calls refresh_page for every subscribed event that is not handled in an earlier branch (app.rs:1263-1265 else). That includes usage.changed, task.changed, mailbox.*, guardrail.*, device.changed, run.changed and others. Events are dropped only when their project_id is a different project (1212-1221). usage.report sets the project to the session's project (handlers/provider.rs:82-83), so an agent working in the shown project triggers rebuilds repeatedly. Each rebuild discards the open expander and the alias and passwords being typed, which contradicts tools.rs:1 ('Forms stay mounted across engine events'). Each rebuild also re-issues device.list, avd.list, device.signing.get and device.run.list.
v1.correction: The category is bug, not data-loss: the lost data is unsaved form input. The finding applies only while the project has no Relay signing configured, because the form is shown only in the else branch at 157-162. A better fix is to build the signing form in the stable part of the page, or to skip rebuilding the list while that expander is expanded or has focus. Separately, the page could filter which events refresh it.

findings.title: Build & run target list and Run button are fixed at first page build, so a phone plugged in later can't be selected
findings.evidence: build_form runs only when `page_projects["devices"] != project` (23, 47). It fills the "Target device" ComboBoxText from that call's `devices` (301-310) and sets `key.set_sensitive(project > 0 && (op != "device.run" || target.active_id().is_some()))` once (329). Later refreshes, including those from device.changed (which the page watches), rebuild only the list below (55-91). Nothing repopulates `target` or recomputes sensitivity, and there is no `target.connect_changed`.
findings.impact: Open the Devices page with no phone, then plug one in. "Connected devices" shows it, but "Target device" stays empty and "Run on device" stays greyed out until the user clicks "Refresh devices and worktrees" or switches project. A device unplugged after the form was built stays selectable, and Run then fails with device.none in the log panel.
findings.fix: On each refresh, repopulate `target`, keeping the selected id if it is still present, and recompute the Run button's sensitivity. Also recompute it in `target.connect_changed`.

v1.reason: build_form runs only when page_projects['devices'] != project (tools_devices.rs:23, 47). page_projects keeps that value across navigation, and only the Refresh button (33) or a project switch clears it. 'Target device' is filled once from that call's devices, keeping only state=='device' (301-310). Run's sensitivity is computed once (329), and there is no connect_changed on target. Later refreshes, including those from device.changed while device.watch is on, rebuild only the list below (55-91). Trigger: visit Devices with no phone attached, then plug one in. 'Connected devices' shows it, but Target stays empty and 'Run on device' stays disabled until the user presses 'Refresh devices and worktrees'. A device unplugged after the form was built stays selectable.
v1.correction: The workaround (the Refresh button) is on the page itself, which keeps this at medium rather than high. The same staleness affects the worktree picker: worktree.changed does not reach this page anyway (the app.rs:1234-1241 branch only invalidates the editor). The fix is to repopulate target on each refresh, keeping the selected id, and to recompute Run's sensitivity there and in target.connect_changed.

findings.title: Mirror control keys keep keyboard focus after a click, so Space and Enter re-press Back, Power and the others instead of reaching the phone
findings.evidence: Every strip, rail and nav control is a plain `gtk::Button::new()` from `glyphs::key` (52-61): focusable, focus-on-click. GtkButton grabs focus on press and binds Space/KP_Space/Return/ISO_Enter/KP_Enter to "activate" in its own bubble-phase shortcut controller. The mirror's key handler is an EventControllerKey on `self.root` (mirror.rs:480-532), which sees an event only after the focused button has. A control click only sends the event (mirror.rs:374-391); focus returns to the picture only on a drag (406).
findings.impact: Click Back (or Recents, Volume, Power, Screen off), then type "hello world". The letters reach the device, but the space activates the focused button again and presses Back mid-sentence. If Power was clicked, the space turns the screen off; Enter after Home re-presses Home. Keyboard input after any mouse use of the controls is unreliable.
findings.fix: In `glyphs::key`, call `button.set_focus_on_click(false)` (or `set_focusable(false)` for rail and nav keys), or have the control click handler call `view.picture.grab_focus()` after sending.

v1.reason: glyphs::key (apps/relay-native/src/mirror/glyphs.rs:52-61) builds a plain gtk::Button and never calls set_focus_on_click(false) or set_focusable(false). A grep of mirror.rs and mirror/ finds no such call. The rail keys (power, volume, rotate, notifications, quick settings, screen off; mirror.rs:251-271), the nav keys (back, home, appswitch; 277-283) and the strip keys (shot, dock, fullscreen, close; 171-178) all come from glyphs::key. The controls' click handler (mirror.rs:374-391) only sends the event. Focus goes back to the picture only on drag_begin (406), present/detach/dock (561, 624, 650). The key handler is a bubble-phase EventControllerKey on self.root (mirror.rs:480-532), an ancestor of the focused button. A GtkButton that grabbed focus on click therefore handles Space/Return/KP_Enter through its own class activate binding before root sees the key. The button emits clicked, which calls view.send(back/power/...) again, and the key never reaches the phone. Trigger: click Power or Back, then type text containing a space or press Enter. The space re-presses that key.
v1.correction: The strip keys are affected as well: after clicking Full screen, Space toggles full screen again. The simplest fix is button.set_focus_on_click(false) inside glyphs::key, which keeps the keys reachable by Tab for accessibility. Calling view.picture.grab_focus() at the end of the controls' click handler also works.

findings.title: Docking a full-screen mirror leaves `fullscreen` set, so Esc in the dock pops it out to full screen instead of sending Back
findings.evidence: `dock()` calls `self.toggle_fullscreen()` → `window.unfullscreen()` (639-641), which only sends a request to the window system, then `self.release()` immediately destroys the window (642, 573). `view.fullscreen`, the root's "fullscreen" class and the "exit-fullscreen" glyph are updated only in `connect_fullscreened_notify` (606-617), which never fires for the destroyed window, and nothing else resets them. The strip with the Dock key stays visible in full screen (mirror.css:27 changes only stage padding). In the dock, the key handler treats `key == Escape && view.fullscreen.get()` as "leave full screen" (484), calling `toggle_fullscreen()` → `detach()` → `window.fullscreen()` (654-662).
findings.impact: Press F11 in a mirror window, then click Dock. The docked mirror keeps the 28 px full-screen padding and its key reads "Leave full screen". Pressing Esc, which is documented as Back ("Back (right-click, Esc)"), pops the mirror out of the dock into a full-screen window, sets PREFER_DOCK=false, and never sends Back.
findings.fix: In `release()` for `Host::Window` (or at the end of `dock()`), call `self.fullscreen.set(false)`, remove the "fullscreen" class, and rekey `fullscreen_key` to "fullscreen".

v1.reason: view.fullscreen, the root's 'fullscreen' class and the fullscreen_key glyph change only in connect_fullscreened_notify on the window (mirror.rs:606-617). dock() calls toggle_fullscreen() → window.unfullscreen() (639-641, 653-662), then release() at once does set_child(None) and window.destroy() (568-575). In GTK4 the fullscreened state changes only when the surface state comes back from the window system (async on X11 and Wayland), so the destroyed window's handler never resets the view. Nothing else writes view.fullscreen (grep). In the dock, the key handler's `key == Escape && view.fullscreen.get()` (484) calls toggle_fullscreen → Host::Dock → detach() → new window, not fullscreen → window.fullscreen(). Esc then pops the mirror into a full-screen window, sets PREFER_DOCK=false via detach, and sends no Back. The docked root also keeps the 28px '.mirror.fullscreen .mirror-stage' padding (mirror.css:27) and the 'Leave full screen' glyph.
v1.correction: I could not compile or run this. That the notify never fires synchronously during unfullscreen()/destroy() is inferred from GTK4 behaviour, not observed. Rated low, not medium: it needs full screen followed by Dock, recovers itself once popped out, and loses nothing. Fix: in release() for Host::Window, reset fullscreen to false, remove the 'fullscreen' class and rekey fullscreen_key.

findings.title: Closing the main window leaves mirror windows, and a docked mirror's stream, running; the process does not exit
findings.symbol: MirrorView::detach / VIEWS / main window close handler
findings.evidence: Mirror windows are application windows: `gtk::Window::builder().application(&ui.window.application().unwrap()).transient_for(&ui.window)`, with no destroy_with_parent (587-593). The main window's close handler (app.rs:1032-1072) closes panels, destroys the Notes window explicitly (1062-1064) and stops panes, but never closes mirror views. VIEWS holds every view and its session task strongly (52-57), including a docked view whose Dock lives in the main window's overlay (643).
findings.impact: With a mirror window open, closing Relay's main window leaves the process running with an orphan mirror window. Its engine connection, the scrcpy server on the phone and FFmpeg keep streaming. A docked mirror inside the destroyed main window keeps streaming invisibly until the last mirror window is closed. Once the `Ui` has been dropped, Retry (`start`, 707), Dock (628/584) and the device picker (956, stuck on "Loading devices…") in the orphan window do nothing.
findings.fix: Add `mirror::close_all()`, which calls `close()` on every view in VIEWS, and call it from the main window's close handler next to the Notes cleanup. Alternatively, set `destroy_with_parent(true)` on mirror windows and close docked views explicitly.

v1.reason: Mirror windows are application windows: `.application(&ui.window.application().unwrap()).transient_for(&ui.window)` with no destroy_with_parent (mirror.rs:587-593). GTK4 transient windows are not destroyed with their parent unless that is set. The main window's close_request (app.rs:1032-1070) closes panels and note drafts, and explicitly destroys the Notes window (1062-1064), a precedent for exactly this problem. It drops the client and stops panes, but never touches mirror::VIEWS (no `mirror::` call anywhere outside tools_devices.rs:82/751). Each mirror session opens its own engine connection (start → session(..., ui.rt, ui.path ...)), so dropping ui.client does not stop it. Closing the main window with a mirror window open therefore leaves the application alive with that window still streaming, plus any docked view whose widgets lived in the destroyed main window, until the user closes the orphan.
v1.correction: Narrower than claimed. With only a docked mirror and no mirror window, no application window remains, so the process exits and nothing leaks. The orphan stays visible and the user can close it, after which the app exits. Fix: add mirror::close_all() and call it in the close handler next to the Notes cleanup.

findings.title: Device control is implemented twice (Devices page and footer panel), and the copies already disagree
findings.impact: Every device fix or feature has to be made twice and already lands inconsistently: the same toggle has two names, and the busy-device warning and AVD errors exist on only one surface. The 296- and 213-line functions also hide the staleness bugs reported here.
findings.fix: Extract shared builders and call them from both surfaces: `avd_rows(ui, parent, avds)`, `device_target(devices) -> ComboBoxText` (with the in-use mark), `signing_section(ui, parent, project, signing)`, `run_payload(...)` and `is_active(state)`. Keep only the layout differences in `open()` and `refresh()`.

v1.reason: The panel `open()` (tools_devices.rs:595-893) does rebuild pieces of `refresh()`/`build_form()` instead of sharing them. AVD rows are at 98-119 and 644-667, the target combo at 302-308 and 694-702, the signing toggle at 140-153 and 769-784, and the active-state `matches!` at 204-207 and 829-834. Some copies really disagree: the same `device.signing.set_enabled` toggle is labeled "Use project signing" on the page and "Use Gradle signing" in the panel. Only the panel marks a leased device " · in use". The panel drops `avd.list` errors (`if let Ok(v)` at 643), while the page shows "Virtual devices unavailable" (124-126). The bulkiest parts are already shared, though: `lease_row`, `signing_form`, `avd_form`, `WorktreePicker` and `run_window`. What is still duplicated is roughly 60 lines of small widget code, and the divergences cost little: one label wording, one missing error line, one missing busy mark. The page also shows lease rows directly under each device, so busy devices are visible there anyway.
v1.correction: Two of the listed "divergences" are intentional. The panel's aab default sits in its RELEASE tab (Play upload), while the page's generic "Build artifact" defaults to a debug variant and apk. "Cold" vs "Cold boot" is a narrow 430px panel vs a full page. Neither is a bug. The real divergences are the signing label, the dropped avd.list error and the missing in-use mark. Downgrade to low: the fix is to extract `avd_rows` and `signing_toggle` (and maybe `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES`), not a full shared-builder refactor. Native code: cannot be compiled in a headless session.

findings.title: Refused mirror input is logged only at debug level; a broken control socket leaves a live picture that ignores every tap
findings.evidence: `Err(error) => tracing::debug!(%error, "mirror input refused")` (1156-1160). The engine returns `device.input_failed` when the scrcpy control-socket write fails (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:954-955) but keeps the video worker running, so the session never ends.
findings.impact: If the device-side control channel dies, or an event's JSON stops matching `InputMsg`, the mirror keeps showing video while every tap, key and hardware button silently does nothing. No hint or card is shown.
findings.fix: On a refusal, flash the error in the hint line (rate-limited). On `device.input_failed`, end the session with a card that offers Retry.

v1.reason: The trigger I could not establish is the control socket dying while the video keeps running. In the engine (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:808-830), video and control are two connections to the same scrcpy server through one adb forward. scrcpy's server shuts down as a whole when any of its processors ends, so the mirror then fails or is lost, and the client receives a terminal status and shows a card. The other refusals are `device.input` invalid errors: a coordinate outside the display during a rotation race (event_coordinate, device.rs:912), or JSON that no longer matches InputMsg. The first loses one tap harmlessly, and a flash would not help the user act. The second is developer-time drift, which is the test-gap finding (#17). The log level makes no difference in a GUI app, whose users do not read logs either way.
v1.correction: If kept at all, it belongs under #17's drift concern. A real dead-control-socket case would already surface as a mirror failed or lost status.

findings.title: Screenshot is PNG-encoded and written synchronously on the GTK thread, and a destination with no local path is silently ignored
findings.evidence: After the file dialog, `let Some(path) = file.path() else { return };` (941) drops any GIO location without a local path, with no message. `texture.save_to_png(&path)` (943) encodes and writes on the main loop.
findings.impact: Choosing a network/GVFS location that has no FUSE path saves nothing and reports nothing. Saving to a slow or FUSE-mounted path freezes the whole UI (main window and every mirror) until the write finishes.
findings.fix: Use `texture.save_to_png_bytes()` with `file.replace_contents_future(bytes, None, false, gio::FileCreateFlags::REPLACE_DESTINATION)`, which is async and works for any GFile, and flash the error on failure.

v1.reason: apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:941 `let Some(path) = file.path() else { return };` returns silently, and line 943 `texture.save_to_png(&path)` encodes and writes on the GTK main loop inside glib::spawn_future_local. Only the dialog is awaited; the save itself is synchronous. Encoding a full-resolution phone frame (about 1080x2400) costs a noticeable stall, and a slow or FUSE destination makes it longer. The no-path case is rare in practice: portal-backed dialogs return document-portal FUSE paths, and GVFS locations get a path whenever gvfs-fuse is running. So the silent drop is a corner case, and the stall is short and happens only when the user saves a screenshot.
v1.correction: The impact is a short, user-initiated UI stall and a rare silent no-op, not a general freeze. The proposed fix (save_to_png_bytes plus File::replace_contents_future, and flashing the error in the None branch) is sound. Note that save_to_png_bytes still encodes on the main thread, so only the write becomes async; moving the encode off-thread needs the texture downloaded first. This is native-client code that cannot be compiled in this environment.

findings.title: Mirror key-up events are recomputed from release-time modifiers, leaving keys stuck down or sending lone key-ups
findings.evidence: Press sends DOWN for `input::keycode(key).or_else(|| (ctrl || alt).then(|| input::chord_keycode(key)).flatten())` (508). Release recomputes that expression from the release event's modifiers (526-529) instead of remembering what was sent. Press also intercepts Escape-in-full-screen (484-487) and Ctrl+V (493-505) without sending a DOWN, while release excludes only F11 (523).
findings.impact: Press Ctrl+A and release Ctrl before A: the device gets DOWN(KEYCODE_A, CTRL) and never an UP, so its input state keeps A pressed. Esc to leave full screen sends a lone UP for KEYCODE_BACK, and Ctrl+V sends a lone UP for KEYCODE_V with CTRL. Android usually drops such events, but the key stream is malformed and effects vary by app.
findings.fix: Record, per hardware keycode (the `keycode` callback argument), the Android keycode sent on press, e.g. in a `RefCell<HashMap<u32, u32>>`. On release, send UP only for a recorded entry and remove it; clear the map when a session ends.

v1.reason: mirror.rs:482-517 key_pressed: F11, and Escape while `view.fullscreen` is set, call toggle_fullscreen and return before any DOWN (484-487). Ctrl+V reads the clipboard and returns without a DOWN (493-505). Otherwise DOWN goes out for `input::keycode(key).or_else(|| (ctrl||alt).then(|| chord_keycode(key)).flatten())` (508). key_released (519-529) skips only F11 and non-Live phases, then works the code out again from the release event's own modifiers. input.rs:92-132: keycode(Escape)=4 (BACK), and letters get a code only via chord_keycode with Ctrl or Alt held. So Ctrl+A with Ctrl let go first gives DOWN(29) and no UP, because at release ctrl is false and keycode(a) is None. Esc that leaves full screen gives a lone UP(4). Ctrl+V gives a lone UP(KEYCODE_V, CTRL). Nothing remembers what was pressed. Real-world effect is small: Android's InputDispatcher drops a key-up with no matching down ('inconsistent key up'), and it sends cancels for tracked downs when focus changes. So this is a malformed stream with rare visible effects.
v1.correction: Rare and mostly absorbed by Android's input consistency checks, so it stays low. Fix as proposed: keep a map from hardware keycode to the Android keycode sent on press, send UP only for a recorded entry, and clear the map in start()/close().

findings.title: Docking a mirror closes every panel, including an open build/logcat log that cannot be reopened
findings.evidence: `let _ = ui.dismiss_panels();` (631) closes all panels (app.rs:1287-1297), though the comment intends only the Devices panel. Closing a `run_window` panel aborts its log task (tools_devices.rs:482), and the UI has no way to reattach to a run's log. The result is ignored: with an unsaved panel the user gets "Save or discard your changes before leaving this page." while the dock opens anyway.
findings.impact: Start "Run debug" (the log panel opens), then click Dock on the mirror window to watch the app beside the wall. The build/logcat log disappears for good while the run continues.
findings.fix: Close only the "Device control" panel (look it up by title), or nothing, since the dock sits outside the panel stack. Don't show the unsaved-changes error from a mirror action.

v1.reason: dock() calls `let _ = ui.dismiss_panels();` (mirror.rs:631), which closes every panel in ui.panels (app.rs:1287-1297), not just the Devices panel the comment names. run_window opens a Panel (tools_devices.rs:428-429), and closing it aborts the log task (`window.on_closed(move || task.abort())`, ~482). The panel's own text says the run stays active. The build/run history (tools_devices.rs:165-200) lists runs with no log view, so the streamed log cannot be reattached. A mirror window is a separate toplevel, so its Dock key can be clicked while a run log panel is open in the main window. If a panel refuses to close, dismiss_panels shows 'Save or discard your changes before leaving this page.' and the dock still opens, because the result is ignored.
v1.correction: Low as rated. Close only the device-control panel by title, or rely on the dock overlay, and skip the error message for this path.

findings.title: Device control footer panel never reflects its own actions (Release, Stop, Boot, signing key)
findings.evidence: The panel's buttons go through `ui.mutate` (tools.rs:34-49, tools_devices.rs:581-592), which refreshes the main page and registry (app.rs:1118-1130) but not this panel. The panel's content is built once in its spawned future (626-890). signing_form's success path calls `ui.refresh_page()` (537), which also skips the panel.
findings.fix: Give `open()` a rebuild closure and call it after its own mutations, or on device.lease.*, run.changed, avd.changed and device.signing.changed while the panel is open. Reuse the shared builders proposed in the duplication finding.

v1.reason: `action()` (tools.rs:34-49) and `action_quiet()` (tools_devices.rs:581-592) both call `ui.mutate`, which on success runs `ui.refresh()` and `ui.refresh_page()` (app.rs:1118-1130). `refresh_page` only refreshes the main page named by `ui.page` (app.rs:1662-1686). The panel's widgets are built once, inside the `glib::spawn_future_local` in `open()` (626-890), and nothing rebuilds them. I grepped the native client: no event handler for device.changed, run.changed, avd.changed, device.lease.* or device.signing.changed touches the panel. app.rs:1188-1192 only calls `refresh_status()`. The only way to rebuild is the header refresh button (`dismiss_panels()` then `open`). So after Release, Stop, Boot or signing-key creation in the panel, its rows stay stale.
v1.correction: For Boot, part of the staleness is unavoidable: `running_serial` appears only after the emulator has registered with adb, so even a rebuild right after `avd.boot` would still offer Boot. The fix needs the panel to rebuild on `avd.changed`/`device.changed` events, not only after its own mutation. Rebuild the panel body from a closure, triggered by its own mutations and by those events while it is open. Native code: cannot be compiled here.

findings.title: Run log panel never updates its status and does not follow new output
findings.evidence: `status` is set once to "Run #N · <state>" (445) and afterwards only on disconnect (471). The engine's run stream on this connection carries only log lines (crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:667-711); state changes go to the main UI connection as run.changed. Lines are appended at `buffer.end_iter()` (456-461) and the view is never scrolled to the end.
findings.impact: After a build finishes or fails, the panel still says "Run #12 · building". While Gradle or logcat output streams, the view stays at the top, so the newest lines (including the failure the user is waiting for) stay off-screen until scrolled to.
findings.fix: Subscribe this connection to `run.changed` and filter by run id (or poll device.run.list) to update `status`. After each insert, scroll to an end mark if the view was already at the bottom.

v1.reason: run_window sets status once from the request result (tools_devices.rs:445). After that it is updated only on Notice::Disconnected (470-472). The run's dedicated connection receives only 'logcat' frames from the attached run (socket.rs:647-711) and subscribes to nothing else, so no state change ever reaches it. Lines are inserted at end_iter (456-461) and nothing calls scroll_to_mark or scroll_to_iter. app::scrolled (app.rs:69-75) is a plain ScrolledWindow, and the TextView is not editable with its cursor at the start, so the view does not follow new output. On failure the engine pushes '{code}: {message}' into the log (handlers/device.rs:2156), but that line arrives at the bottom, off-screen, while the status still reads 'Run #N · building'.
v1.correction: Fix the status by subscribing this client to run.changed and filtering by run id, or by watching for the final log line. Fix the scrolling by keeping an end mark and calling scroll_mark_onscreen after each insert when the view was already at the bottom.

findings.title: Rotation resize swaps the window's axes without clamping to the monitor
findings.evidence: On an orientation change, `window.set_default_size(phone_h + CHROME_W, phone_w + CHROME_H)` (899-901) just swaps the current phone area. The initial size from `window_size` is clamped to 560..=960 px tall (688).
findings.impact: If the window first opened while the device was in landscape (about 1816×918 on a 1080p monitor, per 693), rotating to portrait requests about 878×1856, pushing the nav bar and hint line off-screen.
findings.fix: Clamp the new height to the same monitor-derived bound `window_size` uses, and derive the width from the picture's aspect ratio.

v1.reason: set_dims (mirror.rs:887-903) swaps the current phone area on rotation: set_default_size(phone_h + CHROME_W, phone_w + CHROME_H), with no clamp. window_size clamps height to 85% of the monitor, within 560..=960 (688). A landscape-shaped window gives ~1816x918 on a 1080p monitor for a 2400x1080 device; rotating to portrait then asks for ~878x1856, taller than the screen. Whether the window manager constrains this depends on the compositor.
v1.correction: The trigger is narrower than 'first opened in landscape'. On a fresh open, dims is (0,0), so window_size uses the 9:19.5 portrait default, and the first landscape frame does not count as a rotation (ow==0). A portrait window rotating twice round-trips correctly (455x918 → 878x495 → 455x918). An oversized request needs a landscape-shaped window first: undocking or moving a dock out (detach → window_size with known landscape dims) while the device is in landscape, or a user-enlarged window. Fix: clamp the new height to the window_size bound and derive the width from the aspect ratio.

findings.title: Worktree picker enables search without an expression, so typing in the search field filters nothing
findings.evidence: The picker is built with `gtk::DropDown::from_strings(...)` and `widget.set_enable_search(true)` (238-241), but `set_expression` is never called. The installed GTK 4.22.5 GIR documents that "[property@Gtk.DropDown:expression] must be set for search to work". The smoke check only asserts `enables_search()` (288).
findings.impact: The worktree picker shows a search field for long worktree lists, but typing into it doesn't narrow the list.
findings.fix: Call `widget.set_expression(Some(gtk::PropertyExpression::new(gtk::StringObject::static_type(), None::<gtk::Expression>, "string")))`, and extend the smoke test to type a query and assert the filtered count.

v1.reason: WorktreePicker::new (tools_devices.rs:238-241) uses gtk::DropDown::from_strings and set_enable_search(true), and never calls set_expression. In gtk4-rs 0.11.4, from_strings is a direct binding of gtk_drop_down_new_from_strings, which passes no expression. The installed GTK 4.22.5 GIR (/usr/share/gir-1.0/Gtk-4.0.gir, set_enable_search doc) says: 'Note that [property@Gtk.DropDown:expression] must be set for search to work.' The expression property doc says the same. Without an expression the popup's filter matches every item, so the search entry is shown but narrows nothing. The smoke check (288) asserts only enables_search().
v1.correction: I could not read the gtkdropdown.c source on this machine, so this rests on the installed GTK documentation and not on the code. The fix is set_expression(Some(gtk::PropertyExpression::new(gtk::StringObject::static_type(), None::<gtk::Expression>, "string"))). The custom factory that is already set keeps rendering as it does now.

findings.title: glyphs.rs copies the icons.rs SVG painter but not its render cache, re-parsing an SVG on every hover, focus or window-focus change
findings.evidence: `glyphs::image` (34-49) is the same painter as `icons::image_with_stroke` (icons.rs:222-233): same SVG template, `connect_map` plus `connect_state_flags_changed`. It calls `gtk::Svg::from_bytes(...)` directly (43) instead of icons.rs's `rendered()` cache (icons.rs:6-26), whose comment says the cache exists because icons "repaint on map and on every state change". Geometry is duplicated too: "device", "close", "check" and "chevron-down" are identical in both tables, and the glyph "retry" is icons.rs "refresh".
findings.impact: Each mirror view has about 20 glyphs. Every state-flag change (hover, press, focus, and the BACKDROP flag on every window focus change) parses a new SVG for each glyph, the overhead icons.rs already removed. The two shape tables can also drift apart.
findings.fix: Expose a geometry-taking painter from icons.rs, e.g. `icons::image_from_geometry(shape, size, stroke)` that uses the same cache, and keep only the mirror-specific shapes in glyphs.rs.

v1.reason: apps/relay-native/src/mirror/glyphs.rs:34-49 repeats the icons.rs painter: the same SVG template, connect_map, and connect_state_flags_changed. It calls `gtk::Svg::from_bytes` on every repaint (line 43) instead of going through icons.rs's thread-local `rendered()` cache (icons.rs:6-26), which exists precisely because icons repaint on every state change. Shapes are duplicated byte for byte: close (icons.rs:74), chevron-down (136), check (155), and glyphs "retry", which is identical to icons "refresh" (180). glyphs::rekey (64) also rebuilds images on every display toggle. The performance cost is small, since these are tiny SVGs, about 20 per mirror window on hover and backdrop changes. The main payoff is one painter and one cache.
v1.correction: The impact is mostly maintainability, with a minor parse overhead, not a measurable slowdown. Fix: have icons.rs expose `image_from_geometry(shape: &'static str, size, stroke)` that goes through `rendered()`, keep only the mirror-specific shapes in glyphs.rs, and map retry, close, check, chevron-down and device to the icons.rs names. This is native-client code that cannot be compiled in this environment.

findings.title: Mirror protocol logic and the client's input wire format never run in CI
findings.evidence: The Gate, ppm and decoder_bytes tests in decode.rs (245-311) and the coalesce and map_point tests in input.rs (149-219) live in relay-native, which CI never builds (Cargo.toml default-members; .github/workflows/ci.yml:69-82). decode.rs depends only on tokio, base64 and `client::Notice`, not GTK. No engine test pins the JSON the client sends for `quicksettings` (mirror.rs:255), `resetvideo` (1153) or `scroll` (472): those literals appear nowhere in relay-core/tests or src/mirror.rs.
findings.impact: A change to the sequence-gap logic, the PPM parser, or an `InputMsg` variant's name or fields passes CI and silently breaks the mirror. Refused input is hidden at debug level (see the error-handling finding).
findings.fix: Move the GTK-free pieces (Gate, decoder_bytes, ppm, coalesce, map_point) into a module or crate that the default members build. Add engine tests that deserialize the exact event JSON the native client sends.

v1.reason: Cargo.toml:5 default-members excludes apps/relay-native, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:69-90 documents that relay-native is not built in CI. So the decode.rs tests (Gate, ppm, decoder_bytes) and the input.rs tests (coalesce, map_point) never run there. On the engine side, crates/relay-core/tests/mirror.rs:424-460 round-trips InputMsg through serde (to_string then from_str), which does not pin the literal tag strings. A renamed variant or a changed rename_all would still pass, while the native client's hard-coded literals (`{"type":"scroll",...}` at mirror.rs:472, `"resetvideo"` at 1153, and key.widget_name() at 388, which covers quicksettings and the others) would start failing at runtime. Only a few literal-JSON tests exist (`getclipboard` at tests/mirror.rs:420; tap, touch and text in integration tests at 735-792).
v1.correction: The CI exclusion is deliberate and documented (it is a GTK version gap), so the cheap win is the second half of the fix: add relay-core tests that deserialize the exact literal JSON the native client sends (scroll, resetvideo, quicksettings, displaypower, setclipboard with paste, key, keypress, back, home, appswitch, and so on). Moving decode.rs and input.rs into a headless crate is a bigger optional step. Note that input.rs map_point may depend on GTK types, which I did not verify.

findings.title: Mirror stream has exits that can never fire: `paint` ends in pending(), and `frames.is_closed()` is never true
findings.evidence: The `paint` future always ends in `std::future::pending::<()>().await` (1111-1119), so the select arm `_ = paint => End::Broken(String::new())` (1167) never fires. In decode.rs:195, `frames.is_closed()` cannot be true while `pump` itself holds `stale`, a receiver of the same channel (164/176), so the read loop never stops on its own. The `End::Broken(String::new())` values at 1095 and 1129 are discarded, because `session` returns as soon as `alive()` is None.
findings.impact: These exits make it look as if a session can end through them, when teardown actually relies entirely on `AbortOnDrop` and task abort. The extra select arm and channel checks are noise in the mirror's busiest code.
findings.fix: Remove the `paint` select arm (keep `paint` as a plain loop), drop the `is_closed()` check, and document that the worker ends only through AbortOnDrop or a terminal status.

v1.reason: The `_ = paint => ...` arm in the tokio::select! at mirror.rs:1167 is the only thing that polls the `paint` future, so it is not dead. Removing it, as the fix proposes, would stop frames from being painted. `paint` ends in `std::future::pending()` on purpose, so that a closed picture channel or a vanished view does not end the select before `watch` reports the real reason. Only the value expression on that arm is unreachable, which is the normal pattern. The `End::Broken(String::new())` returns at 1095 and 1129 are not dead either: they are the sentinel for 'view gone or superseded'. session() (1022-1024) correctly discards them because `alive()` is None, and start()/close() (706-713, 668-671) abort the task, as designed. What is left is decode.rs:195 `frames.is_closed()`. That check is indeed always false while pump holds the `stale` receiver, but it is one redundant condition: the read loop still ends when ffmpeg is killed or the task is aborted. That is not worth a finding.
v1.correction: If anything, the only true dead code is the `&& frames.is_closed()` condition at apps/relay-native/src/mirror/decode.rs:195, which is negligible. The paint select arm must stay.

results.coverage:
I read every line of all four assigned files: note_pages.rs (1457 lines), notes_window.rs (225), note_pages/menu.rs (483) and note_pages/glyphs.rs (79). Nothing was compiled or run, as the rules required.

To trace callers and callees I also read:
- In full: note_pages/doc.rs, note_pages/text.rs, pages.rs, icons.rs.
- In part: task_pages.rs 1-330 (Draft); app.rs 1-110, 355-370, 615-650, 1000-1190, 1195-1290, 1290-1445, 1542-1566, 1655-1697; client.rs request timeouts; shell.rs open_project and load_appearance; shell/registry.rs 590-696; smoke_notes.rs 1-260.

Not fully verified:

Observations outside this chunk that I did not file:
- doc::request_close with autosave on calls save(then close). Draft::close silently refuses if the text changed during the save, because its status label was removed from the layout in doc::build. Ctrl+W then appears to do nothing (doc.rs:1285-1287, task_pages.rs:160-163, doc.rs:304).
- app.rs:1062-1064 keeps notes_window.borrow_mut() alive across notes.window.destroy() (a temporary in an if-let condition, edition 2021). It is safe today only because no callback run during destroy borrows notes_window.

findings.title: Notes window keeps listing a removed project: after removal every main-window refresh shows a not-found error, and that project's open notes can't be saved
findings.evidence: refresh_notes only fills in a zero project, with `if window.project.get() == 0 { window.project.set(ui.project.get()); }` (172-174), then lists it with `ui.call("notes.list", json!({"project_id":project}))` (208). Nothing checks that window.project still exists. project.remove deletes the notes and the project row (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:366,380). From then on notes.list fails in assert_actor_project -> get_project with project.not_found (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:340, workspace.rs:41). Once any render has happened, the Err arm runs `ui.show_error(&error.to_string())` (218). The main window handles removal of its own project (app.rs:1391-1410). registry_removed only moves ui.project (shell/registry.rs:678-695). Nothing touches NotesWindow.project. refresh_notes runs at the end of every Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440) and on every notes.* event (app.rs:1209-1211), whether or not Notes is visible. The window is created at startup (app.rs:366).
findings.impact: Trigger: remove the project the Notes window last showed. This is often the project you were working in, because show_notes points Notes at ui.project. After that, every Ui::refresh pops 'NotFound project.not_found: no project N' in the main window. Ui::refresh runs on project/workspace events, on session events not applied in place (app.rs:1225,1230) and after every successful ui.mutate button (app.rs:1124). This continues until the user opens Notes and picks another project, or restarts. Inside Notes, Ctrl+N fails because new_note posts notes.create to the dead project. The stale library and picker still list the removed project. An open draft of that project can't be rescued in-app: Save gives notes.not_found, then 'Save as new note' sends notes.create into the removed project and fails again. If that draft is dirty and hidden, it also blocks quitting (see the hidden-drafts finding).
findings.fix: In refresh_notes, before listing, check whether window.project is in ui.projects. If it is not, or if notes.list returns project.not_found, set window.project to ui.project and loop again; when that is 0, show an empty state. When a project disappears, resolve its docs: offer to save each dirty one as a new note in the project now shown, or to discard it.
