Then remove them from DOCS and note_drafts so they stop blocking quit.

v1.reason: notes_window.rs:172-177 only fills window.project when it is 0. Nothing ever resets it: the only writers are show_project (when project != 0) and that fallback, and registry_removed (shell/registry.rs:662-695) and the removed-project branch of Ui::refresh (app.rs:1391-1410) only move ui.project. project.remove deletes the notes and then the project row (workspace.rs:360,368). notes.list starts with assert_actor_project -> get_project, which returns project.not_found (notes.rs:47-48,339-340; workspace.rs:37-40). Ui::refresh calls refresh_notes at app.rs:1440 whenever ui.project != 0. The notes.changed/notes.deleted event branch calls it unconditionally (app.rs:1208-1211). After any successful render rendered_project != 0, so the Err arm calls ui.show_error (notes_window.rs:213-218). The repeated main-window error is therefore real. It continues after every mutate (app.rs:1124), every project/workspace event and every session event not applied in place, until the user picks another project in Notes or restarts. new_note uses current_project(), which is the shell's stale project (note_pages.rs:318-325), so notes.create targets the removed project and fails. doc.rs:1207 'save as new' uses doc.project and fails the same way.
v1.correction: Minor: when the removed project was the last one, ui.project becomes 0 and Ui::refresh `continue`s before refresh_notes (app.rs:1416-1419). In that case the spam comes only from notes.* events. The picker in Notes goes stale because it is rebuilt only on a successful render (note_pages.rs:1121-1122). Fix as proposed: in refresh_notes, if window.project is not in ui.projects (or notes.list returns project.not_found), fall back to ui.project, or to an empty state when that is 0. Then decide what happens to that project's open docs.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. NotesWindow.project has only two writers: show_project, when project != 0 (notes_window.rs:162-163), and the zero fallback (172-174). registry_removed (shell/registry.rs:663-696) and the removed-project branch of Ui::refresh (app.rs:1391-1410) move only ui.project. project.remove hard-deletes the notes (workspace.rs:366) and the project row (380), and emits only project.deleted (382), with no notes.* event. notes.list goes through assert_actor_project and get_project, which returns project.not_found (notes.rs:340, 47-48; workspace.rs:38-41). rendered_project is set on every successful render (note_pages.rs:1112) and never cleared, so the Err arm calls ui.show_error (notes_window.rs:217-218). The banner reads "NotFound project.not_found: no project N" (relay-bus error.rs:49). The window exists from startup (app.rs:366, ui.project starts at 0 at app.rs:742). refresh_notes runs at the end of Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440) and on every notes.changed/notes.deleted event from any project (app.rs:1208-1211), whether or not Notes is visible. There is no hot loop, because pending stays false after the Err.

(b) Reachability. The desktop user removes a project through the sidebar dialog, which always sends force=true (registry.rs:618-644), or removes its workspace, or removes it from another client. It fires only when the removed project is the one Notes holds. By default that is the first-listed project at startup (there is no last-project restore). Otherwise it is the main window's project when Notes was last opened from the main window, or the last project picked in Notes. Removing a project is an occasional cleanup action, not an everyday flow. smoke_registry.rs:112 removes a project Notes is not showing, so this path is untested.

(c) What happens. Right after a successful removal the main window shows the 6-20 s banner, which reads as if the removal failed. It comes back on each project switch (shell.rs:34), each launch (launch.rs:825), each mutate button (app.rs:1124), each project/workspace event and each notes.* event anywhere. In Notes, the library and picker still show the deleted project. Ctrl+N and duplicate fail, because current_project reads the stale shell.project (note_pages.rs:318-325). For an open dirty draft of that project, Save returns notes.not_found (doc.rs:1171-1174). "Save as new note" then posts notes.create with doc.project (doc.rs:1207) and fails. The text stays in the editor and can be copied, so this bug loses no data; project.remove deleting the notes is designed behavior. Nothing in the main window stops working. The state ends with one ordinary click on the main window's Notes button (app.rs:820-835, then toggle_page, show_notes and show_project(ui.project), notes_window.rs:153-164). Picking another project in the stale picker (pages.rs:236) or restarting also ends it; window.project is not persisted.

(d) Severity is medium, not high. This is a real, reproducible bug, but in a less common path, conditional on Notes holding that project. The effect is a recurring spurious banner plus a stale Notes view. There is no data loss, no freeze, and recovery takes one click.

(e) The fix's direction is right but needs care; details are in the correction.
v2.correction:
Severity should be medium.

Recovery is easier than the finding says. Clicking Notes in the main window (or Notes in the page list) resets window.project through show_notes. The finding says the state lasts until the user picks a project inside Notes or restarts.

"Every Ui::refresh" is too broad in two ways:
- Refreshes with ui.project == 0 skip refresh_notes (app.rs:1416-1419), as do those that break early on a dirty editor (app.rs:1397-1399).
- Session events rarely cause a refresh, because full session.changed rows are applied in place (agent_menu.rs:99-137).

The quit-blocking point belongs to the hidden-drafts finding. While Notes is stuck on the dead project, that project's tabs stay visible, and the deleted notice offers Close (doc.rs:1185-1194).

Fix requirements:
1. Trigger the fallback on the project.not_found code from notes.list, or on the ids from registry_removed / project.deleted. Do not rely only on ui.projects membership, which can be stale when refresh_notes runs from note actions or events.
2. Fall back only to a project that is in ui.projects and differs from the dead id; otherwise show an empty state. Otherwise the retry loops forever whenever ui.project is still the dead id: with a dirty editor, open_project refuses to switch (shell.rs:15-17) and Ui::refresh breaks early (app.rs:1397-1399).
3. For the empty state, also clear shell.project, rendered_project and the library rows, so new_note stops targeting the dead id.
4. Resolving the dead project's docs is required. A successful fallback render hides every doc with doc.project != project (note_pages.rs:1125-1126). A hidden dirty draft then blocks quit (app.rs:1037-1044) with no way back to it, so a naive fix makes things worse. Saving into the shown project needs save_as to take a target project, because Doc.project is a plain i64 (doc.rs:18) and save_as posts doc.project (doc.rs:1207).
5. Optionally, prune the dead project's entry from the persisted SESSION tabs map.

A separate issue, not this root cause: the removal dialog never says that notes, tasks and modules are deleted. It says only "Repository files are never touched." (registry.rs:566-572).

findings.title: A failed first settings.get still marks Notes as loaded, so the first render overwrites saved Notes prefs, library rail and per-project tabs with defaults
findings.evidence: The code is `if !window.restored.replace(true) { if let Ok(value) = ui.call("settings.get", ...).await { ... restore_state(...) } window.loaded.set(true); if window.persist_wanted.replace(false) { window.persist(&ui); } }` (188-205). An Err is ignored, but `loaded` is still set. `restored` is already true, so the read is never retried. This breaks the contract stated in the field's own comment: `/// Settings were read; until then a persist would overwrite them with defaults.` (15). The first workspace() then calls `shell.split.set_position(owner.rail_width.get())` (note_pages.rs:1114). GtkPaned always notifies `position` there, and the handler calls `owner.persist(&ui)` (note_pages.rs:565-573). 300 ms later settings.set writes rail_width 270, rail_collapsed false, the default prefs, and a session map holding only this run's tabs. settings::set first deletes the whole native.notes.window subtree (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:205).
findings.impact: Trigger: the engine restarts or disconnects, or a request hits the 30 s timeout, during the client's first Notes refresh. The next successful library render then silently replaces everything the user saved: autosave, wrap, zoom, sort, toolbar and font prefs, the library width and collapsed state, and every project's remembered open and active tabs. No user action is needed.
findings.fix: Set `restored` and `loaded` only after a successful read. On failure leave `restored` false so the next refresh_notes retries, and keep deferring persist through persist_wanted until a read has succeeded.

v1.reason: notes_window.rs:188-205 runs `if !window.restored.replace(true) { if let Ok(value) = ui.call("settings.get",...).await {...} window.loaded.set(true); ... }`. A failed read still sets loaded, and restored is already true, so the read is never retried. This contradicts the field's own comment at line 15. The next successful workspace() calls shell.split.set_position(owner.rail_width) once (note_pages.rs:1113-1114). The position-notify handler calls owner.persist (note_pages.rs:565-573), and the close_request handler persists too (notes_window.rs:103-108). persist writes rail_width/rail_collapsed plus saved_state(), which holds the default PREFS and this run's SESSION only (note_pages.rs:281-283). settings::set first runs delete_under(path), which wipes the whole native.notes.window subtree (settings.rs:203-205). The saved prefs and the per-project remembered tabs are then silently replaced.
v1.correction: The trigger is narrow. At startup ui.project is 0, so the first real read happens from Ui::refresh after connect. It fails only if the engine drops, or a request times out, during that first notes refresh. A later reconnect does not re-read, but in-memory state is intact by then, so that case is harmless. The fix is as proposed: set restored and loaded only after a successful read.

findings.title: Unsaved notes of other projects are hidden with no indicator, and the quit guard blocks on them without saying where they are
findings.evidence: workspace() hides every other project's tab, dirty or not: `let mine = doc.project == project; doc.draft.layout.set_visible(mine);` (1125-1126). Unsaved dots exist only on library rows of the project being shown (738, 839-846). The project picker shows names only (pages.rs:187-251). Reopening Notes from the main window switches it to the main window's project: show_notes -> `show_project(ui, ui.project.get())` -> `window.project.set(project)` (notes_window.rs:153-164). The quit guard counts drafts of every project, `.note_drafts.borrow().values().any(|d| d.busy.get() || d.dirty())`, and says only 'Save or discard note changes before closing.' (app.rs:1037-1044). It also never calls note_pages::flush (298-307), even with autosave on.
findings.impact: Trigger: edit a note in project A (autosave is off by default), switch the main window to B, and open Notes from the sidebar or pick B in the Notes picker. The A tab disappears, nothing in Notes shows that an unsaved draft exists, and Relay refuses to quit with a generic message. The user has to step the picker through every project to find the draft. If A is then removed, the hidden draft can never be shown again: the picker lists only existing projects, and nothing else calls edit() for it. Relay then can't be closed normally at all. With autosave on, quitting within 1.5 s of the last keystroke is refused instead of saved.
findings.fix: Track drafts that are dirty in a project other than the shown one, and surface them with a picker badge or a banner whose 'Show' links call show_project(doc.project) and focus the tab. Make the quit guard name the notes and their projects, and open Notes on the first one. On quit with autosave on, call note_pages::flush and close once the saves land. Close or migrate docs whose project was removed (see the removed-project finding).

v1.reason: workspace() hides every other project's tab whether or not it has unsaved changes (note_pages.rs:1124-1126: `let mine = doc.project == project; doc.draft.layout.set_visible(mine);`). Hidden GtkNotebook pages also hide their tabs. Unsaved-dot indicators exist only on library rows of the project being shown. The picker (pages.rs:187-251) lists project names only. show_notes (notes_window.rs:153-154), called from the sidebar navigate (app.rs:1303-1304) and at startup, switches the Notes window to ui.project. The 'Open…' action only focuses the library of the current project (menu.rs:263). The main window's close guard (app.rs:1036-1044) blocks on any note draft that is dirty or busy in any project, with the generic message 'Save or discard note changes before closing.' Autosave is off by default (note_pages.rs:36), and hiding the Notes window only flushes when autosave is on (note_pages.rs:298-307, notes_window.rs:105). The native client does nothing for notes when a project is removed: there is no project.deleted handling that closes or migrates docs. A dirty draft whose project was removed can therefore never be shown again through the picker, and the normal window close stays blocked.
v1.correction: There is one partial way out: open_note (pages.rs:26-28) switches Notes to the note's own project. So opening a note of project A from elsewhere in the app shows the hidden tab, but nothing tells the user to do that. The 'with autosave on, quit within 1.5 s is refused' part is minor, because retrying after the timer fires succeeds. Medium severity stands, driven by the hidden draft plus the generic quit refusal, and by the unrecoverable case after a project is removed.

findings.title: Every main-window refresh and every notes event re-lists all notes and rebuilds the whole library, even while Notes is hidden
findings.evidence: refresh_notes has no visibility check. Whenever the window exists, which is always since startup, it fetches `notes.list` with every note body (208) and calls workspace(). It runs from Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440, which itself runs after every successful ui.mutate at app.rs:1124 and on project, workspace and session events). It also runs on every notes.changed / notes.deleted event (app.rs:1209-1211), although that event already carries the full note. workspace() clones the list again with `notes.to_vec()` (1123). It rebuilds the project picker with `clear(&shell.picker); shell.picker.append(&super::workspace_picker(...))` (1121-1122) and reconciles every doc. render_rows then removes and recreates every row (771-785), rebuilding `haystack: format!("{title}\n{body}").to_lowercase()` (763), the preview and the date, and calling doc.dirty() for each open doc (738). The header func scans all rows for every row: `rows.iter().any(|r| r.note["pinned"] == true)` (594). When nothing is pinned this is O(n^2) per render and per search keystroke.
findings.impact: Each refresh does work proportional to all note text, holding about five copies of it, on the GTK thread. This happens for every agent notes.append, every main-window action and every project or session event, even for a window the user may not have open. While Notes is open, the user also sees it: an open project-picker popover closes under the pointer, keyboard focus on a library row is destroyed, and the selection jumps back to the active doc.
findings.fix: While the window is hidden, skip refresh_notes and only mark the library stale, then refresh when the window is presented. Apply notes.changed and notes.deleted payloads in place by updating or removing the one row with that id, instead of re-listing. Rebuild the picker only when ui.projects changes. Compute the any-pinned flag once per render and store it on Shell.

v1.reason: refresh_notes has no visibility check (notes_window.rs:166-222). The window exists from startup (app.rs:366), and the close button only hides it (notes_window.rs:103-104). Every Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440) and every notes.changed/deleted event (app.rs:1208-1211) re-fetches notes.list with full bodies (notes.rs:339-349). Each one then runs workspace(), which unconditionally clears and rebuilds the picker (note_pages.rs:1121-1122) and clones the notes (1123). render_rows removes and rebuilds every row widget, its haystack and preview (note_pages.rs:766-792, 763). The header func scans all rows for each row (note_pages.rs:590-594). This all runs on the GTK thread, triggered by frequent session/mutate refreshes, even while Notes is hidden. While Notes is visible, the rebuild destroys row focus and resets the selection to the active doc (select_active_row).
v1.correction: The cost scales with the note count per project, which is usually tens to low hundreds. The cost is real but moderate, not a freeze. The O(n^2) header scan is a secondary point. The main cost is rebuilding every row and the picker on each refresh. The best fix is to skip refresh while the window is hidden (mark stale and refresh on present) and to rebuild the picker only when projects change.

findings.title: Save as new note drops anything typed while notes.create is in flight and puts the cursor back at the top
findings.evidence: Found while tracing callers of note_pages::open_doc; this file is outside the assigned chunk. save_as snapshots the text when the request starts (`let snapshot = (doc.draft.snapshot)();`, 1202) and does not lock the editor. On success it calls `discard_close(&ui, &doc);` (1215). That copies the *current* text into base so the Draft will let the tab close (1260-1273). It then runs `super::open_doc(&ui, note, position).view.grab_focus()` (1216), which builds the replacement tab from the server's copy of the old snapshot. doc::build places the cursor at the start (147).
findings.impact: Trigger: press Ctrl+Shift+S, or click 'Save as new note' in the conflict or deleted notice, and keep typing. Every keystroke typed during the round trip is discarded without a prompt. The round trip is longer when the engine is busy. Typing that continues afterwards lands at the very top of the new note.
findings.fix: On success, compare the current snapshot with the one that was sent. If they differ, load the current text into the new doc and keep its base as the server copy, so it shows as modified. Carry the cursor offset over. Alternatively, make the view read-only while save_as is in flight.

v1.reason: save_as (note_pages/doc.rs:1197-1224) takes `snapshot = (doc.draft.snapshot)()` before the async notes.create call. Nothing makes the view read-only: draft.busy only changes the status caption in refresh_state (564-565) and gates save/close. On Ok, busy is cleared and discard_close runs (1215). discard_close (1260-1273) takes a fresh snapshot, which includes any text typed since the request went out, copies it into base so the draft is no longer dirty, and closes the tab without asking. open_doc (note_pages.rs:900) then builds the new tab from the server's note, which holds only the old snapshot's body, and doc::build puts the cursor at the start (doc.rs:147). Ordinary save (1110-1180) does not lose text this way: it rebases on the server copy and keeps later edits dirty. So text typed between Ctrl+Shift+S, or the conflict/deleted notice's 'Save as new note', and the reply is dropped without a prompt.
v1.correction: The window is normally a local Unix-socket round trip of milliseconds. It widens when the engine's store mutex is held by other work, so a typical loss is a few keystrokes. That fits medium (a real bug in a less common path), not higher. Fix: on Ok, compare the current snapshot with the one sent. If they differ, load the current text into the new doc over the server base so it shows as Modified, and carry the cursor offset across.

findings.title: update_chrome builds a fresh full-text snapshot to check dirty on every keystroke, after refresh_state has just done the same
findings.evidence: Doc::changed -> refresh_state (doc.rs:556-559) runs on every buffer and title change. refresh_state computes `let dirty = self.dirty();` (doc.rs:563) and ends with `super::update_chrome(ui)` (doc.rs:594). update_chrome then collects every doc into a Vec in current_doc(ui), runs `if doc.dirty() {` again (823), and calls doc.name() again. Draft::dirty runs the snapshot closure: buffer_text copies the whole buffer and compares it with base (task_pages.rs:174-179). With autosave on, schedule_autosave adds a third self.dirty() (doc.rs:601). The capture-phase key handler also computes super::current_doc(ui) on every key press, before it knows whether the key is a shortcut (menu.rs:426).
findings.impact: Per-keystroke cost grows with note size: two or three full copies and comparisons of the note body. Agent-appended standing notes only ever grow, so typing in a multi-MB note spends milliseconds of main-thread time per keystroke.
findings.fix: Pass the (dirty, name) pair that refresh_state already computed into update_chrome, and skip the call when the doc is not the current one. In shortcut(), compute current_doc only after a key has matched. Longer term, track dirty with a cheap edit counter or the buffer's modified flag instead of re-snapshotting.

v1.reason: Every buffer or title change goes through Doc::changed (doc.rs:556-560), which calls refresh_state, then schedule_counts, then schedule_autosave. refresh_state calls self.dirty() (doc.rs:563) and ends with super::update_chrome(ui) (594). update_chrome (note_pages.rs:818-836) collects docs() into a Vec through current_doc, then calls doc.name() and doc.dirty() again. Draft::dirty (task_pages.rs:174-179) runs the snapshot closure (doc.rs:289-300), which copies the whole buffer through buffer_text into a serde_json Value and compares it with base. With autosave on, schedule_autosave runs a third dirty() (doc.rs:600). name() also copies up to 24 lines each time it is called (doc.rs:504-511), and it is called twice. menu.rs:426 computes current_doc for every key press before any shortcut has matched. The cost is real, but it only matters for very large notes.
v1.correction: The repeated work is two or three full-body copies and compares per keystroke. That is two with autosave off, which is the default (note_pages.rs:36), and three with it on. On typical notes the time is negligible; it reaches milliseconds only with multi-MB notes. The fix is to pass the dirty flag and name that refresh_state already computed into update_chrome. Longer term, use the buffer's modified flag or an edit counter instead of re-snapshotting.

findings.title: Notes shortcuts compare raw keyvals, so Ctrl+S/N/W/F/H/G/O do nothing on non-Latin keyboard layouts
findings.evidence: The capture-phase EventControllerKey (379-386) runs `let lower = key.to_lower(); let name = if mods == ctrl { match lower { Key::n => "new", Key::o => "open", Key::s => "save", ... } }` (429-448). The keyval it receives is already translated for the active layout. GTK's own accelerator matching (GtkShortcutController / gdk_key_event_matches) also matches the same physical key in the first layout, so Ctrl+S works under a Cyrillic layout. This hand-written matcher has no such fallback. The accelerator table also exists a second time as the menus' 'accel' attributes in model() (145-226), and the two have to be kept in agreement by hand.
findings.impact: With a Russian, Greek or Hebrew layout active, Ctrl+S produces Cyrillic_yeru (or the equivalent), no arm matches, and the key falls through. Save, new note, close tab, find, replace, go to line and zoom silently stop working in Notes, while GTK's built-in Ctrl+C/V/Z keep working.
findings.fix: Replace the hand-written dispatcher with a capture-phase gtk::ShortcutController built from a single (trigger, action) table, using ShortcutTrigger::parse_string with NamedAction or CallbackAction. A CallbackAction can keep the body-only rule for Ctrl+B/I/K and the Escape condition. Generate the menu accel attributes from the same table.

v1.reason: The Notes window's only shortcut path is a capture-phase EventControllerKey (menu.rs:379-386) that calls shortcut() (menu.rs:416ff). shortcut() matches `key.to_lower()` against Latin keyvals: Key::n, s, w, f, h, r, g, b, i, k, and Key::s for Ctrl+Shift+S. The app never calls set_accels_for_action and builds no ShortcutController, so the menu-model 'accel' attributes only label the menus. The keyval passed to key-pressed is translated for the active layout group, so under a Cyrillic or Greek layout Ctrl+S arrives as a non-Latin keyval, no arm matches, and the key propagates on. GTK's own shortcut controllers have a layout-independent fallback (GDK_KEY_MATCH_PARTIAL ignores the active group), which is why the text view's built-in Ctrl+C/V/Z keep working.
v1.correction: This only affects users who type with a non-Latin layout active. Function-key and Tab/PageUp bindings are unaffected. A smaller fix than rewriting into a ShortcutController: when the keyval does not match, translate the event's hardware keycode in group 0 (gdk::Display::map_keycode / translate_key) and match on that. The duplicated accel table in model() is a separate low-value maintenance note.

findings.title: Switching the Notes project keeps the previous project's scroll offset, search filter and error banner
findings.evidence: workspace() computes `let changed = shell.project.replace(project) != project;` (1109) but uses it only to choose the active tab (1153). render_rows always restores the old scroll offset: `let keep = adjustment.value();` ... `glib::idle_add_local_once(move || adjustment.set_value(keep));` (767-768, 791). The search entry's text keeps filtering the new project's rows (576-585). The banner raised by shell_error (721-725) is never hidden.
findings.impact: Trigger: search 'deploy' in project A, then pick B in the picker. B's library is filtered by 'deploy' (often showing 'No notes match your search.') and scrolled to A's offset. A 'Could not create a note: ...' banner raised in A stays on screen over B.
findings.fix: When `changed` is true, skip the idle scroll restore and scroll to 0, clear the search text, and hide the banner.

v1.reason: In workspace() (note_pages.rs:1109), `changed` is used only to choose the active tab (1153). render_rows always saves the old adjustment value and restores it on idle (767-768, 791), so project B's list opens at project A's scroll offset. The search entry is never cleared, and the filter func (576-585) keeps filtering B's rows. shell_error's banner (721-725) is never hidden when the project changes. The doc comment at 1104-1106 says search text and scroll position are meant to survive a refresh, but nothing suggests they are meant to survive a project switch.
v1.correction: The impact is smaller than claimed. The banner has its own dismiss button (note_pages.rs:471-477). The search query stays visible in the search entry, and the placeholder says 'No notes match your search.', so the filtering is visible, not silent. The clearly wrong part is restoring A's scroll offset into B's list. Fix: when `changed` is true, scroll to 0 and hide the banner. Clearing the search on a switch is a judgment call.

findings.title: With no project, the Notes window (presented at every startup) shows 'Opening Notes…' forever and Ctrl+N silently does nothing
findings.evidence: NotesWindow::new puts `label("Opening Notes…", "notes-window-loading")` in the page (83). app.rs:366 calls show_notes at startup, which presents the window. refresh_notes returns early on `if window.project.get() == 0 { return; }` (175-177), and Ui::refresh skips refresh_notes entirely when project == 0 (app.rs:1416-1419). new_note returns silently on `if project == 0 { return; }` (note_pages.rs:955-958). `loaded` is only ever set inside refresh_notes, so persist() keeps deferring and nothing is saved.
findings.impact: On a fresh install, or after the last project is removed, a Notes window stuck on a loading message sits next to onboarding. File > New note and Ctrl+N do nothing and show no message. Preferences toggled in that window are lost.
findings.fix: When the resolved project is 0, mount an explicit empty state (for example 'Add a project to keep notes') instead of the loading label, and have new_note show a message. Let the settings read and persist work without a project.

v1.reason: app.rs:366 calls show_notes before connect(). At that point ui.project is 0 (app.rs:742), so show_project presents the window and refresh_notes returns at notes_window.rs:175-177, leaving the 'Opening Notes…' label from notes_window.rs:83. With no projects, Ui::refresh `continue`s before reaching refresh_notes (app.rs:1416-1419), so nothing replaces the label. new_note returns silently when current_project() is 0 (note_pages.rs:954-958). `loaded` is set only inside the refresh_notes future, so persist() only sets persist_wanted. Once a project exists, restore_state replaces PREFS with the stored values (note_pages.rs:286-294), so prefs toggled in the meantime are lost.
v1.correction: The impact is confined to a fresh install, or to the state after the last project is removed. The fix should show an explicit empty state and a message from new_note.

findings.title: Creating a module refreshes the Notes library instead of the Modules page (a regression from replacing ui.refresh_page)
findings.evidence: The success arm of module_composer is `super::refresh_notes(&ui); open_module(&ui, m["id"]...)` (1326-1327). Before commit 54e6bbc this line was `ui.refresh_page();`. The modules list still updates only because module.create emits module.changed, which falls through to `ui.refresh_page()` (app.rs:1264). The whole Modules UI (modules, module_composer, open_module and module_detail, 1259-1457) lives in note_pages.rs, which is how a notes refresh ended up in it.
findings.impact: Every module creation triggers a pointless notes.list and a full Notes library rebuild (see the refresh finding). The Modules page relies only on the event echo to show the new module.
findings.fix: Call ui.refresh_page(), or drop the call and rely on module.changed. Move the module functions into their own file (for example module_pages.rs, next to board_view).

v1.reason: In commit 54e6bbc, module_composer's success arm changed from `ui.refresh_page();` to `super::refresh_notes(&ui);` (note_pages.rs:1326). That looks like a mechanical replace done along with the other notes call sites. The module handler emits module.changed (relay-core handlers/module.rs:42). That event is not caught by the notes.changed short-circuit (app.rs:1209), so it falls through to ui.refresh_page() (app.rs:1264), and that is the only reason the Modules list still updates.
v1.correction: The cost is smaller than claimed. refresh_notes returns at once when the Notes window has never been opened (notes_window.rs:169-171), so the extra notes.list and library rebuild only happen while that window exists. Fix: call ui.refresh_page() or remove the call. Moving the module UI out of note_pages.rs is optional tidying, not part of the defect.

findings.title: note_row is unreachable: pages::refresh never runs for 'notes', and its notes branch returns before reaching the call
findings.evidence: The only caller is pages.rs:180 (`note_pages::note_row(ui, &body, note)`). It comes after `if name == "notes" { note_pages::workspace(ui, name, project, &data); return; }` (pages.rs:82-85). pages::refresh is only reached through refresh_page with ui.page, and ui.page can never be "notes": navigate("notes") opens the window and returns (app.rs:1303-1306), and the notes page is not even added to the content stack (app.rs:636-637). For the same reason note_composer (pages.rs:113, 401-451) and workspace()'s `_name` parameter are dead.
findings.impact: About 55 lines in note_pages.rs, plus note_composer and the notes arms of pages::refresh, look like a live second notes UI with its own pin button, preview and refresh_page logic. Readers and future edits have to account for a UI that never runs.
findings.fix: Delete note_row, note_composer, the "notes" arms of pages::refresh, and the `_name` parameter of workspace().

v1.reason: ui.page is only ever assigned at app.rs:1348, inside navigate(). navigate returns early for "notes" at app.rs:1303-1306 (show_notes). Even without that early return, the content-stack check at 1319 would fail, because the notes page is never added to the stack (app.rs:636-637). pages::refresh has one caller, refresh_page (app.rs:1681), which passes ui.page, and pages::refresh also bails if `*ui.page.borrow() != name` (pages.rs:56). So the "notes" arms of pages::refresh can never run: line 46, the workspace call at 82-85, note_composer at 113 and the note_row loop at 178-182. note_row (note_pages.rs:1205) and note_composer (pages.rs:401) have no other callers. The live Notes path is notes_window::refresh_notes, which calls note_pages::workspace directly (notes_window.rs:210) with a hard-coded "notes", so workspace's `_name` parameter is never read.
v1.correction: workspace() itself is live through notes_window.rs:210. Only its `_name` parameter is dead, and removing it means updating that call site as well. The early "notes" return at pages.rs:82-85 and the `"notes" => ("notes.list", "notes")` arm at pages.rs:46 can both go. Check whether `edit` (called by note_row) has other callers before deciding it is still needed.

findings.title: glyphs.rs is a second copy of icons.rs's SVG painter and cache, has already drifted from it, and defines three glyphs nothing uses
findings.evidence: glyph() re-implements icons::image_with_stroke. It has its own `static RENDERED: RefCell<HashMap<String, gtk::Svg>>` (7-9, vs icons.rs:13), the same `<svg ... color="{color}" stroke="{color}" ...>` document, the same cache lookup and the same `image.connect_map(paint); image.connect_state_flags_changed(...)` hookup (60-77, vs icons.rs:213-232). It has drifted: no `#141416` -> @console substitution and a hard-coded 1.5 stroke. No glyph() call ever requests the "rule" (41), "calendar" (46-48) or "goto" (49) geometry. Both copies repaint only on map and state-flag changes, so after a palette switch (load_appearance, shell.rs:1135-1146) glyphs keep the old stroke colour until they are hovered or remapped.
findings.impact: Every painter fix, for example repainting on a palette change, has to be made twice and kept in sync. The dead geometries are maintained for nothing.
findings.fix: Expose `icons::from_geometry(geometry: &'static str, size: i32, stroke: f64) -> gtk::Image`, or add these names to icons.rs's match. Then reduce glyphs.rs to its geometry table or delete it, and drop the unused rule, calendar and goto entries.

v1.reason: note_pages/glyphs.rs:54-79 repeats icons.rs's painter: the same SVG document template, its own thread-local RENDERED cache (glyphs.rs:7-9 vs icons.rs:13), and the same connect_map/connect_state_flags_changed repaint (icons.rs:228-230). None of the glyph() call sites uses "rule", "calendar" or "goto". Callers use sort, note-new, save, undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, search, replace, list, list-numbered, checklist, quote, code-inline, code-block, link, chevron-up/down, close, pin, sidebar, plus and notes. The "rule" and "goto" strings in menu.rs are action names, not glyph lookups.
v1.correction: The claimed drift is overstated. No glyphs.rs geometry contains #141416, so the missing @console substitution changes nothing, and the hard-coded 1.5 stroke equals icons::image's default. The duplication is wider than reported, though: apps/relay-native/src/mirror/glyphs.rs:34-49 is a third copy of the painter, with no cache at all. Better fix: expose one icons.rs painter that takes a geometry string (e.g. icons::from_geometry), have both glyphs modules supply only geometry tables, and drop the unused rule, calendar and goto entries. The palette-switch staleness claim was not verified and affects all three copies alike.

findings.title: Turning autosave off does not cancel autosaves that are already scheduled
findings.evidence: set_prefs only handles the off-to-on change: `if next.autosave && !before.autosave { for doc in docs() { doc.schedule_autosave(ui); } }` (266-270). Pending timers keep running, and their callback saves without re-checking the preference: `if doc.draft.busy.get() { doc.schedule_autosave(&ui); } else { save(&ui, &doc, None); }` (doc.rs:610-614).
findings.impact: Trigger: type, then turn autosave off within 1.5 s using the status bar's 'Autosave on' button or the File menu toggle. The note is still saved once, which is exactly what the user just turned off.
findings.fix: On the on-to-off change, cancel each doc's autosave timer (add a stop_autosave() next to stop_timers()), or re-check prefs().autosave in the timer callback.

v1.reason: set_prefs (apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:259-272) only acts on the off-to-on change: `if next.autosave && !before.autosave { for doc in docs() { doc.schedule_autosave(ui); } }`. Nothing removes a pending autosave_timer when autosave is turned off. The timer callback (note_pages/doc.rs:606-615) takes the timer and then either reschedules or calls `save(&ui, &doc, None)` without re-reading super::prefs().autosave. The guard at doc.rs:600 runs only when the timer is scheduled, not when it fires. So if you type and then turn autosave off within 1.5 s, the note is still saved once.
v1.correction: The best fix is to re-check `super::prefs().autosave` at the top of the timer callback. That one line also covers the reschedule branch. Another option is to remove each doc's autosave_timer on the on-to-off change in set_prefs.

findings.title: Open notes are tracked twice (DOCS and ui.note_drafts) and the shown project is stored twice (Shell.project and NotesWindow.rendered_project)
findings.evidence: open_doc inserts into both maps (`DOCS.with(|docs| docs.borrow_mut().insert(id, doc.clone())); ui.note_drafts.borrow_mut().insert(id, doc.draft.clone());`, 932-933) and on_close removes from both (921-922). ui.note_drafts (app.rs:296) is read only by the quit guard (app.rs:1037-1061) and the smoke tests. workspace() sets `shell.project.replace(project)` and `owner.rendered_project.set(project)` back to back (1109, 1112).
findings.impact: These pairs have to be kept in lockstep by hand. If a future path adds or drops a doc in one map but not the other, the quit guard will disagree with what Notes shows.
findings.fix: Expose note_pages::unsaved() and close_all() over DOCS for app.rs to use, and delete ui.note_drafts. Keep a single 'rendered project' field.

v1.reason: The thread-local DOCS map and ui.note_drafts (app.rs:296) are only ever changed together: insert at note_pages.rs:932-933 and remove in on_close at 921-922. ui.note_drafts is read only by the main window's close guard (app.rs:1037-1061) and by smoke_notes.rs. It holds the same information as DOCS, kept in sync by hand. owner.rendered_project (notes_window.rs:7) is written only next to shell.project (note_pages.rs:1109/1112), and it is read only by the `== 0` check at notes_window.rs:214 and by smoke tests. The two maps have not drifted apart yet, so this is a small cleanup and not a bug.
v1.correction: The category is duplication, not overengineering. The note_drafts half is the worthwhile part: expose note_pages::has_unsaved() and close_all() over DOCS and remove the field from Ui, updating smoke_notes.rs to match. The rendered_project half crosses a module boundary (Shell is private to note_pages) and pays off little, because it is only a 'has anything rendered yet' flag.

results.coverage:
I read every line of all four assigned files: doc.rs (1360), text.rs (307), session_context.rs (255) and notification_center.rs (327).

To trace callers and callees I also read:
- note_pages.rs in full, note_pages/menu.rs in full, notes_window.rs in full;
- task_pages.rs 1-240 (Draft) and client.rs 1-350;
- the relevant parts of app.rs (connect, event loop, reconcile, close guard, navigate), shell.rs (open_project, set_mode, session_actions, refresh_notification_count), terminal.rs (begin_context/context_card), tools.rs (old notifications page), editor.rs (replace) and sounds.rs;
- on the engine side: handlers/notes.rs in full, handlers/notify.rs in full, session.rs (record_agent_notification, done/report, RestorableList), socket.rs (per-connection request loop), guardrail.rs hold/refusal inserts, worktree::is_dirty, time.rs;
- DECISIONS.md D121.

Binding behaviour was checked against the locked registry sources: sourceview5 0.11.2 (search_context.rs manual replace_all with assert_eq!, plus the sys signature returning c_uint), glib 0.22.9 (translate.rs/gstring.rs NUL checks under debug_assertions, main_context_futures.rs catch_unwind for spawned futures, SourceId::remove), and gtk4 0.11.4 (TextBuffer::set_text, extern "C" clicked trampoline).

Some C-side behaviour comes from knowledge of the GTK/GtkSourceView sources, not from code read here: replace_all returning a count, one "changed" emission per insert or delete, and g_utf8_validate rejecting NUL. Nothing was compiled or run; per the hard rules there was no cargo, and relay-native cannot build in this environment anyway.

Not examined: glyphs.rs, and other note_pages parents beyond what tracing needed.

Out of scope, noticed in passing and not reported:
- The engine stores timestamps with jiff's variable-length fractional seconds and compares them as strings, which is not strictly lexicographic.
- Notifications are never pruned.
- The Notes library rebuilds every row on every notes.changed event.

Clippy-pedantic casts in these files (usize→i32 char counts) were checked; none are reachable bugs.

findings.title: Replace all with zero matches panics in the sourceview5 binding and aborts the whole client, losing every unsaved note
findings.evidence: `let note = match self.search.replace_all(&self.find.replacement.text()) {`. The locked sourceview5 0.11.2 implements this by hand (src/search_context.rs): `let is_ok = ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all(...); assert_eq!(is_ok == 0, !error.is_null());`. But the C function returns `guint`, the number of replacements (sourceview5-sys: `-> c_uint`). So 0 replacements with no GError becomes `assert_eq!(true, false)`, a panic in every build profile. The "Replace all" button is always sensitive (doc.rs:204, 436-437: `replace_all.connect_clicked(move |_| all())`). The handler runs inside gtk4 0.11.4's `unsafe extern "C" fn clicked_trampoline`, and unwinding out of extern "C" aborts under Rust 1.98. The app has no panic hook and no catch_unwind.
findings.impact: Trigger: Ctrl+H, type something not in the note (or leave the query empty, or type an invalid regex), click Replace all. Clicking Replace all a second time after a successful run does the same. The native client aborts. Unsaved note text is lost (autosave is off by default, D72), and so are unsaved code-editor buffers. The code editor's "All" button (editor.rs:1075) crashes the same way when its non-empty query has no match. A smaller problem: when occurrences_count() is still -1 (scan unfinished), the result reads "Replaced 0" after N replacements.
findings.fix: Never call the binding when there may be no match. Guard with `self.search.forward(&self.buffer.start_iter()).is_some()`, which is synchronous and works while the count is -1. Better: call `sourceview5::ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all` directly and use the guint it returns for "Replaced N". Apply the same guard in editor.rs. Add a zero-match case to verify_tools: note_pages.rs:1201 only tests a single match. replace() has a similar debug_assert_eq! (search_context auto binding) that fires if GtkSourceView declines a replacement without an error. That is rare (regex lookbehind), but the same guard approach applies.

v1.reason: I checked this in the locked crate. Cargo.lock pins sourceview5 0.11.2. ~/.cargo/registry/.../sourceview5-0.11.2/src/search_context.rs implements replace_all by hand: `let is_ok = ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all(...); assert_eq!(is_ok == 0, !error.is_null());`. sourceview5-sys 0.11.2 declares the C function as returning `c_uint`, the number of replacements. GtkSourceView returns 0 with no GError when nothing matches. Nothing matches when the query has no match, when the search text is empty (smart_forward_search finds nothing), and when the regex is invalid. In each case the assert becomes assert_eq!(true, false), an unconditional panic. Notes' Doc::replace_all (doc.rs:896-905) calls it with no guard at all, from `replace_all.connect_clicked` (doc.rs:436-437). That closure runs inside gtk-rs's extern "C" clicked trampoline, so the panic aborts the process under rustc 1.98. The only panic hook, in smoke.rs:458, is installed just for screenshot fixtures and calls exit(1) anyway. The most common trigger is clicking Replace all a second time, after the first click left no matches. The code editor's "All" button (editor.rs:1069-1079) guards an empty query but not a query with no match, so it crashes the same way. The verify test at note_pages.rs:1201 only covers a case with one match. Autosave is off by default (doc.rs:246 "Autosave off"), so unsaved note and editor buffers are lost.
v1.correction: I rate this high, not critical. The engine is a separate process, so agent sessions survive and only the desktop client aborts. What is lost is unsaved buffer text, not stored data. It is still a guaranteed crash from a routine action, and that is enough for high. The fix is right: guard with `search.forward(&buffer.start_iter()).is_some()`, or better, call the ffi function directly and use the guint it returns to report "Replaced N". This also fixes the wrong "Replaced 0" message while occurrences_count() is still -1.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. Cargo.lock:3125 pins sourceview5 0.11.2. Its hand-written src/search_context.rs makes `replace_all` run `assert_eq!(is_ok == 0, !error.is_null())`, where `is_ok` is the C return value. The C function returns `c_uint` (sourceview5-sys lib.rs:3075-3080), which the installed GIR (GtkSourceView 5.20.0) documents as "the number of replaced matches". I checked the real library with a headless PyGObject script in the scratchpad. These four cases return 0 with no GError: a query with no match, an empty query (None or ""), an invalid regex with regex on, and a second replace_all after a successful one. In the Rust binding each becomes `assert_eq!(true, false)`. That is a plain assert, so it fires in every build profile. Only an invalid replacement string sets a GError, and that path is safe.

Doc::replace_all (doc.rs:896-905) calls the binding with no guard. The click handler is wired at doc.rs:436-437, and nothing ever disables the button: doc.rs has no set_sensitive, and replace_row only changes visibility (doc.rs:770). The panic unwinds into gtk4 0.11.4's `clicked_trampoline` (auto/button.rs:514), a bare `unsafe extern "C" fn`. glib's connect_raw has no catch_unwind, and gtk4's only one is in the test helper `test_synced`. Under the installed rustc 1.98.1, a panic that unwinds out of an extern "C" function aborts the process. The only panic hook (smoke.rs:458) is installed only when RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT is set, and it calls exit(1) anyway.

(b) Who can trigger it, and how. The desktop user, in a normal flow. In Notes, open replace with Ctrl+H, the toolbar's Replace button or the "Replace…" menu item. Then click "Replace all" when the query has no match. That covers a typo, a case mismatch with "Aa" on, an invalid regex while the bar already says "Invalid pattern", a cleared query, and most commonly a second click on Replace all. The code editor's "All" button (editor.rs:1069-1079) only returns early when the view is read-only or the query is empty. Any non-empty query with no match crashes it the same way, including a second click. The trigger is deterministic, not a race. The only test (note_pages.rs:1201) covers a single match.

(c) What happens when it fires. relay-native aborts with SIGABRT, and all unsaved work in the client is lost:
- the text of every open note tab: Draft keeps it in memory only (task_pages.rs:35-47), and autosave defaults to false (note_pages.rs:34-36, D72);
- every modified code-editor buffer;
- in the second-click case, the replacements the first click made.

Nothing persisted is touched. The engine (`relay serve`) owns the PTYs, sessions and worktrees, and relay-native never spawns it. The README says "Closing the window keeps the engine, sessions and worktrees alive." So agent sessions keep running and the store is intact.

(d) Severity: high, not critical. No stored data is lost or corrupted, no session goes down, and find/replace in Notes and the editor is not the app's core flow. It is still a guaranteed crash from a routine action that throws away work the user typed. That is worse than the rubric's "freeze of the UI" (high), but it does not meet critical.

(e) The proposed fix. The guard `search.forward(&buffer.start_iter()).is_some()` prevents all four cases above. forward() is synchronous and works while occurrences_count() is -1. It is not complete, though: GtkSourceView's replace_all loop can still stop at 0 replacements with no GError when its regex_replace returns FALSE on the first match without setting one. The finding's "better" option is the right one: call `sourceview5::ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all` directly, treat only `!error.is_null()` as failure, and report the guint it returns. The ffi is re-exported (sourceview5 lib.rs:20), so no new dependency is needed. This also fixes the stale "Replaced {total}" message.
v2.correction:
Severity: critical becomes high. Only the GTK client aborts. The engine and every agent session survive (README: "Closing the window keeps the engine, sessions and worktrees alive"), and no stored data is lost. The loss is unsaved note and editor text, plus a first Replace all's unsaved replacements when the crash is a second click.

The trigger and mechanism are as stated, and I checked them against the real GtkSourceView 5.20.0. replace_all returns 0 with no GError for a query with no match, an empty query, an invalid regex, and a second call after a successful one. The process aborts because rustc 1.98 aborts when a panic unwinds out of an `extern "C"` function, and nothing on the signal path catches it.

Fix: prefer the direct FFI call over the forward() guard. Call `sourceview5::ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all`, treat only a set GError as failure, and use the returned count. The forward() guard misses the rare case where regex_replace stops on the first match without setting a GError. Put this in one shared helper for doc.rs:899 and editor.rs:1075; their messages have already diverged ("Replaced N" vs "Replaced all matches"). The zero-match regression test must call that helper, because calling `SearchContext::replace_all` directly in verify_tools would itself panic. Per CLAUDE.md, the change cannot be compiled in an agent session; it must be built and tested on a machine with GTK 4.22.

The secondary `replace()` debug_assert_eq! is live in run.sh's dev build, but both callers guard it with occurrence_position > 0, so it is low severity at most.

findings.title: Note bodies have no size limit but the UI socket caps lines at 2 MiB: one large note, or a project's notes over 2 MiB in total, disconnects the UI on every refresh
findings.impact: Trigger: paste a ~2 MB log into a note and save, or let agents keep appending to the standing note until the project's live notes exceed about 2 MiB. The save is committed but reported as "Not saved: Invalid engine response: frame exceeds 2 MiB", and the whole UI goes to "Engine disconnected". Every Reconnect immediately re-fetches notes.list, or receives the next notes.changed, and drops again. The desktop client stays unusable until the note is shrunk from the CLI.
findings.fix: Enforce a body cap in the engine: notes.create, update and append should reject anything over a limit (e.g. 512 KiB) with a typed error, and Doc::save should check the same limit before sending. Make notes.list return previews and fetch bodies with notes.get. Emit notes.changed without the body. At minimum, skip an oversized event line instead of tearing down the whole connection.

v1.reason: client.rs:48 sets `MAX_LINE = 2 * 1024 * 1024`. When a line goes over it, the reader at client.rs:200-205 returns `Error::Protocol("frame exceeds 2 MiB")`, which ends the reader loop, fails every pending request, and emits Notice::Disconnected. app.rs:1267-1275 then drops the client. The engine socket reads requests with an unbounded `BufReader::lines()` (socket.rs:323/335), and notes Create/Update/Append (notes.rs:356-487) impose no body cap. A large body is therefore stored, and then echoed in the update response and in the `notes.changed` event (emit_note at notes.rs:63-66 serializes the full Note). The UI subscribes to notes.changed on the same control connection (app.rs:1154). notes.list (notes.rs:340-350) returns every live note body in the project, and the notes window (notes_window.rs:208) and the notes page (pages.rs:46) both call it. Once one note's JSON-escaped body passes about 2 MiB, every later edit or append to it disconnects the UI. Once the project's notes total that much, every opening of the notes window or page does too.
v1.correction: I rate this medium, not high. Reaching 2 MiB takes a very large paste or long-term accumulation, so it is not a normal-flow failure. Once reached, though, it persists. One mechanism detail: the reconnect loop only re-fetches notes.list when the notes window is open (refresh_notes returns early otherwise, notes_window.rs:168-171). With the window closed, the UI drops on the next notes.changed for the oversized note, for example an agent appending to the standing note. The fix direction is right: an engine-side body cap (create, update and append), list previews, and an event without the body.

findings.title: Every buffer 'changed' signal copies the whole note 2–3 times, so Replace all or undo on a large note freezes the UI for O(matches × size)
findings.evidence:
`doc.buffer.connect_changed(move |_| changed());` calls `fn changed(..) { self.refresh_state(ui); self.schedule_counts(); self.schedule_autosave(ui); }`. That one handler does all of this:
- refresh_state calls `self.dirty()` (563). That is Draft::dirty, which calls `(self.snapshot)()` and so `buffer_text()`: a full copy plus a JSON compare (task_pages.rs:174-179, doc.rs:297).
- refresh_state calls `self.name()` (584).
- refresh_state calls `super::update_chrome(ui)` (594), which clones all docs via current_doc and calls `doc.name()` and `doc.dirty()` again (note_pages.rs:820-824).
- schedule_autosave calls `self.dirty()` once more when autosave is on (601).
GtkSourceView's replace_all does a delete plus an insert per match, which is two 'changed' emissions per match, and undo replays them. The cursor-position notify also runs update_count per shifted offset.
findings.impact: Example: Replace all on a 500 KB note with 5,000 matches. That is 10,000 handler runs, each making 2–3 full-text copies and comparisons, about 15 GB copied. The GTK main thread freezes for seconds, and for minutes on MB-sized notes; undoing it does the same. Typing in a multi-MB note costs several full copies per keystroke.
findings.fix: Coalesce the work. The changed handler should only mark the state stale and schedule one idle callback, as schedule_counts already does, that runs refresh_state and schedule_autosave once. Compute dirty once per idle, or keep a cheap edit counter and compare text only then. Pass the already-computed dirty flag and name to update_chrome.

v1.reason: `doc.buffer.connect_changed(move |_| changed())` (doc.rs:368-369) runs Doc::changed on every emission. That calls refresh_state, which calls self.dirty(). That is Draft::dirty, which calls snapshot, then buffer_text (task_pages.rs:20, a full gtk_text_buffer_get_text plus a String copy), then a JSON compare. refresh_state also calls super::update_chrome (note_pages.rs:818-824), which calls doc.dirty() again on the current doc, and schedule_autosave (doc.rs:597-601) calls self.dirty() a third time when autosave is on. Only the counts are coalesced (schedule_counts, 120 ms timer). replace_all (doc.rs:896-905) calls GtkSourceSearchContext::replace_all, which does a delete plus an insert per match, and each of those emits a 'changed' signal. The handler therefore runs 2×matches times, and each run does 2-3 full O(n) text extractions. On a large note with thousands of matches that freezes the main loop for seconds, and an undo of the replace replays it. Ordinary typing in a normal-sized note costs a few small copies per keystroke and is harmless.
v1.correction: The freeze needs both a large note (hundreds of KB or more, which notes.append can grow) and many matches, so it is an uncommon path and the severity stays medium, not high. The auditor's '15 GB' figure is a worst-case extrapolation and was not measured. The fix stands: mark the state stale in the handler and do one idle refresh that computes dirty once and passes it to update_chrome and schedule_autosave.

findings.title: Describing a stopped pane runs `git status --untracked-files=all` on every restorable worktree in every project, serialised on the UI's only connection
findings.evidence: `if sessions.iter().any(|s| text(s, "state") == "restorable") { if let Ok(data) = self.call("session.restorable", json!({})).await {`. The op takes no filter (`Empty => RestorableOut`, relay-bus ops/session.rs:166). Its handler (session.rs:1484-1503) opens every restorable session's worktree and runs `worktree::is_dirty`. That is `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` with a 10 s timeout, once per worktree, one after another (worktree.rs:78-97). The engine answers each connection's requests strictly in order: socket.rs:335-743 awaits every dispatch before reading the next line. ui.call uses the single control connection (app.rs:1111-1117). describe runs for every stopped pane that reconcile creates: at startup, on reconnect (connect() clears all panes), and on every project switch (shell.rs:10-37 → reconcile → app.rs:1494-1499 → shell.rs:743).
findings.impact: After an app restart most sessions are restorable. On every project switch or reconnect this call goes out first, and the project's own session.list, notes and board requests queue behind N git status walks. That takes seconds on large repos (e.g. UE projects). If it passes the 30 s client timeout (client.rs:65-71), this call and the requests queued behind it fail with "Request timed out". The card then falls back to "Relay was closed" with no uncommitted-changes flag, even after a crash.
findings.fix: Add a session or project_id filter to session.restorable so it covers only the panes being described. Alternatively, return `reason` without the dirty walk and fetch worktree_dirty lazily per pane, or cache it per worktree. Another option is to issue the call on a separate connection, as lifecycle requests already do. Do not show "Relay was closed" when the lookup failed.

v1.reason: describe_batch (session_context.rs:97-106) calls session.restorable with an empty payload whenever any described pane is restorable. The handler is register_unlocked, so it does not hold the store mutex, which is good. It still loops over every restorable session in every project, and for each one runs worktree::is_dirty → status_files: `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` through output_with_timeout with a 10 s cap, one after another (session.rs:1482-1501, worktree.rs:78-97). The engine serves one connection's lines strictly in order: socket.rs:335 reads a line and awaits the dispatch (742) before reading the next. ui.call sends non-lifecycle ops over the single control client (app.rs:1111-1117), with a 30 s default timeout (client.rs:65-71). reconcile (app.rs:1465-1480) drops panes that are not in the current project, so every project switch recreates panes, and session_actions → describe_stopped_session (shell.rs:741-743) re-runs the restorable scan. refresh()'s requests then queue behind it on the same connection.
v1.correction: Impact depends on worktree count and size. With a few small repos the scan takes milliseconds, so how often it really hurts is not established. On large UE checkouts with untracked-files=all it can take seconds per worktree. The visible wall itself switches synchronously from sidebar_sessions (shell.rs:27-31); only refreshed data lags behind. The fix stands: filter session.restorable by project or session, or split the dirty check out and run it lazily per pane, or cache it per worktree.

findings.title: Engine strings containing U+0000 trip glib's NUL check: a panic in the debug build the app runs, an empty editor in release
findings.evidence: `buffer.set_text(text(note, "body"));`. The same happens at line 102 (the title Entry builder) and at lines 523/525 in load. In glib 0.22.9, both `to_glib_none` for str and `GString::from(&str)` run `if cfg!(debug_assertions) { GStr::check_interior_nuls(self).unwrap(); }` (translate.rs:563-565, gstring.rs:1953-1955). The workspace keeps debug assertions in the dev profile, which is what run.sh launches (Cargo.toml:46-57). Nothing in the engine strips NUL from notes.append/create/update text or from session.done summaries, and serde_json decodes "\u0000" into the String. The same labels and tooltips exist in notification_center.rs:220/228/234, session_context.rs:145-159 and note_pages.rs:742.
findings.impact:
Trigger: an agent appends text containing a NUL to a note, for example output read from a binary file.
- Activating that note from the library (a row_activated signal) panics inside an extern "C" trampoline and aborts the client; unsaved notes are lost.
- Inside refresh futures, glib's executor swallows the panic and the render stops part-way: the Notes library list empties, the bell list or slate card is left incomplete.
- In a release build GTK refuses the insert because g_utf8_validate fails on NUL. The buffer stays empty while base keeps the body, the note shows Modified, and any save writes "" over the stored body.
findings.fix: Sanitise at the boundary. Replace '\0' (e.g. with U+FFFD) in `text()`, or before any string reaches GTK. Also reject NUL in the engine's note, session and report text inputs with a typed error.

v1.reason: I checked this myself. Cargo.lock pins glib 0.22.9. In it, `impl ToGlibPtr<*const c_char> for str` (translate.rs ~563) and `From<&str> for GString` (gstring.rs ~1953) both run `if cfg!(debug_assertions) { GStr::check_interior_nuls(self).unwrap(); }`. gtk4 0.11.4 `TextBufferExt::set_text` passes `text.to_glib_none().0`, and `EntryBuilder::text` takes `impl Into<GString>`. Cargo.toml `[profile.dev]` / `[profile.dev.package."*"]` only change opt-level, so glib is built with debug assertions and run.sh launches target/debug. The note body at doc.rs:145 (`buffer.set_text(text(note, "body"))`), the title Entry builder at doc.rs:102 and load() at doc.rs:523/525 therefore unwrap-panic on any interior NUL. The engine does no NUL filtering on notes. notes.create/update/append (handlers/notes.rs:356-410) bind the strings straight to SQLite, and rusqlite returns them with their length, so the NUL survives the round trip. The engine does check for NUL in other places (file.rs:58, git.rs:224, device.rs:1188), but not here. A panic inside a GTK signal trampoline (extern "C") aborts the process. The same goes for the library rows (note_pages.rs:742 label from display_title) and the notification rows (notification_center.rs:220-234). In release, gtk_text_buffer_set_text with an explicit length fails g_utf8_validate on the NUL and inserts nothing, which leaves the editor empty while base holds the body. The trigger is narrow: an agent or a CLI/phone client has to send a JSON string containing \u0000. An LLM rarely does that, but notes.append is open to every agent. The consequence is a whole-client abort in the build the user actually runs, and possibly a repeat crash whenever the library or bell renders.
v1.correction: I could not establish how often agents really produce \u0000, so the frequency is uncertain. The mechanism is not. The best fix is to reject NUL in the engine's text inputs (notes.*, session.done/report summaries, notify bodies) with a typed error, because one rule there covers every client. The client can also map '\0' to U+FFFD in its shared `text()` helper as a second guard.

findings.title: LAST REPORT is chosen by created_at, but the engine's dedup rewrites a notification's body without updating created_at, so the card can show the wrong report and a stale time
findings.evidence: `notifications.iter().find(|n| matches!(text(n, "category"), "agent_done" | "agent_blocked") && text(n, "title").starts_with(&prefix) && ...)` runs over notify.list, which is ordered `created_at DESC` (notify.rs:71). The card then shows `relative_time(text(report, "created_at"))` (177). The engine's dedup (session.rs:261-271) looks for an unread notification with the same project, category, title and link. If it finds one, it runs `UPDATE notifications SET body=?1 WHERE id=?2` and leaves created_at untouched.
findings.impact: Example: a session finishes at T1 (A, "X finished"), blocks at T3 (B, "X is blocked"), then finishes again at T5 while A is still unread. A's body becomes the T5 summary but keeps T1. The slate shows "LAST REPORT Blocked: … · <T3>" although the last report was the T5 completion. Whenever a body is rewritten, the time shown is the first report's ("3 h ago" for a summary written a minute ago). The bell popover shows the same stale time and leaves the row buried (notification_center.rs:224).
findings.fix: When record_agent_notification updates an existing row, also bump created_at, or add an updated_at column and order notify.list by it. In last_report, pick the row with the newest such timestamp instead of the first match.

v1.reason: record_agent_notification (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:261-278) dedups on an unread row with the same project, category, title and link. On a hit it runs `UPDATE notifications SET body=?1 WHERE id=?2` and leaves created_at unchanged. notify.list orders by `created_at DESC,id DESC` (notify.rs:71). last_report (session_context.rs:62-71) takes the first agent_done/agent_blocked row whose title starts with the session name, and render (lines 175-180) shows `relative_time(created_at)`. The finding's sequence works as described: finished at T1 and left unread, then 'needs attention' (agent_blocked, session.rs:1406) at T3, then finished again at T5. The T1 row now carries the T5 body with the T1 timestamp, so the T3 blocked row sorts first and the card says 'Blocked: …'. Even without the blocked step, a rewritten body shows the time of the first report. The bell row has the same stale time (notification_center.rs:224).
v1.correction: Small correction: the blocked title is '<name> needs attention' (session.rs:1406), not 'is blocked'. Line 1209's 'is blocked' is the headline for session.report. The mechanism is the same. The fix stands: bump created_at, or add an updated_at column to order by, when the dedup rewrites the body. Adding a column requires a migration and a SCHEMA_VERSION bump.

findings.title: Following a guardrail-hold notification opens the Guardrails page, and also switches the hidden agent wall to focus mode and saves that layout
findings.evidence: Hold and exception notifications link to `{"op":"guardrail.confirm","payload":{"hold_id":…,"session":…}}` (guardrail.rs:1243-1252, grants.rs:404-411). follow() only matches ui.page.switch, task.get and session.get, so guardrail.confirm falls through to the category match `"guardrail" => "guardrails"`, and the code calls `ui.open_project(project, "guardrails")`. Then `if let Some(session) = payload["session"].as_str() { … *ui.focused.borrow_mut() = Some(..); ui.set_mode("focus"); }` runs. set_mode relays out the wall and saves it with save_layout (shell.rs:281-285), even though the wall is not on screen. D121 (DECISIONS.md:594-600) says: "a session or hold link opens the agent wall focused on the session … A link the UI cannot route shows no affordance and only marks read."
findings.impact: Clicking "Agent requests a guardrail exception" or "Guardrail hold" lands on the Guardrails page, not the session where the exception prompt is waiting. Meanwhile the user's chosen wall layout (grid or mosaic) is replaced by focus mode and saved to settings without them seeing it. Notifications with no link (refusals, disk, system) still get an "Open where this happened" button that routes by category, which contradicts D121.
findings.fix: Map `"guardrail.confirm" => "agents"` so the existing session focus is actually visible. If the Guardrails page is the intended target, leave focused and mode alone instead. Update D121 or the fallback routing so the two agree.

v1.reason: Both hold producers write a link with op guardrail.confirm and payload {hold_id, session}: crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:1250 and crates/relay-core/src/guardrail/grants.rs:409. Center::follow (notification_center.rs:292-304) matches only ui.page.switch, task.get and session.get, so this link falls through to the category arm `"guardrail" => "guardrails"`, and open_project(project, "guardrails") then navigates to the Guardrails page. Next, lines 320-324 check `payload["session"]`; if the pane exists, they set ui.focused and call ui.set_mode("focus"). set_mode (shell.rs:281-285) relays out and calls save_layout, which persists the wall layout for that project while the wall is hidden. D121 (DECISIONS.md:594-600) says a hold link should open the agent wall focused on the session. So the code and the decision disagree, and the code's two halves contradict each other.
v1.correction: Lower to low. Landing on the Guardrails page is not a dead end: pages.rs:45 lists guardrail.holds.list there, and its empty text (pages.rs:129) covers exception requests and held actions, so the user can still find and answer the hold. The concrete harm is smaller than claimed. The saved wall mode silently changes to focus, which the user notices on their next visit to the wall, and D121 has drifted from the code. The claim that link-less notifications get an 'Open' affordance holds: row() always builds the open button (notification_center.rs:203-205). That is minor doc drift. Fix: route guardrail.confirm to "agents", as D121 says, or keep "guardrails" and skip the focus/set_mode block for it, then update D121 to match.

findings.title: Notice buttons discard unsaved note text in one click: the conflict notice's 'Reload theirs' skips the confirmation and clears undo, and the deleted notice's 'Close' skips the save prompt
findings.evidence: Conflict notice: `("Reload theirs", |ui, doc| reload(ui, doc, false))`. reload(…, false) never asks, and doc.load() then replaces the text inside `begin_irreversible_action()` (524-526), which clears the undo stack. The reconcile notice's identical button calls `reload(ui, doc, true)` (1355), which does ask "Your unsaved changes to this note will be lost." Deleted notice: `("Close", |ui, doc| discard_close(ui, doc))` (1191). discard_close copies the snapshot into base and closes. request_close (1277-1311) would have asked "Save changes … before closing?". The notice also has its own × Dismiss button (658-668), so "Close" reads as closing the notice.
findings.impact: These notices appear exactly when the user has unsaved work: after a save conflict or a remote delete. One click on "Reload theirs" or "Close" discards all of it, with no prompt and no undo. Separately, reconcile's automatic load (1343-1346) also clears the undo history every time an agent changes a note the user has open.
findings.fix: Use reload(ui, doc, true) in the conflict notice. Route the deleted notice's "Close" through request_close, or rename it "Discard and close" and confirm when dirty. Load remote text as a user action instead of an irreversible one so Ctrl+Z can bring the user's text back.

v1.reason: The code does what the finding says. The conflict notice (doc.rs:1167) wires `("Reload theirs", |ui, doc| reload(ui, doc, false))`, which skips the `ask && doc.dirty()` confirmation (1240-1252). The reconcile notice's identically labelled button uses `reload(ui, doc, true)` (1355). load() replaces the text inside begin_irreversible_action (524-526), so the user's draft cannot be undone back. The deleted notice's "Close" (1191) calls discard_close, which bypasses request_close's "Save changes … before closing?" dialog (1293-1311), and it sits next to a separate × Dismiss button (658-668). Impact is limited because both buttons are explicit choices with fairly clear labels, and the alternative "Save as new note" is offered right beside them. The real defect is the inconsistency: the same "Reload theirs" asks in one notice and not the other, and "Close" is ambiguous.
v1.correction: I rate this low. Each loss needs a deliberate click on a labelled button. Reconcile's automatic load (1343-1346) runs only when !doc.dirty(), so it never discards unsaved text; it only drops the undo history of already-saved edits, which is minor. The fix is to use reload(ui, doc, true) in the conflict notice and to send "Close" through request_close or rename it "Discard and close".

findings.title: The snapshot trims the title but base keeps it as stored, so a title with surrounding whitespace makes an untouched note 'Modified'
findings.evidence: `let value = title.text().trim().to_string(); json!({"title": if value.is_empty() && null_title.get() { Value::Null } else { json!(value) }, …})`. Base is the note exactly as the engine stores it (set_base, 513-518). notes.create and notes.update store titles verbatim (notes.rs:358-369, 390-394), and agents may call both. Draft::dirty compares `self.base.borrow()[k] != *v` (task_pages.rs:174-179).
findings.impact: Opening a note whose title is, say, "Plan " or "Plan\n" (agent-created) immediately shows Modified and a dirty dot. Closing the tab asks to save. The main window refuses to close ("Save or discard note changes before closing", app.rs:1036-1043) over a note the user never edited. With autosave on, closing the tab silently rewrites the title.
findings.fix: Normalise both sides the same way: trim base["title"] when comparing, or in set_base. Alternatively, stop trimming in the snapshot and trim only in the save payload.

v1.reason: The snapshot at doc.rs:293-297 builds `title.text().trim().to_string()`, while set_base (doc.rs:513-518) stores the engine's note as-is. Draft::dirty (task_pages.rs:174-179) compares each snapshot key with `base[k]`, so a stored title like "Plan " never equals the trimmed "Plan" and the note shows as dirty as soon as it opens. notes.create/update store p.title verbatim (notes.rs:356-394). BUS.md:466 shows that the `docs` role gets notes.create/update, and the CLI and phone can also write titles. The client's own saves send the trimmed snapshot, so notes the user creates in the client are never affected. The app.rs:1036-1043 close guard (`note_drafts ... any(|d| d.busy.get() || d.dirty())`) then blocks quitting until the user saves or discards. With autosave on, the 1.5 s autosave timer is scheduled from refresh_state/changed and rewrites the title.
v1.correction: It only triggers when a title arrives from outside the client with surrounding whitespace, which is rare, so the severity is low. The fix is to normalise both sides the same way, for example by comparing against a trimmed base title in set_base or in the note's dirty check.

findings.title: F3 in a note whose find field is empty skips the first match
findings.evidence: `if self.find.query.text().is_empty() { self.find.query.set_text(&super::last_query()); }`. set_text fires the entry's changed handler (399), so find_incremental runs and selects the first match at or after the cursor (808-813). find_step then calls `self.search.forward(&end)` from the end of that selection (828-833) and selects the second match.
findings.impact: Search "foo" in note A, switch to note B (its find field is empty), press F3: the selection jumps to the second "foo" after the cursor. The first one is skipped.
findings.fix: Pre-fill the query with its changed handler blocked, or set the search text directly without the incremental select, then search forward from the cursor.

v1.reason: doc.rs:819-834: find_step calls `self.find.query.set_text(&super::last_query())` when the entry is empty. The entry's changed handler (doc.rs:399, `doc.find.query.connect_changed(move |_| incremental())`) runs synchronously. find_incremental (808-816) calls sync_query and then `select_match(self.search.forward(&from))`, where `from` is the selection start or the cursor, so the first match gets selected. find_step then takes `selection_bounds()`, which is now that match, and searches `self.search.forward(&end)` from its end. That selects the second match. LAST_QUERY is a process-wide thread-local (note_pages.rs:190-196), while each Doc has its own Find entry, so a freshly opened note does have an empty field with a non-empty last query. F3 is bound through menu.rs:310/459 to find_step(false). Shift+F3 behaves differently: the incremental pass selects the next match forward, then the backward search runs from its start, so it lands on the match before the cursor and does not skip one.
v1.correction: Only the forward direction (F3, Enter in the entry, the down arrow) skips. The simplest fix is to compute (start, end) from the selection or cursor before pre-filling. You can also block the changed handler while pre-filling, or call settings.set_search_text directly.

findings.title: The italic toggle on bold text strips one asterisk from each side, turning bold into italic
findings.evidence: With before = after = "*", the unwrap test `room && buffer.text(&outer_start, &start, false) == before && buffer.text(&end, &outer_end, false) == after` matches the inner asterisks of "**bold**" when only "bold" is selected. The second branch, `selected.starts_with(before) && selected.ends_with(after)`, matches when all of "**bold**" is selected. Both branches delete one '*' from each side.
findings.impact: Select "bold" inside "**bold**" and press Ctrl+I: the result is "*bold*". The bold is lost instead of becoming ***bold***. Selecting the whole "**bold**" does the same.
findings.fix: For single-character markers, unwrap only when the character just beyond the matched marker is not the same marker character. Alternatively, treat "**" as its own token.

v1.reason: menu.rs:296 binds italic to `wrap_inline("*", "*", "italic text")`. In doc.rs:955-966, selecting "bold" inside "**bold**" gives at=2 and b=1, so `room` is true. buffer.text(outer_start..start) == "*" and buffer.text(end..outer_end) == "*", so the unwrap branch deletes the inner pair of asterisks and leaves "*bold*". Selecting the whole "**bold**" hits the second branch (starts_with("*") && ends_with("*")) and strips one asterisk from each side. Both paths turn bold into italic when the user meant to add italic. The edit is a single user action, so Ctrl+Z restores it.
v1.correction: The user can undo the change, so its impact is cosmetic and low is the right severity.

findings.title: Ctrl+scroll zooms a whole step per scroll event, so touchpads and high-resolution wheels jump straight to 50% or 300%
