findings.evidence: The controller is `gtk::EventControllerScroll::new(gtk::EventControllerScrollFlags::VERTICAL)`, without the DISCRETE flag. Every event calls `super::zoom(&ui, if dy < 0. { 1 } else { -1 })`, whatever the size of dy. Each step runs set_prefs, which reloads the CSS provider in apply_font and calls persist (note_pages.rs:259-278).
findings.impact: A two-finger Ctrl+scroll sends dozens of small-delta events, so the zoom hits its limit at once, with a CSS reload per event. One notch on a hi-res wheel (several 1/8-notch events) zooms several steps.
findings.fix: Add EventControllerScrollFlags::DISCRETE so GTK accumulates whole steps, or accumulate dy yourself and step when |acc| ≥ 1.

v1.reason: doc.rs:473 creates `EventControllerScroll::new(EventControllerScrollFlags::VERTICAL)` without DISCRETE. The handler (doc.rs:475-481) calls `super::zoom(&ui, if dy < 0. { 1 } else { -1 })` once per event, whatever the size of dy. zoom (note_pages.rs:274-278) steps through ZOOMS via text::zoom_step, which is clamped to 50..300, and every step goes through set_prefs, then apply_prefs (a CSS reload), then persist(ui). A touchpad Ctrl+pinch/scroll or a high-resolution wheel sends many small-delta smooth events, so the zoom runs to its limit almost at once. An event with dy == 0 also zooms out, because of the `else -1` branch. mirror.rs is the only other scroll controller and does not do this.
v1.correction: Add EventControllerScrollFlags::DISCRETE, or accumulate dy and step only when |acc| >= 1. Also ignore dy == 0.

findings.title: Save as new note and both duplicate actions store the clipped display name as the new title, and their suffixes differ ('(copy)' vs ' copy')
findings.evidence: save_as: `let mut title = doc.name(); if !doc.deleted.get() && snapshot["title"] == doc.draft.base.borrow()["title"] { title = format!("{title} (copy)"); }`. name() falls back to display_title of the body, which clips at 60 characters and appends "…" (text.rs:199-205). The menu's duplicate (menu.rs:274) uses `format!("{} copy", d.name())`, and duplicate_id (note_pages.rs:1053-1061) uses `format!("{title} copy")`.
findings.impact: Saving an untitled note as a new note stores a title like "A long first line … charact… (copy)", with a literal ellipsis. That title no longer follows the body. The same operation, implemented three times, produces "X (copy)" or "X copy" depending on the path.
findings.fix: Use one helper, e.g. copy_title(Option<&str>) -> Option<String>, in all three places. It should keep a null title null, so display_title still derives the name from the body, and otherwise append one agreed suffix.

v1.reason: doc.rs:1197-1205 save_as sets `let mut title = doc.name();` and appends " (copy)" when the title is unchanged. Doc::name (doc.rs:504-511) returns the title field if it has one. Otherwise it returns `tx::display_title("", <first 24 lines>)`, which clips the first plain line at 60 chars with a trailing "…" (text.rs:198-217), or returns "Untitled". That string goes into notes.create as an explicit title. An untitled note therefore becomes a titled copy such as "Some long first line…  (copy)" or "Untitled (copy)", and the copy's title no longer follows its body. menu.rs:274 (`format!("{} copy", d.name())`) and note_pages.rs:1052-1060 duplicate_id (`format!("{title} copy")`, with title from doc.name() or display_title) do the same thing with a different suffix. Both go through new_note (note_pages.rs:954), which also sends an explicit title.
v1.correction: The literal-ellipsis and "Untitled" titles appear only when the source note has no title of its own; a titled note just gets the inconsistent suffix. The deleted-elsewhere path (no suffix) also turns the derived name of an untitled note into a stored title. A shared copy_title helper that keeps a null title null fixes all three call sites.

findings.title: Doc builds a Draft only to dismantle its layout, and Draft::close then reports refusals on a status label that is no longer on screen
findings.evidence: After `Draft::new_note(ui, "Note", …)`, build() calls `draft.layout.remove(&draft.status); draft.layout.remove(&draft.footer);`, unwraps Draft's ScrolledWindow and zeroes its margins. Doc uses only base, busy, snapshot, dirty, close and on_close from it; Draft::controls, its own save with different conflict logic, goes unused. When Draft::close refuses, can_close() writes `self.status.set_text("Save your changes or choose Discard and close.")` (task_pages.rs:131-144) to the detached label.
findings.impact: Example: request_close → Save, and the user keeps typing while the save is in flight. The `then` callback calls draft.close(), can_close() refuses, the message goes to the invisible label, and the tab silently stays open. Every note also builds and throws away a ScrolledWindow, Viewport and footer, and there are two save implementations to maintain.
findings.fix: Give notes a small struct with base, busy, dirty and on_close. Register it in ui.note_drafts behind a minimal dirty/busy interface for the quit guard. Show close refusals in the Doc's own notice bar.

v1.reason: doc.rs:301-318 builds `Draft::new_note`, then removes Draft's status label, footer and ScrolledWindow and resets its margins. For notes, Draft::build has no window and no panel (task_pages.rs:75-76), so Doc only uses base/busy/snapshot/dirty/close/on_close and the note_drafts registry (app.rs:296). The detached-label point holds. save's `then` (doc.rs:1156) calls draft.close(). If the user typed while the save was in flight, can_close (task_pages.rs:131-144) refuses and writes "Save your changes or choose Discard and close." to `self.status`, which is no longer in the widget tree. The tab stays open with no explanation. The Doc's own status bar does show "Modified", so the user is not misled about the note's state; only the reason the close did nothing is lost. Draft itself is not dead code, since task pages use controls(). The cost is the throwaway widgets per note plus coupling to a struct whose UI assumptions do not fit notes.
v1.correction: The payoff is modest. Throwing away three widgets per tab is negligible, and the only user-visible effect is a silent non-close in a race. The cheaper fix is to give Draft an optional refusal callback, or have Doc check can_close itself and show the message in its notice bar, without splitting the struct. The category is code-quality, with a small UX bug in it, rather than overengineering.

findings.title: The Markdown line helpers misread thematic breaks and indented headings
findings.evidence: marker() treats `matches!(first, b'-' | b'*' | b'+') && bytes.get(1) == Some(&b' ')` as a bullet, so the CommonMark thematic breaks "* * *" and "- - -" count as list items and list_enter returns Continue("* ") or Continue("- "). heading() counts '#' only from column 0 (84), so toggle_lines(&["  ## Title"], Heading(2)) finds no heading, takes `line.trim_start()` = "## Title" (119) and produces "## ## Title".
findings.impact: Pressing Enter after a "* * *" or "- - -" rule starts a bullet list. Toggling H2 on a heading indented by 1–3 spaces doubles the hashes.
findings.fix: In marker(), return no marker for a line made only of three or more of the same marker character plus spaces. In heading() and toggle_lines, strip up to three leading spaces before counting hashes. Add test cases for both.

v1.reason: text.rs:29-34 marker() accepts any '-', '*' or '+' followed by a space as a bullet, with no thematic-break check. In list_enter (text.rs:63-70) the line "* * *" yields content "* *", which is non-empty, so it returns Continue("* "), and Enter after a "* * *" or "- - -" rule starts a bullet. heading() (text.rs:84-96) counts '#' only from byte 0. For "  ## Title", has() is false, so remove is false, and toggle_lines' Heading branch (text.rs:117-119) maps it via `line.trim_start()` to "## Title" and formats "## ## Title". Both traces check out against the code.
v1.correction: Impact is narrow. The most common rule spelling, "---", is not affected, because marker() requires a space after the first char. Spaced rules and headings indented by 1-3 spaces are uncommon in hand-written notes.

findings.title: The popover's summary and 'Mark all read' only see the newest 100 notifications, while the bell also counts unread ones beyond them
findings.evidence: load() fetches `notify.list {"limit": 100}` (134). render() computes `let unread = entries.iter().filter(|n| n["read"] != true).count();` and then `self.mark_all.set_sensitive(unread > 0);`. The bell badge counts `notify.list {"unread_only":true,"limit":100}` (shell.rs:747-756). Notifications are never pruned; they are deleted only with their project (workspace.rs:367).
findings.impact: Suppose 100 or more newer notifications, read one at a time by following them, push an older unread one out of the popover's window. The bell keeps showing "1" while the popover says "All read" and Mark all read is disabled, so the badge cannot be cleared from the UI.
findings.fix: Derive Mark all read's sensitivity from an unread count, for example by also fetching unread_only or reusing the bell's count. Alternatively, list unread notifications first.

v1.reason: The popover loads `notify.list {"limit":100}` (notification_center.rs:134). The engine orders by `created_at DESC,id DESC LIMIT ?` (notify.rs:70-71). render() derives both the summary and `mark_all.set_sensitive(unread > 0)` from those 100 rows only (notification_center.rs:167-174). The bell uses `unread_only:true` (shell.rs:753), so it still counts an unread notification that has fallen past position 100. Nothing prunes notifications except project deletion (workspace.rs:367). The only paths that mark one read are notify.ack and notify.ack_all (notify.rs:101,121,127), so the state is reachable: the bell shows 1 while the popover says "All read" with Mark all read disabled.
v1.correction: Reaching that state requires 100 or more newer notifications to have been read one at a time (follow or ack) while an older one stayed unread. Clicking Mark all read whenever it is enabled clears everything, older ones included. So this is a rare edge case; notify.ack_all from another surface (the CLI, for example) still clears it. The simplest fix is to base mark_all's sensitivity and the summary on the bell's unread_only count.

findings.title: Every notify.* event while the popover is open sends a fresh notify.list and rebuilds every row, and each ack reloads twice
findings.evidence: `pub(super) fn changed() { if let Some(center) = center().filter(|c| c.popover.is_visible()) { center.load(); } }`. load() bumps the revision and always sends a request (128-142). The ack handlers call `center.load()` themselves (88, 268), and their own notify.changed event then triggers changed() again. For every notify.* event, app.rs:1196-1200 calls changed() and refresh_notification_count, and sounds::notify adds a notify.settings.get per notify.new (sounds.rs:89-105).
findings.impact: An agent looping on a refused command creates one notification and one notify.new per attempt (handlers/guardrail.rs:538-541). With the popover open, each attempt sends a notify.list (limit 100) on the shared serial connection and rebuilds every row, losing hover and keyboard focus. The revision check then discards all but the last result.
findings.fix: Coalesce the reloads as refresh_notes does: a pending flag plus a single in-flight load that runs once more if events arrived meanwhile. Drop the explicit load() after acks, since the event already triggers one.

v1.reason: app.rs:1196-1199 calls refresh_notification_count() and notification_center::changed() for every notify.* event. changed() (notification_center.rs:114-118) calls load() whenever the popover is visible. load() (127-142) always sends notify.list {limit:100} and, if its revision is still current, render() calls clear(&self.list) and rebuilds every row, which drops hover and focus. Nothing coalesces these calls; the revision check only discards stale results, after the request has already been made. The guardrail refusal path (handlers/guardrail.rs:534-538) inserts a fresh notification and emits notify.new on every refusal, with no dedup in insert_refusal_notification (guardrail.rs:1258-1272). sounds::notify adds a notify.settings.get per notify.new (sounds.rs:89-104). The ack and ack_all handlers (notification_center.rs:78-89, 262-268) call center.load() themselves, and the engine's notify.changed event (notify.rs:110-114, 130-133) triggers a second load.
v1.correction: Only matters while the popover is open. Each load is one indexed query of up to 100 rows, so the cost is wasted bus round-trips and a visible row rebuild (lost hover and focus) during a refusal burst, not a freeze. Dropping the explicit load() after acks and coalescing with a pending flag, as proposed, is the right fix.

findings.title: The old Notifications page in tools.rs is unreachable, and it duplicates Center::follow's routing in a version that has already diverged
findings.evidence: navigate("notifications") returns right after `notification_center::open()` (app.rs:1307-1311), and ui.page is only assigned later in navigate (app.rs:1348). So `*ui.page == "notifications"` is never true, and both tools::refresh's "notifications" arm (tools.rs:66, 84) and tools::notifications (tools.rs:596-650) never run. That copy routes `"ui.page.switch" => payload["page"].as_str().unwrap_or("notifications")` and has no session.get handling, focus or ack-on-follow, unlike Center::follow (notification_center.rs:292-325).
findings.impact: About 60 lines of dead UI, plus a second routing table that has already drifted. The next routing fix, such as the hold link, has to be made twice or the copies diverge further. app.rs:1203-1206 also tests for the unreachable "notifications" page.
findings.fix: Delete tools::notifications, its refresh arm and the unused ui.pages["notifications"] box. If routing is needed anywhere else, share a notification_target(item) -> (project, page) helper.

v1.reason: The only place ui.page is assigned is navigate (app.rs:1348). navigate returns early for "notifications" after notification_center::open() (app.rs:1307-1312), and the nav menu entry (shell.rs:1026) goes through navigate. So *ui.page is never "notifications", and the code below never runs: tools::refresh's arms at tools.rs:66/84, tools::notifications (tools.rs:596-650), and the page checks at app.rs:1218 and 1677. The dead copy's routing has already diverged from Center::follow: it has no session.get arm, defaults ui.page.switch to "notifications", and does no focus or ack.
v1.correction: Also remove the "notifications" entries in the page checks at app.rs:1218 and 1677, and the page box registered at app.rs:630. Its only remaining use is that content.child_by_name("notifications") exists, which navigate never reaches.

findings.title: The slate card's relative times are computed once and never refreshed, so it can say 'just now' for hours
findings.evidence: `let mut value = relative_time(ts);` (209) and `relative_time(text(report, "created_at"))` (177) are written once into static labels. The card is re-rendered only when the pane's render signature changes, and that signature (state, role, provider, branch, worktree, intent, pair_with; app.rs:1494-1503) contains no time.
findings.impact: A session that stopped at 14:02 shows "LAST ACTIVE just now · Oct 6, 14:02" and "LAST REPORT … · just now" all afternoon. The report line has no absolute time that would show the error.
findings.fix: Show an absolute stamp on the report line too, or refresh the relative labels on a minute timer or whenever the pane becomes visible.

v1.reason: render (session_context.rs:177, 209) writes relative_time() into static labels once. The pane is re-rendered only when its signature changes (app.rs:1494-1503: state, role, provider, branch, worktree, intent, pair_with), and that signature holds no time. Nothing refreshes the card on a timer. The LAST REPORT line has only a relative time, so 'just now' stays on screen until something rebuilds the pane.
v1.correction: The impact is smaller than claimed. LAST ACTIVE already shows the absolute stamp ('just now · Oct 6, 14:02'), so only LAST REPORT can mislead. The card is also rebuilt on every project switch, because reconcile recreates panes (app.rs:1465-1480), and on reconnect. Cosmetic, low.

findings.title: text.rs and session_context.rs unit tests claim to run headlessly but live in relay-native, which CI never builds
findings.evidence: The header says "No GTK here, so they test headlessly." But the module is compiled only inside relay-native (`#[path = "note_pages/text.rs"] mod text;` in note_pages.rs). relay-native is excluded from default-members (Cargo.toml:5) and from CI (ci.yml:69-82: "relay-native is deliberately absent"). session_context's tests also need glib::DateTime.
findings.impact: The only automated checks of list continuation, prefix toggling, go-to parsing and relative times never run in CI, so regressions such as the thematic-break case go unnoticed, and the comment misleads contributors.
findings.fix: Move the pure helpers (text.rs, plus relative-time logic written without glib) into a small headless crate, or into a default-member module included with #[path], so plain `cargo test` runs them.

v1.reason: The comment at text.rs:1-2 is accurate. "No GTK here, so they test headlessly" means the tests need no display or GTK initialisation, and `cargo test -p relay-native` runs them that way on a machine that can build the crate. Leaving relay-native out of CI is a deliberate, documented decision: Cargo.toml:4-5 says "build the GTK client with `-p relay-native`", and ci.yml:69-82 gives a long "honest reason rather than an oversight" (the pinned GTK 4.22 / pango 1.56 versions are not on ubuntu runners), as does CLAUDE.md. Every relay-native test shares this property, so it is a known limitation of the whole crate, not a defect in these modules. The "regression" cited (thematic breaks) is a case that was never handled, not something CI would have caught. Moving text.rs into a headless crate is an optional nicety with small payoff, not a finding.

results.coverage:
Read every line of both assigned files: apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs (1-1213) and apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs (1-842).

To trace callers and callees I also read:
- panel.rs (whole file)
- app.rs: helpers, confirm_inline_if, show_error, call, refresh, reconcile, refresh_page, dismiss_panels, the event loop (around 1195-1275)
- client.rs (whole transport)
- shell.rs: open_project, sheet, layout, session_actions
- launch.rs: the launch flow at 775-836

findings.title: Task/module Save treats a change to any editable field as a conflict, so edits fail while an agent works on the task
findings.evidence: The save handler takes every snapshot key, not just the edited ones: `let keys: Vec<String> = next.as_object().unwrap().keys().cloned().collect();` (214), then `if draft_conflicts(&base, &latest, &keys)` (215), which shows "This item changed elsewhere…" (216). `expected` is built from base for all keys (218) and the payload is the whole snapshot (219). For tasks that is 8 fields: title, body, changelog, priority, state, type, size, module_id (596). The engine changes some of them on its own. The session hook flips a builder's active task between running and blocked (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1390-1399). Completion sets awaiting_review (session.rs:104). Agents may rewrite body/changelog (task.rs:868 allowlist; task.changelog.write task.rs:965). The engine's own atomic check rejects any supplied `expected` field that differs (task.rs:871-880). The comment at 986 says "Auxiliary changes never invalidate an unsaved editor", and the unit test (1201-1212) only passes the edited fields, but the real caller passes all of them. The pre-flight `task.get` + `draft_conflicts` repeats the engine's atomic check, adding one extra round trip. Its `deleted_at` arm can never fire, because task.get and module.get never return deleted rows (get_task(..., false)).
findings.impact: A user opens a task an agent is working on, fixes only the description, and clicks Save. Meanwhile the agent's hook flipped state running→blocked, or the agent wrote its changelog. Save is refused with "This item changed elsewhere… Copy it before discarding and reopening the latest version." The user changed none of those fields. For a running task this happens almost every time. The only way out is to copy the text, discard, reopen, paste and save before the next state flip. A Save with no changes still sends get + update, which writes an audit row, bumps updated_at and refreshes the board. The module editor (note_pages.rs:1363-1364) has the same problem.
findings.fix: Take an `initial = snapshot()` when the form is built. On Save, compute the changed keys (`next[k] != initial[k]`). If none changed, say so and stop. Send only the changed fields, and put only those fields' base values in `expected`. Then remove the pre-flight `get` and `draft_conflicts`, and map the engine's `task.edit_conflict` / `module.edit_conflict` codes to the friendly message. The engine check is atomic; the client one is not.

v1.reason: The task snapshot (596) contains title, body, changelog, priority, state, type, size and module_id. The save handler (213-219) takes every snapshot key as `keys`, runs draft_conflicts(base, latest, keys) against a fresh task.get, and if that passes sends the whole snapshot with expected = base for all keys. Task.update (task.rs:867-880) also refuses with task.edit_conflict if any supplied expected field differs from the current row. The engine changes these fields on its own. The builder session hook writes `UPDATE tasks SET state=running|blocked ... WHERE col='active'` (session.rs:1390-1399). Completion sets state='awaiting_review' (session.rs ~104). task.changelog.write updates changelog (task.rs ~969), and agents may task.update body/changelog. Scenario: the user opens an active task, edits only the description, and the agent goes blocked (permission/guardrail wait) or writes its changelog before Save. Save then shows "This item changed elsewhere…" although the user never touched that field. The unit test (1201-1212) passes only the edited fields, which is not how the real caller uses it. The deleted_at arm is unreachable because task.get calls get_task(..., false), which filters deleted_at IS NULL (task.rs:348, 829). A deleted task makes the get itself fail.
v1.correction: "Almost every time" is overstated. A conflict needs the state at Save to differ from the state at open, so a running->blocked->running round trip does not trip it. It still fires in the normal flow of editing a task an agent is working on. The module editor's snapshot is only name/priority/icon, which the engine does not change on its own, so it is affected only by a concurrent human edit of another field and is minor. The fix is as proposed: send only the changed keys and their base values as `expected`, drop the redundant pre-flight get and draft_conflicts, and map task.edit_conflict/module.edit_conflict to the friendly message.

v2.reason:
(a) The claim holds as stated. The save handler takes every snapshot key: `let keys: Vec<String> = next.as_object().unwrap().keys().cloned().collect()` (task_pages.rs:214). The task snapshot has 8 keys (596): title, body, changelog, priority, state, type, size, module_id. The handler calls `draft_conflicts(&base, &latest, &keys)` (215), then sends the whole snapshot with `expected` set to the base value of every key (218-219). `task.update` also refuses on any supplied expected field that differs (task.rs:871-880). The panel's `base` is set only when the page opens and after a successful save (220). A `task.changed` event only calls `refresh_page` (app.rs:1263), and that leaves open panels alone, so the client compares against the row as it was when the page opened. The design intent was edited fields only: the test is named `edited_fields_..._but_unrelated_activity_does_not` and passes just ["title","body"]. Blame shows the handler has been unchanged since e4a60fcf.

(b) Who triggers it: the desktop user. They open a task card (board_view.rs has 6 call sites to `task_pages::open`), edit any field and press Save after the engine has changed that task's row since the page opened. The engine writes `tasks.state` with no user action in several places:
- the builder hook sets running or blocked (session.rs:1390-1399). Claude's Notification hook maps permission_prompt, and idle_prompt (sent about 60 s after each turn ends), to blocked, and PostToolUse to running (hooks.rs:355-359, session.rs:1363-1366).
- dispatch sets dispatched, which becomes running on the first tool use (task.rs:667).
- completion sets awaiting_review (session.rs:104).
- a PTY exit sets failed (session.rs:662).
- a short `session.done` sets blocked (session.rs:1177).

Agents may also write body and changelog (task.rs:868, task.rs:969). How often: not "almost every time". A conflict needs a net change between open and Save; a running→blocked→running round trip does not trip it. For an active task with a Claude builder, though, it is likely whenever the edit window spans the end of a turn plus 60 s. Codex builders install no Notification hook (hooks.rs:527), so their tasks change state less often.

(c) What the user sees: Save shows "This item changed elsewhere…" (216) about a field they never touched. The State combo still shows the old value, so nothing visibly changed. Nothing is written and the draft is kept, so there is no data loss. Because `base` is not refreshed on a conflict, every retry fails the same way. The user has to copy each edited field, discard, reopen, re-enter the edits and save before the next state flip. A Save with no changes still runs `task.update`, which writes an audit row, bumps updated_at and emits `task.changed` (minor).

(d) High is right, at its lower edge. Editing a task fails in an app built around many concurrent agents working on tasks, and the failure is likely in that flow. The module-editor half is low: name, priority and icon are written only by `module.update`.

(e) The fix is sound. With only the changed fields sent, the engine keeps current values for omitted fields (task.rs:882-888), and size and module_id use `crate::nullable`, so an explicit null still clears them. The engine's check is atomic (task.rs:871-880, module.rs:147-155), which makes the pre-flight get and `draft_conflicts` redundant. `Error::Bus` carries the BusError code (client.rs:77), so mapping `edit_conflict` to the friendly message is possible. The `deleted_at` arm is in fact unreachable: `get_task` and `get_module` both run with include_deleted=false.
v2.correction:
1. "Almost every time" is overstated. The Save fails only when a field's value at Save differs from its value at open. Add the other engine writers of `tasks.state`: session.rs:662 (failed on PTY exit), session.rs:1177 (blocked on a short `session.done`) and task.rs:667 (dispatched). The running/blocked oscillation comes mainly from Claude builders, through idle_prompt and permission_prompt.
2. The module editor is low impact. Its snapshot is name/priority/icon, which only a concurrent edit from another client can change.
3. Fix refinements:
   - Diff against an `initial = snapshot()` taken when the form is built, not against `base`, and set `initial = next` after each successful save. Otherwise later saves send fields saved earlier again.
   - Diffing against the initial snapshot also matters for a second reason. `module.list` without `include_archived` excludes completed modules (module.rs:145). A task in a completed module therefore opens with no active row in the module combo, so the snapshot has `module_id: null` while base holds the id. The current code then sends `module_id: null` with a matching `expected` on every Save, which silently unlinks the task from its module. This is a separate bug worth its own finding (inferred from GTK `set_active_id` semantics, not run). A fix that diffed against `base` would keep that bug.
   - Remove or rewrite the `draft_conflicts` test.
   - The change is in apps/relay-native, which cannot be compiled in an agent session, so the summary and PR must say so.

findings.title: A task in a completed module opens as unsaved: close, navigation and every action are blocked, and Save silently unassigns the module
findings.evidence: open() calls `module.list` without `include_archived` (517-520). The engine then returns only modules with `completed_at IS NULL` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/module.rs:145). detail() fills the combo from that list and calls `module.set_active_id(Some(&task["module_id"]...to_string()))` (571-576). For a completed module no row matches, so the combo stays unselected. The snapshot's `"module_id":chosen(&module).parse::<i64>().ok()` (596) is then null while `base["module_id"]` is N. `dirty()` compares the snapshot with the raw row (`self.base.borrow()[k] != *v`, 174-179), so it is true before the user touches anything. Completing a module does not touch its tasks (module.rs:159-175). Those tasks still appear on the board and in the module editor's task list (note_pages.rs:1365-1380). Because of `.unwrap_or(Value::Null)` (520), the same thing happens for every task with a module whenever module.list fails.
findings.impact: Open a done task that belongs to a completed module. Back and the scrim refuse ("Save your changes or choose Discard and close."), and page navigation refuses (dismiss_panels). Move, Approve, Dispatch, labels, relations, Delete and "New agents / pair" all refuse with "Save task changes…". If the user clicks Save as the message tells them to, the update sends module_id:null (the expected module_id:N still matches). The task is silently removed from its module, so module stats and patch-notes drafts lose it.
findings.fix: Fetch modules with `include_archived: true` and label completed ones, or always add the task's current module to the combo. Measure dirtiness against the form's own initial snapshot, not the raw row, so a value the widgets can't show never looks like an edit. Keep `base` only for `expected`. Show module.list/task.list errors instead of rendering with `unwrap_or(Null)`.

v1.reason: open() calls module.list with only project_id (task_pages.rs:517-520). The List handler (module.rs:145) then filters `completed_at IS NULL`. detail() fills the module combo from that list and set_active_id(task.module_id) (571-576), which leaves the combo unselected for a completed module. The snapshot yields module_id null (596). dirty() compares the snapshot with the raw row (174-178), so it is dirty before the user does anything. can_close then refuses ('Save your changes or choose Discard and close.'), ui.dismiss_panels refuses navigation (app.rs:1287-1291), and every action() refuses (1157-1160). Such tasks are reachable: pages.rs:51 lists modules with include_archived:true, and the module editor lists its tasks with open() buttons (note_pages.rs:1370-1380). Completing a module does not touch its tasks (module.rs Complete). Save sends module_id:null. UpdateIn.module_id uses crate::nullable (relay-bus ops/task.rs:53), so null becomes Some(None) and clears the module. expected.module_id=N still matches, and draft_conflicts sees no change, so the save goes through and the task silently leaves its module. Discard and close does work as an escape, but the message points the user to Save.
v1.correction: The trigger is opening any task of a completed module from the board or from the archived module's editor. The module.list-failure path (unwrap_or(Null) at 520) is a secondary trigger. Fix: request include_archived:true, or always add the task's current module_id to the combo. Compute dirty() against the form's initial snapshot rather than the raw row.

v2.reason:
(a) I checked the code myself and it does what the finding says. open() calls `module.list` with only `{project_id}` (task_pages.rs:517-520). The List handler (module.rs:145) then takes the `completed_at IS NULL` SQL branch. The combo is filled from that list using `m["id"].to_string()`. ModuleSummary flattens Module, so an active module's id round-trips correctly. The combo is then set with `set_active_id(Some("N"))` (571-576). gtk_combo_box_set_active_id does nothing and returns FALSE when no row matches, and a new ComboBoxText starts with no active row. So `chosen()` returns "", the snapshot's module_id is null (596), base["module_id"] is N, and dirty() (174-179) is true as soon as the editor opens. Every other snapshot field round-trips: the enums match the combo values, and titles are trimmed on create and update. That makes module_id the only field that breaks.

(b) Who hits it: the single desktop user, whenever they open a task whose module was finished with "Complete module". There are two ways in. The board fetches all tasks through task.list with no module filter, and the Done column is visible by default (hidden starts empty); the board even has a "Module #N" fallback for modules it does not list. The other way is "Open module" on an archived module (pages.rs:51 uses include_archived:true), followed by a task button (note_pages.rs:1370-1380). module.get only excludes deleted modules. module.complete does not touch tasks and does not require them to be done. So every task in every released module triggers this on every open. That is the normal end state of the module feature, not an edge case. A failed module.list (`unwrap_or(Null)`) is a rarer second trigger that affects every task with a module.

(c) What the user sees: Back, the scrim and Close are refused through the panel guard and Draft::can_close, with the message "Save your changes or choose Discard and close." Navigation and panel toggles are refused by dismiss_panels (app.rs:1287-1291). Every action() is refused (1157-1160): Move, Approve, Dispatch, labels, parent, relate/unrelate, link commit, attach/detach, subtask and Delete. "New agents / pair" is refused too (661). Discard (one confirm click) does close the editor, but reopening the task brings the problem back. No in-editor action can ever succeed on such a task without saving first.

Save goes through. draft_conflicts finds no difference, and the expected module_id N still matches before.module_id. `nullable` turns null into Some(None), and assert_module(None) passes, so the task is detached from the released module while the status shows "Saved". The native client offers no undo; audit.undo exists only in the engine. The task editor also cannot put the task back, because completed modules are not offered in the combo. The module's progress, the header counts and module.changelog.draft (the patch notes) all lose the task.

(d) High is the right severity. Opening and acting on a task fails hard, for a whole class of tasks, in a normal flow, and the message steers the user into a silent change to release-tracking data. It is not critical: no content is lost, Discard is a way out, and the link can be restored by reopening the module, reassigning the task and completing the module again.

(e) The fix's first part is necessary and enough for the main trigger: make the combo hold the task's current module. Either request include_archived:true and label archived modules, or add the current id as "Module #N" when it is missing. Refusing to render when module.list fails closes the second trigger. Measuring dirtiness against an initial snapshot is not enough on its own (see correction).
v2.correction:
The proposed fix needs one correction. Measuring dirty() against the form's initial snapshot hides the false dirty state, but on its own it does not stop the data change. Save still sends the whole snapshot (`next`), which includes module_id:null. So if the user edits any other field (the title, say) and saves, the task is still silently detached from its module. If dirtiness switches to an initial snapshot, Save must also send only the fields that differ from that snapshot, with `expected` limited to those fields. The baseline must also be reset after a successful save and on Discard, because today both update `base`.

Draft is shared with the module and note editors, so changing what dirty() compares against changes their behavior too.

The essential fix is to keep the task's current module in the combo: request include_archived:true and label completed modules, or add the current id when it is not listed. On a module.list error, show the error instead of rendering an editor with an empty module list.

The finding's line references are correct.

findings.title: "Discard and close" never closes while a message is typed, and it overwrites the draft base so a later Save reports a false conflict
findings.evidence: `confirm_inline_if(&discard, "Confirm discard", move || pending.dirty() || pending.unsent_message.get(), move |_| { if !d.busy.get() { *d.base.borrow_mut() = (d.snapshot)(); d.close(); } })` (199-204). Because of the unsent-message condition it asks for confirmation. On confirm it overwrites base and calls close(). close() calls can_close(), which returns false while `unsent_message` is set ("Send or clear your message before closing.", 131-136). By then base already holds the snapshot: only the 8 editable keys, with the user's edited values.
findings.impact: With text in the Messages tab composer, confirming Discard and close only shows "Send or clear your message" and the panel stays open. If the form also had edits, base now equals those edits. dirty() becomes false, so a later Back silently drops the edits. A later Save compares the engine's values against the user's edits and reports "This item changed elsewhere" for every edited field, so that draft can never be saved.
findings.fix: Add a `Draft::discard()` that clears the message buffer and `unsent_message`, then closes without going through can_close. Only overwrite base once the close actually happens. Alternatively, refuse up front with "clear your message first" without touching base.

v1.reason: The discard handler (199-204) is gated by confirm_inline_if(... dirty() || unsent_message ...). On confirm it sets *base = snapshot() and then calls close(). close() calls can_close() (131-136), which returns false while unsent_message is set. unsent_message tracks the Messages composer buffer (1012-1017). So with text typed in the composer, confirming Discard and close only shows "Send or clear your message before closing." and the panel stays open. base has already been overwritten with the edited snapshot, so dirty() is false. If the user then keeps the draft and presses Save, the save handler compares base (now the user's edits) with the engine's latest for every key. draft_conflicts (1194) reports a conflict on each edited field, so that draft can never be saved.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low. The trigger needs text in the composer plus a confirmed discard, and the save failure only matters if the user then changes their mind about discarding. The claim that 'a later Back silently drops the edits' is not a separate harm: the user explicitly asked to discard them. Fix: clear the composer and unsent_message, or refuse before the confirmation, and assign base only once the close actually proceeds.

findings.title: Every task detail, module editor and New-task panel leaks its Panel and widgets through closures that hold their owner strongly
findings.evidence: Draft::controls connects `save.connect_clicked(move |_| { … d … })` with `let d = self.clone()` (a strong Rc<Draft>, 205-207). It then moves `save` itself, strongly, into `key.connect_key_pressed(move |...| { … save.emit_clicked(); … })` (228-235). That controller is added to `self.layout` (236). This forms a cycle: Draft.layout → EventControllerKey → closure → save → clicked closure → Rc<Draft>. cleanup() (145-151) clears form and footer, and Panel::close clears the body (panel.rs:278). Nothing removes the controller, so the Draft is never dropped. compose() has the same mistake. `create.connect_clicked` captures `form` and `p` (an Rc<Panel>) (488-507), while `create` sits in `footer` inside `form` (457-459). `cancel` also captures `p` (479-487). After Panel::close clears the body, form ↔ create-closure keeps the form and the Panel alive. GTK4 frees an unparented widget only when its last reference goes, and these cycles never release it.
findings.impact: Each opened task detail leaks. So does each action, because action() closes the detail and reopens a fresh one. Each module editor and each New task panel leaks too. What leaks: the Draft and its Panel (layer, frame, scroll), the base JSON, and the snapshot closure with its widgets, including combos with their models and two TextViews holding the full description text. Panel.focus also keeps the previously focused board card alive. Growth has no bound over a long-running session; roughly tens of KB per open.
findings.fix: In the key controller capture `save.downgrade()` and upgrade it before `emit_clicked`. In compose capture `form.downgrade()` and `Rc::downgrade(&panel)`, or use `glib::clone!(@weak …)`.

v1.reason: Draft::controls (task_pages.rs:205-236) connects save.clicked to a closure that holds `d = self.clone()` (a strong Rc<Draft>), then moves `save` into the key closure on an EventControllerKey added to `self.layout`. That makes a cycle: Rc<Draft> -> layout (a field of Draft) -> controller -> closure -> save -> clicked handler -> Rc<Draft>. Panel::close (panel.rs:256-281) removes the layer, runs the on_closed callbacks (Draft::cleanup clears footer and form), and clears body. That unparents layout, but the Draft still holds it, so it is never disposed and its controller and handlers never drop. The Draft keeps panel: Rc<Panel> (layer/frame/scroll), base, and the snapshot closure, which owns the title/body/changelog/combos. Draft::new+controls is used by the task detail (task_pages.rs:598-599) and the module editor (note_pages.rs:1363-1364). action() closes the detail and calls open() again (1169-1175), so every successful action leaks one more. compose() is also confirmed. `create.connect_clicked` moves `form` and `p` (Rc<Panel>) in, and `create` sits in footer inside form (455-459). After Panel::close clears body, form <-> create-closure keeps the form, the Panel and every captured widget alive. `cancel` also holds `p`. The per-open cost is modest (a few widget trees), so medium is right rather than high.
v1.correction: Note drafts (new_note, doc.rs:301) do not call controls() and do not leak this way. The fix as proposed is right: capture save.downgrade() in the key closure (or have the controller hold a Weak<Draft>), and in compose capture form.downgrade() and Rc::downgrade(&panel). I cannot compile apps/relay-native here; this was established by reading the code.

findings.title: Agent settings "Save changes" always sends model and effort for a session that hasn't started, so saving fails with the default (empty) values
findings.evidence: `if !spawned { payload["model"] = model.text().as_str().into(); payload["effort"] = effort.text().as_str().into(); }` (545-548) sends both fields even when unchanged and when empty. The entries' placeholders are "Provider default" and "Default", and `text(session,"model")` is "" when the provider default is used. session.update passes them to `providers::validate_options` (session.rs:1439). It rejects an empty model (`if model.is_some_and(|model| model.trim().is_empty()) { return Err(... "model cannot be empty") }`, providers.rs:253-255) and any effort not in the provider's list, "" included (providers.rs:260-266). `spawned` is computed once, when the popover opens (476). After the first spawn the engine refuses any model/effort field (session.rs:1433-1436).
findings.impact: Take a session that was created but not started, using the provider's default model. Toggling "Agent bus writes" or "UI control" and pressing Save fails with "Invalid session.model: model cannot be empty". Setting only a model fails on the blank effort. If the agent starts while the popover is open, even a switch-only Save fails with session.already_spawned. The Launch options section can't be used with its defaults.
findings.fix: Build the payload from what changed compared with `original` (522). Include model or effort only when changed and non-empty, and the switches only when changed. Make effort a dropdown of the provider's allowed values instead of free text.

v1.reason: When !spawned, the save handler (agent_menu.rs:543-548) always sets payload model = model.text() and effort = effort.text(). A session launched with the provider default has model None: launch.rs sends `"model": if model.is_empty(){None}`. The entry therefore starts as "". SessionUpdateIn.model is a plain Option<String> (relay-bus ops/session.rs:143-145), so "" deserializes to Some(""). session.update (session.rs:1431-1440) passes it to providers::validate_options, which returns invalid session.model "model cannot be empty" for a blank model (providers.rs:253-255). It also rejects any effort not in the provider list, and "" is not in it (providers.rs:260-266). As a result, toggling only Agent bus writes or UI control on an unstarted default-model session and pressing Save fails. `spawned` is captured once when the popover opens (line 476). If the agent is spawned while the popover is open, any later Save still carries model/effort and the engine refuses it with session.already_spawned (session.rs:1435-1437).
v1.correction: This applies only to sessions that exist but have not spawned yet (spawned_at null and epoch 0), which is less common than a live agent, so medium is right. Also note: model.text() is not trimmed, and effort is free text checked against a fixed list. Fix: send only the fields that differ from `original`, never send an empty model or effort, and make effort a dropdown of the provider's allowed values.

findings.title: Each agent-settings popover leaks, because its own buttons' handlers hold the popover strongly
findings.evidence: `let p = popover.clone();` is moved into the click handlers of `brief` (451-455), `save` (541-556) and both confirm strips (578-580, 608-610). Every one of those buttons lives inside `body`, which is the popover's child. connect_closed only unparents the popover on idle (371-374). confirm_strip also captures `let r = revealer.clone();` in its Cancel handler (835-836), and that Cancel key sits inside the same revealer. An unparented GTK4 widget is disposed only when its last reference is dropped, and these cycles never drop it.
findings.impact: Each click on an agent's settings key leaks a full popover: about 40 widgets (entries, switches, DropDown, revealers) plus their closures. Memory grows with every popover opened, with no bound. phone_status keeps writing to the leaked labels.
findings.fix: Capture `popover.downgrade()` and `revealer.downgrade()` and upgrade them inside the handlers, or use `glib::clone!(@weak popover => …)`.

v1.reason: agent_settings (agent_menu.rs:366-381) creates a gtk::Popover, sets it as `key`'s child, and on closed only unparents it in an idle callback. Strong clones of the popover (`let p = popover.clone()`) are moved into closures on widgets inside it: brief (451-455), save (541, cloned again into the future), and the confirm-strip run closures (578, 608). The cycle is popover -> body -> button -> closure -> popover. A GtkPopover is not a toplevel, so nothing calls dispose on it. Unparenting drops only the parent's reference, so the refcount never reaches zero, and the signal handlers that hold the cycle are only released on dispose. Each open of the settings popover therefore leaks the whole widget subtree. phone_section re-points the global phone.view/phone.stop weak refs at the newest popover, so phone_status writes to the latest, possibly closed and leaked, label. This is harmless.
v1.correction: The Cancel handler's `revealer.clone()` (confirm_strip 835-836) is not a separate root cause. That cycle would be broken by the popover's dispose if the popover were ever disposed. The popover captures are the only real cause. Impact is small: the popover is unrealized on unparent, so its GdkSurface is freed, and the leak is tens of KB of widgets and closures per manual click. Growth is bounded by how often the user opens the popover, which is why low fits better than medium. Fix: capture popover.downgrade() in those closures, or keep the popover per key and reuse it.

findings.title: Closing with "Also remove the worktree" can exceed the 30 s client timeout; the pane comes back while the engine is still deleting it
findings.evidence: close_agent treats every error from session.close as a refusal: it removes the name from `closing`, shows "Could not close {name}: {error}" and calls `ui.refresh()` (157-169). session.close is a lifecycle request with the default 30 s timeout (client.rs:65-72). With remove_worktree the engine kills the PTY with its exit callback silenced (session.rs:1566-1571). It then runs teardown and worktree::remove before answering (session.rs:1572-1586). worktree::remove runs purge_build, a dir_size walk of the whole tree, and an unbounded `git worktree remove --force` (worktree.rs:339-369). The row becomes `closed` only after that (session.rs:1608).
findings.impact: With a large worktree (Unreal or Gradle build output) the client times out. It shows "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown", and refresh() lists the session again because it isn't closed yet. The pane reappears with a killed process and a worktree being deleted under it. If the user clicks Close again, teardown and removal run a second time on the same tree, producing worktree.remove_failed errors, until the first close finally emits session.changed(closed).
findings.fix: Use a long timeout for session.close when remove_worktree is set. In close_agent, treat Error::Timeout as still closing: keep the name in `closing`, show "Still removing the worktree…", and let the session.changed(closed) event settle it instead of refreshing.

v1.reason: The mechanism checks out. close_agent (agent_menu.rs:149-170) treats every Err, Timeout included, as a refusal: it removes the name from `closing`, shows an error and calls ui.refresh(). session.close falls to the 30 s default in request_timeout (client.rs:65-72). The handler is register_staged (session.rs:1547). When remove is set, its unlocked phase does take_pty + silence_exit + kill. It then runs teardown, and worktree::remove runs purge_build (dir_size + remove_dir_all of target/build/.gradle/...), dir_size of the whole tree, and `git worktree remove --force` through the unbounded `git()` helper (worktree.rs:26-33, 351-369). Only after that does the commit phase set state='closed' (session.rs:1608). If that work exceeds 30 s, the client reports a timeout. refresh() still sees the session as non-closed and brings the pane back with its PTY already gone. A second Close runs another unlocked worktree::remove on the same tree at the same time (the read phase holds no lock), which can fail with worktree.remove_failed. I could not establish how often removal actually takes more than 30 s. It depends on disk speed and the size of the build output: a Rust `target/` of several GB with ~100k files is a realistic trigger, but not a certain one.
v1.correction: The remove-worktree path is opt-in from the popover: the checkbox defaults to off, and agent_menu.rs:612 sends remove.is_active(). The engine's own default when the field is omitted is true (session.rs:1548), but the native client always sends the field. Also note the unbounded `git worktree remove` in worktree.rs:26 (Command::output, not proc::output_with_timeout). It runs in an unlocked staged read phase, so it does not freeze the bus, but nothing bounds it. Fix as proposed: give session.close a long timeout when remove_worktree is set, and treat Error::Timeout as still closing.

findings.title: Every session.changed event, from any project, re-fetches the whole board and rebuilds all its cards
findings.evidence: apply_session_event ends with `if matches!(self.page.borrow().as_str(), "board" | "dashboard") { self.refresh_page(); }` (133-135). The event loop lets session.* events through regardless of project (app.rs:1213-1229). For "board", refresh_page runs pages::refresh: task.list + module.list (pages.rs:41-78). Then Board::render clears and rebuilds every card (board_view.rs:1181-1221). The board shows no session-row data, only the task["sessions"] names that come from task.list. Session transitions that affect a task already emit task.changed (session.rs:1396-1398, 104-108), which refreshes the page through the generic branch.
findings.impact: With several agents working, session.changed fires on every idle/running/blocked flip (session.rs:1423-1426, engine.rs:1328-1338). While the board is open, each one triggers (coalesced) a full-project task.list under the store mutex, about 10 queries per task, plus a rebuild of every card on the GTK thread. The board stutters, hover and drag state resets, and every other bus request waits on the mutex.
findings.fix: Remove "board" from that condition and let task.changed drive board refreshes. Refresh the dashboard only if it shows session state, and only for current-project sessions, or debounce it.

v1.reason: apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:133-135) calls refresh_page() whenever the page is board or dashboard. In app.rs:1213-1229, events outside the current project are skipped only when they don't start with `session.`, so session events from every project reach this code. refresh_page (app.rs:1662-1686) is coalesced through page_dirty/page_pending but still runs pages::refresh for board, which does task.list plus module.list (pages.rs:41-78). board_view::show then calls Board::render, which runs clear(&self.content) and rebuilds every card (board_view.rs:1181-1221). The board's only session-derived data is task.sessions (names from task_sessions, row_task task.rs:231) and task.state. The engine already emits task.changed when a builder's state moves a task to running/blocked (session.rs:1391-1398) and when work completes (session.rs:104-108). That event refreshes the page through the generic else branch (app.rs:1263). The board refresh on session.changed is therefore redundant and adds a full rebuild for every session state change in any project.
v1.correction: Frequency is lower than "every flip" might suggest. session.report emits only when state_changed or provider_ref_changed (session.rs:1423), so it fires about once per transition per agent, not once per hook. Scroll positions are restored after render, but the cards are rebuilt, so hover, focus and any in-progress drag are reset. task.list runs under the store mutex with prepare_cached statements: a modest cost, not a bus freeze. Fix: drop "board" from the condition, or skip it when payload project_id is not the current project. Check whether a task.changed is missing for a new task_sessions link before relying on that event alone.

findings.title: Opening a task detail runs four heavy queries, two in sequence, and repeats all of them after every action
findings.evidence: open() awaits task.get, then module.list, then task.list, one after another (514-524). compose() runs the same pair in parallel with tokio::join! (430-433). task.list returns every task in the project. row_task runs about 10 subqueries per row: sessions, commits, attachments, labels, three relation queries, children, a subtree walk and depth_of (task.rs:229-341). All of it runs under the store mutex (`e.register::<List>`, task.rs:831). It is used only to fill two combos and the child list (714, 754, 807). detail() then calls task.activity straight away (1134). Its audit query applies json_extract to the project's audit rows, newest first, until it has 101 matches (task.rs:760-768). That happens even if Messages and History are never opened. A successful action() closes the detail and calls open() again (1169-1175).
findings.impact: On a project with hundreds of tasks and a long audit history, each detail open holds the single store mutex for a full task.list and an audit scan. Each label add/remove, Move or Link reopens the detail and pays it again. Hooks, guardrail checks and other requests wait behind it, and the detail itself is slow to appear.
findings.fix: Run the calls with tokio::join!. Take the child list from task["children"] or task.children. Fill the parent/relation combos from the board's already-fetched list, or lazily. Load task.activity the first time its tab is shown. After an auxiliary action, refetch task.get only.

v1.reason: The call pattern is as described. open() awaits task.get, module.list and task.list one after another (514-524), while compose uses tokio::join!. The full task.list (row_task runs about 10 prepare_cached subqueries per row, under the store mutex via e.register) is used only for the child list, the parent combo and the relation combo. task_activity (960, 1056) runs eagerly, and its audit query scans the project's retained audit rows with json_extract until it has limit+1 matches. For a task with few events that means the whole retained window. action() reopens after each success and also calls refresh_page, so the board runs task.list again. What I could not establish is the real cost. row_task is already optimized (the PERF §1.2 comment), task.list is the same query a board refresh runs anyway, and the audit is pruned by retention. No measurement shows this holding the mutex long enough to be felt. The redundancy is real; the impact is not shown.
v1.correction: Child ids already come back in task['children'], and the board has the list already. Parallelize the calls, defer task.activity until its tab is shown, and avoid the full reopen after small actions. The sequential awaits add latency to the panel opening; they do not add mutex hold time.

findings.title: open() shows late or duplicate task details and misleading ones when list calls fail
findings.evidence: open() starts a future that awaits three round trips and then always calls `detail(&ui, task, …)` (525). That presents a modal page panel on `ui.page_overlay`, which wraps every page including the agents wall (app.rs:542-544), and makes that page insensitive (panel.rs:244-247). After the awaits there is no project, page or serial check, and there is no guard against an open already in flight. Errors from module.list and task.list become `Value::Null` (520, 524).
findings.impact: When the engine is busy, the detail pops up seconds later over whatever page the user moved to, and disables it. Opening the same card twice (e.g. Enter pressed twice) stacks two editable detail panels whose saves conflict with each other. If task.list fails, the task shows no subtasks and an unselected parent combo; pressing "Set parent" then sends parent_id:null (773) and detaches the task.
findings.fix: Record project, page and a per-open serial before awaiting, and drop the result if they changed. Keep the set of open task ids and present the existing panel instead of making another. Show list errors in the detail status.

v1.reason: open() (513-529) has no in-flight or staleness guard. It awaits three calls and then always runs detail(), which makes a Panel::page on ui.page_overlay and presents it, making the host content insensitive (panel.rs:244-252). There is no project, page or serial check. dismiss_panels on navigation only closes panels that already exist, so a late result still appears over the new page. The window is small in practice: the calls are local IPC and normally take milliseconds, and once a detail is presented the board beneath it is insensitive, so a duplicate needs two activations within that window. A stacked duplicate save is caught by the expected/draft_conflicts check, not lost. The parent-detach claim holds as stated. If task.list fails, the parent combo has only the '' row, chosen() returns '', and 'Set parent' sends parent_id:null (773). But that needs a task.list failure followed by a deliberate click.
v1.correction: Severity stays low. Stale or late presentation needs a slow engine (seconds). The parent-null case needs task.list to fail and the user to press Set parent. Fix as suggested: check the page or project after the awaits, de-duplicate by task id, and show list errors.

findings.title: Both "Load older" buttons in the task detail fetch and append messages and history together; a refresh after sending can be dropped
findings.evidence: `for (button, reset) in [(&refresh, true), (&more, false), (&message_more, false)]` (1039) gives "Load older activity" and "Load older messages" the same handler. It sends both cursors (1052, 1056) and appends both pages (1059-1075). `if loading.replace(true) { return; }` (1051) silently drops a click while a load is running, including the `refresh.emit_clicked()` that follows a successful mailbox.send (1124).
findings.impact: Paging History also appends the next page of messages to the Messages tab, and the reverse; the two buttons do the same thing. A message sent while a page is loading doesn't appear until the user presses Refresh.
findings.fix: Give each button its own stream and cursor (send only before_audit for history, only before_message for messages). Queue a pending refresh instead of dropping it while loading.

v1.reason: task_pages.rs:1039 wires `[(&refresh, true), (&more, false), (&message_more, false)]` to one closure. For non-reset clicks it sends both cursors from `*cursors.borrow()` (1052, then the task.activity call at 1056) and appends both `messages` and `history` rows (1059-1075). The server (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:760-800) pages the audit and messages queries separately, each with its own `before_*` cursor. So 'Load older activity' also appends the next page of messages, and 'Load older messages' also appends older history. When a stream runs out, its cursor is set to `Some(0)` (1080), and `id < 0` returns nothing, so the cross-append only happens while the other stream still has more than 100 rows for this task. `if loading.replace(true) { return; }` (1051) silently drops any click while a load is in flight. That includes `refresh.emit_clicked()` after a successful mailbox.send (1124), so a sent message can be missing until Refresh is pressed again. Both are real UI logic bugs, but the triggers are uncommon: the cross-append needs more than 100 linked messages or history rows, and the dropped refresh needs a send to finish while a page load is in flight.
v1.correction: The mixed paging only shows up while both streams still have older pages (each over 100 rows for the task). Once one stream is exhausted its cursor is 0 and that stream adds nothing. Fix as proposed: give each 'older' button its own stream (send only its own cursor and append only its own rows), and set a pending-refresh flag that is replayed when `loading` clears instead of dropping the click. This is apps/relay-native, which cannot be compiled in this environment.

findings.title: "Link" with no task selected sends other_id 0
findings.evidence: The `other` ComboBoxText has no placeholder row and nothing selected (806-812). The payload uses `chosen(&other).parse::<i64>().unwrap_or(0)` (821).
findings.impact: Clicking Link without choosing a task sends task.relate with other_id 0. The engine answers "NotFound task.not_found: no task 0" (task.rs:637), which tells the user nothing useful.
findings.fix: Check before sending ("Choose a task to link"), or add a placeholder row and keep Link disabled until a task is chosen.

v1.reason: The `other` ComboBoxText (task_pages.rs:806-812) has no placeholder or initial selection. The Link payload uses `chosen(&other).parse::<i64>().unwrap_or(0)` (821). Relate calls assert_relatable, which looks up task 0 and returns 'no task 0' (task.rs:353), and action() shows that raw error in the status line. Nothing is corrupted. The error message is just unhelpful.
v1.correction: Validate before sending, or keep Link insensitive until a task is chosen.

findings.title: Draft builds a layout that two of its three users tear down; its window field is always None; detail() re-sorts a flat form into columns
findings.evidence: `let window: Option<gtk::Window> = None;` (75) is never anything else, so the close-request handler (107-118), present()'s window branch (156-158) and close()'s destroy branch (167-169) never run. `base: Rc<RefCell<Value>>` and `busy: Rc<Cell<bool>>` are never shared outside the Rc<Draft>. Draft::build wraps the form in a ScrolledWindow and appends status and footer (85-87). detail() removes status, footer and the ScrolledWindow again (930-932, 961-965), and note docs do the same (note_pages/doc.rs:302-318). detail() appends about 40 widgets to one box, then a 25-line loop (903-929) splits them into two columns: `transitions` marks the boundary, and the "section-label" CSS class marks expander headings. `d.form.set_spacing(8); set_orientation(Vertical)` (955-956) change nothing. The priority/type/size/state option lists are repeated as literals in compose and detail (352-354, 404-413, 546-565).
findings.impact: detail() is 450 lines. Inserting a widget before `transitions` silently moves it to the other column. The dead window code suggests a detached-window mode that doesn't exist. Adding an engine enum value means editing several literal lists that can drift apart.
findings.fix: Delete `window` and its branches, and make base/busy plain RefCell/Cell. Have Draft own only state, status and footer, and let callers place them. Build detail directly into `edit` and `side` boxes with explicit Expanders. Define PRIORITIES/TYPES/SIZES/STATES constants next to COLUMNS.

v1.reason: task_pages.rs:75 `let window: Option<gtk::Window> = None;` is never reassigned, so the close-request hook (107-118), present()'s window branch (156-158) and close()'s destroy branch (167-170) are dead. base/busy are Rc-wrapped but nothing clones those Rcs out; they are only reached through Rc<Draft>. Draft has three users (task detail at 598, module at note_pages.rs:1363, note at note_pages/doc.rs:301). Two of them undo the layout Draft::build creates. The task detail removes the ScrolledWindow (960-964) and status/footer (930-931) and then re-sorts d.form's children into edit/side columns. It uses identity with `transitions` (906) as the boundary and the "section-label" CSS class to build Expanders (909-921). The note editor removes status, footer and the ScrolledWindow (302-308). The type/priority/state literal lists repeat at 352-353, 361, 382, 404-413 and 546-565.
v1.correction: This is a cleanup with modest payoff, not a bug. The fragility claim is fair: the column split depends on child order relative to `transitions` and on a CSS class. Note that d.form.set_orientation(Vertical) at 956 is not strictly a no-op, because the form's orientation comes from the caller. Dropping it would need checking against how the task form was created.

findings.title: action() always closes the Draft on success, so the module editor closes after every "Add task"
findings.evidence: On success action() runs `d.close(); ui.refresh_page(); if let Some(id) = reopen { open(&ui, id) }` (1169-1176). `reopen` can only be a task id, so a Draft that isn't a task can never be reopened. The module editor uses action() for "Add task" with reopen None (note_pages.rs:1391-1400).
findings.impact: Each task added from a module editor closes the editor. To see the new task or add another, the user must reopen the module.
findings.fix: Take a reopen callback (`Option<Box<dyn Fn(&Rc<Ui>)>>`), or add a keep-open mode that refreshes the Draft in place, so module actions can return to the module.

v1.reason: task_pages.rs action() on Ok runs `d.busy.set(false); d.close(); ui.refresh_page(); if let Some(id) = reopen { open(&ui, id) }`. Draft::close (task_pages.rs:160) calls `panel.close()` on the page panel that Draft::new creates. The module editor (note_pages.rs:1391-1399) calls action() for 'Add task' (task.create) with `reopen: None`, so every successful add closes the module page. The module's task list (built from `module["tasks_by_state"]`) is not refreshed in place either. To see the new task or add another, the user has to reopen the module. The same path also closes the module after Complete/Reopen (1430) and Delete (1447). Closing after Delete is correct, and after Complete/Reopen it is arguably fine. Only 'Add task' is clearly wrong.
v1.correction: Keeping the Draft open is not enough on its own, because the module page renders its task list once from module.get. The simplest fix is to make `reopen` a callback, or add a module variant, so 'Add task' re-opens the module editor (the module open function in note_pages.rs) after closing it. The other option is to reload the form in place. Only 'Add task' needs this; Complete/Reopen/Delete can keep closing. This is apps/relay-native, which cannot be compiled in this environment.

findings.title: phone_error matches an error code the engine never sends; duplicate bus_code helper
findings.evidence: `Some("device.sdk_missing") | Some("device.adb_missing") => format!("Android SDK not found: {error}")` (91). An SDK lookup failure comes back as `avd.sdk_missing` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:435); `device.sdk_missing` doesn't exist. `Some("device.busy") => error.to_string()` (90) does exactly what the wildcard arm does. bus_code (77-82) duplicates note_pages/doc.rs:1100-1105.
findings.impact: When the SDK is missing, the user sees the raw "Unavailable avd.sdk_missing: Android SDK root could not be detected" without the engine's hint to set the SDK path in Settings, because BusError's Display drops the hint. A missing adb is reported as "Android SDK not found", which is wrong.
findings.fix: Match "avd.sdk_missing" and give adb_missing its own sentence. Remove the device.busy arm. Add `Error::code()` in client.rs and use it in both places.

v1.reason: agent_menu.rs:91 matches `device.sdk_missing`, which no engine code emits. A search of crates/relay-core finds only `avd.sdk_missing` (device.rs:435) and `device.adb_missing` (device.rs:565, 570). The `avd.sdk_missing` error is reachable from device.run, the op whose errors phone_error formats: device.rs:163-166 returns android_sdk_root's error whenever the default Gradle command is used. It therefore falls to the wildcard arm. BusError's Display is `{kind:?} {code}: {message}` (relay-bus error.rs:49) and leaves out `hint`, so the user sees "Unavailable avd.sdk_missing: Android SDK root could not be detected" and never the "set the Android SDK path in Settings" hint. `device.adb_missing` gets the wrong prefix "Android SDK not found:", although the raw message after it is still accurate. The `device.busy` arm (line 90) returns error.to_string(), exactly what the wildcard does. bus_code (77-82) and note_pages/doc.rs:1100-1105 are two copies of a 4-line helper that differ only in return type.
v1.correction: Category is bug, not docs-drift. The adb_missing case is misleading but not fully wrong, because the real message follows the prefix. The duplicated bus_code is trivial: a shared Error::code() is a nice-to-have, not a defect. The main fix is to match `avd.sdk_missing` and append the BusError hint.

findings.title: Phone install state goes stale: Stop hits the previous run while a new install starts, and a reopened popover's install button stays disabled
findings.evidence: phone_status only sets `phone.run` when given Some (802-804) and never clears it. Stop is shown when `busy && run.is_some()` (652, 812). A new install sets busy=true with run=None ("Looking for a phone…" 685, "Building …" 730), so the old run id stays. Stop (656-667) then sends device.run.stop for the finished run, which the engine accepts and ignores (device.rs:263-288). A popover opened during a run creates its install button disabled (`install.set_sensitive(!phone.busy)`, 653). Only the button that started the run is re-enabled (722); phone_status updates only `view` and `stop` (807-813). Agents.phone gains one entry per session name and is never pruned (25, 644-649, 799).
findings.impact: Pressing Stop while a new build is starting seems to work, but the build keeps going. After a run ends, the Build & install button in a popover opened during the run stays disabled until the popover is reopened. The phone map grows slowly without bound.
findings.fix: Reset `run` to None when an install starts. Keep a weak ref to the install button in Phone and set its sensitivity in phone_status. Remove `phone` entries when a session closes.

v1.reason: phone_status (797-814) assigns phone.run only when run.is_some() and never clears it. A new install calls phone_status(..., true, None) for "Looking for a phone…" (685) and "Building …" (730), so busy=true while run still holds the previous id. That makes Stop visible (812), and Stop (656-667) sends device.run.stop for the old run. RunStop (device.rs:263-288) removes nothing and only updates rows in building/running, so it returns Ok and does nothing. The window is short (device.list plus the device.run request), which is why this is low. The popover is rebuilt on every open (agent_settings 362-381). Opening it during a run creates install with set_sensitive(!phone.busy)=false (653). When the run ends, only the `key` captured by the original popover's click handler is re-enabled (722), and phone_status updates only view/stop. A popover that stays open across the end of the run therefore keeps a disabled Build & install button. The Agents.phone map gets an entry for each session name whose settings popover was opened and is never pruned. Growth is real but tiny.
v1.correction: The map growth is negligible: one small struct per session name whose popover was opened, for the life of the process. It does not justify the 'unbounded' framing. The main fixes are to clear `run` in phone_status when busy starts with None, and to have phone_status update a weak ref to the current install button.

findings.title: The close confirmation says the branch is kept, but the engine deletes merged branches after close
findings.evidence: The confirmation reads "Stop this agent and close its pane? The branch is kept." (609), and the tooltip says "the worktree and branch are kept unless you choose otherwise" (590). session.close schedules `branch_cleanup::after_close` (session.rs:1625-1634). That deletes the branch locally once its work is provably merged, and on GitHub when a merged PR proves it (branch_cleanup.rs:1-21).
findings.impact: After closing a session whose work is merged, relay/<name> disappears locally and possibly on the remote, contrary to what the dialog promised.
findings.fix: Change the copy to "Its branch is kept unless its work is already merged."

v1.reason: agent_menu.rs:609 confirm_strip caption reads "Stop this agent and close its pane? The branch is kept." and the row tooltip at 590 says "the worktree and branch are kept unless you choose otherwise". session.close (session.rs ~1627-1635) queues ctx.after_commit -> branch_cleanup::after_close (skipped only for Instance::Test), and branch_cleanup.rs:1-21 documents that it deletes relay/<name> locally once its work is provably merged (ancestor / git cherry) and on GitHub when a merged PR proves it. So the copy promises something the engine does not do for merged work. Only merged work is deleted, so nothing unmerged is lost; the impact is misleading copy.
v1.correction: Both strings (590 tooltip and 609 caption) need the change, e.g. "Its branch is kept unless its work is already merged." Deletion happens off the request after commit, not inside session.close.

results.coverage:
I read every line of apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs, onboarding.rs and terminal.rs.

To trace callers and callees I read:
- app.rs: Ui fields, call, connect, refresh, reconcile, update_attachments, launch revealer and scrim wiring, close-request.
- agent_menu.rs: launch_placeholders, launch_progress, launch_adopt, launch_done, launch_abort, apply_session_event.
- shell.rs: open_project, layout, install_shortcuts, load_appearance.
- panel.rs and client.rs.
- The launch and setup sections of smoke.rs and roadmap_smoke.rs.

On the engine side I read:
- socket.rs: the per-connection request loop and session.attach streaming.
- pty.rs: the ring, attach and the catch-up bound.
- engine.rs: the input fast path and lock acquisition.
- handlers/session.rs: create, spawn, attach, input, resize.
- handlers/task.rs: list, dispatch, assign_session.
- handlers/workspace.rs: discover, create, add, clone.
- handlers/provider.rs, providers.rs, github.rs.
- The catch-up decisions in docs (D97, the perf baseline, the P3 spike).

Scope notes:

findings.title: project.clone runs `git clone` inside a locked handler with no timeout, freezing the whole engine for the length of the clone
findings.evidence: `e.register::<ProjectClone>(|ctx: &mut Ctx, p| { ... let output = Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()` (workspace.rs:228-235). Plain `register` runs the handler inside the store transaction with the store mutex held (engine.rs:478, CLAUDE.md), and `.output()` has no deadline (it does not use `proc::output_with_timeout`). The client expects it to be long: client.rs:67 `"project.clone" => Duration::from_secs(1800)`. Onboarding's GitHub tab sends it: onboarding.rs:527 `setup.ui.call(if gh {"project.clone"} else {"project.add"},payload)`. Every agent request takes the store lock at least for guardrail authorization (engine.rs:870-871 `if let Some(sid) = session_id { let conn = self.store.lock();`).
findings.impact: A user adds a project from the GitHub tab, which is a normal onboarding flow. For the whole clone every other bus request blocks on the store mutex: all agents' hooks, guardrail checks and MCP calls, session lifecycle, and UI refreshes. The clone can take seconds, or many minutes for a large or LFS repo. It never ends if git stalls on the network or prompts for credentials on the engine's controlling terminal or through an askpass. Every running session hangs until git exits.
findings.fix: Make project.clone a staged op (`register_staged`). Run the clone in the unlocked prepare phase through `proc::output_with_timeout`, with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and stdin null. Do the project.add insert in the locked finish phase, and remove the destination on failure as today. On the client, send it over its own connection (see the onboarding connection finding).

v1.reason: crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:228 registers ProjectClone with plain `e.register`. Engine::register (engine.rs:478) inserts it into `handlers`, so dispatch runs it at engine.rs:954-956: `let mut conn = self.store.lock(); ... conn.transaction()`. It is not in `prepares` or `unlocked`. No other registration of ProjectClone exists. Line 234 runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()` with no timeout, without proc::output_with_timeout, with no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (other git call sites set it: worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943/1349, branch_cleanup.rs:114) and with inherited stdin. So for the whole clone the store mutex is held, and every locked request queues behind it: hooks, guardrail checks, MCP calls, session lifecycle and UI refreshes. The trigger is normal. The native onboarding GitHub tab sends project.clone (onboarding.rs:527), and the client gives it a 1800 s timeout (client.rs:67), which shows the author expects it to be slow. The op's own metadata (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38) says "async; project.changed when done", which the handler does not honour.
v1.correction: Severity is high, not critical. The rubric names "a freeze of the bus" as high.
