It is a user-initiated, one-off action, and session.input does not touch SQLite (D148), so keystrokes keep reaching the PTYs. Agents' hooks, guardrail calls and the UI still stall for the length of the clone. That is seconds for a small repo and minutes for a large or LFS one. The hang can be unbounded if the network stalls, because git has no default low-speed timeout, or if git prompts on an inherited tty, since GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT is not set. The fix stands: use register_staged, run the clone in prepare through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and null stdin, and do the project.add insert in finish, removing the directory on failure. Also fix or honour the docs drift in the op description ("async").

v2.reason:
(a) Confirmed at 361c6f9.
- workspace.rs:228 registers ProjectClone with plain `e.register`. Line 234 runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()`.
- The call does not go through proc::output_with_timeout and does not set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Other git call sites do set it: worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943 and :1349, branch_cleanup.rs:114. Stdin is inherited.
- dispatch_inner takes `self.store.lock()` and opens the transaction before calling the handler (engine.rs:954-956). Store::lock is a blocking std Mutex with no deadline (store.rs:474-476).
- ProjectClone is in neither `prepares` nor `unlocked`. D144 and D149 forbid exactly this, and project.clone is missing from D149's list of converted ops.

(b) How it is reached:
- From "Add project…" (shell/registry.rs:472, then open_repository_in, then onboarding::open) or from first run, through the GitHub tab (onboarding.rs:527). The client allows it 1800 s (client.rs:67).
- The op is UserOnly, so an agent cannot trigger it.
- It is occasional, once per project added from GitHub. It is normally done while agents are running.

(c) What happens while git runs:
- Agents: every agent socket request first blocks in check_session_token, at `self.store.lock()` (engine.rs:1378). That stalls all agents' MCP calls and PreToolUse hooks.
- Lifecycle reports: they hit their 10 s hook timeout and are dropped. They are best-effort.
- bus.ping: it is a locked op, so run.sh's 2 s `ready` check fails and a relaunch reports that the engine is not ready.
- UI on other connections: locked refreshes wait. The phone door waits too.
- UI main connection: it is blocked outright. handle_conn serves one request at a time per connection (socket.rs:335-745 awaits each spawn_blocking before reading the next line). Ui::call sends project.clone on that main connection (app.rs:1111-1116, not a lifecycle op), so every other UI call times out at 30 s.
- What keeps working: keystrokes and PTY output. Small session.input is answered inline from memory (D148 fast path), each terminal has its own connection, and the PTY reader only touches atomics (pty.rs:214). Sessions resume when git exits.
- How long: a local clone of 1,500 files takes 263 ms p50 (BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:210). A real GitHub or LFS clone takes seconds to many minutes.
- It can be unbounded. run.sh:32 starts the engine with nohup and no setsid, so it keeps the terminal. If ./run.sh was started from a terminal and git needs credentials with no helper or askpass, git waits on /dev/tty. Only killing git or the engine ends it, and killing the engine drops every live PTY.

Aggravating effect, also verified:
- Relay installs the Claude and Codex PreToolUse guardrail hooks with `timeout: 30` (hooks.rs:351 and :521).
- The hook's socket client has no deadline (socket.rs:801-818, main.rs:466-471).
- Claude Code's hooks reference says a timed-out PreToolUse command hook does not block the tool call.
- So once a clone passes 30 s, every Claude agent's Bash, Edit and Write calls skip the Relay gate silently for the rest of the clone. Commits stay gated, because the git pre-commit hook has no timeout and simply waits.
- The root cause of that bypass is the hook's missing deadline. Any store-lock hold over 30 s triggers it.

(d) Severity is high. The rubric lists "a freeze of the bus" as high. The trigger is a user-only, occasional action. Typing still works, no data is lost, and the bus recovers when git exits. The unbounded case depends on the environment: a terminal launch, a private repo, and no credential helper or askpass. The guardrail lapse is "a safety check silently bypassed", which is high, and it comes from a separate defect. Neither justifies critical for this root cause.

(e) The fix is the right shape and has precedent: git.fetch is staged, and fetch_remote uses output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (git.rs:580, 938-950). As proposed it is incomplete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
Severity: high, not critical.

Corrections to the impact:
- "It never ends if git stalls on the network" is overstated. git enables TCP keepalive, so a dead peer ends the clone in hours, not never.
- An askpass prompt is a visible dialog that the user can cancel.
- The truly unbounded case is a terminal prompt on an inherited tty, which happens when ./run.sh was started from a terminal (nohup does not detach the tty).
- Add: the UI's main connection is fully serialized behind the clone (socket.rs:335-745). The client half of the fix, sending the clone on its own connection like Client::lifecycle_request, is therefore required, not optional.
- Add a cross-reference: a clone longer than 30 s also lapses the Claude and Codex PreToolUse guardrails. The cause is the 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:351 and :521), no client deadline, and Claude Code treating a timed-out hook as non-blocking. Report that as its own finding; the fix is for the hook to enforce its own deadline under 30 s and exit 2.

Fix refinements:
1. Run the clone in register_staged prepare through proc::output_with_timeout, with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and a long deadline. The client already allows 1800 s; a fetch-style 20 s deadline would break legitimate clones. output_with_timeout already nulls stdin and starts the child in its own process group (proc.rs:31-39). Without GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, a tty prompt would stop git with SIGTTIN until the deadline instead of failing fast.
2. A deadline kill is a SIGKILL to the process group (proc.rs:52-55). That skips git's own cleanup and leaves a partial directory, so a retry then hits project.clone_destination. Remove that directory. Moving the `exists()` check out of the lock lets two concurrent clones to the same dest both pass it. So claim the destination atomically (fs::create_dir, then clone into the empty directory). Remove only a directory this op created, on clone failure, timeout, or a project.add failure in finish.
3. Keep the project.add call through invoke_registered in finish.
4. Fix the docs drift. relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38 says "(async; project.changed when done)", and BUS.md:246-250 lists project.clone among ops that return a handle and get a `.completed` audit row. The handler is synchronous. Either make it async (an after_commit worker, the D144 pattern for long work) or correct the docs.

findings.title: A terminal pane whose stream hits any error stays dead: the loop breaks but `active` stays true, so update_attachments never re-attaches it
findings.evidence: `set_active` returns early when nothing changed: `if self.active.replace(active) == active { return; }` (443). The stream loop: `Ok(()) => { p.status.set_text("Recovering output"); } Err(e) => { p.status.set_text(&e.to_string()); break; }` (462-469). After the break nothing resets `active` or the finished `stream` handle. `update_attachments` (app.rs:1567-1583) is the only caller of set_active, so later calls with `true` are no-ops. `session.attach` is a locked handler (`e.register::<Attach>`, session.rs:1640), queued behind the store mutex, with the default 30 s client timeout (client.rs request_timeout).
findings.impact: Any transient attach or stream error leaves the pane frozen on stale output. Triggers include a 30 s attach timeout while the store lock is held by a long op (project.clone, a large workspace.discover), a handler panic that closes the pane's socket, and `session.not_spawned` during a state race. The pane shows text such as "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown; refresh before retrying.", with no retry and nothing to refresh. It recovers only if the user leaves the Agents page, minimizes and restores, or switches project and back.
findings.fix: On Err, retry with backoff while `active` is still true, and stop only on final errors (for example not_spawned when the row is no longer live). Alternatively, set `active` to false and clear `stream` when the loop exits so the next reconcile re-attaches. Give the status strip a Retry action.

v1.reason: In set_active, the stream loop (terminal.rs:458-471) breaks on any Err from attach_and_render and shows the error text. Nothing resets `active` or takes `stream` afterwards. Later set_active(true) calls from update_attachments (the only caller apart from Pane::stop) return early at 443 because active is already true. Errors that lead here: Client::connect failure; the session.attach timeout (a locked `e.register::<Attach>` at session.rs:1640, run via spawn_blocking in socket.rs:455-459, so it queues behind the store mutex with the default 30 s timeout from client.rs request_timeout); a protocol error on a frame; Notice::Disconnected (engine restart or socket drop); and session.not_spawned. The pane stays frozen with the error text until active flips to false, which happens when the user leaves the Agents page, hides the window, changes focus mode, or the session changes to a non-live state.
v1.correction: The not_spawned race is narrow: the spawn path writes state='running' and set_pty in the same handler (session.rs:678-686). The likelier triggers are the attach timeout under a long locked operation and an engine/socket disconnect. Simplest fix: at loop exit, set `active` to false and drop `stream` so the next reconcile re-attaches. Better: retry with backoff while active, and stop only on terminal errors.

findings.title: Launch stages task queues only after every agent is allocated, so a later allocation failure drops earlier agents' queues while the error says they are preserved
findings.evidence: Allocation loop: `if let Some(task)=tasks.first(){payload["task_id"]=json!(task);} let session=ui.call("session.create",payload).await?;` (804-805). Only after all agents exist: `for(session,tasks,_)in &allocated{for task in tasks{ ... ui.call("task.dispatch",json!({"task_id":task,"session":session["name"],"start":false})).await?;}}` (810). Any `?` exits the block, and the user then sees `"Launch incomplete: {e}. Created sessions and queues are preserved. Start the remaining sessions individually from the wall."` (824). session.create records only the first task in task_sessions (session.rs:821-825). The move to the active column and the rest of the queue come only from task.dispatch (task.rs:667, 671).
findings.impact: Example: a solo launch of 3 agents, where agent 1 has tasks #4, #7 and #9, and agent 3's worktree create fails (fetch error, name reservation, review_group_full). Agents 1 and 2 exist, but #7 and #9 were never staged and #4 was never moved to active. The banner says the queues are preserved, so the user starts agent 1 from the wall and it only ever works on #4. A dispatch failure partway through (for example a task moved to done meanwhile) likewise leaves the later queues unstaged and starts no agent.
findings.fix: Dispatch each agent's tasks (start:false) right after its own session.create, inside the allocation loop. Build the failure message from what was actually staged, naming the agents and tasks that were not.

v1.reason: In the start handler (launch.rs:798-822), the allocation loop calls session.create with only `tasks.first()` as task_id (804-805). session.create (session.rs:821-825) only inserts a task_sessions row. It does not move the task to the active column or set state. task.dispatch, which does that (task.rs:667) and queues the remaining tasks through assign_session, runs only after every agent has been allocated (810). Any `?` failure in a later session.create (a worktree fetch or checkout error, name reservation, pair validation) skips all dispatches. The banner at 824 still says "Created sessions and queues are preserved." `launch_abort` (agent_menu.rs:276) only clears placeholders. A dispatch failure partway through the 810 loop likewise leaves the later queues unstaged and spawns nothing.
v1.correction: The first task is linked through task_sessions but stays in its original column. The rest of the queue is lost. Fix: dispatch each agent's tasks with start:false right after its own session.create, and word the error from what was actually created and staged.

findings.title: After a failed first submit, onboarding keeps the workspace it just created and silently ignores later edits to the workspace directory and name
findings.evidence: `if setup.workspace.borrow()["id"].is_null() { let path = setup.workspace_path.text().trim().to_owned(); ... setup.ui.call("workspace.create", ...).await? ... *setup.workspace.borrow_mut() = workspace; }` (517-523) runs before `project.add`/`project.clone` (527). When the project step fails, `setup.workspace` keeps the new id, so every retry skips this block. `discover` also switches to `self.workspace.borrow()["path"]` (327-330). The fields stay editable (`setup.body.set_sensitive(true)`, 536) and the button is relabelled "Add project" (update_action, 369).
findings.impact: Example: first run with cwd $HOME. The user browses to /mnt/data/dev/repo and clicks Open Relay. Workspace $HOME is created, then project.add fails with project.outside_workspace. The user corrects "Workspace directory" to /mnt/data/dev and retries, but the edit is ignored and the same error repeats indefinitely; Scan also keeps scanning $HOME. An empty, stray workspace stays in the sidebar (the workspace.changed event refreshes the registry) even after the dialog is closed.
findings.fix: Adopt a newly created workspace only once the project step succeeds. Alternatively, on retry compare the entry with the created workspace's path and create or look up a new one if it changed. Disable the workspace fields once a workspace exists, so what is shown matches what is used. Also adopt the `workspace.exists` details.workspace_id instead of failing on a trailing slash or symlinked path.

v1.reason: Confirmed. In submit (onboarding.rs:516-523), the workspace is created or looked up only when `setup.workspace.borrow()["id"].is_null()`, and is stored in `setup.workspace` before project.add/project.clone runs (527). On failure, only created_project is left unset, and setup.workspace keeps the new workspace. The workspace path and name entries were built once in project_step (new_workspace was true at that point, 152-166) and are re-enabled by `setup.body.set_sensitive(true)` (536). Every retry therefore skips workspace creation and ignores an edited directory. project.add rejects a path outside the workspace with project.outside_workspace (workspace.rs:185-188), so the same error repeats. discover prefers `self.workspace.borrow()["path"]` (327-330), so Scan also keeps scanning the stale directory. update_action relabels the button "Add project" (369), the only visible hint. The created workspace is committed and emits workspace.changed (workspace.rs:111), so it stays as an empty workspace. workspace.create returns workspace.exists with details.workspace_id for a duplicate (workspace.rs:101-102). The client's `known` lookup compares raw text against stored canonical paths (520), so a trailing slash or symlinked path errors instead of adopting the existing workspace.

findings.title: Onboarding pre-fills the workspace with the GUI's raw cwd, bypassing the engine's 'use the parent of the enclosing checkout' suggestion
findings.evidence: `workspace_path: gtk::Entry::builder().text(std::env::current_dir().map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default())` (73-79). `discover` and `submit` always send this non-empty text (327-330, 518-521). The engine applies its protection only when the path is empty: `canon_workspace` calls `suggested_workspace()` only for empty input (workspace.rs:54-56, 115-116). Its doc says: "When that directory lives inside a Git checkout, use the checkout's parent so discovery presents the repository itself as a project instead of cloning another copy into its source tree" (69-71). That function also reads the engine process's cwd, not the GUI's. The returned `v["path"]` is never read by the client.
findings.impact: If relay-native is started from inside a checkout (`cargo run` in the repo, or any shell cd'ed into a project), the workspace becomes the checkout itself. Discovery then lists only that repo, and a later GitHub clone into this workspace lands inside that repo's working tree (`clone_destination` = workspace/name). Started from a subdirectory, discovery finds nothing. The engine's fix for exactly this case never runs for the native client.
findings.fix: Compute the suggestion client-side from the GUI cwd: walk up the ancestors for .git and use its parent. Alternatively, add a cwd hint to workspace.discover so the engine applies `suggested_workspace_from` to the caller's directory and returns it in `path`, then fill the entry from the returned `path`.

v1.reason: onboarding.rs:73-79 pre-fills workspace_path with the GUI's raw `current_dir()`. discover (327-330) and submit (518-521) send that non-empty text. The engine's `suggested_workspace` walk-up (workspace.rs:72-88) runs only for an empty path (workspace.rs:54, 115). Started inside a checkout, discover_repositories (393-413) returns just that repo, because the root has .git. Started from a subdirectory, it finds nothing. A clone destination is workspace/name (415-423), so a clone lands inside the checkout. The engine's own protection never runs for the native client.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low. This is first-run onboarding only. The 'Workspace directory' field is visible and editable, with a Scan button (onboarding.rs:154-158), so the user sees the path before committing. The usual desktop-launcher cwd is $HOME, which the engine heuristic would not change anyway. The trigger is mostly a developer running `cargo run` in the repo. Simplest fix: send an empty path (or omit it) on first discover and fill the entry from the returned `path`.

findings.title: Onboarding sends GitHub listing, discovery and 30-minute clones over the shared UI control socket, which the engine answers one request at a time
findings.evidence: Every switch to the GitHub tab calls `setup.load_github()` (264-265). That awaits `setup.ui.call("github.status",...)` (422) and `setup.ui.call("github.repo.list",...)` (429). `submit` awaits `project.clone` (527), and `discover` awaits `workspace.discover` (336). `Ui::call` (app.rs:1111-1117) moves only `is_lifecycle_request` ops to their own connection; these go on the shared control client. The engine handles each connection sequentially: `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? { ... tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(req, Door::Socket)).await? ... out_tx.send(...) }` (socket.rs:335-744). `github::status` and `repositories` run `gh api` (`--paginate`) through plain `Command::output()` with no timeout (github.rs:45, 68).
findings.impact: While a clone runs (up to the 1800 s client timeout), or `gh api --paginate` pages through a large account, every other UI request on the control socket waits behind it. That includes refresh's session.list, settings reads, board and task actions, and editor git status. Each times out after 30 s with a "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown" banner. Every switch from Local to GitHub queues another status and list pair. A hung `gh` blocks the control socket until the user reconnects.
findings.fix: Run long or external ops on their own connection, as `Client::lifecycle_request` already does: extend the predicate to project.clone, github.*, workspace.discover and app.import.v3. Load the GitHub list once per dialog and refresh it only from the Refresh button. On the engine side, run `gh` through `proc::output_with_timeout`.

v1.reason: Confirmed. Every switch to the GitHub tab calls load_github (onboarding.rs:264-265), which awaits github.status and then github.repo.list. submit awaits project.clone (527) and discover awaits workspace.discover (336). Ui::call sends everything except is_lifecycle_request ops (client.rs:50-63, which does not include these) on the shared control client. The engine processes one request at a time per connection (socket.rs:335-744), so every other UI request queues behind these. project.clone has an 1800 s client timeout (client.rs:67). github::status and repositories run `gh api` / `gh api --paginate` with plain Command::output() and no timeout (github.rs:45, 68). That breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout. The engine side is worse than the finding says. project.clone is registered with plain `e.register::<ProjectClone>` (workspace.rs:228) and runs `git clone ... .output()` with no timeout inside the handler (233). So the clone holds the store mutex and SQLite transaction for its whole duration, and every bus request from every door that needs the store blocks: GUI, CLI, MCP calls from agents, and the phone. workspace.discover is also registered with `e.register` (workspace.rs:114) and does a tree walk to depth 4 under the mutex. The GitHub ops use register_unlocked (provider.rs:247, 262), so a slow or hung gh blocks only that connection.
v1.correction: The proposed client-only fix, moving these ops to their own connection, does not help project.clone or workspace.discover. Those hold the store mutex, so the GUI's session.list, settings and board calls on any connection, and agents' bus calls, still wait. Engine fix: register project.clone with Engine::register_staged, running the clone outside the lock and only the project.add insert under it. Register workspace.discover with register_unlocked. Run git clone and both gh calls through proc::output_with_timeout. The client-side fix is still useful for the gh ops: give long or external ops their own connection, and load the GitHub list once per dialog rather than on every tab switch. The engine-wide freeze during a clone is arguably its own finding (category invariant, high or critical), because it stops every session's bus traffic for as long as the clone runs. session.input is answered from memory (socket.rs:731-735), so keystrokes still get through.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says, at 361c6f9.
- The engine handles one request at a time per connection. Its loop (socket.rs:335-744) awaits each `spawn_blocking(dispatch)` (socket.rs:742) before it reads the next line.
- `Ui::call` (app.rs:1111-1116) gives a request its own connection only when `is_lifecycle_request` matches (client.rs:50-63), and none of these ops match.
- So the following all occupy the shared control connection: `github.status` and `github.repo.list` (onboarding.rs:422/429, sent again on every switch to the GitHub tab, 257-269), `workspace.discover` (336, also run when the panel opens, 319), `project.clone` (527) and `app.import.v3` (532).
- `gh` runs through plain `Command::output()` with no timeout (github.rs:45, 68).

(b) Who reaches it, and how often:
- The setup panel opens at first run and from Add project / Add workspace (registry.rs:164/362/472, app.rs:978/1413). Only the local user triggers it, and only occasionally.
- The panel is modal. `present()` makes the main content insensitive (panel.rs:246), and the guard at onboarding.rs:95 refuses to close it while a clone is busy. During a clone the user therefore cannot start board, task or settings actions.
- What queues during a clone is background traffic driven by events: refresh, refresh_status, refresh_page and editor invalidation from the app.rs event loop. That traffic only exists when agents are running in other projects. At first run there is effectively none.
- During the `gh` calls the panel is not busy. The user can close it, or switch tabs repeatedly and queue more status/list pairs.

(c) What happens when it fires:
- Time spent waiting in the queue counts toward each request's 30 s timeout (client.rs:326-333).
- A clone longer than 30 s therefore produces "Request timed out" banners from refresh (app.rs:1386, 1437). The sidebar stays stale until the `ui.refresh()` after the clone (onboarding.rs:548).
- A `gh` call or a page of 100 repos takes about a second, so the usual stall is a few seconds. It passes 30 s only for accounts with thousands of repos. In that case `github.repo.list` itself also hits the default 30 s timeout (client.rs:70), so the GitHub tab cannot list them.
- A hung `gh` wedges the control connection until the user clicks Reconnect.
- No data is lost.

(d) Severity: medium, not high.
- The client-side cause is a real bug on a less common path, and the failure it causes is recoverable.
- The first verifier's "high" rests on a different root cause. `project.clone` is a plain `e.register` handler (workspace.rs:228). It runs `git clone … .output()` (234) inside `dispatch_inner`, after `self.store.lock()` and the transaction are taken (engine.rs:954).
- That engine-side lock is the main reason the UI stalls during a clone. `project.list`, `workspace.list`, `session.list` and `settings.get` are all locked handlers (workspace.rs:132/249, session.rs:1023, settings.rs:216), so they would wait for the clone even on a separate connection.

(e) The proposed client fix is correct but incomplete. The client-side and engine-side causes each produce the stall by themselves, so both have to be fixed.
v2.correction:
Severity goes back to medium. The engine-side lock should be a separate finding rather than folded into this one.

Suggested separate finding: high, category invariant, at crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:228-238.
- The handler runs `git clone` with no timeout while holding the store mutex.
- This contradicts BUS.md:247 and the op's own description in relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:37-38 ("async; project.changed when done"). It also breaks the D149 / CLAUDE.md rules on slow work and subprocesses.
- For the whole clone, every request that needs the store, from every door, waits. That includes:
  - every agent socket call, because `check_session_token` takes the lock (engine.rs:1378);
  - each agent's Edit/Write/Bash PreToolUse `guardrail.gate` hook (a locked handler, guardrail.rs:304, with a 30 s hook timeout, hooks.rs:351).
- `workspace.discover` (workspace.rs:114) is an OpKind::Query that walks directories under the lock. It should be `register_unlocked`, but its walk is usually short, so it is low impact.

Corrections to this finding's impact:
- During a clone the panel is modal and cannot be closed, so user-initiated board, task and settings actions are not affected. Only background refreshes are.
- At first run there is essentially no other traffic.

Corrections to the fix:
1. Moving the ops to another connection on the client side does not help during a clone while the engine holds the store mutex. Fixing only the engine side still leaves the control connection waiting behind the clone. Both fixes are needed.
2. Engine side:
   - Register `project.clone` with `register_staged`. The prepare step runs the clone outside the lock, through `proc::output_with_timeout` with a deadline of at least the client's 1800 s. The finish step runs the `project.add` insert, and removes the clone directory if that insert fails. The documented async-handle design is an alternative.
   - Register `workspace.discover` with `register_unlocked`.
   - Run both `gh` calls through `output_with_timeout`.
3. Client side:
   - Route `project.clone`, `github.status`, `github.repo.list`, `workspace.discover` and `app.import.v3` through a separate connection. Use a predicate with its own name rather than widening `is_lifecycle_request`.
   - Load the GitHub list once per dialog.
   - Give `github.repo.list` a longer timeout than the default 30 s (client.rs:65-71). Otherwise accounts with thousands of repos still fail even on their own connection.

findings.title: workspace.discover walks up to four directory levels while holding the store mutex, and one unreadable directory fails the whole scan
findings.evidence: `e.register::<WsDiscover>(|_, p| { ... Ok(WsDiscoverOut { path: ..., repositories: discover_repositories(&path)? }) })` (114-131) uses a locked `register` although it reads no table. `discover_repositories` recurses to depth 4 with `for entry in fs::read_dir(path)? { let entry = entry?; if !entry.file_type()?.is_dir() ...` (400-402), so any EACCES or ENOTCONN aborts the scan with workspace.discover_failed. The native client runs it automatically: `self.discover(&found);` at the end of `project_step` (onboarding.rs:319). The path defaults to the GUI process's cwd (onboarding.rs:73-79), which is $HOME when launched from the desktop entry (`Exec=relay-native`, no `Path=`).
findings.impact: Opening Add workspace, or first run, walks $HOME four levels deep under the store lock, so every agent request waits for the walk. That takes seconds on a cold cache and has no bound if a FUSE or network mount under the root stalls. One unreadable or dead-FUSE directory (for example ~/.cache/doc when the document portal is down) makes the scan fail, and the dialog lists no repositories at all.
findings.fix: Register it with `register_unlocked`, since it touches no store state. In `walk`, log and skip entries whose read_dir or file_type fails instead of propagating with `?`. Do not descend into other filesystems (compare st_dev).

v1.reason: WsDiscover is an OpMeta::query (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:12-13) with no actor restriction, yet it is registered with locked `e.register` (workspace.rs:114) and never touches ctx/SQLite. discover_repositories (workspace.rs:395-413) calls read_dir on every non-excluded directory down to depth 3, so it checks .git on dirs down to depth 4. It walks hidden dirs (.cache, .local, .cargo...) and has no filesystem boundary. All of this runs inside the store transaction and mutex, which CLAUDE.md forbids for tree walks. Any io error from `fs::read_dir(path)?`, `entry?` or `entry.file_type()?` aborts the whole scan with workspace.discover_failed, and onboarding.rs:356 then shows only the error. The native onboarding calls discover automatically (onboarding.rs:319). Its path is the workspace path or the GUI's cwd (onboarding.rs:73-79), and the desktop entry has `Exec=relay-native` with no Path=, so this is usually $HOME.
v1.correction: Also reachable by agents. The op is a query with default actors, exposed as the MCP tool workspace_discover, so an agent can pass any absolute path (e.g. / or a network mount) and hold the store mutex for the length of the walk. The proposed fix is right: register_unlocked (the op is already a Query, so the debug_assert passes), skip unreadable entries instead of propagating errors, and stay on one filesystem by comparing st_dev.

findings.title: Opening New session builds 11 full agent forms with 11 copies of every open task card synchronously on the GTK thread, and keeps them after the sheet closes
findings.evidence: `let profiles: Rc<Vec<_>> = Rc::new((0..11).map(|i| Profile::new(i, compact)).collect());` (454). The count control only offers 1 to 6 (`gtk::DropDown::from_strings(&["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"])`, 437) and a review group uses profiles 0 to 2, so profiles 6 to 10 can never be shown. After task.list returns, the loader runs `for (profile_index, profile) in p.iter().enumerate() { ... for (index, row) in tasks.iter().filter(|t| text(t, "column") != "done").enumerate() { ... } }` (628-717) with no await. Each card is a ToggleButton, an Overlay, 2 Boxes, 4 Labels (one holding the full task body) and an Image, plus a lowercased search string. Nothing clears `launch_box` when the sheet hides: close, scrim and Escape only call `set_reveal_child(false)` (384, app.rs:985, 1004).
findings.impact: Example: a project with 300 open tasks gets 3,300 task cards, about 30k widgets, each body label holding the whole task text. They are created in one main-loop turn every time the user presses New session (or Ctrl+N), which freezes the whole window, terminals included. Tens of MB stay retained in the hidden revealer afterwards. The cost grows linearly with the backlog.
findings.fix: Create profiles only up to the selected count (at most 6). Use one task model shared by all profiles (a GridView over a ListStore with per-profile selection sets), or build a profile's cards only when its key is first shown. Clear `launch_box` when the sheet hides.

v1.reason: launch.rs:454 builds 11 Profiles every time show_launch runs. Visible profiles come from count.value_as_int(), and count is only ever set from count_select, which offers 1-6 (437, 445). A review group uses profiles 0-2 (561). So profiles 6-10 can never be shown. Once task.list returns, the loader (628-717) runs synchronously in one closure turn: for each of the 11 profiles it builds a card for every non-done task, made of a ToggleButton, an Overlay, 3 Boxes, 4 Labels and an Image, plus a lowercased search string containing the full body. task.list has no limit (handlers/task.rs:831ff) and returns the whole backlog. With N open tasks that is about 11*N cards and roughly 11*11*N widgets created on the GTK thread with no yield, so the window and the terminals stall in proportion to the backlog. Close, scrim and Escape only call set_reveal_child(false) (launch.rs:384, app.rs:955/985/1004). launch_box is cleared only at the next show_launch, so the last form stays retained while hidden.
v1.correction: There are 3 Boxes per card (card, line, overlay child), not 2. Nothing is retained across opens: clear(&self.launch_box) at the start of show_launch frees the previous form, so retention is bounded to one form, and the 'tens of MB' figure is not established. Medium is right: it is a backlog-scaled UI stall, small at typical backlog sizes. The cheapest fix is to build only 6 profiles, or to build lazily the profiles the count shows, and to fill a profile's task grid when its member key is first selected.

findings.title: Catch-up replays only the last 256 KiB with no terminal state, so recreated panes lose bracketed paste, alternate screen and mouse modes
findings.evidence: A fresh Pane starts with `Sequence::default()` (211) and attaches with null epoch and from_seq (483-484). The engine answers with `ring.bounded_bytes_from(0)`: the last ATTACH_CATCHUP_BYTES (256 KiB), aligned to a 64 KiB read boundary (pty.rs:19, 96-101, 314). The client feeds it as-is: `Some((_, s)) if catch_up || seq == s + 1 => Step::Feed` (31), then `self.terminal.feed(&data)` (515). Only a new epoch resets the terminal (512). Panes are recreated on every project switch (`open_project` clears `ordered` and reconciles, shell.rs:24-31; reconcile stops panes that left the wall, app.rs:1473-1480), on reconnect, and on GUI restart. A same-pane re-attach splices the same way after more than 256 KiB was produced while it was hidden. D97 caps catch-up for speed (DECISIONS.md:430), and docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:494 notes the gap. A TUI emits its mode switches once at start-up, so they fall outside that tail for any agent that has run a while. The spike recorded Claude Code using the alternate screen and bracketed paste (docs/upstream-v3/spike/P3-terminal.md:152, 190).
findings.impact: The user switches to another project and back, or restarts the GUI, after an agent has produced more than 256 KiB (minutes of TUI redraws, per D97). The new VTE never saw the mode-set sequences. A multi-line paste is then sent without bracketed-paste markers, and VTE turns each newline into Enter, so a CLI that relies on bracketed paste can submit a partial prompt after the first line. The mouse wheel scrolls VTE's own buffer instead of the app, and redraws land on the normal screen. A splice can also start mid escape sequence and print garbage.
findings.fix: Have the engine track the PTY's terminal modes by scanning output for DECSET/DECRST 1, 25, 47/1047/1049, 1000-1006 and 2004. Prefix every catch-up with a prelude that restores them, plus a clear-screen when the catch-up was truncated. Longer term, keep a headless emulator per PTY (for example the vt100 crate) and send a screen snapshot instead of a byte tail.

v1.reason: Confirmed for the mechanism. open_project clears `ordered` and calls reconcile (shell.rs:24-31). reconcile stops and removes panes whose sessions left the wall, and builds a fresh Pane for each session of the new project (app.rs:1468-1490). A new Pane has an empty Sequence, so attach_and_render sends epoch/from_seq null (terminal.rs:477-484). Pty::attach then answers with `ring.bounded_bytes_from(0)` (pty.rs:314-320). That is only the last ATTACH_CATCHUP_BYTES = 256 KiB (pty.rs:19), starting at a saved frame boundary (pty.rs:96-102). The client feeds it as-is (terminal.rs:31, 515). The fresh VTE never sees mode-set sequences emitted earlier: DECSET 2004 bracketed paste, 1049 alternate screen, mouse reporting 1000-1006. D97 (DECISIONS.md:427-433) says agent TUIs produce megabytes of redraws, so a long-running agent soon pushes those sequences out of the tail. The spike notes Claude Code enables mouse reporting and bracketed paste (P3-terminal.md:152-190). On re-attach the pane re-sends a resize only when the size changed (terminal.rs:553), and an unchanged winsize sends no SIGWINCH. Even a redraw would not re-emit the mode sets. Frame boundaries are arbitrary PTY read chunks, so the tail can also start mid escape sequence or mid UTF-8 character. I could not observe whether a given CLI periodically re-emits ?2004h or its mouse modes, so the user-visible paste and mouse symptoms depend on the CLI. The terminal-state loss itself is deterministic.
v1.correction: A same-pane re-attach (D97 hidden pane) keeps its VTE and so keeps its modes. There the only problem is the splice: the gap is skipped and the tail may start mid-sequence. Mode loss applies only to recreated panes, after a project switch, a GUI restart, or a reconnect that rebuilds panes. The 256 KiB alignment is to a frame boundary (a PTY read chunk), not to a 64 KiB read boundary. The suggested fix is right: track DECSET/DECRST state per PTY in the engine and prepend a restore prelude, plus a clear, to a truncated catch-up, or keep a headless emulator and send a screen snapshot. Full ring replay would not be enough, because the ring itself is capped at 8 MiB.

findings.title: Window-level capture-phase shortcuts steal Ctrl+K, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+1/2/3 from agent terminals, and Ctrl+N wipes an open launch form
findings.evidence: `keys.set_propagation_phase(gtk::PropagationPhase::Capture);` is installed on the window (1066-1067, 1101). Whenever no panel is open it matches the bindings and returns `glib::Propagation::Stop` (1076-1093): `"palette" => ui.command_palette()` for Ctrl+K, `"new_session" => ui.show_launch(None)` for Ctrl+N, and navigate for Ctrl+1/2/3 and Ctrl+, (defaults in shortcuts.rs:3-11). The capture phase runs before the focused VteTerminal handles keys, so the terminal never receives these chords. `show_launch` always runs `clear(&self.launch_box)` and rebuilds (launch.rs:368), even when the sheet is already open.
findings.impact: In an agent pane, Ctrl+K (kill to end of line in readline-style prompt editors) opens the command palette, and Ctrl+N (next history) opens the launch sheet; neither key reaches the CLI. Pressing Ctrl+N while configuring agents, including while typing in the Additional instructions box, discards every prompt, model, provider and task selection in the form.
findings.fix: Skip global shortcuts when the focus widget is a VteTerminal or an editable, or run them in the bubble phase so the terminal and text fields consume their keys first. Make `show_launch` only focus the sheet when `self.launch.reveals_child()` is already true.

v1.reason: Confirmed. install_shortcuts puts a key controller in PropagationPhase::Capture on the main window (shell.rs:1066-1067, 1101). When ui.panels is empty, it matches the DEFAULTS chords (shortcuts.rs:3-11: Ctrl+K, Ctrl+1/2/3, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+, and Ctrl+Shift+B) and returns Propagation::Stop. Capture runs from the toplevel down, so it fires before the focused VteTerminal's own controller (terminal.rs:261-279, which only handles Ctrl+Shift+C/V) and before VTE's key handling. The chord is consumed and never written to the PTY. Ctrl+K (kill to end of line) and Ctrl+N (next history) are standard readline/emacs editing keys in shells and agent CLIs. show_launch (launch.rs:355-368) runs `clear(&self.launch_box)` and rebuilds the form whenever it is called. The launch sheet is a revealer, not a panel, so the panels-empty guard does not stop it, and Ctrl+N while the sheet is open discards everything entered. Mitigation: chords can be rebound or cleared in settings, and tools_settings.rs:741 describes shortcuts as 'global'. That is a decision to make them global, not to take editing keys away from terminals, and nothing excludes focused terminals or text widgets.
v1.correction: Fix: skip the global match when the focus widget is a vte4::Terminal, or an editable or text view without a modifier other than Ctrl. Alternatively use the bubble phase so focused widgets consume the key first. In show_launch, return early and only focus the sheet when launch.reveals_child() is already true. Ctrl+1/2/3 and Ctrl+, are much less likely to matter in a terminal than Ctrl+K and Ctrl+N.

findings.title: Keystrokes are sent one round trip at a time over the pane's output socket, and are dropped when the client is absent or 64 are queued
findings.evidence: The commit handler drops input instead of queuing it: `if p.client.borrow().is_none() { p.status.set_text("Input unavailable: reconnect"); } else if tx.try_send(text.into()).is_err() { p.status.set_text("Input queue full: keystroke not sent"); }` (221-225); the channel is bounded to 64 (217). The sender awaits each `client.request(&p.rt, "session.input", ...)` before taking the next item (229-247). It uses the same connection that carries the PTY frames. The reply waits behind frames in the engine's shared `out_tx` (socket.rs:295, 744) and in the client's 64-slot notice channel (client.rs:179, 242), and the engine reads the next request only after it has queued the previous reply. Items already queued are dropped silently if `p.client` became None in the meantime (234-246, no else branch). The client is None from activation until attach answers (476-487) and during every gap re-attach.
findings.impact: Under heavy output (a build log, a large catch-up), or after a large paste that the agent drains slowly, each keystroke's round trip waits behind the frame backlog. Continued typing fills the 64 slots and further keys are discarded with only a status note. Typing right after restoring the window or returning to the Agents page loses the first keystrokes while the pane re-attaches, which can take up to 30 s when the store lock is busy.
findings.fix: Send input on a connection that carries no frames, either the control client or a per-pane input client. Pipeline requests without awaiting each reply: order is kept by the single writer and the engine's sequential loop. Buffer keystrokes typed while (re)attaching instead of dropping them.

v1.reason: The code works as described. The commit handler (terminal.rs:219-227) drops a keystroke when `p.client` is None ("Input unavailable: reconnect") or when the 64-slot channel is full. The input loop (229-247) awaits each session.input reply before sending the next. It skips a queued item with no else branch, losing it silently, if the client became None in the meantime. client is None from activation until attach succeeds (476-487), and after every attach_and_render return, including Step::Gap (511) followed by a re-attach. Gaps come from dropped frames under heavy output. Input uses the pane's own connection, which also carries PTY frames. The engine reads the next request only after `out_tx.send(resp).await` (socket.rs:744) on the 1024-line out_tx shared with the frame forwarders. The client reader blocks on the bounded 64 notice channel (client.rs:242) before it can read the response line. This contradicts the transport's stated design (client.rs:1-2: own connections so backpressure cannot starve control). The most concrete user-visible failures are keys lost while re-attaching after a gap during heavy output, and keys typed just after returning to the Agents page.
v1.correction: The "64 queued keystrokes fill up" scenario is speculative. The first keystroke (e.g. Ctrl+C) is written at once; only the replies, and therefore later keystrokes, queue behind the frame backlog. VTE feeding is fast, so filling 64 slots needs a long backlog. The real loss path is the client==None window (both the commit-time drop and the silent drop at 234). Fix: buffer input while (re)attaching and flush after attach. Pipeline requests instead of awaiting each reply, or send input on a frame-free connection.

findings.title: Every launch choice is a row of toggle buttons mirrored into a hidden DropDown or SpinButton, implemented three times and already diverged
findings.evidence: `choice_cards` (3-50), `segments` (52-86) and the provider-card loop in `Profile::new` (160-207) each build a grouped ToggleButton row bound to an invisible gtk::DropDown: mode (420), role (215), effort (248), task_filter (293), provider (207) and builders (450). The count is mirrored twice, in a hidden `count_select` DropDown and a hidden `gtk::SpinButton::with_range(1.0, 11.0, 1.0)` (433-447). Two comments record a bug this pattern caused: launch.rs:438-440 ("Segmented keys hold weak references to their backing control. Keep it owned by the form") and roadmap_smoke.rs:198-199 ("An unowned backing DropDown used to be destroyed, silently leaving the count at one"). The provider copy has already diverged: there is no `provider.connect_selected_notify` that updates the cards. After `provider.set_selected(1)` (as roadmap_smoke.rs:155 does), the Claude card still shows as selected.
findings.impact: About 40 hidden widgets per form exist only to hold integers. Each must be parented in the widget tree or its row silently stops working. The three copies of the binding logic drift apart (the provider cards already do not follow their model), and every new choice row repeats the trap.
findings.fix: Add one small `Choice` helper that owns its ToggleButtons and an `Rc<Cell<u32>>`, with `selected()`, `set_selected()` and `connect_changed()`, and read the count as `selected()+1`. This removes the hidden DropDowns, the SpinButton, the reverse-binding closures and the ownership pitfall.

v1.reason: launch.rs:3-50 (choice_cards), 52-86 (segments) and the provider-card loop in Profile::new (160-207) each build a grouped ToggleButton row that writes into a hidden gtk::DropDown through a weak ref. The count is held twice: a hidden SpinButton (433) and a hidden count_select DropDown (437), and count_select's notify copies into the spin (445). The comments at launch.rs:438-440 and roadmap_smoke.rs:198-199 record that this weak-ref pattern already caused a real bug, where the count silently stuck at one. The copies have also drifted apart. segments forwards the control's sensitivity to the row but choice_cards does not. The provider cards have no reverse binding: the only provider.connect_selected_notify (232) updates the effort keys, not the cards.
v1.correction: The provider-card divergence cannot be reached in production. The cards are the only thing that changes `provider` there. Only roadmap_smoke.rs:154-157 calls provider.set_selected directly, and it never checks the cards, so the stale card state shows up only in the test. The hidden DropDowns also act as test handles: smoke tests find them by widget name (launch-provider-N, launch-effort-N, launch-count-control, launch-mode, launch-builders), so a Choice helper must keep a way for tests to reach them. That makes the payoff modest: low, not medium. The redundant SpinButton is the clearest piece to remove (read count_select.selected()+1 instead).

findings.title: A failed provider.list is swallowed: both provider cards claim 'CLI not installed' and the launch is refused
findings.evidence: `let provider_data = providers.ok().map(|v| rows(&v, "providers")).unwrap_or_default();` (621-624) discards the error. Each card then does `let installed = info.is_some_and(|p| p["installed"] == true); key.set_sensitive(installed);` and its caption falls back to "CLI not installed" (632-646), while the footer still says "Ready to launch" (769). The click handler refuses any agent whose card is insensitive: "Choose an installed provider for every agent." (783). The default provider stays index 0 (Claude) even when only Codex is installed.
findings.impact: If provider.list times out (for example because the shared control socket is busy behind a clone or a gh listing), the sheet reports both CLIs as not installed and cannot launch, with no hint that the check itself failed. A Codex-only user must switch every agent's provider by hand before Launch works.
findings.fix: On error, show the error in the provider captions or status and keep the cards sensitive, letting session.create report provider.not_installed. Default each profile to the first installed provider.

v1.reason: launch.rs:621-624 throws away the provider.list error with `.ok()...unwrap_or_default()`. With empty data, every card computes installed=false, calls set_sensitive(false) and shows "CLI not installed" (632-646). The status line still reads "Ready to launch" (769), and the click is refused with "Choose an installed provider for every agent." (783). Each profile's provider defaults to index 0 (Claude) no matter what is installed (roadmap_smoke.rs:144 even asserts this). A Codex-only user therefore has to switch every agent's provider by hand before Launch works.
v1.correction: The trigger the finding suggests is unrealistic. provider.list is registered with register_unlocked and reads the provider_cache table (handlers/provider.rs:13-17), and the client timeout is 30 s (client.rs:65-72), so a busy store or a clone will not time it out. In practice provider.list fails only when task.list fails too, as on a disconnect, and that path already shows task_result's error. The more relevant half is that Codex-only users always start on Claude. Fix: when provider.list fails, show the error, and default each profile to the first installed provider.

findings.title: Review-group launch rejects an empty worktree on members whose worktree is ignored and whose field is disabled
findings.evidence: In group mode `p.worktree.set_sensitive(!group || i == 0);` (574), and the reviewer and second builder drop the field: `payload.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("worktree")` (803). Validation still runs for every index: `if text(&payload,"worktree").is_empty(){ ... ui.show_error("Set a worktree for every agent.");return;}` (784).
findings.impact: If the user clears agent 2's or agent 3's Worktree field in solo mode and then switches to Review group, Launch always fails with "Set a worktree for every agent." The offending field is greyed out, so the user has to switch back to solo, refill it and return.
findings.fix: Validate the worktree only where it is used (`!group || index == 0`).

v1.reason: launch.rs:574 makes the Worktree entry insensitive for profiles 1 and 2 in group mode (`p.worktree.set_sensitive(!group || i == 0)`). The start handler (781-786) still builds a payload for every group index ([0,2] or [0,2,1]) and rejects any empty `worktree` at 784. At 803 that field is removed for index>0 (`payload...remove("worktree")`), so its value is never used. The entry defaults to "new" (259-262), so the trigger needs the user to clear it in solo mode first. After that the group launch keeps failing with "Set a worktree for every agent.", and the field that needs fixing is greyed out.
v1.correction: Rare trigger, because the entry defaults to "new". Fix: guard the check at 784 with `(!group || index == 0)`.

findings.title: A launch sheet left open across an engine reconnect stops working: Launch silently does nothing
findings.evidence: The form captures `let generation = self.generation.get();` (607). The click handler starts with `if !launch_is_current(&ui,project,generation,&heading){return;}` (778), and the loader returns early the same way (618). `Ui::connect` bumps the generation (app.rs:1135) but never hides or rebuilds the sheet. The Reconnect key sits in the top bar, which the sheet does not disable; only `body` is made insensitive (app.rs:666-673).
findings.impact: The engine restarts while the user is configuring agents. They press Reconnect, then Launch, and nothing happens, with no message. If the reconnect happened while tasks were still loading, the sheet stays at "Loading open tasks..." with Launch disabled for good.
findings.fix: Close or rebuild the launch sheet in `Ui::connect`. When `launch_is_current` fails in the click handler, show an error such as "This form is out of date; reopen New session".

v1.reason: The form captures generation at launch.rs:607. Ui::connect bumps generation at app.rs:1135 and never hides or rebuilds the launch sheet. The Reconnect key lives in the top bar (app.rs:432-433), outside `body`, which is the only thing made insensitive while the sheet is open (app.rs:666-673). After a reconnect, launch_is_current fails on the generation check (launch.rs:832-836). The click handler then returns at 778 with no message. If the loader was still waiting, it returns at 618 before calling ready.set_sensitive(true), leaving "Loading open tasks…" and a disabled Launch button.
v1.correction: The silent return is a deliberate stale-form guard (roadmap_smoke.rs:166-185 tests that a stale submit creates no session), but the missing feedback is not deliberate. The user can recover by closing and reopening the sheet. Fix: hide the sheet in Ui::connect (when it is not busy), or show a 'form is out of date, reopen New session' error when launch_is_current fails in the click handler.

findings.title: An agent's starting task is the first ticked card in board-column order, not the task the launch was opened from
findings.evidence: `selected_tasks` returns ids in `tasks` insertion order (325-332). That is task.list's column order (`ORDER BY CASE col WHEN 'backlog' THEN 0 WHEN 'in_review' THEN 1 WHEN 'ready' THEN 2 WHEN 'active' THEN 3`, task.rs:855). `tasks.first()` becomes the session's `task_id` (804), and dispatch order sets the queue order (810). The task the sheet was opened from is only preselected (666).
findings.impact: Example: the user opens New session from Ready task #12 (preselected) and also ticks backlog task #3. The agent is created on #3 as its current task and only reaches #12 second.
findings.fix: Keep the preselected task first, then the tasks in the order the user ticked them (record a click sequence), or let the user reorder the queue.

v1.reason: The mechanism is as described. `selected_tasks` (325-332) returns ids in `tasks` push order. That order follows task.list's default sort, `CASE col WHEN 'backlog' THEN 0 WHEN 'in_review' THEN 1 WHEN 'ready' THEN 2 WHEN 'active' THEN 3` (task.rs:855). `tasks.first()` becomes the create's task_id (804), and dispatch order sets queue_ord through assign_session (task.rs:589-600). The task the sheet was opened from is only preselected (666). Nothing documents that the opening task should go first, though. The queue order matches the card order the user sees on the sheet, so this is a UX expectation, not a broken contract. A backlog task outranking a Ready task in the queue is surprising, but the behaviour is deterministic and visible.
v1.correction: This is a UX ordering issue, not a correctness defect. A cheap fix: put the preselected task first in `selected_tasks` for profile 0, or order by tick sequence.

findings.title: Searching or reopening the GitHub tab overwrites the user's custom clone folder name
findings.evidence: `filter_repos` calls `self.choices.remove_all()` and then `self.choices.set_active_id(Some(&id))` (385, 411). It runs on every search keystroke (271-275) and on every `load_github` (424, 430), which runs on each switch to the GitHub tab (264-266). Each change of the active item fires the choices handler, which unconditionally does `setup.destination.set_text(repo.as_ref().map(|r| text(r, "name")).unwrap_or(""))` (289-291).
findings.impact: The user picks a repo and types a different name under "Clone folder name" (for example to avoid an existing folder). Refining the search, or flipping to Local and back, silently resets the folder to the repo name. The clone then fails with project.clone_destination, or lands in the folder the user meant to avoid.
findings.fix: Reset `destination` only when the selected repository actually changes (remember the last full_name), or track whether the user has edited it.

v1.reason: filter_repos (383-415) calls `choices.remove_all()` and then `set_active_id(previous)`, or `set_active(Some(0))`. Each of these changes the active item and fires the connect_changed handler (277-293), which unconditionally runs `destination.set_text(<repo name or "">)`. filter_repos runs on every search change (270-275) and from load_github (424, 430), and load_github runs on every switch to the GitHub tab (264-266). So a custom 'Clone folder name' is reset to the repo name even when the same repo stays selected.
v1.correction: The consequence is visible, since the field is on screen next to the selector, which keeps it low. Fix: in the changed handler, overwrite destination only when the active full_name differs from the last one applied.

findings.title: An older workspace scan's error overwrites the result of a newer scan
findings.evidence: `discover` bumps `discovery_generation`, and the Ok branch checks `if current != path || setup.discovery_generation.get() != generation { return; }` (340-347). The Err branch has no such check: `Err(e) => setup.message.set_text(&e.to_string()),` (360).
findings.impact: The user scans a slow or unreadable directory, then a good one. The second scan lists its repositories, then the first scan's failure arrives, and the dialog shows an error for a directory that is no longer selected.
findings.fix: Apply the same generation and path check before reporting the error.

v1.reason: The cited code is accurate. In onboarding.rs, discover (322-363) bumps discovery_generation, and the Ok branch checks path and generation before filling the list (340-347). The Err branch at 360 does `Err(e) => setup.message.set_text(&e.to_string())` with no such check. The ordering in the finding is wrong, though. Ui::call (app.rs:1111-1117) sends workspace.discover on the shared control client. The engine handles each connection one request at a time (socket.rs:335-744: spawn_blocking(...).await, then out_tx.send). So an older scan's reply, or its 30 s client-side Timeout, always arrives before a newer scan's reply. The real symptom is a stale error that stays on screen. Neither starting a new scan nor a successful Ok ever clears `message`, so an error from the first directory stays next to the second directory's repository list. The trigger is real: the handler returns Err for a path that is not a directory (workspace.rs:126-128) or for any I/O error in the walk (workspace.rs:410).
v1.correction: Mechanism: replies on one connection arrive in request order, so the newer scan's list never arrives before the older error. The stale message stays because discover never clears `self.message` when a new scan starts or when the Ok branch succeeds. A generation check on Err alone only covers the case where the error is still in flight when the user rescans. Fix: clear the message at the start of discover and in the Ok branch, and also apply the same path/generation check to Err. A related engine issue makes this error more common: discover_repositories's walk uses `fs::read_dir(path)?` and `entry?` (workspace.rs:398-401). One unreadable subdirectory within depth 4, such as a root-owned directory under $HOME, therefore fails the whole scan with workspace.discover_failed instead of skipping that directory.

findings.title: Panes that never attach show a permanent 'Connecting' status strip
findings.evidence: `let status = gtk::Label::new(Some("Connecting"));` (107). The visibility hook is connected afterwards (184). The text is cleared only by a successful attach (490) or by `set_active(false)`, which returns early when the pane was never active: `if self.active.replace(active) == active { return; }` (443). `update_attachments` never activates created, parked, restorable or exited sessions (app.rs:1577-1580), and launch placeholders are in the created state.
findings.impact: Every parked, restorable, exited or still-launching pane shows a "Connecting" strip (styled with background and padding, theme.css:89) under its slate indefinitely. No connection is being attempted, but it reads as a stuck connection.
findings.fix: Create the label empty, and set "Connecting" in `set_active(true)`.

v1.reason: `gtk::Label::new(Some("Connecting"))` at terminal.rs:107. GTK4 widgets are visible by default, and the notify hook at line 184 runs only on later text changes. The text is cleared only in attach_and_render after a successful attach (490) or in set_active(false) (451). set_active returns early at 443 when the pane was never active. update_attachments (app.rs:1567-1583) keeps panes inactive for created/parked/restorable/exited states and while the window is hidden, the page is not agents, or focus mode shows another pane. So those panes keep a styled `.terminal-status` strip (theme.css:89, background and padding) that reads "Connecting" with no connection under way.
v1.correction: Also affects panes created while the window is hidden or another page is shown, until they are first activated. Fix: create the label empty, or set the text to "Connecting" at the start of the active branch of set_active.

findings.title: Pane::new sets a font and colours that apply_appearance always overwrites, with different values
findings.evidence: `Pane::new` sets `FontDescription::from_string("Fira Mono")` at 13 px, `set_color_foreground` #ececea and an opaque `set_color_background` #0a0a0b (82-87). Its only caller immediately runs `pane.apply_appearance(&self.palette.borrow(), self.font_size.get())` (app.rs:1488-1490). That sets the font again from the setting, foreground #dcdcda and a transparent background (terminal.rs:299-314).
findings.impact: There are two sources of truth for the terminal's look, and they already disagree (foreground colour; opaque versus clear background). A change made in Pane::new has no effect, which invites wrong fixes.
findings.fix: Delete lines 82-87, keeping cell height and blink mode, or have Pane::new take the palette and size and call apply_appearance itself.

v1.reason: terminal.rs:82-87 sets a Fira Mono 13px absolute font, foreground #ececea and an opaque background #0a0a0b. The only constructor call site, app.rs:1488, calls install_pane_controls and then `pane.apply_appearance(&self.palette.borrow(), self.font_size.get())` (app.rs:1490). apply_appearance (terminal.rs:284-315) resets everything those lines set: set_colors with foreground #dcdcda, a clear background and a 16-colour palette, set_color_background(&clear), and set_font from the setting. Nothing reads the terminal between those calls, so the values written in Pane::new never take effect, and they already differ from the real ones.
v1.correction: The redundant lines are 82-84 (font) and 86-87 (fg/bg). Keep set_cell_height_scale (85) and set_cursor_blink_mode (88), which apply_appearance does not set. shell.rs:1242 also calls apply_appearance when settings change, so apply_appearance is the single real source.

findings.title: Dead launch code: an effort filter that never matches, stack page titles that nothing displays, progress text written to a hidden sheet
findings.evidence: `.filter(|s| s != "Default")` (345) never matches: the effort model is minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (225), so an effort is always sent. `stack.add_titled(..., &format!("{}", i + 1))` (463) and `stack.page(&p.root).set_title(...)` on every update (568-572) set titles on a Stack that has no StackSwitcher; the selector is built by hand from `member_keys`. After the sheet hides (791), `progress.set_text(...)` (801, 810, 815) updates a label nobody can see.
findings.impact: Misleading code: the filter implies a provider-default effort option that no longer exists, and the title formatting runs on every mode or count change for nothing.
findings.fix: Drop the filter, or restore a real Default entry that sends no effort. Use `add_named`, and delete the set_title block and the hidden progress writes; the panes already show each step.

v1.reason: The effort DropDown model is [minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max] (launch.rs:224). Nothing ever sets it to "Default", so `.filter(|s| s != "Default")` (345) never matches. No StackSwitcher or StackSidebar is attached to this Stack: rg finds StackSwitcher only in tools_devices.rs, onboarding.rs and task_pages.rs, and the selector is built by hand from member_keys. That makes add_titled's title (463) and the set_title on every update (568-572) unused. The click handler hides the sheet with set_reveal_child(false) (791) before the async loop writes progress.set_text (801, 810, 815). launch_busy then blocks show_launch from reopening it until the loop finishes, and the next open clears launch_box, so those writes are never seen.
v1.correction: Line numbers are a little off: the effort model is at 224-225 and the filter at 345. This is pure cleanup. The set_title per update costs almost nothing.

results.coverage:
I read every line of the four assigned files: apps/relay-native/src/tools.rs, tools_settings.rs, tools_skills.rs and tools_plugins.rs. To trace callers and callees I also read: tools_market.rs (all), client.rs (all), panel.rs (all), wallpaper_rotation.rs, shortcuts.rs, provider_updates.rs, sounds.rs, notification_center.rs, app.rs (Ui struct, show_error, call, mutate, connect event loop, navigate, refresh, refresh_page), shell.rs (load_appearance, open_project, apply_ui_event, plugins sidebar panel), agent_menu.rs apply_session_event, guardrail_settings.rs build/editor/open, and parts of roadmap_smoke.rs. On the engine side I read handlers/settings.rs, notify.rs (settings and dashboard parts), handlers/provider.rs (provider, skill and plugin handlers), github.rs (URL parsing and skill collection), plugins.rs (frontmatter and detect), audit.rs (append, limits), recovery.rs (retention), the remote door's wire.rs actor check, and the relay-bus op metadata. I also grepped the pedantic clippy output for my files; the cast warnings are all on small UI indexes and are harmless.

Nothing was compiled or run: relay-native cannot be built here. I checked the GTK4 class hierarchy (CheckButton is not a ToggleButton; SpinButton is not an Entry) and FileDialog's DialogError against the gtk4-0.11.4 crate source. The 'Dismissed by user' text and the lost-click-on-rebuild behaviour come from my knowledge of GTK4, not from running it. Wallpaper sizes were measured by re-encoding /usr/share/wallpapers images with PIL at 1280 px, q80 (25-166 KB as data URLs, ~1.7 ms each to decode). Photographs will be larger. The skills disconnect requires more than about 2 MiB of skill bodies in total; I verified the mechanism, not how often real libraries reach that size.

Engine-side problems I noticed but did not file because they belong to other chunks: provider.refresh is registered with Engine::register and runs provider probe subprocesses with the store mutex held (handlers/provider.rs:18-19, providers.rs:363-367). skill.install's staged read phase runs `git clone` and `git rev-parse` with Command::output(), not proc::output_with_timeout (github.rs:106-110, 155-157); a credential prompt can hang it, and the client gives skill.install the default 30 s timeout (client.rs:65-71), so a slow clone reports 'outcome unknown'. app.backup.now copies the store inside the request transaction (handlers/app.rs:47-51). audit undo_op is stored uncapped for every op, not only wallpapers (audit.rs:123). The phone door forwards any op as the user, including settings.set (relay-remote wire.rs:100).

findings.title: Wallpaper images live in audited settings, so every rotation tick (and every library Save) copies the previous image into the audit table and keeps it for 180 days
findings.evidence: Uploaded wallpapers become data URLs stored in the settings tree: tools_settings.rs:1009-1011 `let image=format!("data:image/jpeg;base64,{}",...); library.push(json!({..."image":image,"preview":image}))`, and Save persists them with `settings.push(("settings.set", json!({"path":format!("appearance.{field}"),"value":wallpaper_snapshot[field]})))` (132-139). The 'Rotate wallpapers randomly' checkbox (338-353) drives wallpaper_rotation.rs:176, which calls `settings.set {"path":"appearance.wallpaper","value":candidates[index]}` every 1-1440 minutes (default 15). In the engine, settings.set is Audit::Always + Undo::Inverse (relay-bus ops/notify.rs:23). The handler records the old value: handlers/settings.rs:218-220 `let before = get(...)?; ... ctx.set_undo("settings.set", json!({ "path": p.path, "value": before }), None)`. audit.rs:88-97 caps payload and result at 64 KB, but audit.rs:123 writes `e.undo_op.map(|u| serde_json::to_string(u)...)` with no cap. recovery.rs:18/193-202 prunes only rows older than 180 days.
findings.impact: With rotation on, each tick adds one audit row holding the previous full image. I re-encoded the system wallpapers the way the app does (1280-px JPEG at q80): the data URLs came out at 25-166 KB, and photographs are larger. At the default 15 minutes that is ~2.4-16 MB a day; at the 1-minute minimum it is ~36-240 MB a day. Rows are kept 180 days, so the single SQLite store grows to gigabytes. The engine copies that store under its mutex for backups and runs VACUUM after pruning. Each Save that changes the library also stores the previous library (up to 1.5 MB, with previews duplicated). Unfiltered audit.list pages also carry these images.
findings.fix: Keep image bytes out of the settings tree. Write uploaded and bundled wallpapers to files under the store or cache directory, and keep only ids/paths in appearance.wallpapers and appearance.wallpaper. If that is too large a change, rotate through a dedicated op with Audit::Never, and cap or hash undo_op the way payload already is.

v1.reason: Even the bundled presets are data URLs: wallpaper_rotation.rs:9-40 base64-encodes the three ~9 KB PNGs. rotate_once (wallpaper_rotation.rs:174-177) sends settings.set {path:"appearance.wallpaper", value:<data URL>} on every tick. In relay-bus ops/notify.rs:23-24, settings.set is OpMeta::mutation, which means Audit::Always (registry.rs:117), plus Undo::Inverse. The handler (handlers/settings.rs:217-219) reads `before` and calls ctx.set_undo("settings.set", {path, value: before}). audit::append (audit.rs:88-99) caps the payload and the result at STORE_LIMIT = 64 KB, but writes undo_op at audit.rs:123 with no cap. The only cleanup is time-based retention: recovery.rs:179-200 deletes rows older than the retention window (180 days by default) and keeps any row an undo points at. So every tick stores one audit row. The previous image is always stored in full in undo_op, and the new image is stored up to twice more (payload and result) whenever it fits under 64 KB. Even with only the bundled presets (~12 KB each as base64), one row is ~36 KB, which is ~3.5 MB a day at the 15-minute default and ~600 MB over the 180-day window. Uploaded JPEGs are larger, and the 1-minute minimum makes it 15x worse. Rotation is opt-in: nothing in the engine sets a default for appearance.wallpaper_rotation. It is still an ordinary checkbox on the Settings page, so this is unbounded growth in normal use.
v1.correction: Each row's cost is not just the undo_op. Payload and result_summary also hold the new image whenever it is 64 KB or less (always true for the bundled presets), so capping undo_op alone does not fix it. The real fix is the one proposed: keep image bytes out of the settings tree and store ids or paths. As a stopgap, rotation could go through an op with Audit::Never, and undo_op could get the same size cap as the payload.

v2.reason:
(a) I traced the code myself and it does what the finding says. rotate_once (wallpaper_rotation.rs:175-177) sends `settings.set {path:"appearance.wallpaper", value:<data URL>}`. The native client sends it as Actor::User with a fresh UUID each time (client.rs:299,312), so no request is ever deduplicated. settings.set is OpMeta::mutation (notify.rs:23-24), which defaults to Audit::Always (registry.rs:117), and should_audit (engine.rs:1397) audits it for every actor. The handler stores the previous value as the inverse (handlers/settings.rs:218-220). The pipeline passes `undo.as_ref()` straight to audit::append (engine.rs:1012). That function caps only payload and result at STORE_LIMIT (audit.rs:88-97) and writes undo_op uncapped (audit.rs:123). The only cleanup is time-based pruning at engine launch (recovery.rs:183-206; default 180 days per settings.rs:43). Nothing in D76, D95, D150 or D151 treats these rows as intended. D151 limits only the session.report and usage.report payloads.

(b) Who and how often: the user turns this on once with the "Rotate wallpapers randomly" checkbox and a Save (tools_settings.rs:338-353, persisted by collect_settings at 621-622). Any first Save on that page also persists the three bundled presets (tools_settings.rs:76-79, 132-139), so even a user who never uploads an image has at least 2 images to rotate. After that, a row is written every interval (default 15 min, minimum 1 min) for as long as the desktop window is open. The glib timer keeps running when the window is hidden. Closing the window quits the app, so the rate depends on how long the app is open. Every user who enables rotation hits this every time.

(c) Consequence: I ran the 40 wallpapers on this machine through the app's exact pipeline (gdk-pixbuf scaled to fit 1280x900, JPEG q80, base64). The data URLs came out at 36-406 KB, median 131 KB, and 30 of 40 were over 64 KB. Over 64 KB, a row costs about one copy of the previous image (in undo_op). At 64 KB or less, it costs three copies: the bundled presets are 11.7-12.5 KB, so each row is about 36 KB. At the default 15 minutes:
- Presets only: about 1.4-3.5 MB/day, settling at about 0.25-0.6 GB.
- Typical uploaded images: about 5-13 MB/day, settling at about 0.9-2.3 GB.
- The range covers 10-24 hours open per day. The 1-minute minimum multiplies everything by 15. With audit.retention_days=0 (a documented option) the growth has no limit.

The code itself assumes "a store measured in tens of MB" (store.rs:535). Knock-on effects:
- Once 180 days of rows exist, almost every launch prunes some, so recovery.rs:217-219 VACUUMs the whole bloated store before the doors open. That rewrites gigabytes at startup and needs that much free space.
- app.backup.now copies the store while holding the store mutex (handlers/app.rs:47-48), so the bus freezes for the length of the copy.
- Pre-upgrade backups run on every schema bump (store.rs:435-449), and 5 backups are kept (store.rs:546), which multiplies the disk cost.
- An unfiltered audit.list (default limit 200, handlers/audit.rs:39) returns tens of MB built under the mutex.
- Each tick also emits settings.changed carrying the full image to every subscriber (settings.rs:222).

There is no data loss and no functional failure.

(d) I keep high under "unbounded growth in normal use". The checkbox is a normal Settings feature, and with no further action from the user the store keeps growing for six months to gigabyte scale, five times that again in backups. The growth is pure waste, since nothing ever surfaces an undo of a rotation. Caveats: the feature is opt-in, and at the default retention the size levels off at 180 days' worth of rows rather than growing forever.

(e) The main fix, keeping image bytes out of the settings tree (files plus ids or paths), is correct and complete. The fallback "cap or hash undo_op" is not enough on its own and has side effects (see correction).
v2.correction:
Anchor: the main driver is the rotation tick, so anchor at apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:175 (trigger) and crates/relay-core/src/audit.rs:123 (the uncapped write). tools_settings.rs:136 is the rarer Save path.

Cost per row:
- Over 64 KB, only undo_op holds a full image (the previous one). Payload and result become {truncated,bytes} markers.
- At 64 KB or less, the row holds three copies. This covers the bundled presets (about 36 KB per row), and images just under 64 KB cost up to about 190 KB per row.
- The finding's per-day figures assume the app is open 24/7. Ticks only happen while the window is open.
- At the default retention the size levels off at the 180-day window. It is only truly unbounded with audit.retention_days=0.
- Prune and VACUUM run only at engine launch (recovery.rs:183-221), not periodically.
- Measured on the system wallpapers: median 131 KB, range 36-406 KB.

Fix:
- Files plus ids/paths: also needs a one-time conversion of the data URLs already stored in appearance.wallpapers and appearance.wallpaper, and the client must load images from files. The rows already written age out over 180 days, unless a one-off scrub and VACUUM removes them sooner.
- The smallest targeted fix for the main source: rotate by writing a small selected-id key that the client resolves against the library, or through an Audit::Never op. This also stops settings.changed (handlers/settings.rs:222) broadcasting the full image on every tick.
- A generic undo_op cap does not help images of 64 KB or less, because payload and result still hold the new image. It also changes behaviour elsewhere: task.update's inverse carries the old body (handlers/task.rs:890), so large-body edits would stop being undoable. If a cap is used, scope it, and store NULL above the limit so audit.undo reports the row as not undoable.
- Any change under apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in an agent session and must be reported as uncompiled (CLAUDE.md).

findings.title: Skills page fetches every skill's full body; past 2 MiB the reply exceeds the client's line cap and the whole engine connection is torn down
findings.evidence: `list_op: "skill.list"` is called with `json!({})` by market::refresh (tools_market.rs:96) on every refresh_page while Skills is visible. The engine (handlers/provider.rs:86-107) returns `SELECT * FROM skills` rows, and the bus `Skill` type includes `body: String`. Each body may be up to 256 KiB (provider.rs:583-591), with no limit on the number of skills. client.rs:48 sets `MAX_LINE: usize = 2 * 1024 * 1024`. At client.rs:200-204 the reader returns `Err(Error::Protocol("frame exceeds 2 MiB"))` from its loop; that fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected (259-265). app.rs:1267-1275 then drops the client. The page needs bodies only for `description()` (tools_skills.rs:54) and the detail view (240). skill.install's reply (provider.rs:244 `SkillInstallOut { skills }`) also echoes every body it installed.
findings.impact: Once installed skills total more than about 2 MiB, opening Skills disconnects the native app from the engine.
