That takes roughly 80 skills of 25 KB, or 9 at the 256 KiB cap, and the installer imports every SKILL.md in a pasted repository, so one large collection repo is enough. Installing such a repo disconnects in the middle of the install, although the install has already committed. After Reconnect, the next engine event while Skills is open does it again. Below the cap, the page still re-downloads and re-parses the whole library on every task, mailbox or notify event, and the engine builds that reply under the store mutex. 'Open on GitHub' goes through ui.mutate, so it also triggers a full re-fetch.
findings.fix: Make skill.list return a summary without bodies (id, name, description, source, enabled_in, dates), or add a summary flag. Load the body with skill.get when the detail opens, as plugins already do with plugin.get. Have skill.install return ids and names only. In client.rs, fail only the oversized response by discarding that line, instead of dropping the connection.

v1.reason: market::refresh (tools_market.rs:96) calls `ui.call(spec.list_op, json!({}))`, so skill.list runs with no filter. The SkillList handler (provider.rs:86-107) returns every live row through skill_row (provider.rs:541-559), which includes `body`. The bus Skill type (relay-bus types.rs:647-657) carries `body: String`. Bodies may each be up to 256 KiB (valid_skill_body at provider.rs:583, and again in github.rs collect_skills), and nothing limits how many skills there are. The main UI connection is opened by Client::connect -> open -> open_with_limit(MAX_LINE = 2 MiB) (client.rs:48, 141-166). Only image_read (24 MiB) and the mirror get a larger limit. When a frame is over the limit, the reader returns Error::Protocol at client.rs:200-205. The code after the loop then fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected. app.rs:1267-1275 drops the client, shows 'Engine disconnected', and breaks out of the notice loop. refresh_page (app.rs:1662-1686) refreshes the 'skills' page on generic events, so after a reconnect the oversized reply comes back again. skill.install is a staged op whose SkillInstallOut (provider.rs:244, ops/provider.rs:44) echoes every installed Skill with its body. collect_skills imports every SKILL.md under the cloned root (up to depth 8), so pasting one large collection repository is enough to hit the limit, and the install reply alone can break the connection after the commit. JSON escaping of the markdown (newlines, quotes) means less than 2 MiB of raw text is enough. The trigger needs a large library, but once it is reached the Skills page cannot be used and every visit drops the UI's engine connection, so high is right.
v1.correction: The line numbers check out. The 'roughly 80 x 25 KB' estimate is high because JSON escaping inflates bodies, so fewer are needed. The fix is right: a bodyless summary list (it could carry a server-computed description, which also deals with native-tools#14), a body fetched only for the detail view, and a skill.install reply that does not echo bodies. Discarding only the oversized response line in client.rs would also stop the failure from taking down the whole connection.

v2.reason:
(a) I traced every step myself. tools_skills.rs:25 leads to tools_market.rs:96, which calls `ui.call(spec.list_op, json!({}))`. Ui::call (app.rs:1111-1117) sends only lifecycle ops on a separate connection, so skill.list goes over the main control client. That client is built by Client::connect -> open -> open_with_limit(MAX_LINE = 2 MiB) (client.rs:48, 143-167). The engine's SkillList handler (provider.rs:86-107, registered with plain `e.register`) returns every live row through skill_row (541-559), and that includes `body`. The bus Skill type (types.rs:647-657) has no serde skip. The engine's socket writer (socket.rs:~300-320) puts no limit on line size. On the client, client.rs:200-205 returns Err(Protocol("frame exceeds 2 MiB")), which ends the reader task. Lines 259-265 then fail every pending request and send Notice::Disconnected, and app.rs:1267-1276 drops the client and leaves the notice loop. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:22 says "wire lines are bounded to 2 MiB", so this unbounded reply breaks a documented contract. The finding missed one trigger. The header Skills button (app.rs:847-849 -> shell.rs:780 project_skills) calls skill.list with `{"project_id":..}` and no `enabled`, and provider.rs:101 applies no filter in that case. That sheet therefore also downloads every body and disconnects in the same way, even though it shows only name, source and the switch.
(b) The trigger needs the live library to serialize to more than 2,097,152 bytes. Each body is capped at 256 KiB (provider.rs:583, github.rs:173), and collect_skills imports every SKILL.md down to depth 8 with no limit on count. I measured the SKILL.md files on this machine: 749 real files average about 10 KB, and single vendor skill packs weigh 270-580 KiB each. So about 200 average skills, or 4-5 such packs, reach the cap. A simulation of collect, dedupe and serialize shows about 6% of JSON and metadata overhead, so the "80 x 25 KB" estimate is about right. The "one large repo paste" path is weaker than the finding says: both real multi-plugin repos I simulated would be refused at the root by skill.duplicate_name (provider.rs:375) before anything is written. That path works only for flat collections with unique names. Installing several packs over time is the dependable path. The author's own libraries currently hold 1-2 skills. Once the cap is crossed, the failure is certain. It fires on every open of Skills or of the Agent skills sheet, and on any event that reaches the else branch at app.rs:1263-1264 while Skills is shown (task, mailbox, notify, guardrail, usage and skill events). That includes the first such event after Reconnect.
(c) No data is lost. The engine and its sessions keep running, and terminals use their own connections. But the UI's control connection drops: every in-flight request fails with "Invalid engine response: frame exceeds 2 MiB", the status shows Engine disconnected, and Reconnect rebuilds every pane. The Skills page and the sheet never load again, so skills cannot be removed from the UI. Only CLI or MCP skill.delete still works, because that client has no line cap. skill.install echoes every body it installed (provider.rs:244), so a large install reports an error even though it has already committed. A smaller install that pushes the library over the cap disconnects as soon as its skill.changed events refresh the page.
(d) High is right, at the edge of the rubric. A normal flow fails hard every time, it takes down the whole UI control plane, and there is no recovery inside the app. The size precondition is what keeps it from critical. The side claim about lock time is minor: a few MiB of SELECT plus N cached lookups takes milliseconds and does not break a CLAUDE.md invariant.
(e) The fix points the right way but is incomplete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
Add apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:832 to `related`. It is the Agent skills sheet, which calls skill.list with only project_id and gets every body back. The "one large collection repo is enough" claim needs a qualifier: real multi-plugin repos usually fail at the root with skill.duplicate_name and install nothing, so several installs adding up is the reliable trigger. The first verifier said JSON escaping noticeably lowers the count needed; it does not, the measured overhead is about 6%.

What the fix needs to cover:
1. No skill.get op exists. It has to be added as a bus op with a handler.
2. A summary list must carry a server-computed description. description() parses the body and is used for search, the card and the detail (tools_skills.rs:34, 106, 144).
3. Besides the detail view at line 240, the Edit dialog (tools_skills.rs:187-190, 410-417) fills its editor from the list row's `body`. A bodyless list would open an empty editor, and saving it would overwrite the real instructions. That is a data-loss trap for a careless fix, so Edit must fetch the body first.
4. Keep the full form available behind an opt-in `summary` flag or a separate op, because agents reach skill.list through MCP.
5. skill.install should return ids and names only. The installer reads only the count (tools_skills.rs:372).
6. To drop only the oversized line on the client, the reader must skip to the newline and read the request id from the line prefix (`{"v":1,"id":"..."`). Otherwise the request waits out its 30 s timeout. A cap in the engine that turns an oversize reply into a typed error would protect every client.

findings.title: Save changes rewrites every setting on the page, not only the edited ones, silently reverting or clamping other values and flooding the audit log and events
findings.evidence: collect_settings (606-692) walks the whole page and, for every widget named `setting:*`, does `settings.push(("settings.set", json!({"path":...,"value":value})))` (652-655) whether or not it changed. That is 23 requests: mode, three sliders, two rotation fields, font size, two auto-update flags, two provider paths, parking, four Android paths and seven shortcuts, plus notify.settings.set (141). Only the wallpaper fields are compared against a saved value (132-139). The values come from a snapshot taken when the page was first built for this project (34, 84-86). Scale::set_value clamps to the widget range, which commit 54e6bbc narrowed from 0.5-1 to 0.72-1 for panel_alpha and from 0-0.85 to 0-0.75 for wallpaper_dim (292-293). load_appearance still accepts 0.5-1 and 0-0.85 (shell.rs:1179, 1217).
findings.impact: (a) A panel opacity of 0.6 set with an older build stays in effect until the user saves anything else, such as a shortcut; that Save silently writes 0.72, and the same happens to wallpaper dim above 0.75. (b) Any setting changed from the CLI or phone after the page was built is reverted by the next Save. (c) Every click writes about 24 audited rows with undo entries, even with nothing changed. Each settings.set also emits settings.changed, which runs load_appearance about seven times and load_keybindings seven times. Each load_appearance makes 8 settings.get calls, including the full wallpaper library via wallpaper_rotation::refresh, reloads the window CSS and decodes the wallpaper on the UI thread.
findings.fix: Record each control's loaded value when it is built, and on Save send only the fields whose current value differs, as the wallpaper fields already do. Do the same diff for the notification patch.

v1.reason: collect_settings (tools_settings.rs:606-692) pushes a settings.set for every `setting:*` widget it finds: the active mode toggle, every Scale, CheckButton, SpinButton and Entry (lines 652-656). None of them is compared with the value it was built from. Only the wallpaper fields are diffed (132-139), and notify.settings.set is always sent (141). The values come from the snapshot taken in refresh() (lines 39-57). The page is not rebuilt on settings.changed (app.rs:1249-1262 only reloads keybindings, usage and appearance), and not after Save either: ui.refresh() goes back through refresh(), which returns early at line 34. So a value changed from the CLI, the phone or an agent after the page was built is overwritten with the stale widget value on the next Save. The engine's settings.set handler (relay-core handlers/settings.rs:216-223) never short-circuits when the value is unchanged. It always deletes and reinserts, records an undo entry, and emits settings.changed. Each appearance.* or terminal.font_size event calls load_appearance (6 settings.get calls plus wallpaper_rotation::refresh, which fetches the whole library). Each keybindings.* event calls load_keybindings. The clamping claim also holds. The sliders are built with ranges 0.72-1 and 0-0.75 (line 292-293; commit 54e6bbc changed them from 0.5 and 0.85). Scale::set_value clamps to that range, while load_appearance accepts alpha down to 0.5 (shell.rs:1179) and dim up to 0.85 (shell.rs:1217). So a stored 0.6 opacity is silently rewritten to 0.72 by any unrelated Save.
v1.correction: Main mechanism to stress: the page snapshot never refreshes while the project stays the same, so the window during which another writer's change can be reverted lasts the whole app session, not just a short race. The exact request count depends on how many controls exist and is not decisive. Fix: record each control's initial value at build time and send only the fields that differ, as the wallpaper fields already do. Do the same for the notification patch. Optionally, also make the settings.set handler skip writing, auditing and emitting when `before == value`.

findings.title: 'Refresh providers' and provider updates never appear: the Settings page is built once per project and never re-read
findings.evidence: `if ui.page_projects.borrow().get("settings") == Some(&project) { return; }`. The button is `action(ui, &agents, "Refresh providers", "provider.refresh", json!({}))` (396-402). That goes through Ui::mutate (app.rs:1118-1130), which throws away the returned ListOut and calls refresh_page, which returns at line 34. The provider.version event that provider.refresh emits is not in the subscription list (app.rs:1154). 'Update now' ends in provider_updates::event, which only calls ui.refresh(). The smoke tests force a rebuild with `ui.page_projects.borrow_mut().remove("settings")` (roadmap_smoke.rs:381, 510).
findings.impact: A user installs codex and clicks Refresh providers. The button greys out and comes back, but the card still says 'Not installed' or shows the old version until they switch projects or restart the app. The same staleness means the form never shows values changed elsewhere, which is what lets Save revert them (see the Save finding).
findings.fix: When provider.refresh succeeds, rebuild only the provider section from the providers it returns (call it directly instead of through mutate). Subscribe to provider.version and settings.changed, and update fields in place unless the user has edited them, instead of gating the whole page on the project.

v1.reason: tools_settings.rs:34 returns early when page_projects["settings"] == project. Only the settings page itself (line 84) and the smoke tests (roadmap_smoke.rs:381, 510) write page_projects["settings"]. Nothing clears it on reconnect: app.rs connect() at 1131 bumps the generation but leaves page_projects alone. The 'Refresh providers' button is tools::action (tools.rs:34-48), which calls Ui::mutate (app.rs:1118-1130). mutate discards the provider.refresh result (a ListOut), then calls ui.refresh() and refresh_page(), and both reach settings::refresh, which returns at line 34. The provider cards (tools_settings.rs:372-394) come from data["detected"], which is fetched only during that one-time build. provider_updates::event (provider_updates.rs:47-56) also only calls ui.refresh(). The button therefore has no visible effect while the user stays on the same project, and this holds even across an engine restart.
v1.correction: The engine restart case is a better reason than provider.version not being subscribed: even a reconnect does not rebuild the page. A minimal fix is for the Refresh button to call provider.refresh directly and redraw the provider section from the returned ListOut. More generally, invalidate page_projects["settings"] on reconnect and on settings.changed when there are no local edits.

findings.title: Unsaved Settings edits, including the embedded guardrail editor, are silently thrown away when the project changes, although nothing on the page is per-project
findings.evidence: The page is rebuilt whenever page_projects["settings"] differs from the current project (34): `clear(page)` (81), then a rebuild from engine values. The content is global settings plus `crate::pages::guardrail_settings(ui)` (458), which is the guardrail editor built with `build(ui, Scope::Global).0` and no guard (guardrail_settings.rs:427-429). The panel version of that editor does install `set_guard(... editor.dirty() == 0)` (guardrail_settings.rs:661). Navigation only checks panels: app.rs:1316 calls dismiss_panels, which looks at ui.panels only.
findings.impact: The user edits shortcuts, Android paths, sliders or guardrail limits without saving, clicks another project in the sidebar (which goes to its agents page), then returns to Settings: every edit is gone with no prompt. The same happens immediately when the phone sends ui.page.switch with another project (shell.rs:443), or when the active project is removed while Settings is open (shell/registry.rs:685). Leaving Settings without switching project keeps the edits, so the behaviour is inconsistent.
findings.fix: Key the page on the connection generation rather than the project; the guardrail editor already reads ui.project when its scope toggles change. Otherwise, check a dirty flag, including the guardrail editor's dirty(), before clearing the page, and block or confirm the switch.

v1.reason: settings::refresh rebuilds the page with clear(page) (tools_settings.rs:81) whenever page_projects["settings"] differs from the current project (line 34). Nothing on the page depends on the project. It holds global settings and pages::guardrail_settings, i.e. guardrail_settings::editor(), which is build(ui, Scope::Global).0 (guardrail_settings.rs:426-429). There is no dirty check on the settings page: the guard at guardrail_settings.rs:661 is installed only on the panel variant, and app.rs:1316 dismiss_panels covers only panels. Switching project, and then landing back on Settings (the phone's ui.page.switch through shell.rs:438-443 open_project, or the sidebar followed by returning to Settings), therefore silently drops unsaved edits. Leaving Settings and coming back without a project switch keeps them.
v1.correction: Category: this is lost unsaved form input, not lost persisted data, so it is a bug rather than data-loss. The edits lost to a guardrail-editor rebuild are only the ones not yet saved there, because that editor saves on its own. Keying the page on the connection generation, not the project, also fixes native-tools#4's reconnect staleness.

findings.title: Each wallpaper's 'preview' is a second copy of the full image: it halves the 1.5 MB library and every gallery redraw decodes every full-size image on the UI thread, even while Settings is hidden
findings.evidence: `library.push(json!({"id":...,"name":name,"image":image,"preview":image}))`, then the cap `if serde_json::to_vec(&library)...len()>1500000` (1012). render_wallpapers base64-decodes `item["preview"].as_str().or(item["image"].as_str())` and calls `gtk::gdk::Texture::from_bytes` for every card (838-853), plus `wallpaper_texture(current_image)` (903). sync_wallpaper (15-31) redraws the gallery whenever the current wallpaper changes and the user has no pending pick, i.e. on every rotation tick. That happens even while another page is visible, because the gallery is kept after leaving Settings.
findings.impact: Each image counts twice against the 1.5 MB cap. Measured data URLs for 1280-px re-encodes were 25-166 KB, and photographs are larger, so 'Wallpaper library is full' arrives after half as many images; with photographs that can be as few as 2-5, which also limits rotation. Every pick, remove, clear or add, and every rotation tick, decodes all full-size images on the main thread to draw 132×66 thumbnails. Every appearance.wallpapers transfer (each load_appearance and each rotation tick) and every library undo row in the audit table is twice as large.
findings.fix: In the spawn_blocking step, also make a small thumbnail (for example Pixbuf::from_file_at_scale(path, 264, 132)) and store that as preview, or omit preview, since the renderer already falls back to image. Cache textures by id, and skip the redraw while the gallery is not mapped.

v1.reason: tools_settings.rs:1011 pushes `"image":image,"preview":image`, the same full 1280x900 JPEG data URL twice, and line 1012 then checks the serialized library against 1,500,000 bytes. Each added image therefore costs twice its size against the cap. A q80 photo at 1280x900 is roughly 150-300 KB as JPEG, or 200-400 KB as base64, so the 'library is full' error can appear after only 2-4 photos, and rotation needs at least 2 images (wallpaper_rotation.rs:120). The built-in presets (wallpaper_rotation.rs:38) duplicate the same way. render_wallpapers decodes every card's full image on the UI thread (lines 838-853) plus the current image (wallpaper_texture, line 903). sync_wallpaper (lines 15-31) re-renders the gallery whenever appearance.wallpaper changes and nothing is staged, which includes every rotation tick: rotate_once sets the wallpaper, then settings.changed triggers load_appearance, which calls sync_wallpaper (shell.rs). The gallery is only held by a WeakRef, but the settings page stays mounted in the content stack after you navigate away, so these redraws continue while Settings is hidden. Nothing in the repo reads `preview` except the renderer, which already falls back to `image`.
v1.correction: The real user-visible cost is that the library holds half as many images as the cap allows. The per-tick decode cost is modest: a few JPEG decodes every 15 minutes by default, minimum 1 minute. Simplest fix: drop `preview` (the renderer falls back to `image`), or generate a small thumbnail in the spawn_blocking step. Raising or recomputing the cap is then optional. Existing stored libraries keep the duplicated data until they are rewritten.

findings.title: Dashboard re-runs dashboard.get and rebuilds every widget on each engine event from any project, with no throttling
findings.evidence: Each call does `let page = &ui.pages[name]; clear(page); match name { "dashboard" => dashboard(ui, page, &data), ...}` (80-86). dashboard() builds 100+ widgets, including about 30 SVG icons, one DrawingArea per project, and a button per hold, review, peer and event. While the dashboard is open, app.rs skips its per-project event filter (1213-1222) and sends every remaining event to refresh_page (1263-1265). session.changed refreshes it through agent_menu.rs:133-135, and every ui.refresh does too (app.rs:1441-1443). refresh_page only coalesces; it does not throttle.
findings.impact: With several agents working, session state changes and task, mailbox and notify events arrive continuously, and the dashboard is torn down and rebuilt back to back. Hover and keyboard focus reset. A click whose press and release fall on either side of a rebuild is lost, because the pressed button is destroyed. The engine runs dashboard.get under the store mutex once per burst: peers for every project, task aggregates, holds, and /proc reads for every pane.
findings.fix: Throttle dashboard refreshes, for example at most once every 1-2 s with a trailing update. Keep the panels and replace only rows whose data changed, and postpone a rebuild while a pointer button is held.

v1.reason: tools::refresh (apps/relay-native/src/tools.rs:55-87) awaits `dashboard.get`, then runs `clear(page)` and rebuilds the whole dashboard on every call. In app.rs:1213-1222 the per-project filter is skipped while ui.page is "dashboard", so events from any project get through. Every event not matched by a specific branch falls through to `ui.refresh_page()` (app.rs:1263-1265): task, mailbox, notify, guardrail, overlap and so on. Session events go through apply_session_event, which calls refresh_page when the page is board or dashboard (app.rs:633-635 in that impl; the finding cites agent_menu.rs:133). The session.list refresh path calls it too (app.rs:1441-1443). refresh_page (app.rs:1666-1688) only coalesces, through page_dirty/page_pending: one dashboard.get is in flight at a time, and if anything arrived meanwhile another full rebuild follows immediately. There is no delay or rate limit. session.changed fires on every idle->running flip (engine.rs mark_session_running, triggered by session.input) and on every state change. With several agents working, the dashboard is torn down and rebuilt back to back. On the engine side, dashboard.get is registered with plain `engine.register` (handlers/notify.rs:157). Under the store mutex it runs awareness::peers for every project, the task aggregate query, holds, notifications and app::resources, which reads per-pane resource rows. So each rebuild also costs the engine a full cross-project query while it holds the lock. Losing a click when the pressed button is destroyed before release is the normal GTK behaviour, and plausible at this rebuild rate.
v1.correction: The session-event refresh is in app.rs (apply_session_event, around lines 633-635: `if matches!(self.page.borrow().as_str(), "board" | "dashboard") { self.refresh_page(); }`), not agent_menu.rs:133. Impact is bounded by the coalescing: at most one dashboard.get in flight, so the cost is one rebuild per round trip during a burst, not one per event. That is still medium for a UI that resets hover, focus and scroll and can drop clicks. Fix as proposed: a trailing throttle of about 1 s on dashboard refreshes. A further option is to stop routing events from other projects that the dashboard does not display.

findings.title: 'Update from GitHub' always reinstalls from the repository's default branch, not the branch the skill was installed from
findings.evidence: The button sends `json!({"url": skill["source_url"], "subdir": skill["source_path"]})` (177). The engine stores source_url without the branch: github.rs:137 `format!("https://github.com/{}/{}.git", parts[0], repo)`. The branch parsed from a tree/<branch>/... URL (138-139) is used only for the clone and is not stored (DownloadedSkill at 190; the UPDATE at provider.rs:491-494 writes no ref). Parsing the stored URL again gives `branch` None, so the update runs `git clone --depth 1` on the default branch. The existing row is matched by source_url + source_path (provider.rs:425-444), so it is overwritten in place.
findings.impact: A skill installed from https://github.com/o/r/tree/dev/skills/x is, on 'Update from GitHub', silently replaced by the default branch's SKILL.md with a new revision. If that path does not exist on the default branch, the update fails with 'skills/x/SKILL.md does not exist in the repository'.
findings.fix: Store the ref, either by keeping the tree/<ref> form in source_url or adding a source_ref column with a migration, and pass it when updating. Until then, show the branch the skill came from and warn that an update uses the default branch.

v1.reason: parse_github_url (github.rs:121-145) turns a tree/<branch>/... URL into source = `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}.git` and passes the branch back separately. The branch is used only for `git clone --branch` (github.rs:108). DownloadedSkill.source_url gets the bare source (github.rs:190), and the skills table has no ref column. SkillInstallIn (relay-bus ops/provider.rs:37-43) has only url, subdir and replace_skill_id. The Update button (tools_skills.rs:177) sends `{url: source_url, subdir: source_path}`. Reparsing gives branch None, so the clone takes the default branch. source_path is the SKILL.md file path, which collect_skills accepts as a start. install_downloaded_skill matches on source_url + source_path (provider.rs:425-431) and runs an UPDATE on that same row with the new body and revision (provider.rs:489-494). A skill installed from a non-default branch is therefore silently replaced with the default branch's version. If the path does not exist on the default branch, it fails with skill.path_not_found.
v1.correction: A related effect: the unique index skills_source(source_url, source_path) (store.rs:277) means the same path installed from two branches collapses into one row, and each install overwrites the other. Store the ref, either in source_url as the tree/<ref> form or in a migrated source_ref column, and include it in the identity.

findings.title: Guardrail branch in collect_settings and its `guardrails` accumulator have been dead since the embedded guardrail editor replaced them
findings.evidence: `} else if let Some(path) = name.strip_prefix("guardrail:") { ... guardrails[group][key] = ...` (668-685) fills a `guardrails` value created at 121 (`let mut guardrails = json!({"caps":{},"destructive_write":{}});`) and passed in as a parameter (610). The Save handler never sends it; commit 4f62e33 removed the `guardrail.config.set` push. No widget is named `guardrail:*` any more: the embedded editor names its inputs `guardrail-field:{path}` (guardrail_settings.rs:509) and saves itself.
findings.impact: About 25 lines of dead serialization plus an unused accumulator. A reader would assume the global Save still writes guardrails. If a `guardrail:` name ever came back, the `ok_or("Invalid guardrail control")?` at 670 could abort the whole Save.
findings.fix: Delete lines 668-685, the `guardrails` parameter, and the accumulator at 121/126.

v1.reason: Nothing in apps/relay-native/src sets a widget name starting with `guardrail:`. The only match for that string is the strip_prefix at tools_settings.rs:668. The `guardrails` accumulator built at line 121 (`json!({"caps":{},"destructive_write":{}})`) is passed to collect_settings (lines 122-127) and never read after that: the Save handler only sends `settings` and the notification patch. Lines 668-685, the parameter and the accumulator are therefore dead.
v1.correction: The 'could abort Save' remark is speculative and should not count toward the finding. It is purely a cleanup: delete lines 668-685, the `guardrails` parameter (line 610) and the accumulator (lines 121 and 126).

findings.title: The notifications page in tools.rs can never be shown, and it has drifted from the bell popover that replaced it
findings.evidence: `notifications()` (596-649) and the "notifications" arms of refresh (66, 84) run only when ui.page == "notifications". But Ui::navigate returns early for that page and opens the popover instead (app.rs:1307-1313), and ui.page is only ever assigned in navigate (app.rs:1348). notification_center.rs handles the same actions and has changed since: it handles `session.get` links and project 0, and it filters out a `notifications` target (277-326). The dead copy still sends an unknown `ui.page.switch` target to "notifications".
findings.impact: About 60 lines, a content page (app.rs:630) and match arms that never run. Anyone maintaining notification routing may update the wrong copy.
findings.fix: Delete notifications(), its refresh arms, the "notifications" page in app.rs:630, and "notifications" in refresh_page's match (app.rs:1677).

v1.reason: ui.page is assigned only in Ui::navigate (app.rs:1348; the initial value is "agents", app.rs:747). navigate returns early for "notifications" and opens the popover (app.rs:1307-1313), so ui.page can never equal "notifications". That makes the "notifications" arms of tools::refresh (tools.rs:66, 84) unreachable. The same goes for notifications() (tools.rs:596-649), the matching entry in refresh_page (app.rs:1677), the event-filter match (app.rs:1218) and the content page created at app.rs:630. Nothing else looks the page up. The live version, NotificationCenter::follow (notification_center.rs:277-326), has diverged from it: it filters `notifications` out of a ui.page.switch target, handles `session.get` links, handles project 0 with ui.navigate, and focuses the session's pane. The dead copy still falls back to "notifications".
v1.correction: Also drop "notifications" from the event-filter match at app.rs:1218, along with the other locations listed.

findings.title: Cancelling the 'Add wallpaper' file chooser shows an error banner
findings.evidence: `let file=dialog.open_future(Some(&ui.window)).await.map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;` turns GTK's GTK_DIALOG_ERROR_DISMISSED ('Dismissed by user') into Err, and line 1017 does `if let Err(e)=result {ui.show_error(&e);}`. The other dialogs ignore a dismissal: onboarding.rs:573 `if let Ok(file) = ...` and mirror.rs:940 `let Ok(file) = ... else { return }`.
findings.impact: Every time the user closes the chooser without picking a file, the error banner says 'Dismissed by user'.
findings.fix: Treat `e.matches(gtk::DialogError::Dismissed)` (and Cancelled) as a silent no-op before mapping other errors to strings.

v1.reason: tools_settings.rs:999: `dialog.open_future(Some(&ui.window)).await.map_err(|e|e.to_string())?`. When the chooser is dismissed, GTK's FileDialog completes with a GtkDialogError::Dismissed error, which this code turns into Err(String). Line 1017 then calls `ui.show_error(&e)`, so closing the chooser without picking a file shows an error banner ('Dismissed by user'). Other dialogs in the codebase ignore a dismissal, as the finding says.
v1.correction: Treat a Dismissed or Cancelled `gtk::DialogError` as a silent no-op (return Ok(()) without rendering) before converting other errors to strings.

findings.title: plugins::switch duplicates market::toggle, and the two copies have diverged
findings.evidence: Both build a gtk::Switch whose connect_state_set skips while insensitive, disables the switch, calls plugin.enable, and calls `set_active(!on)` on failure (tools_plugins.rs:105-161 and tools_market.rs:690-742). The sidebar copy sets no accessible label (market::toggle calls `update_property(Label)`), shows raw errors without explain(), and does not update local data. Both name their widgets `plugin-{id}-{project}` (114, and card at 202).
findings.impact: Two implementations of the same optimistic switch. Fixes go into one only: screen readers announce an unlabelled switch in the sidebar plugin panel, and stale-engine errors read differently there. Smoke-test lookups by name can hit either widget.
findings.fix: Keep one helper that takes the enable op plus on_ok/on_err callbacks, and use it from the sidebar panel (shell.rs:984) and from market::toggle.

v1.reason: tools_plugins.rs:105-161 (plugins::switch, used only by the sidebar plugin sheet at shell.rs:984) and tools_market.rs:690-742 (market::toggle) implement the same optimistic switch. Each skips the handler while the switch is insensitive, disables it, calls the enable op, and calls set_active(!on) on error. The copies have diverged. Only market::toggle sets an accessible Label (`update_property(&[Property::Label(&tip)])`) and passes errors through explain(). The sidebar copy shows `error.to_string()` raw in its feedback label, even though the same sheet runs explain() on its list error (shell.rs:~1000).
v1.correction: The widget-name collision is not a real problem. Both copies use `plugin-{id}-{project}` (tools_plugins.rs:114 and 202), but nothing in the repo looks up widgets by these names (an rg for "plugin-" finds only the setters), so drop that point. A merged helper has to work without a Market (the sidebar has none), so give it on_ok/on_err callbacks. That is a modest payoff, consistent with low severity.

findings.title: Skill 'Remove' re-implements the two-click confirm that app::confirm_inline already provides
findings.evidence: `let armed = Rc::new(Cell::new(false)); remove.connect_clicked(move |key| { if !armed.replace(true) { key.set_label("Click again to remove"); key.add_css_class("armed"); ... timeout_add_local_once(4s ...) ...` (202-220). app.rs:99-202 confirm_inline does the same thing, and also disarms on Escape or focus loss, keeps the button width, updates the accessible label, and uses a serial so an old timer never disarms a newer arm. Other destructive buttons use it (task_pages.rs:1187, shell.rs:732).
findings.impact: Behaviour differs from the rest of the app: Escape and focus changes do not cancel, the button changes width, and it uses its own `.ext-danger.armed` CSS instead of `confirm-armed`.
findings.fix: Call `crate::app::confirm_inline(&remove, "Click again to remove", move |key| ui.mutate("skill.delete", ..., key))` and delete the Cell, the timer, and the .armed CSS rules.

v1.reason: tools_skills.rs:202-220 hand-rolls a two-click arm using `Rc<Cell<bool>>`, a 4 s timeout_add_local_once, and the `.armed` class (css/tools.css:108-109). app.rs:99-202 confirm_inline / confirm_inline_if already provides this with Escape and focus-leave disarm, width preservation, accessible-label updates, and a serial-guarded timer, and shell.rs:732 and task_pages.rs:1187 use it. Unlike confirm_inline, the hand-rolled version does not disarm after the second click. `armed` stays true until the 4 s timer fires, so after a failed skill.delete one more click within that window deletes without re-arming. The impact is UI inconsistency only.
v1.correction: The fix is right: `crate::app::confirm_inline(&remove, "Click again to remove", move |key| ui.mutate("skill.delete", ...))`, then delete the Cell, the timer and the .ext-danger.armed CSS rules.

findings.title: The client parses SKILL.md front matter itself with rules that differ from the engine's, and shows wrong descriptions
findings.evidence: `if body.trim_start().starts_with("---") { lines.next(); for line in lines.by_ref() { let line = line.trim(); if line == "---" { break; } if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix("description:") ...` (54-74). The engine has its own parser, plugins::frontmatter (plugins.rs:162-178): the first line must be `---`, keys must start at column 0, and it already supplies `description` for plugin skills.
findings.impact: A body with a blank line before `---`: lines.next() consumes the blank line, the loop stops at `---`, and the fallback returns the first front-matter line, so the card shows 'name: foo'. An indented `description:` nested under a key such as `metadata:` is chosen over the top-level one. Block scalars (`description: >`) show '>'. The same text drives search.
findings.fix: Add `description` to the bus Skill type, computed with the engine's single frontmatter() parser, and delete the client copy.

v1.reason: tools_skills.rs:54-74 parses front matter itself. Leading blank line: `body.trim_start().starts_with("---")` is true, `lines.next()` takes the blank line, the loop then breaks on `---` straight away, and the fallback returns the first non-empty line that is not '#' or '---', which is 'name: foo'. Nested keys: lines are trimmed before strip_prefix, so an indented `description:` under another key matches. The engine's plugins::frontmatter (plugins.rs:162-178) requires the first line to be `---` and keys at column 0. A third variant, github::frontmatter_name (github.rs:218-229), trims lines like the client does. So three parsers already disagree. All the triggers are uncommon SKILL.md layouts, and the only effect is the wrong card or search text.
v1.correction: The block-scalar case (`description: >`) is not caused by the duplication. plugins::frontmatter also returns '>' for it, so moving the client to the engine parser does not fix that. The real cost is three diverged parsers: client description, plugins::frontmatter, and github::frontmatter_name. Computing `description` once in the engine and putting it on the bus Skill or summary type (see native-tools#2) removes the client copy. github::frontmatter_name should use the same helper.

findings.title: explain() matches substrings in human error messages and misses the most common stale-engine case
findings.evidence: `if error.contains("plugin.") && (error.contains("unknown field") || error.contains("not implemented"))`. An engine without plugin ops replies bus.unknown_op, which displays as `Invalid bus.unknown_op: unknown op "plugin.list"` (relay-bus error.rs:106-108, engine.rs:316), so it does not match. The bus documents BusError.message as 'Human sentence; may change; never parse it' (error.rs:54-55). STALE_ENGINE tells the user to run `target/debug/relay --instance dev q app.quit '{"force":true}'` and `./run.sh`. The plugins empty state (452-467) shows that text whenever the list is empty, including when the engine merely skipped a bundled manifest it could not read (plugins.rs:116-121).
findings.impact: In the case the message was written for, an engine that predates plugins, the user sees the raw 'unknown op' error instead of the guidance. Rewording an engine message would silently break the mapping.
findings.fix: Match `Error::Bus(e)` on e.code (bus.unknown_op, bus.schema, bus.not_implemented) for plugin.* requests instead of matching message text.

v1.reason: explain() (tools_plugins.rs:17-25) maps an error to STALE_ENGINE only if its text contains "plugin." and either "unknown field" or "not implemented". The native client's Error::Bus displays the BusError (client.rs:76, `#[error("{0}")]`), and BusError's Display is `"{kind:?} {code}: {message}"` (error.rs:49). An engine without plugin ops answers BusError::unknown_op, which renders as `Invalid bus.unknown_op: unknown op "plugin.list"` (error.rs:106-108, engine.rs:316/819). That contains neither phrase, so the user sees the raw error. This is exactly the stale-engine case STALE_ENGINE was written for, and the comment at tools_plugins.rs:12-13 says so. A stale engine that has plugin.list but not project_id would hit bus.schema, whose message carries serde's "unknown field" text, so that sub-case does match. The match also depends on message text that error.rs:54 says must never be parsed. The empty state (tools_plugins.rs:452-467) always shows STALE_ENGINE. Since plugins are compiled in (plugins.rs BUNDLED) and a bad manifest is skipped with a warning, an empty list on a current engine would be a build defect, so that half of the claim is a minor point.
v1.correction: Match on Error::Bus(e) by e.code (`bus.unknown_op`, `bus.schema`, `bus.not_implemented`) instead of on message substrings. Impact is low: it affects only a developer running an engine older than the app.

findings.title: settings::refresh is one 555-line function, and Save reads values back by parsing widget names
findings.evidence: One async fn (33-587) fetches 14 values with sequential awaits (41-58), builds seven categories, and wires Save and search. Save serializes by walking the widget tree and parsing names (606-692): `setting:` names with a `=value` suffix for the mode buttons, `notify:` and `notify:category:`, and `guardrail:` (dead). Special cases keyed on path strings are repeated: `terminal.font_size` is fractional both at 624 and at 801; empty becomes null except under `keybindings.` (643); the sound ids appear at 464 and 660 (and again in sounds.rs:109); every category title is in both CATEGORIES and its `category(&stack, name, title)` call; the nav hints sit in a separate match (187-195). The same widget names also serve as smoke-test lookup hooks.
findings.impact: Nothing ties a field to its value, which is how the dead guardrail branch survived. Save cannot diff (see the Save finding), adding a setting means edits in 2-3 places, and the page waits for 14 round trips one after another.
findings.fix: Fill a list of fields (path, initial value, read closure) as each control is built. Save then sends settings.set only for fields that changed, with no widget-name parsing. Split out one builder function per category, and fetch the initial values together with a single join.

v1.reason: settings::refresh runs from tools_settings.rs:33 to about 587, and collect_settings (606-692) rebuilds every value by parsing widget names: `setting:<path>[=mode]`, `notify:*` and `guardrail:*`. No widget anywhere is named `guardrail:` (rg finds only the strip_prefix at line 668), and the `guardrails` value that collect_settings fills is never sent by the Save handler (lines 115-160). That whole branch and its variable are dead. Real duplications: the sound ids at lines 464 and 660 (plus the matching arms in sounds.rs); the terminal.font_size special case at 624 and 801; the category titles and hints split between CATEGORIES and the match at 187-195. The initial values come from 12 sequential settings.get calls plus 2 more requests (lines 41-58).
v1.correction: The 14 sequential awaits run over a local Unix socket, so the latency cost is small. The concrete costs are the dead guardrail branch and the duplicated sound and font-size special cases. A field registry (path, initial value, reader) built while the controls are built would remove the name parsing and make diff-on-save possible. A smaller cleanup is to delete the guardrail branch and the guardrails variable.

findings.title: Settings body's minimum width is fixed to the window width at the moment the page was built
findings.evidence: `shell.set_size_request(ui.window.width().clamp(748, 1180), -1);` is evaluated once, and the page is rebuilt only when the project changes. The page sits in a ScrolledWindow with automatic horizontal scrolling (app.rs:641).
findings.impact: If Settings is opened in a maximized window (minimum becomes 1180 px) and the window is then restored or tiled to about 1000 px, the body keeps its 1180 px minimum: a horizontal scrollbar appears and content is cut off until the project changes.
findings.fix: Remove the size request. Cap the width with a max-width container or CSS max-width with hexpand, or recompute it when the window width changes.

v1.reason: tools_settings.rs:166 `shell.set_size_request(ui.window.width().clamp(748, 1180), -1)` runs once per build. refresh() returns early at line 34 whenever page_projects["settings"] already equals the project, and the only places that clear it are the smoke tests (roadmap_smoke.rs:381/510). The settings.changed branch in app.rs:1249-1262 never rebuilds the page, and no resize handler exists. The page sits in `scrolled(&page)` (app.rs:640, a ScrolledWindow with the default automatic policy), so a min width wider than the viewport makes a horizontal scrollbar appear. Building the page in a maximized window and then restoring or tiling it leaves the 1180 px minimum in place.
v1.correction: The ScrolledWindow is created at app.rs:640 through `scrolled()` (app.rs:69), not at 641. The requested width is the whole window width, but the body also has 24 px of horizontal CSS padding (theme.css:204), and the window has a nav rail. So even without a resize, any window between about 748 px and about 1230 px is likely to get a horizontal scrollbar. That makes it worse than described, though it is still cosmetic. Fix as proposed: drop the size request and use hexpand plus a max-width container.

findings.title: Dashboard helpers append a labelled button, then the caller fishes it back with last_child() and replaces its content
findings.evidence: `navigate(ui, &quick, title, destination); if let Some(key) = quick.last_child().and_downcast::<gtk::Button>() { ... key.set_child(Some(&contents)); }` (196-202). The same append-then-recover pattern is used for navigate_session at 379-380 (`navigate_session(ui, &needs, "", ...); if let Some(key) = needs.last_child()...`) and 547-548.
findings.impact: This depends on each helper appending exactly one widget last, and every button is built twice (label, then custom child). It costs three downcasts for something a return value would give.
findings.fix: Have navigate and navigate_session return the gtk::Button (or take the child widget) and let the caller append it.

v1.reason: tools.rs:196-202 calls `navigate(ui, &quick, title, destination)`, which appends a labelled button (`parent.append(&key)`, tools.rs:96). The caller then gets it back with `quick.last_child().and_downcast::<gtk::Button>()` and calls set_child to replace the label. tools.rs:379-380 (blocked peers in `needs`) and 547-548 (agent rows in `active`) do the same with navigate_session(..., "", ...) followed by last_child(). The pattern depends on the helper appending exactly one widget, and on that widget being last. Returning the button would be simpler and remove the downcasts. It works correctly today.
v1.correction: The extra cost of building the button twice is negligible, since the label is empty or tiny. The real gain is removing a fragile coupling. Have navigate/navigate_session return the gtk::Button and leave the append to the caller.

findings.title: Plugin docs and SKILL.md cache is never cleared across engine restarts, and a failed lazy load is never retried
findings.evidence: `market.cache.borrow_mut().insert(key, found)` (366, 432). The Market lives for the whole app in thread-local MARKETS (tools_market.rs:85-87), and nothing clears its cache on reconnect, even though generation is bumped in app.rs connect(). On error the container gets an error paragraph (368, 434), after which `body.first_child().is_some()` (344) and lazy's `container.first_child().is_none()` (tools_market.rs:933) stop any further fetch.
findings.impact: After the engine restarts from a newer build (the run.sh flow), plugin rules, docs and SKILL.md bodies stay the old bundled versions until the app restarts. A transient timeout or disconnect leaves the error text in the tab until another plugin is selected.
findings.fix: Tag the cache with ui.generation and clear it when the generation changes. Show a Retry button that empties the container on error.

v1.reason: Market instances live for the whole process in the thread-local MARKETS (tools_market.rs:85-87, mount at 124-137), and nothing ever clears market.cache. The only accesses are the insert and get calls at tools_plugins.rs:351/366/419/432. Plugin content is compiled into the engine (plugins.rs:28 include!(bundled_plugins.rs)), so it changes only when a newer engine binary starts. After that, cached rules, documents and SKILL.md bodies stay stale until the app restarts. On error, the expander body gets an error paragraph (line 368), and the guard at line 344, `body.first_child().is_some()`, stops any retry when the expander is re-expanded. The documents tab works the same way through market::lazy (tools_market.rs:931-936), where `first_child().is_none()` fails once the error text is in place.
v1.correction: Staleness is limited to the dev flow of upgrading the engine under a running app, which makes it a low-severity edge case. The no-retry-after-error half is the more likely one to be hit.

results.coverage:
I read all four assigned files in full: tools_market.rs (1088 lines), status_usage.rs (849), status.rs (291) and provider_updates.rs (57).

**Context read to trace callers and engine behaviour:**
- app.rs: all of it (event routing, connect order, refresh, refresh_page, call).
- tools.rs, tools_plugins.rs and tools_skills.rs: the market's only users.
- panel.rs and client.rs: the 2 MiB MAX_LINE limit and request handling.
- shell.rs: open_project, project_skills and project_plugins.
- agent_menu.rs: apply_session_event and the phone run.
- Engine handlers: provider.rs (skill and plugin list/enable, usage.get/report), app.rs (resources), device.rs (list, watch, timeouts), settings.rs, provider_updates.rs, usage.rs.
- Engine core: socket.rs (the per-connection request loop, which processes requests one at a time) and engine.rs (audit on failure).
- relay-cli hook reporting, and DECISIONS D64/D66.

**Verification limits:**
- None of this was compiled or run. relay-native cannot be built here, and the task forbade cargo.
- GTK and glib behaviour was checked against the gtk4-rs 0.11.4 and glib 0.22.9 sources in ~/.cargo/registry and the system Gtk-4.0.gir: SourceId::remove panics on a double remove, JoinHandle::abort, is_sensitive is effective sensitivity, and DropDown search requires an expression. GtkSwitch::set_active re-emitting state-set was confirmed from memory of gtkswitch.c and from the code's own comment.

**Not established:**
- The real size of the user's Relay skill library. I did not query the live engine or its database; the 2 MiB risk is estimated from ~/.claude skills on disk (74 files, 1.08 MB).
- The exact order of requests on the wire at connect. It depends on tokio's task ordering, so the startup-delay claim in the refresh_status finding has medium confidence.

**Overlap with other chunks:**
- The infinite enable loop is in shell.rs:882. I report it as divergence under the duplication finding anchored in tools_market.rs.
- The 2 MiB limit is in client.rs and the per-connection serialisation in socket.rs; both are cited only as related evidence.

**Checked and found no issue:**
- RefCell borrow scopes in render, sync_picker, reveal_banner, set_enabled, refresh_usage and reload_usage_prefs.
- The timer bookkeeping in schedule_usage.
- Weak/strong captures in all closures, with no Rc cycles found.
- Integer casts flagged by pedantic clippy (status_usage.rs:107/134/401/507, tools_market.rs:519/1061/1067, status.rs:230-231): all bounded or display-only.
- Markup injection: label() and tooltips use plain text.

**Deliberately not reported:**
- relay-native tests never run in CI (documented in ci.yml).
- Hard-coded lamp colours.
- Status-bar counts being per-project, which is consistent with the sidebar.

findings.title: The skill catalog and install replies include every SKILL.md body; once they total about 2 MiB, the client drops its only control connection
findings.evidence: tools_market.rs:96 `let result = ui.call(spec.list_op, json!({})).await;` with tools_skills.rs:25 `list_op: "skill.list"`. The engine's skill_row returns the full text for every skill (handlers/provider.rs:551 `body: row.get("body")?`). Each body may be up to 256 KiB (provider.rs:584), and nothing caps the number of skills (github.rs find_skill_files collects every SKILL.md). The client caps a line at `const MAX_LINE: usize = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (client.rs:48). On an over-long line the reader returns `Err(Error::Protocol("frame exceeds .. MiB"))` (client.rs:200-204). That error fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected, and app.rs:1267-1275 then drops the client and shows 'Engine disconnected'. The same bodies also travel in shell.rs:832 (the 'Agent skills' popover) and in the skill.install reply (provider.rs:244 `Ok(SkillInstallOut { skills })`, called from tools_skills.rs:370).
findings.impact: Once the installed skills' bodies add up to about 2 MiB, every load of the Skills page tears down the app's whole control connection. That is about 8 maximum-size skills, or about 100 typical 20 KB ones; the 74 SKILL.md files under ~/.claude on this machine already total 1.08 MB. The same happens on every event-driven refresh of that page, on opening the Agent-skills popover, and on installing a large repo. All in-flight requests fail and the UI shows 'Engine disconnected'. This repeats on every visit, so the Skills page becomes a disconnect trigger.
findings.fix: Have skill.list return summaries without `body` (id, name, description, source, enabled_in, timestamps), and fetch one body when an item is selected (a skill.get, or a `body` flag). Have skill.install return ids and names only. On the client, treat an oversized line as a failure of that one request (drain to the newline) instead of a fatal protocol error for the whole connection.

v1.reason: Verified the full chain. skill.list (provider.rs:86-104, a locked register) returns `body` for every skill through skill_row (:541-559, `body: row.get("body")?`). Bodies are capped only per skill, at 256 KiB (valid_skill_body :583, also enforced on install :424), and nothing caps the skill count. The engine sends arbitrarily large responses: the only frame cap is on the client side. client.rs:48 sets MAX_LINE = 2 MiB, and the reader (:186-209) returns Err(Error::Protocol("frame exceeds ..")) on a longer line. That ends the reader loop, fails every pending reply, and emits Notice::Disconnected. app.rs:1267-1275 then drops the client and shows 'Engine disconnected'. Callers that pull bodies are tools_market.rs:96 (list_op skill.list), shell.rs:832 (the agent-skills popover) and tools_skills.rs:370 (the skill.install reply, provider.rs:244). The Skills page uses the body for its detail view and search (tools_skills.rs:55, :240), which explains why the list carries it. Once total body size plus JSON escaping passes 2 MiB, every load of these views deterministically drops the whole control connection. Finding #2 makes this worse: the page re-lists on unrelated events.
v1.correction: Severity is medium, not high. The trigger needs a skill library of roughly 2 MiB, which a typical user will not reach. Once reached, though, the failure is deterministic and repeats, and it kills the whole UI connection. The deeper root cause is client.rs:200: any one oversized response is fatal to the connection. The fix should cover both points: drain to the newline and fail only the request whose frame was too large (the reader cannot know the id before parsing, so it might fail just that frame, or lift the cap for responses), and drop `body` from skill.list and skill.install in favour of a per-skill fetch.

findings.title: The Skills and Plugins pages reload the whole catalog and rebuild every row on every unrelated engine event, even when nothing changed
findings.evidence: app.rs:1263-1265 sends every event not handled earlier to `ui.refresh_page()`. That covers task.changed, mailbox.*, notify.*, guardrail.*, overlap.*, module.*, device.*, run.*. For these pages refresh_page runs market::refresh, which always does `*market.data.borrow_mut() = rows(&value, spec.list_key);` and then `market.render(ui);` (:102-108), with no check for unchanged data. render clones the whole catalog (`let data = self.data.borrow().clone();` :535) and clones the filtered set again (:553-561). It then calls `self.list.remove_all()` (:566) and recreates every row, card, Switch and FlowBox (:569-599). On the engine side, skill.list is a locked handler (provider.rs:86 `e.register::<SkillList>`) that runs 1+N queries and copies every body under the store mutex. plugin.list (provider.rs:269) does a read_dir of every project root for each plugin.
findings.fix: In refresh(), compare the new rows with `*market.data.borrow()`. If they are equal, skip render() (still hide errors and set loaded). In app.rs, send only skill.*, plugin.* and project.* events to these two pages. Later, patch rows in place instead of calling remove_all().

v1.reason: app.rs:1263-1265: every subscribed event not matched earlier falls through to ui.refresh_page(), as long as it belongs to the current project or carries no project id (:1211-1220). That covers task.*, mailbox.*, notify.*, guardrail.*, overlap.*, module.*, device.*, run.*, usage.changed, skill.* and plugin.*. refresh_page (:1662-1686) coalesces events but re-runs while dirty. For 'skills' and 'plugins' it awaits tools::refresh, which calls market::refresh (tools_market.rs:90-120). That handler always replaces data and calls render() with no equality check. render (:527 onward) clones the data, then calls list.remove_all() and rebuilds every row and card. Only the scroll offset is restored. With agents active, an open Skills or Plugins page is torn down and rebuilt on each burst of events, losing focus and hover state on rows. On the Skills page each pass also re-transfers every body.
v1.correction: plugin.list is registered with register_unlocked (provider.rs:269). Its project-root detection runs without the store mutex; only the enable edges are read under ctx.read. skill.list is locked, but its 1+N prepared queries are cheap at realistic sizes, so the engine-side mutex cost is minor. The real cost is client-side churn and UI disruption, plus re-sending bodies (see #1). The proposed fixes are sound: route only skill.*, plugin.* and project.* events to these pages, and skip render() when the rows are unchanged.

findings.title: The detail pane is cached on (item, scope) only, so it misses project renames and additions and palette changes, and project events never repaint the page
findings.evidence:
`let next = item.map(|v| (v.clone(), scope)); if *self.shown.borrow() == next { return; }` (:633-636). The detail that spec.detail builds also reads other state:
- ui.projects and ui.workspaces: enable_block uses project_name and reach (:766, :777), project_switches reads `ui.projects.borrow().clone()` (:803-804), and switch tooltips embed project names (:705-706);
- ui.palette: markdown() resolves `relay-{palette}` once (:1030).
project.changed and project.deleted events (add, rename via project.update, reorder, remove) only run `ui.registry_dirty.set(true); ui.refresh();` (app.rs:1223-1225). refresh() repaints only board and dashboard (app.rs:1441-1443). This contradicts the module doc, which says 'every engine event repaints it through tools::refresh' (:5-9).
findings.impact: Rename project Foo to Bar while a skill or plugin is selected. On the next repaint the picker and hint say Bar, but the detail still says 'On in Foo' and lists Foo in the Projects tab. Add a project that a plugin does not detect: the plugin's item JSON doesn't change, so its Projects tab never gets a switch for the new project and 'On in X of N projects' stays wrong. Because `shown` lives in the mounted Market, this survives navigating away and back, until a different item is selected. A palette change leaves the SKILL.md and doc views in the old style scheme. A switch for a removed project stays visible, and turning it fails.
findings.fix: Invalidate `shown` whenever the inputs change: set it to None in sync_picker when picker_ids changes, on workspace changes, and on appearance changes. Alternatively, put a projects/workspaces revision and the palette into the cache key. Have app.rs repaint the skills and plugins pages on project.* and workspace.* events, and correct the module comment.

v1.reason: show_detail (tools_market.rs:631-636) returns early when `(item.clone(), scope)` equals `self.shown`. `shown` is assigned only at :357 (None) and :658. The Market is mounted once and kept in MARKETS (mount :121-139), so the cache survives navigation. The detail reads state outside that key. enable_block uses project_name and reach, which read ui.projects. project_switches clones ui.projects and ui.workspaces (:803-804). toggle tooltips embed project_name. markdown() reads ui.palette (:1030). On project.* and workspace.* events, app.rs:1223-1225 only sets registry_dirty and calls ui.refresh(), and refresh repaints a page only for board or dashboard (app.rs ~1441). A later refresh_page or navigation re-runs render. sync_picker then picks up the new names, but show_detail hits the cache, because the item JSON and scope did not change. Trigger: rename a project, or add one the plugin does not detect, while an item is selected. The enable block keeps the old name, the Projects tab keeps the old list, and 'On in X of N' keeps the old N, until a different item or scope is chosen. The module doc (:5-7) claims every engine event repaints the page, which is not true for project and workspace events.
v1.correction: Switches still act on the right project id. A switch for a removed project fails cleanly: get_project returns NotFound and the guarded restore runs. Most of the impact is stale or wrong labels and counts, plus a missing switch for a newly added project. The palette point is minor: the documents also sit in market.cache. Simplest fix: put a projects/workspaces fingerprint (or a revision counter bumped when the registry reloads) and the palette into the cache key, or clear `shown` in sync_picker when picker_ids changes. Also repaint the plugins and skills pages on project.* and workspace.* events, and correct the module comment.

findings.title: The per-project enable switch is written three times; the copy in shell.rs lost the re-entrancy guard and loops forever when an enable fails
findings.evidence: market::toggle (:690-742) guards with `if !switch.is_sensitive() { return glib::Propagation::Proceed; }`. The guard is needed because the error path calls `switch.set_active(!on)`, and GtkSwitch::set_active emits state-set again. tools_plugins.rs:105-161 (`plugins::switch`, used only by shell.rs project_plugins) re-implements the same switch with the same guard (:123). shell.rs:873-888 (project_skills) re-implements it inline without the guard: `Err(error) => { key.set_active(!on); ... }` (:882). The enabled_in and suggested_for checks are also copied (tools_plugins.rs:92-102, shell.rs:860-862, shell.rs:971-973).
findings.impact:
In the 'Agent skills' popover, if skill.enable fails, set_active(!on) re-enters the handler and sends the opposite request. That fails too and flips the switch back, without end. Failure cases:
- engine restarted or disconnected: `ui.call` fails at once, so the main loop spins flipping the switch until reconnect, and then whichever value was last in flight is written, at random;
- skill deleted or project removed by another client: a request storm that never stops; each request takes the store mutex and writes an audit row (skill.enable is Audit::Always and NotFound failures are audited, engine.rs:1075), until the app exits.
The futures hold the switch, so closing the popover doesn't stop the loop.
findings.fix: Keep one implementation: market::toggle, or a small shared `enable_switch(ui, op, id_key, id, project, on_result)`. Call it from shell.rs project_skills and project_plugins, delete plugins::switch and the inline copy, and share the enabled/suggested predicates.

v1.reason: shell.rs:873-887 (the project_skills popover) connects state_set and has no re-entrancy guard. It calls key.set_sensitive(false), spawns `ui.call("skill.enable", {.., enabled: on})`, and on Err runs `key.set_active(!on)` before set_sensitive(true). GtkSwitch::set_active emits state-set synchronously when the value changes. The other two copies rely on exactly this behaviour: market::toggle (tools_market.rs:718) and plugins::switch (tools_plugins.rs:123) both guard with `if !switch.is_sensitive() { return Proceed }` and the comment 'A rejected write restores the switch while it is disabled'. In shell.rs the restore re-enters the handler and sends the opposite request, so any failure that hits both directions recurses with no end. Both directions fail in these cases. (1) Engine disconnected: ui.call returns Error::Disconnected at once (app.rs:1112), so futures spin on the main loop, flipping the switch until a reconnect lets one request succeed with whichever value is current. (2) Skill deleted or project removed by another client: skill.enable runs get_project and then get_skill (provider.rs:193-194), both return NotFound, and the engine audits non-Invalid failures in their own transaction (engine.rs ~1074-1090). Each iteration takes the store mutex and adds an audit row, without bound, until the app exits. The futures hold the switch clone, so closing the popover does not stop the loop. The duplication is real as well: three copies of the switch, and enabled/suggested predicates repeated in tools_plugins.rs:92-102, shell.rs:860-862 and shell.rs:971-973. The copy in shell.rs is the one that has already diverged.
v1.correction: The root cause is a bug (a missing guard that causes an infinite re-entrant request loop), so the category is bug rather than duplication. The trigger needs a failure in a less common path, so medium rather than high. The immediate fix is to add the `if !key.is_sensitive() { return glib::Propagation::Proceed; }` guard in shell.rs:873. The longer-term fix is to consolidate onto one shared switch helper, as proposed.

findings.title: With the default 'Off' interval the usage meters never refresh when a provider reports, although the UI says they do
findings.impact: In the default setup the status-bar meters are read once at connect. After that they change only when a device or run event happens, the popup is opened (:666), or a refresh key is pressed. Over a long session they keep showing the start-of-session figure (for example 40% while the account is near its limit), while the tooltip promises they follow new reports.
findings.fix: Re-read usage when a turn ends, throttled to about once per 30 s: on session.changed to idle, or on a session.report 'stop'. Alternatively, have the engine emit usage.changed when relay-usage.json's mtime or the newest Codex rollout advances. Failing that, default refresh_minutes to a non-zero value and correct both strings.

v1.reason: interval_text(0) reads 'refreshes on new reports and on demand' (status_usage.rs:172-178), and the Auto refresh tooltip says 'Off still refreshes on new reports.' (:726). The default is refresh_minutes: 0 (handlers/settings.rs:23), and schedule_usage returns without arming a timer when minutes == 0 (:399-401). The only event-driven path is usage.changed, device.changed or run.changed calling refresh_status (app.rs:1188-1193). usage.changed is emitted only by the usage.report handler (handlers/provider.rs:83), and usage.report is AgentOnly. Nothing in relay-core or relay-cli sends it automatically. Claude's status-line script only writes relay-usage.json (hooks.rs:577), Codex usage is read from rollout files (D64), and relay-cli has no usage references. So with the default setting the strip is read at connect and refreshed only by a device or run event, opening the popup (:666), or the refresh key. A provider's new report never triggers a refresh, contrary to the UI text.
v1.correction: There is some mitigation: the strip shows how old the reading is through render_usage_age on a 30 s clock (status_usage.rs:298-310), so the staleness is visible. The UI text is still false and the default never updates the meters. Usage.get reads the files live (usage.rs), so the cheapest fix is a throttled refresh_usage(false) when a session.changed moves a session to idle. Otherwise default to a non-zero interval and correct both strings.

findings.title: refresh_status runs adb and usage.get on the shared, sequential control connection for every device/run/usage event, without coalescing, and never retries a failed device count
findings.evidence: refresh_status (:66-85) always runs render_status_counts, refresh_usage(false), and a new `ui.call("device.list")` with no in-flight guard. It runs on every usage.changed, device.changed and run.changed (app.rs:1188-1193), and at connect before the first project/session load (app.rs:1158 vs 1162). device.list runs `adb devices -l` with a 2 s timeout (device.rs:32-34, :577). The engine serves one connection strictly one request at a time: it reads the next line only after `spawn_blocking(..).await` and `out_tx.send` (socket.rs:335, :742-744). The device watcher emits one device.changed per adb output line (device.rs:377). The Devices page already calls device.list itself (tools_devices.rs:11). On failure the label is left as it was (`if let Ok(v) = devices`).
findings.impact: At startup, device.list is probably queued ahead of project.list, workspace.list and session.list. With a cold adb server it takes the full 2 s, delaying the first sidebar and wall load. It then times out, so the strip shows 'No device' with a phone plugged in, and nothing retries until a device or run event arrives (device.changed only flows while the Devices page is open). A hot-plug with N devices sends N adb subprocesses plus a useless usage.get on the window's only control connection, stalling every other UI request. Each run state change spends an adb call as well.

v1.reason: refresh_status (status.rs:66-85) always calls render_status_counts and refresh_usage(false), and starts a new device.list with no in-flight guard. In connect() it runs before ui.refresh() (app.rs:1158 vs 1162), so device.list is pipelined ahead of project.list and workspace.list on the same control connection. The engine handles one line per connection at a time: it awaits spawn_blocking(dispatch) and then out_tx.send before reading the next line (socket.rs:335, 742-744). device.list is register_unlocked, but it runs `adb devices -l` bounded at 2 s (device.rs:31-34, 577). That command starts the adb server if it is not running, so on a cold adb server the first sidebar and wall load can wait up to 2 s. The device label starts as 'No device' (app.rs:704) and is updated only on Ok (status.rs:76). After a timeout it stays 'No device' until the next usage/device/run event. usage.changed effectively never fires (see #5), and device.changed only flows while device.watch is on, i.e. while the Devices page or a mirror is open.
v1.correction: Severity is lower than claimed. Terminal panes use their own connections (terminal.rs:476), so keystrokes are never stalled. refresh_usage is already coalesced through busy/queued (status_usage.rs:321-324), so usage.get is not repeated per event. With a hot adb server each device.list takes tens of milliseconds. The device.changed bursts happen only while the Devices page, which also lists devices, is open. That adb takes longer than 2 s on a cold start is likely but was not measured. Fix: send the connect-time device.list after the first refresh, or on its own connection. Skip device.list on usage.changed, retry it once after device.adb_timeout, and coalesce in-flight calls.

findings.title: The Resources panel rebuilds every row and chart on each 2 s sample, so path tooltips vanish; it keeps 40 samples where D66 says 30
findings.evidence: Every resource.sample (every 2 s) calls render_resources (:131-133). It runs `clear(body);` and recreates the header, three DrawingAreas and every relay, session and worktree row (:178-291). Row labels are ellipsized at the end at 23 chars (`set_ellipsize(End)`, `set_max_width_chars(23)`, :155-156), and the full text is only in a tooltip (:157). The history keeps 40 points (`if history.len() > 40`, :200); DECISIONS.md:272 says 'keeps the last 30 samples'.
findings.impact: The worktree path detail shows only the shared prefix ('/home/anthony/dev3/Rel…'). Its tooltip, the only way to read the full path, disappears within 2 s because its label is destroyed, and it doesn't come back until the pointer moves. Hover and scroll state churn, and about 7 widgets per session or worktree are recreated every 2 s while the panel is open.
findings.fix: Build the rows once, keyed by session or path, and update labels and fractions in place. Keep the history in an Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>> that the draw functions capture, and call queue_draw(). Ellipsize paths at the start or middle. Make the 40/30 constant agree with D66.

v1.reason: Every resource.sample calls render_resources (status.rs:131-133). It runs clear(body) at :203 and rebuilds the header, three DrawingAreas and every relay, session and worktree row. resource_row ellipsizes both labels at the end with max_width_chars(23) and puts the full text only in a tooltip (:153-158). For a worktree the detail label is the full path (:282), so only its common prefix is visible. The full path is readable only in the tooltip, and the tooltip disappears when its label is destroyed at the next sample. history is capped at 40 (:200), while DECISIONS.md:272 (D66) says 30 samples.
v1.correction: The tooltip loss and per-sample widget churn are real but small: the panel is opt-in, and samples arrive only while it is open. The 40/30 mismatch is minor docs drift. The cheapest fix: ellipsize the path label at the start or middle so the useful tail is visible, and update the rows in place. Rebuilding the rows only when the set of sessions or worktrees changes would remove most of the churn.

findings.title: The market's error notice and plugin document cache survive successful reloads and reconnects
findings.evidence: When a reload of an already-loaded page fails, refresh calls `market.say(&message)` (:112-113), which only sets the notice visible (:462-465). The Ok arm (:101-108) never hides it; only the dismiss key does (:365-369). `pub cache` (:79) is filled by plugins' documents() and skill_list() under plugin-id keys (tools_plugins.rs:366, :432) and is never cleared. The Market lives forever in MARKETS and is never reset on reconnect.
findings.impact: After a disconnect and reconnect, the page keeps showing 'Connection closed. Reconnect to the engine.' above a freshly loaded catalog. If the engine is restarted on a newer build while the app stays open (the STALE_ENGINE flow), plugin cards show the new version but the 'Rules & docs' tab and the skill bodies come from the old cache.
findings.fix: Call `market.notice.set_visible(false)` in refresh's Ok arm. Clear `cache` when ui.generation changes, or key it by plugin version.

v1.reason: tools_market.rs:110-114: when a reload of an already-loaded page fails, it calls market.say(), which only sets the notice text and makes it visible (:462-465). The Ok arm (:101-108) never hides it; only the dismiss button does (:367). Example: navigate while disconnected, which records a load error, then reconnect. The successful reload leaves the stale error banner above a correct catalog. The Market persists in MARKETS (:85-87) and mount() reuses it while it is still parented (:122-127), so the stale notice and `cache` survive a reconnect. `cache` (filled at tools_plugins.rs:366 and :432) is never cleared.
v1.correction: The cache half is minor. Plugins are compiled into the engine (crate::plugins::all()), so cached documents go stale only when the engine is replaced by a different build while the app stays open. Clearing the cache on a generation change is enough. The main fix is `market.notice.set_visible(false)` in the Ok arm, or at least when the visible notice came from a load error, so that action errors shown via say() are not hidden by a background refresh.

findings.title: The project picker shows a search entry that filters nothing, because no expression is set
findings.evidence: `picker.set_enable_search(true);` is set on a DropDown built with from_strings and custom factories. Its model is later replaced with `gtk::StringList::new(&names)` (:513), and set_expression is never called. Gtk-4.0.gir documents enable-search as follows: 'Note that search requires GtkDropDown:expression to be set'. Without an expression GtkDropDown filters with an every-filter.
findings.impact: Users with many projects get a search field in the picker popup, but typing in it narrows nothing.
findings.fix: `picker.set_expression(Some(gtk::PropertyExpression::new(gtk::StringObject::static_type(), None::<gtk::Expression>, "string")));` Apply the same fix to the worktree DropDown in tools_devices.rs:241.

v1.reason: tools_market.rs:173-174 builds the picker with `gtk::DropDown::from_strings(&[])` and calls `picker.set_enable_search(true)`. Nothing in apps/relay-native/src calls set_expression (rg finds no hits). sync_picker (:511-513) swaps in `gtk::StringList::new(&names)` and leaves the expression unset. In upstream gtkdropdown.c, gtk_drop_down_new_from_strings is `gtk_drop_down_new(G_LIST_MODEL(gtk_string_list_new(strings)), NULL)`, so its expression is NULL. update_filter uses a GtkStringFilter only when self->expression is set and otherwise uses gtk_every_filter_new(). No code path sets a default expression for GtkStringObject models. The installed Gtk-4.0.gir (4.22.5) also says 'search requires GtkDropDown:expression to be set'. The result is a search entry in the popup that filters nothing. tools_devices.rs:241 has the same problem: from_strings, then set_enable_search(true), with no expression.
v1.correction: The proposed fix is right: set a PropertyExpression on StringObject 'string' (or a ClosureExpression returning the string) for both DropDowns. The custom factories can stay. The other option is to drop set_enable_search.

findings.title: set_enabled patches only enabled_in, so a plugin just switched on stays 'Suggested' for that project
findings.evidence: `item["enabled_in"] = enabled_in.clone();` is the only patch. The engine's suggested_for excludes enabled projects (provider.rs:289 `.filter(|(id, _)| !enabled_in.contains(id))`), but plugin.enable replies with `to_bus(plugin, enabled_in, Vec::new())` (provider.rs:335), so the local suggested_for keeps the project. The plugin.changed event that would correct it is dropped for any project other than the active one (app.rs:1213-1222).
findings.impact:
After switching a suggested plugin on for a project other than the active one:
