With that setting off, which the editor offers (guardrail_settings.rs:66), a committed, unmodified file is held on volume alone, and the hold details carry no flag saying which case applied.
findings.impact: With "Allow rewrites git can restore" off, the hold card states something false about the very safety question the user is deciding.
findings.fix: Have the engine add a `recoverable_checked` field to the details, and show the sentence only when it is true; otherwise say Relay did not check whether git can restore it.

v1.reason: guardrail_pages.rs:124-128 always appends ", and git cannot restore what is there now." to the destructive_write explanation. In crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:725-730, `recoverable()` is consulted only `if limits.allow_if_recoverable`. When that setting is off (it is a toggle in guardrail_settings.rs:66), a committed, unmodified file over the volume limit is held without git ever being asked. The details JSON built at guardrail.rs:745-751 has no field saying whether recoverability was checked. The sentence is also false when it was checked but `recoverable()` returned None because git itself failed (`!out.status.success()` at line 680 gives None). The same text appears on user-bypass holds, since `effective()` unwraps `original`.
v1.correction: The sentence is false in two cases: the toggle is off, or the git status call failed (line 680). Fix: have destructive_decision add a field such as `"recoverable": false | null` (null meaning not checked) to the details, and print the git clause only when it is false.

findings.title: tray.set_focus_on_click(false) has no effect: answering a prompt pulls focus out of the terminal
findings.evidence: The comment says "it never takes keyboard focus". But `focus-on-click` only matters for focusable widgets: GtkBox never grabs focus, while every Button in the card keeps the default and grabs focus on press (445-447, 455). After an answer, the keys go insensitive and the card is removed, leaving no widget focused.
findings.impact: A user typing in an agent terminal who answers a prompt must click back into the terminal before their keystrokes land again.
findings.fix: Call `set_focus_on_click(false)` on each prompt key (once, always, deny, X, more), or remember the previously focused widget and restore it in close_prompt; correct the comment.

v1.reason: focus-on-click is a per-widget property and only matters on focusable widgets. Setting it on the tray Box (517) does not reach the child buttons. The keys are made by app::button and app::icon_button (app.rs:34, 46), and neither changes focus_on_click, so a GtkButton grabs focus when pressed. Elsewhere the codebase sets `set_focus_on_click(false)` on each button, for example note_pages.rs:331 and shell/registry.rs:159/194, which shows the intended pattern. After Approve, `keys.set_sensitive(false)` (469-471) and the later removal of the card leave focus on a widget that is gone or insensitive. Nothing hands focus back to the terminal, so typing does not reach the agent pane until the user clicks it again.
v1.correction: The Deny form grabs focus on purpose (entry.grab_focus at ~399). That is fine and should stay. The fix is to set focus_on_click(false) on once, always, deny, X and the overflow key, and to correct the comments at 516 and 566.

results.coverage:
I read every line of theme.css, the nine css/*.css files and resources/relay-editor.xml. Methods:

- **Class cross-reference:** checked about 930 class names against quoted strings in all of apps/relay-native/src/**/*.rs, excluding smoke tests, `has_css_class` reads and `set_widget_name`. The format!-built status-/priority-/state-/label-hue-/pr-/lane- classes were checked against the values they can take. Multi-line helper calls were hand-verified.
- **Shadowing:** computed exact-selector overrides in the concatenated load order (app.rs:344-355), with shorthand/longhand resets. Specificity-based shadowing was traced by hand for the cases cited.
- **Structure:** checked every element name and child combinator against the Gtk-4.0.gir CSS-node docs.
- **Runtime checks:** ran throwaway PyGObject processes (GTK 4.22, GtkSourceView 5.20, Pango 1.58) under the scratchpad. No window was shown and nothing in the repo or the running Relay was touched. They showed zero CSS parsing errors in the real concatenated sheet, so no unsupported properties. They also confirmed the `menubar`/`entry`/`expander-widget` node names, the computed git name colours, text-decoration non-inheritance and the scheme style resolution, plus a validated `use-style` fix. Font face matching was checked with the real font set and with a private FONTCONFIG_FILE limited to the bundled fonts.
- **Other:** there is no `!important` anywhere. All `@color` references resolve to defined tokens. The pedantic clippy file has no warnings for these files.

Not checked:
- Actual rendering. There were no screenshots, so how the desktop theme draws the unstyled Notes menubar is inferred, not observed.
- Whether `window.notes-window { box-shadow: none; margin: 0 }` (theme.css:478) removes GTK's client-side resize edges on Wayland, despite notes_window.rs:79's intent. This needs a mapped window.
- Cascade interactions for widgets carrying three or more classes, beyond the pairs traced.
- The partial-alpha layering of panels in the Notes window.
- DESIGN.md beyond its statements about styling.

The fonts.rs/resources finding sits outside the CSS file list but determines whether the CSS font-weight declarations work.

findings.title: Explorer and Source Control file names never show their git status colour: `.tree-name`/`.scm-name` override every `.git-*` rule
findings.evidence: git_files.css:31-36 set the status colours with single-class rules (`.git-modified { color: #e2c08d; }`, `.git-added, .git-untracked {…}`, `.git-deleted`, `.git-renamed`, `.git-conflict`, `.git-ignored`), specificity 0,1,0. Later in the same file, line 63 `.tree-name { font-size: 12.5px; color: @ink; }` and line 193 `.scm-name { font-size: 12.5px; color: @ink; }` have the same specificity, so source order makes them win. The Rust puts both classes on the same label: editor.rs:775-780 (`label(name, "tree-name")` then `name.add_css_class(class)`), code_git.rs:873-876 and 1493-1496 (`label(name, "scm-name")` then `title.add_css_class(class)`). Only ignored files were special-cased (`.tree-name.git-ignored`, line 38, 0,2,0). I checked this in a throwaway GTK 4.22 process loading the real concatenated stylesheet: tree-name/scm-name plus git-modified/added/deleted/conflict all compute to #ececea (ink), and scm-name plus git-ignored is also ink. Only the `scm-letter`/`tree-badge` letters get #e2c08d.
findings.impact: Every changed file in the Code explorer and Source Control list shows its name in plain ink. That contradicts the file's own comment (line 30: "names and letters, explorer and Source Control alike") and DESIGN.md. The folder re-tint pass in project_files.rs:566-579 removes and re-adds STATUS_CLASSES on every folder name at each status refresh, with no visible result. Only the strikethrough on deleted names and the one-letter badges show status.
findings.fix: Remove `color: @ink` from `.tree-name` (line 63) and `.scm-name` (line 193). Both labels already inherit ink from `button.tree-row` (line 52), `button.scm-open` (line 189) or the dialog. Alternatively, move the `.git-*` block below those rules. Then delete the now-redundant `.tree-name.git-ignored` (line 38).

v1.reason: All stylesheets are concatenated into one CssProvider (app.rs:344-355), so at equal specificity the rule that comes later in the source wins. git_files.css:31-36 sets the status colours with single-class selectors (specificity 0,1,0). The later rules at git_files.css:63 `.tree-name { ...; color: @ink; }` and :193 `.scm-name { ...; color: @ink; }` have the same specificity and therefore override them. No later stylesheet re-asserts the git colours (an rg search across css/ shows no other .git-* rules). The Rust code puts both classes on the same label: editor.rs:773-780 adds `tree-name` and then the status class, and code_git.rs:873-876 and 1493-1496 do the same with `scm-name`. Result: modified, added, deleted, renamed and conflicted names render in ink in the explorer and in Source Control. That contradicts the comment at git_files.css:30. Only the `.tree-name.git-ignored` override (0,2,0) and the strikethrough get through. git log -S shows both sets of rules arrived together in 3513c94, so the feature has never worked.
v1.correction: A further correction: `.scm-name.git-ignored` is not covered by line 38, though ignored files are filtered out of SCM lists anyway. Status still reaches the user through the badge and letter labels, which is why this is medium rather than high. The fix is as proposed: drop `color: @ink` from `.tree-name` and `.scm-name` (button.tree-row and button.scm-open already set ink), or raise the specificity of the status selectors.

findings.title: Notes menu bar (and tab arrows, task disclosures) styled with GTK node names GTK 4 never creates: `popovermenubar`, `header > arrow`, `expander`
findings.evidence: notes.css:9-12 style `.notes-chrome popovermenubar` and `popovermenubar > item` (including :hover/:selected). The widget is `gtk::PopoverMenuBar::from_model` (note_pages/menu.rs:394, mounted by notes_window.rs:40), and its CSS node is `menubar`. Gtk-4.0.gir says "GtkPopoverMenuBar has a single CSS node with name menubar", and a GTK 4.22 process returns `get_css_name()` = 'menubar'. The same mistake appears in four more places. (1) notes.css:77 `notebook.notes-tabs > header > arrow`: GTK 4 puts scroll arrows under `tabs` (`header > tabs > arrow`), and note_pages.rs:486 turns `set_scrollable(true)` on. (2) notes.css:95 `.notes-scroll > viewport`: the scroller wraps a sourceview5::View, which is Scrollable, so no viewport exists (doc.rs:148-163). (3) theme.css:489 `.task-relations expander` matches the *arrow* node of each gtk::Expander (task_pages.rs:915), because GTK 4's tree is `expander-widget > box > title > expander`; and theme.css:490 `expander > title` can never match. (4) theme.css:255/391 use `searchentry`, but GtkSearchEntry's node is `entry` (confirmed in GTK 4.22); these are also counted in the dead-CSS finding.
findings.impact: The Notes window is presented at every launch (app.rs:366 → notes_window.rs:165). Its File/Edit/Search/View bar never gets the intended transparent bar, flat 30px items, 12px/500 secondary text or @wash hover. The desktop GTK theme's `menubar`/`item` rules (padding, accent highlight, any rule line) apply instead, inside Relay's console titlebar. With many open tabs, the notebook scroll arrows also keep the theme's styling. In task details, each disclosure triangle gets 6px of vertical padding instead of the row.
findings.fix: Rename the selectors: `.notes-chrome menubar`, `.notes-chrome menubar > item` (with :hover/:selected), and `notebook.notes-tabs > header > tabs > arrow`. Drop `> viewport` from notes.css:95. Change theme.css:489-490 to `.task-relations expander-widget` and `.task-relations expander-widget > box > title`. Delete the `searchentry` rules.

v1.reason: The installed Gtk-4.0.gir (GTK 4.22.5) confirms every node name. `GtkPopoverMenuBar has a single CSS node with name menubar` (line 109579), so `.notes-chrome popovermenubar` and `popovermenubar > item` at notes.css:9-11 never match. The widget is gtk::PopoverMenuBar::from_model (note_pages/menu.rs:394), mounted in the notes-chrome CenterBox (notes_window.rs:40). In the GtkNotebook node tree, `[arrow]` sits under `header > tabs`, so notes.css:77 `header > arrow` matches nothing; the notebook is scrollable (note_pages.rs:486). The GtkExpander tree is `expander-widget > box > title > expander`. So theme.css:489 `.task-relations expander` pads the arrow node, and :490 `expander > title` never matches; the widgets are created at task_pages.rs:915 inside `side` (class task-relations, task_pages.rs:901). GtkSearchEntry's node is `entry` (gir line 126401), so `.document-library searchentry` (theme.css:255, 391) is dead. notes.css:95 `> viewport` is dead because app::scrolled wraps a Scrollable sourceview5::View, so no viewport is inserted. All of these selectors are wrong.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low. The consequence is purely cosmetic: the theme's default menubar item padding and hover apply instead of the flat 30px items, and the notebook arrows and expander padding are unstyled. No behaviour or information is lost. The rename fixes are correct as proposed.

findings.title: Bundled Medium/SemiBold fonts are unreachable from CSS weights: Fira Mono 500/600 render Regular on this machine, and without system Fira every weight collapses
findings.symbol: fonts::install register! list / font-weight in theme CSS
findings.evidence: fonts.rs:21-30 registers the fontsource subsets unchanged, and resources/fonts/README.md confirms the naming tables were not edited. fontconfig (fc-scan) therefore sees one family per weight. fira-sans-latin-500 is family 'Fira Sans Medium' and 600 is 'Fira Sans SemiBold'. fira-mono-latin-500 is 'Fira Mono Medium'. Condensed 500/600 are 'Fira Sans Condensed Medium'/'… SemiBold'. Only the Condensed *700* file has family 'Fira Sans Condensed'. The CSS requests weights inside the base families: `'Fira Sans'` at 500/600 (theme.css:25 buttons, :48 session names), `'Fira Sans Condensed'` at 600 (theme.css:20 section labels, board.css:47 lane titles) and `'Fira Mono'` at 500/600 (git_files.css:66 `.tree-badge`, :102 `.git-branch-name`, :199 `.scm-letter`, theme.css:323 `.notification-count`, tools.css:137/143, usage.css:59). Fontconfig matches the family name first. I reproduced this with Pango 1.58 and explicit family+weight descriptions, as GTK builds them. With this machine's real font set plus the app's registered files, 'Fira Mono' 500 and 600 resolve to the Regular face; this machine has no system Fira Mono. With a private FONTCONFIG_FILE that sees only the bundled files, 'Fira Sans' 500/600 resolve to Regular, and 'Fira Sans Condensed' 400/500/600 all resolve to the Bold face. The system ttf-fira-sans package installed here hides the Sans/Condensed part. No italic face is bundled, so the italic rules (guardrails.css:13, git_files.css:68) get synthesized obliques.
findings.impact: On the author's machine, every medium/semibold Fira Mono label renders Regular: git status letters and badges, notification counts, branch names, usage percentages. On any machine without system Fira fonts, which is the case bundling exists for, every 500/600 Fira Sans weight renders Regular and every condensed caption renders Bold. The type hierarchy in DESIGN.md is lost. The smoke assertion (smoke.rs:62-69) only loads 'Fira Mono 10' at weight 400, so it cannot catch this.
findings.fix: Give the bundled files typographic names: with fontTools, set name IDs 1/2 (or 16/17) to 'Fira Sans' + 'Medium'/'SemiBold' etc., or ship the upstream Fira TTFs, which carry these names. Alternatively, install an app fontconfig scan-time rule that maps the per-weight families back to the base family. Extend the smoke font check to assert a 600 Sans, a 600 Condensed and a 500 Mono face.

v1.reason: fonts.rs:21-30 registers the eight fontsource files unchanged, and resources/fonts/README.md says the naming tables were not edited. fc-scan on the bundled files reports the family names 'Fira Mono Medium', 'Fira Sans Medium', 'Fira Sans SemiBold', 'Fira Sans Condensed Medium' and 'Fira Sans Condensed SemiBold'. Only the Condensed 700 file is named 'Fira Sans Condensed', and its style is Bold. fontconfig binds family before weight. With a private FONTCONFIG_FILE that sees only the bundled directory, 'Fira Mono' at weight 100 or 180 and 'Fira Sans' at 100 or 180 all match Regular (weight 80), and 'Fira Sans Condensed' at 80 or 180 matches the Bold face. This machine has no system Fira Mono: fc-list shows none, and fc-match falls back to Noto Sans Mono. The bundled Regular is therefore the only 'Fira Mono' face, and every 500/600 Fira Mono rule renders Regular. The system Fira Sans and Fira Sans Condensed installs hide the Sans and Condensed half on this machine only. fontconfig's synthetic-emboldening rule does not fire below bold, so 500/600 are not even faked. Pango's add_font_file uses the same fontconfig matching.
v1.correction: The impact is visual only (lost weight hierarchy) but appears in normal use, so medium is fair. A further detail: the Condensed 700 face is reached only because its family name happens to be the base family. The fix stands: rename the families (name IDs 1/2 or 16/17) with fontTools, or ship the upstream TTFs. Extend smoke.rs to assert a 500 Mono face, a 600 Sans face and a 600 Condensed face.

findings.title: About a fifth of theme.css is dead: 63 of its 283 classes are never applied, so 97 of 459 rules can never match
findings.evidence: I cross-referenced every class selector in all ten stylesheets against quoted strings in apps/relay-native/src, excluding smoke tests, `has_css_class` reads and `set_widget_name`; format!-built status-/priority-/state-/label-hue-/pr- classes were checked against their value sets. Per file: theme.css has 63 of 283 classes that nothing adds, leaving 97 rules fully dead and 3 partially (86 `.session-identity`, 201 `.page.skills-page`, 203 `.skills-head .title`). mirror, git_files, board, sessions, workspace, guardrails, usage and tools have 0 unapplied classes. notes.css has 0, but 4 of its rules are dead because of the node-name mistakes reported separately. The theme.css blocks: (1) The pre-KWrite Notes UI (`.notes-app-*`, `.notes-workspace`, `.document-*`, `.plan-text`, `.plan-placeholder`, `.notes-window-chrome`, lines 248-273, 388-393, 423-424, 455-461, 479-480, 483-484, 500, 502), left when commit 6bbd432 rewrote Notes without touching theme.css. (2) The old Skills/Plugins pages (`.skills-*`, `.skill-pick`, `.skill-switch`, `.plugins-content`, `.plugin-card`/`-section`, lines 216-227, 372, 387, 396, 492-493, 504-505), left by 280ae4b. (3) The files rail removed in 54e6bbc (183-186). (4) Code publish steps (399-403). (5) The old board lens and card parts (93, 97-98, 231-232, 238-242, 419, 436, 451); `task-title` is only a widget name (task_pages.rs:537). (6) `.layout-menu` (78-79), `.project-branch` (73), `.session-lane` (182), `.code-file-name` (281) and `.code-section-heading` (283). Some selectors also target widgets that are no longer built: `.topbar windowcontrols …` (37-38, 91-92; the app builds its own `.window-control` keys, app.rs:454), `.statusbar .statusbar` (108; there is one statusbar, app.rs:679) and `.code-folder > box > title` (282; folders are buttons, editor.rs:754).
findings.impact: Edits to these rules silently do nothing, and they add bulk to the single provider every widget is matched against. smoke.rs:75 still asserts a 28px width for `files-rail`, but no widget carries that class, so the check always passes.
findings.fix: Delete the listed rules; they belong to UIs already replaced by css/notes.css and css/tools.css. Remove the `files-rail` row from smoke.rs:72-77 or point it at a live class.

v1.reason: I checked this myself. app.rs:344-352 joins theme.css and the css/*.css files into one provider. I took every class selector in theme.css and searched the Rust sources under apps/relay-native/src for it as a quoted string. About 66 classes appear nowhere outside smoke.rs: the notes-app-*/notes-workspace/document-* family, plan-text and plan-placeholder, skills-*, skill-pick, skill-switch, plugin-card, plugin-section and plugins-content, files-rail and files-label, the code-step-*/code-publish-step classes, code-file-name, code-section-heading, layout-menu, project-branch, session-lane, session-identity, board-lens, lane-heading, wall-files-heading, and task-type/-tags/-open/-preview/-priority. That is in line with the auditor's count of 63. My raw list also included `titlebar`, but that one is a false positive: GTK adds the class when set_titlebar is called (app.rs:482, notes_window.rs:80). The format! calls that build names (tools_skills.rs:124/158/242, board_view.rs:1627 `lane-{column}`) produce widget names or other classes, none of these. The structural claims also hold. Nothing in the client builds a `windowcontrols` widget, so `.topbar windowcontrols …` (theme.css:37-38, 91-92) never matches. `statusbar` is added only once (app.rs:679), so `.statusbar .statusbar` (108) never matches. `code-folder` is put on a button (editor.rs:754), so `.code-folder > box > title` (282) does not match. `task-title` is only ever set as a widget name (task_pages.rs:537), so the theme.css:98 rule `.task-title` is dead; the rule at 239 is `button.task-title`, which is also class-based and also dead. The smoke.rs:72-89 loop asserts sizes only on widgets that carry the class. Since no widget has `files-rail`, the 28px width check at smoke.rs:75 never runs and the test passes without checking anything.
v1.correction: Lower the severity from medium to low. Unmatched CSS rules do not change what the user sees and cost almost nothing at runtime: GTK has to match roughly 100 extra selectors in one provider. The real cost is that edits to these rules silently do nothing, plus a smoke-test row that can never fail. The exact class count is about 63 to 66 depending on how GTK-provided classes are counted; it is not a precise 63. The proposed fix is right: delete the listed theme.css rules, and drop or retarget the files-rail row in smoke.rs:75. This is a change under apps/relay-native, which cannot be built in the agent environment (CLAUDE.md).

findings.title: 51 theme.css rules are fully overridden by later identical selectors, mostly re-declared in the area stylesheets, and the values have already diverged
findings.evidence: All ten files are concatenated into one provider (app.rs:344-355), so for identical selectors the later declaration wins. 51 theme.css rules have every property re-set later. The board block (230-243, 420-454) is overridden by board.css, the code block (276-285, 404-418) by git_files.css, the sidebar rules (69-72, 173-179, 494-495) by workspace.css, lines 23, 45, 143-144 and 426 by usage.css, and line 485 by notes.css. Several values already disagree. `.usage-meter.hot progress` is @waiting at theme.css:426 but @held at usage.css:33. `.task-rollup progressbar progress` is @secondary at 440 but @live at board.css:79. `.board-group-heading` is @secondary/11px at 420 but @faint/10.5px at board.css:56. `.code-commit-message` has an @edge border and 52px at 406, but @strong and 46px at git_files.css:143. `.board-drag-rail` is solid @edge at 421 but dashed @strong at board.css:37. `.project-row .manage` has opacity 0 with a hover reveal at 176-177, but opacity 1 at workspace.css:22. findings.title: relay-editor.xml inherits Adwaita-dark's language-specific styles, so Rust attributes, macros, paths and lifetimes (and CSS/XML/diff/Python tokens) bypass the Relay palette
findings.evidence: The scheme declares `parent-scheme="Adwaita-dark"`. GtkSourceView looks up a token's own style id (for example `rust:attribute`) in the scheme and then in its parent before it falls back to the language's `map-to` chain. rust.lang maps `attribute`, `macro` and `scope` to `def:preprocessor`, and `lifetime` to `rust:keyword`. Adwaita-dark defines `rust:attribute`, `rust:macro`, `rust:scope` and `rust:lifetime` itself (plus css:*, xml:*, diff:*, python:*, c:*, go:*), so those win over line 25's `def:preprocessor #c979d6`. Styles the scheme never defines also come from Adwaita-dark. I verified this with GtkSourceView 5.20 on the substituted relay-matte scheme: rust:attribute and rust:macro → #7D8AC7; rust:scope and rust:lifetime → #FFA348; def:constant → #7D8AC7; def:special-char → #F66151; def:heading → #33B2A4 bold; def:link-text → #ED333B; def:note → #3D3D3D on #F5C211; css:property-name → #FF7800; diff:added-line → #33B2A4.
findings.impact: In the Code editor (editor.rs:86-92, 199), every Rust file (the repo's main language) shows `#[derive]`, `format!`/`vec!`, `std::` paths and lifetimes in Adwaita periwinkle and orange. Those hues are absent from the SYN_MATTE palette that the header comment (line 2) promises. Markdown files get Adwaita's teal headings and red links, and TODO/FIXME notes get a yellow block background.
findings.fix: Add entries that re-point the parent's language styles, e.g. `<style name="rust:attribute" use-style="def:preprocessor"/>` (likewise for rust:macro and rust:scope) and `<style name="rust:lifetime" use-style="def:keyword"/>`. I verified this resolves to #c979d6. Do the same for the css/xml/diff/python ids, and define the def:* styles the palette should own: constant, special-constant, special-char, heading, link-text, inline-code, note, list-marker, preformatted-section and net-address. Alternatively, drop the parent and define the few global styles yourself (search-match, bracket-match).

v1.reason: resources/relay-editor.xml:3 declares `parent-scheme="Adwaita-dark"` and defines only def:* and global styles. I extracted the installed libgtksourceview-5 Adwaita-dark.xml resource. It defines `rust:attribute` and `rust:macro` as violet_2 (#7D8AC7), `rust:scope` and `rust:lifetime` as orange_2 (#FFA348), plus css:*, xml:*, diff:*, python:* and c:* ids. It also sets def:constant, def:heading (teal_3 bold), def:link-text (red_2), def:note (yellow background) and def:special-char, none of which the Relay scheme overrides. GtkSourceView resolves a context's own style id through the scheme and its parent before following the language's map-to fallback. So these ids take Adwaita's hues instead of falling back to the Relay def:preprocessor or def:keyword colours. editor.rs:86-92 applies this scheme to every file opened in the Code editor, Rust included. The effect is cosmetic: off-palette colours.
v1.correction: The same `parent-scheme="Adwaita-dark"` inheritance is in NOTES_SCHEME (note_pages.rs:111-113). That scheme does override def:heading, list-marker and inline-code, but it still inherits the language-specific ids. Apply the same fix to both schemes.

findings.title: Colour literals bypass the @define-color tokens: a second status palette in git_files.css, matte-only copies in theme.css, and a fixed Notes paper colour duplicated in Rust
findings.symbol: git status / PR / diff colours, @notes_paper, theme literals
findings.evidence: git_files.css repeats literal status colours instead of tokens. #f0786f appears 5 times (35 `.git-conflict`, 92 `.image-hover-meta.error`, 139 `button.branch-delete:hover`, 212 `.scm-tag.pr-closed`, 246 `.diff-minus`), #73c991 3 times (32, 209, 245), #c9a24c 3 times (9, 222, 239) and #6c6c70 twice (36, 38). Its error red and success green differ from @held (#e5382e) and @live (#2ec469), and the PR chips mix both systems in one widget: `.scm-tag.pr-open { background: alpha(@live, 0.16); color: #73c991; }`, `.pr-closed { background: alpha(@held, 0.16); color: #f0786f; }`. theme.css hard-codes the matte token values: `.statusbar separator { background: #37373c }` (81, = @strong), `.lamp { border: 1px solid #77777a }` (83, = @faint) and `.task-card:hover { border-color: #37373c }` (95). notes.css:4 `@define-color notes_paper #0c0c0e` is the same in every appearance mode and is copied 4 times into NOTES_SCHEME (note_pages.rs:113-119). notes.css:16 colours the Notes close key #c42b1c/white, while the main window uses @held/@ink (theme.css:316). tools.css:73 uses #c4c4c2. relay-editor.xml repeats token values as literals (#ececea ink, #77777a faint, #a5a5a3 secondary, #e5382e held), and its per-mode backgrounds live in fonts.rs:36-40, separately from shell.rs:1141-1153's palettes. Conversely, shell.rs:1206 defines `@backbox`, which no stylesheet references.
findings.impact: Dark and OLED modes swap the tokens (shell.rs:1141-1153) but not these literals. Separators, lamp rings, the Notes paper and the editor's line numbers and cursor keep their matte values. Changing one status colour means finding up to five copies across CSS and Rust. Two different error reds appear side by side: an image-preview error in #f0786f next to notices in @held.
findings.fix: Add tokens in theme.css (e.g. `@define-color git_added #73c991; @define-color git_removed #f0786f; @define-color git_sha #c9a24c;`) and use them everywhere. Replace the theme.css literals with @strong/@faint. Derive notes_paper and the NOTES_SCHEME/relay-editor backgrounds from the active palette in one place. Drop the unused `backbox` definition.

v1.reason: The literals are where the finding says. git_files.css has #f0786f at 35/92/139/212/246, #73c991 at 32/209/245 and #6c6c70 at 36/38. At 209 and 212, the PR chips mix `alpha(@live/@held)` backgrounds with the literal text colours. theme.css:81, 83 and 95 hard-code the matte values of @strong and @faint (#37373c, #77777a). The palette in shell.rs:1141-1153 swaps those tokens per mode: dark uses #33363d/#70747b and oled uses #333336/#77777a. notes.css:4 fixes notes_paper at #0c0c0e, and NOTES_SCHEME repeats that value. shell.rs:1206 defines `@backbox`, which no stylesheet references; only `backbox_chrome` is used, in usage.css:46. The maintainability cost is real but small.
v1.correction: The visual impact is smaller than claimed. The per-mode differences for the theme.css literals are a few RGB units (#37373c vs #33363d/#333336; #77777a is identical in oled). So 'keep their matte values' is technically true but barely visible. #c9a24c at git_files.css:9 is the `.ft-json` file-type tint, not a git or status colour, so it does not belong in the status-palette count. The Notes scheme's comment says it deliberately uses 'the Code editor's matte palette'. A fixed Notes paper may be intended; only the duplication is clearly a cost. The cheap, clear wins are to drop the dead `backbox` definition and replace theme.css:81/83/95 with @strong/@faint.

findings.title: The Notes find bar's whole-word key is never underlined: `text-decoration` on the button doesn't reach its label
findings.evidence: The rule is `button.notes-find-word { text-decoration: underline; }`. The key is `gtk::ToggleButton::with_label("W")` (note_pages/doc.rs:84, 185-186), so its text is drawn by a child `label` node, and GTK 4 does not inherit text-decoration. Every other decoration rule in this codebase targets the label directly (board.css:27, board.css:70, git_files.css:37). I verified this in GTK 4.22: the W label's Pango attributes contain only line-height, while a directly targeted label (tree-name.git-deleted) gets a strikethrough.
findings.impact: The whole-words toggle renders as a plain 'W'. It loses the underline that distinguishes it from a letter key in the Aa / W / .* group.
findings.fix: Use `button.notes-find-word label { text-decoration-line: underline; }`.

v1.reason: notes.css:117 is `button.notes-find-word { text-decoration: underline; }`. The key comes from option_key (note_pages/doc.rs:83-89) as `gtk::ToggleButton::with_label("W")`, and doc.rs:185-186 adds the class, so a child GtkLabel draws the text. I ran a throwaway PyGObject test against the installed GTK 4.22.5 with the same two rules. A ToggleButton with `button.w { text-decoration: underline }` gave its label no Pango attributes. One with `button.x label { text-decoration-line: underline }` gave its label `underline single-line`. text-decoration is not inherited in GTK 4, so the W key renders without an underline. The other decoration rules in the codebase (board.css:27, :70, git_files.css:37) target the label or a label class directly.
v1.correction: Fix: `button.notes-find-word label { text-decoration-line: underline; }`. The impact is cosmetic: W loses the cue that it means whole word.

findings.title: Three diverged copies of the square switch style; the other three GtkSwitches fall back to the desktop theme
findings.evidence: Three scoped rule sets each restyle switches within one area. tools.css:159-167 (`.ext-page switch`): 32×16, off ground @screen, slider @faint, radius 2/0. workspace.css:72-75 (`.registry-editor switch`): 34×18, @screen, slider @secondary, radius 2/1. usage.css:75-78 (`.usage-options switch`): 30×16, @slab, slider @faint, radius 2/2. theme.css has no `switch` rule, so the switches at agent_menu.rs:510, guardrail_settings.rs:498 and shell.rs:858 keep the system theme's rounded switch.

findings.fix: Move one square-switch rule set into theme.css (`switch`, `switch:checked`, `switch > slider`, `switch > image`) and delete the three scoped copies.

v1.reason: Three scoped switch rule sets exist, and their values differ. tools.css:159-167 (`.ext-page switch`, set on tools_market.rs:131): 32x16, @screen ground, @faint slider, radius 0. workspace.css:72-75 (`.registry-editor switch`): 34x18, @screen, @secondary slider, radius 1px. usage.css:75-78 (`.usage-options switch`): 30x16, @slab, @faint slider, radius 2px. Neither theme.css nor any other stylesheet has an unscoped `switch` rule. The switches at agent_menu.rs:510, guardrail_settings.rs:498 and shell.rs:858 sit outside those three containers, so they get the desktop theme's switch.
v1.correction: DESIGN.md does not name a switch rule. It says plates/records are square and keys use the small key radius (DESIGN.md:199), so the 'square-plate rule' is the auditor's reading, not the document's words. The real cost is visual inconsistency, plus a new scoped copy for every new switch area. The proposed fix of one global `switch` rule set in theme.css is right.

findings.title: Skills 'Remove' re-implements the inline confirm with its own `.ext-danger.armed` styling instead of `confirm_inline`/`.confirm-armed`
findings.evidence: tools_skills.rs:198-219 arms the key by hand: `key.set_label("Click again to remove"); key.add_css_class("armed")`, with its own 4s `timeout_add_local_once`. tools.css:105-109 styles it as a red-tinted outline. The shared helper `confirm_inline_if` (app.rs:104-200, CONFIRM_WINDOW = 4s) is styled by sessions.css:4-9 `.confirm-armed` (filled @held, white label) and is used by the other destructive keys (task_pages.rs:199, 1187; shell.rs:732). The helper keeps the key from shrinking (app.rs:159-160), disarms on focus-leave and Esc (app.rs:181-200) and resets the accessible label. The copy does none of this.
findings.impact: The same 'click again to confirm' state looks different on the Skills page (tinted outline) than everywhere else (solid red). The key also changes width when its label swaps, and Esc or clicking elsewhere does not cancel it.
findings.fix: Call `crate::app::confirm_inline(&remove, "Click again to remove", …)` and delete the `.armed` rules in tools.css:108-109. Keep the quiet hover tint if wanted.

v1.reason: tools_skills.rs (around lines 198-219) arms the Remove key by hand with an Rc<Cell<bool>>, a set_label swap, an `armed` class and its own 4s timeout_add_local_once. tools.css:108-109 styles that `.armed` state as a tinted outline with red text. The shared helper confirm_inline_if (app.rs ~104-200) does more. It keeps the key at least as wide as before (`key.set_size_request(key.width().max(..))`), disarms on focus-leave and on Esc, sets and resets the accessible label and tooltip, and uses a serial counter so a stale timer cannot disarm a newer arm. sessions.css:4-7 styles it as `.confirm-armed`, a solid @held fill with a white label. The copy has none of these behaviours and looks different, so the duplication has already diverged in a way the user can see.
v1.correction: Replace the hand-rolled arm with `crate::app::confirm_inline(&remove, "Click again to remove", move |key| ui.mutate("skill.delete", ..))` and delete tools.css:108-109. Keep the hover tint if wanted.

findings.title: DESIGN.md describes styling the CSS no longer implements (editor scheme/font, waiting lamps, focus and disabled keys, window controls, file rail, pills)
findings.evidence: Lines 140-142 say GtkSourceView uses "system monospace and the installed Adwaita-dark syntax scheme". The editor views actually carry `.code-source { font-family: 'Fira Mono' }` (theme.css:278, editor.rs:193/223) and load the shipped relay-{mode} scheme (fonts.rs:36-50, editor.rs:86-92). Line 121 says "Waiting lamps currently use secondary ink", but `.lamp.waiting` and `.lamp.starting` use @waiting (mirror.css:18, sessions.css:108). Line 210 describes "an inset 2px ink outline" and "45% opacity", but theme.css:27 sets `outline-offset: 0` (drawn outside the border) and theme.css:28 sets `button:disabled { opacity: 0.4 }`; other disabled rules use 0.32, 0.45 and 0.55. Line 220 says "GTK owns window controls and menus", but the app draws custom `.window-control` keys (theme.css:313-316) and styles the Notes chrome and menus (notes.css:14-28). Lines 166-167 describe a collapsible file rail beside the wall, which commit 54e6bbc removed; its CSS is dead (theme.css:183-186). Lines 233-234 give board lanes 4px padding, but `.board-cards` has 8px (board.css:51). Line 282 says "Don't add … pill surfaces", but guardrails.css:38 and :40 use `border-radius: 99px` keys and sessions.css:56 rounds the lease card to 8px.
findings.impact: Future agents are told to follow DESIGN.md. Stale statements lead to "fixes" that undo intentional choices, or to new code copying superseded rules.
findings.fix: Update these sentences to match the implemented values, or change the CSS where the document is the intended truth (for example, unify disabled opacity). Record the guardrail prompt's deliberate rounding as an explicit exception.

v1.reason: I checked each claim against the code. DESIGN.md:141-143 says GtkSourceView uses system monospace and the installed Adwaita-dark scheme. In fact theme.css:278 sets `.code-source { font-family: 'Fira Mono' }`, and fonts.rs:36-50 writes relay-{matte,dark,oled}.xml, which editor.rs:86-92 then loads. DESIGN.md:121 says waiting lamps use secondary ink, but mirror.css:18 and sessions.css:108 paint `.lamp.waiting`/`.lamp.starting` with @waiting. DESIGN.md:220 says GTK owns window controls, yet app.rs:446-454 builds custom `.window-control` keys that theme.css:313-316 styles. DESIGN.md:166-167 describes a files rail. No Rust code adds `files-rail`, so theme.css:183-186 is dead and the only reference left is a check in smoke.rs:75 that never runs. v1.correction: The line numbers are slightly off: the window-controls statement is at DESIGN.md:220 and the focus/disabled statement at :209-210. smoke.rs:75 still asserts geometry for `files-rail`; the class never matches, so that check is vacuous now. Remove it together with the dead theme.css:183-186 rules.

findings.title: Smoke harness compiled into relay-native acts on whatever engine it reaches; only env vars gate it, and run.sh's partial scrub points it at the live engine
findings.evidence:
main.rs:10-14 declares `mod roadmap_smoke; mod smoke; mod smoke_project_files; mod smoke_registry;` with no cfg or feature. app.rs:368 calls `crate::smoke::install(&ui)` on every activation, and the only gate is `let Ok(path) = std::env::var("RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT") else { return; };` (smoke.rs:452). Nothing checks which engine `ui.path` points at before acting.

With RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE=1 the page path does the following:
- At 1 s, `verify_terminal_input` (smoke.rs:507-510, app.rs:1616-1621) calls `pane.terminal.paste_text(&format!("native-paste-check-{name}\n"))` on every pane, which terminal.rs:219-241 forwards as `session.input`.
- `edit_fixture` renames `tasks[0]` (smoke.rs:333, 400-411).
- It also overwrites `notes[0]`'s body with 'Native note save verified.' and saves via notes.save (smoke.rs:339, 381-386, 413-416).
- Or, on the launch page, it creates a task and launches a review group (smoke.rs:341-366).
- On page=code it inserts '\nNative editor save verified.\n' into README.md and saves (smoke.rs:709-714, editor.rs:606-611).
- On page=settings it writes terminal.font_size 9.75, appearance.panel_alpha 0.96 and the global guardrail destructive_write.min_removed_pct 62.5, and never restores them (smoke.rs:144-157).

Without FIXTURE:
- page=project-launch clicks Start (smoke.rs:571-585).
- The setup '*-submit' pages click setup-add (smoke.rs:536-568, 660-671).

Roadmap branch:
- It only asserts `fixture && RELAY_INSTANCE == "test"` (smoke.rs:476), yet README.md:22 documents `./run.sh test` as an ordinary persistent instance, with data in ~/.local/share/relay-v4/test.
- smoke_registry.rs:45 and roadmap_smoke.rs:59-62 also require `ui.path.starts_with(std::env::temp_dir())`.
- smoke_notes.rs:39-43 and smoke_project_files.rs:84-88/269-273 check env vars only. The 'files' part edits and saves the project's README.md and writes preview.PNG and broken.png into the project root; the 'lifecycle' part creates and spawns five `claude` sessions.

run.sh:12 runs only `unset RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET` ('Never inherit a stale screenshot/test socket'), so SCREENSHOT, FIXTURE, PAGE and ROADMAP pass through to the real app.
findings.fix:
Make isolation one precondition in `install`: before arming any page, fixture or roadmap action, require `ui.path.starts_with(std::env::temp_dir())`, which all four driver scripts already satisfy, and exit with an error otherwise. Then drop the per-part env-only checks.

Have run.sh also `unset RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE RELAY_NATIVE_PAGE RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP RELAY_NATIVE_BURST`. test-launcher-real.py already pops FIXTURE and PAGE and only needs SCREENSHOT and VERIFY_CONNECTION.

Longer term, put the harness modules and the verify_* helpers behind a `smoke` cargo feature that only the scripts enable.

v1.reason:
main.rs:10-14 declares mod roadmap_smoke/smoke/smoke_project_files/smoke_registry with no cfg. smoke::install (smoke.rs:451-454) is gated only by `std::env::var("RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT")`. The socket comes from app.rs:313-319: RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET, or else $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay-v4/{instance}.sock, which is the live engine.

With FIXTURE=1 the page path takes these actions with no isolation check:
- verify_terminal_input (app.rs:1616-1621) pastes `native-paste-check-{name}\n` into every pane.
- edit_fixture (smoke.rs:325-416) does one of the following: renames tasks[0] and saves it through draft-save; overwrites notes[0]'s body and runs notes.save; or creates a task and clicks launch-start.
- verify_settings_save (smoke.rs:131-157) sets the global guardrail destructive_write.min_removed_pct to 62.5 and saves it.

Without FIXTURE, project-launch and setup-*-submit still click Start or Add.

The roadmap branch (smoke.rs:476) asserts only FIXTURE plus RELAY_INSTANCE==test. smoke_notes.rs:39-43 and smoke_project_files.rs:84-88/269-273 check env vars only. smoke_registry.rs:45 and roadmap_smoke.rs:59-62 additionally require ui.path under temp_dir().

run.sh:11-12 unsets only RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET and exports RELAY_INSTANCE from its argument. So `./run.sh test`, run in a shell with ROADMAP and FIXTURE exported, satisfies the env-only checks against the persistent test instance.

Every driver script puts its socket under a tempfile dir: native-smoke.py:29/63, native-setup-smoke.py:16/50, perf/native-baseline.py:131/145, and test-launcher-real.py's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. So a single temp_dir precondition in install would not break them.

The trigger needs a developer or agent to run the binary with harness env vars set. That is not normal use, which keeps this at medium.
v1.correction: verify_note_tools (note_pages.rs:1178) is pure asserts and does no writes. Keep SCREENSHOT/VERIFY_CONNECTION passing through run.sh, because test-launcher-real.py:20-36 depends on it; unset only FIXTURE/PAGE/ROADMAP/BURST there. The temp_dir precondition in install is the real fix.

findings.title: The five roadmap regression suites never run in the documented smoke; only an undocumented, mutually exclusive RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY reaches them
findings.symbol: native-smoke.py roadmap branch / smoke::install roadmap dispatch
findings.evidence:
native-smoke.py:127-143 reads `if os.environ.get("RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY"): for part in ...split(","): ... RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP=part ...` and ends with `raise SystemExit(0)`. When the variable is set, the 18 page captures are skipped. When it is unset, no roadmap part runs.

README.md:59-66 'Verify' runs a plain `python3 scripts/native-smoke.py`. smoke.rs:475-504 dispatches notes, files, lifecycle, registry and tools only from RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP.

rg over README, CLAUDE.md, docs/ and .github finds RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY and the part names only inside the script. outputs/native-roadmap-results.md:58 reports these regressions 'passed' but gives no command.

CI cannot build relay-native. RELAY_NATIVE_VERIFY_CONTRAST (smoke.rs:736) is likewise set by no script.
findings.fix: Run the roadmap parts in the default native-smoke.py run against the same fixture engine, after the page captures, and fail on a missing ROADMAP_OK line. Keep RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY only as a filter. List the part names in README's Verify section.

v1.reason: Checked independently. scripts/native-smoke.py:127-143 runs the roadmap parts only when `os.environ.get("RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY")` is set. Each part is launched with `RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP=part`, the script asserts `ROADMAP_OK={part}`, and the branch ends in `raise SystemExit(0)`. So when the variable is set, the 18 page captures, the burst check and the final save, paste and survival assertions are all skipped. When it is unset, no roadmap part runs. apps/relay-native/src/smoke.rs:475-504 is the only consumer of RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP. It dispatches notes, files, lifecycle, registry and tools to notes::run, smoke_project_files::run, smoke_project_files::profile_lifecycle, smoke_registry::run and roadmap_smoke::run. A repo-wide rg (hidden files included, target and relay-mobile excluded) finds RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY and RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP only in the script and in smoke.rs. Nothing in README, docs, CLAUDE.md or .github mentions them. README.md:59-66 'Verify' documents a plain `python3 scripts/native-smoke.py`. Its prose (README:76-79) describes only captures, saves, the review-group launch and the eleven-session burst. outputs/native-roadmap-results.md:56 says the 'Dedicated Notes/task, launch/Settings/Skills/wallpaper, registry drag/drop, and Files/Git interaction regressions passed' but gives no command. RELAY_NATIVE_VERIFY_CONTRAST (smoke.rs:736) is likewise set by nothing in the repo. Severity stays medium: there is no runtime impact, but CI cannot build relay-native, so these suites are the native client's only regression coverage for the behaviours they pin. Following the documented verification never runs them, so they can rot or miss regressions unnoticed.
v1.correction: The results file's 'passed' line is at outputs/native-roadmap-results.md:56, not :58. The proposed fix needs a caveat. The roadmap parts mutate the fixture engine: registry removal, file move/rename/trash, and a launch scenario that can create sessions. If they run right after the page captures, they would break the default run's later assertions: `len(live) == 9` and the 5/4 builder/reviewer split around line 181, the README.md 'Native editor save verified.' check, and the burst and paste checks. Run them after all the default assertions have completed, or against a fresh fixture engine and repository, and fail on a missing ROADMAP_OK line. Keep RELAY_SMOKE_ROADMAP_ONLY as a filter, and document the part names and RELAY_NATIVE_VERIFY_CONTRAST in README's Verify section (or have the script set the contrast variable on one capture).

findings.title: No harness drives the native guardrail decision UI (Allow once / Reject / Approve once or session / Deny / Revoke), although the fixture already creates a hold
findings.symbol: smoke::install page dispatch; guardrail_pages hold and exception cards

v1.reason:
native-smoke.py:107-113 creates exactly one held write and only counts holds over the bus. 'guardrails' is in the screenshot page list (native-smoke.py:146), but it falls through to navigate() at smoke.rs:697. edit_fixture handles only board/notes/launch (smoke.rs:698). No smoke or roadmap module touches hold, confirm, reject or grant: rg finds only the threshold field in verify_settings_save.

The untested client handlers exist as described:
- Allow, kept insensitive until Review (guardrail_pages.rs:276-311): guardrail.confirm {hold_id}.
- Reject: guardrail.reject at :380.
- Approve once/session (:445-477): the scope comes from the array `[(&once,"once"),(&always,"session")]`.

I read these handlers and found no bug in them. Engine semantics, such as hold resolution and grant scope, are covered in relay-core tests, and the engine is the authority, so a client bug cannot widen a grant beyond what the user's click requested. With no demonstrated defect, this is a coverage gap on a short, readable code path, so I rate it low rather than medium.
v1.correction: Severity low: this is a coverage gap with no defect found. The 'Allow insensitive until review' rule is enforced only in the client, which a UI test would pin down. That is the most valuable assertion to add.

findings.title: Fixed sleeps stand in for synchronization throughout the harness and are followed by hard asserts, so a loaded machine produces false failures
findings.evidence:
- smoke.rs:162: `glib::timeout_add_local_once(Duration::from_millis(900), ...)` then `assert!(ui.pages["settings"].is_sensitive(), "Settings save must finish")`. The Settings save issues one sequential `settings.set` per `setting:` widget (tools_settings.rs:143-149), with the guardrail save running alongside.
- smoke.rs:477: every roadmap part starts after a fixed 2 s. smoke_registry.rs:48 then does `ui.workspaces.borrow()[0]`, which panics if the initial refresh hasn't landed; roadmap_smoke.rs:69 calls `.expect("Fixture workspace")`.
- smoke.rs:350: 700 ms before unwrapping the launch form or task/note editors.
- smoke.rs:554/557, 578, 601, 632/642/652/661: 100/700, 700, 700, 100/500/250/1000 ms before asserting setup, launch and device controls.
- smoke.rs:705: `verify_burst(false)` asserts all 11 panes are attached 500 ms after navigation (app.rs:1634, terminal.rs:316-321).
- smoke.rs:712: `verify_save` asserts `!self.busy` 500 ms after the README read started.
- smoke_registry.rs:24-26 `settle()` sleeps 400 ms. The drop needs ui.projects refreshed, and the order check needs the drop handler's sequential project.update calls to have finished (shell.rs:104-127).
- smoke_notes.rs:227: 500 ms for a 300 ms debounce plus settings.set (notes_window.rs:123-124).
- smoke_project_files.rs:151-165: the coalescing check waits 1250 ms after the save, against a 125 ms engine debounce (watch.rs:120) and a 1000 ms client debounce (editor.rs:514).

v1.reason:
The fixed delays are real and are followed by hard asserts or unwraps:
- smoke.rs:162 waits 900 ms, then asserts "Settings save must finish".
- smoke.rs:477 waits 2 s before every roadmap part; smoke_registry.rs:48 then indexes `ui.workspaces.borrow()[0]`.
- smoke.rs:350 waits 700 ms, then unwraps the launch-form widgets.
- smoke.rs:705 waits 500 ms, then verify_burst asserts readiness.
- smoke_registry.rs:24 settle() is a 400 ms sleep.
- smoke_project_files.rs:151-165 runs the coalescing check after a fixed 1250 ms wait.
The coalescing race is mechanically possible. Editor::invalidate (editor.rs:508-529) arms a 1000 ms timer only when none is pending. If the save's own file.changed event (125 ms engine debounce) arrives late, the 20 invalidates join that earlier timer, and tree_revision moves before the 250 ms check. A wait_for poll helper already exists in smoke_project_files.rs and smoke_notes.rs, so the fix is cheap.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low. The harness cannot build or run in CI (CLAUDE.md), and runs by hand on the developer's machine, so the cost is an occasional false failure and a re-run. Nothing in the git history shows a flake actually happening, and the timing margins (for example 900 ms for a few local settings.set calls) are usually generous. Poll the same way the existing wait_for helper does, as the finding suggests.

findings.title: Confirmation and settings-save checks run in detached futures the run never waits for, so a hang passes
findings.evidence:
verify_confirmations is `glib::spawn_future_local(async move { for accept in [false, true] { ... assert_eq!(panel.response("Confirm").await, accept); ... } println!("In-app confirmation accept and cancel verified"); })` (smoke.rs:426-448).

The screenshot timer at `duration` (smoke.rs:724-808) closes the window regardless. The main close handler (app.rs:1032-1072) tears everything down and the app exits 0, dropping pending futures.

native-smoke.py:173-178 checks only 'Shell layouts verified' and GTK log noise. It never checks 'In-app confirmation accept and cancel verified' or 'Settings save verified across categories...' (smoke.rs:183).

edit_fixture's loop over toplevels (smoke.rs:369-420) silently does nothing if the editor field hasn't appeared after 700 ms.
findings.impact:
Trigger: a regression in Panel::close that stops running its `closed` callbacks (panel.rs:255-282). `response()` then never resolves on the cancel case, so verify_confirmations never reaches an assert. The 8 s screenshot closes the window, the process exits 0, and native-smoke.py passes.

The same applies elsewhere:
- verify_settings_save's round-trip asserts are skipped if its three bus reads stall past the 5 s close;
- a skipped board-compact edit is masked by the end-of-script `any(...)` title check (native-smoke.py:188), which the other board run satisfies.
findings.fix: Have the screenshot step wait for these verifications, for example by setting a completion flag that the capture loop polls before saving, or have native-smoke.py require their success lines in the relevant page logs. Make edit_fixture panic when the field never appears.

v1.reason: verify_confirmations (smoke.rs:425-448, called at line 524 only for the agents page) runs in a detached spawn_future_local. Panel::response awaits `recv.recv().await.unwrap_or(false)` (panel.rs:312). If close() stopped draining `closed` callbacks, the `send` held in that callback would never fire or drop, the future would block forever, and no assert would run. The installed panic hook only catches panics, not futures that never finish. The screenshot timer closes the window at `duration` regardless, and native-smoke.py:175 requires only "Shell layouts verified". It never looks for "In-app confirmation accept and cancel verified" or "Settings save verified across categories...". edit_fixture's toplevel loop (smoke.rs:369-420) ends silently if the field never appears. The end-of-run `any(...)` checks at native-smoke.py:188-189 are satisfied by either board run, so a skipped board-compact edit goes unnoticed.
v1.correction: Simplest fix: have native-smoke.py require each success line in the matching viewport log (agents: the confirmation line; settings: the settings-save line). Also make edit_fixture panic when its field is missing.

findings.title: Several negative checks wait less time than the behaviour they rule out, so they cannot fail
findings.evidence:
- smoke_notes.rs:171-179: `glib::timeout_future(Duration::from_millis(850)).await;` then `require(stored["body"] == "Ordinary Plan fixture", "Plan was silently autosaved")`, but the autosave timer is `Duration::from_millis(1500)` (note_pages/doc.rs:606).
- smoke_notes.rs:242-247 checks 'Refresh reopened a deliberately closed tab' 200 ms after `refresh_notes`, instead of waiting for `owner.renders` to increment as lines 208-210 do.
- tools_devices.rs:284-292, called from roadmap_smoke.rs:256, does `window.present()`, waits 100 ms, then `assert!(window.width() <= 430, ...)`. An unallocated window reports 0.
- smoke_project_files.rs:122-126 checks the window did not widen 80 ms after a click.
- smoke_project_files.rs:166-170 calls a 1.1 s sample 'must not poll when idle'.
- roadmap_smoke.rs:282-283 reads back `split.set_position(position + 40)` from GTK's own property.
findings.impact:
Each of these passes regardless of the regression it targets:
- If the `!super::prefs().autosave` guard in schedule_autosave (doc.rs:601) is dropped, the dirty Plan autosaves at 1500 ms, after the 850 ms check.
- If the Notes refresh takes more than 200 ms, the reopen check runs before the refresh lands.
- If the transient picker window is not allocated within 100 ms (a Wayland configure round trip under load), width() is 0 and the overflow assert holds whatever the content width.
- Any poll interval longer than 1.1 s goes unseen.
- The Paned read-back can only test GTK's setter.
findings.fix:
- Wait past the debounce (≥1.7 s), or assert the doc's autosave timer is unset.
- Wait for `owner.renders` to increase before the reopen check.
- Measure the picker with `picker.widget.measure(Horizontal, -1).0`, as roadmap_smoke.rs:301 does, rather than the window width.
- Assert the Paned allocation after a frame, or drop the read-back.

v1.reason:
The strongest case is solid. smoke_notes.rs:166-179 sets the body, closes the window, waits 850ms and asserts the stored body is unchanged. schedule_autosave (note_pages/doc.rs:597-606) arms a 1500ms timer, and the `!super::prefs().autosave` guard is at :601. If that guard regressed, the save would land at about 1500ms, after the check had already passed, so the check cannot catch it.

The Paned read-back is tautological: roadmap_smoke.rs:281-283 calls set_position(p+40) and immediately asserts position()==p+40.

The picker check (tools_devices.rs:283-292) asserts `window.width() <= 430` 100ms after present(). An unallocated GTK4 window reports 0, so if allocation has not happened the assertion passes trivially.
v1.correction:
'Cannot fail' is overstated for several items.
- The 200ms wait after refresh_notes (smoke_notes.rs:241-247) races only if notes.list on a local fixture engine takes more than about 200ms. That is unlikely, so it is weak rather than vacuous. Waiting on owner.renders, as at :208-210, is still the right fix.
- The 80ms width check and the 1.1s 'no idle poll' sample are bounded samples that could still catch a regression; they are not tautologies.

The autosave timing and the Paned read-back are the clear defects.

findings.title: Harness clicks call emit_clicked() directly, which runs handlers on disabled buttons, so disabled-control regressions pass
findings.impact:
Trigger: a regression that leaves `guardrail-save` disabled, for example breaking the `row.input.on_change` → `editor.refresh()` wiring at guardrail_settings.rs:575. Users can no longer save guardrail edits, yet verify_settings_save still sees 62.5 persisted (smoke.rs:179-182) and passes.

The launch fixture can likewise submit a half-loaded form that no user could submit.
findings.fix: Route every harness click through one helper that requires `is_sensitive() && is_mapped()`, as smoke_project_files::click already does, and use it in all five modules.

v1.reason: The gtk4 crate's ButtonExt::emit_clicked is `self.emit_by_name::<()>("clicked", &[])`, a raw signal emission, and GTK does not gate connected handlers on sensitivity. Production creates guardrail-save insensitive (guardrail_settings.rs:551) and enables it only in refresh() when dirty() > 0 (line 225). refresh() runs from the row.input.on_change hook (line 575ff). Editor::save() recomputes the patch from the widgets (line 354ff), so verify_settings_save (smoke.rs:148-152) would still persist 62.5 and pass even if that wiring broke and users could not click Save. The same raw emit is used for launch-start in edit_fixture (smoke.rs:362-366), draft-save (406-411), device-refresh (602-606) and setup-connect (653-657). By contrast, click_control/verify_pointer_target and smoke_project_files::click check is_sensitive().
v1.correction: Some raw-emit sites do check sensitivity first: project-launch asserts start.is_sensitive() before click_control. Only the sites listed above are blind. Fix: give one shared helper the sensitive-and-mapped check and use it everywhere.

findings.title: verify_burst hard-codes 11 panes, so the perf baseline's burst run (6 sessions) always panics
findings.evidence:
app.rs:1634 asserts `assert_eq!(self.panes.borrow().len(), 11);` and app.rs:1659 prints `println!("BURST_RENDERED=11");`. Both are reached from smoke.rs:706 and 749 whenever RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE=1 and RELAY_NATIVE_BURST=1.

native-smoke.py happens to build exactly 9+2 sessions. scripts/perf/native-baseline.py:190-193 creates six, then runs `open_page("agents-burst", "agents", {"RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE": "1", "RELAY_NATIVE_BURST": "1"}, ...)` (line 259).
findings.impact: The measurement documented in docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:563-567 ('once with the smoke harness's 2 048-line burst into every pane') can never be produced. About 2.5 s in, `assert_eq!(6, 11)` panics and the hook exits 1. The perf row then records exit 1 with counters sampled from a dead process.
findings.fix: Assert against `self.sessions.borrow().len()`, or an expected count passed in an env var, and print the actual count. Let native-smoke.py assert `BURST_RENDERED=11` itself.

v1.reason: app.rs:1634 begins verify_burst with `assert_eq!(self.panes.borrow().len(), 11);`, and app.rs:1659 prints a hard-coded `BURST_RENDERED=11`. smoke.rs:701-707 calls verify_burst(false) 500 ms after navigation whenever RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE=1 and RELAY_NATIVE_BURST=1. scripts/perf/native-baseline.py:190-193 creates and spawns only six sessions, then at line 259 opens agents with exactly those two env vars. The panic hook that install() sets up (smoke.rs: previous(info); process::exit(1)) turns the failed assert into exit 1 about 2.5 s in. 11 is right only for native-smoke.py: 9 live sessions (asserted at line 181) plus the 2 extra it spawns at lines 190-192, which is the count it checks at line 199. The burst row that docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:566-567 describes therefore can never be produced by this script.
v1.correction: Only the perf script's burst row is affected; the smoke harness itself passes. Fix: assert against the session count, or an expected count passed in an env var, and print the real count. native-smoke.py keeps its own `BURST_RENDERED=11` check.

findings.title: record_geometry's "plan" branch is unreachable since the Plan page was removed, and the perf script and its doc still list a plan page
findings.evidence:
smoke.rs:103-108: `if *ui.page.borrow() == "plan" { assert!(!widgets.iter().any(|w| w["name"] == "note-title"), ...) }`.

The only writer of `ui.page` is `navigate` (app.rs:1348), which first returns on `if self.content.child_by_name(page).is_none()` (app.rs:1319-1321). The content stack holds agents, board, modules, mailbox, guardrails, dashboard, settings, skills, plugins, notifications and devices (app.rs:618-642). Commit 54e6bbc removed 'plan'.

scripts/perf/native-baseline.py:35 still has "plan" in PAGES, and docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:564 lists it.
findings.impact: The assertion reads like coverage but can never execute. The perf baseline's 'plan' row silently measures whatever page was restored (agents) under a Plan label.
findings.fix: Delete the branch, and drop 'plan' from PAGES and from the baseline doc.

v1.reason: The content stack is built at app.rs:618-642 from agents, board, modules, mailbox, guardrails, dashboard, settings, skills, plugins, notifications and devices. notes is deliberately not added, and there is no plan page. navigate() returns at app.rs:1319-1321 when `content.child_by_name(page).is_none()`, before `*self.page.borrow_mut() = page.into()` at line 1348. So ui.page can never be "plan", and the branch at smoke.rs:103-108 is unreachable; no other code in apps/relay-native mentions a "plan" page. record_geometry's requested-page assert (smoke.rs:28-37) does not list plan, so the baseline's "plan" run (native-baseline.py:35) succeeds silently. It captures whatever page startup restored, under a Plan label, and docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:564 still lists plan.
v1.correction: Part of this is docs and script drift rather than dead code alone. Delete the branch, and drop "plan" from PAGES in native-baseline.py and from the baseline doc's page list.

findings.title: Harness helpers are copy-pasted per module and have drifted: named() five times, wait_for/require twice, three wait strategies, two error contracts
findings.evidence:
- An identical `fn named(root: &impl IsA<gtk::Widget>, name: &str)` appears in smoke.rs:11, smoke_notes.rs:8, smoke_project_files.rs:8, smoke_registry.rs:7 and roadmap_smoke.rs:9. smoke_notes is already a child module of smoke (`#[path = "smoke_notes.rs"] mod notes;` at smoke.rs:8-9).
- `wait_for` and `require` are duplicated in smoke_notes.rs:22-37 and smoke_project_files.rs:22-39.
- The wait strategies differ. roadmap_smoke.rs:24-32's `wait` polls 250×20 ms and panics. `wait_for` polls 160×25 ms and returns Err. smoke_registry.rs:24-26's `settle()` just sleeps 400 ms.
- The error contracts differ. roadmap_smoke::run panics on failure and returns the constant `json!({"launch_scope":true,...})` (roadmap_smoke.rs:512), which smoke.rs:484-488 wraps as `Ok(())`. The other parts return `Result`.
- note_pages.rs:1178-1203 `verify_tools` re-asserts list_enter, toggle_lines and parse_goto cases already covered by `#[test]`s in note_pages/text.rs:245-288, and does so at app start in the shipping binary.
findings.impact: Timeout and diagnostic fixes have to be made in five places, and they have already drifted: 4 s vs 5 s budgets, panic vs Err. Failures in the tools part bypass the 'Roadmap regression {part}' reporting, and `ROADMAP_TOOLS=` always prints all-true, so it carries no information.
findings.fix: Add one smoke support module with `named`, a single `wait_for`, `require`, and a sensitivity-checking `click`. Make every part return `Result<(), String>` and drop the constant JSON. In verify_tools keep only the GtkSourceView search checks, and leave the pure helpers to text.rs unit tests.

v1.correction:
Two claims are overstated.
- verify_tools does not run 'at app start in the shipping binary'. It is called only under `if fixture` (smoke.rs:504-505), after the SCREENSHOT gate.
- Roadmap 'tools' failures do not go unreported. The panic hook installed at smoke.rs:458-461 exits with status 1, so the harness still fails; only the 'Roadmap regression {part}' wording is lost.

The duplicated asserts in verify_tools are harmless; its value is the GtkSourceView checks. Payoff is modest.

findings.title: The drag-and-drop regressions hand-build the drag payload, so production DragSource::prepare is never exercised
findings.evidence:
smoke_registry.rs:35-36 builds `let token = glib::BoxedValue(format!("relay-{kind}:{source}").to_value());` and calls `drop.emit_by_name::<bool>("drop", ...)`. smoke_project_files.rs:193-196 builds `json!({"project":project,"worktree":"","path":"project-smoke.txt"}).to_string()`.

Both re-type the formats produced by shell.rs:47-51 (`format!("relay-{kind}:{id}")` in `connect_prepare`) and project_files.rs:330-335. Only the DropTarget half is real code under test.
findings.impact: Trigger: a change to either `connect_prepare` closure, such as the token prefix, the JSON keys or the worktree encoding. Real drag-and-drop between rows then breaks while both regressions stay green, because neither one calls the source.
findings.fix: Take the payload from the real source. Find the row's DragSource via `observe_controllers`, emit `prepare` (x, y), read the returned ContentProvider's value, and pass that to the target's `drop`.

v1.reason: smoke_registry.rs:35 builds `glib::BoxedValue(format!("relay-{kind}:{source}").to_value())` and emits 'drop' directly. smoke_project_files.rs:193-197 hand-builds `{"project","worktree":"","path"}` and emits 'drop' on the folder's DropTarget. The production sources are shell.rs:47-51 (connect_prepare returning ContentProvider::for_value(token)) and project_files.rs:330-335 (JSON with `*ed.worktree.borrow()`). Neither test calls these, so a change to the source encoding would not fail either regression.
v1.correction: The practical risk is small for the registry. In shell.rs the source token and the target's strip_prefix(`relay-{kind}:`) (shell.rs:62) sit in the same function a few lines apart, so drift there is unlikely. Divergence is more plausible for the file-tree JSON, where the source (project_files.rs:330) and the drop handler (bind_tree_drop) are separate functions. Low severity, modest payoff.

results.coverage:
Read every line of crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs (1-1396) and crates/relay-core/tests/store.rs (1-218).

Production code traced:
- Read in full: recovery.rs, pty.rs, handlers/session.rs, store.rs, handlers/import_v3.rs, skills.rs, providers.rs, paths.rs, serve.rs, time.rs.
- Read in part: engine.rs 60-160 and 380-1495; hooks.rs 1-445; worktree.rs 1-80 and 160-380; handlers/git.rs 96-155, 486-610 and 890-1060; guardrail.rs 596-677; handlers/app.rs 1-140; handlers/provider.rs 1-45; relay-remote bridge.rs 1-200 and the wire.rs gate; relay-cli unreal_process.rs 255-334, unreal.rs 305-320 and 620-660, main.rs 198-218.
- Native-app call sites of session.close, provider.refresh, app.import.v3 and worktree.remove.
- Not read beyond grep: awareness.rs, socket.rs, task.rs, notes.rs, plugins.rs, device*.rs, branch_cleanup.rs, the rest of guardrail.rs.

Checks run:
- In the scratchpad, `git worktree remove --force` on a directory that is not a worktree exits 128. That is the case that sends worktree::remove into its remove_dir_all fallback.
- A read-only /proc check (key names only) showed the running `relay --instance dev mcp` processes carry RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_STORE, RELAY_INSTANCE and RELAY_TOKEN.
- kernel.pid_max is 4194304 here.
- The developer's global git config sets none of gpgsign, hooksPath, fsmonitor or templateDir, so I did not report the fixture's missing git-config isolation.

Not reported, because documented or out of this chunk (worth a look by the owning chunk):
- The socket door accepts any same-uid `user` actor without a token. This is a documented trade-off (BUS.md §0.6, §4.2, §9.5, §14).
- guardrail::write_roots always grants std::env::temp_dir() (guardrail.rs:617). That includes the /tmp/relay-v4-<uid> runtime fallback.
- session.close defaults to remove_worktree=true and removes with --force, with no dirty check, for API callers. The native UI opts in explicitly.
- git::briefing_state walks commit graphs under the store lock during spawn, brief and bootstrap.
- hooks::writes() is documented as 'held for milliseconds' but is held across the skill-folder copies.
- store.rs's test sets RELAY_V3_SESSIONS_JSON process-wide and never restores it. Only one test reads it today.
- session_lifecycle_over_socket's frame loops spin without sleeping if the connection hits EOF.

No dead helpers in either test file. The tests do not touch the real data dir or socket: handlers use store-relative paths, Instance::Test skips user-home skill and write-root writes, and every spawning test points the provider at a fake binary before spawning.

findings.title: Closing the most recently launched of several sessions in one checkout deletes the active hook dir: the commit gate silently stops running and the user's core.hooksPath is later unset
findings.evidence: Close prepare only undoes hooks when it is the last session in that worktree: `let teardown = if others == 0 { Some(read_teardown(conn, &s.worktree)?) } else { None };` (session.rs:1559). It then deletes its own hook dir unconditionally: `crate::hooks::remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name);` (1596). Every create and every launch re-points the shared checkout at its own dir: `git(worktree, &["config", "--worktree", "core.hooksPath", &hook_dir_s])` (hooks.rs:150-154, called from session.rs:481 and 892). So the most recently created or launched session owns the active hooksPath. At the last close, uninstall_git_any reads `<active dir>/.relay-previous-hooks-path`; when that file is gone it falls to `git config --worktree --unset core.hooksPath` instead of restoring (hooks.rs:256-276). remove_hook_dir's doc assumes a wired dir 'is left alone by uninstall_git before this runs' (hooks.rs:283-284), but uninstall never runs while others > 0. Both tests that close shared checkouts avoid the bug by their close order: sessions.rs:1364 `// Closed oldest first, so the newest session's hook stays active until the very last close.`; the pair test closes builder, then reviewer, then the last-spawned second builder (sessions.rs:1218-1226). A PAIR create refused in its finish phase also leaves its never-inserted name's dir active (session.rs:900 skips the undo when pair_with is set), and recovery's sweep_hook_dirs later deletes that dir too (recovery.rs:136-139).
findings.impact: Two or more sessions share a checkout: a PAIR or review group, or primary-checkout agents, which D160 makes the default for Unreal projects. The user closes the most recently launched one with the UI default (remove_worktree:false, agent_menu.rs:612 and shell.rs:734). `.relay/hooks/<name>` is deleted while core.hooksPath still points at it. From then on, `git commit` from the remaining agents' shells runs no pre-commit hook, so Relay's commit guardrail (caps, protected paths) and the user's own chained pre-commit hook are skipped silently. When the last session closes, the user's original core.hooksPath (e.g. `.husky`) is unset rather than restored, so their hooks stay off after Relay is gone.
findings.fix: In Close, when others > 0 and this session's hook dir is the active core.hooksPath, re-point the checkout at a live sibling (run install_git for that sibling; it records the same pre-Relay path) before deleting, or keep the dir until the last close. Store the pre-Relay path somewhere not tied to one session's dir, so uninstall can never fall back to `--unset` while a Relay dir is active. Add a test that closes the newest session first and asserts hooksPath points at an existing gate hook, and that the original path is restored at the end.

v1.reason: session.rs:1559 computes the teardown only when others == 0, yet session.rs:1596 calls `remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name)` unconditionally. Every launch (session.rs:481) and every create (892) calls install_git, which points `core.hooksPath --worktree` at `.relay/hooks/<that session>` (hooks.rs:150-154), so the newest launched session owns the active hook dir. Closing that session while siblings are live deletes the dir that git config still references. Git then silently runs no hooks for shell `git commit` from the remaining agents, which skips both the Relay commit gate and the chained user hook. At the last close, read_teardown (session.rs:334-347) lists every name that ever used the worktree, including the closed one. uninstall_git_any (hooks.rs:242-276) treats the dangling dir as owned, fails to read .relay-previous-hooks-path, and falls into `git config --unset core.hooksPath`, losing a pre-Relay path such as .husky. The doc comment on remove_hook_dir (hooks.rs:281-283) assumes an uninstall that never ran for this close.
v1.correction: There is a partial self-heal. A Relay `git.commit` op calls refresh_git (git.rs:548), which recreates the dead session's hook dir from the still-configured path. Because PREVIOUS_HOOKS_PATH is gone, previous_dir falls to `rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which resolves to the Relay dir itself and is filtered out, so the user's chained hook stays lost. Shell commits by agents get no repair. The fix as proposed is sound: when others > 0 and the closing session's dir is the active hooksPath, re-run install_git for a live sibling before deleting the dir.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. Close's read phase computes `others` (non-closed sessions in the same worktree) and builds a teardown only when `others == 0` (session.rs:1553-1559). It then calls `remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name)` with no condition (1596). install_git always points `core.hooksPath --worktree` at `.relay/hooks/<that session>` (hooks.rs:150-154). It runs on session.create (892) and on every staged launch through prepare_launch:481: spawn 918, resume 944, wake/clear_restorable 960 and 1000. So the session that last created or launched owns the active path. Closing it while a sibling is still open deletes the directory git config points at. I checked this against real git 2.55. With a worktree-level hooksPath that points at a deleted directory, `git commit` runs no hook and exits 0, silently. I also ran a line-for-line Python model of install_git, refresh_git, uninstall_git_any and Close against real git. Closing the newest session first produced "hooks-output=NONE" for the remaining agent's commit. The tests avoid the bug only through their close order: sessions.rs:1364-1367 has the explicit comment, and 1218-1226 closes the builders and the reviewer before the last-spawned second builder. The bug is older than the 853e635 refactor: the earlier Close had the same "uninstall only if no other session, always remove the dir" shape (853e635^:1374-1398).

(b) Who can trigger it and how often. The user closes a session from the desktop UI: "Close session…" leaves "remove worktree" unchecked by default (agent_menu.rs:589-612), and "Discard session" sends remove_worktree:false (shell.rs:734). Agents and the CLI can close sessions too. In a shared checkout, remove_worktree:true is refused while a sibling is open (1556), so every close except the last goes down this path. Checkouts are shared in two normal flows. First, PAIR and review groups share one checkout by design. Second, under D160 the Unreal plugin sets `default_checkout: "primary"` (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18), so every agent in such a project shares the primary checkout. Any close of the most recently created, launched or resumed session while others are open fires the bug. That is common: the newest helper agent is often the first one closed.

(c) What happens. BUS.md §9.3 says the pre-commit hook is the door that applies commit caps and protected paths to agents, which commit with their own `git`: "This binds both providers' commits, and yours." After the bad close, every shell `git commit` in that checkout runs no pre-commit hook at all, with no error, log or UI sign. That covers agents and the user's own terminal in the primary checkout. Two checks are lost: Relay's commit gate and the user's own chained pre-commit hook. This lasts until the next create or launch in that checkout. A Relay `git.commit` op also partly repairs it (see correction 2). Relay's own git.commit still gates in-process (git.rs:561).

(d) Severity. High fits the rubric's "a safety check that can be silently bypassed" in a normal flow. It is not critical: no data is lost, the agent is not escaping on its own, nothing is reachable by another user or a network peer, and an agent could already skip the hook with `--no-verify`. The default denied_commands (settings.rs:33) do not block that. So this hook is a cooperative safety net that a routine close switches off silently, not a hard boundary.

(e) The proposed fix is the right direction but incomplete. See corrections 5 and 6.
v2.correction:
1. The second half of the impact is overstated. At the last close, `git config --worktree --unset core.hooksPath` (hooks.rs:263-276) removes only the worktree-level key. That loses the user's path only if they set it with `git config --worktree`, as the sessions.rs:1357 test does. In the common setups the user gets their hooks back: no hooksPath at all, a husky/lefthook-style path in `.git/config`, or a global path. I verified this: after the unset, the effective path was the local `.husky/_` and the user's hook ran. So ".husky stays off after Relay is gone" is wrong as written.

2. The finding misses a worse lasting effect.
