So SQLite JSON-parses project rows until it finds limit+1 (default 101) matches, which for a typical task means all of them. D151 says the audit table 'becomes most of the database', with `session.report` adding a row on every agent tool use. The handler is a plain `register` (task.rs:757), so the scan holds the one connection. The task page calls it on refresh and 'load more' (task_pages.rs:1056).
findings.impact: Trigger: opening a task's history in a project with months of agent activity (hundreds of thousands of audit rows inside the 180-day window). Consequence: each call parses every row's payload/result JSON while holding the store connection. All other requests freeze for the duration, and the cost grows linearly with history.
findings.fix: Record the task id as a real, indexed audit column at append time, or in a task_audit(task_id, audit_id) side table filled for task ops and dispatch results. Then page with an index range scan, `WHERE task_id=? AND id<? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?`, and backfill in a migration.

v1.reason: Task.activity is a plain `register` (task.rs:757). Its query (763-767) filters by `project_id` and `id < ?3`, plus an OR of json_extract predicates, and the third disjunct, `json_extract(result_summary, '$.task.id') = ?2`, has no op filter. The audit indexes are ts, actor/ts, session/ts, op/ts, project/ts, parent, undo_of and undone_by (store.rs:28-34, 128), and none covers the task id. A typical task has far fewer than limit+1 (101) matching rows, so SQLite reads every audit row of the project in the retention window and evaluates json_extract on each. D151 (DECISIONS.md:832-843) confirms the table is the bulk of the store: `session.report` is audited for agents (`Audit::AgentOnly`, ops/session.rs:151) on every tool use, with payloads up to 2 KB, kept 180 days by default. All of this runs while holding the single connection. The native task page calls it on open and on 'load more' (task_pages.rs:960, 1056).
v1.correction: Most rows are session.report and usage.report, which fail `op LIKE 'task.%'` and pay only for a json_extract on a small `result_summary` plus the page I/O. The cost is roughly a full scan of the project's audit rows: likely hundreds of milliseconds rather than seconds on a heavy store, but it grows linearly and blocks every request. The fix is right: an indexed task_id column or a side table, backfilled by a migration that bumps SCHEMA_VERSION.

findings.title: session.report sets state from the hook kind without checking the session is live; the identity test pins created → running
findings.evidence: The new state comes only from the kind (`"session_start" | "tool_use" => "running"`, `"stop" | "idle" => "idle"`, session.rs:1359-1367). It is written unconditionally: `UPDATE sessions SET state=?1, … WHERE id=?4` (1372-1373). A builder's active task is also flipped (1390-1398). Only closed sessions are excluded, because by_name filters `state != 'closed'` (sessions.rs:156). By contrast, the PTY exit path guards with `WHERE id=?3 AND epoch=?4 AND state IN ('spawning','running','idle','blocked')` (session.rs:652-655). agent_surface.rs:326-327 asserts that a tool_use report on a never-spawned session makes it `running`.
findings.impact: Trigger: a hook report (PostToolUse/Stop, or Codex's notify) that the engine processes after `session.park` has committed `parked`. Park kills the PTY in its unlocked prepare (session.rs:977-980) and then commits (990-993), so a report still queued for the store runs afterwards. Consequence: a session with no process reads `running`/`idle` and its builder task flips to running. `session.wake` refuses it ('only parked sessions wake', 1001-1007) and `session.spawn` refuses it as already spawned, so it stays stuck until closed.
findings.fix: Apply report transitions only `WHERE state IN ('spawning','running','idle','blocked')` (ideally also matching the current epoch), and return a typed refusal otherwise. Change the test to spawn the session first, or to assert that a report on a created session is refused.

v1.reason: Confirmed in the code. The Report handler (`e.register::<Report>`, session.rs:1348) derives `state` from `p.kind` alone (1358-1367) and runs `UPDATE sessions SET state=?1 ... WHERE id=?4` (1371-1374) with no liveness or epoch guard. `sessions::by_name` (sessions.rs:155-156) excludes only `closed`, so a report reaching a parked, exited or restorable session moves it to running or idle. The builder-task flip at 1388-1398 follows from that. By contrast, the PTY exit callback (session.rs:652-655) and Park's commit (`is_live` check at 986) are both guarded. No reconciler heals a 'running' row that has no PTY, and Wake (1001-1007) and Restore (962-964) both refuse anything not parked or restorable, so a corrupted state sticks until the session is closed. What I could not establish is how often the trigger happens. It needs a hook's `session.report` to reach the store after Park's commit (or after the exit or app_restart transitions, engine.rs:676). Park kills the PTY in its unlocked prepare and up to 3 s pass before the commit, so a report already queued usually lands before the commit and does no harm. Claude's Stop and PostToolUse hooks are synchronous children of the agent and normally die with it. Only an asynchronous reporter, such as Codex `notify` or a hook outliving its parent, makes a post-commit report likely. The finding's test reference (agent_surface.rs:326-327, created -> running through tool_use) is accurate.
v1.correction: The trigger is a race with a narrow window, so this is plausible rather than demonstrated. The same unguarded transition also covers `exited` and `restorable` (after app_restart, engine.rs:676), not just `parked`. The fix is right: add `AND state IN ('spawning','running','idle','blocked')` (ideally plus the epoch) to the UPDATE, and skip the task flip when nothing changed.

findings.title: task.relate records an undo even when INSERT OR IGNORE inserted nothing, so undoing a repeat relate deletes the original edge
findings.evidence: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO task_relations(from_task,to_task,rel,created_at) …` (task.rs:1261-1266) ignores the row count. The handler then always calls `ctx.set_undo(if replaced.is_some() { "task.relate" } else { "task.unrelate" }, …)` (1269-1277). Edges are unique: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_relations_edge ON task_relations(from_task, to_task, rel)` (store.rs:336). LabelAdd, LabelRemove and Unrelate only set an undo when something changed (`if added > 0`, 1204; `if removed > 0`, 1224 and 1296). audit.undo checks only updated_at, which the repeat call's `touch` refreshed (audit.rs:58-65).
findings.impact: Trigger: `task.relate {A, blocked_by, B}` issued twice (a double click, or a CLI/agent retry with a new request id), then Undo on the latest audit row. Consequence: the inverse `task.unrelate` deletes the blocked_by edge that the first call created, and the board silently loses the dependency.
findings.fix: Use the execute count. Only touch updated_at and set the undo when a row was inserted or a duplicate_of was actually replaced, as LabelAdd does.

v1.reason: Relate (task.rs:1251-1281) ignores the row count of `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO task_relations` (1261-1266), always calls `touch`, and always records an undo. For a non-duplicate_of relation, `replaced` is None, so the undo is `task.unrelate` with the same edge (1269-1277). A second identical relate inserts nothing, refreshes updated_at, and records that inverse. audit.undo (audit.rs:48-68) checks only `updated_at`, which matches, and then calls task.unrelate, which deletes the edge created by the first call. Unrelate, by contrast, records its undo only `if removed > 0`. Bus request ids differ between a double click and a CLI retry, so nothing deduplicates the repeat.
v1.correction: A repeat duplicate_of to the same target is harmless: replaced equals the same target, so the undo re-relates it. The bug applies to the multi-valued relations, such as blocked_by. Fix: only touch and set the undo when the insert's row count is greater than 0 or a different duplicate_of target was replaced.

findings.title: Undoing task.approve is a plain task.move: the commit link stays and the task's prior state is lost
findings.evidence: Approve inserts a task_commits row (`link_commit`, task.rs:1128) and forces `state='none'` (1132). Its undo is only `task.move {task_id, column, position}` (1141-1145). Move keeps `before.state` except for Done→InReview (`moved_state`, 902), and it never touches task_commits. `link_commit` accepts any non-empty string as a sha (540-559), and the board tests pass `"cafe"`/`"deadbeef"`. board.rs:732-736 checks only column order after the undo.
findings.impact: Trigger: approving an active or ready task by mistake, then pressing Undo. Consequence: the card returns to its column with state `none` instead of `dispatched`/`running`. task.get still lists the approval's commit link, so the board shows a commit on an unapproved task, and a later approval adds a second one.
findings.fix: Give approval its own inverse: an undo payload that restores column, position and state, and deletes the task_commits row only if this approval inserted it. Assert state and commits in the undo test.

v1.reason: Approve (task.rs:1086-1146) calls `link_commit` (`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO task_commits`, 545-559) and sets `col='done', state='none'` (1131-1138). Its undo is `task.move {task_id, column, position}` (1141-1145). The Move handler (898-905) never touches task_commits. It keeps `before.state`, which after the approval is 'none', except that Done -> InReview is restored to AwaitingReview. So after an undo the commit link remains, and task.get still lists it (task.rs:240). Approving a task out of Active (allowed, since only Done is refused at 1088) and then undoing leaves it in Active with state 'none' instead of dispatched, running or blocked. The board test (board.rs:733-735) checks only the column order.
v1.correction: State loss happens only when the approval came from a column other than in_review. Approving from in_review, the normal path, is restored correctly to awaiting_review by `moved_state`. Approving from ready also loses nothing in practice, since ready tasks presumably already carry state 'none'. The stray task_commits row is the part that always happens. A re-approval with the same sha is absorbed by INSERT OR IGNORE, so a second link appears only if the branch head moved.

findings.title: mirror text-truncation tests never exercise the char-boundary backoff they claim to test
findings.evidence: Both tests use `"é".repeat(151)` (302 bytes). 300 is even, so byte 300 is already a char boundary. The `while !s.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }` loops in `text` (src/mirror.rs:503-506) and `text_chunks` (532-535) therefore never run, and a naive `&s.as_bytes()[..300]` gives identical output. The test's own comment notes the cap 'would land on 300 exactly'. Because 300 = 2²·3·5², no repeated 2-, 3- or 4-byte char ever straddles it. set_clipboard_caps_on_a_char_boundary (mirror.rs:375-388) does this correctly.
findings.impact: Trigger: a refactor that drops or breaks the boundary loop. Consequence: INJECT_TEXT messages split a UTF-8 char, so the device types garbage (or the slice panics), while both tests stay green.
findings.fix: Offset the input by one ASCII byte, e.g. `format!("a{}", "é".repeat(150))` (301 bytes). Assert the first message carries 299 bytes and the chunks concatenate back to the input.

v1.reason: Both tests use `"é".repeat(151)`, which is 302 bytes. INJECT_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH is 300, and 300 is a char boundary for 2-byte chars. So the `while !s.is_char_boundary(end)` loops in mirror.rs text (~503-506) and text_chunks (~532-535) never run. 300 is also a multiple of 3 and of 4, so no repeated multi-byte char straddles it. If either loop were removed, text() would still emit 300 valid bytes and text_chunks would still slice at a valid boundary, and both tests would stay green. set_clipboard_caps_on_a_char_boundary (tests/mirror.rs:375-388) does exercise its backoff, because 3 does not divide 262130.
v1.correction: If the loop regressed, text_chunks would panic at `&rest[..end]` on a non-boundary rather than send garbage; text() would send invalid UTF-8. Either way it is uncaught. Fix: prefix one ASCII byte, e.g. `format!("a{}", "é".repeat(150))`, which is 301 bytes. Assert that the first message carries 299 bytes and that the chunks concatenate back to the input.

findings.title: run_worker_until_it_ends hangs forever if the worker fails before connecting (fake server blocks in accept and is joined without a timeout)
findings.evidence: `serve_then_vanish` blocks in `listener.accept().unwrap()` twice (mirror.rs:816, 818) with no timeout. The helper then calls `worker.join().unwrap(); server.join().unwrap();` unconditionally (863-864). The worker can reach a terminal state without ever connecting: a push or forward failure calls `fail(...)` and returns (device.rs:768-780). The fake adb answers only the argv shapes it knows and exits 1 otherwise (`*) exit 1 ;;`, mirror.rs:679). The CI engine job sets no `timeout-minutes` (ci.yml:19-41), so GitHub's 360-minute default applies.
findings.impact: Trigger: any change to push_args/forward_args, a new adb step the fake doesn't recognise, or a failed exec of the freshly written script. Consequence: instead of failing with the worker's message, both worker tests hang in `server.join()`. `cargo test` never finishes, and CI burns hours before timing out with no diagnosis.
findings.fix: Accept with a deadline (set_nonblocking plus polling, or a channel with recv_timeout). Join the server only after the worker has connected; if the worker ends without connecting, fail with `runtime.status()`. Add `timeout-minutes` to the CI job.

v1.reason: Confirmed by reading crates/relay-core/tests/mirror.rs. `serve_then_vanish` (mirror.rs:813-837) moves the listener into a thread and calls `listener.accept().unwrap()` twice with no deadline. Nothing else ever closes that listener. `run_worker_until_it_ends` (845-877) waits for a terminal status with a 15 s assert, then calls `worker.join().unwrap(); server.join().unwrap();` unconditionally (863-864). `mirror_worker` (device.rs:758-802) can reach a terminal Failed state without ever connecting, and it then returns at once. The paths are push failure (768-770), forward failure or an unparsable port (772-779), and a spawn failure (795-801). In each case the status loop exits normally, `worker.join()` returns, and `server.join()` blocks forever in `accept`. The 15 s deadline does not help: it guards only the status wait, which has already ended. A worker that never ends trips the assert and panics, so the only hang is the 'failed before connecting' case the finding describes. The fake adb answers only devices/push/get-state/forward/shell and exits 1 on anything else (mirror.rs:679). So a change to `push_args`/`forward_args` that the fake does not match, or a new adb step before the connect, would turn both worker tests from a failure with a message into a hang. The CI `engine` job (ci.yml:19-41) sets no `timeout-minutes`, so the hang runs until GitHub's 6-hour default. Today the fake matches the real argv, so nothing hangs now. This is a latent diagnosability problem in the tests, not a product bug.
v1.correction: Hang site: mirror.rs:864 (`server.join()`), with the blocking accepts at 815 and 817 (the finding says 816/818). An easy fix: after the status turns terminal, check whether the runtime ever reached Running or connected. If it did not, panic with `runtime.status()` before joining the server, or poke the listener with a throwaway `TcpStream::connect` so the accepts return. Separately, add `timeout-minutes` to the CI engine job.

findings.title: Device-to-host parsers are dead in production: the drain thread discards every message, so getclipboard replies and clipboard acks go nowhere
findings.evidence:
The worker's control drain is `while drain.read(&mut bytes).is_ok_and(|count| count > 0) {}` (device.rs:826-829). No production code calls `parse_device_msg`/`parse_device_event`: rg over crates/ and apps/relay-native/src finds only mirror.rs and the tests. Yet the docs claim otherwise:
- mirror.rs:711-713: 'the shell's drain thread matches [`DeviceMsg`] exhaustively'.
- InputMsg::GetClipboard: 'the answer arrives as a `DeviceEvent::Clipboard`' (818-822).
- A non-zero SetClipboard sequence 'asks for a ClipboardAck' (814-816).
Tests mirror.rs:464-547 cover only these unused parsers.
findings.impact: Trigger: `device.mirror.input {"type":"getclipboard","copy":"cut"}`. Consequence: the call returns `{}`, the device performs the cut and sends its clipboard back, and the drain thread throws the reply away, so nothing can ever observe it. The parsers and their three tests are upkeep for a feature that does not exist.
findings.fix: Either feed the drain through parse_device_event and surface Clipboard/ClipboardAck as `mirror` frames or events, or drop GetClipboard and the ack sequence from the accepted InputMsg surface and delete the parsers, their docs and their tests.

v1.reason:
The drain thread at device.rs ~826-829 is `while drain.read(&mut bytes).is_ok_and(|count| count > 0) {}`, so every device-to-host byte is thrown away. rg across crates/ and apps/relay-native/src finds no production caller of parse_device_msg or parse_device_event (mirror.rs:696 and 732). Their only users are the tests. Three doc comments describe behaviour that does not exist:
- mirror.rs:711-713 refers to 'the shell's drain thread matches [`DeviceMsg`] exhaustively', a leftover from an earlier shell.
- InputMsg::GetClipboard (818) promises the answer 'arrives as a `DeviceEvent::Clipboard`'.
- SetClipboard.sequence (814) promises a ClipboardAck.
GetClipboard is still encoded and accepted (mirror.rs:859), so the request is sent and its reply discarded.
v1.correction: The impact is limited to a dead feature surface plus misleading docs. A GetClipboard with copy=cut is not data loss, since the cut text stays on the device clipboard. The category is dead-code with some docs-drift.

findings.title: existing_tasks_keep_neutral_board_defaults never touches a pre-v16 row, and no test migrates a store that holds data
findings.evidence: The comment says 'Rows written before v16 are typed `task` … the migration must not invent a classification'. But the test creates its row with `task.create` on a freshly opened v20 store (board.rs:577-580), so it checks column defaults, not the v16 migration (store.rs:308-338). every_prior_version_migrates_forward builds stores from MIGRATIONS[..k] holding a single meta row (tests/store.rs:23-29). No test upgrades a store with tasks in it, despite SPEC §16's 'open DBs at every historical user_version'.
findings.impact: Trigger: a future migration that rebuilds the tasks table, backfills, or changes a CHECK. Consequence: existing users' tasks could be mis-typed or lost on upgrade while the test named for that guarantee keeps passing.
findings.fix: Build a v15 store from MIGRATIONS[..15] with a task row, open it with Store::open, and assert the board defaults through task.get. More generally, seed representative rows in every_prior_version_migrates_forward.

v1.reason: board.rs:577-590 creates its task through `task.create` on a store that Fixture::new opened fresh at the current schema. Its comment talks about 'rows written before v16', but the test only checks the defaults of rows created now. It never runs migration v16 over an existing row. every_prior_version_migrates_forward (tests/store.rs:17-58) builds each historical version with only a `meta` row inserted, so no test migrates a store that holds tasks or other domain rows.
v1.correction: No present bug: this test gap matters only if a future migration rebuilds the tasks table or backfills it. The suggested fix is right: seed a task, and ideally a session and a project, into the MIGRATIONS[..k] stores and read them back after Store::open. The test's name and comment should also stop claiming it covers pre-v16 rows.

findings.title: board activity test accepts any error as proof that agents are refused
findings.evidence: `assert!(response.error.is_some(), "agent cannot read user-wide task conversations")` (board.rs:675-678). task.activity is `Actors::UserOnly` (crates/relay-bus/src/ops/task.rs:34-35) and is refused with `actor.allowlist` (engine.rs:855-864). A schema error, an actor error or a handler failure would satisfy the assertion just as well. The test's name says 'read_only_for_agents', but it asserts that agents cannot read at all.
findings.impact: Trigger: an agent-side regression that fails for an unrelated reason, such as a payload validation change. Consequence: the test passes without proving the authorization boundary it names.
findings.fix: Assert `error.code == "actor.allowlist"` and rename the test to match (e.g. `…_and_user_only`).

v1.reason: board.rs:669-678 asserts only `response.error.is_some()`. task.activity is `Actors::UserOnly` (relay-bus/src/ops/task.rs:34-35). engine.rs runs schema validation (line ~852) before the allowlist check (855-868), which returns `actor.allowlist`. So the test would also pass on a schema error or a not_found. The test name says 'read_only_for_agents', but agents are refused even reads.
v1.correction: Assert `error.code == "actor.allowlist"` (BusError::allowlist), and rename the test to say user-only.

findings.title: Every integration test file re-implements git/call/ok/Fixture; the copies have drifted and none isolates the developer's git config
findings.evidence:
There is no tests/common module. Of 18 test files, 14 define `fn git(`, 17 define `fn call(` and 11 define `struct Fixture` (rg). The copies have drifted:
- board.rs's `git` uses `.status()` and asserts bare success (board.rs:13-21), so a failing fixture command panics without git's stderr; agent_surface.rs's copy prints it (line 15).
- board.rs:50-60 re-creates sessions.rs's fake provider (sessions.rs:150-161), and says so (45-49).
No helper sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM (rg finds none). So fixture commits (board.rs:77, agent_surface.rs:50, 458) and the engine's own git calls run under the developer's ~/.gitconfig. Both Fixtures declare `_root` before `engine`, so the temp tree is deleted before the engine and its PTYs are dropped.
findings.impact: Trigger: a developer with `commit.gpgsign=true` or a global `core.hooksPath` runs `cargo test`. Consequence: fixture commits fail, or run the developer's own hooks (install_git chains whatever `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` returns, hooks.rs:98), and board.rs reports only a bare 'assertion failed'. Every fixture fix has to be made in about a dozen places, and the copies already disagree.
findings.fix: Add tests/common/mod.rs with one Fixture builder, one fake provider, and one `git()` that sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and reports stderr. Alternatively set those in `.cargo/config.toml [env]`, which also isolates the engine's own git calls. Declare `engine` before `_root` so it drops first.

v1.reason: crates/relay-core/tests has no common module. rg -l counts 13 files with `fn git(`, 18 with `fn call(` and 10 with `struct Fixture`. The copies have drifted. board.rs:13-21 uses `.status()` and a bare `assert!(...success())`, while agent_surface.rs:13-16 uses `.output()` and prints stderr. board.rs:40-60 re-creates sessions.rs's fake provider and its comment says so. No test sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL or GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM; the only GIT_CONFIG_* use is phase12.rs:90-92 (protocol.ext.allow). So fixture `git commit` runs under the developer's global config: `commit.gpgsign=true` makes it fail, and a global core.hooksPath runs the developer's hooks. In both Fixtures `_root` is declared before `engine`, so fields drop in that order and the tempdir is removed before the engine.
v1.correction: Counts are 13/18/10, not 14/17/11. The gitconfig and hook exposure affects developer machines only. CI runners have a clean config, and a gpgsign failure is loud rather than silent, so the realistic payoff is maintainability: fix it once, not in a dozen copies. The drop-order point is minor: Linux unlinks directories that are in use, and nothing shown depends on the order. Keep the severity low.

findings.title: Instance::Test gate in device.mirror.start leaves the production worker wiring untested (harness branch, not reachable in normal use)
findings.evidence: `if ctx.engine().instance != Instance::Test { ctx.after_commit(move |engine| { std::thread::spawn(move || mirror_worker(engine, runtime)); }); }` (device.rs:103-105). The jar check is also skipped under Test (86). Instead, the tests call the `pub #[doc(hidden)]` `mirror_worker` directly (mirror.rs:854-857; device.rs:754-758). Instance::Test comes only from `RELAY_INSTANCE=test` or `--instance test` (paths.rs:15-28), so stable and dev users never hit the gate.
findings.impact: Trigger: a regression in the after_commit spawn path (a missing spawn, wrong ordering, or a panic in the closure). Consequence: no test notices, and real mirrors sit on 'Starting' forever. Separately, under a `test` instance a real phone's mirror never starts at all.
findings.fix: Inject the worker launcher (e.g. an engine hook that tests replace) instead of gating on the instance, so device.mirror.start's real spawn path runs in at least one test. The fake adb and the serve_then_vanish server already make that possible.

v1.reason: The description is accurate: device.rs:103-105 spawns mirror_worker only when instance != Test, and the tests call mirror_worker directly. But gating real subprocesses and threads on Instance::Test is the codebase's standard test-isolation pattern; it repeats across device.rs, git.rs:638, provider.rs:60, session.rs:553/1633 and skills.rs:188. The untested part is one line, `ctx.after_commit(move |engine| { std::thread::spawn(move || mirror_worker(engine, runtime)); })`, and its logic is covered through the direct call. The 'test instance cannot mirror a real phone' point does not affect stable or dev users. A launcher-injection hook would add machinery to cover one trivial line, so this is not worth changing.

results.coverage:
I read every line of agent_features.rs, awareness.rs, phase7.rs and phase8.rs.

Production code traced:
- Read in full: engine.rs, handlers/integration.rs, handlers/audit.rs, watch.rs, proc.rs, paths.rs, skills.rs.
- Read in part: handlers/session.rs (create, launch, done, intent, claim, release, report, update, discard, close; spawn/park/wake skimmed); handlers/task.rs (dispatch, create, update, move, delete, restore, approve, attachments); handlers/git.rs 80-725 and 855-1010; handlers/guardrail.rs 530-777; handlers/notes.rs (delivery and send); handlers/settings.rs (set); handlers/workspace.rs (90-135, 300-413); hooks.rs 1-320 and 576-612; worktree.rs 1-240 and 335-375; branch_cleanup.rs 1-130 and 200-456; recovery.rs 140-175; guardrail.rs 560-660 and 811-900; store.rs 370-609.
- Docs: BUS.md §4-§5.5 and §9.2, DECISIONS D115-D121, D144, D149.

Not fully read: awareness.rs core (brief/bootstrap/peers internals), overlap.rs scan internals, file.rs handlers other than delete/restore/restore_head, socket.rs, pty.rs, device*.rs.

Searches (rg): data_dir, backup_dir, skills_dir, env::var, Instance::Test, Door::InProcess, ensure_after_commit, emit_system, git_mutate callers, handler registration kinds, `FROM claims`, task.approve callers.

Scratch experiments (git 2.55 with isolated config) confirmed two facts: `rev-parse --git-path hooks` honours a global core.hooksPath, and a branch at main's tip passes `merge-base --is-ancestor`. I could not delete the scratch directories; the guardrail blocks `rm -rf`. Nothing was compiled or run.

Isolation check: no test in these four files touches ~/.local/share/relay-v4, engine sockets, provider binaries, the network, or provider homes. `git fetch --all` with no remotes is a no-op. skills::user_bases is empty for Instance::Test, and write roots are not created for Test. Events are published synchronously, so phase7's quiet-window `try_recv` assertion is sound. The only shared global state across parallel tests is hooks::writes() and the registry.

Harness item 4: Door::InProcess (trusted, tokenless agent binding) is compiled into the engine, but only #[cfg(test)] modules (socket.rs:927, provider_updates.rs:221) and examples/perf.rs use it. It is not reachable in normal use.

Leads outside this chunk, noticed but not verified:
(a) BUS.md §4.2 lets `user` act on the socket without a token. guardrail.rs:850-853 admits self_approval only catches the relay CLI, so an agent writing raw JSON to the socket (nc, python) acts as the user.
(b) integration.request is in the builder allowlist (settings.rs:36). With `deploy` it runs run_cmd against a device through untimed `fish -lc` (integration.rs:185-242) without taking a device lease.
(c) workspace.discover walks a directory tree to depth 4 inside a locked handler (workspace.rs:115-133, 393-413), and one unreadable directory fails the whole scan.
(d) attach_bytes writes files before the transaction commits, which leaves orphan files when task.create fails later (task.rs:505-530).

findings.title: task.approve fails once branch cleanup deletes a closed session's merged branch; phase7's approve-after-close test only passes because Test engines skip that cleanup
findings.evidence: task.rs:1105-1114: the comment says "session.close deliberately keeps its branch", then the handler requires that branch to exist: `repo.rev_parse_single(format!("refs/heads/{}", session.session.branch).as_str()).map_err(|e| BusError::unavailable("git.head", e.to_string()))?`. That comment and phase7's test date from fcbdbce (2026-09-04). Commit 2d38f75 (2026-10-05) added branch_cleanup. Since then, session.close's after_commit calls `crate::branch_cleanup::after_close(engine, project_id, branch)` guarded by `if engine.instance != crate::Instance::Test` (session.rs:1630-1635). `evaluate` treats a branch as merged when `git.is_ancestor(&tip, base)` (branch_cleanup.rs:246-249) and deletes it with `update-ref -d refs/heads/{branch}` (314). The 20-minute sweeper does the same. I checked with git 2.55 that a branch sitting at main's tip passes `merge-base --is-ancestor`. That is exactly the shape of phase7.rs:324-379 (session.create, session.close, task.approve with no sha). The test passes only because Test engines never run after_close, and it never calls `branch_cleanup::run`, which the session.rs:1632 comment says tests must do instead. Its sha assertion (phase7.rs:358-361 compares against `git rev-parse HEAD` of the project) cannot tell the branch tip from HEAD anyway, because nothing is committed on the branch. Both UI callers send no sha: board_view.rs:841 `self.act("task.approve", json!({"task_id":task["id"]}))` and task_pages.rs:625-627.
findings.impact: In the normal review flow (agent finishes, task goes to in_review, the work is merged into main, the user closes the session), after_close deletes `relay/<name>` within seconds, as does the periodic sweep. When the user later drags the card to Done or clicks "Approve task", the call fails with unavailable/git.head (reference not found). The UI cannot supply a sha, so such a task cannot be approved at all. The board also shows "Approved #N into Done" before the call fails (board_view.rs:838-841).
findings.fix: When `refs/heads/<branch>` no longer resolves, fall back to the task's newest `task_commits` sha, or else to the base branch tip (cleanup only deletes branches already merged into base), and keep the recorded branch name. Correct the stale comment. Alternatively, have `branch_cleanup::candidates` skip branches whose task is not yet done. Rewrite the phase7 test to commit on the session branch, close the session, call `relay_core::branch_cleanup::run(&engine, Some(1), None, &Options::default())`, then approve and assert the linked sha is the branch tip.

v1.reason: task.rs:1086-1118: with no `sha`, Approve resolves `refs/heads/{session.branch}` through `rev_parse_single(...).map_err(|e| BusError::unavailable("git.head", ...))?`. Nothing falls back if that ref is gone. The comment there says "session.close deliberately keeps its branch", which stopped being true with branch_cleanup. session.rs:1626-1636 calls `branch_cleanup::after_close` in after_commit for every non-Test instance. branch_cleanup::candidates (74-80) picks closed sessions' branches and never looks at task column or state. evaluate (213-250) treats the branch as merged when `is_ancestor(tip, base)` (or via git cherry or a merged GitHub PR) and deletes it with `update-ref -d refs/heads/{branch}` (~314). after_merged_prs and the 20-minute sweeper do the same. So in the normal flow (agent finishes, task goes to in_review, the work is merged or the PR lands, the session is closed, then the user approves), the branch is gone and Approve fails with unavailable/git.head. The only native callers send no sha: board_view.rs:838-841 shows "Approved #N into Done" before the call, and task_pages.rs:625 does the same. The user therefore cannot approve the task from the UI at all. phase7.rs:324-379 (`approve_uses_the_recorded_branch_after_the_assigned_session_is_closed`) passes only because Test engines skip after_close. Its sha assertion compares against project HEAD, and with no commits on the branch it cannot tell the branch tip from HEAD.
v1.correction: The test is at phase7.rs:324 and the stale comment at task.rs:1105-1107. A branch with no commits (tip == base) is also deleted as 'merged into <base>', so even a session that committed nothing makes its task unapprovable once closed. Fix as proposed: when refs/heads/<branch> no longer resolves, fall back to the newest task_commits sha, or else to the base tip (cleanup deletes only branches already in base or merged by PR), and keep the recorded branch name. Alternatively, skip cleanup for branches whose task is not yet done.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. When no `sha` is given, Approve (task.rs:1086) reads the newest task_sessions row. task_sessions rows and closed session rows are only deleted on project.remove (workspace.rs:359-360), so that row is still there after a close. Approve then resolves `refs/heads/{session.branch}` with `rev_parse_single(...).map_err(|e| BusError::unavailable("git.head", ...))?` (task.rs:1112-1114) and has no fallback. In gix 0.86, find_ref calls `repo.refs.find(name)` and bails on NotFound (revision/spec/parse/delegate/revision.rs:18-31). Since 2d38f75 (2026-10-05), every non-Test close runs `branch_cleanup::after_close` (session.rs:1630-1635). serve.rs:35 also starts a sweeper that runs 90 s after start and then every 20 min, over every closed session. `candidates` (branch_cleanup.rs:74-80) never looks at task state. `evaluate` deletes the branch if `is_ancestor(tip, base)` holds, if git cherry finds every commit upstream, or if gh reports a merged PR (246-280). It first removes a clean pooled worktree that still holds the branch (306-312), then runs `update-ref -d` (314). I checked with git 2.55 that a branch at main's tip passes `--is-ancestor` and that update-ref -d makes it unresolvable. new_worktree_base (git.rs:978) starts new branches at the tip of local or upstream base, so a branch with no commits always counts as merged.

(b) Who and how: the user, in a flow the author built and tested for (phase7.rs:324, the BUS.md:685 default). The agent finishes, the task goes to in_review, the work is merged (locally, or through a PR when gh is present) or there is no work, the user closes the session, then approves. The native close keeps the worktree by default (agent_menu.rs:612, shell.rs:734), but cleanup removes a clean pooled worktree anyway. The startup and 20-minute sweeps go back over old data too: any task still waiting for approval whose session is closed and whose branch is merged or empty loses that branch soon after the first start on this build. Approving before closing, or approving an unmerged branch, still works.

(c) What happens: the task cannot reach Done from the UI. Only task.approve sets col='done', and task.move refuses done (task.rs:897). Both native callers send no sha (board_view.rs:841; task_pages.rs:625-627). The board shows "Approved #N into Done" (839) before the call fails, and the task page shows the git.head error in its status line. The only workaround is the CLI with an explicit sha. No data is lost.

(d) High is correct: a hard, user-visible failure of a core flow under a normal, documented ordering. It is not critical, because it needs close-before-approve with merged or empty work, and nothing is lost.

(e) The direction of the fix is right, with two errors (see correction).
v2.correction:
Locations: the Approve handler is at task.rs:1086, the stale comment at 1105-1107 and the failing resolve at 1112-1114. The test function is at phase7.rs:325 (its #[test] is at 324), and the toast is at board_view.rs:839.

Fix rationale: "cleanup only deletes branches already merged into base" is wrong. Cleanup also deletes a branch on a squash merge that only gh can prove, so local base may not contain the work. Branches can also disappear through git.branch.clean_merged or a manual git command. The fallback is therefore best effort: use the newest task_commits sha, or else the project checkout HEAD (as the no-session path does), and keep the recorded branch name. For an exact link, have branch_cleanup record the tip it deletes (in task_commits for the session's open tasks, or in the audit summary). The other way is to skip deletion while any non-deleted task linked to the session through task_sessions is not done; that has to cover multi-task queues and still needs the Approve fallback.

Test rewrite: as written it does not reproduce the bug. Cleanup keeps an unmerged commit, so that test passes on the current code. The branch must be merged (or stay empty) before `branch_cleanup::run`. Adding `relay_core::branch_cleanup::run(e, Some(1), None, &Options::default())` after session.close in the existing test is enough to make it fail, because the empty branch is "merged into main". Asserting the branch tip only works with deferral, a recorded tip, or a fast-forward merge.

Related stale promises: BUS.md:733 ("session.close … branch is kept"), agent_menu.rs:589 and 609 ("The branch is kept"), shell.rs:724 ("its worktree and branch are kept").

findings.title: worktree::git (behind git_mutate) runs git with bare Command::output(), and locked handlers call it, so slow or hung git holds the store mutex with no deadline
findings.evidence: worktree.rs:26-27: `fn git(repo, args) { let out = Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()`. It neither goes through proc::output_with_timeout nor sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, unlike `worktree::create` (212-214) and `fetch_remote` (git.rs:938-945). Callers registered with plain Engine::register, which holds the store mutex for the whole handler: git.stage (git.rs:490 then `git add --` at 503), git.unstage (507/527), git.branch.create (345, then `switch -c <name> [start]` at 374), git.branch.delete (445/485), git.branch.clean_merged (693, `branch -d` per branch at 712), file.restore_head (file.rs:253, `checkout --` at 256), and integration.discard (integration.rs:64). Also git.commit's locked finish phase (git.rs:571, `commit --no-verify`, which still runs the prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hooks). The same mistake appears in git.pr.open (git.rs:666-681), which runs `gh pr create`, a network call, via `cmd.output()` in a locked handler. D144 states "Every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout", and none of these ops appear in D149's list of converted ops. phase8 drives most of them (phase8.rs:228, 320, 333, 412-458, 419, 539) on 3-file repos, so the stall never shows.
findings.impact: Staging a large Git LFS asset (Unreal .uasset/.umap) runs git-lfs's clean filter for its full duration while the global store lock is held. Creating a branch from another start point checks out the tree and can download LFS objects. Under `relay serve` started from a terminal, git can even block on a credential prompt on /dev/tty. Meanwhile every other request waits, indefinitely if the child stalls: agents' guardrail.gate hook calls, UI refreshes and the phone door.
findings.fix: Run `worktree::git` through `proc::output_with_timeout` with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and return a typed timeout error. Move the subprocess of stage, unstage, branch.create, branch.delete, clean_merged, restore_head and pr.open into a `register_staged` prepare phase, leaving only the record and events in finish. For the commit finish phase, where the gate must stay atomic with the commit, at least bound the subprocess with the timeout.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:26-33: `fn git` runs `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()` with no deadline and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and `git_mutate` (line 36) is just `git(repo, args)`. Compare worktree::create (213-214), which sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and goes through proc::output_with_timeout. Handlers registered with plain `e.register` (store mutex and transaction held for the whole closure) call it: git.branch.create (git.rs:345, `switch -c`/`branch` at 374), git.branch.delete (445/485), git.stage (490/503 `add --`), git.unstage (507/527), git.clean_merged (693, `branch -d` per candidate at 712), file.restore_head (file.rs:253/256 `checkout --`), and integration.discard (integration.rs:59-64). git.commit's finish phase (git.rs:571) runs `commit --no-verify` inside the transaction, so prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg-free hooks such as post-commit, and LFS/GPG signing still run under the lock. git.pr.open (git.rs:666-689) runs `gh pr create`, a network call, with bare `cmd.output()` inside a locked handler. D144 (DECISIONS.md:729-738) says every subprocess forked from a handler goes through output_with_timeout, and D149's converted list (797-822) does not include any of these ops. Trigger: staging large LFS assets, `switch -c <name> <start>` checking out a big tree, gh waiting on the network, or a signing/pinentry prompt on commit. Consequence: every other bus request, guardrail.gate hook calls from agents included, waits until git or gh returns, indefinitely if the child stalls.
v1.correction: The worst instance is one the finding names only in passing. integration.discard (integration.rs:59-64) calls worktree::remove under the lock, and remove (worktree.rs:352-369) runs purge_build (rm -rf of target/, build/, node_modules/.cache and similar), then a full dir_size walk of the worktree, then `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune`, all with the store mutex held. On a worktree with a built Rust or Gradle tree that can take many seconds. Separately, git.push's staged prepare (git.rs:600-618) also uses git_mutate. It does not hold the lock, but it has no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, so under a terminal-launched `relay serve` a credential prompt can hang that request forever. Fix as proposed: give git() a timeout and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Move pr.open, discard's remove, and the stage, unstage, branch and restore subprocesses into register_staged prepare phases. Keep only the commit itself in git.commit's finish, bounded by the timeout.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. worktree.rs:26-33 runs `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()` with no deadline and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and git_mutate (36) only wraps it. A plain `e.register` handler runs after `self.store.lock()` plus `conn.transaction()` (engine.rs:954-956), so the mutex is held for the whole closure. Callers on that path: git.stage (git.rs:503), git.unstage (527), git.branch.create (374), git.branch.delete (485), clean_merged (712), file.restore_head (file.rs:256) and integration.discard (integration.rs:62-64). git.commit's finish (571) and git.pr.open (666-681, a bare `cmd.output()` of `gh pr create`) are also on it. D144 (DECISIONS.md:729-738) requires every handler subprocess to go through output_with_timeout, and D149's converted list (797-822) names none of these ops. The author's own comment at git.rs:531-534 calls staging a subprocess "of unbounded length" that must not hold the store. git.branch.switch (384) was made staged because `git switch` walks the checkout, yet git.stage, and git.branch.create (which also runs `switch -c`), still hold the lock.

(b) Reachable in normal use. The native Git panel calls git.stage and git.unstage; "Stage all changes" sends every changed path (code_git.rs:467-483). It also calls git.commit, git.pr.open (662), git.branch.create (1035) and git.branch.delete (1136). Agents (Actors::All) can call stage, unstage and commit. Concrete triggers:
- Every "Open PR": gh makes several GitHub API round trips, so seconds of hold.
- Staging large .uasset or .umap files. Without LFS, `git add` deflates the whole blob; with LFS, the clean filter hashes and copies it. Either way this is seconds per GB.
- branch.create with a distant start point, which does a full checkout.

(c) While the child runs, every op that needs the store waits:
- guardrail.gate is a plain register (guardrail.rs:304), so every agent's next tool call blocks in its PreToolUse hook.
- Unlocked::read (engine.rs:173-186) takes the same mutex, so D149 queries stall too, along with UI panels and the phone door.
Keystrokes are exempt (D148 fast path), and the GTK client calls asynchronously (spawn_future_local), so this is a bus stall, not a UI-thread freeze. No data is lost. The stall is unbounded only if the child never exits: gh stalled on the network, a GPG pinentry, a waiting hook, or a prompt. On this machine gh is the github.com credential helper and commit.gpgsign is unset, so the prompt variant is unlikely here.

(d) High fits "a freeze of the bus" in normal flows such as Open PR and staging big assets. It is not critical, because the common case is a stall of seconds, not a permanent hang.

(e) Moving the work into register_staged is right and matches commit, push, switch and create. A single blanket deadline inside worktree::git is not. It would also cover callers that do not hold the lock and legitimately run long, and kill them:
- git.push's prepare (617), uploading packs or LFS objects
- the integration worker's `git merge` (integration.rs:128)
- the device-sync `git fetch` (device.rs:1575)
- `git worktree remove --force` on a large tree
Also, output_with_timeout SIGKILLs the whole process group (proc.rs:55). A timed-out add, reset, checkout, switch or commit therefore leaves index.lock behind, and every later git command in that checkout fails until someone deletes it.
v2.correction:
Missed locked caller: worktree.remove (git.rs:129-143, plain register, purge_build defaults to true). Under the lock it runs worktree::remove:
- purge_build: a dir_size walk plus remove_dir_all of target/, build/, .gradle and similar
- dir_size of the whole worktree
- `git worktree remove --force`, then `git worktree prune`
session.close and session.discard_restorable already do this same work in their staged prepare (session.rs:1505, 1547), so worktree.remove and integration.discard are the copies still left under the lock. The first verifier calls integration.discard "the worst instance", but no client in the repo calls integration.discard, worktree.remove, file.restore_head or clean_merged; they are reachable only through `relay cmd` or the phone door's generic forwarding. The severity comes from the UI- and agent-reachable ops: stage/unstage, pr.open, branch.create, branch.delete and commit.

Smaller locked subprocesses the finding misses:
- validate_branch_name (git.rs:1269-1273) runs a bare `git check-ref-format` in branch.create and branch.delete.
- branch.delete and clean_merged also run branches_for (gix merge-base walks) and list_with_dirty under the lock.
- session.update's rename_branch (session.rs:1460) runs two quick git calls under the lock.

Narrow two claims:
- "commit --no-verify still runs prepare-commit-msg/post-commit". In session worktrees, Relay's worktree-local core.hooksPath directory holds only pre-commit (hooks.rs:103, 153; D23), so those hooks run only in checkouts without Relay's hook path, such as the primary checkout. GPG signing applies everywhere.
- "credential prompt". Only network-touching commands can prompt: gh, or an LFS smudge during switch/checkout. With gh as the github.com helper, GitHub HTTPS does not prompt.

Fix refinements:
- Use per-call deadlines, or apply the timeout only where the lock is held. Never put one short deadline inside worktree::git.
- Set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 everywhere.
- For branch.delete and clean_merged, move the branches_for and list_with_dirty reads into prepare as well.
- Put worktree.remove and integration.discard on one staged helper shared with session.close.
- For the commit finish, a timeout must be generous, and the typed error must name the stale index.lock. A cleaner option: write the tree in prepare, then in finish only run `git commit-tree` and `git update-ref HEAD <new> <old>`, which are fast, keeping the ref update atomic with the gate.

Separate lead, not this finding and unverified: D23 chains only pre-commit into Relay's per-worktree hooksPath, so git-lfs's pre-push hook never runs in session worktrees. In an LFS repo, a push from a session worktree uploads no LFS objects. The push is then either rejected by the server (GitHub GH008) or lands pointer files whose objects are missing. Worth its own check.

findings.title: session.done never applies the per-task caps BUS.md §9.2 says it enforces, and agents may run git commit --no-verify, so over-cap work reaches review unchecked
findings.evidence: BUS.md:497 (§9.2) lists `session.done` as an enforcement point: "per-task caps (files, lines) | gate {kind: commit}, git.commit, session.done | refused / guardrail.cap". SPEC.md:134-138 requires per-task caps "enforced in core, never prose". The Done handler (session.rs:1140-1226) contains no guardrail or caps evaluation, and `git log -S guardrail.cap -- session.rs` shows it never had one. At commit time the only enforcement is Relay's pre-commit hook (hooks.rs:116-132), which `git commit --no-verify` skips. `evaluate_exec` (guardrail.rs:811-847) checks only self_approval and `denied_commands`, whose default is ["rm -rf","git reset --hard","git clean -fd","git push --force"] (settings.rs:33). The engine tests call session.done many times (agent_features.rs:207-260, awareness.rs:391-484, phase7.rs:305-313) and none checks caps.
findings.impact: Suppose the pre-commit hook refuses an agent's commit with guardrail.cap, or the agent simply skips hooks. The agent can run `git commit --no-verify` (or `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit`) and then `session.done`. The task moves to in_review with no refusal, hold or notification, silently bypassing a guardrail the spec says core enforces. I could not establish whether the §9.2 row was meant as a hard guarantee or is aspirational.
findings.fix: Either implement the documented check and add a test: stage session.done, diff the session worktree against its base in prepare, evaluate GateKind::Commit caps in finish, refuse guardrail.cap for agents and hold for the user. Or remove session.done from §9.2 and close the hook bypass in the exec gate by treating `commit --no-verify` / `-n` and `-c core.hooksPath=` as denied for agents.

v1.reason: BUS.md:497 (§9.2) lists `session.done` as an enforcement point for per-task caps (refused / guardrail.cap), and the row has been there since fcbdbce. The Done handler (session.rs:1140-1226) has no guardrail or caps evaluation, and complete_group_assignment does not add one either. The cap check exists only in evaluate_commit (guardrail.rs:~792), reached through git.commit, gate{kind:commit} and Relay's pre-commit hook. An agent commits with its own git (BUS.md §9.3), and evaluate_exec (guardrail.rs:811-847) checks only self_approval and denied_commands, whose defaults do not cover `commit --no-verify`/`-n` or `-c core.hooksPath=`. So an over-cap commit made with --no-verify, followed by session.done, moves the task to in_review with no refusal. The code facts are established.
v1.correction: The impact is narrower than 'security high'. The trigger needs an agent that deliberately skips hooks after a cap refusal. The over-cap work is not merged; it lands in in_review, where the user sees the diff. Caps exist to keep review sizes small, and a guardrail.rs comment itself calls agent-side gating best effort ('closes the obvious door, not every door'). The root problem is a documented enforcement point that was never implemented, plus a known hook bypass not in the default exec denials. Rate medium. Fix: either implement the cap check in session.done (staged: diff against base in prepare, evaluate in finish) or correct §9.2, and add the hook-skipping git forms to the agent exec denials.

findings.title: integration.discard (and worktree.remove) purge build dirs, walk and delete the worktree inside the locked transaction
findings.evidence: integration.rs:58-64: `e.register::<IntegrationDiscard>(|ctx: &mut Ctx, p| { ... worktree::remove(Path::new(&project.path), Path::new(path), true) ... git_mutate(... ["branch","-D", ...]) })`. With purge=true, `worktree::remove` (worktree.rs:352-370) runs purge_build (339-349: dir_size plus remove_dir_all over target, build, .gradle, app/build, node_modules/.cache, dist), then dir_size over the whole worktree, then an untimed `git worktree remove --force`, all with the store mutex held. worktree.remove (git.rs:129-140) does the same, since purge_build defaults to true. Contrast session.close (session.rs:1543-1597) and project.remove (workspace.rs:320-345), which keep exactly this disk work off the lock: "deleting checkouts (build purge, git worktree remove) is seconds of disk work". integration.request defaults to `build: true` (integration.rs:32), so a discarded integration of a Rust or Gradle project holds a multi-GB build tree. phase8.rs:519 exercises discard only on a 3-file worktree.
findings.impact: Discarding an integration that ran its build, or removing a worktree from the Worktrees page, freezes every bus request (agent hook calls, UI, phone door) for as long as it takes to measure and delete the target/ tree: seconds to minutes.
findings.fix: Register both ops as staged: run worktree::remove in prepare with the lock released, then mark the row discarded and emit events in finish. Alternatively, mark the row discarded in the transaction and do the removal in after_commit on a worker, as project.remove does.

v1.reason: integration.rs:58-69 registers IntegrationDiscard with plain `e.register` and calls `worktree::remove(project, path, true)` inside it. worktree.rs:352-370 then runs purge_build (dir_size plus remove_dir_all over target/, build/, .gradle and the rest), a dir_size of the whole tree, and `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune` through worktree.rs:26-33's `git()`, which is a bare `Command::output()` with no timeout. git.rs:129-145 (WorktreeRemove) does the same under the lock, with purge_build defaulting to true. By contrast, session.close is register_staged and does this work in its prepare phase. integration.request defaults build to true, so an integration worktree can hold a full target/ tree, and deleting it while holding the store mutex blocks every bus request for seconds. However, the stated reach is overstated: neither op has a caller in apps/relay-native, relay-cli or relay-remote; both are Actors::UserOnly and reachable only by invoking the op directly (the CLI/MCP as the user). There is no 'Worktrees page' that removes a worktree.
v1.correction: No native UI calls worktree.remove or integration.discard (a grep of apps/relay-native/src finds only worktree.list and integration.list/request), so this is a less common path and medium, not high. The lock also covers untimed git subprocesses (worktree.rs:27 `Command::new("git")...output()`, used by remove and git_mutate `branch -D`), which separately breaks the proc::output_with_timeout rule. Fix as proposed (register_staged, with the disk and git work in prepare), and route worktree::git through proc::output_with_timeout.

findings.title: The user's pre-commit hook runs with no timeout, and on guardrail.confirm of a held commit it runs while the store mutex is held
findings.evidence: hooks.rs:210-213: `let output = Command::new(&hook).current_dir(worktree).output()` has no deadline. `output()` waits for EOF on stdout and stderr, so a hook that backgrounds a child hangs it; proc.rs's descendants_cannot_keep_probe_pipes_open_after_parent_exit test guards against exactly this. The hook runs in git.commit's prepare phase (git.rs:555), normally with the lock released. However, guardrail.confirm is a locked handler (handlers/guardrail.rs:339) that replays the held op through `ctx.replay_registered` (583). `invoke_registered` then runs the staged prepare phase with `held: Some(self.tx)` (engine.rs:325-342), so the hook, refresh_git and staged_numstat all run inside confirm's transaction. engine.rs accepts that cost ("It costs what the op cost before the split, and only on this path"), but the cost is unbounded once a user hook is involved. phase8's a_held_commit_still_commits_when_confirmed (528-562) covers this replay path with no hook installed.
findings.impact: Suppose a user with a pre-commit hook (lint-staged, cargo fmt/clippy, the pre-commit framework) commits an over-cap change through Relay. The commit is held as guardrail.user_bypass. On Confirm the hook runs a second time with the global store lock held, freezing all bus traffic for its duration, and forever if it hangs or leaves a background process holding its stdout.
findings.fix: Run the hook through proc::output_with_timeout with a generous, configurable deadline and a typed git.pre_commit_timeout error. Do not run staged prepare phases inside confirm's transaction: for a staged op, resolve the hold, then re-dispatch the frozen request through the normal pipeline (prepare runs unlocked) with skip_policy attached.

v1.reason: hooks.rs:210-213 runs the user's pre-commit hook with `Command::new(&hook).current_dir(worktree).output()`, which has no deadline and waits for EOF on both pipes, so a hook that leaves a background child holding stdout never returns. On the normal git.commit path (git.rs:535-557, register_staged) this runs in prepare, unlocked, but it still breaks the 'every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout' rule. guardrail.confirm is a locked handler (handlers/guardrail.rs:339) that replays the frozen op via ctx.replay_registered (583). engine.rs:323-342 then runs a staged op's prepare 'against the transaction already open' (held: Some(self.tx)), so refresh_git, run_user_pre_commit and staged_numstat all run with the store mutex held. A user commit over the caps or touching a protected path is held as user_bypass (D141, Git panel), and confirming it runs the hook again under the lock, blocking all bus traffic for the hook's duration, or indefinitely if it hangs.
v1.correction: The trigger needs a user commit that gets held (over the caps or on a protected path) in a repo with a user pre-commit hook. That is an uncommon path, so medium is right. Fix as proposed: bound the hook with proc::output_with_timeout, and have confirm resolve the hold and re-dispatch a staged op through the normal pipeline rather than running prepare inside its transaction.

findings.title: session.done with status blocked or partial releases all of the session's claims and deactivates its overlaps, although its task stays current
findings.evidence: Done computes `let session_state = if status == "completed" { "idle" } else { "blocked" };` and then calls `release_claims(ctx, s)?;` for every status. release_claims (248-257) runs `DELETE FROM claims WHERE session_id=?1` and `UPDATE overlaps SET active=0 ...`. BUS.md:734 says blocked/partial "leave only the current task in place, set it blocked, notify agent_blocked" and says nothing about claims. The role instructions (providers.rs:42) say "Declare the files you are taking on with session.claim", and after a blocked report the task stays current, with no queue advance. The hook path for the same situation, session.report {kind:"blocked"} (1349-1414), keeps claims. done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move (agent_features.rs:207-260) never claims anything, and finishing_or_closing_releases_claims_for_the_next_agent (123-138) covers only a completed done. I could not establish author intent; no decision entry covers it.
findings.impact: Agent A claims src/parser.rs, hits a blocker and reports session.done {status:"blocked"}. Peers now see no claim. Agent B's `session.claim {exclusive:true}` on the same file succeeds with no collision, and B starts editing the file A resumes once unblocked. Active overlaps involving A disappear until the next scan.
findings.fix: Release claims only when status == "completed". Extend done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move to claim a path before the blocked report and assert the claim survives.

v1.reason: session.rs:1186-1187 calls `release_claims(ctx, s)?` unconditionally after computing session_state, so a `blocked`/`partial` done deletes every claim the session holds and deactivates its overlaps (release_claims, session.rs:248-257), even though the task stays current and the session is only 'blocked'. git log -L shows release_claims was added in 3674096 ('finishing or closing releases claims'), and its test covers only completed. Neither D118 nor BUS.md:734 says a blocked report gives up claims, while the session.report{kind:blocked} path keeps them. The behaviour is inconsistent with that path and probably unintended.
v1.correction: Severity is low, not medium. Claims are advisory and not enforced (D116), so the consequence is only that a peer's session.claim/peers no longer reports A's files during the blocked interval. The blocked/partial done path is itself uncommon. Fix as proposed: release only on completed, and extend done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move to assert that a claim survives.

findings.title: git/call/ok/Fixture helpers are copy-pasted into 10-17 engine test files and have already diverged
findings.symbol: git / call / ok / Fixture test helpers
findings.evidence: phase7.rs:11-19 `git` runs `.status()` with a bare `assert!(...success())`, so a failure reports neither the args nor stderr. awareness.rs:12-20 runs `.status()` and reports only the args. agent_features.rs:13-16 and phase8.rs:20-33 capture and print stderr. The `ok()` panic formats differ ("{op} failed: ..." vs "{op}: ..."), and phase8 has no `ok()` at all, unwrapping BusError Debug instead. Fixture::new in agent_features.rs:41-71 and awareness.rs:39-109 is the same sequence: tempdir, ws/app, git init/config/commit, Store::open, Engine::new, workspace.create, project.add, a raw INSERT into tasks, two session.create calls. phase7.rs:48-75 and phase8.rs:34-58 repeat the repo half. Across crates/relay-core/tests, `fn git(` appears in 13 files, `fn call(` in 17 and `struct Fixture` in 10, and there is no tests/common module.
findings.impact: Any fixture change has to be repeated 10-17 times: hermetic git config (see the git-config finding), an Engine::new or Store::open signature change, a new NOT NULL column in the raw INSERTs. When a phase7 or awareness fixture git command fails, the panic carries no stderr; the child writes straight to the terminal, interleaved with the other parallel tests.
findings.fix: Add crates/relay-core/tests/common/mod.rs containing: a stderr-capturing git helper, call/ok/refusal/code, a repo() builder that writes hermetic local git config, and a Fixture builder that seeds tasks and sessions through the bus. Add `mod common;` to each test file.

v1.reason: Counts verified: under crates/relay-core/tests, `fn git(` appears in 13 files, `fn call(` in 18 (not 17), and `struct Fixture` in 10, with no tests/common module. The divergence is real. phase7.rs:11-19 and awareness.rs:12-20 use `.status()`, so a failing git command reports no stderr (phase7 does not even report the args). agent_features.rs:13-16 and phase8.rs:20-33 capture stderr. The ok() panic formats differ. The Fixture setup sequence (tempdir, git init/config/commit, Store::open, Engine::new, workspace.create, project.add) is repeated.
v1.correction: Severity is low, not medium. The duplication is confined to test helpers, and the divergence so far is in panic-message quality rather than in behavior. The ongoing cost is real but modest: an Engine::new or Store::open signature change, or adding hermetic git config, means editing about 10-18 files. A tests/common/mod.rs with a stderr-capturing git helper and call/ok is the right fix. Pull in the Fixture only where the files truly share its shape, because their seeds differ (modules, tasks, sessions).

findings.title: The integration test allows only 2.5 s for a background merge, and the watcher test's negative checks rely on fixed 250/350 ms windows
findings.evidence: phase8.rs:500-510: `for _ in 0..100 { ...integration.get...; if matches!(state, "passed"|"failed"|"conflict") { break; } sleep(25ms) } assert_eq!(state, "passed");`. That is 2.5 s in total for a background thread that does set_state, `git worktree add` (production allows that call 120 s, worktree.rs:214), an octopus `git merge` and another set_state, while the other 11 phase8 tests run git in parallel. filesystem_reads_do_not_retrigger_refresh_but_writes_do (603-662) sleeps 250 ms and 350 ms and then asserts that no file.changed arrived. The watcher emits from a per-burst thread that sleeps 125 ms (watch.rs:119-121), so these windows are only 2-3x the delay; the positive checks wait 3 s.
findings.impact: On a loaded CI runner, or a desktop where several agents run cargo builds and tests at once (the normal workload here), the integration test fails with state "merging" although nothing is wrong. When the notify or timer thread is delayed past the window, the watcher's "no refresh" assertions pass without testing anything.
findings.fix: Subscribe before integration.request and wait for the integration.result event with a 30-60 s deadline, or poll with a deadline of that size. In the watcher test, make the 125 ms delay a pub(crate) const and derive the quiet windows from it with a generous multiple.

v1.reason: phase8.rs:499-510 polls integration.get 100 times with 25 ms sleeps, about 2.5 s plus call time, then asserts state == "passed". integration.request spawns a background thread (src/handlers/integration.rs:40) that sets Merging, runs the worktree add and the octopus merge, and records the result. On a tiny repo this normally finishes well under 2.5 s, so the margin is roughly 10-25x. On a heavily loaded machine (parallel cargo test plus agent builds) it can still time out and fail with "merging" although nothing is wrong. The watcher test (phase8.rs:603-662) asserts absence with fixed 250/350 ms windows, against an emitter thread that sleeps 125 ms (src/watch.rs:120). If notify or the timer thread is delayed past the window, those negative checks pass without testing anything. The positive checks have 3 s deadlines, so the asymmetry is real.
v1.correction: The integration test can only flake under heavy load; it is not broken in normal runs, so low severity is correct. In the watcher test, the vacuous negative checks are a coverage gap and not a source of flakes: they never fail spuriously. For the fix, the integration poll should use a deadline of 30 s or more, or wait on the integration.result event subscribed before the request. A pub(crate) debounce constant for the watcher windows would also help.

findings.title: Fixtures seed task state 'working', which is not a TaskState and reads back as none, so the 'queue untouched' check cannot see a reset to none
findings.evidence: agent_features.rs:60-61 inserts `VALUES (1,'Ship the thing','','','active','working',0,?1,?1)`, and awareness.rs:76-77 does the same. TaskState has only None/Dispatched/Running/Blocked/Failed/AwaitingReview (relay-bus types.rs:33-40), and parse_task_state maps anything else with `_ => TaskState::None` (task.rs:61-68). done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move reads `queued_state = task.get(1)["state"]` (line 215), which is "none", and then asserts `task["state"] == queued_state, "blocking the current task must not touch its queue"` (line 225).
findings.impact: If a regression reset queued tasks to `none`, or rewrote the row to any other unknown value, the assertion would still pass, because the fixture's state already reads back as none. The seeded row also holds a value no handler writes, so SQL filters such as `state='none'` and the API disagree about the same task.
findings.fix: Seed a real state (for example 'dispatched', or create and dispatch the task through the bus) and assert the literal expected value instead of a value round-tripped through the API.

v1.reason: agent_features.rs:60-61 seeds state 'working'. TaskState (relay-bus types.rs:33-40) has no such variant, and parse_task_state (task.rs:61-69) maps it to None. In done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move, `queued_state` is read at line 215 after task.update (line 213). The Update handler (task.rs:887-888) writes `state_str(p.state.unwrap_or(before.state))`, so the row is rewritten to 'none' before the snapshot. queued_state is therefore 'none', and the assertion at line 225 cannot tell 'untouched' from 'reset to none'. A regression that marks task 1 blocked would still be caught, so the gap is narrow.
v1.correction: Mechanism detail: by the time of the snapshot the stored value is not 'working'. The agent's task.update has already persisted 'none' through the parse round-trip. That round-trip is a small product quirk in its own right: an unknown stored state is silently rewritten to 'none' on any body edit. Seed a real state such as 'dispatched' (task.update preserves it) and assert the literal value. awareness.rs:77 has the same seed.

findings.title: The mailbox delivery assertion accepts three of the four possible values although the fixture makes the answer deterministic
findings.evidence: awareness.rs:161-164: `assert!(["queued", "session_parked", "not_running"].contains(&broadcast["delivery"].as_str().unwrap()), ...)`. delivery_hint (notes.rs:155-166) has exactly four outcomes: no_recipients, queued, session_parked and not_running. Both fixture sessions are in state `created` (never spawned), and sessions::is_live (sessions.rs:172-174) excludes Created, so the only correct answer is "not_running".
findings.impact: A regression that classifies never-started sessions as live ("queued", telling the sender the message will be read soon) or as parked still passes. The comment's claim that the send "names where the message stands" goes unchecked.
findings.fix: Use `assert_eq!(broadcast["delivery"], "not_running")` and assert that each recipient's state is "created".

v1.reason: awareness.rs:161-164 accepts any of queued, session_parked or not_running. delivery_hint (notes.rs:155-167) returns 'queued' only if a recipient is_live (sessions.rs:172-174: Spawning, Running, Idle or Blocked), 'session_parked' if one is Parked, and 'not_running' otherwise. Both fixture sessions are inserted as 'created' (session.rs:806) and never spawned, and nothing before the send changes their state. The only correct answer is 'not_running', so a regression that reports never-started sessions as 'queued' would pass.

findings.title: Fixtures and the engine's git calls inherit the developer's global git config (core.hooksPath, commit.gpgsign, push.default)
findings.evidence: Only user.name and user.email are set locally (agent_features.rs:48-49, awareness.rs:46-47, phase7.rs:55-56, phase8.rs:39-40). No test pins commit.gpgsign, core.hooksPath, push.default or init.templateDir, and there is no .cargo/config.toml or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL; phase12 sets GIT_CONFIG_COUNT for one subprocess only. install_git falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (hooks.rs:98). In a scratch repo with git 2.55 and a global `core.hooksPath=/home/someone/.githooks`, that command returned the global directory, while `config --worktree --get core.hooksPath` returned nothing.
findings.impact: With a global core.hooksPath, the hook-chaining test chains to the developer's real global pre-commit hook, run_user_pre_commit executes it against the temp repo, and the assertion at phase8.rs:246 fails. v1.reason: real_repo (crates/relay-core/tests/phase8.rs:34-46) sets only user.name and user.email locally. The test at phase8.rs:187-246 writes the user hook into .git/hooks/pre-commit and then asserts that .git/previous-hook-ran exists. install_git (src/hooks.rs:76-99) first reads `config --worktree --get core.hooksPath`, which ignores global config, and then falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`. So a developer with a global hooksPath gets a chained hook that points at the global directory, the repo-local hook never runs, and the assertion at line 246 fails. The author's global config sets none of these today (grep of `git config --global --list` found no hooks/gpg/template keys), so this is a latent hermeticity gap, not a current failure.
v1.correction: Production behavior is correct here: chaining to the global hooks directory matches what git itself would run. The defect is in the test fixture only. The simplest fix is to run the fixture's git, and the test process, with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1. Alternatively, set core.hooksPath=.git/hooks and commit.gpgsign=false locally in real_repo; the same pattern in the other test files (agent_features.rs, awareness.rs, phase7.rs) would need the same change.

findings.title: project.remove never deletes `labels`, so any project that ever had a label can't be removed, and a forced attempt strips live agents' hooks first
findings.evidence: project.remove deletes FK children from a fixed list (workspace.rs:354-375: messages, session_scrollback, claims, task_sessions, sessions, task_commits, attachments, module_unlinked_tasks, tasks, modules, notes, notifications, overlaps, file_trash, integrations, ui_layouts, device_runs, skill_projects, plugin_projects), then runs `ctx.tx().execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1", [pr.id]).bus()?` (380). `labels` is not in the list. Migration v16 declares `labels.project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id)` with no ON DELETE action (store.rs:315-319), and the store runs `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` (store.rs:397). Label rows come from task.create with `labels` (task.rs:745, INSERT at 136-140) and from task.label.add (task.rs:1191-1194). The native board uses both (task_pages.rs:495, 707). task.label.remove only deletes the task_labels row (task.rs:1219), so a label row outlives its last use. I replayed all 20 MIGRATIONS and the 20 project.remove DELETEs in sqlite3 with foreign_keys=ON and one labelled task: `DELETE FROM projects` fails with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. No test creates a label: not registry_remove.rs, and not bus.rs:958-976, which covers only tasks, notes and skills.
findings.impact: Once a project has ever had a label, project.remove (with or without force) and workspace.remove{force} fail with `internal: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. The project can't be removed without editing the DB by hand. With force it is worse. Before the failing DELETE, each nested session.close (workspace.rs:327-329, remove_worktree:false) has already run its prepare phase: run_teardown strips the session's git, Claude and Codex hooks, and remove_hook_dir deletes its hook dir (session.rs:1573-1596). The rollback cannot undo those file changes. Its finish phase has also called take_pty on the live PTY and queued the kill as after_commit (session.rs:1602-1607). The rollback drops that closure. Then either Pty::drop SIGKILLs the agent (pty.rs:381-390) and its exit callback marks it exited, or, when an attached terminal holds another Arc, the agent keeps running outside the engine's PTY map and session.input answers session.not_spawned. Every retry repeats this.
findings.fix: Add "DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1" after the tasks delete (task_labels cascades). Add a test that walks PRAGMA foreign_key_list for every table referencing projects, tasks or sessions and fails when one is not covered. Add a labelled task (and a message, claim, overlap, ui_layout and file_trash row) to the registry_remove fixture. Run the metadata deletes, or a removability check, before the nested session.close calls, so a failure can't leave live agents without their hooks and outside the PTY map.

v1.reason: Migration v16 creates labels.project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) with no ON DELETE action (store.rs:315-319), and foreign_keys=ON is set on every connection (store.rs:397, 414). Label rows are created by label_id() (task.rs:124-141) from task.create and task.label.add. Nothing in relay-core ever runs DELETE FROM labels: task.rs:431 and :1219 delete only task_labels rows. project.remove's delete list (workspace.rs:354-375) omits labels before DELETE FROM projects (380), so the FK fails and the request rolls back for any project that has ever had a label. workspace.remove{force} reaches the same path through invoke_registered (workspace.rs:173). The force side effects also hold. invoke_registered runs session.close's prepare phase inline (engine.rs:328-348), and that phase runs run_teardown and remove_hook_dir: filesystem changes that the rollback cannot undo. The finish phase take_pty()s the live PTY and moves it into an after_commit closure (session.rs:1601-1606). On rollback the after_commit list is dropped (engine.rs:1073 rolls back with no closures run), which drops the Arc<Pty>; if it was the last handle, Pty::drop SIGKILLs the agent (pty.rs:381-390). Either way the PTY has left the engine's map while the session row stays live.
v1.correction: Fix: add "DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1" after the tasks delete (task_labels cascades from both sides). Also run the removable-metadata checks and deletes, or at least a FK-coverage check, before the nested session.close calls. Add a labelled task to the registry_remove fixture. Of the tables referencing projects, labels is the only one without ON DELETE CASCADE that the list misses.

v2.reason:
(a) Confirmed, and I reproduced it. Migration v16 (store.rs:315-319) creates `labels.project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id)` with no ON DELETE action. No later migration or trigger changes that. foreign_keys=ON is set by both Store::open (store.rs:397) and open_memory (store.rs:414). Label rows are inserted by label_id() (task.rs:124-141), reached from task.create's `labels` (task.rs:745) and from task.label.add (task.rs:1191). Nothing in the repo ever runs DELETE FROM labels: set_labels (task.rs:431) and task.label.remove (task.rs:1219) delete only task_labels rows. project.remove's delete list (workspace.rs:354-375) omits labels, then runs `DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1` (workspace.rs:380).

I extracted all 20 MIGRATIONS and the handler's 20 DELETE strings verbatim and replayed them in sqlite3 with foreign_keys=ON:
- No label: the remove commits.
- Labelled task: `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.
- Label later removed from its task: also fails, because the label row persists.
- With `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?` added after the tasks delete: all three cases commit.

A walk of the FK graph over every table the handler deletes shows labels is the only non-cascading child the list misses.
