Both the list and the labels table date to fcbdbce. plugin_projects (9b4a327) was added to the list later; labels never was. No test covers it: neither registry_remove.rs nor bus.rs:958-976 creates a label, and board.rs exercises labels but never removes a project.

(b) Reachable in normal use. Labels come from an ordinary field on the native create form (task_pages.rs:495) and from task.label.add (task_pages.rs:707). The native Remove dialog always sends `force: true` (registry.rs:626) for project.remove and for workspace.remove. workspace.remove reaches project.remove through invoke_registered (workspace.rs:173). Once a project has ever had a label, every removal attempt fails, and so does removal of its whole workspace.

(c) The dialog shows `internal: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` (IntoBus maps it to internal, engine.rs:1413-1416). The project can't be removed, and nothing in the app can fix that: no op deletes label rows, and task deletion or label removal leaves them in place. The only way out is hand-editing store.db with the engine stopped (EXCLUSIVE lock).

With live agents the force path also leaves a mess. invoke_registered runs session.close's prepare phase inline (engine.rs:328-348). That phase runs run_teardown, which uninstalls the git, Claude and Codex hooks (session.rs:352-362, 1575), and remove_hook_dir (session.rs:1596). Both are file changes the rollback cannot undo. Finish calls take_pty and moves the Arc into an after_commit closure (session.rs:1602-1606). On the ordinary failure path, dispatch_inner rolls back and drops after_commit without running it (engine.rs:1073-1093). The DB stays consistent, so there is no data loss.

(d) High is right: a deterministic, permanent failure of a normal registry flow, with no workaround in the app. Not critical: no data is lost or corrupted, and project removal is infrequent.

(e) The core fix is correct and complete; I verified it in the replay. The ordering part of the fix is wrong as written; see correction.
v2.correction:
1. Impact branch is wrong. The finding says that when an attached terminal holds another Arc, the agent keeps running outside the PTY map. In fact the socket attach task (socket.rs:469-497) captures only `pty.attach()`'s `Attached { rx }`, a broadcast receiver, so the Arc<Pty> drops at the end of the match arm. Every other engine.pty() caller is request-scoped. The dropped closure therefore holds the last handle. Pty::drop SIGKILLs the agent's process group at once (pty.rs:381-390), skipping the SIGTERM grace that kill_detached gives.

2. What actually happens to the sessions. The exit callback is not silenced, so it marks the row 'exited', not 'closed' (session.rs:646-676). For a Builder whose task sits in the active column, it also marks that task 'failed'. The title's "strips live agents' hooks" overstates this: agents are not left running without hooks. They die moments after teardown, which the user had confirmed in the dialog. The real damage is the unclean end state and a spurious failed task.

3. Additional irreversible effect. The nested device.run.stop (workspace.rs:349, device.rs:263-267) kills the run's child process and drops its runtime and leases inline. The rollback reverts its state='stopped' update.

4. "Every retry repeats this" applies only to the failure. The destructive part happens once: the rows are now 'exited', take_pty finds nothing, and teardown is a no-op.

5. Fix. Add `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1` anywhere before the projects delete; task_labels cascades. Add a test that walks PRAGMA foreign_key_list, and put a labelled task in the registry_remove fixture. Do NOT move the metadata deletes ahead of the nested session.close calls. Both of its phases re-read the session row (sessions::by_name / by_id) and get_project, so they would fail not_found. Use a pre-flight check instead, for example running the deletes in a SAVEPOINT and rolling it back. Better still, have session.close's finish phase call engine.pty() and do the take_pty inside the after_commit closure, so a rollback leaves the PTY in the map.

findings.title: project.clone runs `git clone` inside a locked handler with no timeout and prompts left on, freezing the whole bus for the clone
findings.evidence: `e.register::<ProjectClone>` (workspace.rs:228) is a plain locked handler. Line 234 runs `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()`. It does not go through proc::output_with_timeout and does not set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, which every other git network call sets (git.rs:943, git.rs:1349, worktree.rs:213, branch_cleanup.rs:114). The op is documented as "Clone a repo into the workspace and register it (async; project.changed when done)" (crates/relay-bus/src/ops/workspace.rs:37-38), and BUS.md §14 says slow work returns a handle. The native client already allows this op 1800 s (apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:67), and onboarding calls it with a GitHub clone_url (onboarding.rs:527).
findings.impact: Cloning a real repository from onboarding or add-project holds the single store mutex for the whole network transfer. That is minutes for a large or LFS-heavy repo, and forever if git or ssh waits on a credential or host-key prompt (engine started from a terminal, or a GUI credential helper). Every other request queues behind it: the UI, and every agent's guardrail.gate. The Claude PreToolUse hook has a 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:349-352), and the relay CLI exits 5, which is non-blocking, on failure (relay-cli main.rs:104-115). So after 30 s, agents' Bash, Edit and Write calls go ahead without the guardrail check until the clone ends. phase12's two clone tests clone a local path or a local ext helper in milliseconds, so they can't show this.
findings.fix: Use register_staged, or make it truly async as documented. Run the clone in the prepare phase through proc::output_with_timeout with a long bound, stdin null, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes'; the finish phase only does project.add. For the documented async shape, return a handle and emit project.changed from a worker.

v1.reason: ProjectClone is registered with plain e.register (workspace.rs:228), and line 234 runs Command::new("git")...arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output(). That is not proc::output_with_timeout, and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is not set, whereas git.rs:943/1349, worktree.rs:213 and branch_cleanup.rs:114 all set it. The whole network clone therefore runs with the single store mutex held and with no upper bound. The op metadata says "async; project.changed when done" (ops/workspace.rs:37-38), but the implementation is synchronous. The client already allows it 1800 s (client.rs:67). A large clone, or git/ssh waiting on /dev/tty or an askpass helper for credentials or a host key, freezes the UI and every agent's guardrail.gate for the duration. This clearly breaks a CLAUDE.md invariant and freezes the bus.
v1.correction: One sub-claim is wrong. The relay CLI does not exit 5 (non-blocking) on PreToolUse failure: the ClaudePreTool and CodexPreTool hook paths deliberately map every error to exit 2, which blocks (relay-cli main.rs:348-357). So engine unavailability fails closed. Only Claude Code's own 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:351) could let tool calls proceed unchecked, and how Claude Code treats a timed-out hook was not established here. The concrete impact is that agent tool calls stall or are blocked, plus the UI freezes, for the length of the clone. Output::output() already nulls stdin, but git/ssh prompt through /dev/tty or askpass, so the prompt hang still stands. Fix as proposed: register_staged with the clone in the prepare phase through proc::output_with_timeout, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and ssh BatchMode, and only project.add in the finish phase.

v2.reason:
(a) The claim holds. ProjectClone is registered with plain `e.register` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:228). Nothing else registers it: there is no prepare stage and no unlocked variant. `dispatch_inner` takes `self.store.lock()` (a plain std Mutex with no timeout, store.rs:474), opens a transaction and then calls the handler (engine.rs:953-980). The handler runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()` at workspace.rs:234, with no `proc::output_with_timeout` and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. Both CLAUDE.md invariants are broken. It also contradicts the documented contract: the op meta says "async; project.changed when done" (ops/workspace.rs:38), and BUS.md §5.1 (lines 228 and 246) lists project.clone among the ops that return a handle. D149 converted git.fetch, git.push and worktree.create but missed this op. It has been locked since the initial commit fcbdbce. The perf baseline only timed a local clone (263 ms).

(b) Reachability. The trigger is the user adding a project by cloning from GitHub. `onboarding::open` serves first run and also "Add workspace / Add project to <ws>" (onboarding.rs:27-35, app.rs:1695), so a clone can start while agent sessions are live. That happens once per cloned project. The op is UserOnly, so agents cannot trigger it. The lock is held for the whole network transfer plus LFS smudge downloads: seconds for small repos, minutes for large or LFS-heavy ones.

An indefinite hang is possible under narrower conditions. Onboarding clones the HTTPS `clone_url`. Relay's own `gh auth login` runs with stdin set to null (github.rs:57-62), so it does not install gh as git's credential helper. A private repo with no other credential helper therefore makes git prompt:
- With the engine run from a terminal (`relay serve`), git prompts on /dev/tty and waits until the user finds the prompt.
- An askpass or GCM dialog waits for an answer.
- Under the systemd user unit with no tty and no askpass, git fails fast instead.

(c) Effects. Everything that touches the store queues behind the clone:
- every locked op;
- unlocked queries, at their short `Unlocked::read` burst;
- every agent socket request, at `check_session_token`, which locks the store (engine.rs:1377-1378) before dispatch;
- `guardrail.gate`, a plain locked handler (guardrail.rs:304), so every agent's PreToolUse hook stalls;
- the phone door and system writes.

User keystrokes are exempt: D148 handles them in memory, and each terminal pane has its own connection (terminal.rs:476).

The native UI is hit twice. project.clone goes over the shared main UI connection (app.rs:1111-1116); it is not in `is_lifecycle_request` (client.rs:50-63). The socket door handles one connection's requests strictly in order (socket.rs:335-744 awaits each dispatch). So every other UI refresh or action fails after 30 s (client.rs:70) with "Request timed out" for as long as the clone runs. No data is lost.

(d) High is right: the rubric names "a freeze of the bus or the UI" in a normal flow. It would only rise to critical in the conditional prompt-hang case, or if Claude Code lets a timed-out hook through. Neither was established.

(e) Staging the clone is the right direction and frees agents, the phone door and other connections. On its own it is incomplete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
1. The guardrail-bypass sub-claim is wrong as written. The CLI does not exit 5 on a pre-tool failure: errors map to exit 2, which blocks (relay-cli main.rs:348-357), so a failure fails closed. However, the CLI has no deadline of its own: `socket::Client::call` waits forever (socket.rs:801-819). Only Claude Code's 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:351) ends the wait, and this repo does not show whether Claude Code then blocks or allows the tool call. The established impact is that agent tool calls stall for the length of the clone.

2. "Every other git network call sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0" is overstated. `github::download_skills` (github.rs:106-110, called from skill.install's staged prepare) runs `git clone` via `.output()` with neither prompt suppression nor a timeout. That runs unlocked, so it is not part of this freeze.

3. "Freezes the whole bus" should exclude user keystrokes (D148 fast path, per-pane connections). PTY typing keeps working. Everything that takes the store lock does not.

4. Gaps in the proposed fix:
   - (i) The UI still freezes after staging. The socket door serializes requests per connection, and the native client sends project.clone on its shared main connection. Send it on its own connection, as `is_lifecycle_request`/`lifecycle_request` already do for lifecycle ops, or make the op truly async: return a handle, then finish on a worker that emits project.changed and writes a `project.clone.completed` audit row, as BUS.md §5.1 describes.
   - (ii) Once unlocked, two clones to the same destination can race between the `destination.exists()` check and `git clone`. The existing failure cleanup could then delete another clone's directory. Create the destination atomically with `fs::create_dir`, clone into the empty directory, and only remove what this call created.
   - (iii) `output_with_timeout` SIGKILLs the process group at the deadline, so git cannot remove its partial directory. The prepare phase must remove it on timeout or failure, or a retry hits `project.clone_destination` "already exists".
   - (iv) GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 does not disable askpass (GIT_ASKPASS, core.askPass, SSH_ASKPASS) or GUI credential helpers. Set GIT_ASKPASS to empty, or accept a GUI prompt deliberately. That is harmless once the clone is unlocked and bounded.
   - (v) Keep the bound long, in line with the client's 1800 s, because LFS-heavy clones legitimately take that long.

findings.title: device.run.stop kills only the wrapper shell, so Gradle keeps building and installing after Stop while the device lease goes to the next session
findings.evidence: `RunRuntime::stop` is `self.stop.store(true, …); if let Some(child) = self.child.lock().unwrap().as_mut() { let _ = child.kill(); }` (device.rs:403-408). The child is the wrapper shell. stream_command spawns `Command::new(shell).current_dir(root).args(["-lc", &format!("{command} 2>&1")])` with shell = fish (sh under Instance::Test) and no process_group (handlers/device.rs:1821-1828). In one request, device.run.stop removes the runtime, calls stop() and releases the run's lease (handlers/device.rs:265-270). The worker returns Streamed::Stopped on the next output line and closes the pipe (1842-1845). I checked in a scratch shell: both `fish -c 'sleep 3 2>&1'` and `sh -c 'sleep 3 2>&1'` fork sleep as a child (ps shows its parent is the shell), so killing the shell leaves the command running. build_worker uses the same stream_command (1902-1914).
findings.impact: Stopping a 'Build & install' run reports the run stopped and gives the device lease to the next session, but `./gradlew installDebug` keeps building. Gradle is a JVM that ignores the closed pipe, so it then installs over whatever the next lease holder just put on the phone. That is exactly the clobber the lease exists to prevent. project.remove with force and Engine::shutdown at quit (engine.rs:637-640) behave the same way. Stopping a release build with publish does not stop the Play upload. In device_lease.rs:181-185 the stopped `sleep 30` is orphaned for 30 s and holds the worker thread; the test can't see it because it only checks the lease.
findings.fix: Spawn the run shell with `process_group(0)` and make stop() signal the group: `kill(-pid, SIGTERM)`, then SIGKILL after a grace period, then wait. proc::output_with_timeout and Pty::kill already do this. Release the run lease from the worker once the group is gone, not in the RunStop request. Add a test that the run's descendants are dead after device.run.stop.

v1.reason: RunRuntime::stop (device.rs:403-408) sets the flag and calls child.kill() (SIGKILL) on the direct child only. stream_command (handlers/device.rs:1820-1828) spawns `fish -lc "<command> 2>&1"` in production (sh under Instance::Test) with no process group. fish does not exec its last command, so gradlew/java survives as an orphan. RunStop (265-270) removes the runtime, calls stop() and releases the run's lease all in the same request, so another session can take the device at once while the orphaned build/install continues. stream_command then returns Stopped on its next line (1842-1845), and nothing waits on or signals the descendants. Engine::shutdown (engine.rs:637-640) and build_worker (1902-1914, release builds) share the same path. A second gap makes it worse: a stop that arrives after spawn() but before runtime.set_child (1840) finds no child at all, so the shell itself runs to completion.
v1.correction: How Gradle behaves after its stdout reader goes away (EPIPE) was not verified. The general consequence is established either way: the command keeps running after Stop and the lease is already released. The clobber needs a second session to install inside that window. Fix: spawn with process_group(0) and signal -pgid (TERM, then KILL), as proc::output_with_timeout does. Release the run lease from the worker once the group has exited, and handle stop() racing set_child. The killed shell is also never waited on (it becomes a zombie until the runtime drops).

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. RunRuntime::stop (device.rs:403-408) sets the flag and calls Child::kill, which sends SIGKILL to the direct child only. stream_command (handlers/device.rs:1821-1828) spawns `fish -lc "<command> 2>&1"` (sh under Instance::Test) with no process_group. I checked this here with fish 4.9.3: `fish -c 'sleep 17.31 2>&1'` forks sleep as its child, and after SIGKILL of fish the sleep keeps running (reparented to the user subreaper). bash-as-sh does the same, because the redirect turns off its exec optimisation. The default command is `./gradlew [--init-script ...] install<Variant>` (run_command, :1037-1055). A standard gradlew ends in `exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"`, so the surviving child is the Gradle client JVM. I also checked a JVM writing to a pipe whose reader exits after one line: it ran to completion, and System.out.checkError() was true. So the client survives the worker dropping the pipe at :1843-1844, and the daemon's build and install go on. In the same request, RunStop (:265-270) removes the runtime, kills the shell, releases the run lease and marks the row stopped.

(b) Reachable in the main flow, by the user, every time Stop is pressed while a run is in the 'building' state in production. This is deterministic, not a race. Stop is offered in three places in the native client: agent_menu.rs:652/662 next to "Build & install", and tools_devices.rs:212 and :847. Two more paths stop runs the same way: project.remove with force (workspace.rs:349) and Engine::shutdown (engine.rs:637-640). The lease design leads straight to the clobber. A run lease cannot be released except by "device.run.stop; its lease goes with it" (device_lease handler :48). Blocked agents are told to `bus.wait` on device.lease.released and retry (device_lease.rs:149). So an agent waiting with a built APK installs within seconds of the Stop, and the stopped Gradle's installDebug (run with `-d`, downgrade allowed) lands later on top of it.

(c) The UI tells the user "Stopped before the install finished." (agent_menu.rs:779) and turns Build & install back on (:720). Gradle actually keeps building, burning CPU and holding the daemon, so a re-run spawns a second daemon and competes in the same build dir. It then installs the app anyway. When it lands after another holder's install, the device runs the wrong build while that session's logcat and testing assume its own. A release build with publish keeps uploading to Play after Stop (build_worker :1902-1914). This breaks the documented contract BUS.md:869 ("also stops a build") and departs from the D18 teardown pattern used for PTYs.

(d) High is right. It is user-visible wrong behaviour in a normal flow, and a safety mechanism (the device lease) is silently bypassed. There is no loss of user data and no security impact, so not critical.

(e) The fix direction is right: process_group(0) plus signalling -pgid, as proc.rs:32/55 and pty.rs:348-358 already do. It is incomplete as written, though; see the correction.
v2.correction:
1. The pre-spawn gap is wider than the race between spawn() and set_child. For primary-checkout runs, run_worker first calls sync_primary_checkout, which does a network `git fetch` (:1575). That can take seconds, and the row already shows 'building' with Stop visible. A Stop in that window finds no child. stream_command never checks stopped() before spawning, so it spawns the full Gradle command anyway, stores it with set_child, returns Stopped on the first line and drops it. Neither the shell nor Gradle is ever signalled. The fix must check stopped() after sync and immediately after set_child, and kill the group if it is set.

2. The grace period must not run inside RunStop. That handler is registered with Engine::register, so it holds the store mutex, and a SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL, wait sequence in stop() would freeze the bus (CLAUDE.md invariant). Send SIGTERM to the group in the handler, since that is cheap. Do the grace, the SIGKILL, the reap and the lease release on the worker or an after_commit thread; Engine::shutdown may wait. Do not tie the lease release to EOF on the blocked line reader, because a daemonised grandchild can hold the pipe open. Wait on the group leader and poll kill(-pgid, 0) until ESRCH, with a time bound.

3. The Gradle daemon detaches into its own session, so a group kill reaches only the client JVM. Stopping the build then depends on the daemon cancelling when its client disconnects, and an adb install already in flight may still finish. That remaining window is inherent and acceptable.

4. After Stopped, the SIGKILLed shell is never waited on. Each stopped run leaves one zombie for the engine's lifetime. This is minor and fixed by reaping it.

5. The device_lease.rs:181-185 test point holds on this machine, where sh is bash and forks the redirected `sleep 30`. On dash, sh probably execs the command, in which case the kill works. Either way the test checks only the lease and never checks that the process is gone.

findings.title: avd.create and avd.boot run Android SDK tools with no timeout while holding the store mutex, and booted emulators are never reaped
findings.evidence: `e.register::<AvdCreate>` (device.rs:321) spawns `avdmanager create avd --name … --package …` and blocks in `child.wait_with_output()` (332-335) with the store mutex held. It then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339), which runs `Command::new(emulator).arg("-list-avds").output()` (478) and, for each running emulator, `Command::new(adb).args(["-s", serial, "emu", "avd", "name"]).output()` (505). None of these goes through proc::output_with_timeout. `AvdBoot` (344-349) runs the same list_avds under the lock. Its after_commit `command.spawn()` (353-358) drops the Child without ever waiting on it. avd.catalog (315: `avdmanager list device -c` via `.output()`) and avd.list (478, 505) don't hold the lock but have no timeout either.
findings.impact: Every avd.create freezes the whole bus while avdmanager's JVM runs, which takes seconds. A stalled avdmanager or emulator, or `adb emu` against a hung or booting emulator console, freezes it indefinitely; agents' guardrail hooks then fail open after 30 s, as described for project.clone. Each emulator started by avd.boot becomes a zombie of the engine when it exits. phase12's AVD test uses fakes that exit instantly, so it can't catch any of this.
findings.fix: Use register_staged for avd.create and avd.boot (or register_unlocked plus an after_commit worker). Read settings under the lock, then run every SDK tool through proc::output_with_timeout; its null stdin makes avdmanager's custom-profile prompt take its default. Start the emulator in its own process group from a thread that waits on it. Route list_avds_with, running_avds_with and avd.catalog through output_with_timeout as well.

v1.reason: AvdCreate is registered with e.register (handlers/device.rs:321). It spawns avdmanager and blocks in wait_with_output (332-335), then calls list_avds(ctx.tx()) (339). That runs `emulator -list-avds` via .output() (478) and `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` via .output() for every running emulator (505). All of this happens inside the transaction with the store mutex held and no output_with_timeout. AvdBoot (344-349) also calls list_avds under the lock. Its after_commit spawn (353-358) drops the Child, and the engine has no SIGCHLD/waitpid reaping (rg found none), so each emulator leaves a zombie when it exits. avd.catalog (315) and avd.list (478/505 via list_avds_with) are unlocked but unbounded. The handler itself shows the intended pattern: list_avds_with's doc cites D144 for running these calls with nothing locked.
v1.correction: Severity is lowered to medium. avd.create and avd.boot are rare, user-initiated actions, and the normal cost is a freeze of a few seconds (avdmanager's JVM start), not an indefinite one. avdmanager's prompt cannot hang, because wait_with_output closes stdin after `no\n`. An indefinite hang needs a stalled tool or a hung emulator console answering `adb emu`. session.input bypasses the store lock (engine.rs:1261-1277), so keystrokes keep working; what freezes is every other bus request, including guardrail gates. The claim that the guardrail fails open after 30 s was not verified. The zombie is one per boot and lasts until the engine exits. Fix: register_staged / register_unlocked, and route every SDK call through output_with_timeout.

findings.title: A shell device lease drops to 90 s on any PostToolUse or Stop, including a background install's own PostToolUse
findings.evidence: `command_finished(engine, session_id, command, turn_ended)` is `if turn_ended || command.is_some_and(|command| device_lease::device_command(command).is_some()) { engine.device_leases.shell_finished(session_id); }` (handlers/device_lease.rs:137-141). `shell_finished` caps every Shell lease of the session at now + SHELL_GRACE, 90 s (device_lease.rs:253-261). session.report calls it for every `tool_use` (Claude or Codex PostToolUse) and every `stop` (session.rs:1379-1383; hooks.rs:355-360 map PostToolUse to tool_use). The hook payload carries `tool_input.run_in_background`, but nothing reads it. device_lease.rs:118-122 pins this behaviour: the lease taken for `adb … install` is shortened by the PostToolUse of a different command, `adb … shell am start`.
findings.impact: Three common cases cut an agent's device lease to 90 s in the middle of an install. It runs a long `./gradlew installDebug` with run_in_background, where PostToolUse fires as soon as the job starts. It runs a quick `adb shell …` in parallel with a long install. Or it ends its turn while the install is still running. After 90 s another session's install is admitted with no device.busy and lands mid-install. That is the clobber the lease exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Record which command took each shell lease (tool_use_id or command text) and shorten only that lease on its own PostToolUse. Ignore PostToolUse for run_in_background calls and let SHELL_RUNNING or the background shell's completion end the lease. On Stop, don't shorten leases whose background commands are still running. Add tests where a background install's lease survives its own PostToolUse and a parallel command's.

v1.reason: session.report calls command_finished for every tool_use and every stop (session.rs:1379-1383). command_finished (handlers/device_lease.rs:137-141) calls shell_finished(session_id) when the turn ended or when the finished command is any device command. shell_finished (device_lease.rs:253-261) caps every Shell lease the session holds at now+90 s, not just the lease that command took. Nothing reads tool_input.run_in_background (rg finds no reference in hooks or lease code). With Claude Code's Bash run_in_background, PostToolUse fires as soon as the job starts. A background `./gradlew installDebug` therefore drops to a 90 s lease while it is still building or installing, and so does any lease when the turn's Stop arrives while that background job runs. The test at tests/device_lease.rs:114-118 shortens the lease from `adb install` with the PostToolUse of a different command (`adb shell am start`), which pins the cross-command behavior. Once the lease lapses, another session's install passes the gate without device.busy.
v1.correction: The parallel-command case needs the other command to be device-writing too (device_command must match it), not any `adb shell`. The foreground Stop case cannot happen, because Stop only arrives after a foreground tool returns; it applies to background commands only. Fix: key a shell lease to the tool_use_id or command that took it, and ignore PostToolUse (and Stop) for run_in_background commands. Let SHELL_RUNNING expire them, or end them when the background shell completes.

findings.title: Branch cleanup can delete a user's own branch, locally and on GitHub, when a session ran in the primary checkout or on an existing branch
findings.evidence: candidates() selects every closed session's branch with `WHERE s.state = 'closed' AND s.branch != '' AND s.branch != p.base_branch …` (branch_cleanup.rs:76-79). Nothing checks that Relay created the branch. session.create records the checkout's existing branch for `worktree:"primary"` (session.rs:860-863) and for explicit paths (878-887), and accepts an explicit `branch` that may be a user branch (867). Unreal projects put every session in the primary checkout by default (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18 `"default_checkout": "primary"`, D160). evaluate() deletes the branch with `update-ref -d refs/heads/<branch>` once it is an ancestor of the base (246-248, 314). When gh reports a merged PR whose head is the tip, it also runs `git push <remote> --delete <branch>` (322-331). Every test in branch_cleanup.rs uses pooled relay/* sessions.
findings.impact: Example: a user works on `develop` (or any feature branch) in an Unreal project's main checkout and runs sessions there. Once that branch is merged and the checkout is switched back to main, the 20-minute sweep or the next git.pr.list deletes `develop` locally. After a develop→main PR, it deletes it on GitHub too. Relay never created that branch, and the module doc describes cleanup of the `relay/<name>` branches sessions leave behind.
findings.fix: Only consider branches Relay created for the session: branch == worktree::branch_for(name), or a created_branch flag set in session.create. At minimum, only consider sessions whose worktree is under pool_dir. Never delete a remote branch Relay didn't push. Add a test with a primary-checkout session on a user branch to branch_cleanup.rs.

v1.reason: candidates() (branch_cleanup.rs:74-79) selects every closed session's branch except the project's base branch, with no check that Relay created it. session.create (session.rs:859-863) records the primary checkout's current branch for worktree "primary". That is the default for Unreal projects (plugins.rs:210-213, plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18). It records a chosen worktree's branch for explicit paths (878-887) and reattaches an existing p.branch for "new" (867-870). evaluate() keeps a branch only while it is checked out (primary, an open session's worktree, or outside the pool) (219-233). Once the user switches the primary checkout back to main, a merged user branch such as `develop` is no longer checked out, so evaluate() runs `update-ref -d` on it (314). When gh reports a merged PR whose head is the tip and ls-remote still shows that tip, it runs `git push <remote> --delete` (322-331). The module doc describes cleaning up `relay/<name>` branches, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:40-41 says no cleanup path silently deletes a branch. So this is not an intended decision. No commits are lost, because the branch is merged. But deleting a long-lived branch on GitHub (for example develop after a develop->main PR) also closes or retargets open PRs based on it.
v1.correction: Scope candidates to branches Relay created, either branch == worktree::branch_for(session name) or a flag recorded at create time when the "new" path made a fresh branch. A primary-checkout session, or one reattached to an existing branch, should never be a candidate. Add a test with a primary-checkout session on a non-relay branch.

findings.title: workspace.discover is a query but walks the directory tree with the store mutex held; the phase12 test walks the developer's real tree
findings.evidence: workspace.discover is a query (crates/relay-bus/src/ops/workspace.rs:12-13) but is registered with `e.register::<WsDiscover>` (workspace.rs:114). So `discover_repositories` (393-413) runs inside the transaction with the store mutex held. It is a recursive read_dir to depth 4 that skips only .git, .relay, node_modules, target, build, .gradle and symlinks. With no path it starts from the process's working directory via suggested_workspace (72-87), which is $HOME for a desktop-launched engine. phase12.rs:33-37 calls it with `{}`, so the test walks the developer's real tree above the checkout (~/dev3 from the main checkout). It computes the expected path by re-implementing suggested_workspace_from, which workspace.rs:437-453 already unit-tests.
findings.impact: Discovering a large folder holds the store for seconds on a warm cache and much longer on a cold one, while every agent gate and UI op waits. Examples: a home directory with caches and registries, or a workspace full of checkouts. The onboarding and add-workspace dialog calls it on every path change (onboarding.rs:336). The test's result depends on directories outside the repo.
findings.fix: Register it with register_unlocked; it needs no store access. Bound the walk: skip dot-directories and cap the entry count. Point the phase12 test at a temp tree with known repositories and assert the repositories list.

v1.reason: workspace.discover is declared OpMeta::query (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:12-13), but it is registered with e.register::<WsDiscover> (workspace.rs:114), so it runs inside the locked transaction. The handler never touches ctx. discover_repositories (393-413) is a recursive read_dir to depth 4 that skips only .git/.relay/node_modules/target/build/.gradle and symlinks; dot-directories such as ~/.cache and ~/.local are walked. With no path it starts from suggested_workspace() (72-87), which is the process cwd or a git checkout's parent. That is typically $HOME for a desktop-launched engine. Walking that while holding the store mutex blocks every other request, including guardrail.gate. phase12.rs:33-37 calls it with {} and re-derives the expected path the same way suggested_workspace_from does, so the test walks the real directory tree around the checkout.
v1.correction: The native client calls it when the setup step is built (onboarding.rs:319) and when the Scan button is clicked (onboarding.rs:173), not on every path change. Fix: register_unlocked (the handler needs no store), skip dot-directories, cap the entry count, and point the phase12 test at a temp tree.

findings.title: workspace.discover fails entirely on the first unreadable subdirectory
findings.evidence: `walk` applies `?` to every read: `for entry in fs::read_dir(path)? { let entry = entry?; if !entry.file_type()?.is_dir() …; walk(&entry.path(), depth + 1, out)?; }` (workspace.rs:394-408). The caller maps any error to `workspace.discover_failed` (410).
findings.impact: One unreadable directory within four levels makes discovery return an error and list nothing: a root-owned docker volume, another user's directory, or lost+found. Onboarding then can't suggest any repository in that workspace.
findings.fix: Skip entries whose read_dir or file_type fails, logging at debug level, instead of propagating the error.

v1.reason: walk (workspace.rs:394-408) applies ? to fs::read_dir(path), to each entry, and to entry.file_type(). The caller maps any io error to workspace.discover_failed (410), discarding everything found so far. One EACCES directory within four levels is enough to make discovery return an error and no repositories: a root-owned volume dir, another user's home under a chosen /home, or a dot-dir under $HOME since dot-dirs are not skipped. So is a directory that disappears mid-walk (ENOENT).
v1.correction: Skip and log entries whose read_dir or file_type fails instead of propagating. This can be done together with #7 (move the walk off the lock, skip dot-dirs, cap entries).

findings.title: A finished or failed run writes its terminal state before dropping its lease; the device_lease test races that window
findings.evidence: fail_run is `let _ = advance_run(engine, runtime.id, parent, "failed", true); engine.device_runs.lock().unwrap().remove(&runtime.id); super::device_lease::release_run(engine, runtime.id);` (handlers/device.rs:2155-2160). The normal finish does the same (1789-1793). prune keeps a Run lease while its id is still in device_runs (handlers/device_lease.rs:94-96). device_lease.rs:196-203 polls device.run.list until state is `failed`, then immediately asserts device.leases is empty.
findings.impact: Between the commit and the map removal, a client that already reads the run as failed or finished is still refused with device.busy '…it is device run N, which holds the device until it stops'. The test fails if the worker thread is preempted in that window, for example on a loaded CI runner.
findings.fix: Remove the runtime and release the lease before writing the terminal state. In the test, wait for the lease release or the device.lease.released event rather than for state=failed.

v1.reason: fail_run (handlers/device.rs:2155-2160) and the normal finish (1789-1793) call advance_run first. advance_run commits state=failed/finished via system_write and fans out run.changed. Only then do they remove the id from device_runs and call release_run. device.leases (handlers/device_lease.rs:18-21) prunes with live_runs taken from device_runs (94-96), so in that window the Run lease is still listed. device_lease.rs:196-203 polls until state == failed and then asserts the lease list is empty, so a worker preempted between the commit and the removal fails the test.
v1.correction: The window is microseconds (one mutex removal after a commit), so the effect for users (a device.busy for a run already shown as failed) is negligible. The real cost is a test that can flake. The category is test-quality rather than concurrency. Fix: release the runtime and lease before advance_run, or have the test wait for device.lease.released.

findings.title: The phase12 AVD test can't fail on avd.create or avd.boot behaviour
findings.evidence: The fake avdmanager is `if [ "$1" = "list" ]; then echo 'pixel_9'; fi\nexit 0` (phase12.rs:66), so `create avd` succeeds whatever arguments it gets. avd.create returns `list_avds(…).find(name).unwrap_or(Avd { name, device: p.device, package: Some(p.package), … })` (device.rs:339-340), and the fake emulator never lists New_API_35. So `assert_eq!(created["name"], "New_API_35")` (phase12.rs:79) only echoes the request back. avd.boot (phase12.rs:80) is checked only for Ok. The launch happens in after_commit and reports through an `avd.changed` event the test never reads.
findings.impact: Wrong --name, --package or --device arguments, a create that silently does nothing, or a broken `@name -no-snapshot-load` command line all pass the test.
findings.fix: Have each fake append its argv to a file and assert the exact invocations. Subscribe before avd.boot and assert avd.changed {state:"started"}. Make the fake emulator list New_API_35 after creation.

v1.reason: The fake avdmanager (phase12.rs:66) exits 0 for any arguments. The fake emulator (phase12.rs:65) only ever lists Pixel_9_API_35. So AvdCreate (device.rs:339-340) always falls back to `Avd { name, device: p.device, package: Some(p.package), .. }`, which echoes the request, and the assertion at phase12.rs:79 cannot fail on what create actually did. avd.boot (phase12.rs:80) checks only Ok. The `@name` / `-no-snapshot-load` spawn and its started/failed avd.changed event run in after_commit (device.rs:353-360) and are never observed. Wrong argv or a broken boot command line would still pass.
v1.correction: While verifying, I found a more important issue in the same code that the auditor missed. AvdCreate (device.rs:322) and AvdBoot (device.rs:345) are registered with plain Engine::register. AvdCreate runs avdmanager (a JVM tool that takes seconds) through spawn + wait_with_output, with no proc::output_with_timeout, while holding the store transaction and mutex. Both handlers also call list_avds(ctx.tx()), which runs the emulator binary under the lock. AvdCatalog's `avdmanager list device -c` (device.rs:314) has no timeout either. This breaks two CLAUDE.md invariants and should be raised as its own invariant finding: a hung avdmanager freezes the bus. The fix the test finding proposes (argv log file, avd.changed subscription, fake emulator that lists the new AVD) is right.

findings.title: Production code branches on Instance::Test, and two assertions describe behaviour production doesn't have
findings.evidence: Production code changes behaviour under the test instance in four places. session.close skips the after-close cleanup: `if engine.instance != crate::Instance::Test { crate::branch_cleanup::after_close(…) }` (session.rs:1633-1635). git.pr.list skips after_merged_prs (git.rs:638). usage.get skips the provider file reads (provider.rs:60-71). Run commands use `sh` instead of `fish` (device.rs:1821). The tests then assert the test-only behaviour. branch_cleanup.rs:108-110 asserts that a merged branch survives session.close ("close alone keeps the branch for cleanup to judge"), but in production after_close deletes it on a background thread right away. phase9.rs:94-106 asserts usage.report → usage.get. Nothing in Relay sends usage.report on its own: the Claude status line writes ~/.claude/relay-usage.json instead (hooks.rs:576-578), although audit.rs:16 and BUS.md:883 still say the hooks call usage.report. In production, usage.get then overwrites the reported value with the file read regardless of age.
findings.impact: The paths users actually run have no engine-level test: the after-close cleanup thread with the real gh lookup, usage.get's file reads and precedence, and run commands under fish. Two assertions document behaviour production doesn't have.
findings.fix: Inject the dependency instead of branching on the instance: the gh path and cleanup trigger through Options or settings, the usage home through an env override like RELAY_SKILLS_HOME, the run shell through a setting. Test the production paths with fakes. Either give usage.report a real producer or remove it along with usage.changed.

v1.reason: All four Instance::Test branches exist: session.rs:1633-1635 skips branch_cleanup::after_close, git.rs:638 skips after_merged_prs, provider.rs:60-71 skips crate::usage::read, and device.rs:1821 uses `sh` instead of `fish`. In production, after_close (branch_cleanup.rs:405-413) starts a thread that calls run() on the closed branch right away, with the gh path and audit_kept. So the assertion at branch_cleanup.rs:110, "close alone keeps the branch for cleanup to judge", describes something that only happens in tests. In production a merged branch is deleted asynchronously after close. In usage.get, the file read replaces the reported value for the same provider whatever its age (provider.rs:66-67). The only producer of the Claude usage file is the status-line script at hooks.rs:577, which writes ~/.claude/relay-usage.json and never calls usage.report. audit.rs:16 ('provider hooks call ... usage.report on every window refresh') and BUS.md:519/883 still describe the old producer.
v1.correction: The branches are documented as deliberate (session.rs:1632 comment, device.rs:1818-1820 comment), and the core logic they bypass is tested elsewhere: branch_cleanup::run is driven synchronously by branch_cleanup.rs, and usage::read_claude_file has unit tests (usage.rs:213). What is actually untested is thin glue: the thread spawn with the real gh, provider precedence in usage.get, and fish quoting of run commands. usage.report is not dead. Agents can call it as a builder/reviewer/docs op (settings.rs:36-38), and it is exposed as an MCP tool. It just has no automatic producer. The most concrete part is docs drift (audit.rs:16, BUS.md:519, BUS.md:883) plus the misleading assertion message at branch_cleanup.rs:110. Fix: reword that message to say the test instance defers cleanup, update the doc comments, and add one test of usage.get precedence with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at a temp dir. That is cheaper than refactoring all four branches into injection.

findings.title: phase9's app.resources.watch check asserts only Ok, and its sampler never starts outside a tokio runtime
findings.evidence: phase9.rs:119-124 turns app.resources.watch on and off and asserts only that both calls return Ok. The handler starts its sampler in after_commit with `let Ok(handle) = tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() else { return };` (app.rs:98-99). The plain #[test] thread has no runtime, so the loop never starts and nothing is sampled.
findings.impact: The watch loop, its 2 s sampling, the epoch and client bookkeeping, and the off switch are all untested. The test passes whether they work or not.
findings.fix: Run the test under #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")], subscribe, and assert that a resource.sample arrives after on and none after off. Alternatively, move the tick into a sync function and test that directly.

v1.reason: phase9.rs:44 is a plain #[test], and phase9.rs:119-124 asserts only Ok for on and off. Engine dispatch runs after_commit closures on the calling thread (engine.rs:1030-1034). The closure returns early when `tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current()` fails (app.rs:99), so this test never starts the sampler.
v1.correction: The impact is overstated. Client counting, the epoch bump, and the off switch are covered by socket.rs:835 (resource_watch_leases_stop_on_disconnect_and_preserve_other_clients, a multi-thread tokio test). It asserts resource_watch_clients counts, resource_watch true/false transitions, and the epoch increasing on re-enable. What remains untested is the loop body: that resource.sample events actually arrive every 2 s while on, stop after off, and that the disk refresh fires every 15th tick. Fix: in the existing socket test, or a tokio test, subscribe and assert a resource.sample arrives within about 3 s after on and none after off. Or extract the tick body into a sync function and test that directly.

findings.title: git.branch.switch classifies failures by git's English stderr, so it breaks under a non-English locale
findings.evidence: run_switch sets only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT (git.rs:1347-1349). It classifies failures by matching English text: "is already checked out at ", "is already used by worktree at ", "local changes to the following files would be overwritten" and "untracked working tree files would be overwritten" (1361-1384). git translates these messages through gettext; for example, /usr/share/locale/fr/LC_MESSAGES/git.mo is installed on this machine. device.rs:1937 and 1944 already force LC_ALL=C for the same reason.
findings.impact: Under a non-English locale, switching to a branch held by another worktree, or a switch that would overwrite changes, returns the generic git.branch_switch_failed with translated stderr. The user loses the git.branch_checked_out and git.checkout_conflict codes and their guidance. git_branch_switch.rs:92 and :146 fail on such a machine.
findings.fix: Add `.env("LC_ALL", "C").env("LANGUAGE", "C")` to the run_switch command, and to any other git call whose stderr is parsed.

v1.reason: run_switch (git.rs:1347-1388) sets only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 on the git command, then sorts failures by matching English stderr: "is already checked out at " / "is already used by worktree at " (1365-1367), "local changes to the following files would be overwritten" (1376) and "untracked working tree files would be overwritten" (1382). git translates these messages through gettext, so under a non-English LANG/LC_MESSAGES each one falls through to the generic git.branch_switch_failed with the translated stderr. listed() keys on tab-indented lines, which also changes nothing in that case. device.rs:1937/1944 already set LC_ALL=C for the same kind of parsing. The tests at git_branch_switch.rs:92 and :146 assert the specific codes, so they would fail under such a locale.
v1.correction: No correctness or safety impact: git refuses and changes nothing on every one of these paths. Only the error code and the guidance text are lost. Set LC_ALL=C (or LANGUAGE=C plus LC_MESSAGES=C) on this command. Today it is the only git stderr-text classifier in relay-core.

findings.title: Every test file copies its own engine and git fixture helpers; the copies have diverged and none isolates git from the developer's config
findings.evidence: 17 of the 18 files in crates/relay-core/tests define their own call, ok, git, engine and fixture helpers; there is no tests/common module. The copies have diverged. Only branch_cleanup.rs commits with --no-verify (branch_cleanup.rs:51); the others run plain `git commit` (registry_remove.rs:40, device_lease.rs:49, git_branch_switch.rs:37, phase12.rs:46). phase9.rs:30-42 builds an empty repo with no identity. registry_remove.rs:28 uses .status(), which sends git's output into the test log. No helper isolates git from the developer's config (no GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL or GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM). The Test-instance run shell is a login shell that sources ~/.profile (`sh -lc`, device.rs:1821-1825). phase12.rs:107 needs python3 on PATH.
findings.impact: On a machine with commit.gpgsign=true, a global core.hooksPath or init.templateDir hooks, fixtures hang on pinentry or fail. That is not the case on this machine today. Any fixture fix has to be made in up to 17 places.
findings.fix: Add crates/relay-core/tests/common/mod.rs with the engine, call, ok and repo helpers. Run git there with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, identity through GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_*, and --no-verify. Use `sh -c` rather than `sh -lc` for the test shell.

v1.reason: crates/relay-core/tests has 18 files and no common/ module. 17 of them define their own call/ok helpers, and there are 53 top-level call/ok/git/engine/fixture/command helper fns. The copies have diverged. Only branch_cleanup.rs passes --no-verify (lines 51, 73, 107, ...). registry_remove.rs:28 uses .status(), which lets git output through, while phase9.rs/phase12.rs use .output() and report stderr. No fixture sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL or GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM; the only GIT_CONFIG_* use is the ext-protocol allowance at phase12.rs:90-92. So a developer with commit.gpgsign=true or a global hooksPath would see the fixture commits prompt or fail.
v1.correction: The claim that 'phase9.rs builds an empty repo with no identity' is not a defect. phase9's project() only runs `git init` and never commits, so it needs no identity. The config-isolation risk is hypothetical on this machine, and setting env in the fixture helpers alone would not isolate the git commands the engine itself runs (worktree add, merge checks), so a real fix would set the env process-wide in the shared helper. Per-file helpers are also the default Rust integration-test pattern, so the payoff is modest. A tests/common/mod.rs with engine/call/ok/repo helpers that sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and author/committer env is still a reasonable cleanup. The `sh -lc` point (device.rs:1824) is a trivial nit.

results.coverage:
I read every line of all five assigned files: perf.rs (1596 lines), baseline.py, native-baseline.py, compare.py and report.py.

**Production code traced:**
- engine.rs: Engine::new, dispatch after_commit, shutdown and mark_restorable, arc.
- recovery.rs (all), plus pty.rs pid_alive and relay_children.
- store.rs: open, backup and pruning, notification indexes.
- skills.rs: user_bases and refresh_all.
- Handlers: ui.rs (os.*), provider.rs (github, usage), github.rs, device.rs (watch, avd, signing, SDK discovery, mirror), git.rs (pr.list, pr.open), notify.rs, app.rs (resources.watch).
- Also: provider_updates.rs, socket.rs (subscribe and attach forwarding), worktree.rs (list, is_dirty), audit.rs (payload truncation), session spawn env, relay-cli main.rs (instance, env, actor, project fill).
- relay-native app.rs, smoke.rs and shell.rs, for the env vars, smoke timer and notify calls.
- Docs: BUS.md §6.5, §7 and §10.17; DECISIONS D144 and D149; docs/perf README, BASELINE and FIXES.
- The committed run in docs/perf/runs/2026-09-19 (native, scale10, strace, process and soak JSON).

**Scratch experiments** (in the scratchpad, run with python -I): SocketIO after a timeout raises OSError; unbuffered readline runs at 2.2 MiB/s against 820 MiB/s buffered; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for notify.list; the bash burst loop takes about 33 ms.

**Host checks (read-only):** ptrace_scope is 1; pid_max is 4194304; gh, adb, wl-copy, xdg-open, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, ~/Android/Sdk and ~/.android/avd are all present; strace and valgrind are not installed; DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY are set.

**Not run:** cargo, the harness itself, valgrind or strace (not installed), and relay-native (cannot build here). Three things are therefore unverified:
- vgdb stalls under ptrace_scope=1.
- The exact XWayland fallback (inferred from libwayland and GDK backend order, and from sibling scripts setting GDK_BACKEND=x11).
- perf record's finalisation delay.

**Checked and found fine or intended, so not reported:**
- Percentile maths, warm-up handling and drain ordering.
- Socket subscribe replaces its forwarder rather than stacking.
- provider.update is a no-op for the fake provider path.
- Instance::Test guards exist for signing, mirroring, usage and user-scope skills.
- Audit truncates oversize payloads.
- baseline.py's relay serve is isolated through XDG_* and does not open the phone door.
- The CLI subcommands used for CLI timing exist.
- The pty.burst wall time being dominated by the child is documented in the BASELINE.
- gix buffers use resize, so the allocator wrapper's missing alloc_zeroed does not matter there.

**Minor items left out:**
- In the callgrind and scale passes, exact names are re-used as prefix filters, so about 20 cases (for example session.close.created and session_list.during_session_close_keep) run twice. This wastes time but the data stays valid.
- Engine log file handles leak in baseline.py.
- report.py hard-codes '50 000 lines (4.9 MB)'.

perf.rs is an example target and the scripts are not shipped, so none of this harness code can be triggered in normal use of the app.

findings.title: perf example runs host side effects for real: hundreds of xdg-open windows/tabs, `gh auth login --web --clipboard`, authenticated gh API calls, real adb/AVD tools; all labelled 'refusal paths'
findings.evidence: perf.rs:1044 says `// ---- ui / os (executor = ui; no client is attached in-process, so this is the refusal path)` and :990 `(no SDK here: these measure the refusal path)`. Nothing isolates the host: Fixture::build (233-256) keeps the caller's HOME, PATH, DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY and gh config. The handlers really run. ui.rs:342-346 and :356-360 spawn `xdg-open` after commit, and nothing gates on a UI or on Instance::Test (no code reads OpMeta.executor). github.rs:58 runs `gh auth login --hostname github.com --web --clipboard`, spawned on a thread per call (provider.rs:248-261). github.rs:45 runs `gh api user` and :69 runs `gh api --paginate user/repos`. device.rs:44-66 starts `adb track-devices -l`, which no case turns off and Engine::shutdown does not stop. device.rs:321-361 runs avdmanager `create avd` and `emulator @name` against the real ~/Android/Sdk and ~/.android/avd. Only signing, mirroring, usage and skills have Instance::Test guards. In the committed run (docs/perf/runs/2026-09-19/native.jsonl), op.os.open_url and op.os.reveal were 200/200 ok at about 130 us each, which is the cost of the xdg-open fork, not a refusal. That run was on a headless VM without gh or an SDK. This machine has DISPLAY=:0, WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, /usr/bin/xdg-open, /usr/bin/gh with ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, wl-copy, /usr/bin/adb, ~/Android/Sdk (cmdline-tools/latest, emulator) and ~/.android/avd.
findings.impact:
Running `cargo run -p relay-core --example perf -- run` or `python3 scripts/perf/baseline.py` on the dev desktop does the following:
- os.open_url (Cheap) runs xdg-open 202 times in the native pass, 52 in strace and 21 in callgrind: about 275 browser tabs on https://example.invalid/. os.reveal opens about as many file-manager windows.
- github.connect starts about 45 `gh auth login --web --clipboard` processes. Each overwrites the clipboard with a device code and polls github.com for about 15 minutes after the run ends. Completing one would replace the stored gh token.
- github.status and github.repo.list make about 90 API calls with the user's token.
- avd.catalog and avd.create each run the JVM avdmanager about 45 times. Where system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64 is installed, avd.create makes a real AVD "perf" that avd.boot then boots as a detached emulator.
- device.list starts an adb server, and device.watch leaves `adb track-devices` orphaned.
Run from a Relay terminal, the launched browser and file manager inherit RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_STORE, so the live engine's next crash recovery reaps them. These rows also measure the host's tools, not refusal paths.
findings.fix:
Sandbox the harness before building the fixture:
- Re-exec with, or set before any thread starts, HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and ANDROID_* pointing into the fixture.
- Prepend a fake-bin directory with stub gh, adb, avdmanager, emulator and xdg-open (as scripts/native-setup-smoke.py does).
- Unset DISPLAY, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and RELAY_*.
Alternatively, skip os.*, github.connect and avd.* unless an explicit --allow-host is given. In production, gate xdg-open and `gh auth login` on Instance::Test the way signing and mirroring already are. Correct the comments and report.py GROUP_TITLES.

v1.reason:
The handlers really run against the host.
- os.reveal and os.open_url (ui.rs:335-361) spawn `xdg-open` in after_commit. Nothing checks for an attached client or for Instance::Test, so the comment at perf.rs:1044 ('this is the refusal path') is false for os.*. The committed native.jsonl confirms it: op.os.reveal shows 200/200 ok, codes {}.
- github.connect (provider.rs:248-261) spawns a thread per call running `gh auth login --hostname github.com --web --clipboard` (github.rs:58) whenever gh is on PATH.
- github.status and github.repo.list run `gh api user` and `gh api --paginate user/repos` (github.rs:45, :69).
- device.watch starts `adb track-devices -l` (device.rs:44-66). Engine::shutdown (engine.rs:633+) does not stop it.
- avd.catalog and avd.create run avdmanager, resolved through which/ANDROID_*/~/Android/Sdk (device.rs:397-434). avd.boot spawns `emulator @perf` if that AVD exists.
The Instance::Test guards exist only for signing, mirroring, skills and similar (provider.rs:60, device.rs:86/103/1362...). Fixture::build does not touch HOME, PATH, DISPLAY or the gh config. This machine has DISPLAY=:0, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, /usr/bin/xdg-open, /usr/bin/gh with ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, /usr/bin/adb and ~/Android/Sdk. baseline.py:13 states 'No user store, no paid provider, no display.' That docstring and report.py GROUP_TITLES ('refusal paths', 'no client attached') are wrong on such a machine.
v1.correction:
Re-rate to medium, not high. This is a developer-only benchmark, not an app flow, and nothing here loses data or opens a security hole. Running it on the dev desktop is still very disruptive: about 200+ browser tabs and file-manager windows per native pass, plus repeated `gh auth login` device flows that overwrite the clipboard. Two details in the finding are not fully established.
- The `gh auth login` count and behaviour with stdin=null on an already-authenticated host depend on the gh version, and replacing the token would need the user to finish the device flow.
- On this machine system-images;android-34 is not installed (only android-36), so avd.create fails and avd.boot returns not_found. The 'real AVD perf' outcome is conditional.
The fix is right: sandbox the environment, use stub binaries on PATH, unset DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DBUS and RELAY_*, or skip host-effect ops behind an opt-in flag. A separate note for the production audit, outside this finding: avd.create (device.rs:~321) runs avdmanager via spawn/wait_with_output inside Engine::register, under the store mutex and with no timeout. The gh calls in github.rs use Command::output/status without proc::output_with_timeout.

findings.title: avd.create, avd.boot and git.pr.open run subprocesses with no deadline while holding the store mutex (the perf cases only ever hit their refusal paths)
findings.evidence: `e.register::<AvdCreate>` (321) spawns `avdmanager create avd ...` and blocks in `child.wait_with_output()` (332-335). It then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339), which runs `Command::new(emulator).arg("-list-avds").output()` (478) and, for each running AVD, `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` with `.output()` (505). `e.register::<AvdBoot>` (344-346) runs the same list_avds inside the transaction. git.rs:666-680 `e.register::<PrOpen>` runs `gh pr create --title .. --fill` with `.output()`, which is a GitHub network round trip. None of these uses proc::output_with_timeout, and all run with the store mutex held. CLAUDE.md and D144/D149 forbid this, and D149's list of converted ops omits these three. Three more calls are unlocked but have no deadline: github.rs:45 (`gh api user`), github.rs:69 (`gh api --paginate`) and device.rs:315 (`avdmanager list device -c`). On the measuring VM the perf cases for these ops returned avd.tool_missing or github.gh_missing, so the baseline never saw the lock being held.
findings.impact: Creating an AVD stalls every locked request for the JVM's several seconds. That includes task and session lists and guardrail.gate from every agent's PreToolUse hook; only keystrokes (D148) keep going. Opening a PR stalls them for a GitHub round trip, and indefinitely if the network hangs. A wedged emulator console hangs avd.create and avd.boot, and the whole bus with them, forever.
findings.fix: Re-register avd.create, avd.boot and git.pr.open with register_staged. Run avdmanager, emulator/adb and gh in prepare through proc::output_with_timeout, and keep finish to the event and audit write. Route the unlocked github/avd subprocesses through output_with_timeout as well.

v1.reason: device.rs:321 `e.register::<AvdCreate>` is the ordinary locked shape. Inside it, avdmanager is spawned and the handler blocks on `child.wait_with_output()` (332-335) with no deadline. It then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339), which runs `Command::new(emulator).arg("-list-avds").output()` (478) and, through running_avds_with, `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` with `.output()` (505). Neither call has a timeout. device.rs:344-346 `e.register::<AvdBoot>` runs the same list_avds under the lock. git.rs:666-680 `e.register::<PrOpen>` runs `gh pr create ... .output()`, a GitHub network round trip, with the store mutex held. The comment on list_avds_with (473-474) even says the subprocesses are meant to run 'with nothing locked (D144)', but these two callers still reach it through the locked tx. D144 requires proc::output_with_timeout. D149's converted list (DECISIONS.md:797-815) names avd.list and avd.catalog but not avd.create, avd.boot or git.pr.open. github.rs:45 (`gh api user`) and github.rs:69 (`gh api --paginate`) are reached from register_unlocked handlers (provider.rs:247 and 262). device.rs:315 (`avdmanager list device -c`) is likewise unlocked. These three have no deadline, but they block only their own request.
v1.correction: The locked ones (avd.create, avd.boot, git.pr.open) are high: each freezes every locked request for the subprocess's lifetime, which is seconds for the avdmanager JVM and a network round trip for gh, and the freeze is indefinite if the child hangs. The unlocked github.rs:45, github.rs:69 and device.rs:315 calls are a lower-severity related issue: they violate the 'every subprocess goes through output_with_timeout' rule but stall only the caller. Fix as proposed: use register_staged, read tool paths under the lock, run subprocesses in prepare through proc::output_with_timeout (avdmanager needs a stdin-writing variant), and emit and audit in finish.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. A plain `register` handler runs between `self.store.lock()` plus `conn.transaction()` (engine.rs:953-956) and the commit (1024). No watchdog limits that: `LockSpan` only logs. `avd.create` blocks in `child.wait_with_output()` on avdmanager (device.rs:332-335). It then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())` (339), which runs `emulator -list-avds` `.output()` (478), `adb devices -l` (2 s timeout, 577/582) and `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` `.output()` for each online emulator (505). `avd.boot` runs the same list before commit (346); its emulator spawn is correctly after_commit (353-360). `git.pr.open` runs `gh pr create` with `.output()` (git.rs:666-681). Only `adb devices` has a deadline. The neighbouring ops were already converted: `git.pr.list` uses output_with_timeout(PR_LIST_TIMEOUT) (git.rs:83), `avd.list`/`avd.catalog` are unlocked (device.rs:301-320) and `git.push` is staged (git.rs:600-624). D149's conversion list (DECISIONS.md:810-814) leaves these three out. The perf report backs the title: report.md:268/324/325 show all 30 iterations ending in github.gh_missing or avd.tool_missing.

(b) The user reaches all three in normal flows: Code page "Open PR" (code_git.rs:662, behind a confirm dialog), Devices "Create AVD" (tools_devices.rs:419) and "Boot"/"Cold boot" (110-117, 656-663). The avd ops are UserOnly. `git.pr.open` is Actors::All, but no default agent role grants it (settings.rs:36-38), so in practice the user starts it. Opening PRs and booting AVDs are routine; creating an AVD is occasional.

(c) While the child runs, every request on every other connection that touches the store waits. That covers:
- each agent's PreToolUse `guardrail.gate` (locked, guardrail.rs:304; the hook matches Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash, hooks.rs:349-352);
- the agent authorize step, even for unlocked queries (engine.rs:870-872);
- session lifecycle sockets (client.rs:131-141), the phone door and MCP.

Keystrokes (the D148 fast path) and PTY output (atomics only in pty.rs) keep flowing. Typical stalls: gh, a few seconds of API round trips and local git; avdmanager, several seconds of JVM start-up; avd.boot, usually under a second. No data is lost. On a stalled network gh holds the global lock for as long as its TCP/HTTP failure takes, with no Relay-side bound. Past 10 s the agents' report hooks time out (hooks.rs:373) and those reports are dropped. Past 30 s Claude Code kills the PreToolUse hook (hooks.rs:351). Whether that fails open depends on Claude Code, so I could not establish it.

(d) High matches the rubric ("a freeze of the bus" in a normal flow). It fires on every PR open and AVD create or boot, and breaks both CLAUDE.md rules at once. It is not critical: the usual stall lasts seconds, and the indefinite variants need an abnormal network or emulator.

(e) The proposed fix is right in shape. Use register_staged: prepare reads the tool paths through `ctx.read` and runs the subprocesses unlocked via output_with_timeout; finish only emits and audits. `git.push` together with resolve_root_unlocked (git.rs:768) is the template. Caveats:
1. output_with_timeout forces `stdin(Stdio::null())` (proc.rs:35), so avdmanager's "no\n" answer (device.rs:334) needs a variant that can write stdin.
2. Killing `gh pr create` at the deadline leaves the outcome unknown (the PR may exist). The refusal should say so, and the deadline must be generous.
3. A held `git.pr.open` replayed by guardrail.confirm still runs prepare under the lock (engine.rs:325-342). D149 accepts that path.
4. The engine serves one request at a time per socket connection (socket.rs:335-743), and the native client sends these ops on its single control connection (app.rs:1111-1116). So the fix ends the stall for other connections, but the UI's own control plane still waits unless these ops use a separate connection the way lifecycle_request does.
v2.correction:
1. "Indefinitely if the network hangs" overstates it. Accurate: as long as gh takes, with no Relay-side bound — usually seconds, minutes on a stalled network.
2. "A wedged emulator console hangs the bus forever" is plausible but not established from this repo. It depends on adb's `emu` reading the console with no deadline.
3. The locked span in avd.create and avd.boot also includes `adb devices -l`. That call is bounded at 2 s (ADB_LIST_TIMEOUT, device.rs:577), but D149 says a timeout under the lock is still not enough.
4. The UI's own requests (task and session lists) on its control connection would wait during these ops anyway, because the engine serializes each connection. The extra victims the mutex adds are agents (guardrail.gate, reports), lifecycle sockets, the phone door and MCP.
5. The related unlocked calls (github.rs:45, github.rs:68-70, device.rs:315) do more than "stall only the caller": they block the caller's whole connection. The native client calls them on its control connection (onboarding.rs:422/429, tools_devices.rs:377), so a hung `gh api` freezes the UI's control plane until gh exits. That is still medium and separate, not a global freeze.
6. The same deadline-free pattern also runs under the lock through `worktree::git` (worktree.rs:27, `.output()`), via git_mutate in git.branch.create (git.rs:374), git.branch.delete (485), git.stage (503), git.unstage (527) and git.branch.clean_merged (712). These are usually fast local git ops; either fold them into this fix or track them separately.

findings.title: Every op.* timing includes the harness's own JSON serialization of the result (`r.to_string()` runs inside the timed closure)
findings.evidence: Outcome::of computes `bytes: resp.result.as_ref().map(|r| r.to_string().len())` (94). dispatch() returns `Box::new(move || Outcome::of(&engine.dispatch(req, Door::InProcess)))` (470-474), so the serialization runs inside `perf_measured(work)`, between t0/allocs0 (1417-1420) and the counter reads (1422-1430). In-process dispatch returns a Value, and query results are never stringified by the engine (only audited mutation results are). Committed run: op.file.read.1mib alloc_bytes 8.82 MB for a 1.07 MB result, of which String doubling to that size is about 4.19 MB (48%). op.session.scrollback is 10.29 MB for 1.81 MB (about 41%). BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:315 and :372 attribute these bytes to the op ('UTF-8 check, JSON escape'; 'read, UTF-8, JSON').
findings.impact: Wall time, CPU, allocation counts/bytes and the callgrind json bucket and markers of every op are inflated by work that in-process callers never do. The effect is largest for big results (file.read, scrollback, file.tree.deep, bus.schema.whole, the x10 list queries). It double counts against path.response.serialize.* and has already misattributed cost in the analysis.
findings.fix: Have the work closure return the Response. Compute `bytes` after perf_measured returns and after the counters are read. Leave serialization to path.response.serialize.*.

v1.reason: Outcome::of (perf.rs:94) does `resp.result.as_ref().map(|r| r.to_string().len())`. dispatch() (perf.rs:470-474) builds `Box::new(move || Outcome::of(&engine.dispatch(req, Door::InProcess)))`, so the stringification runs inside perf_measured, between t0/allocs0/cpu0 and the counter reads (run_case, ~1417-1430). Engine::dispatch (engine.rs:759-777) returns a Response holding a Value and does not serialize query results itself. So the op.* rows include the harness's own serialization of the result. The socket.* cases call Outcome::of too, after the client has already parsed the result.
v1.correction: The impact is overstated. No real client uses Door::InProcess. apps/relay-native, the CLI and the remote door all reach the engine through the socket, which serializes the whole Response anyway. The extra cost is therefore close to what a real caller pays. What goes wrong is attribution and labelling: the cost is double counted against path.response.serialize.*, and the BASELINE notes say 'JSON escape' as if the op did it. The numbers do not mislead about real-world cost. That makes this low, not medium. The suggested fix is still right: return the Response from the work closure and compute bytes after the counters are read.

findings.title: strace pass counts each iteration's uncounted setup, cleanup and fixture git processes as the op's syscalls
findings.evidence: strace attaches before the loop (1409) and detaches after it (1440). Inside the loop, every iteration runs `fx.drain_cleanup()` (1412) and `(case.prepare)(fx)` (1413), which is exactly the work the timer excludes, and `strace -f` (1360) also follows forked children. The committed strace.jsonl gives a fingerprint: one getrandom per bus request (its req_id UUID). op.task.update shows 50 getrandom for 50 iterations, but op.task.delete shows 150 (fresh_task's create, the measured delete, the cleanup delete), op.task.restore 200 and op.audit.get 100. op.task.delete is 125 syscalls/iter against 45 for task.update. op.project.add is 3,075 and op.project.remove 2,994 syscalls/iter, mostly rt_sigaction/openat from the five `git` commands small_repo runs in prepare. BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:375 then calls file.create/rename/move/delete 'a few hundred syscalls' each, which includes the prepare's file.create.
findings.impact: Per-op syscall counts are 2-4x too high for every case whose prepare creates rows, and wrong by orders of magnitude where prepare forks git. Conclusions in the analysis inherit the error.
findings.fix: Count only between markers: issue a distinctive marker syscall immediately before and after perf_measured, record with `strace -f -ttt -o`, and sum only the events between the markers. Alternatively, count raw_syscalls:sys_enter with perf stat toggled around the measured call. At minimum, subtract a calibrated no-op iteration that runs the same prepare and cleanup.

v1.reason: perf.rs:1409 starts strace before the iteration loop and 1440 stops it after the loop. Every iteration runs `fx.drain_cleanup()` and `(case.prepare)(fx)` (1412-1413) inside that window, and `-f` (1360) also follows forked git children. The committed strace.jsonl matches the claimed numbers exactly. op.task.update: 50 iters, 50 getrandom, 2260 total. op.task.delete: 150 getrandom, 6254 total (125/iter). op.task.restore: 200 getrandom. op.audit.get: 100 getrandom for 50 iters. op.project.add: 21526 over 7 iters (3075/iter), dominated by rt_sigaction and openat from the git commands in small_repo, which the prepare at perf.rs:657 and 662-663 calls. op.file.create: 9291 over 50. So the syscall counts include uncounted setup and cleanup. BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:375 inherits the inflated 'few hundred syscalls' figure.
v1.correction: Severity lowered to low: the effect is limited to the accuracy of the perf report and does not touch the app. The marker or calibrated-baseline fix is reasonable. A simpler fix is to measure a no-op case that runs the same prepare and cleanup, and subtract it.

findings.title: strace pass silently reports 0 syscalls under Yama ptrace_scope=1 (this machine's setting): strace cannot attach to its own parent
findings.evidence: strace_start spawns `strace -f -c -o <file> -p <own pid>` as a child of the process it is meant to trace (1359-1366). /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope is 1 here, which is also the Ubuntu and Arch default. Under that setting a process may only ptrace its descendants, so the attach fails and strace exits. strace_start still returns Some after its 400 ms sleep. strace_stop (1372-1395) parses whatever the file holds and returns `{"total": 0, "top": []}`, without checking strace's exit status or that a 'total' row exists. In report.py:154-155, `st = ... or {}` treats that dict as truthy and prints `0.0` instead of '-'. The committed run was made as root on a Firecracker VM, where the attach succeeds.
findings.impact: With strace installed, baseline.py on this desktop writes 0 syscalls/iteration for every scenario into strace.jsonl and the report, presented as real data. The callgrind pass's callgrind_control/vgdb toggling also relies on ptrace to wake a valgrind process whose threads are all blocked (per the valgrind manual), so it may stall under the same setting. That part is unverified: valgrind is not installed here.
findings.fix: Call prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER, PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY) before spawning strace, or make strace the parent (`strace -f -c -o f -- perf run ...`). In strace_stop, treat a nonzero exit or a missing total row as failure and emit null. Have report.py render null as '-'.

v1.reason: perf.rs:1357-1370: strace_start spawns `strace -f -c -o <file> -p <own pid>` as a child of the traced process and returns Some after a fixed 400 ms sleep, without checking that the attach succeeded. /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope is 1 on this machine, and nothing in perf.rs or scripts/perf calls prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER) (grep finds no prctl or ptrace). Under scope 1 a non-root strace cannot attach to its parent, which is not its descendant, so it fails with EPERM and exits. strace_stop (1372-1395) ignores the exit status, parses an empty file or a zero summary, and returns {"total":0,"top":[]}. In report.py:154-155, `st = ... or {}` treats that non-empty dict as truthy, so `sc` renders as 0.0 rather than '-'. baseline.py:633 runs the pass whenever `shutil.which("strace")` finds strace. On this desktop strace is not installed today, so the pass is currently skipped. The defect bites as soon as strace is installed. The valgrind part of the finding is speculative and unverified.
v1.correction: Severity lowered to low: this is dev tooling only, and it is latent on this machine because strace is not installed, so baseline.py skips the pass. Drop the callgrind/vgdb speculation. Fix: call prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER, PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY), or the strace pid, before spawning strace. Alternatively, wait for strace's first output or check `child.try_wait()` after the sleep. Emit null when strace exited early or no 'total' row exists.

findings.title: All cases share one mutating fixture, so results depend on case order; the 'x10 rows' table compares a residue-laden x1 store against a clean x10 store
findings.evidence:
`let fx = Fixture::build(scale, keep);` (1566) builds one fixture for every selected case. The doc comment at 142-145 claims cleanup keeps 'the store a case sees is the fixture and not the residue of every case before it', but cleanup only undoes rows a case created. Audit rows, messages ('Messages have no delete', 755), notifications and holds ('neither can be deleted', 844-846), closed sessions and kept worktrees all accumulate. The scale pass (baseline.py:628-632) runs only read-only list cases, on a fresh --scale 10 fixture. Committed `rows` fields:
- op.notify.list: 203 notifications at x1 vs 2 at x10 (ratio 0.04).
- op.dashboard.get: 25,238 audit rows, 405 notifications and 145 closed sessions at x1 vs 1,127, 2 and 0 at x10 (ratio 4.14).
- op.mailbox.list: 74 vs 100 messages (ratio 1.29).
- op.task.activity: 1,523 vs 1,127 audit rows (ratio 0.52).
