findings.title: run.sh leaves the engine in the launching terminal's process group: Ctrl+C there shuts the engine down and kills every agent PTY, Ctrl+Z freezes it
findings.evidence: run.sh:32 `nohup "$relay" --instance "$RELAY_INSTANCE" serve --remote >>"$log" 2>&1 </dev/null &` starts the engine as a plain async child: no setsid and no job control, so it shares the script's process group and the terminal's session. run.sh:46 then execs relay-native in that same group. nohup only ignores SIGHUP. Bash sets SIGINT to SIG_IGN for the async child, but the engine's `tokio::select!` on `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` (crates/relay-cli/src/remote.rs:130, crates/relay-core/src/serve.rs:47) installs a handler through signal-hook-registry 1.4.8, which replaces an inherited SIG_IGN (it only declines to chain to it). On SIGINT it calls `served.engine.shutdown()` (remote.rs:137), which marks every PTY restorable and kills it (engine.rs:649-658). I reproduced this in the scratchpad with the same shell construct and a child that installs a SIGINT handler. SIGINT sent to the launcher's process group (what the tty sends on Ctrl+C) reached the background child. SIGTSTP sent to a non-orphaned job's group left the child in state T until SIGCONT. With `setsid nohup ... &`, neither signal reached it and `$!` was still the child's PID.
findings.impact: The user runs ./run.sh from fish (the README's launch path) with no engine running, so this invocation starts one. Pressing Ctrl+C in that terminal to close the window also sends SIGINT to the engine. The engine shuts down and kills every agent mid-task; the agents come back only as 'restorable'. This contradicts run.sh:45, 'The engine outlives the window so closing the UI preserves agent sessions'. Pressing Ctrl+Z in that terminal stops the engine process: every bus request, keystroke and agent hook hangs until the job is resumed.
findings.fix: Start the engine in its own session: `setsid nohup "$relay" --instance "$RELAY_INSTANCE" serve --remote >>"$log" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Verified: setsid does not fork here because the async child is not a process-group leader, so `engine_pid=$!` and the `kill -0` liveness check keep working. Optionally, have `serve --remote` skip the SIGINT listener when stdin is not a TTY.

v1.reason: run.sh:32 starts the engine with `nohup ... serve --remote ... &` and no setsid. A non-interactive bash has no job control, so the async child stays in the script's process group. run.sh:46 then `exec`s relay-native in that same group, and that group is the terminal's foreground job when fish runs ./run.sh, the README's launch path (README.md:17). Bash sets SIGINT to SIG_IGN for async children, but `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` (remote.rs:130, serve.rs:47) registers through signal-hook-registry 1.4.8 (Cargo.lock:3087-3088). That library installs its own sigaction and declines to chain only to a previous SIG_IGN/SIG_DFL (lib.rs:249/268), so the inherited ignore is replaced. On SIGINT the select ends and `served.engine.shutdown()` runs (remote.rs:137). At engine.rs:633-658 that stops mirrors and device runs, marks every PTY session restorable and kills each PTY. This contradicts the promise at run.sh:45. For Ctrl+Z: the engine has no SIGTSTP handler. relay-native's parent is fish, which is in another group of the same session, so the group is not orphaned and the default stop applies. The engine is then frozen until it gets SIGCONT. The trigger needs three things: launching from a terminal, no engine already running, and Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Z in that terminal while the window is open. All three are ordinary for a GUI app started from a shell. After the window closes, the engine is in a background group and is safe. Launching from the .desktop entry (Terminal=false) is not affected.
v1.correction: Impact calibration: the agents' PTYs are killed, not their data. The sessions come back as restorable through the resume flow, so in-flight work is interrupted, not lost. That still justifies high: it is a normal flow that kills every concurrent agent. The fix stands: `setsid nohup ... &`. Because the async child is not a group leader, setsid does not fork, so `$!` and the `kill -0` check keep working.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. run.sh:32 starts the engine with `nohup "$relay" ... serve --remote ... </dev/null &`, with no setsid. run.sh:46 then execs relay-native from the same process. The engine's `tokio::select!` waits on `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` (remote.rs:130). In tokio 1.53.1 that becomes `signal_hook_registry::register` (signal/unix.rs:290). In signal-hook-registry 1.4.8, `Slot::new` installs its own handler with sigaction (lib.rs:199). `Prev::execute` skips a previous SIG_IGN/SIG_DFL (lib.rs:268) but still runs the registered actions, so the SIGINT that bash ignored for the async child is no longer ignored. When the select ends, remote.rs:137 calls `engine.shutdown()`. engine.rs:633-658 then stops mirrors and device runs, marks every live session restorable, and kills each PTY: SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL after 2s (pty.rs:344-358). The engine has no sigprocmask or SIGTSTP handling anywhere.

I reproduced this independently on a real pty, not with killpg. A fish with job control ran a copy of run.sh's construct, and the stand-in engine set a real SIGINT handler the way signal-hook-registry does. ps showed the engine in the launcher's pgid, which was also the tty's TPGID (stat `+`), and the engine started with SIGINT and SIGHUP ignored. Typing the \x03 byte (Ctrl+C) delivered SIGINT to the engine. With fish still alive, typing \x1a (Ctrl+Z) left both the window and the engine in state T. With `setsid nohup ... &`, the engine had sid=pgid=pid and TPGID -1, `$!` was still the engine's pid (no fork), Ctrl+C did not reach it, and after Ctrl+Z it stayed in S.

(b) Reachability. All three conditions are ordinary:
- The user launches with `./run.sh` from fish, as README.md:16-17 documents.
- That run started the engine: the first launch after a login or reboot, or after any engine restart. The app's own STALE_ENGINE message (tools_plugins.rs:14) tells the user to app.quit and then `./run.sh again`.
- The user presses Ctrl+C in that terminal while that first window is open. This is the usual way to stop a GUI launched from a terminal, for example to relaunch after a UI rebuild.

Once that window closes, the engine sits in a background group and is safe. Later runs that reuse the engine are also safe. So whether Ctrl+C kills every agent depends on which run started the engine, and a user who has done it harmlessly before has no warning. Launching from the .desktop entry (Terminal=false) is not affected. Calibration: /home/anthony/dev3/RelayV4/target/engine-dev.log records about 16 engine starts since 2026-09-05 and no "SIGINT" shutdown (only SIGTERM and app.quit). The bug is latent for the author, not frequent.

(c) What happens when it fires. Every concurrent agent in every project is killed mid-turn, along with its in-flight tool calls. Device runs and mirrors stop, and the phone door closes. Sessions become restorable with restore_reason 'app_restart'. Resume restarts each provider with `--resume <provider_ref>` (providers.rs:185), so conversations and worktree files survive. The loss is the interrupted work and a manual resume of each session. This contradicts run.sh:45 and README.md:32-33 ("Closing the window keeps the engine, sessions and worktrees alive"). nohup only covers SIGHUP. Ctrl+Z freezes the engine and the window until fg or bg. That part is minor because it is user-started and temporary.

(d) Severity: high is right. It is a failure in the documented normal launch flow, and one keystroke takes down every session. It is not critical: the user triggers it, only during the window opened by the run that started the engine, it is recoverable with no data loss, and it has not occurred in a month of the author's logs.

(e) The fix is correct and complete for run.sh. util-linux setsid forks only when the caller already leads a process group. Bash without job control leaves the async child in the script's group, so `$!` and the `kill -0` liveness check still work (verified). The engine does not need a controlling terminal: git children set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, nothing opens /dev/tty, and the desktop-entry path already runs it with none. setsid fixes both Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Z. The engine-side change alone would fix only Ctrl+C.
v2.correction: Impact: PTYs are killed and sessions become restorable, but resume uses `--resume <provider_ref>`, so conversations and worktree files survive. What is lost is in-flight turns and tool calls, plus a manual resume of each session. Device runs, mirrors and the phone door also stop. Frequency: target/engine-dev.log in the main checkout records no SIGINT shutdown since 2026-09-05, so this is a latent trap, not something the author hits often. Fix caveat: `setsid` keeps `$!` only because run.sh runs without job control. Under `set -m` or `bash -i`, setsid would fork and the `kill -0` check would falsely fail. That is fine for `./run.sh` and the desktop entry. For the optional engine-side hardening, a more precise test than "stdin is not a TTY" is to skip registering ctrl_c when SIGINT was inherited as SIG_IGN, which is the POSIX convention for background jobs. That covers SIGINT only, so setsid remains the primary fix.

findings.title: run.sh rebuilds both binaries but silently reuses a running engine of any age, and nothing on the bus can reveal the mismatch
findings.evidence: run.sh:17 rebuilds relay and relay-native on every launch. run.sh:26-28 only asks `relay ping` whether some engine answers, then execs the new client against it. The only identity on the wire is `version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/bus.rs:18), which is '4.0.0-dev' for every build. app.version's `git_sha`/`built_at` read `option_env!("RELAY_GIT_SHA")`/`option_env!("RELAY_BUILT_AT")` (handlers/app.rs:21-22), but no build step sets them: build.rs emits only rerun-if-changed, and neither ci.yml nor run.sh exports them, so both fields are always null. The cost already shows. The client carries hand-written 'older engine' explanations (apps/relay-native/src/tools_plugins.rs:13-23 STALE_ENGINE, reused at shell.rs:959; guardrail_settings.rs:324), and README.md:31 and docs/MOBILE.md:31 tell the user to restart by hand. README documents the reuse, but it is not harmless. A live engine's hooks also resolve `current_exe().parent().join("relay")` (hooks.rs:38-43), which is the freshly rebuilt CLI, so running agents' hook adapters and MCP servers become new code talking to the old engine.
findings.impact: After any pull or rebuild, the next launch (desktop icon or ./run.sh) opens a new client against the old engine. Any op or field added since then fails with 'unknown field' or 'not implemented' on pages that have no special-case message, and the user is not told why. Every new feature adds another ad hoc STALE_ENGINE-style string.
findings.fix: Detect it in run.sh, where it is cheap. Read the engine PID from `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay-v4/$RELAY_INSTANCE.lock` and test `[[ $(readlink /proc/$pid/exe) == *' (deleted)' ]]`. This is true exactly when the binary was relinked after the engine started (verified in the scratchpad with a cargo-style relink). When it is true, print one clear notice, and offer `relay q app.quit` when no sessions are live. For the client, have the engine report its executable's mtime (or a real build id) in bus.ping and show one banner, replacing the per-feature STALE_ENGINE strings. Either populate or remove the dead RELAY_GIT_SHA/RELAY_BUILT_AT fields.

v1.reason: run.sh:17 rebuilds both binaries. Lines 26-28 reuse any engine that answers ping and then exec the new client. README.md:31-33 documents the reuse ('needs a deliberate restart'), so the reuse itself is intended. Detecting the mismatch is what is missing. bus.ping returns only CARGO_PKG_VERSION (bus.rs:18). app.version's git_sha/built_at read option_env!("RELAY_GIT_SHA"/"RELAY_BUILT_AT") (app.rs:21-22), but nothing in the repo sets them: build.rs only bundles plugins, and rg finds no other reference. Both fields are therefore always null and dead. The cost is concrete: hand-written skew explanations already exist in tools_plugins.rs:13-23 (STALE_ENGINE, which hard-codes the dev instance in its text), in shell.rs:959, which shows STALE_ENGINE whenever plugin.list is empty, and in guardrail_settings.rs:324. Every op added later fails without explanation on any page that lacks such a string.
v1.correction: The category is better described as error-handling/design: the reuse works as documented, and the defect is that the mismatch is never detected. The claim about agent hooks is accurate: sessions resolve RELAY_BIN to the absolute target/debug/relay path, which gets relinked. But the CLI is a thin forwarder, so the impact there is small. The /proc/<pid>/exe '(deleted)' check in run.sh is a sound, cheap detector. Populating RELAY_GIT_SHA/RELAY_BUILT_AT from build.rs, or removing them, settles the dead fields.

findings.title: Every launch rewrites the user's single desktop entry to the checkout and instance of the last run, and a failure in that step blocks the launch
findings.evidence: run.sh:18 `python3 scripts/install-native-desktop.py "$RELAY_INSTANCE"` runs after every successful build. The script writes one fixed file, applications/com.quietsoftware.Relay4.desktop (install-native-desktop.py:24), with `Exec="<this checkout>/run.sh" <instance>` (line 22; the checkout is `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`, line 7). README.md:22 documents `./run.sh stable` and `./run.sh test`. Agents run run.sh from their worktrees (outputs/ui-parity-review.md:25: '`./run.sh` launches this worktree's build'), and those worktrees are later deleted (crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:362). The call sits in the `then` branch under `set -e`, so any failure of this cosmetic step exits run.sh before the window opens: a relative XDG_DATA_HOME raises SystemExit at lines 13-14, an unwritable ~/.local/share fails the write, missing resources fail the read. test-launcher.py dies exactly this way today (exit 2).
findings.impact: After one `./run.sh test`, the menu or dock 'Relay' entry opens the empty test instance, so projects and sessions appear to have vanished. After an agent runs ./run.sh in .relay/worktrees/<name>, the menu entry points into that worktree and silently does nothing once the worktree is removed (Terminal=false, so no error appears).
findings.fix: Make desktop registration an explicit step (`./run.sh --install-desktop`, or a documented one-off run of the script). At minimum, skip it outside the primary checkout (`git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir` in a linked worktree) and for non-default instances. If several instances need launchers, write per-instance entries (com.quietsoftware.Relay4.<instance>.desktop, Name=Relay (test)). Make it non-fatal: `python3 ... || echo 'warning: desktop entry not updated' >&2`.

v1.reason: run.sh:18 calls install-native-desktop.py "$RELAY_INSTANCE" after every successful build. The script writes one fixed path, $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/com.quietsoftware.Relay4.desktop (line 24), and replaces Exec with "<this checkout>/run.sh" <instance> (lines 7, 22). After `./run.sh test`, or after any run from a .relay/worktrees/<name> checkout, the user's single menu entry opens that instance or that worktree. The entry is Terminal=false, so it fails silently once the worktree is deleted. The call sits in the `then` branch under `set -euo pipefail`, so a failure in it (relative XDG_DATA_HOME raising SystemExit at lines 13-14, a missing resource, an unwritable data dir) exits run.sh before the window opens. scripts/test-launcher.py copies only run.sh into a temp root (line 11), so python3 cannot find scripts/install-native-desktop.py, exits 2, and `assert launch().returncode == 0` at line 42 fails. The test is broken today in exactly this way. Nothing in the README documents that a launch rewrites the desktop entry.
v1.correction: A second problem makes this worse. test-launcher.py does not isolate XDG_DATA_HOME, so if it copied the script along it would overwrite the developer's real desktop entry with an Exec pointing into a deleted temp dir. The fix should make the step non-fatal (`|| true` with a warning) and should run it only for the primary checkout and the default instance, or behind an explicit flag.

findings.title: scripts/test-launcher.py has failed since run.sh began calling install-native-desktop.py; VERIFICATION.md still lists it as Passed and CI never runs it
findings.evidence: Line 11 copies only run.sh into the fixture root. run.sh:18, added in 54e6bbc after this test was written in 073019a/34802a7, then runs `python3 scripts/install-native-desktop.py` relative to that root. I reproduced this with an isolated copy (TMPDIR in the scratchpad, same fakes). The first launch() returns 2 with stderr `python3: can't open file '.../relay launcher w4gqrrfu/scripts/install-native-desktop.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory`, so `assert launch().returncode == 0` (line 42) fails. docs/VERIFICATION.md:34 still reports '`python3 scripts/test-launcher.py` | Passed'. The test env (lines 34-35) also leaves XDG_DATA_HOME unset. Copying the script in would therefore make the test overwrite the developer's real ~/.local/share/applications entry with a path into a temp dir that is deleted when the test ends.
findings.impact: The launcher has no working regression test: none of the engine-reuse, instance-selection or failure-path checks run. The verification doc is wrong, and the obvious repair would corrupt the user's desktop entry.
findings.fix: Copy scripts/install-native-desktop.py and apps/relay-native/resources/com.quietsoftware.Relay4.{desktop,svg} into the fixture (or put a fake python3 in fake_bin). Set XDG_DATA_HOME to a temp dir and assert the generated Exec line. The test needs no GTK and no real cargo, so add `python3 scripts/test-launcher.py` to the CI engine job. Update VERIFICATION.md.

v1.reason: test-launcher.py:11 copies only run.sh into the temp root. run.sh:4 cds to its own directory, and run.sh:18 then runs `python3 scripts/install-native-desktop.py "$RELAY_INSTANCE"` inside the `then` branch of the cargo `if`, where `set -e` applies. The script does not exist in the fixture, so python3 exits 2 and run.sh exits 2. The first `assert launch().returncode == 0` at test-launcher.py:42 therefore fails. Commit 54e6bbc added both the run.sh line and install-native-desktop.py, after test-launcher.py was written (073019a/34802a7), and the test was never updated. docs/VERIFICATION.md:34 still lists it as Passed. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs only cargo test and clippy for the Rust crates, not this script. The XDG_DATA_HOME point is also correct. test-launcher.py:34-35 inherits os.environ without setting XDG_DATA_HOME, and install-native-desktop.py:12 falls back to ~/.local/share. Copying the script in naively would rewrite the developer's real com.quietsoftware.Relay4.desktop with an Exec line pointing into a temp dir that is deleted when the test ends.
v1.correction: Lower to low. The claim that the launcher has no working regression test is overstated. test-launcher-real.py runs the real run.sh (including line 18, with XDG_DATA_HOME set to a temp dir) and checks engine reuse and instance isolation on a machine with GTK. What is actually lost is the headless coverage of the failure paths: build exit code passthrough, rejecting an invalid instance, engine start failure, and that no window opens after a failure. The proposed fix is right. The simplest version puts a fake `python3` (or a stub scripts/install-native-desktop.py) in the fixture and sets XDG_DATA_HOME to a temp dir. Because the test needs no GTK or cargo, adding it to the CI engine job is cheap. Also correct the stale VERIFICATION.md row.

findings.title: The launcher defaults to the dev instance while the CLI and the shipped login service default to stable, so the service runs a second engine that owns the phone door
findings.evidence: run.sh:5 `export RELAY_INSTANCE="${1:-dev}"`, but crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:24 has `#[arg(long, global = true, env = "RELAY_INSTANCE", default_value = "stable")]`. deploy/relay-remote.service:9 `ExecStart=%h/.cargo/bin/relay serve --remote` passes no instance, so it runs stable, from a different binary than the one run.sh builds. Its line 4 nevertheless claims 'The desktop app reuses a running engine, so it keeps working as before'. The mismatch is already worked around in crates/relay-cli/src/remote.rs:151-172 (resolve_instance). Both engines bind the door on 0.0.0.0:7420 (main.rs:68, registry.rs:60). The second one only prints 'phone door not opened' (remote.rs:107-113) into target/engine-dev.log and runs without a door.
findings.impact: A user who enables the login service, as docs/MOBILE.md:43-46 suggests, and keeps launching the desktop app gets two engines. The service starts a stable engine at login and takes port 7420; run.sh then starts a separate dev engine with no door. `relay remote pair` resolves to the live stable engine, so the phone pairs with and shows the stable store, not the dev sessions on the desktop. The result is two engines and two stores, with the phone silently showing the wrong one.
findings.fix: Use one default instance for the launcher, the CLI and the unit: make run.sh use the CLI's default, or set `Environment=RELAY_INSTANCE=dev` in the unit and document it. Point the unit at the same binary run.sh builds, or state that it is for installed builds only. Correct the comment on line 4.

v1.reason: run.sh:5 defaults RELAY_INSTANCE to `dev`, and relay-native's app.rs:304 also defaults to dev. relay-cli main.rs:24 defaults to `stable`. deploy/relay-remote.service:9 runs `%h/.cargo/bin/relay serve --remote`, which is the stable instance from the installed binary, yet line 4 of the unit claims 'The desktop app reuses a running engine'. With the unit enabled, run.sh's `ready` check (line 26) pings the dev socket, finds nothing and starts a dev engine with `--remote`. In remote.rs:107-113 that engine's door bind fails because the stable engine already holds 0.0.0.0:7420, so it logs 'phone door not opened' and runs without a door. `relay remote pair` probes stable first (resolve_instance, remote.rs:151-172), finds it alive and pairs the phone with the stable store. So the desktop shows dev while the phone shows stable. The comment on line 4 is false for the default launcher path.
v1.correction: Downgrade to low. The split is partly deliberate: docs/MOBILE.md §1 is the dev/run.sh flow, §2 is the installed `relay` flow, and its table documents `RELAY_INSTANCE=dev relay remote serve` to serve dev instead. The outcome is two engines and a phone showing a different store than the desktop, which is confusing but loses no data. The concrete defects are the false comment on line 4 of the unit and the missing documentation of the instance the unit runs. Fix the comment to say the unit runs the stable instance of the installed binary, and that run.sh's dev engine is separate unless both use the same instance. Optionally, have run.sh warn when another instance's engine already holds the door.

findings.title: The fixture-engine harness is copy-pasted across three scripts and has diverged in teardown, env scrubbing and error checking
findings.evidence: native-smoke.py:29-81 and 210-218, native-setup-smoke.py:16-67 and 107-110, and test-launcher-real.py:12-28 and 45-51 each re-implement temp XDG dirs, env scrubbing, engine start, the connect loop, call() and teardown. They have diverged in four ways. (a) native-smoke kills the engine when `wait(timeout=10)` times out (213-217). native-setup-smoke just calls `engine.wait(timeout=5)` (110), so a slow shutdown raises TimeoutExpired from `finally`, masking the original failure, and leaves the engine and its PTY children running while TemporaryDirectory deletes their store and socket. test-launcher-real sends SIGTERM (49) and never waits. (b) native-smoke pops RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN/RELAY_BRIEF from the client env (115-116). native-setup-smoke builds the client env from raw os.environ (77). test-launcher-real pops a different set, without RELAY_BRIEF (27). (c) native-smoke sets RELAY_BIN and NO_COLOR for the fixture engine (35); native-setup-smoke does not. Run from inside a Relay session, its fixture sessions therefore use the parent's RELAY_BIN (hooks.rs:32-37 prefers it) instead of the build under test. (d) call() raises RuntimeError in native-smoke (79-80) but uses `assert result["ok"]` in native-setup-smoke (66), which `python -O` strips.
findings.impact: Each fix lands in only one copy, as the kill fallback and the env scrubbing already have. A failing setup smoke can leak an engine plus fixture providers and report TimeoutExpired instead of the real assertion.
findings.fix: Extract one scripts/fixture_engine.py: a context manager that creates temp XDG dirs, scrubs the env (including RELAY_BIN), starts the engine, connects with a deadline, provides a call() that raises on error, and tears down with terminate, wait, then kill. Add a native_env() helper for the client. Import both from the two smoke scripts and from test-launcher-real.py.

v1.reason: The harness really is copied three times. native-smoke.py:29-81 and 209-218, native-setup-smoke.py:16-67 and 107-110, and test-launcher-real.py:12-28 and 45-51 each build temp XDG dirs, start the engine and tear it down, and the copies have diverged. (a) is true: native-setup-smoke.py:109-110 calls `engine.terminate(); engine.wait(timeout=5)` with no kill fallback, while native-smoke.py:213-217 catches TimeoutExpired and kills. A slow shutdown therefore raises from `finally`, which hides the real assertion, and can leave the engine running while TemporaryDirectory removes its store. test-launcher-real.py:49 only sends SIGTERM to the PID in the lock file and never waits. (c) is true and reachable: a Relay session exports RELAY_BIN (handlers/session.rs:571), and hooks.rs:25-37 prefers it over the sibling binary. native-setup-smoke.py:39 builds the engine env from os.environ without overriding or removing RELAY_BIN. Run from inside an agent session, its fixture hooks therefore run the parent's relay binary, not the build under test. (d) is true: native-setup-smoke.py:66 uses `assert result["ok"]`, which `python -O` strips.
v1.correction: Lower to low. These are developer smoke scripts that need GTK and a display. CI does not run them and no user ever runs them, so the cost is limited to the developer's own verification runs. Divergence (b) is mostly harmless. relay-native/src never reads RELAY_SESSION or RELAY_TOKEN, and the client is pointed at the fixture explicitly with RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET. So native-setup-smoke.py:77 building runenv from raw os.environ does not change behavior today. Smallest worthwhile fix: in native-setup-smoke.py, add the terminate/wait/kill fallback, set RELAY_BIN to the built binary, and raise instead of assert in call(). The shared fixture module in the finding is optional, with modest payoff for three scripts of about 100 lines each.

findings.title: Launcher failures are invisible when Relay is started from the desktop entry, and a failed build makes Relay impossible to open
findings.evidence: The installed entry runs run.sh with `Terminal=false` (apps/relay-native/resources/com.quietsoftware.Relay4.desktop:8; the installed copy in ~/.local/share/applications was confirmed). run.sh reports progress and failures only on stdout and stderr: 'Building Relay...' (16), the build log on failure (20-23), and 'Relay engine did not become ready' plus a log tail (37-38). A failed `cargo build` exits even when a previously working target/debug/relay-native exists. relay-native is not compiled in CI (ci.yml:69-82), so a commit that breaks only the native client can reach main.
findings.impact: After pulling a change that breaks the build, or with a half-edited main checkout, clicking the Relay icon does nothing: no window, no message, and the error lands only in the journal. A cold build after a dependency change runs for minutes with no feedback, which invites repeated clicks that queue parallel launches.
findings.fix: When stderr is not a terminal (`[[ -t 2 ]]`), report failures with notify-send or zenity, including the last lines of the log, and show a 'Building Relay...' notification. Consider offering the last good build, with a visible warning, when the build fails and target/debug/relay-native exists. Add StartupNotify=true to the template.

v1.reason: The desktop template sets Terminal=false (resources/com.quietsoftware.Relay4.desktop:8). The installed Exec runs run.sh, which writes all of its feedback to stdout/stderr: 'Building Relay…' (16), the build log on failure (20-23), and 'did not become ready' plus the log tail (37-38). A failed cargo build exits even when a working target/debug/relay-native exists. A launch from the menu therefore gives no visible feedback during a long build and none on failure. The mechanism is real. The impact is limited, though: this is a launcher for a developer running the app from source, the build log is kept in target/launcher-build.log, and a failure only blocks opening the window. It does not lose data or affect running sessions, because the engine outlives the window.
v1.correction: Downgrade to low: it is a usability gap in a source-checkout launcher, not a failure in a core flow. The claim that 'repeated clicks queue parallel launches' is weak. Concurrent cargo builds serialize on the target-dir lock, and the GTK application id makes a later client register against the first. A notify-send fallback when `! [[ -t 2 ]]` is a reasonable, cheap fix. Falling back to the last good build is a product choice and does not fix a bug.

findings.title: The launcher's readiness check treats a busy engine as absent and starts a duplicate that cannot open the store
findings.evidence: `ready() { timeout 2 "$relay" --instance "$RELAY_INSTANCE" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; }`. bus.ping is registered with `e.register` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/bus.rs:14), so it waits for the store mutex like any handler. If ping takes more than 2 s, line 28 starts a second `serve`. That process cannot open the store, which the live engine holds in locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE (store.rs:394-400), and exits with 'database is locked'. The loop at 35-39 then sees `kill -0` fail, prints 'Relay engine did not become ready' with the duplicate's error as the log tail, and exits 1. `timeout` exits 124 for 'connected but slow' and `relay ping` exits 5 when nothing listens (main.rs:104), but run.sh treats both the same.
findings.impact: Launching while the engine is slow for a few seconds (the condition CLAUDE.md warns about) fails to open the window, blames engine startup, and spawns a stray serve process each time.
findings.fix: Capture ping's exit status. Spawn only on 5 (no engine). On 124, keep polling until the deadline and then report 'engine is running but not answering'. Optionally, check the instance lock (`flock -n .../relay-v4/$RELAY_INSTANCE.lock true`) before spawning.

v1.reason: run.sh:26 checks readiness with `timeout 2 relay ... ping`. bus.ping is registered with e.register (handlers/bus.rs:14), so it waits for the store mutex. If any locked handler holds the mutex for more than about 2 s (including CLI startup and connect), ready() fails and run.sh:32 spawns a second `serve`. serve::start opens the store (serve.rs:21) before it takes the socket flock (socket.rs:68). The duplicate therefore blocks on the EXCLUSIVE store for up to busy_timeout 5000 ms (store.rs:398-400) and exits with an error. kill -0 fails, run.sh prints 'Relay engine did not become ready' with the duplicate's error and exits 1, and the window does not open. The duplicate cannot damage the store, because it never acquires it. I could not show that a 2 s mutex hold happens in normal use at launch. The trigger depends on a slow locked handler, which CLAUDE.md treats as a bug in itself.
v1.correction: The consequence is a failed launch with a misleading message, followed by a retry. No stray process is left behind, because the duplicate exits on its own, so 'spawns a stray serve process each time' overstates it. The fix is right: tell exit 124 (slow) apart from 5 (unreachable), or check the instance flock before spawning. Registering bus.ping with register_unlocked would also remove the dependence on the mutex.

findings.title: install-native-desktop.py escapes Exec only for the quoting layer, so checkout paths containing $, a double quote or a backtick produce an entry GLib rejects
findings.evidence: Lines 18-20 prefix each of backslash, double quote, backtick and dollar with one backslash. The Desktop Entry spec applies the string-value escape before the quoting rule, so a literal $ inside a quoted argument must be written as two backslashes followed by $. I checked this against GLib 2.88 (PyGObject GLib.KeyFile plus g_shell_parse_argv). For /home/a/$HOME/run.sh, /home/a/say "hi"/run.sh and a path containing backticks, the generated line makes get_string fail with 'Key file contains key "Exec" which has a value that cannot be interpreted'. The comment at 16-17 claims such paths are handled. Line 22 `desktop.replace("Exec=relay-native", ...)` also does nothing, silently, if the template line changes, and would also rewrite a future TryExec=relay-native line.
findings.impact: A checkout under such a path gets a launcher entry that GLib-based menus cannot read or launch.
findings.fix: After the quoting-level escapes, add `argument = argument.replace('\\', '\\\\')`, which doubles every backslash. With this, all five test paths round-trip through GLib to the original argv[0]. Replace the substring edit with a line-anchored one that fails loudly unless ^Exec=relay-native$ occurs exactly once.

v1.reason: scripts/install-native-desktop.py:18-20 adds only one backslash before each of \ " ` $. The Desktop Entry spec applies string-value unescaping before the quoting rule, so a literal $ or ` inside a quoted argument must be written with a doubled backslash. I reproduced it with PyGObject GLib.KeyFile and the script's exact escaping. Paths with `$` or a backtick fail with 'Key file contains key "Exec" which has a value that cannot be interpreted'. A path containing a space round-trips correctly. The comment at 16-17 says such paths are handled. Line 22's `replace("Exec=relay-native", ...)` silently does nothing if the template changes, but today the template (com.quietsoftware.Relay4.desktop) has exactly one `Exec=relay-native` and no TryExec.
v1.correction: The trigger is rare: the checkout path has to contain $, " or a backtick. The broken entry is only a menu launcher, and ./run.sh still works. The fix is right: double every backslash after the quoting-level escapes. The line-22 fragility is a secondary note, not a current bug.

findings.title: CI runs third-party actions by mutable tag or branch, with default token permissions, persisted credentials and no job timeout
findings.evidence: `uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` (28) runs whatever is on that branch at run time. `actions/checkout@v4` (23, 50), `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` (33) and `actions/setup-node@v4` (52) are movable tags. There is no `permissions:` block, so GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository default. checkout keeps persist-credentials true, which puts the token in .git/config where every build script and test that `cargo test` compiles can read it. There is no timeout-minutes, so the default of 360 applies. `cancel-in-progress: true` (13) also applies to pushes to main, so the next merge can cancel a merge's run before it completes. No dependency advisory scan (cargo-deny or cargo-audit) runs.
findings.impact: A compromised or retargeted upstream action, or a malicious crate's build.rs, runs with the workflow token and can poison the main-branch rust-cache that later runs restore. A hung engine test can burn six hours of runner time.
findings.fix: Pin each action to a full commit SHA, with the tag in a comment. Add top-level `permissions: contents: read`, `with: persist-credentials: false` on checkout, and `timeout-minutes: 30` per job. Use `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`. Add a `cargo deny check advisories` (or cargo-audit) step.

v1.reason: .github/workflows/ci.yml:28 is `uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master`. Lines 23 and 50 use `actions/checkout@v4`, line 33 `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` and line 52 `actions/setup-node@v4`, all movable refs. ci.yml has no `permissions:` block and sets no `persist-credentials: false`, and neither job has `timeout-minutes`. Lines 11-13 set `cancel-in-progress: true` with the group keyed on `github.ref`. Pushes trigger only on `main`, and origin's HEAD is main, so two quick merges to main cancel the first merge's run. No advisory scan (cargo-deny or cargo-audit) runs. The impact is hardening-level. Any malicious crate build.rs already runs code in CI whatever these settings are; what these settings add is reach for the token and poisoning of the main-branch cache. What GITHUB_TOKEN can actually do depends on a repository setting this audit cannot see; repos created recently default to read-only. Low is right.
v1.correction: For contrast, mobile-apk.yml already sets `timeout-minutes: 120` and an explicit `permissions: contents: write`, which is broader than it needs only if it never publishes releases (it does attach APKs on tags, so write is justified there). Apply the fix to ci.yml only: SHA pins, `permissions: contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`, a job timeout, and `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`. An advisory scan is a reasonable addition but is a separate ask from hardening.

findings.title: CI pins Rust 1.94, but the workspace declares no rust-version while local and agent builds use 1.98
findings.evidence: [workspace.package] (lines 7-11) sets version, edition, license and publish but no rust-version. ci.yml:30 pins `toolchain: "1.94"`. This machine builds with the distro package rust 1:1.98.1 (no rustup, so a rust-toolchain.toml would not be honoured either). CLAUDE.md tells agents to run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` locally.
findings.impact: Code that uses a std API stabilized in 1.95-1.98 builds and passes clippy locally and in agent sessions, then fails CI on 1.94. In the other direction, lints added in clippy 1.95-1.98 fail local -D warnings runs that CI would pass, so agents change code that CI never asked about.
findings.fix: Add `rust-version = "1.94"` to [workspace.package] and `rust-version.workspace = true` to each member. Clippy's incompatible_msrv lint then flags newer std APIs on the local 1.98 toolchain. Bump it in the same PR as ci.yml's pin.

v1.reason: Cargo.toml:7-11 [workspace.package] has no rust-version. ci.yml:30 pins `toolchain: "1.94"`. On this machine `pacman -Q rust` reports `rust 1:1.98.1-1.1` and there is no ~/.rustup, so a rust-toolchain.toml would not be honoured. CLAUDE.md tells agents to run clippy with -D warnings locally. So code using an API stabilised after 1.94 passes local checks and then fails CI. The drift is real and its cost is small: a red CI run that is then fixed.
v1.correction: `rust-version` plus clippy's incompatible_msrv lint only covers the 'newer std API' direction. It does nothing about lints that are new in the 1.95-1.98 clippy firing locally but not in CI. Telling the two toolchains apart for that direction needs a note in CLAUDE.md, or a toolchain the agent image can actually select.

findings.title: Unused dependency declarations: serde and anyhow in relay-native, and tracing-subscriber's json feature
findings.evidence: apps/relay-native/Cargo.toml:11 declares `serde = { workspace = true }` and :19 declares `anyhow = { workspace = true }`. Searching apps/relay-native/src for `\bserde\b` (excluding serde_json) and for `\banyhow\b` finds no use: no derive, no serde::, no anyhow::. Cargo.toml:24 enables tracing-subscriber's "json" feature, but all three subscribers (relay-cli main.rs:209, remote.rs:49, relay-native main.rs:21) use the default text formatter, and nothing calls .json().
findings.impact: These are declarations to keep in sync that do nothing. The unused feature compiles tracing-serde into every binary, and the manifest misstates what the client depends on.
findings.fix: Delete the two relay-native lines and drop "json" from tracing-subscriber's features.

v1.reason: apps/relay-native/Cargo.toml:11 declares `serde` and line 19 declares `anyhow`. Searching apps/relay-native/src with rg for serde (excluding serde_json), Serialize, Deserialize and anyhow finds no use. Cargo.toml:24 enables tracing-subscriber's `json` feature. The only crates that depend on tracing-subscriber are relay-cli and relay-native, and all three subscribers (relay-cli main.rs:209, remote.rs:49, relay-native main.rs:21) use `tracing_subscriber::fmt()` with the default text formatter. Nothing calls `.json()`.
v1.correction: Removing serde from relay-native does not stop it being compiled, because serde_json and relay-bus pull it in anyway. The gain is an accurate manifest, not build time. Dropping "json" does stop tracing-serde from being built. Because relay-native cannot be built in agent sessions, the change to its manifest needs a compile on the developer machine.

findings.title: Workspace dependency choices compile avoidable crates: rand 0.9 beside tungstenite's rand 0.10, and gix with its full default feature set
findings.evidence: Cargo.toml:32 declares `rand = "0.9"`. Cargo.lock has rand 0.9.5 (pulled by relay-core and relay-remote) and rand 0.10.3 (pulled by tungstenite 0.30.0), so rand, rand_core and getrandom are each built twice (getrandom 0.3.4 is reached only through rand_core 0.9.5), plus rand_chacha 0.9. Cargo.toml:35 declares `gix = { version = "0.86", features = ["status", "worktree-mutation", "revision"] }` with default features left on. gix 0.86's defaults ('basic' + 'extras') already include those three features. They also pull gix-blame, gix-archive, gix-worktree-stream, gix-mailmap, gix-credentials, gix-prompt and gix-negotiate (all present in Cargo.lock), none of which relay-core calls. Its gix uses are open, status/is_dirty, rev_parse_single, tree diff and remote_tracking_ref_name.
findings.impact: Clean builds take longer for code that never runs, and the cost recurs in every checkout or worktree that builds its own target/.
findings.fix: Use `rand = "0.10"`. It has 5 call sites; RngCore becomes Rng at relay-remote/src/registry.rs:8 and relay-core/src/sessions.rs:92. Use `gix = { version = "0.86", default-features = false, features = ["status", "worktree-mutation", "revision", "sha1", "max-performance-safe"] }` and add back only what the compiler asks for (this audit could not compile to confirm the minimal set).

v1.reason: Cargo.lock has rand 0.9.5 (used by relay-core and relay-remote) and rand 0.10.3 (used by tungstenite 0.30.0). It also has rand_core 0.9.5 and 0.10.1. getrandom 0.3.4's only dependent is rand_core 0.9.5, and 0.4.3 comes in through rand 0.10, tempfile and uuid. So rand 0.9 adds rand, rand_chacha, rand_core and getrandom 0.3 as duplicate builds. In gix-0.86.0/Cargo.toml the default features are max-performance-safe, comfort, basic, extras, auto-chain-error and sha1. `extras` turns on worktree-stream, worktree-archive, revparse-regex, mailmap, credentials (gix-credentials, gix-prompt, gix-negotiate) and blame. The lockfile's gix entry lists gix-archive, gix-blame and gix-credentials. The crate sources use gix::open, status, remote, reference, object, progress and bstr, and none of blame, archive, mailmap or credentials. The extra crates are real, but the cost is clean-build time only.
v1.correction: In rand 0.10 the trait renames (RngCore and Rng) change the imports at relay-remote/src/registry.rs:8 and relay-core/src/sessions.rs:92 (`fill_bytes`). sessions.rs:75 also uses `rand::seq::IndexedRandom`, so check that import too. The minimal gix feature set must be found by compiling: `status` brings in dirwalk, attributes and index on its own, so the savings are mainly blame, archive, worktree-stream, mailmap and credentials.

findings.title: The scripts put the actions they verify inside assert statements, so python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE turns them into no-ops
findings.evidence: native-pointer-click.py:56 `assert translate(display, window, root, int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), ...)` performs the coordinate translation only inside the assert. native-smoke.py:135, 164 and 196 use `assert native.wait(timeout=...)==0`. Every check in native-smoke.py, native-setup-smoke.py and test-launcher*.py is an assert, including native-setup-smoke's call() error check (66).
findings.impact: With PYTHONOPTIMIZE set (or python3 -O), the pointer driver clicks at (0,0) of whatever display it is on. native-smoke kills every client immediately, because the wait is skipped and the finally block terminates the process, then skips every check. It still prints the success summary at line 209, claiming that saves, bursts and paste echoes were verified.
findings.fix: Perform side effects outside asserts and fail explicitly, e.g. `rc = native.wait(timeout=30); if rc: raise SystemExit(...)` and `if not translate(...): sys.exit(...)`. Alternatively, refuse to run when sys.flags.optimize is set.

v1.reason: Two calls with side effects sit inside asserts: native-pointer-click.py:56 `assert translate(...)` and native-smoke.py `assert native.wait(timeout=...)==0` (in the roadmap loop, the screenshot loop, and `try: assert burst.wait(timeout=20)==0`). Under python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE, those calls are removed. The `finally` then terminates each client at once, every check is skipped, and native-smoke still prints its JSON success summary claiming paste echoes, saves and bursts were verified. The driver would click at root (0,0) because px/py stay 0. smoke.rs:217 runs `python3 driver` and inherits the environment, so PYTHONOPTIMIZE reaches it.
v1.correction: The trigger is uncommon, since a developer has to have PYTHONOPTIMIZE set or run with -O. The concrete harm is a false pass from a verification script, not a product bug. The cheapest fix is a one-line guard at the top of each script, `if sys.flags.optimize: raise SystemExit('run without -O')`, rather than rewriting every assert.

findings.title: Running a subset with RELAY_SETUP_CASES fails on assertions that depend on the skipped cases
findings.evidence: Lines 72-73 skip any page not listed in RELAY_SETUP_CASES, but later checks assume the earlier cases ran. Line 93 asserts `len(call("project.list")["projects"]) == 2`, which needs the project created by workspace-project-submit. Line 100 hard-codes `{"project_id":1}`. Line 106 asserts `len(call("workspace.list")["workspaces"]) == 1` unconditionally after the loop.
findings.impact: `RELAY_SETUP_CASES=toggles` fails at line 106 ('Retry must reuse the workspace', 0 workspaces). `RELAY_SETUP_CASES=setup-github-connect-submit` fails at line 93 with one project. The filter, meant for quick iteration, reports false failures.
findings.fix: Encode prerequisites, e.g. a map from each case to the earlier cases it needs, which are then included automatically. Look up the project by path instead of id 1, and run the final assertion only when workspace-project-submit ran.

v1.reason: native-setup-smoke.py:71-73 skips any page that is not in RELAY_SETUP_CASES, but line 106 asserts `len(call("workspace.list")["workspaces"]) == 1` after the loop unconditionally. Only workspace-project-submit creates the workspace: smoke.rs:536-568 drives setup-scan/setup-add. The toggles page only runs verify_panel_toggles (smoke.rs:589-592), so `RELAY_SETUP_CASES=toggles` ends with 0 workspaces and fails at 106. Line 93 (`projects == 2`) needs the project created by workspace-project-submit. Line 100 hard-codes project_id 1. The filter was added in 6c09885 for quick iteration, and on most subsets it reports a false failure.
v1.correction: This affects developer iteration only. Running the full script still passes, and no product behavior is involved. The simplest fix is to make the prerequisites explicit: always include workspace-project-submit when filtering, or guard lines 93, 100 and 106 on whether it ran.

findings.title: native-pointer-click.py injects real pointer events into whatever $DISPLAY is, with no check that it is a test display
findings.evidence: Line 29 `display = open_display(None)` uses $DISPLAY. Lines 57-61 raise and focus the window, then call XTestFakeMotionEvent and XTestFakeButtonEvent at absolute screen coordinates. The only guard is `assert display, 'An X11 test display is required'` (30), which also passes on the user's own X11 or XWayland session. native-setup-smoke.py:78-79 enables the driver when RELAY_SETUP_POINTERS is set and forces GDK_BACKEND=x11, but never starts Xvfb.
findings.impact: Running the pointer variant from a desktop session moves the user's real pointer and clicks repeatedly. If focus-stealing prevention keeps another window above the smoke window, the clicks land in that window.
findings.fix: Have native-setup-smoke.py start its own Xvfb (or require xvfb-run) when RELAY_SETUP_POINTERS is set. Make the driver refuse to run unless an explicit RELAY_TEST_DISPLAY matches $DISPLAY.

v1.reason: The pointer driver is reached only when the developer explicitly sets RELAY_SETUP_POINTERS (native-setup-smoke.py:78-79). It is not in any CI workflow or documented run, and README and VERIFICATION.md list only native-smoke and test-launcher. Its purpose, stated in its docstring and in smoke.rs:215-224, is to inject real X11 pointer clicks into the uniquely titled disposable smoke window. It finds that window by exact title, raises and focuses it, and clicks at translated coordinates. When a developer opts in on their own display and the pointer moves, the tool is doing what it is for. No security boundary or user data is involved. The 'clicks land in another window' case depends on a window manager refusing raise/focus, which the finding does not establish. This is a developer-tool convenience preference, not a defect worth an audit finding.

findings.title: run.sh passes a Relay session's environment (RELAY_BIN, RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_STORE, ...) into the engine and client it starts
findings.evidence: run.sh only runs `unset RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET` (12) before starting `serve` (32) and exec'ing the client (46). Every agent PTY carries RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_STORE, RELAY_WORKTREE, RELAY_BRIEF and RELAY_BIN (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:565-575). relay_bin() prefers an explicit RELAY_BIN over the engine's own sibling binary (crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:32-37), and sessions take their hook and MCP binary from it (session.rs:435). The smoke scripts already scrub these variables (native-smoke.py:36-37).
findings.impact: When an agent verifies its worktree with `./run.sh test`, the new test engine inherits the parent session's RELAY_BIN. Every session that engine launches then runs hooks and the MCP server from the parent engine's relay (the main checkout's build), not the worktree build under test, so hook and MCP changes look verified without ever having run.
findings.fix: Next to line 12, add `unset RELAY_SESSION RELAY_TOKEN RELAY_BRIEF RELAY_STORE RELAY_WORKTREE RELAY_PROJECT RELAY_BIN` (or use `env -u ...` for the serve command only).

v1.reason: run.sh:12 unsets only RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET. Agent PTYs get RELAY_BIN set to an absolute path from the parent engine's relay_bin() (handlers/session.rs:571). When run.sh starts `serve` (run.sh:32), the new engine inherits that variable. In the new engine, hooks::relay_bin_from (hooks.rs:32-37) returns the explicit RELAY_BIN before it tries current_exe's sibling. plan_launch (session.rs:435) then uses that path for hooks, plugin MCP servers and the RELAY_BIN it passes on to its sessions. So when an agent runs `./run.sh test` from a worktree, the test engine's sessions use the parent checkout's relay CLI and not the one just built in the worktree. I checked whether the inherited RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN would break the launch some other way. They do not: `relay ping` always sends Actor::User (relay-cli main.rs:271), so ready() works. The orphan scan in pty.rs:408-421 matches on RELAY_INSTANCE, which run.sh re-exports, so the parent engine does not adopt the test engine as one of its own processes. native-smoke.py:34-37 sets RELAY_BIN explicitly, and test-launcher-real.py pops RELAY_SESSION/TOKEN. That shows the author knows these variables leak.
v1.correction: The only variable with a proven effect is RELAY_BIN. RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN/RELAY_STORE/RELAY_WORKTREE/RELAY_BRIEF/RELAY_PROJECT leak too but do no demonstrated harm here. Unsetting them is still good hygiene, because the engine's children and any CLI call without --actor would act as the agent. The fix in the finding is right: unset them all next to line 12.

results.coverage:
Read in full: the six assigned files (plugin.json, instructions.md, README.md, docs/mcp-tools.md, docs/setup.md, docs/agent-workflow.md); crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs (all 2170 lines) and unreal_process.rs; crates/relay-core/src/plugins.rs, skills.rs and build.rs; and the embedded scripts common.py, capture.py, play.py, anim_preview.py, anim_inspect.py, asset_audit.py, asset_refs.py, data_table.py, project_check.py, preview_asset.py and blueprint_info.py. Also traced, for the plugin wiring: handlers/session.rs (plan_launch, prepare_launch, create, close), handlers/provider.rs (plugin.list/get/enable), hooks.rs (install_claude, add_claude_mcp_servers, install_git, uninstall_git, hook matchers), providers.rs (codex_mcp_config), recovery.rs, pty.rs (relay_children), the guardrail.rs authorize/destructive_write/exec paths, the role allowlists in settings.rs, BUS.md §9.1 and D159-D162.

Skills: every SKILL.md front matter was checked. Names are valid and equal their folders; descriptions are single-line plain YAML scalars with no ': ' or ' #', 489-835 chars, all within 1024. unreal-editor-automation SKILL.md and its three reference files were read in full. For the other 19 skills, every fenced code block (about 5,500 lines of C++/Python/C#/ini/json) was extracted with line numbers and checked against current UE5 APIs, along with each skill's "Relay tools" section and spot-read prose; the rest of their prose was not read line by line.

Not covered: import_fbx.py and blender_to_unreal (Blender chunk), unreal_py/tests, the native client's plugin UI.

Limits: no engine source was available, so UE-side facts were judged from memory. Specifically, Remote Control CORS and passphrase defaults, the str() format of Unreal Python enums, and whether Codex clears the environment of stdio MCP servers could not be verified; inspecting the local Codex binary was denied by the auto-mode classifier. Those findings carry the matching confidence.

Pedantic clippy casts in these files were checked; none touch a real bug.

Search patterns used included: ue_* names and argument examples across plugin docs and skills, RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_WORKTREE, plugins::, mcp_servers, PreToolUse/matcher, task.create, b_ property names, remove_hook_dir/install_git, relay_children.

findings.title: Editor launched by ue_editor_launch / ue_build restart_editor inherits the agent's RELAY_* identity, so Relay's startup orphan reaper SIGKILLs the human's editor on the next engine start
findings.evidence: launch() builds `std::process::Command::new(&binary).arg(uproject).arg("-RCWebControlEnable").args(extra)…process_group(0)` and spawns it with no env_remove/env_clear ("Its own process group: the editor outlives this MCP server and the agent", line 302). `relay unreal-mcp` runs under Claude with the session env: hooks.rs:401 says the MCP config "inherits the session/token/project environment from the Claude process", and handlers/session.rs:563-574 sets RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_INSTANCE and RELAY_STORE. At engine start, recovery.rs:64-73 calls `pty::relay_children(instance, &store_path)`. That returns every live pid whose /proc environ has a matching RELAY_INSTANCE + RELAY_STORE + RELAY_SESSION (pty.rs:411-430), and each one gets kill_wait: `kill(-pid, SIGTERM)`, then SIGKILL 2 s later (recovery.rs:20-35).
findings.impact: Trigger: an agent applies a C++ change the way instructions.md rule 5 says (`ue_build restart_editor:true`, which calls launch_editor at unreal.rs:1572), or calls ue_editor_launch. The human keeps working in that editor, then Relay restarts (app update, crash, quit/relaunch). Recovery treats the editor as the agent's orphan and kills its whole process group (UnrealEditor, ShaderCompileWorkers) after 2 s; unsaved level and asset edits are lost. Second effect: the editor and its children carry agent A's RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN. Commits from the editor's Git integration then run the pre-commit gate as agent A (hooks.rs:122-129) with agent caps. Any `relay` call made from the editor (e.g. another agent's ue_python subprocess) also acts as A.
findings.fix: In unreal_process::launch, strip Relay's identity from the child: `for (k, _) in std::env::vars_os() { if k.to_string_lossy().starts_with("RELAY_") { command.env_remove(k); } }`, or at least RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_INSTANCE and RELAY_STORE. Add a test that the launch Command carries no RELAY_SESSION. The same applies to any other long-lived child the bridge starts.

v1.reason: unreal_process.rs:285-306: launch() builds the Command with no env_remove/env_clear (the only env_remove anywhere in crates/ is NO_COLOR in pty.rs:179). It sets process_group(0), so the editor leads its own group. Under Claude the unreal MCP server inherits the agent's environment (hooks.rs:401 says so, and session.rs:563-574 sets RELAY_SESSION/TOKEN/INSTANCE/STORE on the PTY), so the editor carries them too. On every engine start, recovery.rs:66-73 calls pty::relay_children(instance, store). pty.rs:411-430 matches any live pid with RELAY_INSTANCE + RELAY_STORE + RELAY_SESSION, and kill_wait (recovery.rs:20-35) sends SIGTERM to -pid (the editor's group), then SIGKILL after 2 s. Trigger: an agent runs ue_editor_launch or ue_build restart_editor:true (unreal.rs:1572 -> launch_editor -> launch at :649), the human keeps working in that editor, and Relay restarts. The editor and its process group are killed; unsaved edits are lost. The secondary claim also holds: the pre-commit hook script (hooks.rs:122-129) acts on RELAY_SESSION from the environment, so a commit from inside the editor is gated as that agent.
v1.correction: This affects Claude agents. Codex clears the MCP server's environment to a short allowlist (see #12), so an editor launched from a Codex agent likely carries no RELAY_* and is not reaped. Fix as proposed: strip RELAY_* from the launch Command. The reaper could also skip processes that lead their own process group outside the session's tree, but stripping the env is the direct fix.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. unreal_process.rs:285-306 launch() builds Command::new(UnrealEditor) with no env_clear or env_remove, sets process_group(0) ("Its own process group: the editor outlives this MCP server and the agent", :302) and spawns it. Both ue_editor_launch (unreal.rs:389) and ue_build restart_editor (unreal.rs:1572) go through launch_editor -> launch (:649). I checked that Claude passes the identity to its stdio MCP servers: the four live `relay --instance dev mcp` processes, children of `claude --mcp-config .relay/relay.mcp.json`, all have RELAY_SESSION/TOKEN/INSTANCE/STORE/BIN/BRIEF/PROJECT/WORKTREE in /proc/<pid>/environ. I read only the variable names. The unreal server sits in that same file with no env override (plugin.json has no env, hooks.rs:405-436), so it inherits the same values. holder_id (unreal.rs:510) reads RELAY_SESSION, which shows the bridge expects to have it. Nothing in relay-cli removes the variables outside tests. serve.rs:23 runs recovery on every engine start, not only after a crash. recovery.rs:66-73 reaps every pid that pty.rs:411-430 matches; the match uses only RELAY_INSTANCE + RELAY_STORE + RELAY_SESSION. kill_wait (:20-35) sends SIGTERM to -pid, which is the editor's own group, then SIGKILL after 2 s. Pty::kill and Engine::shutdown signal only the agent's own process group, so the editor survives the agent and the engine shutdown, and is then killed when the next engine starts. This is not intended: SPEC §14 says recovery reaps "orphaned claude/codex processes", and the bridge says the editor should outlive the agent. No DECISIONS entry covers it.
(b) Who and how often: Linux users of the Unreal plugin with Claude agents. instructions.md:7 (rule 5) tells agents to apply every C++ change with ue_build restart_editor:true, because Linux has no Live Coding. So the editor the human is using is often one an agent launched. It fires whenever the Relay engine restarts while that editor is open: app.quit then relaunch, an engine update (the native app's STALE_ENGINE text tells users to do exactly this), or an engine crash. Closing and reopening the GUI window does not trigger it, because the engine outlives the window (run.sh:45). A reboot or logout ends both processes anyway.
(c) Consequence: within about 2 s of engine start, with no prompt, the editor and its group (ShaderCompileWorkers etc.) are terminated. UE's SIGTERM handler only requests an engine exit, without a save prompt, and SIGKILL follows. Unsaved level and asset edits since the last UE autosave are lost; the default autosave interval is 10 min, and UE may offer a package restore on the next launch. The only trace is "reaped orphan pid N (session A)" in app.recovery.last.
(d) High is right. It is real data loss of in-memory work and a silent kill of the user's main tool in a normal plugin flow. It does not reach critical: it needs the plugin, a Claude agent, an engine restart and unsaved work, autosave bounds the loss, and saved assets are not corrupted.
(e) The fix is correct and safe. Nothing that runs in the editor reads RELAY_* (I checked unreal_py and the plugin docs). Stripping every RELAY_* variable stops the reap and also removes the leaked token.
v2.correction:
Narrow the trigger to an engine restart (app.quit/relaunch, an update, a crash). Closing and reopening the desktop window does not trigger it, because the engine outlives the window (run.sh:45).

The secondary claims are minor:
- **Commits from the editor:** these are gated as agent A only when the editor's checkout has Relay's per-worktree hooksPath. That is true for the primary checkout once any agent has been launched there.
- **Bus calls "as A":** this adds no new privilege. ue_python already runs arbitrary Python as the user, and it can shed RELAY_SESSION to act as `user`, since the socket does not authenticate `user` (guardrail.rs:849-850).

After the fix, git or relay calls made from the editor run as the user, which is the right identity for the human and opens no new hole.

**Testing the fix:** factor the Command construction out of launch() and assert that get_envs() lists ("RELAY_SESSION", None) etc. Avoid mutating the process environment in a parallel test.

**Codex:** the Codex exemption is likely (Codex launches MCP servers with an allowlisted environment), but I did not verify it here.

**Optional defense in depth:** limit the env-based reaper to what SPEC §14 promises, claude/codex processes and members of recorded session process groups. Then no intentionally detached descendant can be killed this way.

findings.title: ue_editor_quit / ue_build restart_editor immediately SIGTERM an editor that doesn't answer Remote Control within 3 s, without saving, contrary to the docs; the tools' own remedy for a failed bind leads straight there
findings.evidence: `match remote("GET", "/remote/info", None, Duration::from_secs(3)) { Ok(_) => {…save_dirty_packages…quit_editor()…} Err(_) => notes.push("the editor did not answer; asking the process to terminate instead (unsaved changes are lost)".into()) }`. Then line 600: `if signalled.is_none() && (notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("terminate")) || …) { for pid in &before { kill(*pid) } }` runs on the first loop iteration. mcp-tools.md:91-93 and editor-automation SKILL.md:270-272 say quit "saves dirty packages … sends a terminate signal if it is still running 20 s later".
findings.impact: When the editor is open but Remote Control is not listening, the editor is terminated at once and nothing is saved. That happens when the web server isn't started (setup.md step 2), when the bind failed, or when the game thread is blocked for more than 3 s. ue_editor_status's own advice for a bind failure (unreal.rs:1657) and editor-automation SKILL.md:273-276 tell agents to "quit the editor … and use ue_editor_launch". An agent following that advice, or running the documented C++ loop `ue_build restart_editor:true` (unreal.rs:1518-1520), loses the human's unsaved work. The agent learns this only from a note in the result. No argument lets it quit safely.
findings.fix: When /remote/info does not answer, refuse with an error asking the human to save and close the editor; only send a signal with an explicit `force: true` argument (and expose it in the ue_editor_quit and ue_build schemas). Keep the 20 s escalation only after a successful save request. Fix the docs to describe the unreachable case.

v1.reason:
quit_editor (unreal.rs:582-628) first sends GET /remote/info with a 3 s timeout (remote_at: connect timeout 3 s, read timeout 3 s). If that fails it pushes a note containing "terminate". On the first loop iteration, line 600's condition `notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("terminate"))` is true, so it runs unreal_process::kill (a plain `kill <pid>`, i.e. SIGTERM) on every editor for the uproject without any save request. SIGTERM makes UE request engine exit with no save prompt, so dirty packages are lost. Triggers that are reachable:
- The web server was never started.
- The bind failed. editor_status's advice at 1655 says to quit and relaunch, and SKILL.md 273-276 tells agents to use ue_editor_quit.
- The game thread stalls for more than 3 s, so the request is accepted but never answered.
ue_build restart_editor:true (1518-1520), which instructions.md rule 5 prescribes for every C++ change, calls quit_editor on the same path. The docs (mcp-tools.md 91-93, SKILL.md 270-272) promise a save, then a signal only after 20 s. There is no argument to refuse instead of kill. The only warning is a note in the result, which comes after the fact.
v1.correction: The decisive line is the condition at unreal.rs:600 together with the Err arm at 594. Fix: when /remote/info does not answer, bail and ask the human to save and close, and send the signal only with an explicit force argument (in both the ue_editor_quit and ue_build schemas). Correct the docs for the unreachable case.

v2.reason:
(a) Verified at 361c6f9.
- In crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs, quit_editor (:572) probes `remote("GET","/remote/info",None,3s)` (:577). remote_at has a 3 s connect timeout and a 3 s read timeout.
- Any Err pushes a note containing "terminate" (:589).
- On the first pass of the loop, `notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("terminate"))` (:600) runs unreal_process::kill on every PID in `before`. kill (unreal_process.rs:66) is a plain `kill <pid>`, i.e. SIGTERM. No save request is sent.

The UE 5.8.2 source installed on this machine confirms the consequence:
- UnixCommonStartup.cpp:248 installs GracefulTerminationHandler for SIGTERM (UnixPlatformCrashContext.cpp:156-173, 1154-1164). It only sets the exit flag through RequestExitWithStatus(false, …).
- MainFrameHandler.h:59: once exit is requested, CanCloseTab approves the close without calling CanCloseEditor. CanCloseEditor holds the only SaveDirtyPackages prompt (:164).
- UUnrealEdEngine::FinishDestroy calls PackageAutoSaver->UpdateRestoreFile(false) (UnrealEdEngine.cpp:520-524), so the next launch does not even offer the autosave restore.

(b) Reachability.
- ue_editor_quit and ue_build are not in LIVE (:33), so call() applies no guard first. The Err arm also skips the guard_project check that the Ok arm runs.
- Trigger 1, no web server. The human opened the editor by hand without the web server running. setup.md step 2 offers "run WebControl.StartServer … each session" as a normal option, and Tier-1 users may not have Remote Control at all. instructions.md rule 5 prescribes `ue_build restart_editor:true` for every C++ change. build() calls quit_editor whenever editors_for is non-empty (:1518-1519), and build's own refusal (:1524) points agents at restart_editor or ue_editor_quit.
- Trigger 2, bind failure. A failed bind after a quick relaunch is documented as recurring. The advice at :1657 and SKILL.md:273-276 tells agents to quit and relaunch.
- Trigger 3, setup advice. :1487 tells agents to run "ue_editor_quit, then ue_editor_launch" right after ue_setup_check fix writes the ini, which typically happens while the server is not up yet.
- Trigger 4, a game-thread stall of 3 s or more. FHttpServerModule is an FTSTickerObjectBase, so it is serviced from the core ticker on the game thread. The Slate AddModalWindow loop ticks only Slate and ModalLoopTickEvent, and no subscriber of that event ticks the core ticker. So any open modal dialog, a map load, or a peer agent's long lock-free script makes the probe time out. ue_asset_audit is such a script: it is not in MUTATING and allows 1800 s.
- Relay's PreToolUse hooks match only Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash (hooks.rs:350, 517), so guardrails never see these MCP calls.
- Any provider permission prompt shows "Quit a running editor first (saving)".
- Linux only (/proc), which is the platform this plugin targets.

(c) Impact. The human's level and asset edits since their last save are discarded. The editor vanishes at once, or as soon as the modal or stall ends, because the flag is already set. The agent sees only a note afterwards. Recovery means digging through Saved/Autosaves by hand.

(d) Severity. High fits: data loss in the documented C++ loop, gated on the editor not answering Remote Control within 3 s. Critical is arguable from the literal "data loss" line, but the precondition, the optional plugin and the volatile unsaved state keep it at high.

(e) Fix. The proposed fix is correct: refuse when the probe fails, signal only with an explicit force, and escalate after 20 s only once a save request has succeeded. It needs the additions in the correction to be complete.
v2.correction:
Line slip: the first verifier puts the Err arm at :594; it is unreal.rs:589 (594 is the wait loop). The decisive pair is 589 and 600.

Add to related:
- unreal.rs:1487: the setup_check advice "ue_editor_quit, then ue_editor_launch".
- unreal.rs:1524: build's refusal, which steers agents to restart_editor or ue_editor_quit.
- unreal_process.rs:57: editors_for also matches any argv entry that ends with the same .uproject file name. Because the Err arm skips guard_project, an agent in an explicit worktree (D160: an explicit worktree still wins) would SIGTERM the human's main-checkout editor as well.

Fix completeness:
1. Even with force, signal only PIDs whose argv contains the canonicalized .uproject path. Do not use the file-name fallback for kill.
2. Pass `force` through build() to quit_editor, and expose it in both the ue_build and ue_editor_quit schemas. The description should say it discards unsaved work and needs the human's say-so.
3. Escalate after 20 s only when the save-and-quit python_tx returned Ok. Otherwise keep waiting and bail without signalling.
4. Reword the advice at :1487 and :1657, and the docs at mcp-tools.md:91-93 and SKILL.md:270-276, to "ask the human to save and close the editor" for the unreachable case.

findings.title: With the plugin's default_checkout "primary", closing an agent can delete the hook dir the shared checkout's core.hooksPath points at, silently disabling the commit guardrail for everyone else there
findings.evidence: Each create and launch runs install_git (session.rs:481, 892). It sets `git config --worktree core.hooksPath <repo>/.relay/hooks/<session>` (hooks.rs:150-153), so the shared primary checkout points at the most recently launched session's directory. In Close, `let teardown = if others == 0 { Some(read_teardown(..)) } else { None };` (line 1558) means uninstall_git_any runs only when no other session lives in that worktree. Line 1596 `crate::hooks::remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name);` then deletes the directory unconditionally. hooks.rs:283-284 claims a still-wired directory "is left alone by uninstall_git before this runs", which does not hold when others > 0. plugin.json:18 sets `"default_checkout": "primary"`, and plugins.rs:210-215 makes every new agent of an Unreal project share the main checkout.
findings.impact: Trigger: launch agent A, then agent B, in an Unreal project (both in the main checkout; hooksPath points at .relay/hooks/B). Close B, e.g. from the native menu, which sends remove_worktree:false. The main checkout's core.hooksPath now names a deleted directory. Git silently runs no pre-commit hook, so every later `git commit` by A (and by the human) skips guardrail.gate: commit caps, protected paths and shape gates. This lasts until some session in that checkout is launched or resumed again. PAIR sessions had the same exposure; the plugin makes sharing the default.
findings.fix: In Close, when others > 0 and the worktree's core.hooksPath is this session's directory, re-point it to a live session's hook directory, or keep the directory, before removing it. Simpler: since the script reads RELAY_SESSION from the environment, use one hook directory per checkout instead of per session and remove it only when the last session leaves.

v1.reason: install_git (hooks.rs:150-153) sets `core.hooksPath` to .relay/hooks/<session> per worktree on every launch (session.rs:481, 892), so the last-launched session's directory is the active one in a shared checkout. In Close (session.rs:1558), `teardown` is Some only when `others == 0`, so uninstall_git_any (via run_teardown, session.rs:352-354) does not run when another live session shares the checkout. remove_hook_dir at session.rs:1596 then deletes .relay/hooks/<closing session> unconditionally. The doc comment at hooks.rs:283-284 claims a still-wired directory is left alone; that is false here. Reachable: plugin.json sets `default_checkout: "primary"` (plugins.rs:210-215), so every Unreal agent shares the main checkout. remove_worktree:true is refused when others > 0 (session.rs:1555), but the native shell closes with remove_worktree:false (shell.rs:734), and so does agent_menu.rs:612 when its box is unchecked. Sequence: launch A, launch B, close B. hooksPath now names a deleted directory, and git silently runs no pre-commit. evaluate_commit (guardrail.rs:757: protected paths, caps) is enforced only through that hook, so A's and the human's `git commit` skip the gate until some session in that checkout is launched or resumed again.
v1.correction: Calibration: the commit gate is already cooperative (nothing in guardrail blocks `git commit --no-verify`), and write-time gating of protected paths still applies. This is a silent loss of one layer, not a full escape, but it fits the "safety check silently bypassed" high. Fix: when others > 0 and the worktree's active hooksPath is this session's directory, re-point it to a live session's directory before removing; or skip remove_hook_dir while it is still wired. A per-checkout hook directory also works, because the script reads RELAY_SESSION from the environment.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. install_git (hooks.rs:100-154) points the checkout's worktree-level core.hooksPath at .relay/hooks/<session> each time it runs. It runs on create (session.rs:892) and through prepare_launch (session.rs:481) on spawn, resume, wake and clear_restorable. So in a shared checkout the most recently created or launched session's directory is the active one. In Close, teardown is Some only when others == 0 (session.rs:1559, not 1558). Yet `crate::hooks::remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name)` at session.rs:1596 always runs. The doc comment at hooks.rs:283-284 assumes uninstall_git ran first, which is false when others > 0. I checked git's behaviour with git 2.55.0 in a scratch repo (worktreeConfig on, hooksPath at an absolute dir, then the dir removed): the commit succeeds with exit 0 and no warning.

(b) Who can trigger it, and how often: any user with 2+ agents in one checkout. plugin.json:18 `"default_checkout": "primary"` goes through plugins.rs:210-215 to session.rs:858-864, so every new agent of an Unreal project shares the main checkout, and D160 expects several agents there. PAIR sessions share one too. The native "Close session…" checkbox defaults to unchecked, so it sends remove_worktree:false (agent_menu.rs:612), and "Discard session" does the same (shell.rs:734). remove:true with others > 0 is refused anyway (session.rs:1556). Trigger: close the agent created or launched last while another stays. Creating a second agent and closing it without ever spawning it is enough.

The hook is the only commit gate agents have. git.commit needs bus_writes (guardrail.rs:363-367), which is off by default, and it is not in the builder allowlist (settings.rs:36). evaluate_exec (guardrail.rs:811-847) checks only denied commands and self-approval. So an agent's raw `git commit` is gated by nothing else. The Unreal instructions also tell agents to commit often (plugins/unreal-engine/instructions.md:16).

(c) What happens: evaluate_commit (guardrail.rs:757-809) stops running for raw commits in that checkout. Agents' commits over the caps (default 40 files / 2000 lines, settings.rs:29) or touching protected paths are no longer refused. The human's terminal commits no longer get the confirm hold (guardrail.rs:1028-1034). Nothing tells anyone. For Codex agents, the pre-tool adapter submits every tool as kind exec (relay-cli main.rs:506-512), so the commit hook is the only place their protected paths are enforced. The same holds for files Claude agents change through Bash. The test at sessions.rs:1347-1372 closes sessions oldest first "so the newest session's hook stays active until the very last close": the dangerous order is known and untested.

(d) High is right: a safety check silently disabled in a normal flow. It is not critical: the gate is cooperative (`--no-verify` is not denied by default), Claude's Edit/Write gates still apply, and the window is bounded.

(e) The proposed fix is right in direction but incomplete; see correction.

SIDE EFFECT TO REPORT TO THE USER (not part of this finding): while verifying, a scratch experiment wrote fish syntax (`set -l X ...`), but the Bash tool runs zsh. X came out empty, `cd $X` went to $HOME, and the commands ran in an existing throwaway repo ~/repo. That repo was created at 04:17 by another process, with one commit `91843cd init` by `t <t@t>`. My run at 05:09:28 added:
- commits 1956e2b "init" and 3ca689c "one" (adds file f)
- the file ~/repo/f and ~/repo/.relay/hooks/A/pre-commit
- `extensions.worktreeConfig=true` in .git/config (most likely mine; the existing [user] t@t/t values may have been there already)
- .git/config.worktree with `core.hooksPath=/repo/.relay/hooks/B`

I made no further writes, because I can't establish the config's earlier state well enough to roll it back exactly. Nothing in RelayV4 or the user's own projects was touched.
