Restoring would mean moving main back to 91843cd and deleting f, .relay/ and config.worktree; or ~/repo can simply be deleted if it is not needed.
v2.correction:
Lines and mechanism:
- The teardown line is session.rs:1559, not 1558.
- The impact over-claims "shape gates": evaluate_commit checks only protected paths and caps; shape gates are write-time only (evaluate_write).
- The human's commits through Relay's own git.commit stay gated in-process (git.rs:560-571). That path's refresh_git (git.rs:548, hooks.rs:160-185) also re-creates the dead session's directory.
- So the window closes on the next create, spawn, resume, wake or clear_restorable in that checkout, or on a bus git.commit there. It can reopen after an engine restart, because the startup fsck sweep (recovery.rs:123-143) deletes every closed session's hook directory, wired or not.

Extra consequence, same root cause: once the path is dangling, the healing install_git cannot read the dead directory's .relay-previous-hooks-path. It falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which I verified returns the dangling hooksPath itself. The surviving session then records the dead directory as its "previous" hook dir. The user's own pre-commit hook (.git/hooks/pre-commit, or a local core.hooksPath such as husky) silently drops out of the chain until the last session closes. That last close then unsets the worktree hooksPath instead of restoring a worktree-level user value. Running the existing test sessions.rs:1347-1372 newest-first fails its `assert_eq!(hooks(&f.repo), "user-hooks")`, which makes it a ready-made regression test.

Related location: the refused-create cleanup at session.rs:900-910 is guarded only by `p.pair_with.is_none()`, which predates D160. When a create into a shared primary checkout is refused after hooking, uninstall_git restores the pre-Relay path while other agents are still live. This trigger is rare.

Fix:
- In Close's staged phase, under hooks::writes(): when others > 0 and the active hooksPath is this session's directory, re-point it to a surviving live session's existing directory (or rerun install_git for that session) before remove_hook_dir. The survivor's previous-path file still holds the pre-Relay path.
- Apply the same handling to the refused-create cleanup.
- Make sweep_hook_dirs keep or re-point a directory that is still wired.
- "Keep the dir while wired" alone just moves the dangling path to the next engine start, because of the sweep.
- A per-checkout hook directory is not the simpler fix: the human branch of the script bakes the session name into its payload (hooks.rs:111, 132), and refresh_git and uninstall_git_any derive the session from the directory name (hooks.rs:170-182, 248-252).

findings.title: editors_for matches any editor whose argv ends with this project's .uproject file name, so other checkouts' (and other projects') editors count as this project's
findings.evidence: `.filter(|p| p.cmdline.iter().any(|a| Path::new(a).canonicalize().map(|c| c == want).unwrap_or(false) || a.ends_with(&*uproject.file_name().unwrap_or_default().to_string_lossy())))`. The suffix test matches /home/u/game/Game.uproject for a worktree's .relay/worktrees/x/Game.uproject, and also matches MyGame.uproject for Game.uproject.
findings.impact: The README recommends giving an agent its own worktree for C++ work. Such an agent's `ue_build` is refused whenever the human's editor is open on the main checkout (prebuild reports `editor_running`; unreal.rs:1522-1526 bails "the editor is running this project"). Building that separate copy cannot hot-reload the main editor. ue_editor_launch returns `already_running` for the other checkout's editor. ue_editor_quit, or ue_build restart_editor, sends SIGTERM to the other checkout's editor when it doesn't answer Remote Control (finding on quit_editor).
findings.fix: Compare canonical paths only. Resolve a relative argv entry against /proc/<pid>/cwd before canonicalizing instead of falling back to a file-name suffix match.

v1.reason: unreal_process.rs:57: `.any(|a| Path::new(a).canonicalize().map(|c| c == want).unwrap_or(false) || a.ends_with(&*uproject.file_name()...))`. The suffix test is OR'd in unconditionally, not used as a fallback, so it decides on its own. Any editor whose argv ends with "Game.uproject" counts as this project's editor. That includes another checkout of the same project and an unrelated project whose name ends that way ("MyGame.uproject"). The README (plugins/unreal-engine/README.md:20) explicitly supports giving an agent its own worktree for C++ work. In that worktree: build() at unreal.rs:1522 refuses with "the editor is running this project" while the human's editor has the main checkout open, launch_editor at unreal.rs:624 returns `already_running`, and engine_root (unreal_process.rs:119) may take the engine from the wrong editor. quit_editor (unreal.rs:575-601) calls guard_project when Remote Control answers, which protects that path. When the editor does not answer, it sends `kill` to every pid in `before`, which can be the other checkout's editor. That is reachable from ue_editor_quit, or from ue_build restart_editor:true.
v1.correction: The worst outcome needs Remote Control not to answer (otherwise guard_project stops the quit). The common outcome is a worktree agent's builds and launches being wrongly refused or skipped. The fix stands: compare canonical paths only, and resolve a relative argv entry against /proc/<pid>/cwd. At minimum, require the suffix match to start at a path-separator boundary and check the parent directory too.

findings.title: Any editor-script result above 60 KB is cut from the front before its RELAY_JSON line is parsed, so larger but valid ue_* calls fail with "printed no result"
findings.evidence: python_tx stores `"output": tail(&output.join("\n"), 2000)`. tail() then does `if out.len() > MAX_OUTPUT { … out = out[cut..].to_string() }` with MAX_OUTPUT = 60_000 (line 30), which removes the start of a long final line. python_json_tx then looks for `line.trim().strip_prefix("RELAY_JSON:")` (1724-1728) and fails with "the editor script printed no result", pasting the 60 KB tail into the error. A scratch measurement with realistic entries: 250 ue_level_actors rows ≈ 60.8 KB, 300 ue_search_assets rows ≈ 60.7 KB, 250 ue_asset_audit findings ≈ 60.9 KB.
findings.impact: Several documented ranges fail. ue_search_assets accepts limit up to 2000 (schema line 177) and fails from about 300 hits. ue_level_actors accepts up to 5000 (line 185) and fails from about 250. ue_asset_audit caps itself at 400 findings (asset_audit.py:13), yet fails from about 250, i.e. exactly on the projects with the most problems. ue_blueprint_info in folder mode (up to 50 Blueprints with 300 nodes each) and ue_anim_inspect with many samples fail the same way. The agent gets a misleading error plus 60 KB of noise in its context.
findings.fix: Extract the RELAY_JSON line from the raw LogOutput entries before tailing the human-readable output. Also give the scripts a byte budget with an explicit `truncated: true` flag (or write large results to a file under Saved/Relay and return its path), and lower the schema maxima to sizes that fit.

v1.reason: python_tx stores `"output": tail(&output.join("\n"), 2000)` (1707). tail() (1590-1600) keeps the last MAX_OUTPUT = 60_000 bytes, cutting from the front, so a single RELAY_JSON line longer than 60 KB loses its `RELAY_JSON:` prefix. python_json_tx (1721-1730) then fails with 'the editor script printed no result' and puts up to 60 KB of output into the error. Every structured tool emits one line via common.py emit() (`print("RELAY_JSON:" + json.dumps(value))`). ue_search_assets (limit up to 2000), ue_level_actors (up to 5000), ue_asset_audit and ue_blueprint_info folder mode can all produce more than 60 KB.
v1.correction: The most common trigger is missing from the finding. ue_data_table export emits the whole table as a JSON-escaped string in `text` (unreal_py/data_table.py:8), so exporting any Data Table whose CSV/JSON exceeds about 60 KB fails outright. That is ordinary for balancing, loot or dialogue tables, which is the plugin's advertised CSV-first workflow. Fix: find the RELAY_JSON entry in the raw LogOutput entries before tailing the human-readable output. For data_table export, have the script write the file itself (or write to a temp path) instead of round-tripping the text through the log.

findings.title: instructions.md rule 13 tells every Unreal agent to create its own task with task.create, which no default agent role may call
findings.evidence: "If `session.bootstrap` gives you no task, create one for what you were asked to do (`task.create`), move it as you go (`task.move`), link your commits (`task.link_commit`)". The default builder allowlist (handlers/settings.rs:36) is `["task.move", "task.link_commit", "task.changelog.write", "task.update", …]`, with no task.create; reviewer and docs lack it too, and BUS.md:464 agrees. guardrail::authorize refuses ops outside the allowlist (guardrail.rs:358-379). Agents may move only their own task, active→in_review (BUS.md:672). task.link_commit requires the task to be assigned to the session (guardrail.rs:338-347).
findings.impact: Every agent launched without a dispatched task (the common case of a typed prompt) is told by its standing brief to call an op that is not even in its MCP tool list and is refused over the CLI. It wastes turns or raises guardrail.request exceptions to the human for something the default policy never allows. "Move it as you go" also overstates what task.move permits.
findings.fix: Rewrite rule 13 to match what agents can do: report with session.report/session.done, and ask the human (or the dispatching user) for a task. Alternatively add task.create to the builder allowlist deliberately and document that in BUS.md §9.1.

v1.reason: instructions.md:15 (rule 13) says 'If session.bootstrap gives you no task, create one ... (task.create), move it as you go (task.move), link your commits (task.link_commit)'. The default role allowlists in handlers/settings.rs (builder/reviewer/docs) contain no task.create. guardrail::authorize falls through to `BusError::allowlist` for any mutation outside role_allowlist (guardrail.rs:357-384), and a task_id payload must be assigned to the session (guardrail.rs:340-349). BUS.md limits task.move for agents to their own task, active->in_review. Empirically, this agent session's filtered relay MCP tool list has task_move and task_link_commit but no task_create. These instructions go into the brief of every agent in a plugin-enabled project.
v1.correction: Only the guardrail.request route remains for task.create, and it puts a needless prompt in front of the human. Rewrite rule 13 to match what agents can do (report with session.report/done, ask the human for a task), or deliberately add task.create to the builder allowlist and record that in BUS.md §9.1.

findings.title: Plugin skills are copied into the machine-wide ~/.claude/skills (and ~/.codex/skills) when the plugin is on in any project, so every Claude Code session on the machine gets the 20 Unreal skills
findings.evidence: enabled_anywhere() returns `with_plugins(rows, &crate::plugins::enabled_anywhere(conn)?)`, and plan_user writes those rows to `user_bases()` = `vec![home.join(".claude").join("skills"), codex.join("skills")]` (line 196). plan_user runs on every launch (session.rs plan_launch) and on every plugin toggle (refresh_all). Evidence on this machine: ~/.claude/skills/unreal-cpp/.relay-skill contains `plugin unreal-engine 0668aa7957a39104 unreal-cpp`, and this RelayV4 audit session's own skill list includes all unreal-* and blender-* skills, while the checkout's .claude/skills holds only audit and impeccable.
findings.impact: This contradicts plugins.rs:9 ("Nothing is written for a project that has it off"), D159 ("Plugins are off by default … switched on per project") and README.md:12, which says the plugin writes to "the provider homes for Codex" only. Every Claude Code session for this user, in Relay or not and in any project, carries about 18 KB of Unreal/Blender skill descriptions and may auto-load them for unrelated work. Claude agents in the enabled project don't need the user copy; they already get `<checkout>/.claude/skills/`.
findings.fix: Keep plugin skills out of `~/.claude/skills`: materialize them only into checkouts of enabled projects, plus the Codex home if Codex still needs it. Update the README row and the plugins.rs doc comment to say what is written machine-wide.

v1.reason: skills.rs:165-173 enabled_anywhere appends `crate::plugins::enabled_anywhere(conn)` (plugins.rs:193-198, `SELECT DISTINCT plugin_id FROM plugin_projects`), and plan_user (skills.rs:220-224) writes those rows to user_bases() = [~/.claude/skills, $CODEX_HOME/skills] (skills.rs:196). On this machine ~/.claude/skills holds all unreal-* and blender-* folders, and ~/.claude/skills/unreal-cpp/.relay-skill reads `plugin unreal-engine 0668aa7957a39104 unreal-cpp`. This very non-Unreal audit session lists every unreal-*/blender-* skill. The user-scope copy is deliberate for installed skills: the comment at skills.rs:175-178 says Claude's user scope is included 'for the same reach outside Relay's own projects', and plugins.rs:193 labels enabled_anywhere 'what the machine-wide skill folders carry'. For plugins it contradicts plugins.rs:9 ('Nothing is written for a project that has it off'), D159's reason for keeping plugins off by default ('they change how every agent in a project works'), and README.md:12, which promises only 'the provider homes for Codex'. So every Claude Code session on the machine, in any project and outside Relay, gets the Unreal and Blender skills.
v1.correction: The mechanism is intended for installed skills (D147) and only leaks for plugins. Fix it by filtering plugin rows out of the ~/.claude/skills base in plan_user and keeping them for the Codex home, which has no per-checkout lookup. Otherwise, if the machine-wide reach is wanted, correct plugins.rs:9, the README row and D159. Category is bug with a docs-drift aspect.

findings.title: ue_editor_launch looks for bind failures in whatever log sits at Saved/Logs/<Project>.log right after spawning, i.e. the previous session's log, so the documented quit-and-relaunch recovery reports a false bind failure
findings.evidence: Right after `let pid = crate::unreal_process::launch(...)?;`, the loop tries remote (connection refused immediately), then `let lines = log_since(project, 0, None); let bind = bind_failures(&lines); if !bind.is_empty() { bail!("the editor started (pid {pid}) but its web server could not bind port…") }`. There is no check that the file belongs to the new process; UE truncates and rewrites the log only once the new editor's logging starts. editor_status (1654-1657) likewise scans the last 400 KB of the log and gives the bind-failure advice first, even when `editors` is empty. mcp-tools.md:91 promises "failing early on a bind error in the new log".
findings.impact: After a failed bind, the documented recovery is ue_editor_quit then ue_editor_launch (editor-automation SKILL.md:273-276). The old log still holds "HttpListener unable to bind…", so launch bails within milliseconds while the new editor goes on starting normally. The agent is told to run WebControl.StopServer/StartServer by hand, and its lock stays taken. ue_editor_status meanwhile reports "The editor is running but its web server could not bind" when no editor is running.
findings.fix: Record the log's inode, size and mtime before launch, and scan only once the file has been replaced or truncated by the new process; or scan only lines after the new session's log header, timestamped after the spawn. In editor_status, consult bind failures only when an editor process is running and the log is newer than that process's start.

v1.reason: launch_editor (unreal.rs:632-670) spawns the editor through unreal_process::launch (it waits for the port to be free first, then spawns at once). In the first loop iteration, remote() fails within milliseconds with connection refused, then `log_since(project, 0, None)` reads all of Saved/Logs/<Project>.log (log_path at 1309-1310). At that moment the file is still the previous session's log: the new process has not yet rotated it. If that log has an HttpListener bind error, which is exactly the case after the documented bind-failure recovery (quit, wait for the port, ue_editor_launch), bind_failures matches and launch bails, telling the agent to run WebControl.StopServer/StartServer, while the new editor goes on starting normally. The same applies when the old session hit a bind error and crashed. editor_status (1650-1656) also scans the last 400 KB of the log and checks bind failures first, without looking at `editors`, so it reports "The editor is running but its web server could not bind" when no editor runs.
v1.correction: Record the log's size, mtime and inode before the spawn and scan only once the file has been replaced, or only lines from the new session. In editor_status, check bind failures only when an editor process exists and the log is newer than its start. The lock stays held by the launching agent, which is fine for that agent, but its retries will hit the same false bind error until the new log replaces the old one.

findings.title: ue_editor_lock is in the LIVE list, so a lock stored in a file can't be inspected or released while the editor is down or another checkout is open
findings.evidence: `const LIVE: [&str; 16] = [… "ue_editor_lock", …]`, and call() runs `if LIVE.contains(&name) { let project = Project::find()?; guard_project(&project)?; … }` (323-325). guard_project calls editor_project(), which needs a Python round trip to the editor. The handler itself (406-412) only reads or removes Saved/Relay/editor-lock.json.
findings.impact: instructions.md:9 tells agents to run `ue_editor_lock` with `action: release` when their editor work is done. After an editor crash, or when Remote Control or remote Python is off, the holder cannot release and nobody can read the status. Other agents' ue_editor_launch and ue_python calls are refused for up to 15 idle minutes. Agents in a worktree can never see who holds the lock.
findings.fix: Remove "ue_editor_lock" from LIVE. The lock is offline state, so status and release need only Project::find().

v1.reason: unreal.rs:33-35 lists "ue_editor_lock" in LIVE. call() at 323-325 runs Project::find() then guard_project() for every LIVE tool before it dispatches. guard_project (488-501) calls editor_project() (503-515), which makes a python_json round trip to Remote Control, so when the editor is down or Remote Control is unreachable the call fails before the handler at 406-412 runs. That handler only touches Saved/Relay/editor-lock.json through read_lock/release_lock. The bad case: an editor crash while agent A holds the lock. A cannot release it, nobody can read the status, and B's ue_editor_launch, ue_editor_quit or import_fbx (all call acquire_lock) are refused until the 15-minute idle expiry. instructions.md rule 7 tells agents to release when they are done, and that fails exactly when the editor is gone. If the editor has a different checkout open, status and release are refused too.
v1.correction: The finding says agents in a worktree can never see who holds the lock. That is slightly off: lock_path is per checkout (project.root/Saved/Relay), so a worktree agent's lock file is a different file from the main checkout's anyway. The real cost is that status and release fail whenever the editor is unreachable or has another project open. The fix stands: drop ue_editor_lock from LIVE (or skip guard_project for it). Impact is bounded by the 15-minute auto-expiry and by UE_ALLOW_PROJECT_MISMATCH.

findings.title: Plugin MCP tools sit outside Relay's guardrails: ue_data_table export overwrites any project file with no destructive-write hold, despite instructions rule 14
findings.evidence: The only path check is `anyhow::ensure!(!f.contains("..") && !Path::new(f).is_absolute(), …)`, followed by `std::fs::write(file, value["text"]…)` (970). The guardrail hook matchers are `"Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash"` (hooks.rs:350) and `"Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write"` (hooks.rs:517), so `mcp__unreal__*` calls are never gated. ue_setup_check fix also rewrites the .uproject and Config/*.ini (1459, 710, 743). ue_python, ue_console and ue_call run arbitrary code in the editor; an editor the human launched has no RELAY_SESSION, so a `relay` CLI call from it resolves to Actor::User (relay-cli main.rs:122-129). That bypasses the self-approval refusal that guardrail.rs:813-826 applies to Bash.
findings.impact: instructions.md:16 promises "Relay's guardrail holds a write that removes a lot of lines from a file with uncommitted changes", but the plugin's own tools are exempt. Example: the CSV-first workflow keeps Data/Weapons.csv in the repo. A human or agent edits the CSV, then another agent runs `ue_data_table {action:export, file:"Data/Weapons.csv"}` and silently overwrites the uncommitted edits. A mistaken `file` can also overwrite .git/config or a modified source file, and protected_paths never apply.
findings.fix: Route the bridge's own file writes through guardrail.gate kind=write (the session env is available to the MCP server), or at least refuse to overwrite an existing file with uncommitted changes and reject paths under .git/. Document in the plugin docs that ue_python, ue_console and ue_call run outside the guardrails. Consider a PreToolUse matcher for mcp__unreal__ that gates the writing tools.

v1.reason: data_table() (unreal.rs:962-972) checks only `!f.contains("..") && !Path::new(f).is_absolute()` and then calls `std::fs::write(file, value["text"]…)`. Export does not even take the editor lock (call() at 328 counts ue_data_table as writing only for import). The guardrail PreToolUse matchers are `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash` (hooks.rs:350) and `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write` (hooks.rs:517), so the unreal MCP tools are never gated. An export onto an existing CSV with uncommitted edits, or onto a tracked file such as .git/config, therefore overwrites it with no hold, unlike the Write tool. instructions.md rule 14 implies that protection applies.
v1.correction: The security framing is overstated. ue_python, ue_call and ue_console exist to run arbitrary code in the editor, and the user enables this plugin knowingly. Relay's guardrails are also cooperative rather than a sandbox: the self_approval check in evaluate_exec (guardrail.rs:813-826) parses only the Bash command string, so other indirections (python -c, scripts) evade it too. The editor-launched-without-RELAY_SESSION path is not a unique hole. What remains is that a file-writing plugin tool skips the uncommitted-change hold the instructions promise. That is a low-severity data-loss risk in an edge case: the agent asked to export over a file that has uncommitted edits. Fix: in data_table export, refuse to overwrite an existing file that differs from HEAD (or route it through guardrail.gate kind=write), reject paths under .git/, and document in instructions.md that ue_python, ue_call and ue_console sit outside the guardrails.

findings.title: ue_setup_check fix writes Remote Control remote-execution switches into the committed Config/DefaultRemoteControl.ini, turning on an unauthenticated localhost code-execution endpoint for every clone of the project
findings.evidence: `RC_KEYS = [("bAutoStartWebServer","True"),("bEnableRemotePythonExecution","True"),("bAllowConsoleCommandRemoteExecution","True"),("bAllowAnyRemoteFunctionCall","True")]` are merged into `project.root.join("Config/DefaultRemoteControl.ini")` (705-711). Config/ is version-controlled (the plugin's gitignore template ignores only Saved/, Binaries/ etc.). The per-user throttle preference likewise goes into Config/DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini (728). setup.md:52-55 says only "Keep it bound to localhost … do not expose port 30010". editor-automation SKILL.md:26 tells agents to run fix=true on their own.
findings.impact: Once an agent commits its Config changes, as instructions rule 4 encourages, every developer and machine that opens the project starts an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:30010 that runs arbitrary Python and console commands as the editor's user. No passphrase is required for local clients, so any other local user or process on that machine can reach it, Relay installed or not. Epic leaves remote Python execution off by default. The security note does not say the change is repository-wide.
findings.fix: Write the Remote Control switches and the throttle preference to the per-user, uncommitted layer (Saved/Config/<Platform>Editor/RemoteControl.ini and EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini, or Config/User*.ini, ignored by the template). Keep only the plugin entries in the .uproject. Make setup.md say which files change and who is exposed.

v1.reason: write_remote_control_ini (unreal.rs:702-719) merges bEnableRemotePythonExecution, bAllowConsoleCommandRemoteExecution, bAllowAnyRemoteFunctionCall and bAutoStartWebServer into project.root/Config/DefaultRemoteControl.ini. Config/ is version-controlled: the gitignore template ignores /Saved/ and the build dirs, not Config. Once that file is committed, every clone's editor auto-starts an HTTP server on localhost:30010 that runs Python, console commands and any UFUNCTION. Other local users can reach it, since the passphrase is not enforced for localhost clients. The code already knows the per-user layer: launch_editor writes the throttle setting to Saved/Config/<Platform>Editor at 650-656. Even so, setup_check writes both this file and DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini (728) to the committed layer.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low. The server binds localhost only. Exposure needs a shared multi-user machine or an untrusted local process on a teammate's machine. The change is documented: SKILL.md 26 and the advice text both name Config/DefaultRemoteControl.ini, so the human sees the diff. Enabling remote Python is also the plugin's purpose, and launch passes -RCWebControlEnable anyway. Moving these keys to Saved/Config (per user) and saying in setup.md that the Default*.ini change applies to the whole repository is still the right fix.

findings.title: For Codex agents the unreal MCP server is registered without any env, so UE_* settings and RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_WORKTREE probably never reach relay unreal-mcp (setup.md says agents inherit them)
findings.evidence: codex_mcp_config emits only `mcp_servers.{name}.command`, `.args` and an `.env` table built from the manifest's (empty) env (lines 115-124). session.rs:546-548 passes the unreal server this way. setup.md:66: "Agents inherit these from the Relay engine's environment." The bridge reads UE_PROJECT, UE_ROOT, UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_URL, UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_PASSPHRASE, RELAY_SESSION (holder_id, unreal.rs:511) and RELAY_WORKTREE (unreal.rs:1294) from its environment.
findings.impact: If Codex starts stdio MCP servers with a cleared environment plus a small allowlist (Codex has an `env_vars` allowlist option for MCP servers), Codex agents talk to 127.0.0.1:30010 even when UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_URL is set. They also send no passphrase, ignore UE_ROOT/UE_PROJECT, and hold the editor lock as "pid N" rather than their session name (D160 says session name). Not established: whether Codex 0.154 actually clears the MCP server environment. Inspecting the local Codex binary was denied in this session.
findings.fix: Add `--config mcp_servers.<name>.env_vars=["RELAY_SESSION","RELAY_WORKTREE","UE_PROJECT","UE_ROOT","UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_URL","UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_PASSPHRASE"]`, or put the engine's values into `env` explicitly, when registering plugin servers with Codex. Note in setup.md how the variables reach each provider.

v1.reason: providers.rs:104-125: codex_mcp_config emits command, args and `env` only from the manifest's env, which is empty for unreal. It passes no `env_vars` passthrough. The local Codex 0.154 binary (~/.codex/packages/standalone/releases/0.154.0-.../bin/codex) contains the stdio MCP default env allowlist (`LOGNAME SHELL __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING LC_ALL TMPDIR TZ` next to cwd/command) and the `env_vars` config option. That matches codex-rs, which env_clears the MCP child and passes only that allowlist plus the configured env and env_vars. So relay unreal-mcp under Codex does not see RELAY_SESSION, UE_PROJECT, UE_ROOT, UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_URL or UE_REMOTE_CONTROL_PASSPHRASE. holder_id (unreal.rs:510-511) falls back to "pid N" (the session name is what D160 wants). A user-set Remote Control URL or passphrase, or UE_ROOT, is ignored, so live tools or builds fail for Codex agents while Claude agents work. setup.md:66 says agents inherit these variables, which is wrong for Codex.
v1.correction: Evidence comes from strings in the binary, not from running it. RELAY_WORKTREE matters less than claimed: Project::find (unreal.rs:1294-1296) falls back to current_dir, which is the session's cwd. Impact is limited to Codex agents in Unreal projects whose user set UE_* variables, and to lock-holder naming. Fix as proposed: add `mcp_servers.<name>.env_vars=[...]` for RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_WORKTREE and the UE_* variables, or write the values into `env`. Fix setup.md too. This also explains why #1 does not reach Codex-launched editors.

findings.title: Editor lock acquisition is read-check-write on a plain file, so two agents can both believe they hold it
findings.evidence: acquire_lock calls `read_lock(project)` (`std::fs::read_to_string` then `serde_json::from_str(&raw).unwrap_or(Value::Null)`), checks `lock["holder"]`, and later does `std::fs::write(&path, json!({...}))`. There is no create_new, flock or rename. fs::write truncates before writing, so a concurrent reader can see an empty file, parse it as Null, conclude there is no holder, and overwrite the lock.
findings.impact: With the plugin's primary-checkout default, many agents share Saved/Relay/editor-lock.json. Two mutating calls landing together (for example after a broadcast) both pass, and both drive the editor at once: interleaved transactions, or one agent's PIE starting during another's asset script. That is exactly what the docs say cannot happen. The window is small, so it is rare.
findings.fix: Take a fresh lock with OpenOptions::create_new (atomic), refresh it by writing a temp file and renaming it, or hold an flock on the lock file around read-modify-write.

v1.reason: acquire_lock (unreal.rs:535-552) reads with read_lock, which does read_to_string and then serde_json::from_str(...).unwrap_or(Value::Null). It then checks lock["holder"] and writes with std::fs::write. Nothing makes this atomic: no create_new, no flock, no rename. Each agent's MCP server is its own process, so two near-simultaneous mutating calls can both see no holder, or the other's mid-truncate empty file read as Null, and both go ahead. The window is a few milliseconds of file I/O, so it is rare.
v1.correction: Take the lock with create_new, and refresh it by writing a temp file and renaming it over the original, or hold an flock around the read-modify-write. release_lock has the same read-then-remove race.

findings.title: The editor lock lapses mid-operation: it is never refreshed during long calls and ue_build restart_editor gives it up for the whole build
findings.evidence: `acquire_lock(project, &holder_id())?` runs once. The in-editor test loop then polls the log until `secs(args, "timeout_s", 1800)` with no refresh of `last_used`, while `LOCK_IDLE` is 15 minutes (line 40). ue_python accepts timeouts up to 1800 s. quit_editor ends with `let _ = release_lock(project, &holder_id());` (611), so during `ue_build restart_editor` the lock is free for the entire build until launch_editor takes it again (1571-1572).
findings.impact: A test suite or script running longer than 15 minutes looks idle. Another agent takes the lock and starts ue_play or ue_python in the editor where the tests are running, causing spurious test failures and interleaved edits. During a restart build, another agent can launch the editor on half-replaced binaries.
findings.fix: Refresh last_used inside the long waits (in-editor test loop, play loop), or store a `busy_until` timestamp. Keep the lock held across the build in ue_build restart_editor (don't release in quit_editor when called from build).

v1.reason: acquire_lock writes last_used once (550), and nothing refreshes it. run_tests in_editor (1080-1096) acquires once and then polls the log for up to timeout_s (default 1800 s) without touching the lock. read_lock marks the lock expired after LOCK_IDLE = 15 min (40, 525-528), and acquire_lock lets another holder take an expired lock (538). quit_editor ends with `let _ = release_lock(project, &holder_id());` (611). build() calls quit_editor (1519), runs UBT for up to 3600 s, and only then calls launch_editor, which re-acquires (628). During the build the lock file is gone, so another agent's ue_editor_launch can start the editor mid-build. The original launch then just returns already_running (624-626).
v1.correction: The ue_python 1800 s case is weaker than claimed. A long Python call blocks the editor's game thread, so another agent's Remote Control calls stall rather than interleave. The real windows are in-editor automation tests longer than 15 min (tests run across frames, so ue_play or ue_python from another agent can interleave) and the build gap in restart_editor. Fix: refresh last_used in the in-editor test poll loop and the play loop. Give quit_editor a keep_lock flag that build() uses, releasing only after launch or on failure.

findings.title: ue_play skips cleanup on early errors: the RelayPlayCapture actor stays in the level (and ue_play/ue_profile don't stop PIE or restore the throttle) when play start fails
findings.evidence: play() runs `play_step("prepare_outside", …)?` (856), which spawns a tagged SceneCapture2D into the editor level (play.py:89-100). Then `let started = play_step("start", …)?; wait_for_play(true)?;` (862-863) both return early with `?`. `cleanup_outside` (926-928) and the throttle-restoring stop (921-922) are reached only after them. play.py:32-33 raises when a PIE session is already running. profile() has the same pattern (1031-1032).
findings.impact: Calling ue_play with `outside` while a PIE session runs (for example a previous ue_play with stop:false), or when PIE takes more than 30 s to start, leaves a "RelayPlayCapture" actor in folder RelayPreview with the level dirty. The next ue_editor_quit or ue_build restart_editor saves all dirty maps (save_dirty_packages(True, True)), so the stray actor gets saved into the human's map and committed. A timed-out start also leaves PIE running with the throttle setting unrestored. The capture folder under Saved/Relay/Captures is leaked whenever `outcome?` fails (929).
findings.fix: Wrap everything after prepare_outside in a closure and always run cleanup_outside, plus stop/restore_throttle if start was requested, before propagating the error. Do the same for profile().

v1.reason: In play() (crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:852-863), `play_step("prepare_outside", …)?` spawns a SceneCapture2D tagged RelayPlayCapture in folder RelayPreview (unreal_py/play.py:86-100). Then `play_step("start", …)?` and `wait_for_play(true)?` both return early through `?`. The `cleanup_outside` call (926-928) sits after the closure and is never reached on those paths. play.py:32-33 raises "a play session is already running" when PIE is active. That happens if ue_play is called with `outside` and without stop_existing after an earlier ue_play with stop:false. wait_for_play bails after 30 s (801-809). The dispatcher (call(), 319-404) and tool_result (1870ff) do no cleanup on error. quit_editor saves with save_dirty_packages(True, True) (582), so the stray actor can end up saved into the map. profile() has the same shape at 1031-1032: if wait_for_play(true) fails, PIE keeps running and nothing stops it.
v1.correction: The throttle sub-claim is mostly moot. By default `start` persists the throttle off via save_config and reports was_throttled=False (play.py:40-45), so normally there is nothing to restore. The real consequences are a stray capture actor in the level (with an extra save risk on the next quit or restart build) and a PIE session left running after a start timeout. The leaked Saved/Relay/Captures/<uuid> folder on `outcome?` failure (929) is trivial. Fix: run cleanup_outside (and stop, when start succeeded) before propagating any error after prepare_outside, for example with a scope guard. Make profile() stop PIE when wait_for_play fails.

findings.title: ue_build reads `save` and `launch_timeout_s`, which its schema (additionalProperties:false) doesn't expose, so a restart always saves every dirty map, including ones Relay's own preview tools dirtied
findings.evidence: `quit = quit_editor(project, args["save"].as_bool().unwrap_or(true))?;` and `launch_editor(project, &json!({"timeout_s": args["launch_timeout_s"]}))`. The ue_build schema (129-139) lists only target, platform, configuration, timeout_s, restart_editor, allow_editor_open and keep_crash_reporters. Quit saves with `save_dirty_packages(True, True)` (582), maps included. mcp-tools.md:189-191 says ue_anim_preview leaves "the level … marked modified, so do not save it for this"; ue_screenshot and ue_play's outside capture dirty the level too.
findings.impact: The documented C++ loop (`ue_build restart_editor:true`) always saves the human's maps after any preview or screenshot. That produces unintended binary .umap churn on LFS/lockable files that rule 8 says must not be touched casually, and agents cannot opt out. A first launch after the build that needs more than 900 s of shader compilation fails, and the advice to "raise timeout_s" doesn't apply to ue_build.
findings.fix: Add `save` (and `launch_timeout_s`) to the ue_build schema, or delete the dead reads. Consider saving content packages only (maps only when asked), and document the behavior in mcp-tools.md.

v1.reason: build() reads `args["save"]` (1519) and `args["launch_timeout_s"]` (1572). The ue_build schema (129-139) declares neither, and tool() sets `additionalProperties:false` (116), so a schema-following agent never sends them. A restart therefore always quits with save_dirty_packages(True, True) (582, maps included), and the relaunch always uses launch_editor's default 900 s (650). Maps dirtied only by Relay's own preview tools get re-saved. mcp-tools.md:189-191 says the level 'stays marked modified, so do not save it for this'. The result is binary .umap churn the agent cannot opt out of. A first relaunch that needs more than 900 s of shader compilation fails, and ue_build exposes no way to raise that limit.
v1.correction: The ue_build description does say 'Quit a running editor first (saving)', so the save itself is documented. The defect is the unreachable options plus the preview-dirtied maps getting saved. The category is better as bug than dead-code, since the reads are live but can't be reached through the schema. Fix: add `save` and `launch_timeout_s` to the ue_build schema.

findings.title: remote-control-api.md says ue_search_assets maps onto /remote/search/assets and advises retrying with full class paths, but the tool runs editor Python and compares short class names, so that advice returns nothing
findings.evidence: Doc: "Depending on engine version, `ClassNames` may need full class paths (`/Script/Engine.StaticMesh`); if a short name returns nothing, retry with the full path. `ue_search_assets` maps its arguments to this body." Code: `"ue_search_assets" => python_json(&search_assets_script(args), …)` (unreal.rs:367). The script compares `cls.lower() not in classes`, where `cls = str(cls_path.asset_name)` is the short name (1747-1752).
findings.impact: An agent following the doc retries with `/Script/Engine.StaticMesh`, which matches nothing and returns 0 assets. The doc also implies the tool works when remote Python is disabled; it does not, because it needs ExecutePythonCommandEx.
findings.fix: Say that ue_search_assets runs an Asset Registry query in editor Python, takes short class names (StaticMesh, Blueprint, …), and needs remote Python enabled. Drop the full-path advice for the tool.

v1.reason: remote-control-api.md:113-115 says to retry with full class paths and that 'ue_search_assets maps its arguments to this body'. In fact unreal.rs:367 routes ue_search_assets to python_json(search_assets_script). That script (1732-1760) compares `cls.lower() not in classes`, where cls = str(asset_class_path.asset_name), the short name. A full path such as /Script/Engine.StaticMesh can never match, and the tool needs remote Python, not /remote/search/assets.
v1.correction: The tool schema (unreal.rs:175) already gives short-name examples ('StaticMesh, Blueprint, ...'), so an agent is only misled when it follows the reference doc's retry advice. Low is right.

findings.title: mcp-tools.md describes defaults and behaviors the implementation doesn't have (anim_preview isolation, screenshot isolation, which tools take the lock)
findings.evidence: Line 189: "returns images from the chosen views (default `front` and `right`, isolated)", but the code passes `"isolate": args["isolate"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false)` (unreal.rs:1244) and the schema says "default false" (240); `altitude` is undocumented. Line 169: "`isolate` renders only the framed actors on black", but capture.py:106-121 only hides actors within 6x the framing radius (at most 2000), so sky, fog, lights and far geometry still render. Lines 56-59 list the locking tools as ue_python, ue_call, ue_property writes, ue_console, ue_screenshot and ue_anim_preview; MUTATING (unreal.rs:37-38) also includes ue_play, ue_profile, ue_data_table import and ue_blueprint_info compile, and ue_editor_launch, ue_editor_quit and ue_run_tests in_editor lock too. editor-automation SKILL.md:63 says ue_editor_status reports the engine version, but editor_status() drops project_check's `engine` field.
findings.impact: Agents plan around documented behavior. They expect isolated, black-background previews, and they are surprised when ue_play or ue_profile are refused with "being driven by" for a lock the docs never mention.
findings.fix: Update mcp-tools.md: isolate default false, add `altitude` and `coverage`, describe isolation as hiding nearby actors, and list every tool that takes the lock. Either return the engine version from ue_editor_status (project_check.py already reports it) or fix the SKILL table.

v1.reason: mcp-tools.md:189 says anim_preview defaults to 'isolated'. The schema at unreal.rs:240 says 'default false: the preview spawns 500 m above the editor camera', and unreal.rs:1244 does `unwrap_or(false)`. The `altitude` (241) and screenshot `coverage` (198) arguments are not documented. mcp-tools.md:169 says isolate renders 'only the framed actors on black', but capture.py neighbours() hides only actors within 6x the radius, capped at 2000. mcp-tools.md:56-57 lists six locking tools, while MUTATING (unreal.rs:37-38) also has ue_play, ue_profile, ue_data_table and ue_blueprint_info, and acquire_lock is also called at 422, 573, 628 and 1082. editor_status (unreal.rs:1633-1646) returns reachable/url/project/lock/routes/info with no engine-version field, though SKILL.md:63 says it reports one.
v1.correction: The tool's own MCP schema description is correct about the isolate default, so an agent that reads the schema is not misled. That keeps the impact low.

findings.title: unreal-blueprints recipe sets a bool property as "b_enabled"; Unreal Python strips the b prefix, so the call raises
findings.evidence: `cdo.set_editor_property("b_enabled", True)       # C++ bEnabled -> Python b_enabled; verify with dir(cdo)`. The Python name of a bool UPROPERTY bEnabled is `enabled`; the C++ name `bEnabled` is also accepted. The plugin's own editor-automation SKILL.md:85-86 says "`bCastShadow` becomes `cast_shadow`". This was the only error found in the skills' code recipes; every other block in all 20 skills was checked and matches current UE5 APIs.
findings.impact: Agents copy the snippet. set_editor_property fails with a "failed to find property" error, and the comment teaches a wrong naming rule that will be reused for other bool properties.
findings.fix: Use `cdo.set_editor_property("enabled", True)` and fix the comment to "C++ bEnabled -> Python enabled (the b prefix of bools is dropped)".

v1.reason: unreal-blueprints/SKILL.md:192 has `cdo.set_editor_property("b_enabled", True)  # C++ bEnabled -> Python b_enabled`. Unreal's Python name generation (PythonizeName) drops the b prefix of bool properties, so bEnabled becomes `enabled`, as the plugin's own editor-automation SKILL.md:85-86 says (`bCastShadow` becomes `cast_shadow`). `b_enabled` matches neither the Python name nor the C++ name, so set_editor_property raises.
v1.correction: The comment's 'verify with dir(cdo)' hedge lets an agent recover after one failed call, so the impact is low. Use "enabled" and fix the comment.

findings.title: ue_asset_audit's "world textures without mips" check compares the enum's string form and may never fire
findings.evidence: `if str(mips).endswith("NO_MIPMAPS") and "ui" not in path.lower():`, where `mips = t.get_editor_property("mip_gen_settings")`. Elsewhere the script compares enums by value (`comp != unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_NORMALMAP`) or by substring (`"USE_COMPLEX_AS_SIMPLE" in str(…).upper()`).
findings.impact: If Unreal's enum `str()` is the repr-like `<TextureMipGenSettings.TMGS_NO_MIPMAPS: 13>`, the documented check (mcp-tools.md:150, "world textures without mips") never reports anything and the audit passes wrongly. Not established: the exact `str()` format of Unreal Python enums, since no engine was available here.
findings.fix: Compare by value: `if mips == unreal.TextureMipGenSettings.TMGS_NO_MIPMAPS and …`.

v1.reason: asset_audit.py:63: `if str(mips).endswith("NO_MIPMAPS")`, where mips is the enum from get_editor_property("mip_gen_settings"). Unreal's Python enum wrapper commonly prints as `<TextureMipGenSettings.TMGS_NO_MIPMAPS: 13>`. With that form, endswith never matches and the documented "world textures without mips" check is dead. The script itself compares enums by value at line 57 and by case-insensitive substring at line 96, which suggests the author was unsure of the string form. No Unreal source or Python stub is available locally, so I could not confirm str() as opposed to repr() output.
v1.correction: Compare by value: `mips == unreal.TextureMipGenSettings.TMGS_NO_MIPMAPS`. At minimum, use a substring test as line 96 does. Even if the check is broken, the impact is one advisory audit line that never appears.

results.coverage:
Read every line of the 5 assigned files, all 6 SKILL.md files, all 9 reference recipe files, crates/relay-cli/src/blender.rs, crates/relay-core/src/plugins.rs, crates/relay-core/build.rs and all of crates/relay-cli/src/blender_py/*.py (including tests/make_fixture.py). For tracing behaviour I read only the relevant parts of: unreal.rs (import_fbx, script, tool_result, acquire_lock), unreal_py/import_fbx.py (options, measure, fix_sockets), hooks.rs (install_claude matchers), guardrail.rs (exec gate, role allowlist), handlers/session.rs (plan_launch) and DECISIONS D5/D22/D23/D132/D159-D162.

Verified with the installed Blender 5.2.1 LTS, scratchpad only:
- Ran every ```python block of all 9 recipe files in documented order; a small prelude added the objects and actions the recipes assume (Hero, Partner, Cup, twist bones, A_Hero_* actions).
- Ran the real tool scripts (info, rig_check, anim_inspect, export, render with every engine/colour/view, mesh_check, run) on the repo's fixture.
- Ran variants for each behavioural finding: slot reuse, contact window, sunk feet, excluded collection, posed export, .blend1, add-on typo, failure output.
- The materials-baking bake recipes and the blender-to-unreal prep recipes run clean on 5.2.1. The only prep failure is the placeholder path `//../base/SK_Base.blend`.

Frontmatter of all six skills is valid: single-line name and description, no ': ' or ' #' in values, every description under 1024 characters, every name equal to its folder.

Not verifiable here:
- Blender 4.x behaviour. The EEVEE id finding rests on the skill's own note and the known 4.2 rename.
- Anything needing a running Unreal editor.
- The claim that `cargo test` fails locally is inferred from the code path; cargo was not run.

Considered and not reported separately: plugin MCP tools bypassing guardrail.gate. Bash already permits arbitrary interpreters, and D5/D132 make the git pre-commit gate the write boundary, so it is only noted in the path-containment finding. Clippy pedantic output for blender.rs and plugins.rs has nothing material; the only cast is a skill's file count.

findings.title: Blender 5.x: blender_info and skeletal/animation exports crash on the removed Action.fcurves
findings.symbol: info.py actions loop; export.py control-bone warning
findings.evidence: info.py:45-46 run `set(fc.data_path.split('"')[1] for fc in a.fcurves ...)` and `len(a.fcurves)` for every action in the file. export.py:48 runs `keyed = set(... for fc in act.fcurves ...)` whenever the armature has an action assigned and kind != static. Blender 5.0 removed Action.fcurves (slotted actions); blender-animation/SKILL.md:44-45 says so itself. Verified on the installed Blender 5.2.1 LTS: the real info.py and export.py, run the way `run()` runs them on the repo's own fixture (blender_py/tests/make_fixture.py), both exit with `AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves'`. setup.md:3 says '4.0 or newer; LTS releases are the safest', but the current LTS is 5.2. Every recipe file says it was verified on 4.0.2 only. The real-Blender test the_blender_tools_work_on_a_real_rig (blender.rs:539) unwraps PY_INFO on that fixture. It is skipped in CI (no Blender), and here, with 5.2.1 on PATH (~/.local/bin/blender), it would fail.
findings.impact: On the current Blender release, `blender_info {file}` fails on any file that holds an action, i.e. every animated character; it is step 1 of every task in instructions.md. Every `kind: "animation"` export fails. Every skeletal `blender_export` or `blender_to_unreal` of a rig with an assigned action fails. `cargo test` fails on any dev machine with Blender 5.x on PATH (inferred from the code path; cargo not run).
findings.fix: Add an `action_fcurves(action)` helper to common.py that reads through slots with `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot(action, slot)` (present in 5.2.1) for each slot, falling back to `action.fcurves` when `hasattr(action, 'fcurves')` (4.0-4.3). Use it in info.py and export.py. State the tested Blender range in setup.md, add 5.x to the fundamentals version notes, and have the real-Blender test print the Blender version (ideally run it in one CI job with a pinned Blender).

v1.reason: info.py:44-46 iterates every action in bpy.data.actions and reads `a.fcurves` (both in the set comprehension and in `len(a.fcurves)`), so any .blend that holds an action fails, whether or not it is assigned. export.py:45-48 reads `act.fcurves` whenever the armature has an assigned action and kind != static. I ran the installed ~/.local/bin/blender with --factory-startup in the scratchpad: it reports `5.2.1 LTS` and `hasattr(bpy.data.actions.new('X'), 'fcurves')` is False. So both lines raise AttributeError on the current Blender. The fixture (tests/make_fixture.py:105-108) creates and assigns a 'Swing' action, so blender.rs `the_blender_tools_work_on_a_real_rig` unwraps PY_INFO and would fail on this machine. It is skipped only where Blender is missing. setup.md:3 says '4.0 or newer' with no upper bound, and blender-animation/SKILL.md:44-45 already says the legacy view is removed in 5.0.
v1.correction: Did not run cargo; the failing test is inferred from the code path plus the confirmed missing attribute. Many skill recipe files also use act.fcurves (animation-recipes.md:13,26,72,82,109; rig-recipes.md:83; rigging-recipes.md:212; rigify-game-skeleton.md:131), so agents following them on 5.x hit the same error. Those should be updated alongside the helper.

v2.reason:
(a) I reproduced it myself in the scratchpad with the installed Blender (~/.local/bin/blender, which points to blender-5.2.1-linux-x64 and reports "5.2.1 LTS"). I built the repo's fixture (make_fixture.py works on 5.2.1). Then I ran common.py plus each tool script exactly as run() does (blender.rs:330-350: `-b file --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python job.py -- args.json`). info.py stops at line 45 with `AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves'`, exit 1 and no RELAY_JSON, so run() bails with "Blender failed:". export.py stops the same way at line 48 in three cases: a skeletal export with action=Swing, a skeletal export with no action argument (the fixture has Swing assigned), and kind=animation. A static export succeeds. rig_check and anim_inspect pass the test's assertions on 5.2.1, so the fcurves reads are the only blocker in those steps. common.py has no shim, and no try/except or fallback exists anywhere in the call chain.

(b) Who hits it: any agent in a project with the Blender plugin on (it is opt-in per project) whose machine has Blender 5.x. find_blender() takes the first `blender` on PATH. This Relay-launched session resolves ~/.local/bin/blender, so this user's agents get 5.2.1. The trigger is deterministic. blender_info fails on every .blend that holds any Action, because info.py loops over all of bpy.data.actions, fake-user and orphan actions included. instructions.md step 1 sends agents to blender_info first. blender_export and blender_to_unreal fail for every skeletal or animation export of a rig that has an action assigned or passed in. The user's own Codex memories show exactly this workflow on Blender 5.2.1: an animated greatsword/arms rig exported as FBX clips (Idle, Light1-3, Heavy, Guard) to Unreal.

(c) The tool returns an error with the traceback. No data is lost: the .blend is not saved, and the script fails before the FBX is written or Unreal is reached. The documented pipeline is unusable for animated assets, though, and an agent falling back to blender_python with the skill recipes hits the same error. Those recipes use act.fcurves too. On a dev machine with Blender 5.x on PATH, the relay-cli test the_blender_tools_work_on_a_real_rig (not #[ignore]; relay-cli is a default member) would panic at blender.rs:539 on `.unwrap()`. I inferred that from the identical script run; I did not run cargo. CI skips the test because no workflow installs Blender.

(d) High is right. This is a deterministic hard failure of the plugin's main flow on the current Blender release line and on the user's installed version. It is not critical: the plugin is opt-in, the error is loud, nothing is corrupted, and a hand-written script is a workaround.

(e) The fix works. With an `action_fcurves()` helper added to common.py in a scratch copy, info.py on 5.2.1 reports Swing with fcurves=3, bones_animated=1 and frame_range [1, 20]. The skeletal and animation exports of the fixture then succeed (FBX written, no warnings).
v2.correction:
"Every kind: animation export fails" overstates it slightly. The failure happens only when an action is assigned or passed as `action`. An animation export with all_actions and nothing assigned skips export.py:46-48. That is the rare case, so the severity stands.

Fix details:
1. Branch on `hasattr(action, "slots")` (or "layers"), not on fcurves. Use the channelbag path on 4.4+ and `action.fcurves` on 4.0-4.3.
2. In export.py, pass the armature's own slot: `action_get_channelbag_for_slot(act, arm.animation_data.action_slot)`, falling back to all slots when the slot is None. One slotted action can animate several IDs, so a union of all slots mixes in another character's keyed bones. I tested this variant on 5.2.1 and it exports cleanly.
3. If there is any doubt that bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot exists on 4.4, walk `action.layers[*].strips[*].channelbags[*].fcurves` directly instead.

Add to related, beyond the first verifier's list:
- plugins/blender/skills/blender-animation/SKILL.md:59, which recommends `act.fcurves.new(...)` for bulk keys
- animation-recipes.md:182, which uses `act.fcurves.remove`

Separately, and not verified here: render.py:35 maps eevee to "BLENDER_EEVEE". The fundamentals skill itself says 4.2 uses BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT, so any "tested Blender range" statement in setup.md should account for that as well.

findings.title: set_action assigns an action without a slot, so on Blender 4.4+ anim_inspect, render and export silently use the rest pose
findings.evidence: `set_action` only does `arm.animation_data.action = action` (common.py:124-126). Since 4.4 an action animates nothing unless `animation_data.action_slot` is set, and Blender auto-picks only a slot matching the ID or its last-used slot. Verified on 5.2.1 with the fixture: assigning 'Swing' (keyed on Hero) to Partner left `action_slot = None`. The real anim_inspect.py run with `{armature: 'Partner', action: 'Swing', samples: 3, track: ['upper_arm.R:tail']}` returned `action: 'Swing'`, `passed: true` and identical positions [0.0, 45.0, 135.0] at frames 1, 10 and 20. blender-animation/SKILL.md:44-48 tells agents to check `obj.animation_data.action_slot` after assigning by code; the tools never do.
findings.impact: Any action keyed on a different object than the one being checked, rendered or exported produces silent wrong results. Examples: a second character sharing the skeleton, an FBX-imported or mocap clip, a re-imported rig. blender_anim_inspect, the plugin's 'must pass' gate, passes on the rest pose. blender_render returns rest-pose images labelled with the requested frames. blender_export with `action` writes a frozen take (4.4/4.5).
findings.fix: After assigning, if `ad.action_slot is None` and the action has slots, assign `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_first_suitable_slot(action, 'OBJECT')` (or the only OBJECT slot). Otherwise raise 'action X has no slot usable by Y'. Return the slot used in each tool's result.

v1.reason: common.py:118-127 `set_action` only does `arm.animation_data.action = action`. I reproduced this on the installed Blender 5.2.1 (scratchpad experiment). An action keyed on object 'Hero' has slot 'OBHero'. Assigning it to object 'Partner' leaves `animation_data.action_slot` as None, and at frame 20 Partner's keyed channel still reads the rest value. Blender auto-assigns a slot only by last-used identifier, by matching ID name, or for a single slot with no ID type. anim_inspect (lines 9, 19), render.py:20 and export.py:32 all go through set_action and never check the slot. anim_inspect also reports `action: <name>` (line 175), so the result looks valid while it measures the rest pose. Nothing in the repo reads `action_slot` except the SKILL note.
v1.correction: Downgraded from high. The trigger is an action authored on a different object than the one inspected, rendered or exported. Examples are a clip shared between characters, or a clip imported or keyed on another rig. The skill's own workflow gives each character its own actions (SKILL.md:42-43, section 6), so this is a less common path, not the normal flow. When it does happen it is silent. Fix as proposed: after assignment, if `action_slot is None`, pick a suitable slot via `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_first_suitable_slot` (4.4+). Otherwise raise a clear error. Report the slot in the results.

findings.title: blender-animation recipes: 7 of 11 snippets fail on Blender 5.x (Action.fcurves, Bone.select)
findings.evidence: Ran every block in order on 5.2.1, on the fixture rig plus the actions the recipes expect. These raise `AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves'`: recipe 1 (`act.fcurves` at :13 and :26); recipe 2 at `len(act.fcurves)` (:72), after the keys were inserted; recipe 3 `set_keys` (`act.fcurves.find/new`, :82-83); recipe 4 (`for fc in act.fcurves`, :109); recipe 5 (via set_keys at :150; the in-place advice `act.fcurves.remove` at :182). Recipe 6 raises `'Bone' object has no attribute 'select'` at `b.select = ...` on `arm.data.bones` (:196): 5.x moved selection to PoseBone.select, and the same nla.bake call works on 5.2.1 with `pb.select`. SKILL.md:59-60 teaches `act.fcurves.new(...)`. SKILL.md:44-46 notes the 5.0 removal, yet every recipe still uses the removed API.
findings.impact: On the installed Blender, every recipe for writing many keys, loops, root motion and the IK/constraint bake raises. Recipe 6 is the bake that the animation skill (section 9), the rigging skill (section 7) and the Rigify guide all point to. Agents fall back to inventing API calls, which the skills tell them not to do.
findings.fix: Add a channelbag helper: `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(act, slot)` / `action_get_channelbag_for_slot`, falling back to `act.fcurves` before 4.4. Use `cb.fcurves` in recipes 1-5. In recipe 6, select with `arm.pose.bones[n].select` on 5.x and `data.bones[n].select` on 4.x. Re-run the file on 5.x and state which versions it was verified on.

v1.reason: animation-recipes.md:1 is headed 'verified in Blender 4.0 background mode', and recipes 1-5 use `act.fcurves` (lines 13, 26, 72, 82-83, 109, 182). The installed Blender is 5.2.1 (~/.local/bin/blender -> blender-5.2.1). Its own bundled code (rigify utils/animation.py, action_layers.py) reaches F-curves only through `channelbag.fcurves`, and bpy_extras.anim_utils provides action_get/ensure_channelbag_for_slot, consistent with the legacy Action.fcurves being removed in 5.0. SKILL.md:44-46 even says it is removed in 5.0, yet SKILL.md:59 and the recipes still teach it. Recipe 6 (:196) sets `b.select` on `arm.data.bones`. Bundled 5.2 scripts select only pose bones (bone_selection_sets.py:250) or edit bones and never set Bone.select, which supports the claim that it moved to PoseBone.
v1.correction: Downgraded from high to medium and recategorised as docs-drift. These are agent-facing reference snippets, and they fail loudly with an AttributeError, not silently. SKILL.md:44-48 already warns about the 5.0 removal and tells agents to check with dir(), so an agent can recover, at the cost of wasted turns and improvised API calls. I could not run Blender to reproduce the Bone.select failure myself. The evidence for that half is the bundled scripts plus the auditor's run. The suggested fix (a channelbag helper with a pre-4.4 fallback, PoseBone.select on 5.x, and a corrected 'verified on' header) is right.

findings.title: Concurrent blender_python saves to one .blend silently lose work when agents share the checkout
findings.evidence: Each call loads the file, runs the code, then calls `bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()` or `save_as_mainfile(...)` (run.py:12-21). Nothing in blender.rs or blender_py takes a lock or lease or checks whether the file changed since load (the only `lock` is stdin.lock). With the Unreal Engine plugin on (`"default_checkout": "primary"`, plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18, D160), every agent of the project works in the same checkout, and the Blender plugin is built to pair with it (blender_to_unreal). The skills keep a character's rig and all its actions in one .blend, so a rigging agent and an animation agent naturally edit the same file. The Unreal bridge added an editor lease for this shared-checkout case (unreal.rs:535 acquire_lock); the Blender server has none. Overlap detection is claims plus file collisions between checkouts. The agent-facing instructions.md never asks agents to claim a .blend; only setup.md:20 tells the human 'do not let two agents edit the same file'.
findings.impact: Agent A and agent B both load Hero.blend; A saves a rig fix, then B saves a new action. A's work is overwritten and neither agent is told. The exposure window is the whole call, which can be minutes for a bake.
findings.fix: In blender.rs, take an exclusive lock file (`<file>.relay-lock`, flock or create_new) from load to save for calls with `save` or a `save_as` target. Refuse `save` when the file's mtime or size changed since load. In instructions.md, ask agents to session.claim a .blend before editing it.

v1.reason: In blender.rs:197-206, blender_python resolves the file and runs one Blender process that loads it, executes the code, and saves at the end (run.py:12-21). There is no lock or lease, and no mtime or size check between load and save. D160 (DECISIONS.md:930-938) confirms that with the Unreal plugin on (`default_checkout: "primary"`) every new session uses the primary checkout, and that only the Unreal live tools got a lease file. The Blender server got nothing comparable. So two agents in that shared checkout running blender_python with `save` on the same .blend is a last-writer-wins lost update, the whole call is the window, and neither agent is told. Worktree-based overlap and collision detection cannot see it because both writes land in one checkout.
v1.correction: Downgraded from high to medium. The trigger needs the Unreal plugin on as well, two agents working on the same .blend at the same time, and both saving over it. setup.md:20 tells the human not to let two agents edit the same file. The lost work is an agent's edit that can be redone, not user-authored data being destroyed. The fix proposed in the finding is reasonable: create an exclusive lock file with `create_new` around load-to-save for `save`/`save_as`, and refuse the save when the file's mtime changed since load.

findings.title: anim_inspect: a 'touch' contact suppresses partner clipping at every frame, ignoring its window
findings.evidence: `intended = any(c.get('expect', 'touch') == 'touch' and name in (c['a'], c['b']) for c in ARGS.get('contacts', []))` is followed by `if best[0] < radius and not intended: problem(...)` (153-155). Neither `window` nor the partner bone is consulted, and matching is by exact probe name. So 'hand.R' suppresses clipping at every frame, while the documented form 'hand.R:tail' (blender-animation/SKILL.md:132) never matches a probe, because probes are bone heads (144-145). Verified on 5.2.1 with a partner segment in the fixture's swing path. With no contacts: `partner_clipping` at frame 20, passed false. With `{a: 'hand.R', b: 'partner:head', expect: 'touch', window: [1, 1]}` added: no problems, passed true.
findings.impact: A hand passing through the partner outside the planned contact frame passes the check. That contradicts the skill's rule 'Any partner_clipping outside a contact is a real problem' (SKILL.md:138-139), so paired moves ship with interpenetration.
findings.fix: Suppress only when the frame is inside that contact's window and the nearest partner segment is the contact's partner bone. Normalise 'bone' and 'bone:tail' references, or add hand and foot tails as probes.

v1.reason: anim_inspect.py:153 computes `intended = any(c.get('expect','touch') == 'touch' and name in (c['a'], c['b']) for c in ARGS.get('contacts', []))` for each probe and suppresses `partner_clipping` at line 154 whenever it is true. `c['window']` is used only for the contact distance check (line 138) and never here, and the partner segment (`best[1]`) is not compared with the contact's other end. Probe names are bare deform bone names whose head is the measured point (lines 144-145: `head(arm, n)`), plus `item:<n>:<end>`. A contact written as `a: 'hand.R'` (or `item:sword:end_a`) therefore exempts that probe from partner clipping at every sampled frame. The `bone:tail` form shown in SKILL.md:130-131 never equals a probe name, so it never suppresses anything. That direction is safe but inconsistent. The skill's rule at SKILL.md:138-139 ('Any partner_clipping outside a contact is a real problem') is not what the code enforces.
v1.correction: The false pass needs a contact whose a or b is a bare probe name or an item reference. The documented `hand.R:tail` form gives the opposite symptom: a wrist near the partner is flagged even inside the contact window. Fix: suppress only when `f` is inside that contact's window and the nearest partner segment is the bone named by the contact's partner reference. Map `bone:tail` references to the bone, or probe tails as well.

findings.title: anim_inspect 'ground' check measures the ankle, so a foot can sink about 10 cm before it fails
findings.evidence: `feet = [b.name for b in arm.data.bones if 'foot' in b.name.lower() and b.use_deform]` (101). `heights = dict((n, round((head(arm, n).z - ground) * TO_CM, 1)) for n in feet)` and `if min(heights.values()) < -2.0` (157-160). `head()` is the foot bone's head (the ankle), while `ground` is the lowest rest-pose bone point (the toes). Verified on 5.2.1: keying the fixture's root 9 cm down puts the toes at -9.0 cm, yet anim_inspect reports feet_height -1.0 and passed true. The docs promise a `ground` problem 'when a foot is more than 2 cm below the rest-pose ground' (blender-animation/SKILL.md:161-163).
findings.impact: Feet sinking through the floor by up to the ankle height (8 cm on the fixture) plus 2 cm still pass, although agents rely on this check passing for foot contact.
findings.fix: Measure the lowest point of each foot chain (minimum z of the foot bone's head and tail and its descendants' tails, e.g. ball or toe) and compare it with that chain's rest-pose minimum or with `ground`.

v1.reason: `ground = frame['center'].z` (anim_inspect.py:102). body_frame (common.py:79-85) sets this to the minimum z over all rest-pose bone heads and tails, which is normally a toe or foot tail. The per-foot height at line 157 is `head(arm, n).z - ground`, which measures the foot bone's head (the ankle). At rest this already reads about +ankle-height: in the fixture, foot.L has head z 0.08 and tail z 0.0 (make_fixture.py:24), so it reads +8 cm. The `< -2.0` test at line 159 only fires once the ankle is 2 cm below the toe level, so the toes can sink about 10 cm before a `ground` problem appears. This contradicts SKILL.md:161-163 ('more than 2 cm below the rest-pose ground').
v1.correction: Compare like with like. Either measure each foot chain's lowest point (min z of foot head/tail and descendant tails) against `ground`, or compare the foot head against its own rest-pose head height.

findings.title: blender-rigging recipes: pick-up/drop and the Rigify bake fail on Blender 5.x (Action.fcurves)
findings.evidence: Recipe 8 sets the switch keys to CONSTANT with `for k in (k for fc in cup.animation_data.action.fcurves for k in fc.keyframe_points)` (:212). rigify-game-skeleton.md section 3 ends with `print(baked.name, ..., len(baked.fcurves))` (:131). On 5.2.1 both raise `AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves'`: recipe 8 after its keys were inserted, the Rigify block after nla.bake produced the 74-bone export skeleton's action. Every other rigging and Rigify block ran on 5.2.1 (Rigify generate gave 706 bones; the export skeleton had 74 bones and one root).
findings.impact: The 'verified' pick-up/drop recipe cannot run as written; dropping the failing line leaves Bezier-blended Child Of influence, though the recipe says switches must step. The bake block's exception discards the bake, because blender_python saves nothing when code raises.
findings.fix: Iterate the channelbag F-curves (the same helper as the animation finding) and print `len(cb.fcurves)`.

v1.reason: rigging-recipes.md:212 iterates `cup.animation_data.action.fcurves`, and rigify-game-skeleton.md:131 prints `len(baked.fcurves)` after nla.bake. Both recipe files are headed 'verified in Blender 4.0'. Action.fcurves was removed in 5.0, per the repo's own blender-animation/SKILL.md:44-45 and the 5.2 bundled scripts, which use only the channelbag helpers. The installed Blender is 5.2.1, so both blocks raise. For the Rigify block the exception comes after the bake, and blender_python saves nothing when the code raises (fundamentals SKILL.md:39), so a potentially long bake is thrown away because of a print line. If an agent deletes the failing line in recipe 8, the Child Of influence keys stay Bezier and blend instead of stepping.
v1.correction: Same root cause as #8(a) and the animation recipes (animation-recipes.md:13, 26, 72, 82-83, 109, which the fix references). The engine's own blender_py/info.py:45-46 and export.py:48 also use Action.fcurves and would break blender_info and blender_export on 5.x. Fix them all with one channelbag helper based on bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot, falling back to action.fcurves on versions before 4.4.

findings.title: blender-fundamentals rig recipes: armature-scale fix fails on 5.x and the influence-limit fix silently does nothing
findings.symbol: Apply an armature's scale / Python for blender_rig_check's fixes
findings.evidence: (a) 'Apply an armature's scale, with its animation' rescales location keys with `for fc in act.fcurves:` (:83). On 5.2.1 this raises AttributeError after `transform_apply` has already run. It is the fix the troubleshooting table prescribes for `root_bone_scale` not 1 and 'animations move it 100x too far' (blender-to-unreal/reference/troubleshooting.md:15, :17; SKILL.md:165-166). (b) 'Python for blender_rig_check's fixes' calls `vertex_group_limit_total` and `vertex_group_normalize_all` inside `temp_override(object=body, active_object=body)` without selecting the mesh (:98-101). The rigging skill says these operators act only on objects selected in the view layer (blender-rigging/SKILL.md:161-164). Verified on 5.2.1 with an unselected mesh carrying 10 influences: the operator returned `{'FINISHED'}` and 10 influences remained. The doc's one-session verification passed only because the previous block had selected the mesh.
findings.impact: The documented fix for the most common skeletal import problem raises on the current Blender. The influence-limit fix reports success and changes nothing whenever the body isn't already selected (selection is restored from the file), so the agent reports a fix that never happened.
findings.fix: (a) Use the channelbag helper. (b) Run `for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects: o.select_set(o == body)` before the operators, as rigging recipe 6 does, then print the maximum influence count.

v1.reason: (a) rig-recipes.md:83 has `for fc in act.fcurves:` after `transform_apply` (:79-80). The installed Blender is ~/.local/bin/blender -> blender-5.2.1. The repo's own blender-animation/SKILL.md:44-45 says `action.fcurves` "is removed in 5.0", and none of the bundled 5.2 scripts use action.fcurves; they go through bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot. So on the installed Blender the block raises AttributeError. Because blender_python saves nothing when the code raises, the scale apply is thrown away rather than half-applied. The fix still fails loudly every time, and troubleshooting.md:15 and :17 send users to it. The recipe file header says it was verified on Blender 4.0.2, not 5.x. (b) rig-recipes.md:98-100 calls vertex_group_limit_total and normalize_all under temp_override(object=body, active_object=body) and never selects the mesh. The repo's own blender-rigging/SKILL.md:161-164 and rigging-recipes.md recipe 6 say these operators act only on objects selected in the view layer, return FINISHED and change nothing otherwise. The recipe only worked in its verification run because the earlier skinning block (:62-64) had left body selected. Run against a saved file whose selection differs, it silently does nothing.
v1.correction: Same root cause, more serious location: the engine's own scripts also use the removed API, at crates/relay-cli/src/blender_py/info.py:45-46 (`a.fcurves`, which runs for every action in blender_info) and export.py:48 (`act.fcurves`, on every skeletal or animation export with an action). There is no compatibility shim in common.py. On 5.2.1, blender_info and blender_export would therefore raise on any file that has actions. That is probably more severe than the recipe and should be tracked with the channelbag fix, if the animation finding did not already cover it. Re-running blender_rig_check would show the leftover influences in (b), so it can be caught, but the recipe should select the mesh and print the max influence count as proposed.

findings.title: blender-modeling: the geometry-nodes input idiom mod[socket.identifier] = value raises on Blender 5.x
findings.evidence: The recipe sets `gm[dens.identifier] = 40.0` (:293), and SKILL.md:203 teaches 'Set a modifier input via `mod[socket.identifier] = value`'. On 5.2.1 this raises `TypeError: bpy_struct[key] = val: id properties not supported for this type`. On 5.2.1 the modifier exposes inputs as `mod.properties.inputs.<identifier>.value`, and `getattr(gm.properties.inputs, dens.identifier).value = 40.0` works. Every other modeling recipe ran on 5.2.1.
findings.impact: Every geometry-nodes modifier set up the way the skill teaches fails when its parameters are set, on the installed Blender.
findings.fix: Branch on the API: `if hasattr(gm, 'properties'): getattr(gm.properties.inputs, ident).value = v`, else `gm[ident] = v`. Update SKILL.md:203 to match.

v1.reason: modeling-recipes.md:293 does `gm[dens.identifier] = 40.0`, and SKILL.md:203 teaches `mod[socket.identifier] = value` as the general idiom. The installed Blender is 5.2.1. Its own bundled scripts set geometry-nodes modifier inputs only through `modifier.properties.inputs.<identifier>` (startup/bl_operators/geometry_nodes.py:172, object_quick_effects.py:184-198), which confirms the 5.x API change. The recipe header says it was verified on Blender 4.0.2, so it was never run on the installed version. I did not run Blender to reproduce the TypeError myself; I am relying on the auditor's run plus the bundled code showing the new access path.
v1.correction: Fix as proposed: use `getattr(gm.properties.inputs, ident).value = v` when `hasattr(gm, 'properties')`, otherwise the 4.x item assignment. Update SKILL.md:203 to match. The failure is loud (an exception, nothing saved), so the agent sees it; it does not corrupt anything.

findings.title: Modeling and fundamentals skills predate blender_mesh_check and point mesh checks at blender_rig_check
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:234 says '`blender_rig_check` also works as a mesh check (inside-out, loose, zero-area, missing UVs)'. SKILL.md:154-155 says it 'flags loose verts, zero-area faces and inside-out closed meshes on any mesh'. In fact rig_check.py raises 'no armature in the file' when there is none (16-18) and inspects only meshes skinned to the armature (61-66). Verification step 3 (:231) uses the recipe `mesh_report`, which reads `obj.data` without modifiers (modeling-recipes.md:92), so it misses the bevel-collapse case the tool exists for. `blender_mesh_check`, which checks the evaluated mesh and is also run by export, was added in b3ea46d. That commit updated the README, mcp-tools, instructions and the animation and to-unreal skills, but not modeling or fundamentals, whose 'The tools, in order' list (SKILL.md:33-55) never mentions it.
findings.impact: A modeling agent following its own skill gets an error for every static prop, or checks only the unevaluated base mesh. It learns about modifier-induced degenerate faces only when the export refuses.
findings.fix: Point both places at `blender_mesh_check {file, objects}` and add it to the fundamentals tool list. Keep the recipe mesh_report for ad-hoc use, changed to evaluate modifiers.

v1.reason: blender-modeling/SKILL.md:154-155 says blender_rig_check 'also flags loose verts, zero-area faces and inside-out closed meshes on any mesh', and :234 says it 'also works as a mesh check'.
