But rig_check.py:16-18 raises 'no armature in the file' when there is none, and :61-66 only looks at meshes skinned to the armature. Verification step 3 (:231) uses the recipe mesh_report, which builds bmesh from obj.data (modeling-recipes.md:92), so it never sees modifier output. blender_mesh_check (mesh_check.py, added in b3ea46d) checks the evaluated mesh. The modeling skill never mentions it, nor does the fundamentals 'The tools, in order' list (SKILL.md:33-55). Only blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:202 does.
v1.correction: Lowered to low. blender_export runs the same evaluated-mesh check itself and refuses broken meshes (export.py), so nothing broken ships. The cost is a confusing error, or a check that misses modifier-induced faces until export time. fundamentals/SKILL.md:51 ('rig_check for any rig or skinned mesh') is accurate. Its only fault is that it leaves out mesh_check.

findings.title: blender_render ignores `action` unless an armature is listed in `objects`
findings.evidence: `arm = next((o for o in targets if o.type == 'ARMATURE'), None)`, then `if arm is not None: set_action(arm, ARGS.get('action'))` (18-20). With `objects: [<mesh>]` the action is never applied, yet rigify-game-skeleton.md:158 tells agents to call `blender_render {objects: [<mesh>], action: 'A_Hero_Wave', frames: [...]}`. With `objects` omitted, the action and the camera facing go to whichever armature comes first in `scene.objects`, which can be the partner in a two-character file. The result does not say which armature or action was posed.
findings.impact: Agents 'look at' key frames of an action that was never applied (they see the assigned action or the rest pose), during the visual check the skills require before calling animation done.
findings.fix: Find the armature from the listed meshes (Armature modifier object or parent). Require an `armature` argument when several exist, and raise if `action` is given but no armature is found. Return the armature and action used.

v1.reason: render.py:18-20 looks for the armature only in `targets`, the objects named in `objects`: `arm = next((o for o in targets if o.type == 'ARMATURE'), None)`, then `if arm is not None: set_action(...)`. When `objects: [<mesh>]` is passed, `action` is silently ignored, and the result does not report this. Yet rigify-game-skeleton.md:158 prescribes exactly `blender_render {objects: [<mesh>], action: ..., frames: [...]}`. With `objects` omitted, names are all visible MESH/ARMATURE objects in scene order, and the action plus body_frame facing go to the first armature found. In a two-character file, like the repo's own fixture with a partner rig, that can be the wrong one. The rendered key frames then show the assigned action or the rest pose instead of the requested one, during the visual check the skills require.
v1.correction: Resolve the armature from the listed meshes (an Armature modifier's object, or the parent). Raise if `action` is given and none, or more than one, is found. Return the armature and action that were used.

findings.title: blender_to_unreal never imports materials or textures by default, contrary to its docs
findings.evidence: `to_unreal` builds import_args with `"materials": args["materials"]` (404-407). When the caller omits it this is JSON null, and `script()` serialises it into ARGS (unreal.rs:466-467). import_fbx.py:30-31 then does `bool(ARGS.get('materials', kind != 'animation'))`; `.get` returns None for a key that is present with a null value, so import_materials and import_textures are False. blender_to_unreal is the only caller of `import_fbx`, so the `kind != 'animation'` default never takes effect. The docs say the opposite: blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:107-108 ('`blender_to_unreal` imports materials and textures by default for static and skeletal kinds'), troubleshooting.md:67, and blender-materials-baking/SKILL.md:154-159.
findings.impact: A first import, which the skill says should create placeholder materials, arrives with no materials or textures, so agents chase a texture or material problem that is really an argument default.
findings.fix: Forward only keys the caller gave, as already done for importer, normals and socket_rotation at 409-413. Decide the default in one place and make the docs match it.

v1.reason: to_unreal builds import_args with `"materials": args["materials"]` (blender.rs:406). serde_json Index returns Value::Null for a missing key, so the key is always present, as null when the caller leaves it out. script() serialises it into ARGS_JSON (unreal.rs:466-467), and unreal_py/common.py:5 json.loads it. Python's `ARGS.get('materials', kind != 'animation')` then returns None because the key exists, so bool(None) is False, and import_materials and import_textures are always off unless the caller passes true (import_fbx.py:31-32). blender.rs:414 is the only caller of unreal::import_fbx, so the documented default never applies. blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:107-108, troubleshooting.md:67 ('imports materials by default') and blender-materials-baking/SKILL.md:154-159 all describe the opposite.
v1.correction: The keys at :409-413 are already forwarded only when present, so `materials` should be handled the same way (forward it only if it is a bool). Also decide which default is actually wanted: compare() at :462-464 already tells agents to import with materials=false when transient materials appear, and import_fbx.py's header says Interchange produced transient materials. Today's de facto 'no materials' may be the safer default, in which case the docs, not the code, should change. Either way, code and docs disagree in a normal flow, so medium stands.

findings.title: blender_to_unreal compares Unreal's bind-pose height with Blender's posed height
findings.evidence: After writing the FBX, export.py measures `size_cm` with `world_bbox(meshes)` (84-85, 109). That uses the evaluated, armature-deformed mesh at the file's current frame and pose (common.py:99-108). The FBX exporter writes skinned meshes in rest pose (armature modifiers disabled), and Unreal's `get_bounds()` is the imported bind pose (import_fbx.py:72-73). `compare()` flags any ratio outside 0.9-1.1 (blender.rs:447-459). Verified on 5.2.1: the fixture rig, posed in a crouch without keys, exports with `size_cm` [168.0, 54.1, 123.3], while re-importing the same FBX at rest measures 178.0 cm.
findings.impact: A character saved in a posed state, normal after animation work, gets a false problem such as '178 cm in Unreal but 123 cm in Blender (x1.44); check the object's scale' and `passed: false`, sending the agent after the wrong fix.
findings.fix: Measure skinned meshes in rest pose: set `arm.data.pose_position = 'REST'` and update the view layer before world_bbox, then restore it.

v1.reason: export.py:84-85,109 computes size_cm with common.world_bbox (common.py:99-108), which reads `o.evaluated_get(deps).bound_box`. That is the armature-deformed mesh at the current frame and pose. export.py:30-33 has just assigned the requested action, and the default use_mesh_modifiers=True lets the Blender FBX exporter temporarily disable Armature modifiers on skinned meshes when ARMATURE is in object_types. As a result the FBX carries the undeformed bind-pose mesh. import_fbx.py:72-74 measures `a.get_bounds()` of the imported SkeletalMesh, which is the reference pose. blender.rs compare() (around 447-459) flags any Z ratio outside 0.9-1.1. A skeletal blender_to_unreal of a rig whose current frame or unkeyed pose is crouched, or arms-up, therefore returns `passed: false` with a misleading scale message.
v1.correction: This affects only skeletal exports that include meshes. For kind=animation, selected={arm}, so meshes is empty and size_cm is None. The fix suggested is reasonable: temporarily set arm.data.pose_position='REST', or measure the meshes with the Armature modifier disabled, for every armature in `selected`, then restore it.

findings.title: blender_render engine 'eevee' hard-codes BLENDER_EEVEE, which Blender 4.2-4.5 (both LTS lines) reject
findings.evidence: `engine = {'workbench': 'BLENDER_WORKBENCH', 'eevee': 'BLENDER_EEVEE', 'cycles': 'CYCLES'}[...]` then `scene.render.engine = engine` (35-36). The fundamentals skill records that 4.2 renamed the id to `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` (blender-fundamentals/SKILL.md:241-242). 5.0 renamed it back, which is why it works on the installed 5.2.1, where workbench, eevee and cycles render with every colour mode and view. setup.md:3 recommends '4.0 or newer; LTS releases'. 4.2 and 4.5 LTS could not be run here.
findings.impact: On 4.2-4.5, `engine: "eevee"` fails with an enum error, though fundamentals SKILL.md:49 and materials SKILL.md:180-181 recommend it for lookdev.
findings.fix: Try `BLENDER_EEVEE` and fall back to `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` on TypeError.

v1.reason: render.py:35-36 maps 'eevee' to the literal 'BLENDER_EEVEE' and assigns `scene.render.engine = engine`. The repo's own blender-fundamentals/SKILL.md:241 records that the id is `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` from 4.2, and in 4.2-4.5 'BLENDER_EEVEE' is not in the enum, so the assignment raises TypeError. On the installed 5.2.1 the enum lists only 'BLENDER_EEVEE' (checked), which is why it works here. setup.md:3 recommends '4.0 or newer; LTS releases', which includes 4.2 LTS and 4.5 LTS.
v1.correction: Not run on 4.2/4.5 (unavailable). The rejection rests on the repo's own version note and the known 4.2 rename. The failure is loud and the agent can fall back to workbench or cycles, which keeps this at medium rather than higher. Fix: try 'BLENDER_EEVEE', fall back to 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT' on TypeError, and report the engine id actually used (render.py already emits `engine`).

findings.title: save / save_as leave full-size .blend1 backups in the checkout that nothing ignores or LFS-tracks
findings.evidence: Blender runs with --factory-startup, where `preferences.filepaths.save_version` is 1 (verified on 5.2.1), and run.py saves with `save_as_mainfile(...)` (:15) or `save_mainfile()` (:20). Verified: both `save: true` and `save_as` onto an existing file leave `hero.blend1`, a copy of the previous version. The recommended .gitattributes (unreal-source-control template :67) puts only `*.blend` in LFS, the gitignore template has no `*.blend1`, and the plugin docs never mention the backups.
findings.impact: Every overwrite leaves an untracked multi-megabyte binary next to the art. A `git add -A`, by an agent or by the human committing the changed .blend files as instructions.md asks, commits it into plain git history outside LFS and permanently bloats the repo.
findings.fix: Set `bpy.context.preferences.filepaths.save_version = 0` in run.py before saving (this affects only that process), or add `*.blend[0-9]*` to the documented .gitignore guidance.

v1.reason: run.py:15 calls `save_as_mainfile(filepath=..., copy=False)` and run.py:20 calls `save_mainfile()`. Under --factory-startup the default preferences keep Save Versions at 1, so overwriting an existing .blend writes `<name>.blend1`. Nothing in run.py or blender.rs changes `save_version`, and grep finds no `blend1` or `save_version` anywhere in plugins/ or crates/. The only LFS guidance (gitattributes-template.md:67) has `*.blend`, which does not match `.blend1`. gitignore-template.md has no Blender entry, and plugins/blender/docs/setup.md:19-20 points to that template as covering .blend files. instructions.md:7 tells agents to tell the human which .blend files changed so they can be committed, and a broad `git add` then picks up the backup outside LFS.
v1.correction: A backup is written only when an existing file is overwritten (`save: true`, or `save_as` onto an existing path). `save_as` to a new path, which instructions.md recommends, does not create one. The simplest fix is `bpy.context.preferences.filepaths.save_version = 0` in run.py before saving. Adding `*.blend[0-9]*` to the gitignore template as well would also cover saves made by hand.

findings.title: blender_python panics the blender MCP server when the script emits non-object JSON
findings.evidence: For PY_RUN, `run()` parses the last `RELAY_JSON:` line into `value` (366-369), then assigns `value["output"]` and `value["saved"]` (372-373). serde_json 1.0.151's `IndexMut<&str>` panics on any value that is not an object or null ('cannot access key ... in JSON ...'), and relay-cli has no catch_unwind. `emit` is in the agent's scope (run.py:5) though undocumented, and `emit('done')` or `emit([...])` prints exactly such a line. Malformed JSON after the prefix instead fails `serde_json::from_str(json_text)?`, which discards the agent's output.
findings.impact: One call kills `relay blender-mcp`, and every later Blender tool call in that agent's session fails until the provider restarts the server.
findings.fix: For PY_RUN, ignore RELAY_JSON (the script's printed output is the result) or wrap non-object values as `json!({"value": v})`. Remove `emit` from the scope or document it as object-only.

v1.reason: For PY_RUN, run() takes the last stdout line that starts with `RELAY_JSON:` (blender.rs:362), parses it (:367), then does `value["output"] = ...` and `value["saved"] = ...` (:372-373). In serde_json 1.0.151 (Cargo.lock:2970), IndexMut<&str> turns Null into an object but panics for any other non-object value. relay-cli has no catch_unwind, so the panic ends `relay blender-mcp` (main.rs:231), and every later Blender tool call in that session fails. `emit` is placed in the script's scope (run.py:5; defined in blender_py/common.py:12-13), so `emit('done')`, `emit([..])` or a printed `RELAY_JSON:42` line reaches the panic. Malformed text after the prefix makes the `?` at :367 fail, which discards the script's printed output.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low. The trigger needs the agent to use `emit`, which neither the tool description (:110) nor any skill documents (the only 'emit' hits in plugins/blender are about the shader Emission socket), or to print a line that starts with the internal `RELAY_JSON:` prefix. The mechanism is certain but the trigger is rare. Fix: in the PY_RUN branch, wrap non-object values (`if !value.is_object() { value = json!({"value": value}) }`) and treat a parse failure as no result instead of an error.

findings.title: blender_python hides its own diagnostics: printed output is dropped on failure, add-on load errors on success
findings.evidence: `failure_text` joins stdout then stderr and starts at the first 'Traceback' line (379-384). Blender sends the script's prints to stdout and the traceback to stderr (verified: the script's print appeared on stdout, the Traceback on stderr), so everything printed before the exception is discarded. On success, only lines between RELAY_OUT_BEGIN and RELAY_OUT_END are returned (358-361). `addon_utils.enable` (run.py:3-4) reports failures before that marker and does not raise. Verified: `addons: ['rigifyy']` printed 'Add-on not loaded: "rigifyy"' outside the markers and the call returned success.
findings.impact: The skills say to print the state after every step, and that output disappears exactly when a step fails. A mistyped add-on only shows up later as an unrelated 'operator could not be found' error.
findings.fix: In failure_text, include the tail of the RELAY_OUT_BEGIN..END block before the traceback. In run.py, treat a None return from `addon_utils.enable` as failure and raise with the add-on's name.

v1.reason: failure_text (blender.rs:379-384) chains stdout before stderr and starts at the first line beginning with 'Traceback'. Python writes uncaught tracebacks to stderr, and the agent's print() goes to stdout, so on a failed blender_python run everything the script printed before the exception (the RELAY_OUT_BEGIN..END block, which run.py:9-10 closes in `finally`) comes before the start index and is dropped. On success, only the lines inside the markers are returned (:358-361), and run.py:3-4 calls addon_utils.enable before RELAY_OUT_BEGIN without checking its return value. Blender's addon_utils.enable reports a failed load and returns None rather than raising, so a mistyped add-on is never shown and fails later as an unrelated missing-operator error.
v1.correction: If the add-on failure prints a Python traceback to stderr (handle_error), a later failure's failure_text starts at that traceback, so the add-on error then shows up only on the failure path. The silent case is the success path, and the case where the add-on is not found without raising a traceback. Fix as proposed: in failure_text, prepend the tail of the marker block, and in run.py, raise when enable() returns None.

findings.title: Docs and the tool description still promise a hand-side check that blender_to_unreal no longer performs
findings.evidence: The tool description says it measures '...which way it faces, and which hand ends up on which side' (blender.rs:170), and D161 says it 'compares height, root bone scale and hand sides' (DECISIONS.md:955). Checklists tell agents to confirm 'hands on the right side' (blender-rigging/SKILL.md:229-230, rigify-game-skeleton.md:159, blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:234). Since 42b325d, `compare()` (blender.rs:426-483) checks facing, not sides. `hand_sides` is derived from bone names (import_fbx.py:97-99), so it always reads correctly, as blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:171-173 itself says. troubleshooting.md:89 lists a `nothing was imported` error that no code emits; the actual failure is `failed: true` with 'the import failed with every importer tried...'.
findings.impact: Agents report 'hands on their sides' as verification evidence even though that check cannot fail, and they look for an error message that never appears.
findings.fix: Remove the hand-side wording from the tool description, D161 and the three checklists, saying 'facing about +Y' instead. Update the troubleshooting row to the real failure message.

v1.reason: compare() (blender.rs:426-483) checks failed imports, render_check, height ratio, transient materials, root bone scale and facing. It never checks hand sides, and its own doc comment (:422-425) says sides come from bone names. import_fbx.py:97-99 computes hand_sides using body_frame (unreal_py/common.py:241-258), whose right axis is built from the name pairs themselves. So a name-left hand always reads as left, and the skill admits this (blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:171-173, 'informational only... always read correctly'). Even so, D161 (DECISIONS.md:955) says it 'compares ... hand sides', and the checklists at blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:234, blender-rigging/SKILL.md:229-230 and rigify-game-skeleton.md:159 treat 'hands on the right side' as verification. troubleshooting.md:89 lists a `nothing was imported` error that appears nowhere in the code. The real failure is `failed: true` (import_fbx.py:183) plus the compare() message at blender.rs:430.
v1.correction: The tool description at blender.rs:170 is only partly wrong: the tool does report hand_sides in `imported`, so 'measure ... which hand ends up on which side' is literally true, but it suggests a meaningful check. The real drift is in D161 and the three checklists, which treat a check that cannot fail as evidence, and in the troubleshooting row's error text.

findings.title: blender-fundamentals (loaded first) contradicts its siblings on the operator-existence check and on Rigify
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:122-124 says '`hasattr(bpy.ops.object, "shade_auto_smooth")` tells you whether this Blender has it'. bpy.ops submodules answer any attribute: on 5.2.1, `hasattr(bpy.ops.object, 'definitely_not_an_operator_xyz')` is True, and blender-modeling/SKILL.md:122-123 says it 'is always True - do not use it (verified)'. SKILL.md:243-244 says 'Many bundled add-ons (Rigify among them) moved to the online extensions platform, so `addons: ["rigify"]` can fail'. Rigify ships in scripts/addons_core/rigify and enabled fine on 5.2.1, as blender-rigging/SKILL.md:117 and setup.md:16-17 say.
findings.impact: The skill every agent loads first teaches an existence check that always says yes, which leads to calls to operators the installed Blender lacks. It also suggests Rigify may be unavailable when it is bundled.
findings.fix: Check with `'name' in dir(bpy.ops.object)` or `hasattr(bpy.types, 'OBJECT_OT_name')`. Correct the 4.2 note to say Rigify stays bundled.

v1.reason: blender-fundamentals/SKILL.md:122-124 says `hasattr(bpy.ops.object, "shade_auto_smooth")` tells you whether Blender has the operator. In 5.2's scripts/modules/bpy/ops.py, the submodule's `__getattr__` returns `_bpy_ops_submodule__getattr__(module, func)` for any name, so hasattr is always True. blender-modeling/SKILL.md:122-123 says exactly that ('always True - do not use it (verified)'). SKILL.md:243-244 says Rigify moved to the extensions platform, but the installed 5.2 ships scripts/addons_core/rigify, and blender-rigging/SKILL.md:117 and setup.md:16-17 both say it is bundled.
v1.correction: No correction to lines or mechanism. Fix: use `name in dir(bpy.ops.object)` (the submodule's `__dir__` lists real operators), and say Rigify stayed in core add-ons in 4.2.

findings.title: blender_export fails when an exported child (UCX_/SOCKET_/LOD) is in an excluded collection
findings.evidence: Static exports add `o.children_recursive` (16-18), then call `o.hide_set(False); o.hide_viewport = False; o.select_set(True)` on each (57-60). Verified on 5.2.1: SM_Crate with its UCX_ child in an excluded 'Collision' collection fails with `RuntimeError: Object 'UCX_SM_Crate_00' cannot be selected because it is not in View Layer 'ViewLayer'!`. An unrelated excluded object is harmless. The docs promise the static export brings collision, socket and LOD children (mcp-tools.md:47-48).
findings.impact: Hiding collision in an excluded collection, a common practice, makes every static export of that asset fail with a raw traceback.
findings.fix: Temporarily un-exclude the layer collections that hold the selected objects for the export, or fail with a clear message naming the collection.

v1.reason: export.py:16-18 adds `o.children_recursive` for non-armature objects. Lines 57-60 then call `hide_set(False)`, `hide_viewport = False` and `select_set(True)` on every selected object. I reproduced this on Blender 5.2.1 with a UCX_ child in a collection excluded from the view layer. `hide_set(False)` succeeded, but `select_set(True)` raised `Object 'UCX_SM_00' cannot be selected because it is not in View Layer 'ViewLayer'!`. The export therefore aborts with a raw traceback. Nothing upstream filters excluded objects.
v1.correction: The failing call is select_set at line 60. hide_set at line 58 did not raise in my test. Severity stays low: hiding collision by excluding its collection is less common than the eye toggle. Fix: temporarily un-exclude the owning layer collections, or skip and report objects that are not in the view layer.

findings.title: Modeling recipe make_lods creates LODs as siblings, so blender_export with `objects` drops them
findings.evidence: `make_lods` creates each `<base>_LODn` with `bpy.data.objects.new(...)`, sets its matrix_world and links it to the source's collections, but never parents it (196-205). blender_export's static branch adds only `o.children_recursive` (export.py:16-18), and the modeling skill says '`blender_export` (static) includes `_LODn` children' (SKILL.md:182-183). The to-unreal prep recipe does parent its LODs (`lod.parent = ob`, prep-recipes.md:79).
findings.impact: `blender_export {objects: ['SM_Rock_LOD0'], kind: 'static'}` after the modeling recipe silently exports LOD0 only. Without `objects`, each LOD is exported as a separate root mesh.
findings.fix: Parent the copies in make_lods (`o.parent = src; o.matrix_parent_inverse = src.matrix_world.inverted()`), as prep-recipes.md does.

v1.reason: modeling-recipes.md make_lods (lines ~196-205) creates each LOD with bpy.data.objects.new, copies matrix_world and links it to the source's collections, but never sets a parent. export.py:16-18 adds only o.children_recursive to an explicitly chosen object. So `objects:['SM_Rock_LOD0']` exports LOD0 alone. Without `objects`, every parentless mesh becomes a root (export.py:7), so each LOD is exported as a separate mesh. That contradicts modeling SKILL.md:182-183 ('includes _LODn children'). prep-recipes.md:79 does set `lod.parent = ob`, so the two recipes disagree.
v1.correction: The fix should also keep the world transform: either set the parent and then reassign matrix_world, as prep-recipes does, or set matrix_parent_inverse. Separately, parenting is not enough for Unreal to build a LOD group from children named _LODn; the skill already hedges on this ('If they arrive as separate meshes...'). The impact stays low.

findings.title: UCP_ capsule collision is documented, but the tools treat it as render geometry
findings.evidence: The pipeline contract lists UCX_ '(also `UBX_` box, `USP_` sphere, `UCP_` capsule)' (blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:37; blender-modeling/SKILL.md:193). The tools recognise only UCX_, UBX_ and USP_: info.py:29 (role detection), export.py:39 (mesh-check exclusion), export.py:84 (size exclusion) and export.py:107 (the `collision` list).
findings.impact: A UCP_ capsule is mesh-checked as render geometry, can inflate `size_cm` and so the height comparison, and is missing from `exported.collision`. The skill calls that list 'exactly what went into the FBX' (SKILL.md:159-161), so the agent concludes the collision was not exported.
findings.fix: Add 'UCP_' to the prefix tuples, ideally as one shared constant in common.py.

v1.reason: The pipeline docs list UCP_ capsule collision (blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:37, blender-modeling/SKILL.md:193), but every prefix check in the tools stops at UCX_/UBX_/USP_: info.py:29 (unreal_role), export.py:39 (mesh-check exclusion), export.py:84 (size exclusion) and export.py:107 (the `collision` list). The export comment at export.py:1 also names only three prefixes. A UCP_ child of a static mesh is still exported, because children_recursive is selected. However, it is not reported in `collision`, it gets mesh-checked as render geometry, and it can enlarge size_cm if it sticks out past the render mesh.
v1.correction: The practical impact is small. A closed capsule normally passes mesh_report, and it only inflates size_cm when it extends beyond the visual mesh. The main harm is the misleading `collision` list. Use one shared COLLISION_PREFIXES tuple in common.py, including 'UCP_'.

findings.title: 'Files outside the checkout are refused' is not enforced for writes: fbx_options.filepath and symlinked folders bypass it
findings.evidence: mcp-tools.md:4-5 says paths are relative to the checkout and files outside it are refused. blender_export validates `path` (blender.rs:236), but `for key, value in (ARGS.get('fbx_options') or {}).items(): options[key] = ...` (export.py:78-79) lets `fbx_options: {filepath: '/anywhere.fbx'}` replace it; the FBX is written there before `os.path.getsize(path)` fails. `resolve_new` (blender.rs:266-270) checks only the string (not absolute, no '..'), so a symlinked directory inside the checkout sends `save_as` or `path` outside. `list_files` follows directory symlinks (blender.rs:283 `path.is_dir()`) and lists outside files that `resolve()` then refuses. Plugin MCP calls never reach guardrail.gate (PreToolUse matcher `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash`, hooks.rs:350). Bash already allows arbitrary interpreters, so this is defence in depth, not a new hole.
findings.impact: The documented containment of tool arguments is incomplete: a careless option or a symlink writes outside the worktree, and Relay's audit never sees it.
findings.fix: Reject `filepath` and `use_selection` in fbx_options. In resolve_new, canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor and require it to be under the canonical root. Don't follow symlinked directories in list_files. Reword the docs to say this is an argument guard, not a sandbox.

v1.reason: The same MCP server exposes `blender_python` (blender.rs `call`, the `blender_python` arm). It runs arbitrary agent-supplied code with `bpy` in a full Blender Python interpreter, so it can already write any file anywhere (`open(...)`, `bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath='/anywhere')`, `os`). The path checks in `resolve`/`resolve_new` are argument hygiene against mistakes, not a containment boundary. Rejecting `filepath` in fbx_options or canonicalising symlinked parents would close nothing. The docs also say plainly that `fbx_options` 'overrides any exporter option' (mcp-tools.md export section, blender.rs tool description). A symlinked directory inside the checkout has to be created by the repo or the agent, and the agent can already write anywhere through blender_python or Bash. The finding itself concedes there is no new hole. At most, the 'files outside it are refused' sentence could be reworded, which is not worth a finding.
v1.correction: If kept at all, it is a one-line docs clarification: path arguments are checked to be inside the checkout, but blender_python and fbx_options are unrestricted. It is not a security issue.

findings.title: The blender MCP server ignores cancellation, so a long run blocks every later call from that agent
findings.evidence: `serve()` handles stdin requests strictly one at a time (37-51). `handle()` returns None for messages without an id (`message.get("id").cloned()?`, line 56), so `notifications/cancelled` is dropped. `run()` then blocks in `output_with_timeout` for up to `timeout_s`, whose schema maximum is 3600 (blender.rs:117), and the skills tell agents to raise it for bakes.
findings.impact: When the user interrupts a long bake or render, Blender keeps running for up to an hour, and the agent's next Blender call queues behind it and appears hung.
findings.fix: Run each call on a worker thread keyed by request id, keep the Child handle and kill it on `notifications/cancelled`, and keep answering ping while busy.

v1.reason: blender.rs:37-51 handles stdin one line at a time on one thread. handle() at :56 returns None for any message without an id, so `notifications/cancelled` is dropped silently. blender_python's timeout_s goes up to 3600 (:117) and is passed to run(), which blocks in relay_core::proc::output_with_timeout (:351) until Blender exits or the deadline passes. Nothing reads stdin during that wait, so if the client gives up on a call (the user interrupts) and the agent makes another Blender call, the new request waits in the pipe until the old Blender process ends. output_with_timeout also puts the child in its own process group (proc.rs:32), so Blender keeps running even after the MCP server exits. The impact claim holds. Low severity fits: it affects one agent's Blender tools, not the engine.
v1.correction: The same single-threaded serve loop, which also ignores cancellation, is in crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:57-76 (the unreal MCP server, where ue_* calls can also run for minutes: import_fbx uses 900 s). Fix both together or share one serve loop. The smallest fix is to keep the Child/pid of the in-flight job and have a reader thread kill its process group on notifications/cancelled for that request id. Full per-request concurrency is not needed.

findings.title: Silent caps: blender_render drops frames after 12, and the file listing stops at 500 files
findings.evidence: `for f in frames[:12]:` (render.py:69) drops later frames and says nothing in the result. tool_result also returns at most 16 images (unreal.rs:42, 1875); it reports `requested`, but not the dropped frames. `list_files` stops at depth 8 or 500 files (blender.rs:274) with no truncation flag. mcp-tools.md documents none of these limits.
findings.impact: An agent asking for every key frame of a long action (say 15 frames) never sees the last ones and reports them as checked. A large art tree's listing looks complete when it isn't.
findings.fix: Return `skipped_frames` and a `truncated: true` flag, and document the limits in mcp-tools.md.

v1.reason: render.py:69 `for f in frames[:12]:` truncates the requested frames and the emitted result (render.py:88) only lists the files rendered, with no skipped-frames field. blender.rs:274 `if depth > 8 || out.len() >= 500 { return; }` stops the walk, and list_files (blender.rs:294-297) returns `files` with no truncation flag. unreal.rs:1875/1885 caps images at MAX_IMAGES=16 but does report `{shown, requested, limit}`, so the image cap is not silent. plugins/blender/docs/mcp-tools.md (the file is under plugins/blender/docs/, not docs/) documents neither the 12-frame nor the 500-file limit.
v1.correction: The mcp-tools.md cited is plugins/blender/docs/mcp-tools.md. The 16-image cap is not silent, because tool_result reports `requested` and `limit`. Only the 12-frame cap and the 500-file/depth-8 listing cap are silent. With the default 3 views, 12 frames already gives 36 images, so the 16-image cap usually bites first, and it is reported. Fix: emit `frames_skipped` in render.py and `truncated: true` from list_files.

results.coverage:
Scope: crates/relay-core, relay-bus, relay-cli and relay-remote. apps/relay-native was read only for call sites and client timeouts; apps/relay-mobile was excluded.

**Registrations enumerated.** I found 220 sites with `rg "register(_unlocked|_staged)?::<"` across 19 handler files plus provider_updates.rs: 176 plain, 25 unlocked, 19 staged. I classified every one.
- Plain handlers: read the body and the helpers it calls, looking for subprocesses, gix work, filesystem walks, large reads and network calls.
- Staged handlers: checked that finish is short, and looked for TOCTOU between prepare and finish.
- Unlocked handlers: checked that none mutate the store or depend on inconsistent multi-read state. None found; device.list and device.leases only prune the in-memory lease map.

**Other registration and lock paths followed:**
- Nested invocation via `rg "invoke_registered|replay_registered"`: task.dispatch, guardrail.confirm, audit.undo, project.clone, project.remove, workspace.remove.
- Every `system_write(` caller (9 sites).
- Every direct `store.lock()` site: socket door, recovery, branch_cleanup, skills::refresh_all, integration worker, device workers, the app resource loop and pty_by_name.
- Ops the socket door answers itself (bus.wait/subscribe, attach, mirror and run streams).
- The fast paths (pty_fast_path, mirror_fast_path, answers_from_memory).

**Other search patterns:**
- `Command::new|.output()|.status()|.spawn()|output_with_timeout`: classified each subprocess site as locked or unlocked.
- `gix::`, `fs::read|read_dir|remove_dir_all|copy`, `ctx.read(`, `after_commit`, `spawn_blocking`.
- `guardrail::enforce(`, to find which ops can be held and replayed.

**Lock ordering.** I checked store → hooks::writes, creating_sessions, device_runs, ui, mirrors, ptys and SWEEPING. I found no reachable deadlock. git.branch.cleanup's prepare calls engine.store.lock() directly, which would self-deadlock if it were ever nested; nothing nests it today.

**Not verified:**
- No timings: cargo was not run. Magnitudes come from code reading. The only measurements are two throwaway sqlite3/Python checks in the scratchpad: AUTOINCREMENT reuse after rollback, and the task.activity query plan.
- Claude Code's behaviour when a PreToolUse hook times out (whether the tool then runs or is blocked) is outside this repo, so I could not confirm it.
- relay-cli's Unreal/Blender tooling was not reviewed; it does not touch the store. relay-remote was checked only for direct store access, and has none.

findings.title: project.clone (and git.pr.open) run network subprocesses inside the request transaction with no timeout
findings.evidence: workspace.rs:228 registers ProjectClone with plain `e.register`, so it runs inside dispatch_inner's transaction with the store MutexGuard held (engine.rs:954-980). Line 234: `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()`. That is plain std `output()`: it does not go through proc::output_with_timeout and does not set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. The op's own summary says the opposite: ops/workspace.rs:38 "Clone a repo into the workspace and register it (async; project.changed when done)". BUS.md:228 says slow work "is a handler that returns quickly with a handle", and proc.rs:8 says "Long-running work belongs on a worker thread after commit, not here". The GTK client waits up to 1800 s for this op (client.rs:67), so the authors expect clones to take many minutes. git.pr.open has the same shape (git.rs:666-681): a plain handler that runs `gh pr create` via `cmd.output()` inside the transaction, again with no deadline.
findings.impact: When the user clicks Clone (onboarding.rs:527), the global store mutex stays held for the whole network clone. That can be seconds or tens of minutes, and has no upper bound if the connection stalls or ssh/askpass waits for input. Everything else queues behind it. Every agent request takes the same lock in resolve_actor and authorize (engine.rs:871, 1378), so every agent's PreToolUse guardrail hook (guardrail.gate, 30 s hook timeout, hooks.rs:351) and every session.report blocks. Ordinary UI requests time out after 30 s, and the phone door stalls. Only PTY keystrokes keep working (D148).
findings.fix: Make project.clone return a handle as BUS.md §5.1 describes: run `git clone` on a worker thread after commit, or in a staged prepare phase through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. The worker then emits project.changed and a `project.clone.completed` audit row through system_write. The locked phase should only call project.add. Convert git.pr.open the same way: staged prepare plus output_with_timeout.

v1.reason: workspace.rs:228 registers ProjectClone with plain `e.register`. In engine.rs dispatch_inner, any handler that is in neither `unlocked` nor `prepares` runs after `let mut conn = self.store.lock(); let tx = conn.transaction()` (engine.rs ~954-958), so the MutexGuard is held across `(h.call)`. Line 234 runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()`, which is plain std output: no proc::output_with_timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Other git calls in the crate do set that variable (worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943/1349, branch_cleanup.rs:114). The op metadata says "(async; project.changed when done)" (ops/workspace.rs:38), and the GTK client allows 1800 s for project.clone (client.rs:67). So a long or stalled network clone holds the global store lock for its whole length, and every other non-unlocked request queues behind it, agent guardrail gates included. git.pr.open (git.rs:666-686) has the same shape: a plain register calling `cmd.output()` on `gh pr create`, a network call with no deadline, under the lock.
v1.correction: The git.pr.open call is at git.rs:678-680 (`cmd.output()`). Stdin is null under std output(), but git/ssh can still prompt through /dev/tty or an askpass helper when the engine has a controlling terminal, so the hang has no upper bound unless GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and a deadline are set. The fix is as proposed: register_staged with the clone in prepare through output_with_timeout (or a worker after commit), with only project.add in the locked phase. Do the same for gh pr create.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says.
- workspace.rs:228 is the only registration of `project.clone`, and it uses plain `e.register`.
- In dispatch_inner, only ops in the `unlocked` or `prepares` maps avoid the lock (engine.rs:906, 920). Every other op runs `(h.call)` while holding `self.store.lock()` and an open transaction (engine.rs:954-980).
- The lock is a blocking std Mutex (store.rs:474-476). LockSpan only logs (engine.rs:106-118); it enforces nothing.
- Line 234 runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()`. That bypasses proc::output_with_timeout and does not set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. The other git calls in the engine do set it (worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943/1349, branch_cleanup.rs:114).
- No decision covers this. D149's list of ops moved off the lock (DECISIONS.md:810-814) does not include `project.clone`. BUS.md:227-229 and the op summary (ops/workspace.rs:38, "async") both describe the opposite design.

(b) The user triggers it in a normal flow; agents cannot (the op is UserOnly).
- Three entry points open the onboarding panel: "Add project…" in the sidebar (shell/registry.rs:472), the add-project button (app.rs:976-978), and the first-run prompt shown when there are no projects (app.rs:1412-1413).
- On the GitHub tab, onboarding sends `project.clone` with the repository's https `clone_url` (onboarding.rs:506-527).
- It happens each time the user clones a project. That is occasional, and usually while other agent sessions are running.
- How long the lock is held depends on the network: seconds for a small repository, many minutes for a large or LFS-heavy one. The client allows 1800 s for this op (client.rs:67).
- It can also be unbounded. When the engine is started by `./run.sh` from a terminal, `nohup ... &` (run.sh:32) keeps it in that terminal's session and foreground process group. A private repository with no credential helper then makes git prompt "Username for ..." on /dev/tty and wait forever. When launched from the .desktop entry there is no terminal, and git fails quickly instead.

(c) While the clone runs, every request that needs the store mutex waits.
- Agents: every agent request on the socket takes the lock in check_session_token (engine.rs:1378), in fill_identity (engine.rs:1157) and in authorize (engine.rs:871). Even the unlocked queries take it briefly through `Unlocked::read` (engine.rs:181).
- Guardrail hook: `guardrail.gate` is a plain `register` handler (guardrail.rs:304). The CLI hook has no deadline of its own (socket.rs:801-819). So each agent Edit/Write/Bash call waits until Claude Code's 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:351). What Claude Code does after that timeout (block the tool or let it run) is not in this repo, and I did not establish it.
- Other agent traffic: MCP tool calls and lifecycle reports stall the same way.
- Phone: the phone door forwards its requests to the same socket (relay-remote bridge.rs:156), so those stall too.
- Desktop UI, which the finding understates: the socket server handles one request at a time per connection; its loop at socket.rs:335-744 awaits each dispatch before reading the next line. `ui.call` sends `project.clone` on the shared UI connection; only lifecycle ops get their own connection (app.rs:1111-1116). So every UI refresh and page request queues behind the clone. Each one fails after 30 s with "Request timed out" (client.rs:70, 81), and still runs later.
- What keeps working: terminal keystrokes, because each terminal pane opens its own connection (terminal.rs:476) and `session.input` takes no lock (engine.rs:891-897).
- No data is lost. The freeze ends when git exits.

(d) High is the right severity: it freezes the bus and the UI in a normal user flow. It is not critical: the user starts it, nothing is lost, and the stall normally lasts only as long as the clone. The unbounded case needs both a terminal launch and a credential prompt.

On `git.pr.open`: it has the same shape (git.rs:666-692, plain `register`, `cmd.output()` at 679-681). The user starts it from the Code page after a confirmation (code_git.rs:662, 1240-1241), and the default agent roles do not include it (settings.rs:36-38). Under `output()`, stdin is null and stdout is piped, so `gh` runs non-interactively. It usually holds the lock for a second or a few. Same root cause, much smaller impact; it is fine listed as related, but it does not carry the severity.

(e) The proposed fix is only partly complete; see the correction.
v2.correction:
The impact leaves out a second stall: the desktop UI's shared connection is blocked by the clone itself, separately from the store lock. The socket server handles one request at a time per connection (socket.rs:335-744), and onboarding sends `project.clone` on the shared UI connection (app.rs:1111-1116).

So the "staged prepare" option in the fix is necessary but not enough:
- It releases the store mutex, which fixes agents, the phone and every other connection.
- The UI would still queue behind the clone. Either the client must send `project.clone` on its own connection, the way `is_lifecycle_request` does (client.rs:50-63, app.rs:1113-1114), or the op must take the documented async shape.
- The async shape is: return a handle, clone on a worker after commit, then emit `project.changed` and write a `project.clone.completed` row through system_write. That changes `ProjectCloneOut`, which today returns the created Project that onboarding.rs:528 reads, so the client would have to wait for `project.changed` instead.

Details for whichever route is taken:
- The `output_with_timeout` deadline must be long. Clones legitimately take minutes, and the client allows 1800 s. A deadline sized for a short probe would kill real clones.
- Set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and BatchMode for ssh URLs. output_with_timeout puts the child in its own process group (proc.rs:32), so a git that tries to prompt on /dev/tty is stopped by SIGTTIN and only dies at the deadline.
- Keep removing the destination directory when `project.add` fails in the locked phase.

Small corrections:
- The `git.pr.open` subprocess call is `cmd.output()` at git.rs:679-681.
- "Only PTY keystrokes keep working" is slightly too narrow. Mirror touch input (engine.rs:901) and unlocked queries that never read the store also keep working.

findings.title: task.dispatch runs the staged session.create/spawn/wake/resume prepare phases inside its own transaction, under the store mutex
findings.evidence: task.dispatch is a plain `register` (task.rs:1049). dispatch_task calls `ctx.invoke_registered("session.create", …)` (task.rs:683). It then calls `ctx.invoke_registered(op, json!({"session":name}))` for session.spawn, session.wake or session.resume (task.rs:693-713). invoke_registered runs a staged op's prepare synchronously against the transaction that is already open: `Unlocked { engine, held: Some(self.tx), … }; let out = prepare(&mut stage, &payload)?;` (engine.rs:328-342). Those prepare phases hold exactly the work D149 moved out of the lock. session.create's prepare runs refresh_new_worktree → `git fetch --all --prune` (20 s cap), worktree::create → `git worktree add` (120 s cap, includes the LFS checkout), and hooks::install_git (session.rs:854-893). A launch's prepare runs skills::apply, which copies skill folders (session.rs:492-496), plus hook/adapter installs, brief writes and the briefing rev-walks. With `fanout`, all of this repeats for every descendant inside the same transaction (task.rs:1067-1075). DECISIONS.md:816-819 says guardrail.confirm's replay is the only nested path ("only that path"). DECISIONS.md:767-768 (D147) says skill copying "never runs under the store mutex". The GTK client already allows 180 s for task.dispatch (client.rs:69). The same mechanism runs git.commit's prepare under the lock when guardrail.confirm replays it (guardrail.rs:583). That prepare includes run_user_pre_commit, which runs the user's own pre-commit hook via `Command::new(&hook)…output()` with no timeout (hooks.rs:210-213). It also covers project.remove/workspace.remove nesting session.close's teardown (workspace.rs:173, 328).
findings.impact: Dispatching a task from the board to an existing created/parked/restorable session holds the global lock for the whole launch preparation. task_pages.rs:652 sends start, which defaults to true, and every session becomes restorable after an app restart. A CLI or phone dispatch with `create` holds the lock for a network fetch plus a full worktree checkout, multiplied by the fanout count. Confirming a held commit holds it for the user's pre-commit hook (tests, linters). For that whole time every agent's gate/report hooks and every UI request stall.
findings.fix: Register task.dispatch as staged. Its prepare runs the nested ops' prepare phases unlocked (the checkout, hooks and skills) and passes the results to finish. Finish then only performs the row updates and the PTY start. Alternatively, split dispatch into create → commit → launch steps that the client sequences, as launch.rs already does with start:false. Give run_user_pre_commit a deadline (proc::output_with_timeout).

v1.reason: task.dispatch is a plain `e.register` (task.rs:1049). dispatch_task nests `invoke_registered("session.create", ...)` (task.rs:683) and `invoke_registered(op, ...)` for session.spawn, session.wake or session.resume (task.rs:712). For a staged op, invoke_registered runs prepare synchronously with `held: Some(self.tx)` (engine.rs:328-342), which is inside the outer transaction with the store mutex held. session.create's prepare runs refresh_new_worktree → fetch_remote, capped at 20 s (git.rs:969-971, 939-948). It also runs worktree::create, capped at 120 s (worktree.rs:214), and hooks::install_git (session.rs:861-893). The launch prepare runs install_git, install_claude or install_codex, skills::apply copies (session.rs:479-496) and brief writes. D149 (DECISIONS.md:816-819) says the nested prepare costs extra 'only on that path' (guardrail.confirm). This is a second, larger path, and D147's 'the copying never runs under the store mutex' is false for it. The trigger is common. The board's Dispatch button (task_pages.rs:652) sends {task_id, session} with start defaulting to true, so dispatching to a created, parked or restorable session runs the full launch prepare under the lock. The native client allows task.dispatch 180 s (client.rs:69). guardrail.confirm replaying git.commit (guardrail.rs:583) also runs run_user_pre_commit (hooks.rs:210-213), which has no deadline, under the lock. That is the user's whole pre-commit suite, and it holds up every other request.
v1.correction: launch.rs:810 already dispatches with start:false and launches afterwards, so the cheapest fix is to have the board path do the same: commit the dispatch, then call session.spawn/wake/resume as separate staged requests. For `create`, have the client sequence session.create, then task.dispatch {session}. Separately, bound run_user_pre_commit with proc::output_with_timeout. The docs drift in D149 and D147 should be corrected either way.

v2.reason:
(a) Confirmed in the code. task.dispatch is a plain `e.register::<Dispatch>` (task.rs:1049). dispatch_task nests `ctx.invoke_registered("session.create", …)` (task.rs:683) and `ctx.invoke_registered(op, json!({"session":name}))` for spawn, wake or resume (task.rs:711-712). All four are `register_staged` (session.rs:833, 917, 943, 999). invoke_registered runs a staged op's prepare synchronously with `held: Some(self.tx)` (engine.rs:328-342). dispatch_inner holds the store MutexGuard for the whole handler (engine.rs:954-980). skills::apply does not lock the store itself, so this is a long hold, not a self-deadlock. The launches were staged only yesterday (853e635), so this path still costs what it did before the split. It was never converted, which makes D149's "only that path" and D147's "never runs under the store mutex" false, as is fetch_remote's own doc comment (git.rs:937).

(b) The heavy trigger is the phone door, a normal flow for anyone using it. The phone's "Ask an agent" sheet and its Board dispatch both send `task.dispatch {task_id, create:{project_id,provider,role}, start:true}`. relay-remote/tests/remote.rs:311 pins that payload, using start:false only to avoid needing a provider binary. The bridge forwards bus lines to the engine's socket door (bridge.rs:156). With no `branch`, refresh_new_worktree always calls fetch_remote (git.rs:969-971). For any project without a plugin setting default_checkout:"primary" (only plugins/unreal-engine does), the nested create then runs `git fetch --all --prune` (20 s cap) and `git worktree add`, a full checkout including LFS filters (120 s cap, worktree.rs:214), plus install_git. The nested spawn then runs install_git again, the adapter writes, a first-time copy of every enabled skill into the new worktree (session.rs:492-496), and the brief writes. All of this happens under the mutex on every phone dispatch. The desktop board's Dispatch (task_pages.rs:652, start defaults to true) also nests resume, wake or spawn when the target is restorable, parked or created, which is common after a restart (Engine::shutdown marks live sessions restorable). Its extra hold is small, though: install_git's ~4 git calls (10 s cap each) plus small file writes and skill stamp checks, about tens of ms. The desktop never sends `create`. launch.rs:810 uses start:false followed by standalone staged spawns, so it is unaffected. fanout repeats a fetch and a checkout per descendant, but only a generic socket client (`relay cmd`) can send it.

(c) While the lock is held, every request that touches the store queues. That includes every authenticated agent request (check_session_token locks the store, engine.rs:1377-1384), every PreToolUse gate and report hook, all desktop UI reads and writes, and the short reads inside unlocked queries. Only the session.input/resize and mirror-input fast paths keep working. On an ordinary repo with a remote, each phone dispatch freezes all agents' tool calls and the desktop's data for seconds. A slow network or a large checkout stretches that to tens of seconds. Past 30 s, desktop requests fail with "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown" (client.rs:70). The gate hook's own 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:351) is also exceeded, and I could not establish from this repo whether Claude Code then blocks or proceeds. No data is lost, and the hold is bounded by the subprocess caps.

(d) High fits the rubric's "a freeze of the bus" in a normal flow, namely the phone door's headline action on ordinary projects. It is not critical: the freeze is bounded and nothing is lost.

(e) The proposed fix "stage task.dispatch and run the nested prepares in its prepare" does not work as stated for create plus start. stage_launch reads the session row by name (session.rs:605), and that row exists only after finish_create inserts it inside the transaction. The launch op (spawn, wake or resume) also depends on the row's state, which can change between the two phases. The client-sequencing alternative, or the equivalent done engine-side, is sound and matches what launch.rs already does.

1) Where the impact lies. The multi-second freeze comes from the phone door's create dispatch: RequestSheet and Board both send create with start:true, which runs fetch, worktree add, and the first-time skill copy under the mutex, for any project not on the "primary" checkout. The desktop Board Dispatch to a restorable or parked session adds only about tens of ms (install_git's ~4 bounded git calls plus small writes; skill folders are pre-materialized at engine start). The first verifier overstates that desktop path. The desktop never sends create.

2) The "briefing rev-walks" are not specific to the nesting. plan_launch's awareness::brief runs inside ctx.read, so it is under the lock in the standalone staged path as well.

3) The fix as written does not work for create plus start (see reason (e)). A workable version:
- Stage the create half. session.create's prepare is already designed to run unlocked, using the creating_sessions reservation and the finish_create recheck.
- Commit the dispatch.
- Run spawn, wake or resume as its own staged pipeline request after the commit, engine-side, so the phone's existing payload keeps working. Alternatively, the clients send session.create, then task.dispatch {session, start:false}, then the launch op.
- Accept that a failed launch no longer rolls back the dispatch. That is already launch.rs's behaviour.

4) guardrail.confirm replaying git.commit is the exception D149 documents. The actionable defect there is a separate root cause: run_user_pre_commit (hooks.rs:210-213) uses a bare Command::output() with no deadline. That breaks CLAUDE.md's proc::output_with_timeout rule on every git.commit, and on the confirm path it holds the store for the user's whole hook. It should be its own finding. The comment at git.rs:531-534 ("before anything is locked") is also false on that path.

5) workspace.rs:173/328 (nested session.close with remove_worktree:false) is the same mechanism with low impact: run_teardown makes one git config --get plus a set or unset per worktree, each timeout-bounded, and only on a rare op.

6) Related docs that are now wrong: D149 ("only that path"), D147 ("never runs under the store mutex"), git.rs:937 ("called outside the store transaction") and session.rs:350-351 (run_teardown "runs with the store unlocked").

findings.title: worktree::git has no timeout, and plain-register git handlers (plus git.commit's locked finish) call it with the store mutex held
findings.evidence:
worktree.rs:26-36: `fn git(repo, args) { let out = Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output() … }` and `pub fn git_mutate(…) { git(repo, args) }`. There is no deadline and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. These call it inside the request transaction:
- git.stage `git add --` (git.rs:503)
- git.unstage (git.rs:527)
- git.branch.create `git switch -c <name> [start]` (git.rs:374). validate_branch_name also runs its own unbounded `git check-ref-format` `.output()` (git.rs:1269-1273).
- git.branch.delete `git branch -d` (git.rs:485)
- git.branch.clean_merged (git.rs:712)
- file.restore_head `git checkout -- <path>` (file.rs:256)
- session.update → rename_branch `git branch -m` (session.rs:1460, worktree.rs:377-378)
- git.commit's staged finish, which runs `git commit --no-verify -m` inside the transaction (git.rs:571).
branch.delete and clean_merged also run branches_for in the transaction (git.rs:455, 695, 1445-1513). That is a full-history gix walk whenever any branch is unmerged, plus a divergence walk per branch. git.branches does the same work unlocked. proc.rs:3-6 and CLAUDE.md require every subprocess forked from a handler to go through output_with_timeout.
findings.impact: This app targets LFS-heavy repositories (Unreal/Blender tooling). There, `git switch -c name start`, `git checkout -- file` and `git add` run LFS smudge/clean filters, which means network downloads or hashing GB-sized assets. `git commit` can wait on a gpg pinentry prompt, or on user prepare-commit-msg/post-commit hooks, which --no-verify does not skip. Each of these holds the global lock for its whole run with no upper bound, freezing every agent's hooks and the UI. A hung filter, prompt or credential helper freezes the bus indefinitely.
findings.fix: Route worktree::git through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Register these mutations as staged, with the git subprocess and gix walks in prepare and only events/audit in finish, as was already done for git.branch.switch, git.fetch and git.push. For git.commit, see the companion finding about committing a tree frozen in prepare.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:26-33 `fn git` runs `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()`. There is no deadline and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, and `git_mutate` (line 36) is a passthrough. Every call site the finding names sits in a plain `e.register` handler, which runs inside the request transaction with the store mutex held: git.rs:345/374 BranchCreate (`switch -c`, a full checkout), 445/485 BranchDelete, 490/503 Stage (`git add --`), 507/527 Unstage, 693/712 CleanMerged; file.rs:253-256 RestoreHead (`git checkout -- path`); session.rs:1431/1460 Update -> worktree.rs:377-378 rename_branch (`check-ref-format`, then `branch -m`). validate_branch_name (git.rs:1269-1273) runs its own unbounded `.output()`. BranchDelete (455) and CleanMerged (695) call `branches_for(ctx.tx(), …)` (1445-1513) under the lock. That function does a merged_tips history walk plus an upstream_metrics walk per branch. The unlocked git.branches handler does the same work with nothing held. CommitOp's finish (571) runs `git commit --no-verify -m` inside the transaction. The comment at 531-534 makes that deliberate, but the call is still unbounded. --no-verify skips pre-commit and commit-msg but not prepare-commit-msg, post-commit or gpg signing. Contrast run_switch (1347-1352), which uses `proc::output_with_timeout` with a 120 s limit and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. That proves the bounded pattern exists and was applied only to some paths. proc.rs:3-6 and CLAUDE.md both require it for every subprocess forked from a handler. Trigger: git.stage, file.restore_head or git.branch.create in an LFS repo, or a commit with signing or a slow post-commit hook. Consequence: the store lock is held for the child's full runtime, so every session's hooks, session.* ops and the UI wait; a child that never exits freezes the bus for good. Kept at high: these are normal flows (stage, commit, restore), but in an ordinary repo each takes milliseconds. The indefinite freeze needs an LFS filter, a credential or signing helper, or a hook that stalls.
v1.correction: Add a closely related case the finding missed. git.pr.open (git.rs:666-680) is a plain `e.register` handler that runs `gh pr create` with a bare `.output()`. That is a network call to GitHub with no timeout, made under the store lock, which makes it the clearest instance of this root cause. It belongs in `related` or in a sibling finding. git.worktree.remove (git.rs:129, a plain register) also runs worktree::git `worktree remove --force` plus purge_build/dir_size tree walks under the lock (worktree.rs:360-366). Fix: route worktree::git and validate_branch_name through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Move Stage, Unstage, BranchCreate, BranchDelete, CleanMerged, RestoreHead, PrOpen and WorktreeRemove to register_staged, with the subprocess and gix walks in prepare. In the finish step, branches_for should only read session owners. For session.update's rename, run check-ref-format in prepare and either bound `branch -m` or stage the whole op.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what is claimed.
- worktree.rs:26-33 `git()` is `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()`. There is no deadline and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, and `git_mutate` (line 36) just passes through.
- Every handler named is a plain `e.register`, and nothing re-registers any of them: git.rs:345 BranchCreate, 445 BranchDelete, 490 Stage, 507 Unstage, 693 CleanMerged; file.rs:253 RestoreHead; session.rs:1431 Update.
- engine.rs dispatch_inner takes `self.store.lock()` and opens the transaction before calling the handler, and holds both until commit. Store::lock (store.rs:474) is a plain std Mutex with no deadline. LockSpan only logs a warning past 16 ms.
- git.commit's finish (git.rs:571) runs `git commit --no-verify` inside the transaction.
- D144 (DECISIONS.md:729), proc.rs:3-6 and CLAUDE.md all require output_with_timeout. The bounded pattern exists: run_switch (git.rs:1347) and worktree::create (worktree.rs:212) use a 120 s deadline with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
- The authors' own comment at session.rs:854-856 says checkout "can invoke slow network/LFS filters. None of it belongs under the global store mutex".

Scratch-repo check (isolated config, a filter that sleeps 1 s):
- `git add --` took 1.0 s (clean filter).
- `git reset HEAD --` (unstage) took 1.0 s; its index refresh re-runs the clean filter.
- `git checkout --` took 1.0 s (smudge filter).
- `git switch -c b side` took 2.0 s (clean and smudge).
- `git switch -c b` with no start point took 1 ms.
- `commit --no-verify` still ran prepare-commit-msg and post-commit.
So whatever a filter costs is spent while holding the store lock.

(b) Reachable in normal use, by the user and by agents.
- The UI's "Stage all changes" (code_git.rs:470-484), the "Create branch" popover (always `checkout: true`, optional `start_point`, code_git.rs:1033-1037), commit, Restore and Open PR are ordinary actions.
- Agents can call stage, unstage, commit and pr.open.
- On a small fixture these ops hold the lock 4-8 ms (perf BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:344-377), so plain code repos barely notice.
- In the LFS/Unreal repos this app targets (worktree.rs:84 and :415, client.rs:68), staging or restoring assets and creating a branch from a start point run git-lfs clean or smudge. That means hashing multi-GB assets and possibly downloading them, so holds of seconds to minutes in normal flows.
- An askpass or credential GUI, a pinentry or signing approval, or a hung filter makes the hold unbounded.

(c) Consequence: every other connection queues on the mutex.
- Agents stall at their next tool call: every agent's PreToolUse `guardrail.gate` waits (claude_pre_tool has no deadline; the Claude hook timeout is 30 s, hooks.rs:351).
- MCP calls, lifecycle requests on their own connection, the phone door and background store writes also wait.
- The UI client gives up after 30 s with "outcome unknown" while the engine keeps holding the lock.
- Typing in terminals is unaffected (each pane has its own connection, terminal.rs:476, plus D148's in-memory path), and the GTK thread stays responsive because calls are async.

(d) High is right: this is "a freeze of the bus" in normal flows for the target repos. It is not critical, because in the common case the freeze ends when the child exits; an indefinite freeze needs a stuck prompt or helper.

(e) The proposed fix is right in direction: stage the work off the lock and keep a deadline as a backstop. It is incomplete in places and risky as worded; see the correction.
v2.correction:
1) Missing instances of the same root cause:
- git.pr.open (git.rs:666-680) runs `gh pr create` through a bare `.output()` under the lock. That is a network call on every use, in any repo, and the clearest instance.
- worktree.remove (git.rs:129-143, into worktree.rs:352-369) runs purge_build, dir_size tree walks, `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune` under the lock. session.close and project.remove deliberately keep this same disk work off the lock (workspace.rs:320-324: "seconds of disk work per agent").
- integration.discard (integration.rs:58-64) runs the same worktree::remove plus `git branch -D` under the lock.
- When guardrail.confirm replays a held git.commit, the whole commit prepare runs inside the confirming transaction (engine.rs:325-345). That includes the user's own pre-commit hook through a bare `.output()` (hooks.rs:210-212). D149 accepts the cost, but it is unbounded.

2) Precision:
- The ops that actually carry the impact are stage, unstage, restore_head, branch.create with a start point, commit's finish (signing, hooks), pr.open, worktree.remove / integration.discard, and branches_for's full-history walk in branch.delete and clean_merged.
- validate_branch_name's check-ref-format and `git branch -d` / `-m` touch refs only and are practically never slow. They break the D144 rule but carry no real cost.
- In session worktrees, core.hooksPath points at a Relay directory that holds only pre-commit (hooks.rs:98-153). So the user's prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hooks only run in checkouts without it, such as the primary. Commit signing applies everywhere.
- "Freezes the UI" should read "stalls the UI's data and actions". The window and keystrokes stay live, and the UI's main socket already serves its requests strictly in order (socket.rs handle_conn awaits each dispatch).

3) Fix caveats:
- (a) One fixed deadline inside worktree::git would also kill long callers that already run off the lock: git.push's prepare (git.rs:617), the integration worker's `git merge` (integration.rs:128), the device-sync `git fetch` (device.rs:1575), and `git worktree remove` inside session.close's prepare. Use a deadline per call site, or a bounded variant only for callers inside the transaction.
- (b) output_with_timeout kills the process group with SIGKILL. A timeout during add, reset, checkout, switch or commit therefore leaves .git/index.lock behind, and every later git command in that checkout fails until the user deletes it. Moving the work off the lock is the real fix; the deadline should be a generous backstop, ideally sending SIGTERM first so git can remove its lock.
- (c) GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 does not stop GIT_ASKPASS or SSH_ASKPASS dialogs, or gpg/ssh signing prompts. Only the deadline bounds those.
- (d) git.commit cannot move its commit into prepare: the gate-plus-commit atomicity and the confirm replay both depend on finish. Bound it in finish instead.
- (e) For session.update, keep `git branch -m` in finish with a deadline. Moving it to prepare means a later failure in finish would leave the git branch renamed while the session row still has the old name.

Side note, a separate issue I did not verify: because the per-worktree hooksPath directory contains only pre-commit, git-lfs's pre-push, post-checkout, post-commit and post-merge hooks never run in session worktrees. A push from a session worktree would then send LFS pointer files without uploading the objects they point to.

findings.title: git.commit gates a numstat computed before the lock, then commits whatever the index holds at commit time
findings.evidence: Prepare (unlocked): `let numstat = staged_numstat(&root)?; Ok((project, root, numstat))` (git.rs:557-558). Finish (locked): `super::guardrail::enforce(ctx, project.id, &root, GateKind::Commit, None, None, Some(&numstat), None)?;` then `worktree::git_mutate(&root, &["commit", "--no-verify", "-m", &p.message])` (git.rs:561-572). evaluate_commit uses the diff it is handed and does not read the index: `let numstat = match request.diff { Some(diff) => diff.to_string(), None => git_output(… ["diff", "--cached", "--numstat"])? }` (guardrail.rs:758-761). `--no-verify` skips Relay's own pre-commit gate (hooks.rs:129-132). So nothing re-reads the index between the gate and the commit. The window includes the whole wait for the store lock.
findings.impact: Anything staged in that checkout between prepare and finish is committed without being counted against caps or protected_paths. Two realistic sources: a second builder sharing the worktree (PAIR and review groups share one checkout, session.rs:759-781), or the same agent issuing a parallel `git add` tool call (`git add` is an exec, gated only by denied_commands). For example, the gate approves 3 files, the commit contains 60 including a protected path, and no hold or refusal is recorded.
findings.fix: Freeze what is judged. In prepare, run `git write-tree` (bounded) and compute numstat between HEAD and that tree. In finish, gate that numstat and create the commit from exactly that tree: `git commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD` plus `git update-ref HEAD <new> <old>`. At minimum, re-run `git write-tree` in finish and refuse with a conflict if it differs from the prepared tree. Freezing the tree also lets the commit itself leave the locked phase.

v1.reason: The code does what the finding says. git.rs:557 computes `staged_numstat(&root)` in the unlocked prepare. Finish (git.rs:561-572) passes that string to `guardrail::enforce(..., Some(&numstat), ...)`, and evaluate_commit (guardrail.rs:758-761) uses `request.diff` without reading the index again. Finish then runs `git commit --no-verify`, which commits whatever the index holds at that moment. The check and the commit are a real TOCTOU pair, and the window includes the wait for the store lock. Two things limit the impact. First, the window is normally milliseconds; it is long only when another op holds the lock (see #2). Second, this is not a meaningful guardrail escape. The default denied_commands (settings.rs:33) are `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd` and `git push --force`, so an agent that wants to beat caps or protected_paths can simply run `git commit --no-verify` in its own shell, and nothing gates that. The same race also exists on the ordinary shell-commit path: Relay's pre-commit hook gates with diff=None and reads the index while another process can still stage. What remains is an accidental case: a co-worker in a shared PAIR checkout stages files inside the window, and they are committed without being counted.
v1.correction: Re-rate from security/high to concurrency/low, because the cap gate can already be skipped with `git commit --no-verify` from an agent shell. That bypass is the larger guardrail gap and deserves its own finding. If this race is fixed anyway, the cheap fix is enough: in prepare, record `git write-tree`; in finish, run it again and refuse with a conflict if the tree changed. A tree computed this way could also be committed with commit-tree + update-ref.

findings.title: worktree.remove and integration.discard delete checkouts (tree walks, rm -rf of build output, git worktree remove) inside the transaction
findings.evidence:
git.rs:129-144 registers WorktreeRemove with plain `register` and calls `worktree::remove(repo, Path::new(&want), p.purge_build.unwrap_or(true))`. integration.rs:58-65 (IntegrationDiscard, also plain) calls `worktree::remove(…, true)` and then `git_mutate(["branch", "-D", …])`. worktree::remove (worktree.rs:352-370) does, in order:
1. purge_build: `dir_size(&p)` + `remove_dir_all` over target/, build/, .gradle, node_modules/.cache and dist (worktree.rs:339-349).
2. `dir_size(path)` over the whole checkout.
3. `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune` through the timeout-less `git()` helper.
session.close does the same work in its unlocked prepare and says so: "Removing the checkout stops the child first, with the store unlocked" (session.rs:1543-1546). project.remove defers it to after_commit (workspace.rs:330-345).
findings.impact: Removing a worktree, or discarding an integration (which ran build_cmd, so it has build output), from the CLI or phone holds the global lock for the whole deletion. For multi-GB target/ trees that is seconds to minutes (the "73GB problem" named at worktree.rs:11). Every agent hook and UI request waits for it.
findings.fix: Register both as staged. Read the owner/integration row and project path in a short ctx.read. Run worktree::remove (and `branch -D`) in prepare. Record the state change and events in finish. This is the same split session.close already uses.

v1.reason:
WorktreeRemove is a plain register (git.rs:129-144) that calls `worktree::remove(repo, ..., p.purge_build.unwrap_or(true))`. IntegrationDiscard (integration.rs:58-68, plain) calls `worktree::remove(..., true)` and then `git_mutate(["branch","-D",...])`. worktree::remove (worktree.rs:352-370) runs these steps, all with the store mutex held:
1. purge_build, which does dir_size plus remove_dir_all over the build dirs (worktree.rs:339-349).
2. dir_size over the whole checkout.
3. `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune`.

The git calls go through the `git()` helper (worktree.rs:26-33), which is plain `Command::output()` with no timeout. That breaks the output_with_timeout rule too. Both ops are Actors::UserOnly (relay-bus ops/git.rs:15-16, 145-146), and apps/relay-native never sends either op string, so the trigger is the CLI, the user's MCP/bus clients, or the phone. findings.title: Bounded but slow subprocesses still run inside the transaction: the guardrail commit gate, device.run's adb probe, provider.refresh
findings.evidence:
guardrail.gate is a plain `register` (handlers/guardrail.rs:304). Relay's pre-commit hook sends only `{"session":…,"kind":"commit"}` with no diff (hooks.rs:129-130). For that request, evaluate_commit runs `git_output(request.worktree, &["diff", "--cached", "--numstat"])` (guardrail.rs:760). The code says so itself: "Both git probes here run with the store lock held, so they get a deadline (D144)" (guardrail.rs:1119-1120, 10 s). Destructive writes also run `git status --porcelain …` via recoverable() (guardrail.rs:670-679), which the guardrail.check/explain queries can reach too.
device.run (plain, device.rs:140) calls require_device → `adb devices -l` with a 2 s deadline inside the transaction (device.rs:152). The comment at device.rs:574-576 says "This runs inside the request transaction".
provider.refresh (plain, provider.rs:18-19) runs four probes in the transaction: `claude --version`, `claude auth status`, `codex --version` and `codex login status`, each with a 3 s deadline (providers.rs:320-331, 358-360). provider.update's completion runs the same refresh inside system_write (provider_updates.rs:61-62).
D149: slow work runs outside the transaction, "not merely with a timeout".
findings.impact: Every agent `git commit` holds the global lock for a full staged diff: typically tens of ms, up to 10 s for large staged changes. That is far over the 16 ms LOCK_BUDGET (engine.rs:71), and it stalls every other agent's gates and the UI on each commit. device.run blocks the bus for up to 2 s whenever the adb server is cold. provider.refresh blocks it for up to about 3 s.
findings.fix:
Split each into a prepare phase that runs unlocked:
- guardrail.gate (and the check/explain queries): compute numstat and recoverable status in prepare from the session's worktree; only evaluate and insert holds in finish.
- device.run: call require_device in prepare.
- provider.refresh: probe in prepare and write provider_cache in finish.
- provider.update's worker: probe before calling system_write.

v1.reason: guardrail.gate is a plain register (handlers/guardrail.rs:304). Relay's pre-commit hook sends only `{"session":...,"kind":"commit"}` (hooks.rs:129-130), so evaluate_commit takes the `None` branch. That branch runs `git_output(worktree, ["diff","--cached","--numstat"])` (guardrail.rs:760) under the transaction, and the comment at guardrail.rs:1119 admits it: "Both git probes here run with the store lock held, so they get a deadline (D144)" (10 s). recoverable() (guardrail.rs:671-679) runs `git status --porcelain` the same way. device.run (device.rs:140, plain register) calls require_device, which runs `adb devices -l` with a 2 s deadline in the transaction; device.rs:574-576 says "This runs inside the request transaction". provider.refresh (provider.rs:18, plain register) calls providers::refresh(ctx.tx()), which runs `--version` and the auth probe for both CLIs in parallel threads, each with a 3 s deadline (providers.rs:320-331, 358). provider_updates.rs:61-62 also runs refresh inside system_write. Impact by site:
- Commit gate: the one with ongoing cost. It costs a git process spawn plus the staged diff on every agent `git commit`, usually tens of ms, and stalls other gates and UI ops for that time.

findings.title: session.brief and every launch compute git divergence (gix open plus unbounded rev-walks) while holding the store lock
findings.evidence:
awareness::brief calls `crate::handlers::git::briefing_state(Path::new(&session.worktree), &session.branch, &project.2)` (awareness.rs:211-215). briefing_state runs `gix::open` and up to three divergence() walks, each `repo.rev_walk([from]).with_hidden([hidden]).all()…try_fold` (git.rs:922-935, 1018-1033). The three walks are branch vs upstream, base vs its upstream, and branch vs base.
brief() is reached two ways:
- session.brief, a plain `register` query (session.rs:1124-1129), so it runs inside the transaction.
- plan_launch (session.rs:451), which runs inside `ctx.read(|conn| { … plan_launch(conn, engine, row, kind) })` in stage_launch (session.rs:604-609). plan_launch also calls guardrail::write_roots, which does another gix::open (guardrail.rs:607).
Unlocked::read's own contract (engine.rs:171-172): "Keep the closure to plain queries: whatever runs in here is back on the one global lock".
findings.impact: The cost grows with history. new_worktree_base (git.rs:978-1014) bases new worktrees on origin/<base> whenever it is ahead, so a local base branch nobody pulls falls further behind origin with every fetch. Each brief or launch then walks every commit in between (thousands in an active repo), several times, under the global lock.
