Also unused: Instance::from_env (paths.rs:15; it defaults to Stable while the native client defaults to dev), time::now_ts (time.rs:9), Store::size_mb (store.rs:488), Event::in_project (envelope.rs:250), OpMeta::is_mutation (registry.rs:181), OpEntry::namespace (registry.rs:224), and about 19 KEYCODE_*/META_* consts (mirror.rs:362-396) whose values the native client hard-codes again (mirror/input.rs:92-115).
findings.impact: The dead API invites reuse of a helper that breaks an invariant. An engine run from an installed binary (deploy/relay-remote.service runs ~/.cargo/bin/relay) has no way to locate the scrcpy jar once the source tree moves.
findings.fix: Delete the unused helpers. Wire configure_mirror_server to an environment variable or CLI flag, or delete it too.

v1.reason: rg over all Rust sources finds no callers for list_with_owners (git.rs:72; it takes a &Transaction and runs `git worktree list` through worktrees_owned_by, which is the D144 trap the comment at git.rs:62-63 warns about), configure_mirror_server (device.rs:56), Instance::from_env (paths.rs:15), time::now_ts, Store::size_mb, Event::in_project, OpMeta::is_mutation or OpEntry::namespace. Because nothing sets MIRROR_SERVER, mirror_server_path (device.rs:62-67) always falls back to the compile-time `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../../apps/relay-native/resources/scrcpy-server-v4.1`. About 17 of the KEYCODE_*/META_* consts in mirror.rs:359-396 appear only in their own definition. KEYCODE_HOME/BACK/POWER/VOLUME_*/APP_SWITCH/WAKEUP/VOLUME_MUTE and META_NONE/CTRL_ON are used by mirror.rs or its tests.
v1.correction: The native client does not depend on relay-core (its Cargo.toml has no relay-core entry), so it cannot reuse the KEYCODE consts. That part is cross-crate duplication, not something to fix by calling the existing consts. The mirror-jar point is a real side effect worth keeping. An engine installed with `cargo install --path` from a Relay worktree (for example .relay/worktrees/<name>) bakes that worktree's path into the binary, and mirroring stops with 'no scrcpy server' once the worktree is removed. Either wire configure_mirror_server to an env var or flag, or install the jar under XDG data, and delete the other unused helpers, starting with list_with_owners.

findings.title: Stub functions and consts that exist only to silence unused-import warnings
findings.evidence: `#[allow(dead_code)] fn _ctx_used(_: &Ctx, _: Empty) {}` and `const _CALLABLE_USED: Callable = Callable::Yes;` (bus.rs:117-121; Callable is already used at line 82). Also `fn _ctx(_: &Ctx) {}` (app.rs:287-288; Ctx is already used at line 72), `const _ACTORS_USED: Actors = Actors::All;` (ops/bus.rs:58-59) and `fn _touch(_: Value) {}` (ops/app.rs:62-63).
findings.impact: Dead code whose only job is to keep the compiler from reporting genuinely unused imports.
findings.fix: Delete the stubs and any imports that only they use.

v1.reason: handlers/bus.rs:117-121 holds `fn _ctx_used(_: &Ctx, _: Empty)` and `const _CALLABLE_USED`. Ctx and Empty are imported at lines 4 and 10 and used nowhere else in the file; Callable is genuinely used at line 82. handlers/app.rs:287-288 holds `fn _ctx(_: &Ctx)`, though Ctx is already used at lines 72 and 88. ops/bus.rs:58-59 holds `const _ACTORS_USED: Actors`, and Actors is otherwise unused there (line 2 import only). ops/app.rs:62-63 holds `fn _touch(_: Value)`, and Value is otherwise unused (line 5 import only).
v1.correction: Deleting the stubs also means removing the imports that only the stubs keep alive: Ctx and Empty in handlers/bus.rs, Actors in ops/bus.rs, and Value in ops/app.rs. _CALLABLE_USED and app.rs `_ctx` are pure dead code, since their types are used elsewhere.

findings.title: Leftovers from the Tauri door: Door::Tauri is never constructed and Doors::TauriOnly is never used
findings.evidence: Production code constructs only Door::Socket (socket.rs) and Door::InProcess (socket.rs:927, provider_updates.rs:221); Door::Tauri appears only in tests (tests/bus.rs:108,114,220). It is still handled at engine.rs:785, 822 and 1356. No op uses `.doors(Doors::TauriOnly)` (registry.rs:85), yet mcp.rs:161 filters on it. Instance::bundle_id, documented as "The Tauri bundle identifier" (paths.rs:37-44), is unused, and relay-bus lib.rs:4 still names Tauri as a door.
findings.impact: Door-rule branches (the mail-hint skip, the door/doors mismatch check, and agent refusal on Door::Tauri) can never run in production. Anyone reasoning about how doors are enforced has to read and maintain them, and the docs still describe a door that no longer exists.
findings.fix: Remove the variants and their branches, and update the docs.

v1.reason: `Door::Tauri` (engine.rs:32) is never built in production code. Every non-test dispatch uses `Door::Socket` (socket.rs:459-742, engine.rs:764) or `Door::InProcess` (socket.rs:927, provider_updates.rs:221, examples/perf.rs). `Door::Tauri` appears only in tests/bus.rs:108, 114 and 220. Neither relay-native nor relay-remote references it. No op sets `Doors::TauriOnly` (registry.rs:85), yet mcp.rs:161 still filters on it. `Instance::bundle_id` (paths.rs:38) has no callers. The branches at engine.rs:785, 822 (the TauriOnly/Socket arm) and 1356 cannot fire in production.
v1.correction: These branches are exercised by tests (tests/bus.rs:107-114, and the mirror test at :220), so removing the variant means rewriting those tests: the mirror test can use InProcess, and the door-rule tests should be deleted. Stale Tauri wording also appears in comments at serve.rs:1, relay-core lib.rs:2, relay-bus lib.rs:3, envelope.rs:261/267 and ops/device.rs:15. Docs drift belongs in the same cleanup.

findings.title: 55 CSS classes in theme.css match no widget
findings.evidence: No Rust file in relay-native sets these classes; the only file that mentions each one is theme.css. Whole families are dead: document-* (251-272, 454-456; superseded by notes-* in 6bbd432), skills-* (200-226, 386, 395, 491-492; superseded by ext-* in 280ae4b), code-step-*, code-publish-step, code-git-section, code-section-heading and code-file-name (280-282, 398-402), plan-* (269, 423, 459-460), task-preview, task-open, task-tags, task-type and task-priority (98, 238-241, 435), notes-app-*, notes-workspace, notes-window-chrome, session-identity, session-lane, board-lens, layout-menu, files-label, wall-files-heading and plugins-content.
findings.impact: Roughly 60 dead rules sit beside the live ones in the main stylesheet. Anyone restyling a page has to work out which rules still apply, and the dead selectors can be mistaken for the live notes-*/ext-* designs.
findings.fix: Delete the rules.

v1.reason: I extracted every class selector from theme.css (283) and searched each one as a fixed string in all other relay-native sources, including css/*.css. About 65 appear nowhere but theme.css. These include the whole document-*, skills-*, code-step-*/code-git-section/code-publish-step/code-section-heading/code-file-name and plan-* families, task-preview/open/tags/type/priority, notes-app-*, notes-workspace, notes-window-chrome, session-identity, session-lane, board-lens, layout-menu, files-label, wall-files-heading and plugins-content. I also checked the dynamically built class names (status-{}, priority-{}, state-{}, label-hue-{}, lane-{column}). None of them produce the dead names (board_view uses priority-{p}, not task-priority).
v1.correction: The dead set is slightly larger than listed. It also includes plugin-card, plugin-section, skill-pick, skill-switch, note-draft, project-branch and lane-heading (lane-{column} uses board column ids). Deleting them is safe, but the payoff is maintainability only.

findings.title: Engine names hard-coded in the native client have drifted: git.worktree.create, device.sdk_missing and the missing workspace.deleted subscription
findings.evidence: request_timeout matches `"session.create" | "git.worktree.create" | "task.dispatch" => 180 s` (69), but the op is named worktree.create (ops/git.rs:11). phone_error maps `Some("device.sdk_missing")` (agent_menu.rs:91), a code the engine never produces; it uses avd.sdk_missing (device.rs:435). The subscription list (app.rs:1154) omits workspace.deleted, which workspace.remove emits (workspace.rs:179), although the dispatcher refreshes the registry on any `workspace.` event (app.rs:1223).
findings.impact: These are dead match arms. When an empty workspace is removed from the CLI, the native sidebar keeps showing it until some other registry event arrives.
findings.fix: Correct the names, and keep op, event and error-code names as shared consts in relay-bus.

v1.reason: client.rs:69 matches "git.worktree.create", but the op is registered as "worktree.create" (relay-bus/src/ops/git.rs:11), and relay-native never calls either name, so the arm is dead. agent_menu.rs:91 maps "device.sdk_missing". The engine produces "avd.sdk_missing" (device.rs:435) and "device.adb_missing" (device.rs:565/570), but never "device.sdk_missing". The bus.subscribe list at app.rs:1154 has workspace.changed but not workspace.deleted, and socket.rs:207 filters on exact names, `prefix.*` or `*`. workspace.remove emits only workspace.deleted (workspace.rs:179) when the workspace has no projects. When it has projects, the project.deleted events (subscribed) still trigger a refresh. So an empty workspace removed from the CLI or by another client stays in this window's sidebar. When the native client removes it itself (shell/registry.rs:622), the caller presumably refreshes.
v1.correction: The stale sidebar only happens when an empty workspace is removed by another door (CLI or a second window). Removing a workspace that has projects still refreshes through project.deleted. The git.worktree.create arm has no effect today because the native client never sends worktree.create. Fix: subscribe to workspace.deleted (or `workspace.*`), use "avd.sdk_missing", and drop or rename the timeout arm.

findings.title: Relative-time formatting is implemented six times, with output that differs between panels
findings.evidence: The copies are guardrail_pages.rs:39-50 ("just now" under 45 s, rounded "N min ago" and "N h ago"), session_context.rs:27-52 (truncated minutes, "yesterday"), board_view.rs:143-163 ("now", "5m", "3h"; truncates the timestamp to 19 chars and appends Z), status_usage.rs:110-117 ("Nm ago"), note_pages.rs:208-219, and device_lease.rs:295-301 in core. Reset spans are also formatted twice (usage.rs:168-177 and status_usage.rs:119-131).
findings.impact: The same timestamp reads differently depending on the panel. For example, 90 minutes is "2 h ago" in the guardrail tray, "1 h ago" in the session context, "1h" on the board and "1h ago" in usage.
findings.fix: Use one helper in app.rs.

v1.reason: Three prose-style 'N ago' helpers in relay-native disagree. guardrail_pages.rs:39 rounds ((s+30)/60 min, (s+1800)/3600 h, so 90 min shows "2 h ago"). session_context.rs:27 truncates ("1 h ago") and adds "yesterday" and dates. status_usage.rs:110 truncates and is compact ("1h ago"). This is real, already-diverged duplication with visible inconsistency, but it is cosmetic. Several of the other cited locations are not the same helper. note_pages.rs:208 fmt_date is an absolute date/time formatter, not relative time. board_view.rs:143 is deliberately compact ("5m", "3h") for card chrome. device_lease.rs:295 is a core-side elapsed-duration formatter ("3m 12s") in a different crate with no glib.
v1.correction: Narrow the finding to guardrail_pages.rs:39, session_context.rs:27 and status_usage.rs:110, which could share one rounding rule and one helper (session_context::relative_time is the most complete). Leave board_view's compact form, fmt_date and core's device_lease/usage formatters out. The reset span duplicated between usage.rs:168 (core) and status_usage.rs:119 (native) crosses crates. The only consolidation there is for the native client to show the engine's label, so it is minor.

findings.title: The MCP stdio server plumbing is copied three times (mcp.rs, unreal.rs, blender.rs)
findings.evidence: FALLBACK_PROTOCOL and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS are defined three times (mcp.rs:13-14, unreal.rs:22-23, blender.rs:19-20). The serve loops are identical (unreal.rs:57-76, blender.rs:34-52, mcp.rs:16-33), and so is the initialize/ping/tools.call dispatch (unreal.rs:78-110, blender.rs:54-89, mcp.rs:36-74). mcp.rs keeps its own copy of rpc_error (214-218), identical to unreal.rs:1899-1905.
findings.impact: Any protocol-version or error-shape change has to be made in three places.
findings.fix: Write one generic stdio server parameterised by server info, tools() and call().

v1.reason: FALLBACK_PROTOCOL and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS are defined identically at mcp.rs:13-14, unreal.rs:22-23 and blender.rs:18-19. `serve()` and `handle()` in unreal.rs (57-110) and blender.rs (33-86) match line for line, apart from serverInfo/instructions. The initialize/ping/error branches in mcp.rs:36-74 repeat the same logic. mcp.rs:214 is a private copy of `rpc_error`, identical to the `pub(crate)` one at unreal.rs:1899.
v1.correction: blender.rs already imports `rpc_error`, `tool` and `tool_result` from unreal.rs (line 10), so the triple copy covers only the protocol constants and the initialize/dispatch skeleton. mcp.rs cannot drop straight into a generic sync server: its serve/handle are async, carry an actor and token, add the `exposed()` check and wrap errors as -32603 transport errors. Practical fix: one sync serve/handle shared by unreal and blender, parameterised by server info, tools() and call(). mcp.rs then reuses the shared constants, the initialize response builder and rpc_error. No divergence exists yet, so the cost is maintenance only.

findings.title: SKILL.md front-matter parsing is implemented three times, with different edge cases
findings.evidence: plugins::frontmatter is public (plugins.rs:162-178), yet github::frontmatter_name (github.rs:218-229) re-implements it: it trims indentation, truncates to 120 chars and skips empty values. Native tools_skills::description (tools_skills.rs:53-74) is a third copy that accepts leading blank lines.
findings.impact: The same SKILL.md can produce a different name or description depending on which path reads it.
findings.fix: Have github.rs call plugins::frontmatter.

v1.reason: The three helpers are small and serve different needs, and the claimed impact does not occur. github::frontmatter_name (github.rs:218) reads only the `name` of a skill downloaded at install time (github.rs:176). It deliberately skips an empty value, so the directory-name fallback applies, and it caps the name at 120 chars. plugins::frontmatter returns Some("") for an empty value and has no cap, so the proposed fix ("have github.rs call plugins::frontmatter") would drop both behaviours unless wrapped. plugins::frontmatter reads Relay's own bundled plugin skills, a separate set of files, so no single SKILL.md has its name extracted by two different paths. The native copy (tools_skills.rs:54) is a display helper that falls back to the first prose line. relay-native does not depend on relay-core (its Cargo.toml has no relay-core entry), so it could not call plugins::frontmatter anyway. The payoff is about 10 lines with no realistic user-visible divergence.

findings.title: Layer-3 authorization logic is duplicated between authorize() and callability()
findings.evidence: authorize (guardrail.rs:350-384) and callability (413-438) each restate the guardrail.request exception, the role allowlist, the bus_writes op set (`starts_with("file.") || matches!(…"git.stage" | "git.unstage" | "git.commit")`, lines 363 and 422) and the ui./os. allow_ui set. D104 calls callability "the single source".
findings.impact: An escape hatch added to only one of them makes discovery (bus.ops, the MCP tool list) and enforcement disagree again, which is the bug D104 fixed.
findings.fix: Use one function that returns (allowed, why) for both callers.

v1.reason: In guardrail.rs, `authorize` (lines 353-384) and `callability` (lines 409-438) each restate the layer-3 logic: the `grants::OP` exception, the role allowlist (authorize inlines `role_allowlist(...).iter().any(op_matches)`, which is exactly `role_admits` at line 451), the bus_write set (`starts_with("file.") || matches!(…"git.stage" | "git.unstage" | "git.commit")`, lines 363 and 422) and the `ui.`/`os.` allow_ui set. D104 (DECISIONS.md:477) describes `callability` as the single source so that discovery and enforcement cannot disagree, yet enforcement keeps its own copy. The two copies agree today.
v1.correction: Enforcement (authorize) stays authoritative, so a future divergence would make discovery (bus.ops, the MCP tool list, session.bootstrap) over- or under-promise; it would not bypass a guardrail. Fix: extract a single layer-3 helper that returns an enum such as Allowed(reason) / Denied{bus_write, ui}, called from both. authorize maps it to the BusError with its details and hint, and callability maps it to its why string. authorize should call `role_admits` rather than inlining it.

findings.title: adb_path treats an empty configured path as a missing adb, unlike its sibling readers
findings.evidence: sdk_tool and android_sdk_root filter with `.filter(|value| !value.is_empty())` (device.rs:399, 418) and fall back to discovery. adb_path (550-570) has no such filter and returns device.adb_missing "configured adb does not exist: ". All three read settings through raw SQL instead of settings::get.
findings.impact: `relay cmd settings.set '{"path":"device.adb_path","value":""}'` (clearing the override) breaks every device op even though adb is on PATH. The native settings page avoids this only because it sends null for empty fields.
findings.fix: Add the same filter, or share one helper between the three readers.

v1.reason: device.rs:550-570: adb_path parses the stored JSON string with no `.filter(|v| !v.is_empty())`, so a stored "" becomes PathBuf(""). `is_file()` is false, and it returns `device.adb_missing "configured adb does not exist: "` before it ever reaches `which::which("adb")`. sdk_tool (device.rs:397-399) and android_sdk_root (418) do filter empty values and fall back to discovery. The settings handler does not normalise "" to null. The native settings page avoids the problem only because tools_settings.rs:642-646 turns an empty Entry into `Value::Null`. `relay cmd settings.set` with value "" therefore breaks every adb-backed op: device.list (device.rs:33), mirror (46, 73, 151), and the adb fallback inside android_sdk_root (430).
v1.correction: The trigger needs a direct settings.set with "" (CLI or a script), because the native UI sends null, so low severity is correct. Fix: share one `configured_path(conn, key)` helper that filters empty strings and use it for all three readers. It could use settings::get, but the raw SQL is fine either way.

findings.title: User-only ops with no caller anywhere: file.import, file.restore_head and git.branch.clean_merged
findings.evidence: None of them is referenced by native, remote, CLI or tests, and agents are refused at layer 1. file.import (file.rs:262-297) recursively copies whole trees (copy, 612-627) inside the transaction and gates only the top-level entry. file.restore_head (253-261) runs git checkout under the lock. git.branch.clean_merged (git.rs:693-720) re-implements git.branch.delete's eligibility rules (445-489) and runs `git worktree list` plus one `git branch -d` per branch under the lock; it is superseded by the staged git.branch.cleanup.
findings.impact: They add maintenance surface, and when reached through `relay cmd` they hold the bus.
findings.fix: Delete them, or wire them to the UI with staged registration.

v1.reason: The claim of no caller in native, remote or CLI holds, and all three are UserOnly (ops/file.rs:32-37; BUS.md:449 lists clean_merged as user_only). Each also does slow work under the lock: RestoreHead runs `git checkout` (file.rs:253-261), Import recursively copies whole trees (file.rs:262-297, copy at 612-627), and CleanMerged runs list_with_dirty plus one `git branch -d` per branch (git.rs:693-720). However, the evidence is wrong that tests do not reference them: crates/relay-core/tests/phase8.rs:419 exercises git.branch.clean_merged, and examples/perf.rs:924, 977 and 981 benchmark all three. All three are also documented bus API in BUS.md:830, 851 and 852. file.import is the specced 'OS drag-in' and file.restore_head is the specced 'one-click answer to a post-hoc guardrail.violation' (§9.3), so they are unwired features rather than plainly dead code.
v1.correction: Narrow the finding. git.branch.clean_merged duplicates the newer git.branch.cleanup (branch_cleanup.rs, with a sweeper started in serve.rs:35) using simpler eligibility rules that have already diverged. Retiring it, or making it an alias of cleanup, is the real cleanup. For file.import and file.restore_head, the actionable point is that if they are wired into the UI as BUS.md intends, they must be registered staged or unlocked, because they copy trees and run git under the store lock. Deleting them would drop documented features.

findings.title: Smoke-test helpers are copied verbatim into five native modules
findings.evidence: An identical recursive `fn named(root, name)` appears in smoke.rs:11, smoke_notes.rs:8, smoke_registry.rs:7, smoke_project_files.rs:8 and roadmap_smoke.rs:9. wait_for and require are also duplicated between smoke_notes.rs:22-31 and smoke_project_files.rs:22-29.
findings.impact: Every fix to the harness has to be applied five times.
findings.fix: Move them into a shared smoke_util module.

v1.reason: The same 13-line recursive `fn named(root: &impl IsA<gtk::Widget>, name: &str)` appears at smoke.rs:11, smoke_notes.rs:8, smoke_registry.rs:7, smoke_project_files.rs:8 and roadmap_smoke.rs:9. require is duplicated in smoke_notes.rs:31 and smoke_project_files.rs:22. wait_for is nearly duplicated in smoke_notes.rs:22 and smoke_project_files.rs:29. The project_files copy also prints PROJECT_WAIT/PROJECT_READY markers.
v1.correction: wait_for is not identical: the smoke_project_files copy prints progress markers, so a shared version needs an optional label/log hook. The payoff is modest because these are small, stable helpers in smoke-test code.

results.coverage: Lens: overengineering/design debt across relay-bus, relay-core, relay-cli, relay-remote and relay-native (relay-mobile not read). Searches used: trait definitions (`trait `) and `impl X for Y`; a brace-matching script listing every fn over ~100 lines (refresh_git 711, Ui::build 702, the handler `register` fns, socket handle_conn 481, show_launch 474, ...); `#[path]` modules and `impl Ui`/`impl Editor` spread; `Command::new("git")`, `.output()`, `.status()`, `wait_with_output` vs proc::output_with_timeout, cross-checked against register / register_unlocked / register_staged per handler; `invoke_registered` / `replay_registered` callers; glob and pattern matchers (`strip_suffix(".*")`, glob_match, op_matches, Filter); shell tokenizers (guardrail shell_commands, device_lease split_commands); skip-dir lists (`"node_modules"`); hand-written enum/string fns (`fn *_str`, `parse_*`) and SQL state literals; every settings default key against its readers; Door/Doors/Executor/ui_connected/bundle_id; the ui.* handlers against native apply_ui_event and layout keys; Driver trait uses and spawn_profile consumers; the three MCP servers; native JSON key lookups against keys the engine produces (no drift beyond Page and a dead `pct` fallback). Throwaway experiments in scratchpad/exp: glob.py (ported glob_match vs a reference regex; 4490 disagreements), denied.py (ported denied-command matcher on common spellings), ops.py (registry ops with no handler: only project.stats), undo.py (Undo::Inverse metadata vs set_undo calls: consistent, no finding). Checked and not reported as too minor or not diverged: watch::Defer has two impls but all four callers pass Unlocked; usage.rs SaturatingSubF64 is a one-call trait; lib.rs hex(); serve.rs and remote.rs repeat the run-until-quit/sigterm block; socket.rs bind returns the same AlreadyRunning error from both probe branches; five native relative-time formatters print differently; guardrail authorize() and callability() duplicate the allowlist predicates without functional divergence; overlap.rs uses gix status where worktree.rs moved to the git CLI to avoid LFS rehashing; smoke harness (~2,150 lines) ships in the native binary behind env vars; native socket path logic duplicates paths.rs. Not finished: the long native UI builders (show_launch, task_pages::detail, tools::dashboard, tools_settings::refresh, note_pages/doc build, board_view mount) were skimmed for duplicated business logic, not read line by line; relay-remote (bridge/direct/tunnel/rendezvous/pairing) only checked for structure and duplication; awareness.rs brief/bootstrap overlap, store migrations, the native mirror decode pipeline and audit/recovery were not examined in depth. Nothing was compiled or run (GTK client cannot be built here); the GTK-visible effects in the refresh_git finding are inferred from the code, hence medium confidence.

findings.title: invoke_registered runs a staged op's slow prepare phase inside the caller's open transaction (held-commit confirm, task.dispatch), undoing D149
findings.evidence: engine.rs:324-356: "A staged op reached this way — `guardrail.confirm` replaying a held `git.commit` — has no read/external phase behind it, so run it here, against the transaction already open. It costs what the op cost before the split, and only on this path." then `let staged = match self.engine.prepares.get(entry.name).cloned() { Some(prepare) => { let mut stage = Unlocked { ..., held: Some(self.tx), ... }; let out = prepare(&mut stage, &payload)?;`. Callers that hold the store mutex (Engine::register): guardrail.rs:583 `confirm` -> `ctx.replay_registered(&frozen.op, ...)` replays git.commit, whose prepare (git.rs:535-558) runs `git add -A`, hooks::refresh_git and hooks::run_user_pre_commit, the latter `Command::new(&hook).current_dir(worktree).output()` with no timeout (hooks.rs:210). git.rs:530-534 itself says a slow pre-commit "used to hold the one store connection for its whole run, so every keystroke in every terminal waited on it". Also task.rs:683 (task.dispatch, Engine::register at task.rs:1049) -> invoke_registered("session.create"), whose prepare (session.rs:833-893) calls refresh_new_worktree -> fetch_remote (`git fetch --all --prune`, 20 s, git.rs:969-971) and worktree::create (`git worktree add`, 120 s), under the comment "None of it belongs under the global store mutex"; task.rs:712 likewise runs session.spawn/wake/resume prepares (hook install, skill folder copies, brief files). So "only on this path" is not true.
findings.impact: The user commits more than 40 files / 2000 lines from Source Control (caps, settings.rs:31): refuse_or_user_hold gives the user actor a hold, the UI asks "Allow this held action once?" (code_git.rs:1722-1760) and guardrail.confirm runs the project's own pre-commit hook (lint/tests, unbounded; forever if it waits on stdin) with the global store mutex held — every agent's PreToolUse guardrail hook, every bus call and the UI stall until it ends. The pre-commit hook also runs twice (unlocked on the first attempt, locked on confirm). task.dispatch with a `create` payload (CLI/phone) freezes the bus for a network fetch plus a full worktree checkout per task, multiplied by fanout.
findings.fix: Make the composite ops staged as well: register guardrail.confirm and task.dispatch with register_staged and run the nested op's prepare from their own prepare phase (e.g. an Engine::prepare_nested(op, payload) whose result is handed to finish), or have invoke_registered refuse ops that have a prepare and queue them as separate requests after commit. Independently, run the user pre-commit hook through proc::output_with_timeout with stdin closed.

v1.reason: engine.rs:309-361: invoke_registered looks up `self.engine.prepares.get(entry.name)`. If the op has a prepare, it builds an `Unlocked { held: Some(self.tx), .. }` and runs `prepare(&mut stage, &payload)` inside the caller's open transaction. The comment at 325-327 claims this happens "only on this path", which is false. guardrail.confirm is registered with plain `engine.register::<Confirm>(confirm)` (guardrail.rs:339). confirm calls `ctx.replay_registered(&frozen.op, ..)` (guardrail.rs:583) for any frozen op other than guardrail.gate. git.commit's finish phase calls `super::guardrail::enforce` (git.rs:561), and on a Hold that function freezes `ctx.op`/`ctx.payload()`, i.e. git.commit (guardrail.rs:691). For Actor::User, refuse_or_user_hold (guardrail.rs:1028) turns cap and protected-path refusals into holds. The defaults are caps files 40 / lines 2000 (settings.rs:31). The UI's Source Control commit then offers "Allow this held action once?" and calls guardrail.confirm (code_git.rs:1726-1750). The replayed prepare (git.rs:536-558) runs `git add -A` (when all), hooks::refresh_git and hooks::run_user_pre_commit. That last one is `Command::new(&hook).current_dir(worktree).output()` with no timeout (hooks.rs:210-213), and here it runs with the store mutex held. git.rs:530-534 itself documents that this is what froze every terminal. task.dispatch is also plain `e.register::<Dispatch>` (task.rs:1049). It calls invoke_registered("session.create") (task.rs:683), whose staged prepare does refresh_new_worktree (fetch) and worktree::create, under a comment saying "None of it belongs under the global store mutex" (session.rs:853-855). It also calls invoke_registered("session.spawn"/"wake"/"resume") (task.rs:712), whose stage_launch writes hooks, skill folders and brief files, per the D149 comment at session.rs:915-916. The UI's task Dispatch button (task_pages.rs:652) sends `{task_id, session}` with start defaulting to true, so the spawn/wake prepare runs under the lock in a normal flow too. The pre-commit hook also runs twice: once unlocked on the first attempt, then again locked on confirm.
v1.correction: One part of the impact is wrong. `Command::output()` gives the child a null stdin, so a hook that reads stdin gets EOF; it does not hang "forever". What remains true is an unbounded wait for a slow hook (lint or tests) with the store mutex held. run_user_pre_commit also skips proc::output_with_timeout on the normal unlocked path, which breaks the CLAUDE.md subprocess rule separately. Other callers of invoke_registered need checking against the same pattern, since session.close is staged too: workspace.rs:173/239/328/349 (project.remove/add, session.close, device.run.stop) and audit.rs:68 (undo inverse). The proposed fix stands: make composite ops staged, or forbid prepare-bearing ops from invoke_registered, and run the user hook through output_with_timeout.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. dispatch_inner takes the store mutex at engine.rs:954 and opens the transaction before calling any handler registered with plain `register`. Inside that handler, invoke_registered (engine.rs:328-347) looks up `prepares.get(entry.name)`. If the op has one, it runs it with `held: Some(self.tx)`, so the slow phase of a staged op runs with the global lock held. guardrail.confirm (guardrail.rs:339) and task.dispatch (task.rs:1049) are both plain `register`. confirm replays the frozen git.commit (guardrail.rs:583). The git.commit prepare (git.rs:536-558) runs `git add -A`, refresh_git, run_user_pre_commit (`Command::new(&hook)...output()` with no timeout, hooks.rs:210) and staged_numstat. dispatch_task calls invoke_registered("session.create") at task.rs:683. That prepare (session.rs:833-893) runs list, `git fetch --all --prune` (20 s cap, git.rs:938-959), `git worktree add` (120 s cap, worktree.rs:214) and install_git. It also calls spawn/wake/resume at task.rs:712, which runs stage_launch -> prepare_launch (git hooks, provider adapters, skill folder copies, brief/role files). The claim "only on this path" (engine.rs:325-327 and :145-148, and D149 in DECISIONS.md:816-819) became false when session.create was staged in 6e7b044 and the launch ops in 853e635.

(b) How the trigger is reached:
- **Phone.** Every "New request" or Board dispatch sends task.dispatch with `create` and `start:true`. remote.rs:305-314 asserts this is the phone's exact payload. On any project without a "primary" plugin (default_checkout defaults to "new"), that means a fetch plus a full checkout plus the launch prepare under the lock. With fanout (CLI), this repeats for every child.
- **Desktop commit.** A Source Control commit over the default caps (40 files / 2000 lines, settings.rs:29) becomes a user hold through refuse_or_user_hold. code_git.rs:1722-1760 then asks "Allow this held action once?" and sends guardrail.confirm, which runs the prepare under the lock.
- **Desktop Dispatch button.** task_pages.rs:646-653, with start defaulting to true, nests a launch prepare only when the target session is created, parked or restorable. Sessions auto-park after 30 idle minutes, so this is common, but the hold is short.

(c) What happens while it runs:
- **Agents.** Every agent request blocks in check_session_token (engine.rs:1378), including every PreToolUse guardrail.gate. The Claude hook has a 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:351).
- **Desktop UI.** Its requests wait, and the client times them out after 30 s.
- **Duration.** The lock is held for seconds per phone dispatch, bounded by roughly 140 s. On a confirm it is unbounded: it lasts as long as the project's pre-commit hook. Even with no hook, staged_numstat re-opens the repo with gix twice and re-parses the index for every staged file, and it is heaviest exactly for over-cap commits.
- **Hook runs twice.** The user's hook runs once unlocked on the first attempt and again on confirm.
- **Unaffected.** No data is lost; everything resumes afterwards. Keystrokes are not blocked (D148 fast path, one connection per terminal pane at terminal.rs:476).

(d) High fits the rubric: this is a bus freeze in normal phone and commit flows. By the project's own standard (16 ms lock budget, "None of it belongs under the global store mutex" at session.rs:853-855), this is the exact problem D149 set out to fix. One mitigation: D149 explicitly accepts the confirm-path cost. What D149 did not accept, and what is new, is task.dispatch.

(e) The fix direction is right but incomplete; see correction.
v2.correction:
1. **"Undoing D149" overstates it.** Direct calls still run unlocked. D149 explicitly accepts the confirm path ("that path costs what it cost before the split, and only that path"). What is false is "only that path": task.dispatch reaches it, and so does project.remove with force through session.close (workspace.rs:328). That second case is minor: run_teardown does a few git config calls and file rewrites per session. audit.undo is unaffected because none of its inverse ops are staged.

2. **Keystrokes are not stalled.** The quoted git.rs:530-534 comment about keystrokes is out of date: D148 plus per-pane connections keep typing working. The UI window stays responsive; only its bus requests wait.

3. **Stdin cannot hang the hook.** "Forever if it waits on stdin" is wrong, because `Command::output()` gives the child a null stdin.

4. **The expensive variant comes from the phone and CLI, not the desktop.**
   - The phone sends task.dispatch with `create` and `start:true` (contract in crates/relay-remote/tests/remote.rs:305-314).
   - The desktop's New-agents flow calls session.create directly, then task.dispatch with `start:false` (launch.rs:810), so it avoids the fetch and checkout.
   - The desktop Dispatch button only nests a roughly 100 ms launch prepare, and only for created, parked or restorable sessions.

5. **staged_numstat adds to the confirm-path hold even with no pre-commit hook.**

6. **What the fix must handle.**
   - Running the nested prepare inside the composite op's own prepare works for confirm. It also works for dispatch to an existing session, since finish_launch already re-checks state and epoch.
   - It does not work for create followed by spawn. spawn's prepare (stage_launch -> sessions::by_name) needs the row that create's finish inserts in the same transaction. The launch must instead be planned from the prepared create, or issued as a follow-up staged request after commit. That changes the response (the session is not yet running) and the rollback behaviour.
   - Fanout must list its descendants without the lock, and should fetch once rather than once per child.
   - Making invoke_registered refuse ops that have a prepare only turns the freeze into an error unless those composite ops are restructured.
   - The user hook needs a generous timeout, since hooks that run tests can take minutes. On the locked path a timeout only bounds the freeze; it does not remove it.

7. **The desktop's main connection stays blocked even after the fix.** The desktop sends guardrail.confirm, and the original git.commit, on its main UI connection, and socket.rs handles each connection's requests one at a time. So a staged confirm still blocks that connection for as long as the hook runs, unless it is sent on its own connection the way lifecycle ops are (client.rs:50-62).

findings.title: Home-grown guardrail glob drops its `**` backtrack point at a later `*`, so `dir/**/*.ext` protected paths miss files two or more directories deep
findings.evidence: glob_match keeps a single backtrack slot: on each star `star = Some((p, t, crosses)); continue;`, so a segment-local `*` after a `**` overwrites the `**` entry, and the mismatch arm `Some((after_star, star_text, crosses)) if crosses || text[star_text] != b'/' => {...} _ => return false` returns false at the next `/` instead of retrying the earlier `**`. A line-for-line port checked against a reference (`**`->`.*`, `*`->`[^/]*`) gives: `**/*.pem` vs `certs/old/x.pem` -> false; `src/**/*.rs` vs `src/a/b/main.rs` -> false; `migrations/**/*.sql` vs `migrations/2024/01/x.sql` -> false (4490 disagreements on a small exhaustive alphabet). The tests (guardrail.rs:1331-1349) only put one directory under `**`. path_matches feeds protected_paths (512), shape gates (526, 548), the commit protected-path check (778), path grants (grants.rs:105,107) and file.search's glob (file.rs:330). gix 0.86 re-exports gix-glob 0.27 unconditionally (`pub use gix_glob as glob;`), whose `wildmatch(pattern, value, Mode::NO_MATCH_SLASH_LITERAL)` implements exactly the `*`-within-a-segment / `**`-across semantics D113 asks for.
findings.impact: A user protects `secrets/**/*.key` or `src/**/*.rs`; an agent's Write/Edit to `secrets/prod/eu/a.key` passes guardrail.gate and a commit touching it passes the commit check — the protection silently stops one directory below `**`. Shape gates skip nested files the same way, and file.search globs under-report.
findings.fix: Keep the exact/prefix fast path and replace glob_match with `gix::glob::wildmatch(pattern.into(), path.into(), gix::glob::wildmatch::Mode::NO_MATCH_SLASH_LITERAL)` (already compiled in via gix); add tests with two and three directories beneath `**`.

v1.reason: guardrail.rs:1171-1205 glob_match keeps a single `star` slot. Any later `*` runs `star = Some((p, t, crosses))` and overwrites the `**` entry. The mismatch arm then returns false when the overwriting segment-local star would have to consume a '/' (`_ => return false`). I ported the function line for line (Python, scratchpad/exp/g.py) and got: `**/*.pem` vs `certs/old/x.pem` -> false; `src/**/*.rs` vs `src/a/b/main.rs` -> false; `secrets/**/*.key` vs `secrets/prod/eu/a.key` -> false; one-level cases -> true. path_matches (1161) falls back to glob_match whenever the exact-path/prefix check fails. Its callers are protected_paths (512), shape gates (526, 548), the commit check (778), path grants (grants.rs:105, 107) and file.search's glob filter (file.rs:330), so all of them under-match. The tests at 1331-1349 only use one directory under `**`. gix 0.86 is a relay-core dependency, and its lib.rs:133 has `pub use gix_glob as glob;`, so the suggested replacement is already compiled in.
v1.correction: One more case: a root-level file does not match a leading `**/` (`**/*.pem` vs `x.pem` -> false), while git wildmatch lets `**/` match zero directories. Add that case to the new tests. Impact is two-sided. Protected paths and shape gates silently stop applying below the first directory under `**` (the security part). Path grants also under-match, which only over-restricts. file.search's `glob` filter under-reports. When adopting gix::glob::wildmatch, keep the exact-path and directory-prefix fast path in path_matches.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. glob_match (guardrail.rs:1171) keeps one `star` slot. A later segment-local `*` runs `star = Some((p, t, crosses))` and overwrites the `**` entry. The mismatch arm then hits `_ => return false` as soon as that `*` would have to consume a '/'. I wrote my own line-for-line port (scratchpad/exp/skeptic-glob-ow2/port.py) and checked it against the D113 reference (`**` -> `.*`, `*` -> `[^/]*`):
- `**/*.pem` vs `certs/old/x.pem` -> false
- `src/**/*.rs` vs `src/a/b/main.rs` -> false
- `secrets/**/*.key` vs `secrets/prod/eu/a.key` -> false
- `config/**/*.json` vs `config/a/b/c.json` -> false
- one-directory cases -> true

On an exhaustive small alphabet there were 2735 false negatives and 0 false positives. Every miss has a single `*` after a `**`. Patterns without one (`secrets/**`, `secrets`, `**/.env`, `**/secrets.toml`) work at any depth. Because the matcher never over-matches, path grants never over-grant.

(b) Trigger and reach. A user has to write such a pattern as a protected path or shape gate, through the Guardrails page (hint "Worktree-relative paths or globs agents may not write", with no syntax examples), `guardrail.config.set`, or the legacy project field. The defaults are empty (settings.rs:31-32), so nothing fires out of the box. Once a pattern is set, every agent write to a file two or more directories below the `**` is affected. The paths in:
- Claude Code Write/Edit/MultiEdit hooks send the file_path to `guardrail.gate` (relay-cli main.rs:413-458), and write_target turns it into a worktree-relative path.
- Commits go through the pre-commit gate, evaluate_commit (778).
- The bus file ops use the same check.

`**/*.pem` matches only .pem files exactly one directory deep. It misses both root-level and deeper files. The code's own test (`src/**/*.rs` vs `src/deep/main.rs`) shows this pattern shape is intended to work.

(c) Consequence. The protected_path refusal (or the hold for a user) is skipped. The agent's write lands and its commit passes the hook, with no hold and no notification. `guardrail.check` and `guardrail.explain` also report allow, so nothing tells the user. Shape gates skip nested critical files in the same way. Grants under-match, which only over-restricts. The `glob` filter in file.search under-reports. The destructive-write rule still applies independently.

(d) High is right: this is "a safety check that can be silently bypassed". It is not critical. It needs a user-written pattern of this shape, the agent does nothing adversarial, and BUS.md principle 6 frames guardrails as seatbelts, not a sandbox.

(e) The proposed fix fixes the reported cases but is not exactly D113, and it would weaken some patterns that work today; see correction.
v2.correction:
1. There is a second failure point: the trailing-`*` early return at guardrail.rs:1181-1183, `return crosses || !text[t..].contains(&b'/')`. It also gives up instead of falling back to an earlier `**`. Examples: `**/*` vs `a/b/c` -> false, `**/x/*` vs `x/x/x/y` -> false, `**/secrets/*` vs `a/secrets/b/secrets/k` -> false. Any fix and its tests must cover this case too.

2. `**/*.pem` vs `x.pem` and `src/**/*.rs` vs `src/main.rs` (zero directories) also fail under the D113 reference itself. They are git-convention expectations, not deviations from D113. Decide that behaviour explicitly.

3. The gix swap is real but changes meaning. gix 0.86 lib.rs:133 has `pub use gix_glob as glob;`, and gix-glob 0.27 wildmatch.rs:404 defines `wildmatch(&BStr, &BStr, Mode) -> bool`. In NO_MATCH_SLASH_LITERAL mode, `**` crosses '/' only when it is a whole path component (wildmatch.rs ~104-126); anywhere else it sets `match_slash = false`.
   - `**.pem` vs `a/b/x.pem`, `secrets**` vs `secrets/a/b` and `a/**b` vs `a/x/yb` are all true today and would become false. That silently narrows existing protection.
   - It also makes `?`, `[...]` and `\` special characters, so `app/[locale]/**` stops matching `app/[locale]/x`. The exact-path and prefix fast path still covers plain paths.
   - It returns false when it hits its recursion limit. That is fail-open, but only for pathological patterns.

   Adopting it means rejecting or migrating `**` that is not a whole component in validate_pattern, and updating D113 and the settings hint.

4. A smaller fix keeps current semantics: hold separate backtrack slots for the last `**` and the last segment `*`. When the `*` cannot advance (next byte is '/' or text is exhausted), restore the `**` slot: advance it by one byte and clear the `*` slot. I checked such a matcher against the D113 reference on 2,457,818 pattern/path pairs with 0 disagreements. An alternative is to translate each pattern into an anchored regex: `regex` is already a normal dependency of relay-core and runs in linear time.

5. Add tests with two and three directories under `**`, plus `**/*` and `**/x/*` on deep paths.

findings.title: denied_commands match only a contiguous window of unquoted words from a hand-rolled shell reader, so everyday spellings of every default denial run unchecked
findings.evidence: denied_matches (969-998): `let bare: Vec<String> = command.iter().filter(|word| !word.quoted)...collect();` then `if bare.windows(wanted.len()).any(|window| window == wanted.as_slice())`. shell_commands (894-952) splits only on `; \n | &` and leaves `(`/`)` inside words. Defaults (settings.rs:33): ["rm -rf", "git reset --hard", "git clean -fd", "git push --force"]. A port of the matcher allows: `git push origin main --force`, `git push -f origin main`, `rm -fr build`, `rm -r -f build`, `git reset HEAD~1 --hard`, `git clean -fdx`, `(cd repo && git push --force)`, `git 'push' --force origin main`, `bash -c 'git push --force'`; only the literal order `git push --force ...` is refused. This is the only gate on agent Bash commands (relay-cli main.rs:405 sends kind=exec; hooks.rs installs only a pre-commit git hook, no pre-push, and no provider deny rules). device_lease.rs:365 is a second, different reader for the same hook input (splits on `(`, `)`, backtick and `$(`, unquotes by trimming). shlex and shell-words are already in Cargo.lock.
findings.impact: An agent force-pushes with `git push origin HEAD --force` or wipes with `rm -fr` / `git clean -fdx` and the guardrail allows it without a hold or refusal — the safety check is bypassed by ordinary command spelling, not just by an adversarial agent.
findings.fix: Use one shared argv reader (shlex, or the device_lease reader extended) that splits subshells, `$(…)` and backticks and keeps quoted words as argv elements; match a pattern as program + subcommand in order, then require the remaining pattern tokens anywhere in that command's argv, expanding bundled short flags (`-fr`, `-fdx`) and known aliases (`-f`/`--force`). Route guardrail, grants (command_words, 1001) and device_lease through it; add tests for reordered, bundled and subshell forms.

v1.reason: guardrail.rs:965-998 denied_matches collects the lowercased unquoted words of each command and matches only `bare.windows(wanted.len()).any(|w| w == wanted)`, i.e. a contiguous, exact, in-order sequence. shell_commands (guardrail.rs:894-952) splits only on `; \n | &`. It does not split `(`, `)`, `$(` or backticks, so `(cd x && git push --force)` produces the word `--force)` and `$(git ...)` produces `$(git`. A word that is fully quoted is dropped from bare, so `git 'push' --force` becomes [git, --force]. The defaults (settings.rs:33) are `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd` and `git push --force`. That leaves these unmatched: `git push origin main --force`, `git push -f`, `rm -fr`, `rm -r -f`, `git clean -fdx`, `git clean -df`, `git reset HEAD~1 --hard`, and the subshell forms. The agent's Bash hook sends kind=exec with the raw command (relay-cli main.rs:405-410). Exec evaluation goes through denied_matches, so these ordinary spellings are allowed with no hold or refusal. D103 (DECISIONS.md:469) defines the intent as "match a pattern only against unquoted words in one command". Nothing there accepts reordering or flag-spelling bypasses. device_lease.rs:364-394 is a second reader that does split `(`, `)`, backtick and `$(` and unquotes by trimming, so the two readers already disagree.
v1.correction: `bash -c 'git push --force'` and `git 'push' --force` are outside the documented D103 contract: quoted words are treated as data by design. Fixing them means deliberately revising D103 (for example, re-parsing the argument of `sh -c`/`bash -c`), not just fixing a bug. The core bypasses are reordered flags, `-f` vs `--force`, bundled short flags (`-fr`, `-fdx`) and subshell/`$(` splitting, and they are real without any of the quoted cases. Treat denied_commands as a speed bump, not a sandbox: an agent can always write a script file and run it. Even so, silently passing the everyday spellings of every default denial justifies high.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. In guardrail.rs:969-998, denied_matches builds `bare` from the unquoted words in lowercase and matches only `bare.windows(wanted.len()).any(|window| window == wanted.as_slice())`, which is a contiguous, exact, in-order run of words. shell_commands (894-952) splits commands only on `; \n | &`, so `(`, `)`, `$(` and backticks stay attached to words. The path from the hooks has no normalisation step: the Claude hook (relay-cli main.rs:403-407, Bash becomes kind=exec with the raw command) and the Codex hook (main.rs:506-512) call guardrail.gate (handlers/guardrail.rs:511), which runs evaluate_granted, then evaluate_exec, then denied_matches (guardrail.rs:831). I ported the reader and matcher to Python and checked them. The canonical forms are still refused: `git push --force origin main`, `rm -rf x`, `rm -Rf x` (lowercasing makes it `-rf`), `sudo rm -rf x`, `git reset --hard HEAD~1` and `cd r && git push --force`. These are ALLOWED: `git push origin main --force`, `git push -f origin main`, `git push -uf origin main`, `git -C /repo push --force origin main`, `/usr/bin/git push --force`, `rm -fr x`, `rm -r -f x`, `rm --recursive --force x`, `git reset HEAD~1 --hard`, `git -C . reset --hard`, `git clean -fdx`, `git clean -df`, `git clean -xfd`, `git clean -f -d`, `git -C . clean -fd` and `(cd r && git push --force)`. The existing tests (agent_surface.rs:229-251, guardrails.rs:590-657) cover only the canonical word order.

(b) Reachability. Every Claude session is affected, because install_claude puts a PreToolUse hook on Bash. Every Codex session whose hooks have been trusted is affected too (D132). Nothing else in Relay catches these commands: hooks.rs installs only a pre-commit git hook, with no pre-push hook and no provider deny rules. These are ordinary agent spellings, not tricks: `git push -f origin <branch>`, a trailing `--force`, `git -C <worktree> …` and `git clean -fdx` are all common. A refusal of the canonical spelling also leaves an equivalent spelling one retry away for an agent pushing toward its goal. The settings copy (guardrail_settings.rs:70, "Commands agents may not run, matched word by word") and the denied_commands list that session.bootstrap hands agents both tell the user and the agent that the command itself is denied.

(c) What happens. The gate returns Allow and the hook exits 0, with no hold, refusal or notification. The command then runs, gated only by the provider's own layer, and that depends on configuration. For Claude, the normal permission flow applies because Relay passes no permission mode: in default mode the user is prompted, unless an allow rule, bypass mode or auto mode applies. For Codex, the `--approve-for-me` automatic reviewer runs inside its workspace-write sandbox (D135), where network is normally off. If the command runs: a force push overwrites the remote branch's history; `git clean -fdx` and `rm -fr` delete untracked and ignored files for good, since they are in neither git nor Relay's file undo; `git reset … --hard` throws away uncommitted worktree changes.

(d) Severity high fits the rubric: "a safety check that can be silently bypassed", in normal agent use, with data loss that cannot be undone. It is not critical. BUS.md principle 6 ("Seatbelts, not sandboxes") puts deliberate evasion out of scope, and the provider permission layers may still catch the command depending on the user's configuration. The trigger here is ordinary mistake-shaped spelling, which is exactly what the seatbelt exists to stop.

(e) The fix points the right way but is incomplete as written; see the correction.
v2.correction:
1. "This is the only gate on agent Bash commands" should read: the only Relay-side gate. After the hook exits 0, Claude Code's own permission flow still applies, and Codex still has its automatic reviewer and sandbox (D135). Both depend on configuration, and neither makes the Relay check work.
2. Additional ordinary bypasses: git global options placed before the subcommand (`git -C <dir> push --force`, `git -C . reset --hard`, `git -C . clean -fd`), which agents use all the time; a path-qualified binary (`/usr/bin/git push --force`); `git push -uf`; `rm --recursive --force`; `git clean -d -f`. `git push origin +main` and `--force-with-lease` are not matched either; the second is probably intentional.
3. I agree with the first verifier that `git 'push' --force` and `bash -c '…'` are outside D103 by design and should not be counted in the core claim.
4. Corrections to the fix:
   - (i) Do not anchor the match at argv[0]. Today's sliding window does catch `sudo rm -rf`, `xargs rm -rf`, `nice`/`env`/`command git push --force` and `GIT_DIR=x git push --force`. A program-plus-subcommand matcher must skip wrappers and environment assignments, skip git's global options (`-C <dir>`, `-c <k=v>`, `--git-dir=`, `--work-tree=`) and compare the program's basename, or it will stop catching those forms.
   - (ii) shlex and shell-words appear in Cargo.lock only as transitive dependencies; no crate depends on them directly. Neither splits on `;`, `&&`, `|`, `(`, `$(` or backticks, and neither reports which words were quoted, so they cannot replace shell_commands. Extend the existing reader instead, splitting on `(`, `)`, `$(` and backticks the way device_lease::split_commands already does.
   - (iii) Treat a fully-quoted single word as an ordinary word, and keep a quoted string containing spaces as one opaque argv element. That keeps D103's rule that a quoted mention is data, and fixes `git 'push'`. It is still a change to D103 and should be recorded as one.
   - (iv) Aliases and bundled short flags must be handled per program: `-r`/`-R`/`--recursive` and `-f`/`--force` for rm, `-f`/`--force` for git push. covers_command compares hit.bare with command_words(grant), and both come from the same reader, so sending both through the new reader keeps exact-command grants consistent.
   - (v) Add tests for every spelling listed above.

findings.title: Subprocess-timeout invariant is convention only: seven separate git runners, and the shared one behind git_mutate runs untimed under the store mutex
findings.evidence: worktree.rs:26-33 `let out = Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()` — no timeout, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 — backs git_mutate, remove and rename_branch. Other git runners each re-decide safety: hooks.rs:583 (10 s), branch_cleanup.rs:111 (timeout + GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 + GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0), guardrail.rs:1122 (timeout), worktree.rs:86/212 and git.rs:938/1347 (timeouts) vs device.rs:1500-1535, git.rs:1269, github.rs:106/155 and workspace.rs:234 (none). Untimed work inside Engine::register handlers (store mutex held): project.clone `git clone` (workspace.rs:228-235, used by onboarding.rs:527), git.pr.open `gh pr create` over the network (git.rs:666-683), worktree.remove -> worktree::remove = purge_build walk + rm, dir_size walk, `git worktree remove --force` (git.rs:139, worktree.rs:352-370 — project.remove deliberately defers this very work after commit, workspace.rs:320-344), git.stage/unstage/branch.create/branch.delete via git_mutate (git.rs:374/485/503/527; LFS clean/smudge filters), file.restore_head `git checkout --` (file.rs:256), avd.create `avdmanager create avd` with wait_with_output plus `emulator -list-avds` / `adb emu avd name` (device.rs:332-338, 478, 505), session.update rename_branch (session.rs:1460). There is no clippy disallowed-methods rule behind CLAUDE.md's rule.
findings.impact: Cloning a large or credential-prompting repo from onboarding, "Open PR" on a slow network, "Stage all" on an LFS-heavy Unreal checkout, creating an AVD, or removing a worktree with a multi-GB target/ holds the global store mutex for seconds to minutes (indefinitely if git waits on a prompt): every agent's guardrail hook and every UI request blocks meanwhile.
findings.fix: Add one `proc::git(repo, args, timeout)` runner (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, stdin null, output_with_timeout) and delete the per-module runners; move project.clone, git.pr.open, worktree.remove, git.stage/unstage and avd.create to register_staged with the subprocess in the prepare phase; add a relay-core clippy.toml `disallowed-methods` for std::process::Command::output/status and Child::wait_with_output, with explicit allows only in after-commit workers.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:26-33 runs `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()` with no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. git_mutate at line 36 is a thin wrapper around it. Handlers registered with plain Engine::register, which holds the store mutex, call it or other untimed subprocesses: ProjectClone (workspace.rs:228-236, a raw `git clone ... .output()`; the native client even gives project.clone an 1800 s timeout, client.rs:67), PrOpen (git.rs:666-683, `gh pr create` via `.output()`), WorktreeRemove (git.rs:129-139 -> worktree::remove: purge_build, dir_size and `git worktree remove --force`, worktree.rs:352-370), BranchCreate, BranchDelete, Stage and Unstage (git.rs:345/445/490/507 via git_mutate), RestoreHead (file.rs:253-256) and AvdCreate (device.rs:321-337, `wait_with_output`). The fix pattern already exists in the codebase: Fetch and Push are register_staged (git.rs:580, 600), and timed runners with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 exist at worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943/1349 and branch_cleanup.rs:114. So the untimed calls are inconsistencies, not a design decision. Trigger: cloning a large repository from onboarding, or 'Open PR' on a slow network, holds the global store mutex for the whole subprocess. Every agent's guardrail hook and every UI query blocks until it finishes.
v1.correction: Further sites: git.push (git.rs:617) and integration merges (integration.rs:128) also use the untimed git_mutate. Push is staged, so it does not hold the mutex, but it still breaks the output_with_timeout rule and can stall its own connection indefinitely. The git fetch in device.rs:1575 runs inside run_worker (1652), a background worker, so it does not hold the mutex; it still lacks a timeout. A mutex hold 'indefinitely if git waits on a prompt' depends on the engine having a controlling TTY or an askpass helper that blocks. For the GUI-launched engine that path is less likely, but a credential helper or SSH host-key prompt could still hang. The fix stands as proposed: one timed proc::git runner, and moving project.clone, git.pr.open, worktree.remove, stage/unstage and avd.create to register_staged.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. worktree.rs:26-33 runs `Command::new("git")...output()` with no deadline, and git_mutate (line 36) only wraps it. A handler registered with plain `Engine::register` runs inside `dispatch_inner`, which holds `self.store.lock()` (a std Mutex with no timeout) and an open transaction for the whole handler (engine.rs:953-956). The following run untimed inside such handlers:
- ProjectClone: an inline `git clone ... .output()` (workspace.rs:234).
- PrOpen: `gh pr create` via `.output()` (git.rs:680). `git.pr.list` in the same file is timed (git.rs:1094).
- BranchCreate, BranchDelete, Stage, Unstage: via git_mutate (git.rs:374/485/503/527).
- RestoreHead (file.rs:256).
- WorktreeRemove: purge_build, dir_size, then `git worktree remove` (git.rs:139 -> worktree.rs:352-370).
- AvdCreate: `wait_with_output`, then list_avds under the lock (device.rs:332-340).
- session.update: rename_branch (session.rs:1460).

No clippy.toml exists. The code's own rules say this is wrong. D144 says every handler subprocess goes through output_with_timeout, and D149 says slow work belongs outside the transaction. The commit handler's comment (git.rs:531-534) calls staging a subprocess "of unbounded length". skill.install's comment (provider.rs:209-210) moved "a slow clone off every other op". session.close does the same worktree removal in a staged prepare (session.rs:1547-1580), and project.remove defers it until after commit (workspace.rs:320-344).

(b) Who reaches it, and how often:
- project.clone: the native "Open repository" GitHub flow (app.rs:1687-1695 -> onboarding.rs:527). This is a normal way to add a project, at any time, while other agents run. The client gives it an 1800 s timeout (client.rs:67), so clones of minutes are expected.
- git.pr.open: Git panel "Publish a pull request" (code_git.rs:662/1240). Agents can also call it, since it is not UserOnly.
- git.stage/unstage: Git panel "Stage all" and per-file staging, and agents with bus_writes through MCP. Usually milliseconds (perf baseline 4 ms), but seconds or more when `git add` hashes large LFS or binary assets.
- avd.create: Devices tool (tools_devices.rs:419). avdmanager is a JVM tool and takes seconds.
- worktree.remove and file.restore_head: no GUI caller at all; only `relay cmd` or the phone door. Rare.
- branch.create/delete and rename_branch: local and millisecond-scale; untimed only in principle.

(c) What happens when it fires: for the whole subprocess, every request that needs the store blocks. That includes:
- every agent's PreToolUse guardrail.gate: check_session_token locks the store (engine.rs:1378), and Relay installs that hook with a 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:351);
- MCP calls;
- the phone door;
- session.create/close on the lifecycle connection;
- every unlocked query's ctx.read.

Keystrokes are spared: session.input takes the D148 fast path, and each terminal pane has its own connection. GUI requests time out after 30 s ("Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown"). Requests the engine has already queued still run later, after their clients gave up. There is no deadline, so a git blocked on an askpass prompt or a stalled transfer holds the bus until git exits.

(d) High is right: this is a bus freeze in normal flows (clone, PR, staging assets). It is not critical by default, because the freeze is bounded by the subprocess runtime unless git hangs. One thing I could not establish: what Claude Code does when the 30 s hook times out. If it lets the tool call proceed, a hold longer than 30 s would also let agent tool calls through without the guardrail check.

(e) Moving these ops to register_staged is the right pattern (it is what git.commit, fetch, push, session.close and skill.install already do), and it frees the mutex. On its own it does not fix the GUI side; see the correction.
v2.correction:
Corrections to the finding:
1. Title: the two worst sites, project.clone (workspace.rs:234) and git.pr.open (git.rs:680), build their own Command. They do not go through git_mutate.
2. Reach: worktree.remove, file.restore_head and integration.discard have no native-app caller; only `relay cmd` or the phone door reach them. "Every UI request blocks" is too broad: keystrokes keep working (D148 fast path, per-pane connections).
3. Missed sites under the lock:
   - avd.boot runs list_avds, which calls untimed `emulator -list-avds` and `adb emu avd name` (device.rs:344-346).
   - integration.discard runs worktree::remove: purge, walk and git (integration.rs:58-64).
   - git.branch.clean_merged loops git_mutate (git.rs:693-712). This one is fast.
4. Docs drift: the ProjectClone summary says "(async; project.changed when done)" (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38), and BUS.md §5.1 lists project.clone among handle-returning async ops. The handler is in fact synchronous.

Gaps in the proposed fix:
- The engine handles one connection's requests strictly in order: handle_conn awaits each spawn_blocking before it reads the next line (socket.rs:333-747). So even with project.clone staged, the GUI's main UI connection stays blocked behind a minutes-long clone or PR. Either route these ops over a dedicated connection, as `is_lifecycle_request` does (client.rs:50-62), or make project.clone truly async with a handle, as the spec says.
- A shared git runner needs a per-call timeout and per-call env:
  - status_files deliberately sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1, and branch_cleanup sets it to 0.
  - status parsing needs the raw stdout bytes.
  - clone and push need long deadlines, and a short uniform timeout would kill clones that would otherwise succeed.
- GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 does not stop askpass helpers or ssh prompts. Add something like GIT_SSH_COMMAND with BatchMode=yes if a prompt must never block.
- The clippy disallowed-methods rule only enforces D144 (have a deadline), not D149 (work outside the transaction). A timed 120 s call under the lock still freezes the bus, so the rule is a guard, not the fix.
- Unaffected: the guardrail.confirm replay path (engine.rs:325-327) still runs staged prepares under the lock, by design.

findings.title: refresh_git (711 lines) rebuilds the whole Source Control panel and lists every GitHub PR via `gh api --paginate` on each agent file save
findings.evidence: app.rs:1233-1240 sends every file.changed/git.changed/worktree.changed/integration.* event to editor.invalidate, which (editor.rs:508-526, 1 s debounce) calls refresh_git whenever the page is "agents" — the main wall, since navigate maps "code" to "agents" (app.rs:1314-1315). refresh_git does `clear(&e.git)` (170), recreates every widget, recomputes the splitter `panes.set_position(if folded("history") { free - 34 } else { (free - 280).max(120) })` (250), then `tokio::join!(git.branches, git.log, integration.list, git.pr.list)` (578-583). git.pr.list (handlers/git.rs:625-645, 1083-1090) runs `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100` — every PR the repo ever had, one GitHub request per 100 — uncached. watch.rs:128 emits file.changed for any write in a watched worktree after a 125 ms debounce. All of it shares the native control connection, which the socket door serves one request at a time.
findings.impact: While agents edit files the UI re-downloads the full PR history every few seconds per open project, burning the user's gh token quota (hundreds to thousands of calls an hour; a repo with a few hundred PRs can reach GitHub's 5,000/h limit, which then also breaks the agents' own gh use); the user's dragged history splitter snaps back, scroll position and open branch popovers are lost on every agent save, and other UI requests queue behind each gh call.
findings.fix: Split refresh_git into a status refresh (file list and counts, updating the existing sections in place) driven by file events, and a remote refresh (branches, PR list, integrations) driven by branch switch, fetch/push, the Refresh key or a minutes-long timer; keep the Paned and sections alive across refreshes. Server side, cache git.pr.list per project for a short TTL or query only the current branch (`gh pr list --head <branch> --state all`).

v1.reason: app.rs:1232-1240 routes file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed, integration.changed and integration.result to ui.editor.invalidate. The only filter is the event's project id (app.rs:1212-1222), with none on worktree. invalidate (editor.rs:508-531) runs refresh_git after a 1 s debounce whenever the page is "code" or "agents", and navigate maps "code" to "agents" (app.rs:1314-1315). Nothing checks whether the Source Control panel is visible. In refresh_git, git_refresh_pending/dirty (code_git.rs:146-149) coalesces concurrent refreshes, so the result is at most one rebuild per about (1 s + refresh duration) while files keep changing. Each rebuild does `clear(&e.git)` (code_git.rs:170) and recreates the header, picker and popover. It builds a new gtk::Paned whose position is computed from the window height (code_git.rs:242-250), which throws away a user-dragged splitter, any scroll position and an open branch popover. It then calls `tokio::join!(git.branches, git.log, integration.list, git.pr.list)` (code_git.rs:578-583). git.pr.list (git.rs:625-645) is uncached and runs list_pull_requests (git.rs:1083-1090): `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100`. That fetches every PR in the repo's history, one request per 100, on every refresh. watch.rs:118-128 emits file.changed after a 125 ms debounce for any non-generated write in a watched worktree. An agent editing continuously therefore makes the UI re-download the full PR list every couple of seconds. The handler is register_unlocked with output_with_timeout, so the store is not blocked. The real costs are GitHub API quota (1-5 requests per refresh, up to thousands per hour) and repeated UI state resets.
v1.correction: git.pr.list is register_unlocked and runs through proc::output_with_timeout (git.rs:625, 1093), so it does not hold the store. The claim that "other UI requests queue behind each gh call" depends on the native client's connection multiplexing and was not established, so drop it. The rate-limit impact scales with PR count: a small repo costs one request per refresh, roughly 1,000-1,800 an hour during active editing. That is wasteful but reaches the 5,000/h limit only with several pages of PRs or several projects or instances. The UI-state loss (splitter, scroll, popover) is certain on every agent save in the open project, so high is justified. The fix stands: refresh status in place on file events, refresh the remote and PR data only on branch, fetch or push, manual refresh, or a long timer, and cache git.pr.list server-side or query only the current head branch. apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in this environment, so this was established by reading the code.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. refresh_git spans code_git.rs:142-852. It clears and rebuilds the panel (170), builds a new Paned whose position comes from the window height (249-250), and joins git.branches, git.log, integration.list and git.pr.list (578-583). git.pr.list (git.rs:625) runs `gh api --paginate --slurp .../pulls?state=all&per_page=100` (git.rs:1083-1109) with no cache. app.rs:1213 filters events by project only, and app.rs:1240 sends file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed and integration.* to editor.invalidate. invalidate (editor.rs:508-531) has a 1 s leading debounce, checks only that the page is "agents" (the default page, app.rs:747) and never checks whether the Source Control panel is shown.

(b) Who triggers it, and how often. Watchers are registered only by file.tree, file.read, file.search and git.status (file.rs:21/41/301, git.rs:164), and they are never removed. prepare_project always registers the primary checkout. So these always trigger a refresh:
- edits in the primary checkout, including the user's own edits and sessions created with worktree "primary", which is the default for Unreal-plugin projects (plugins.rs:210-214, plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18);
- every agent commit, because it rewrites the shared .git/refs/heads/<branch>, which is_generated_path deliberately keeps.

A pooled agent worktree triggers on every save only after something has queried it: the user pointing Code at that checkout (select_checkout), or the agent calling relay file/git query tools, which default to its own worktree (file.rs:401-405). Refreshes then run about once per max(1 s, refresh duration), merged by git_refresh_pending/dirty.

(c) What happens when it fires:
- Each refresh sends 7 control requests and makes ceil(PRs/100) GitHub calls.
- Each refresh also schedules branch_cleanup::after_merged_prs (git.rs:630-641). That runs `git rev-parse` for every closed-session branch with a merged PR, including branches already deleted, because candidates() never drops them.
- The first verifier's correction is wrong: requests do queue. socket.rs:335-743 dispatches one request per connection at a time, and Ui::call (app.rs:1111-1116) puts every non-lifecycle op on the one shared client (client.rs:131 says as much). The user's file.read and file.write wait behind gh, usually for under a second to a few seconds and at most PR_LIST_TIMEOUT, 10 s.
- With Source Control open, each rebuild resets the splitter and scroll, closes the branch popover, clears the Merge Test ticks (685, 697), and moves the commit box to a new parent (297).
- This contradicts DECISIONS.md D130 (635-640): "File-watch refreshes do not repeat the network request."

(d) High is right: normal agent activity on the default page, wrong behaviour the user can see, and wasted API quota. There is no data loss.

(e) The direction of the fix is right.
v2.correction:
- Narrow the trigger. Pooled agent worktrees cause a refresh on every save only once their watcher exists, after the user or the agent has queried that worktree. Edits in the primary checkout and every agent commit always cause one.
- Put back the claim that requests queue, which the first verifier dropped. The socket door handles one request per connection at a time (socket.rs:335-743), and Ui::call puts every non-lifecycle op on the one shared control client (app.rs:1111-1116).
- The panel is hidden by default (editor.rs:300). The visible resets therefore affect only users who open Source Control. The gh calls and the queueing happen either way.
- Add these effects:
  - the conflict with D130;
  - Merge Test selections are cleared on every refresh;
  - the commit box is moved to a new parent each time, which probably drops keyboard focus mid-typing (not run);
  - each git.pr.list call spawns a branch_cleanup thread that runs a git subprocess for each matching closed-session branch.
- Quota: a repo with fewer than 100 PRs costs about one request per refresh, from hundreds up to about 1,800 an hour. Reaching the 5,000/h limit takes several hundred PRs or several windows.
- Fix, smallest version (effort S): follow D130. Skip git.pr.list on refreshes driven by file events and reuse the last result. Fetch again on project open, branch switch, push, fetch, opening a PR, and the Refresh key. Also filter events by the worktree the panel shows, and skip the refresh while the panel is hidden.
- Do not change git.pr.list itself to list only the current branch. Its merged-PR cleanup trigger and agents calling it over MCP need the full list. Add an optional head filter or a separate op instead.
- Any cache on the engine side must be cleared on git.pr.open and git.push.
- BUS.md:828 still says the op lists "open" PRs; it now lists every state.
- apps/relay-native was not compiled.

findings.title: Socket door answers each connection's requests strictly in order, so one slow query stalls the UI's whole control channel and clients grow workarounds
findings.evidence: The read loop `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await?` (335) awaits each request — `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(req, Door::Socket)).await?` (742) — before reading the next line, and bus.wait waits inline for up to an hour (424). BUS.md §6.2 promises "correlation by id; pipelining allowed". The native client multiplexes every ui.call over one connection with an id-keyed pending map and a 30 s timeout (client.rs:65-71, 298-330) and compensates: is_lifecycle_request (client.rs:50-63) sends session.create/close/park/wake/... and task.dispatch on throwaway connections (app.rs:1113), image_read opens yet another (client.rs:124), and its test is named `lifecycle_actions_bypass_a_stalled_status_request` (client.rs:346).
findings.impact: A git.status on a big LFS checkout (up to 10 s), git.pr.list (up to 10 s), file.search or worktree.list delays every queued click on the control connection; queued mutations can hit the client's 30 s timeout and show "Its outcome is unknown" while the engine still executes them later, inviting duplicate retries (e.g. a second task.create).
findings.fix: Keep the stateful ops (subscribe/unsubscribe, watch, attach/detach, mirror and run streams) inline, but spawn ordinary requests as tasks bounded by a per-connection semaphore that write their response to out_tx when done — responses are already id-correlated. Then delete is_lifecycle_request/lifecycle_request and the separate image connection.

v1.reason: socket.rs:335 reads requests one at a time (`while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await?`). Each ordinary request is awaited inline with `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(req, Door::Socket)).await?` (751-752) before the next line is read. bus.wait also waits inline (424-438). So every request on a connection waits behind the slowest one ahead of it. The native client works around this: is_lifecycle_request (client.rs:50-63) routes lifecycle ops to separate connections, image_read opens its own connection (client.rs:124), and the test lifecycle_actions_bypass_a_stalled_status_request (client.rs:346) covers exactly this case. request_with_id starts the 30 s timeout (client.rs:65-71, 325-332) before the request is queued and sent. A request stuck behind slow unlocked queries (git.status, git.pr.list, worktree.list) can therefore time out on the client and show 'outcome is unknown' while the engine still runs it later.
v1.correction: BUS.md §6.2 'pipelining allowed' is not strictly broken: in-order pipelining is still pipelining. The problem is head-of-line blocking, not a broken promise. Any fix must keep ordering where it matters. session.input (answered from memory at 755-759), resize, attach/detach and subscribe must stay in order on a connection, or keystrokes could be reordered. Clients may also rely on a mutation being answered before a query sent after it. Running requests concurrently does not help ops registered with plain Engine::register, because they still serialize on the store mutex. Only unlocked and staged ops would overlap.

findings.title: Engine keeps a pane/window model and layout fallback that the GTK client never implements; ui.* ops report success for nothing
findings.evidence: ui.pane.open (67-100) invents `pane-N` ids with PaneInfo targets; ui.window.popout (262-290) invents `popout-N` windows; ui.window.list and ui.state (43, 326) return that model; ui.pane.move emits ui.changed with a different shape, `{"move":{...}}` (180).
