The only consumer, the native apply_ui_event (shell.rs:438-463), reads just page/project_id and the focused pane's target.session; nothing in apps/relay-native opens diff/note panes or pop-out windows. ui.page.switch accepts Page::Plan, but the native stack has no "plan" child, so navigate returns silently (app.rs:619-631, 1319-1321). fallback_state (ui.rs:32-39) reads `layout.current.{id}`, which nothing writes — the client saves `native.layout.current.{id}` (shell.rs:308, 334) — and project.remove deletes `layout.current.{id}` (workspace.rs:378-379) while leaving the native key. BUS.md §6.5 still describes forwarding ui.* to a UI executor and `ui.absent` when headless.
findings.impact: An agent with allow_ui (or the CLI) calls ui.pane.open {kind: diff, sha} or ui.window.popout and gets an id back while nothing appears; ui.state then reports panes, windows and pages the person cannot see; ui.layout.save without `state` stores the hardcoded {"page":"agents","agent_layout":"grid"} instead of the current arrangement.
findings.fix: Delete UiRuntime and the pane/window ops (keep page switch, toast and the named-layout ops) or implement them in the GTK client; point fallback_state and project.remove at `native.layout.current.{id}` (or have the client write the engine key); emit one ui.changed payload shape.

v1.reason: ui.rs keeps an in-engine pane/window model: PaneOpen (66-100) mints `pane-N`, WindowPopout (262-290) mints `popout-N`, and State/WindowList return them. The native client consumes only `page`, `project_id` and the focused pane's `target.session` (shell.rs:438-463). Native calls only ui.page.switch and ui.layout.save/list/apply/delete. A diff, note, run or mirror pane, or a popout, gets an id and success while nothing appears. ui.pane.move emits `{"move":{...}}` (ui.rs ~180), a different ui.changed shape that apply_ui_event ignores. fallback_state (ui.rs:32-39) reads `layout.current.{id}`, but the client writes `native.layout.current.{project}` (shell.rs:308, 334). project.remove deletes `layout.current.{id}` (workspace.rs:378-379) and leaves the native key orphaned. BUS.md:366 still describes `ui.absent` forwarding to a UI executor.
v1.correction: The impact is narrower than stated. The native client always passes `state` to ui.layout.save (shell.rs:590-593), so the hardcoded fallback is reachable only from the CLI or an agent. ui.* ops are callable by agents only when `allow_ui` is set, and that defaults to false (session.rs:809). ui.pane.open with a session target does work: the client focuses that session. That leaves a phantom model, docs drift and an orphaned settings row, which is low severity. Fix: drop the unimplemented pane kinds and window ops, or reject them as unavailable; point fallback_state and project.remove at `native.layout.current.{id}`; emit one ui.changed shape.

findings.title: Settings knobs with no reader: 'Park idle sessions after' and undo.grace_days do nothing, so idle agents never park and deleted files are never purged
findings.evidence: defaults() declares `"undo": { "grace_days": 7 }` (42) and `"parking": { "idle_minutes": 30 }` (44); the Settings page exposes "Park idle sessions after (minutes)" bound to parking.idle_minutes (tools_settings.rs:429-436). No code in relay-core, relay-cli, relay-remote or relay-native reads idle_minutes or grace_days; session.park is only manual. SPEC.md:264 specifies idle parking; BUS.md §5.4 (286-292) says soft-deleted task/module/note/file rows are "hard-deleted by the reconcile pass" after undo.grace_days — no such pass exists (recovery.rs prunes audit rows only). file.delete moves payloads to `<checkout>/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` (file.rs:226-236), and file_trash rows and payloads are removed only by project.remove. `roles: {}` (51), `theme: {}` (46) and `appearance.wallpaper_preview` (17) are also never read.
findings.impact: A user sets 10 minutes expecting idle Claude/Codex processes to be parked; they keep running indefinitely. Everything deleted from the primary checkout through Relay stays on disk under .relay/trash forever, so deleting a large asset folder frees nothing.
findings.fix: Implement both features as after-commit sweepers (like branch_cleanup::spawn_sweeper): park sessions idle longer than parking.idle_minutes, and hard-delete soft-deleted rows and trash payloads older than undo.grace_days — or remove the knobs from defaults(), the Settings page, SPEC.md and BUS.md. Drop the other unread defaults.

v1.reason: settings.rs:42 and :44 set the defaults `undo.grace_days: 7` and `parking.idle_minutes: 30`. Outside settings, a repo-wide rg (excluding relay-mobile) finds idle_minutes only in tools_settings.rs:431-433, which renders the 'Park idle sessions after (minutes)' control. grace_days appears only in BUS.md and two settings round-trip tests (tests/bus.rs:729, 786). Nothing parks a session automatically: session.park (session.rs:971+) is reached only through the manual button (shell.rs:690). Nothing hard-deletes soft-deleted rows or trash payloads. file.delete renames the file to `<root>/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` (file.rs:230-232). file_trash rows go only through `DELETE FROM file_trash WHERE project_id` in project.remove (workspace.rs:369), and that statement does not touch payloads on disk. BUS.md:288-291 promises a reconcile pass that hard-deletes after grace_days. SPEC.md:264 promises idle parking.
v1.correction: The category is better described as a bug: the UI exposes a setting that silently does nothing, and the docs promise behaviour that does not exist. Trash payloads under a session worktree's .relay/trash go away when that worktree is removed, so the permanent growth applies to files deleted from the primary checkout. That growth depends on how much the user deletes, so it does not meet the 'high' bar for unbounded growth in normal use. The unread `theme: {}`, `roles: {}` and `appearance.wallpaper_preview` defaults are trivia, worth at most a cleanup note.

findings.title: Skip-directory lists are copied six ways and have diverged; file.search reads every byte of Unreal/Gradle caches
findings.evidence: file.search's skip_dir (629-636) skips only `.git | .relay | node_modules | target`, then reads each file whole with no size cap (`read_to_end(&mut file, &mut buffer)`, 333-335) before the UTF-8 check. The watcher's is_generated_path (watch.rs:158-185) also skips build, .gradle, .svelte-kit, .next, dist, coverage, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache, Binaries; unreal.rs:29 and blender.rs:22 skip the Unreal dirs; workspace.rs:404, device.rs:1998/2136 and worktree.rs:12 each carry another list. The editor re-runs file.search on every file.changed while a query is in its search box (editor.rs:519-523).
findings.impact: Searching an Unreal or Android project reads DerivedDataCache/Intermediate/Saved/Binaries/build and every binary asset (often tens of GB; a multi-GB .uasset is loaded whole and the reused buffer keeps that capacity) and repeats it after each agent save, occupying a blocking thread and the UI's control connection.
findings.fix: One shared generated-directory predicate (the watcher's list) used by file.search, workspace.discover, the device output scans and the CLI tools; skip files above a few MB or sniff the first 8 KB for NUL before reading the rest.

v1.reason: In file.rs:629-636, skip_dir excludes only `.git | .relay | node_modules | target`. The Search handler (file.rs:298-372) reads every other file whole with `read_to_end` before its UTF-8 check: no size cap, no binary sniff, no .gitignore. It only stops early once `limit` hits are found, so a query with few matches walks and reads everything, including Unreal Intermediate/Saved/DerivedDataCache/Binaries and Android build/.gradle. The watcher's is_generated_path (watch.rs:158-185) already lists those directories. editor.rs:519-523 re-runs run_search on every debounced (1 s) invalidate while the search box is non-empty. The handler is register_unlocked, so it does not hold the store mutex, but it ties up a blocking thread for the whole walk.
v1.correction: The real defect is file.search's walk and read cost, so the category is performance rather than duplication. The 'six diverged copies' framing overstates it. worktree.rs:12 BUILD_DIRS is a purge list with different semantics ('app/build', 'node_modules/.cache') and must not be merged into a skip predicate. workspace.discover stops descending at any `.git` directory, so it is a separate concern. The useful fix: have file.search reuse the watcher's generated-directory list (or honour .gitignore), and skip files over a size cap or sniff the first bytes for NUL before reading the rest. Agent saves that trigger the re-run come from the source tree, because the watcher filters generated paths.

findings.title: Legacy project.update protected_paths/critical_files are a second, unvalidated way to set guardrail patterns; one bad entry blocks every agent in the project
findings.evidence: ProjectUpdateIn still accepts protected_paths and critical_files (ops/workspace.rs:46) and the handler stores them verbatim (workspace.rs:271-277) — no validate_pattern. guardrail::layers merges those columns into the project's effective config (guardrail.rs:154-178) and typed() runs validate_config (292-302), which rejects empty, absolute or `..` patterns. The UI path, guardrail.config.set, validates before writing.
findings.impact: `relay q project.update '{"project_id":1,"protected_paths":["/home/me/secrets"]}'` succeeds; afterwards guardrail::config for project 1 errors, so authorize() fails every agent mutation and guardrail.gate fails every PreToolUse hook — all Bash/Edit/Write calls of every agent in the project are blocked with "bad relative path pattern" until the user finds the legacy column, which the guardrail settings page does not edit.
findings.fix: Migrate the two columns into the project guardrail layer once and drop them from ProjectUpdateIn, or at minimum run validate_pattern on them in project.update.

v1.reason: ProjectUpdateIn (ops/workspace.rs:46) still accepts protected_paths and critical_files. The handler (workspace.rs:271-277) stores them verbatim with no validate_pattern. guardrail::layers merges both columns into the project stage: protected paths at guardrail.rs:160-171, and critical files as `non_empty` shape gates at 175-184. config_for -> typed -> validate_config (292-302) rejects absolute, empty or `..` patterns, so once a bad entry is stored, every guardrail::config(conn, Some(project_id)) call errors. authorize (~358) calls it for every non-query agent op, so every agent mutation in that project fails.
v1.correction: The trigger is narrow. project.update is Actors::UserOnly, and the native UI never sends these fields (guardrail_settings.rs edits the settings layer). Only a user typing a hand-written CLI/bus call with an absolute or `..` pattern can store a bad entry. The op is undoable (Undo::Inverse), and a second project.update fixes it. A real but rare self-inflicted failure, so low severity. The fix stands: run validate_pattern on both lists in project.update, or migrate the columns into the guardrail settings layer and drop them from ProjectUpdateIn.

findings.title: Tauri-door scaffolding survives the move to GTK: Door::Tauri, Doors::TauriOnly, Executor::Ui and ui_connected are never set
findings.evidence: Door::Tauri is constructed only in tests (tests/bus.rs:108, 114, 220); production dispatch is Door::Socket or InProcess (socket.rs:459-742, provider_updates.rs:221). No op uses Doors::TauriOnly (only SocketOnly, ops/bus.rs:32-56), so the door check (engine.rs:821-829) cannot fire in production. Executor::Ui (set by `.ui()`, registry.rs:157-160) is only echoed into OpInfo (registry.rs:273). Engine.ui_connected (engine.rs:406) is never stored, so app.status always reports `ui_connected: false` (handlers/app.rs:33) with the GTK window open. Instance::bundle_id (paths.rs:37-44, "The Tauri bundle identifier") is unused. Docs still describe the Tauri door: lib.rs:2, serve.rs:1, envelope.rs:261/267 ("mirror is Tauri-channel only" though socket.rs:518-640 streams mirror frames), BUS.md §6.1, §6.5, §7.
findings.impact: app.status tells agents and the CLI that no UI is connected while one is; BUS.md says ui ops fail with ui.absent when headless but they succeed silently; the door rules imply a separate user-only UI door that does not exist (the GTK client shares the socket door with agents). Dead branches cost readers of the dispatch pipeline.
findings.fix: Delete Door::Tauri, Doors/.doors(), Executor/.ui(), ui_connected (or set it from the native client's subscription) and bundle_id, and rewrite BUS.md §6.1/§6.5/§7 and the module docs for the socket-only design.

v1.reason: Door::Tauri (engine.rs:32) is constructed only in tests (tests/bus.rs:108, 114, 220). Its production branches (mail_hint engine.rs:785, the door check engine.rs:822, actor resolution engine.rs:1356) never run. No op uses Doors::TauriOnly: only SocketOnly appears (ops/bus.rs:32, 54, 56), and mcp.rs:161 checks TauriOnly for nothing. `.ui()` sets Executor::Ui (registry.rs:158) on the ui.* ops, but the executor is only echoed into OpInfo (registry.rs:273). handlers/ui.rs answers those ops in-core from `engine.ui` state, with no forwarding and no `ui.absent`, which contradicts BUS.md §6.5 (lines 362-370). Engine.ui_connected is initialized false (engine.rs:446) and never stored anywhere, so app.status (handlers/app.rs:33) always reports `ui_connected: false`. Instance::bundle_id (paths.rs:37-38) is documented as the Tauri bundle id. Module docs at lib.rs:2 (relay-core), relay-bus lib.rs:3, serve.rs:1 and envelope.rs:261/267 still describe a Tauri shell.
v1.correction: Practical impact is small. Nothing in the native client or the CLI reads ui_connected, so the false value only misleads an agent or person reading app.status, and the remaining branches are unreachable. Fix ui_connected (set it, or drop it), delete the dead Tauri branches, and update BUS.md §6.5 together with the module docs. Classing this as docs-drift would fit equally well.

findings.title: Three copies of the MCP stdio server, and three copies of the op-pattern matcher
findings.evidence: mcp.rs:13-74, unreal.rs:22-23/57-110 and blender.rs:19-20/34-87 each define FALLBACK_PROTOCOL and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS (["2026-07-28", "2025-11-25", "2025-06-18"]), the same stdin loop, initialize negotiation, ping/tools/list/tools/call dispatch and JSON-RPC error codes; rpc_error exists in both mcp.rs:214 and unreal.rs:1899, and blender.rs:10 imports `crate::unreal::{rpc_error, tool, tool_result}`, so the Blender server depends on the Unreal module. mcp.rs:109 pattern_matches is a verbatim copy of guardrail::op_matches (guardrail.rs:455) although relay-cli depends on relay-core; socket.rs:208-221 Filter::matches is a third copy.
findings.impact: Adopting a new MCP protocol revision or fixing a framing bug takes three coordinated edits; a missed one leaves one server negotiating an older protocol. A change to op-pattern semantics in the guardrail silently diverges from what RELAY_MCP_OPS selection and bus.subscribe filters accept.
findings.fix: Extract a small `mcp_stdio::serve(server_info, instructions, list_tools, call_tool)` plus rpc_error/tool_result used by all three servers; call relay_core::guardrail::op_matches from mcp.rs and socket.rs.

v1.reason: mcp.rs:13-14, unreal.rs:22-23 and blender.rs:19-20 each define the same FALLBACK_PROTOCOL/SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS. The serve loops (mcp.rs:16-34, unreal.rs:57-76, blender.rs:34-53) are line-for-line identical apart from async. The handle functions repeat the same initialize negotiation, ping, tools/list and tools/call dispatch and the same JSON-RPC codes (-32700/-32602/-32601/-32600). rpc_error is defined in both mcp.rs:214 and unreal.rs:1899, and blender.rs:11 imports `crate::unreal::{rpc_error, tool, tool_result}`. mcp.rs:109 pattern_matches is a body-for-body copy of relay_core::guardrail::op_matches (guardrail.rs:455-462), differing only in `is_some_and` vs `map().unwrap_or(false)`. socket.rs:212-222 Filter::matches has the same semantics. The copies have not diverged yet.
v1.correction: No divergence exists today, so the cost is only the risk of a missed edit. Low is right. The Blender server depending on the Unreal module is a layering smell rather than a bug. Making socket.rs Filter use op_matches is optional, because event names and op names are different namespaces that happen to share the syntax.

findings.title: Driver trait encapsulates little: provider branches live outside it, and profile() is a hand-copied args() that has drifted
findings.evidence: Driver (128-137) has two impls, yet prepare_launch still branches on the provider for hook installation and extra args (session.rs:482-487, 541-548), and usage.rs:20-21, provider_updates.rs:17-20 and validate_options (providers.rs:255-258) match on Provider too. profile() (193-198, 236-241) is a literal JSON description of args(), persisted to provider_cache.spawn_profile on every refresh (338-345) and returned by provider.list, and it already disagrees: both `resume` entries omit the --model / --effort (model_reasoning_effort) flags args() adds on resume (183-188, 222-226). Its only consumer is a test asserting `fresh` is an array (tests/sessions.rs:666). guarded() returns true in both impls.
findings.impact: Adding or changing a provider means edits in six files; provider.list advertises spawn command lines Relay does not run, and a stale copy sits in SQLite until the next refresh.
findings.fix: Either move hook installation, extra args, the usage reader and the effort list into Driver, or drop the trait for one `match provider` module; delete profile()/spawn_profile (or derive it by calling args() on a placeholder session) and guarded().

v1.reason: providers.rs:128-137 defines Driver, and it has exactly two impls (Claude 167-207, Codex 209-247). prepare_launch still branches on the provider outside the trait: session.rs:482-487 for hook and MCP installation, and session.rs:541-548 for codex_notify_config and codex_mcp_config args. usage.rs:20-23, provider_updates.rs:17-20 and validate_options (providers.rs:255-258) match on Provider as well. profile() is a hand-written JSON copy of args() and has already drifted. Both `resume` entries (Claude 195, Codex 238) omit the model/effort flags that args() adds on resume (`args.extend(model_effort_args(session, true))` at 187, and the Codex equivalent at 225). They also omit everything prepare_launch appends: the Codex notify and MCP config and `--add-dir`. The profile is written to provider_cache.spawn_profile on every probe (338-345) and returned in ProviderInfo. Its only consumer in the repo is the array-shape assertion at tests/sessions.rs:666. guarded() returns true in both impls (171, 212).
v1.correction: guarded is not dead: the native UI reads the ProviderInfo.guarded field (launch.rs:651 and tools_settings.rs:388 show 'Unguarded'). Removing the trait method is fine, but the wire field must stay or be set to a constant. The real impact is small: provider.list describes command lines that are incomplete and slightly wrong, and nothing acts on them. The simplest fix is to derive spawn_profile by calling args() with a placeholder Session for Fresh and Resume, or to drop it. Pulling hook installation and the extra Codex args into Driver is optional. This is better filed as code-quality than overengineering.

findings.title: Closed vocabularies are strings at every boundary: ~25 hand-written enum/string tables with silent defaults, and wire fields that skip existing enums
findings.evidence: Conversion fns re-spell relay-bus's serde names by hand (sessions.rs:21-70, task.rs:17-110, audit.rs:71, overlap.rs:22, notify.rs:23); column_str is duplicated verbatim in task.rs:17 and import_v3.rs:39. The parse side maps anything unknown to a default: parse_state `_ => SessionState::Closed` (sessions.rs:45), parse_column -> Backlog, parse_provider -> Claude, parse_role -> Builder. TaskState is never constructed in relay-core — tasks.state is written as SQL literals in task.rs/session.rs — and the live set `'spawning','running','idle','blocked'` is repeated as SQL text five times beside sessions::is_live. On the wire, BootstrapTask has `column: String, state: String` although Column/TaskState exist (ops/session.rs:101-104); device.mirror.input's `event: Value` (ops/device.rs:18) is really relay_core::mirror::InputMsg plus ad-hoc "tap"/"swipe" (handlers/device.rs:925-956); Frame.stream, Run.kind/state and PaneMoveIn.edge are free strings.
findings.impact: Adding a state or column needs coordinated edits the compiler cannot check, and a value one table misses is silently read as Closed/Backlog/Claude instead of failing (a session in a new state would be treated as closed by is_live-based logic). bus.schema, which agents are told to trust rather than guess, shows `string`/`any` for these fields.
findings.fix: Generate as_str()/FromStr for each relay-bus enum from one macro (or serde_plain), use them for SQL parameters and row parsing with an error on unknown values, and type BootstrapTask.column/state, Frame.stream and the mirror input event in relay-bus.

v1.reason: Confirmed parts: sessions.rs:36-46 parse_state ends with `_ => SessionState::Closed`, and parse_provider, parse_role (sessions.rs:53-66) and parse_column/parse_priority (task.rs:25-49) also default silently. column_str is duplicated verbatim in task.rs:17-25 and import_v3.rs:39-47. The live-session set `state IN ('spawning','running','idle','blocked')` is repeated as SQL text in engine.rs:677, recovery.rs:80, notify.rs:178 and session.rs:387/654, with a variant that adds 'parked' at recovery.rs:149. BootstrapTask has `column: String, state: String` (ops/session.rs:101-104). Mitigations: the serialize side is an exhaustive match, so a new variant cannot be forgotten there. tasks.col has a CHECK constraint (store.rs:76) and provider_cache.provider has one (191). All writes go through the code's own *_str functions. So the silent-default path is only hit if a future change misses a parse table, or if an older binary opens a newer database. Today nothing triggers it.
v1.correction: One claim is wrong. 'TaskState is never constructed in relay-core' is false: task.rs:51-70 has state_str and parse_state for TaskState, used at 741, 841, 888 and 903. The concrete, cheap wins are to de-duplicate column_str in import_v3.rs, to name the live-state SQL fragment once next to sessions::is_live, and to type BootstrapTask.column/state as Column/TaskState. A macro or serde_plain for every enum is optional. Impact today is maintenance cost only, with no wrong behavior.

results.coverage: Method: (1) Extracted every op's payload/result field names and required fields from schema/bus.v1.json (221 ops; op list identical to the op! declarations). A script compared all 293 payload!/result! structs in crates/relay-bus/src/ops and every entity struct in types.rs with schema $defs: 0 drift, so the schema is current (the CI test committed_schema_is_current also guards this). (2) Checked 236 literal call("op", json!({...})) payloads in apps/relay-native against the payload schemas. The only differences were project_id/worktree, which Editor::payload() adds. I also reviewed the 154 non-literal call sites by hand (launch, agent_menu, code_git, editor, guardrail pages, settings, onboarding, task/board pages, devices, notifications). (3) A heuristic script checked result-field reads per call site, and another checked every field name the native client reads against all schema property names. The leftovers were settings subtrees, hold details and usage windows. I verified the hold details keys against guardrail.rs. (4) Error codes the clients match on (bus_code, code ==, failure_title) were checked against the codes the engine produces; only device.sdk_missing was unmatched. (5) Events: I listed every emit/emit_system/system_write event in relay-core and compared them with the native subscription list, BUS.md §3.3 and the declared emits. (6) Roles: I compared authorize, callability, bus.ops, session.bootstrap can_call and the MCP tools/list filter with the default role allowlists and the handler-level project checks. (7) Undo: I checked every set_undo inverse against the target op's payload, its rules and audit.rs target_updated_at. (8) Doors: socket.rs special cases, mcp.rs, CLI main.rs (hooks, fill_project) and relay-remote bridge.rs/wire.rs plus the phone payloads in tests/remote.rs. Grep patterns used: register(_unlocked|_staged)?::<, emit(_system)?\(, set_undo\(, invoke_registered, actor_session_id\(\)|not_own\(, code\s*==\s*\"|bus_code, \.output\(\)|wait_with_output, git_mutate\(, worktree::remove\(, meta\.scope|Scope::Project, Door::Tauri|TauriOnly|ui_connected, guardrails\.(workspaces|projects), INTO notifications, \"notify.new\". Not finished or not verifiable: (a) result-field use in the native client was checked heuristically plus spot reads, not line by line across all 33k lines; (b) the Codex PreToolUse tool_input shape for apply_patch/Edit/Write is an external schema I could not verify, so whether codex_pre_tool's required 'command' field exists for those tools is unchecked; (c) the device.rs run/build/mirror workers, import_v3.rs, awareness.rs brief assembly and branch_cleanup.rs were not reviewed for per-field payload use; (d) the relay-cli unreal/blender MCP servers were not reviewed because they are not bus clients; (e) apps/relay-mobile is excluded per scope. Several invariant findings (5, 3, 4) fall outside the strict contract lens but cross module boundaries (shared helper, nested staged ops), so I included them. Nothing was compiled or run.

findings.title: Confirming a hold raised by guardrail.gate never lets the blocked tool call or commit through
findings.evidence: For agents, refuse_or_user_hold turns destructive_write and shape_gate into holds (guardrail.rs:1035 'else if matches!(policy, "destructive_write" | "shape_gate") { hold(...) }'). The Claude PreToolUse adapter sends one guardrail.gate and exits 2 on any non-ok response (relay-cli main.rs:472-483 'if response.ok { return Ok(0); } ... Ok(2)'); the generated git pre-commit hook does the same (hooks.rs:130-132). guardrail.confirm on a frozen guardrail.gate (handlers/guardrail.rs:598-641) only re-runs guardrail::evaluate(... skip_policy: Some(&hold.policy)), returns the verdict as `outcome` to the confirmer, marks the hold confirmed and mails 'Guardrail hold N was confirmed by user' (660). Nothing is recorded that a retry could use: Grants::load reads only op='guardrail.request' holds (grants.rs:51-55) and the hook path always calls gate(ctx, payload, None) (guardrail.rs:304). Held gate errors carry `confirm` but no hint/details.exception (suggestions are added only on refusals, guardrail.rs:1041-1046). The engine's own test shows the retry held again (tests/guardrails.rs:263 held_again). BUS.md:511 promises 'the hook blocks the tool while the verdict is hold'.
findings.impact: An agent rewriting >50 lines / >40% of an uncommitted or untracked file gets its Write blocked as held; the user clicks Allow on the Guardrails page (guardrail_pages.rs:299-305 treats outcome.ok as success) and nothing is written; the agent is told the hold was confirmed, retries, and is held again - an endless loop. The same applies to the user's own `git commit` in a session worktree (user_bypass hold). The documented way out of a hold does nothing.
findings.fix: On confirm of a frozen guardrail.gate, record a one-use grant for that session covering exactly the held policy and payload (path/cap/command) that evaluate_granted honours on the retry, or make the hook wait on bus.wait {events:['guardrail.resolved'], matching:{hold_id}} within its timeout and exit 0 when confirmed. Also attach the exception suggestion/hint to held gate errors so agents know they can use guardrail.request.

v1.reason: For agents, refuse_or_user_hold (guardrail.rs:1034-1035) turns destructive_write and shape_gate into holds. The Claude PreToolUse adapter makes a single guardrail.gate call and returns Ok(2) on any non-ok response (relay-cli main.rs:471-484), and the git pre-commit hook execs the same single call (hooks.rs:128-132). Neither waits, so the tool call or commit has already failed when the hold is created. confirm() for a frozen guardrail.gate (handlers/guardrail.rs:597-665) only re-evaluates the verdict, returns it as `outcome` to the confirmer, marks the hold confirmed and mails 'Guardrail hold N was confirmed'. It writes nothing that a retry can use. Grants::load reads only op='guardrail.request' holds (grants.rs:49-55), and gate() evaluates with skip_policy None (guardrail.rs:304, 511-526), so the agent's retry is held again. The engine's own test shows exactly this (tests/guardrails.rs:262-267, held_again). Held errors carry no exception hint: hints are attached only on the refuse branch (guardrail.rs:1036-1046), even though grants::suggestion supports destructive_write as a Path exception. The Guardrails page reports a successful Allow (guardrail_pages.rs:298-304). BUS.md:500 ('you confirm, it proceeds') and :511 ('the hook blocks the tool while the verdict is hold') promise behaviour that does not exist.
v1.correction: allow_if_recoverable (guardrail.rs:725) limits the destructive_write case to rewrites of uncommitted or untracked files, which is common for agents but not universal. Workarounds exist: an agent that knows about guardrail.request can get a Path grant that covers destructive_write, or it can rewrite through Bash, which is not path-gated. Neither is surfaced by the held error. The user_bypass case on a user's git commit through the hook is likewise unrecoverable: confirming does not make the commit run. Preferred fix: on confirm of a gate hold, record a one-use grant matching the held policy and path that evaluate_granted honours, and attach the guardrail.request hint to held errors.

v2.reason:
(a) I checked this against the code and it holds. For an agent, refuse_or_user_hold (guardrail.rs:1035-1036) turns destructive_write and shape_gate into holds. Those holds carry no hint and no details.exception, because the suggestion code (1040-1046) runs only on the refuse branch. gate() stores a hold with op 'guardrail.gate' (handlers/guardrail.rs:545-565; insert_hold writes request.op at guardrail.rs:1233). The Claude adapter makes one call and returns Ok(2) on any non-ok response (relay-cli main.rs:471-483). It prints neither the hold_id nor the confirm. The pre-commit hook execs a single `relay cmd guardrail.gate`, and exit_for turns Held into a nonzero exit (main.rs:188-192). So the tool call or commit has already failed before anyone can confirm. confirm() for a gate hold (598-666) re-runs evaluate with skip_policy and returns the verdict to the confirmer. It then marks the hold confirmed, writes an audit row of guardrail.gate 'ok' on the agent's behalf, emits guardrail.resolved and mails 'Guardrail hold N was confirmed'. It records nothing a later call reads. Each hook call is a new Request with a new uuid (envelope.rs:122). It goes through evaluate_granted with skip_policy None (304, 511-526), and Grants::load reads only op='guardrail.request' rows (grants.rs:51-53), so the retry is judged from scratch. No other code looks at confirmed gate holds; the only `state='confirmed'` reads are in grants.rs and the requests list.
(b) The trigger is common. Claude agents write with their own Write/Edit/MultiEdit tools, since bus_writes defaults to false and the PreToolUse matcher is installed at hooks.rs:350. The default thresholds are more than 50 lines removed, or more than 40% of a file of 30+ lines (settings.rs:30). allow_if_recoverable lets committed-and-unmodified or ignored files through, so the hold fires on rewrites of untracked or modified files. That is the usual case when an agent re-Writes a file it created or already changed in the session. Shape gates are empty by default. The user_bypass case is the user's own `git commit` from a shell without RELAY_SESSION. It needs more than 40 files or 2000 lines, or a configured protected path. That is rarer, and `--no-verify` or the in-app Git panel get around it; the panel's git.commit hold replays correctly (D141, code_git.rs:1725).
(c) The user clicks "Allow once" on a card that says "<session> is waiting on you". guardrail_pages.rs:299-305 shows no error, because outcome.ok is true, and nothing is written. The audit row says the action was allowed. The agent is told the hold was confirmed. If it retries the same Write, it gets a fresh hold and notification. The agent has three ways out: guess guardrail.request {kind:path}, which works because a Path grant lifts destructive_write (grants.rs:345, guardrail.rs:722); split the change into small Edits; or rewrite through Bash, which is not path-gated and defeats the guardrail. No data is lost.
(d) High is right. The documented way to resolve the default-on flagship guardrail does nothing in a normal agent flow (SPEC §5: "agent gets a typed refusal with a confirm op"; BUS.md:500/§9.4/550). It is not critical, because there is no data loss and workarounds exist.
(e) The proposed fix is the right direction but needs the corrections listed below.
v2.correction: 1. "Endless loop" overstates it. What actually happens is that every retry along the documented path raises a fresh hold and notification, so that path never succeeds. 2. tests/guardrails.rs:263 retries with different new_text ("tiny\n"), not the same payload. It still shows that confirming records nothing that later gates use. 3. BUS.md:511 is ambiguous, and BUS.md:517 itself says the adapter exits 2 on hold. The contract that is actually broken is §9.4/BUS.md:500/550 together with SPEC §5. 4. Fix, grant option: routing through evaluate_granted would not cover the user_bypass commit hook, because evaluate_granted consults grants only for agent actors (guardrail.rs:484). Existing grant kinds cannot lift shape_gate (guardrail.rs:548-559 never consults grants). A Path grant is also broader than the held action: it covers any rewrite of that path, and protected_path/write_root too. A better design: when confirm's re-evaluation returns Allow, mark that gate hold as a one-use pass. In gate(), before evaluating, look for a confirmed, unspent guardrail.gate hold for this session whose frozen payload matches the current one. For writes, match new_text or diff, or a hash of it. For commits, store the numstat at hold time and compare it. If one matches, evaluate with skip_policy = hold.policy and mark the pass spent on Allow. Grant nothing when the confirm returned Refuse or a nested Hold. 5. Fix, wait option: the PreToolUse hook has a 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:351), which is too short for a person to answer. guardrail.resolved reports state "confirmed" even when the confirm's re-evaluation refused or re-held (handlers/guardrail.rs:619-656). So "exit 0 when confirmed" would let through an action the confirm refused, and the outcome is not stored on the hold. Gate holds also have no resolved-event replay (grants::resolved_event covers only op guardrail.request), so the hook must check state before it waits. 6. Attaching the grants::suggestion hint to held agent errors is correct and cheap: suggestion already maps destructive_write to a Path exception. The adapter should also print the hold_id.

findings.title: Desktop launch dialog always sends worktree:"new", so a plugin's default_checkout (D160) never applies to desktop launches
findings.evidence: The Worktree entry is built with .text("new") (launch.rs:259-262); the payload always includes "worktree":self.worktree.text().trim() (346); launch refuses an empty value (784 'Set a worktree for every agent.'). The engine applies the plugin default only when the request omits worktree: p.worktree.as_deref().or(pair_worktree.as_deref()).unwrap_or(prepared.default_checkout) (session.rs:858), default_checkout being "primary" when an enabled plugin asks (plugins.rs:210-215; plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18 "default_checkout": "primary"). D160 (DECISIONS.md:930-935): 'session.create without an explicit worktree then uses the primary checkout ... An explicit worktree still wins.'
findings.impact: In a project with the Unreal Engine plugin on, every agent launched from the desktop (launch sheet, board 'New agents / pair') gets a new pooled worktree instead of the main checkout the editor has open; its C++ lands in the worktree while editor edits land in the main checkout, and the unreal-mcp live tools refuse to act on an editor with a different copy of the project open. Phone-launched agents (no worktree) behave differently from desktop ones.
findings.fix: Default the field to empty ('Default') and omit `worktree` from the session.create payload unless the user typed one (drop the empty refusal at 784), or prefill it from plugin.list for the current project.

v1.reason: launch.rs:258-261 builds the Worktree entry with .text("new"). Profile::payload always includes "worktree": self.worktree.text().trim() (launch.rs:346), and the launch refuses an empty value (launch.rs:784). Only paired group members (index>0) have worktree removed (launch.rs:803), and they inherit the first agent's worktree anyway. The engine applies the plugin default only when no worktree is sent: requested = p.worktree.or(pair_worktree).unwrap_or(prepared.default_checkout) (session.rs:858). default_checkout returns "primary" when an enabled plugin's manifest asks for it (plugins.rs:208-214), and plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json sets "default_checkout": "primary" and promises 'New agents start in the project's main checkout'. The native client never reads default_checkout or plugin settings when launching (rg finds nothing), and commit 7ab2769, which introduced D160, touched no native file. So every desktop launch in an Unreal-enabled project gets a fresh pooled worktree, contrary to D160 (DECISIONS.md:930-935). The unreal-mcp live tools are documented to refuse when the editor has a different copy of the project open, so desktop-launched agents lose the plugin's editor bridge unless the user opens 'Worktree and permissions' and types 'primary'.
v1.correction: The plugin default is at plugins.rs:208-214, not 210-215. The desktop launch sheet is the main way to start agents, so this defeats D160 for the primary client; the workaround (typing 'primary' in the collapsed Advanced field) is undiscoverable. Fix: default the entry to empty with a 'Project default' placeholder, omit worktree from the payload when it is empty, and drop the refusal at launch.rs:784. Or prefill the entry from plugin.get/list for the current project.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. In apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs, lines 259-262 build the Worktree entry with `.text("new")`. Line 346 always puts `"worktree": self.worktree.text().trim()` into the payload, and line 784 refuses an empty value with "Set a worktree for every agent.". Ui::call (app.rs:1111) passes the payload through unchanged. In relay-bus/src/ops/session.rs:10, `worktree` is an `Option<String>`, so "new" arrives as `Some("new")`. At session.rs:858, `p.worktree.as_deref().or(pair_worktree).unwrap_or(prepared.default_checkout)` therefore never reaches the plugin default. The engine's own D160 test (tests/sessions.rs:827) asserts that an explicit "new" gets its own worktree even with the plugin on. Nothing in apps/relay-native reads default_checkout or plugin settings. git blame shows the "new" default (e4a60fcf, 2026-09-04) is older than D160 (7ab2769, 2026-09-22), and the D160 commit touched no native file. So this is a feature that was never wired into the desktop, not a deliberate choice.

(b) Reachability. The launch sheet is the only desktop path that creates sessions. It is opened by the new_session action (shell.rs:1086, app.rs:957) and by the task page's "New agents / pair" button (task_pages.rs:669). Every launch from it, in any project with the Unreal Engine plugin on, hits the bug every time. Only that plugin sets default_checkout (plugin.json:18); Blender does not. This user really is affected: ~/.claude/skills/unreal-fundamentals/.relay-skill contains the stamp "plugin unreal-engine". The materializer writes that stamp only for plugins switched on in at least one project (skills.rs:165-172, plan_user).

(c) What happens. Each desktop-launched agent gets a fresh pooled worktree on a new branch instead of the main checkout. Its C++ goes into that worktree. The 16 LIVE editor tools run guard_project and refuse whenever the human's editor has the main checkout open, which setup.md:49 tells the user to do. The refusal (crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:484) even says "the Unreal plugin does that by default for new agents", which is false for desktop launches. If no editor is running, ue_editor_launch opens the worktree's own .uproject, which has no Binaries and needs a long first build. The agent's asset edits then land on a separate branch, and binary assets cannot be merged. That split is exactly what D160 was written to stop. Nothing is lost or corrupted. The workaround is to expand the collapsed "Worktree and permissions" section and type "primary" for each agent, and nothing in the UI points the user there.

(d) Severity: high is right. In the projects this applies to, the launch flow does the wrong visible thing every time. It defeats a documented feature (D160, plugin README.md:16-21, setup.md:49, the plugin.json description) in the main client and disables the plugin's live tools. It is limited to plugin-enabled projects and causes no data loss, so it is not critical.

(e) The main fix is right: leave the field blank by default, omit `worktree` (or send null) when it is blank, and drop the refusal at 784. The group path at 803 already removes worktree for pair members. The alternative fix (prefill from plugin.list/plugin.get) does not work as written. The bus `Plugin` type (relay-bus/src/types.rs:662-678, built by plugins::to_bus) has no default_checkout field, and copying the rule into the client would duplicate plugins::default_checkout.
v2.correction:
1. Drop the phone-app comparison from the impact; apps/relay-mobile is out of scope.
2. The default lives at plugins.rs:208-215 (doc comment 208-209, fn 210). The engine line is session.rs:858 as cited.
3. Remove the "or prefill it from plugin.list" alternative. plugin.list/plugin.get do not expose default_checkout (relay-bus/src/types.rs:662-678), so it would need a bus type change and would copy engine logic into the client. Recommended fix: an empty Worktree entry with a "Project default" placeholder, worktree omitted or null when blank, and no refusal at launch.rs:784.
4. Also update the placeholder at launch.rs:261 and the hint at launch.rs:590 ("Each solo agent has its own worktree"), which is wrong for plugin projects.
5. Caveat for the fix: review groups in an Unreal project would then also land in the primary checkout. validate_pair (session.rs:764-772) counts builders and reviewers by `worktree=?1`, so solo sessions already in the primary checkout make the second builder of a two-builder group fail with session.review_group_full, or session.pair_exists if another reviewer is there. This is an existing engine issue already reachable with an explicit "primary". Either keep groups on an explicit "new" unless the user chooses otherwise, or count group membership by pair links.
6. Add as evidence: the bridge's refusal text at crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:484 claims "the Unreal plugin does that by default for new agents", which is false for desktop launches.

findings.title: task.dispatch runs session.create/spawn prepare phases (git fetch, worktree add, launch prep) with the store lock held
findings.evidence: task.dispatch is an Engine::register handler; with `create` it calls ctx.invoke_registered("session.create", ...) (task.rs:683), when `start` it calls ctx.invoke_registered(op, json!({"session":name})) for session.spawn/wake/resume (712), and with `fanout` repeats per descendant (1068). invoke_registered runs a staged op's prepare against the already-open transaction (engine.rs:328-351, held: Some(self.tx)) - the code says this nested path is meant to be the rare guardrail.confirm replay (engine.rs:145-149, 325-327). session.create's prepare does refresh_new_worktree -> fetch_remote ('git fetch --all --prune', 20 s timeout, git.rs:938-946), worktree::create ('git worktree add', 120 s timeout incl. LFS, worktree.rs:214) and hooks::install_git (session.rs:858-893); spawn/wake/resume prepare writes hooks, skills and the brief (stage_launch).
findings.impact: The phone's 'New request' sends task.dispatch {create: ...} (relay-remote/tests/remote.rs:311-314), and the desktop 'Dispatch' to a created/parked session takes the launch path. For the whole fetch + checkout (seconds; up to ~140 s on slow networks or LFS repos, times fanout) every other request queues on the mutex: other agents' guardrail.gate hooks (30 s timeout) fail closed, session.report and MCP calls stall, the desktop UI freezes.
findings.fix: Register task.dispatch with register_staged and perform the session.create / launch prepare work in its unlocked prepare phase (create checkouts first), leaving only assignment and PTY start in the transaction; or have the client create the session separately (as the desktop launcher does) and dispatch with start:false.

3. "Gates fail closed" is not established. The relay CLI's pre-tool hook has no timeout of its own (main.rs:466-471), so gates wait. They are killed only if the hold passes Claude's 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:351), and what happens then is decided by Claude Code, not by Relay's exit-2 path (main.rs:352-355).
4. Unreal projects with the unreal-engine plugin enabled default to the primary checkout (plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18, D160): no fetch and no worktree add. The 120 s LFS case therefore applies to non-Unreal LFS repos.
5. Add docs drift: D149 (DECISIONS.md:816-819) says the nested prepare runs only for guardrail.confirm.

Fix: moving session.create's prepare into a staged task.dispatch prepare works. That prepare needs only the payload plus short ctx.read calls. For fanout, read the descendants with ctx.read, fetch once per repo instead of once per child, and keep every PreparedCreate reservation alive until finish. Re-validate the task's state in finish, and if finish refuses, uninstall the hooks the way session.create's finish closure does (session.rs:897-912).

"Leave only assignment and PTY start in the transaction" does not work as written. stage_launch/plan_launch reads the session row by name and builds the brief, which includes the task assignment, from the store, and both the row and the assignment exist only inside finish. Two workable options:
- Keep prepare_launch in finish. The remaining cost is small: 4 `git config` calls plus file and skill writes.
- Commit create and assign first, then start the provider through a separately dispatched staged session.spawn after the commit (the D133 launcher shape). This gives up atomicity.

The alternative "the client creates the session first" fixes only the phone, which is out of scope, and leaves the engine op slow for every other caller.

Separate root cause, noted for the rewrite: a nested failure later in the same dispatch rolls back the session row but leaves the new worktree, branch and hook config on disk. An example is `provider.not_installed` from the nested spawn's plan_launch (providers.rs:286-289).

findings.title: project.clone runs git clone synchronously and untimed inside its locked handler although its contract says async
findings.evidence: e.register::<ProjectClone> (workspace.rs:231) runs Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output() (234): no proc::output_with_timeout, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, inside the request transaction, then invoke_registered("project.add"). The op's summary promises 'Clone a repo into the workspace and register it (async; project.changed when done)' (crates/relay-bus/src/ops/workspace.rs:38). The native client compensates with a 30-minute request timeout (client.rs:67 '"project.clone" => Duration::from_secs(1800)') and calls it from onboarding (onboarding.rs:527).
findings.impact: Cloning a large or slow repository from desktop onboarding holds the single store mutex for the whole clone: every agent's hooks, MCP calls and UI requests block for minutes; a credential helper prompt or a stalled network blocks the engine indefinitely.
findings.fix: Implement the contract: validate, return immediately, clone on a worker under proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, then register through system_write and emit project.changed; at minimum make it register_staged so the clone runs unlocked.

v1.reason: workspace.rs:228 registers ProjectClone with plain `e.register`, so the store mutex and the transaction are held. Line 234 runs `Command::new("git").current_dir(..).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()`: it has no proc::output_with_timeout, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and no null stdin, while other git calls do set these (worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943, git.rs:1349). The op metadata (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38) says 'async; project.changed when done', but the handler is synchronous. The native client works around it with `"project.clone" => Duration::from_secs(1800)` (client.rs:67) and calls it from onboarding (onboarding.rs:527) for GitHub repos. The repo's own perf runs record about 4 s for a tiny local clone (docs/perf/runs/2026-09-19/strace.log:26).
v1.correction: Real effect: for the whole network clone, every other bus request queues behind the mutex, including agents' guardrail.gate hooks (which fail closed on their timeout), session.report and UI refreshes. A credential or askpass prompt, or a stalled transfer, holds it with no time limit. Minimum fix: make it register_staged, running the clone in the unlocked prepare phase through output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. The finish phase then calls project.add. Alternatively make it truly async, as documented. Note that tests/phase12.rs:114 depends on the clone using the workspace as its CWD; keep that.

The lock is a plain std Mutex (store.rs:474). Line 234 runs `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone")...output()` with no proc::output_with_timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Other git calls in the codebase do set that variable (worktree.rs:213, git.rs:943, git.rs:1349). The op summary says "async; project.changed when done" (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38), and BUS.md:246-250 promises a `project.clone.completed` audit row. No such row exists. This is an oversight, not a design choice: D144 says long-running work goes through after_commit plus a worker thread, and D149's list of converted ops (DECISIONS.md:809-813) leaves out project.clone. git history records no reason for keeping it synchronous.

(b) Who can trigger it and how often. The op is user-only. The native "Add project" dialog calls it whenever the user picks a GitHub repo (onboarding.rs:527). This is not just first-run onboarding. The same dialog opens from the sidebar "+" (app.rs:976), the workspace "+" (registry.rs:352) and the workspace menu "Add project…" (registry.rs:472). Its text reads "Register another repository in this workspace … or clone it from GitHub" (onboarding.rs:115). So it runs while agents in other projects are live. It is an occasional but normal flow.

(c) What happens when it fires. The lock is held for the whole network clone: seconds for a small repo, minutes for a typical one, and possibly tens of minutes for a large LFS game repo. The client already allows 1800 s for it (client.rs:67). Every agent request takes the store lock just to check its token (engine.rs:1378). That includes the PreToolUse guardrail.gate on Bash/Edit/Write, which has a 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:351) and no client-side timeout (socket.rs:801). Keystrokes and PTY output are not affected: they use the D148 fast path, and pty.rs never takes the store lock.

(d) Severity. This is a freeze of the bus in a normal flow, which the rubric rates high. It is not critical: it ends when the clone ends, and the indefinite variants depend on the environment.

v2.correction:
Accuracy fixes:
- The register call is at line 228, not 231.
- `.output()` already gives the child a null stdin (the Rust std default), so the first verifier's "no null stdin" is wrong.
- A credential prompt reaches the user only through /dev/tty or an askpass helper. /dev/tty applies when the engine was started by run.sh from a terminal, because nohup does not detach it from the controlling terminal. When the engine is launched from the desktop entry with no askpass helper, git fails at once. So the "indefinite hang" is environment-dependent; the reliable trigger is simply how long the clone takes.
- When the provider's hook times out at 30 s, it decides whether the tool call is refused or allowed to run unchecked. relay-cli fails closed only on errors it sees itself (main.rs:349-356). I could not establish the provider's choice from the repo. Either outcome disrupts agents.
