- register_staged alone frees the store but not the desktop UI. The engine serves each socket connection one request at a time (socket.rs:335 loop, which awaits each dispatch at :742). Ui::call sends project.clone on the shared main connection (app.rs:1111-1116); only is_lifecycle_request ops get their own connection (client.rs:50-62, 131-139). Every other UI request made during the clone would still queue behind it and hit the 30 s timeout. The fix must also move project.clone onto its own connection (add it to is_lifecycle_request) or make the op truly async.
- In the staged prepare phase:
  - use output_with_timeout with a generous deadline, comparable to the client's 1800 s;
  - set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0;
  - keep current_dir(&workspace.path), which phase12.rs:114 depends on;
  - remove the partial destination when the deadline SIGKILLs git. A killed git cannot clean up, so a retry would fail with project.clone_destination (workspace.rs:231-232).
- The finish phase can still invoke_registered("project.add").
- If the op is made truly async, these must change together: ProjectCloneOut, onboarding.rs:527-528 (which reads value["project"]), and the completion audit row. Otherwise, correct the op summary (ops/workspace.rs:38) and BUS.md:246-247 to say the op is synchronous.

findings.title: worktree::git_mutate has no timeout and runs inside many Engine::register handlers (plus other untimed subprocess / tree-walk work under the lock)
findings.evidence: fn git(...) { let out = Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output() (worktree.rs:27) - no proc::output_with_timeout, inherited stdin, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. Called with the store mutex held from git.commit's finish phase 'git commit --no-verify' (git.rs:571), git.stage (503), git.unstage (527), git.branch.create 'switch -c' (374), git.branch.delete (485), git.branch.clean_merged (712), file.restore_head 'checkout --' (file.rs:256) and integration.discard (integration.rs:64). The same mistake elsewhere: worktree::remove (purge_build + dir_size tree walk + 'git worktree remove', worktree.rs:352-369) from locked worktree.remove (git.rs:139) and integration.discard (integration.rs:62), whereas session.close/discard_restorable deliberately stage that work (session.rs:1503-1504); avd.create child.wait_with_output() (device.rs:335); git.pr.open 'gh pr create ... .output()' (git.rs:666-683); workspace.discover's depth-4 directory walk (workspace.rs:114-130, 393-413), which onboarding runs on the app's CWD (often $HOME) when it opens.
findings.impact: A commit from the Code view with commit.gpgsign (pinentry waits for the passphrase), an LFS smudge during switch -c / checkout --, a slow gh call, avdmanager, or deleting a multi-GB worktree holds the one store connection for its duration (forever if git waits for input). Every other request - agents' guardrail.gate hooks (30 s), session.report, UI refreshes - queues behind it and hooks fail closed. Violates CLAUDE.md 'Every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout' and the no-slow-work-under-register rule.
findings.fix: Route worktree::git through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and stdin null, and move the slow halves (git commit/add/switch/checkout, worktree removal, avdmanager, gh pr create, the discovery walk) into register_staged prepare phases or register_unlocked queries, as already done for session.close and git.branch.switch.

v1.reason:
worktree.rs:26-36: git()/git_mutate run `Command::new("git")...output()` with no timeout, inherited stdin and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. worktree::add in the same file (213-215) does use output_with_timeout, so the two paths have diverged. These run under the store lock in plain `register` handlers:
- git.branch.create (git.rs:345/374)
- git.branch.delete (445/485)
- git.stage (490/503)
- git.unstage (507/527)
- git.clean_merged (693/712)
- file.restore_head (file.rs:253/256)
- integration.discard (integration.rs:58-64)
- the finish phase of git.commit (git.rs:571, `git commit --no-verify` after guardrail::enforce)

The same applies to worktree.remove (git.rs:129-139), which runs worktree::remove (purge_build, a dir_size walk, remove_dir_all and `git worktree remove --force`) under the lock. session.discard_restorable deliberately stages the same work, with the comment at session.rs:1503-1504. Also under the lock: git.pr.open runs `gh pr create ... .output()` (git.rs:666-680), a network call; avd.create runs `child.wait_with_output()` (device.rs:321-335) without a timeout; workspace.discover (workspace.rs:114-130) walks directories to depth 4 under `register` even though it never touches ctx.
v1.correction: The most serious cases are the ones that are slow in normal use: gh pr create (network), worktree.remove on a large worktree with build dirs (tree walk plus deleting gigabytes), avd.create, and workspace.discover over $HOME. These freeze the bus for seconds to minutes. git add, commit, switch and checkout are usually fast, but they hang indefinitely on gpgsign/pinentry, LFS or credential prompts. Smaller related issue: git.push (git.rs:617) and the git.commit prepare phase use the same untimed git_mutate. They run unlocked, so they hang only their own request, not the bus. Fix: route git() through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Move worktree.remove, pr.open, avd.create and the slow halves to register_staged, and make workspace.discover register_unlocked. git.commit's finish phase may intentionally keep the commit atomic with enforce; give it a timeout at least.

v2.reason:
(a) The core claim holds. worktree.rs:26-36 `git()`/`git_mutate` run `Command::new("git")...output()` with no deadline. Plain `register` handlers run with `self.store.lock()` held across `(h.call)` (engine.rs:954-980). The following call untimed subprocesses or walk trees inside such handlers:
- git.branch.create `switch -c` (git.rs:374), git.branch.delete (485), git.stage (503), git.unstage (527), git.branch.clean_merged (712), file.restore_head (file.rs:256), and git.commit's finish `git commit --no-verify` (git.rs:571).
- git.pr.open runs `gh pr create ... .output()` (git.rs:666-681). This is a network call.
- avd.create calls `wait_with_output()` (device.rs:335).
- worktree.remove (git.rs:139) and integration.discard (integration.rs:62) both call purge_build, dir_size and `git worktree remove` (worktree.rs:352-369). session.close and session.discard_restorable deliberately stage this same work (session.rs:1503-1504).
- workspace.discover walks to depth 4 (workspace.rs:114-130, 393-413). It never uses ctx and is a Query.
This breaks D144 ("every subprocess ... output_with_timeout"). D149 names `gh`, `git` and recursive walks as slow work that must run unlocked, yet git.pr.open, avd.create and workspace.discover were never converted.

(b) Reachability from the native UI:
- Code view "Publish a pull request": git.pr.open (code_git.rs:662/1240). This is the clearest normal-flow trigger: a few seconds of GitHub round-trips on every PR, and unbounded if the network stalls.
- "Stage all changes" sends every changed path to git.stage (code_git.rs:474-483). LFS clean filters on large assets then run under the lock, which is relevant to this user's Unreal work.
- Branch create with a start point (checkout plus LFS smudge), branch delete, and commit.
- Devices: avd.create (tools_devices.rs:419) and avd.boot.
- Onboarding: workspace.discover on the app's CWD (onboarding.rs:73-80, 336).
Agents with bus_writes can also reach stage, unstage and commit.

(c) While the child runs:
- Every agent request blocks. check_session_token takes the store lock for every agent call (engine.rs:1378), and guardrail.gate is a plain register handler (guardrail.rs:304). So every running agent's PreToolUse hook and MCP call stalls.
- Session lifecycle connections, the phone door and background workers also stall.
- User keystrokes and PTY output are not affected (fast path, no store lock).
If the child never exits, the engine thread stays parked holding the mutex after the UI's 30 s client timeout. That happens with a stalled `gh` connection, gpg pinentry, an LFS credential prompt, or a /dev/tty prompt; `relay serve` is started by hand (app.rs:1282), possibly from a terminal, and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT is unset.

(d) High is correct: a bus-wide freeze in a normal flow (pr.open on every PR; stage/branch work on LFS repos). It is not critical, because the indefinite hang needs uncommon conditions.

(e) The fix is right in direction but needs the caveats listed under correction.
v2.correction:
Corrections to the evidence:
1. "Inherited stdin" is wrong. `Command::output()` defaults stdin to null, so git cannot block on stdin. Unbounded waits come from /dev/tty prompts (no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), GUI pinentry or askpass, LFS transfers, user prepare-commit-msg/post-commit hooks, and stalled `gh` network calls.
2. These ops have no caller in apps/relay-native: worktree.remove, integration.discard, git.branch.clean_merged and file.restore_head (UserOnly). They are reachable only via `relay q`, a paired phone, or tests. The "delete a multi-GB worktree" scenario is therefore a rare path, not a normal flow.
3. Remove these from `related`:
   - device.rs:150 is an in-memory lease check, and device.run's adb probe (:152) is bounded at 2 s via output_with_timeout, which D144 allows.
   - git.rs:617 (git.push) runs in an unlocked prepare phase, so it hangs only its own request.
4. Add avd.boot to `related`: device.rs:346 calls list_avds under the lock, which runs an untimed `emulator -list-avds` (device.rs:478) and an untimed `adb emu avd name` (device.rs:505). avd.create also calls list_avds (device.rs:339).
5. Impact wording: the UI control-plane socket is served one request at a time (socket.rs:335 loop), so the user's own UI queue stalls whether or not the lock is held. The lock-specific harm is to all agents, lifecycle connections, the phone door and background workers. "Hooks fail closed" holds only for Relay's own CLI error path. What the host does when its 30 s hook timeout fires is host-defined and unverified.

Corrections to the fix:
- Do not put one short timeout on all of `git()`. git.push (unlocked network) and `git worktree remove --force` on large trees legitimately run long. Use per-call deadlines plus GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and note that killing a mutating git can leave .git/index.lock behind.
- git.commit: D149 lists it as converted, and it deliberately keeps `git commit` beside guardrail::enforce in finish. guardrail.confirm also replays held commits through invoke_registered. Moving the commit into prepare would commit before the gate, which bypasses the guardrail. Give it a timeout only.
- Convert to register_staged: git.pr.open, avd.create, avd.boot, git.stage, git.unstage, git.branch.create, git.branch.delete, clean_merged, file.restore_head, worktree.remove and integration.discard. Read ownership through ctx.read, as git.branch.switch already does.
- workspace.discover can become register_unlocked directly, since it is a Query.
- Bound list_avds_with and running_avds_with.

findings.title: Agents are not confined to their own project or worktree on file.*/git.* (bus_writes) and integration.request
findings.evidence: Layer-2 authorization scopes only payload `session` and `task_id` (guardrail.rs:328-349); OpMeta.scope (Scope::Project) is never enforced anywhere in relay-core. default_worktree_in honours an explicit worktree for agents: 'Some(PROJECT_ROOT) => Ok(repo), Some(path) => Ok(PathBuf::from(path))' (file.rs:399-400), and root_verify only checks the path is a worktree of the *requested* project (file.rs:427-441); git uses the same resolver (git.rs:751, 768). file.* and git.stage/unstage/commit are allowed whenever session.bus_writes (guardrail.rs:363-366), which the desktop launcher enables by default (launch.rs:265 writes.set_active(true)) and the agent menu mislabels as 'Let this agent change tasks, notes and settings through Relay' (agent_menu.rs:497). integration.request is in the builder baseline (settings.rs:36) and takes any project_id (integration.rs:16-17). By contrast notes/mailbox (notes.rs:47-60 assert_actor_project), overlap (overlap.rs:66-80) and session.list (D106) do confine agents; guardrail.check/explain judge the caller's own worktree even for another project's id (handlers/guardrail.rs:155, 182).
findings.impact: A builder with bus_writes can file.write {project_id: <other>, worktree: "@project", path, text} into another project's main checkout, or into a peer session's worktree in its own project, and git.commit there - the exact writes the PreToolUse gate refuses as guardrail.write_root for the same agent's Write/Edit tools (D102). Any agent can file.read/file.search/git.diff every registered project, and integration.request {project_id: other} builds and deploys another project. D111 tells agents '@project' is how to reach the project root.
findings.fix: For agent actors, require payload project_id to equal the session's project and restrict an explicit `worktree` to the session's own (or PAIR partner's) worktree for mutations, ideally once in authorize/root resolution (enforcing OpMeta.scope generically); correct the bus_writes description in the agent menu.

v1.reason: default_worktree_in (file.rs:391-410) returns the repo root for `@project` and `PathBuf::from(path)` for any explicit worktree, whoever the caller is. root_verify (file.rs:427-441) checks only that the path is a worktree of the project the payload names. authorize (guardrail.rs:316-376) looks only at payload `session` and `task_id`; nothing enforces Scope::Project. For mutations it allows file.* and git.stage/unstage/commit whenever session.bus_writes is set (guardrail.rs:363-366). The launcher defaults that switch on (launch.rs:263-264), and the agent menu describes it as 'change tasks, notes and settings' (agent_menu.rs:497). The file.write handler (file.rs:72-101) runs guardrail::enforce with `worktree = root`, the chosen root, so write_target treats a relative path as InWorktree and the write_root policy the PreToolUse gate applies (guardrail.rs:625-665) never fires. integration.request is in the builder baseline (settings.rs:36) and takes any project_id (integration.rs:16-17). Trigger: a builder with default bus_writes calls file.write {project_id: other, worktree: "@project", path, text}, and the write lands in another project's main checkout with no hold or refusal.
v1.correction: This is not a hard sandbox boundary. The Exec gate (guardrail.rs:828-840) checks only denied_commands substrings, so an agent's Bash tool can already write outside its worktree. The practical risk is a confused agent, steered by D111's advice to use `@project`, writing to or committing on the main checkout or a peer's worktree through the bus, without the write_root confinement its Write/Edit tools get. Medium is right. Fix: for agent actors, require payload project_id to equal the session's project, and for mutations accept only the session's own (or PAIR partner's) worktree. Also correct the agent-menu wording.

findings.title: audit.list / audit.get give every agent the payloads that guardrail.hold.get and task.activity reserve for the user
findings.evidence: op!(List, "audit.list", ..., OpMeta::query(Scope::Global, 1, ...)) and op!(Get, "audit.get", ...) (ops/audit.rs:13, 16) default to Actors::All, and authorize returns Ok for every query (guardrail.rs:350-352). The handlers return stored payloads unfiltered (handlers/audit.rs:30-47; audit.rs:216-226). Meanwhile guardrail.hold.get is UserOnly (ops/guardrail.rs:29-30) with a test asserting 'an agent must not inspect another actor's frozen action' (tests/guardrails.rs:166-169), and task.activity - task-scoped audit history - is UserOnly (ops/task.rs:34-35). The held request's payload is audited (engine.rs:1040-1057); session.create/spawn payloads carry `prompt`, which D101 treats as delivered privately by session.bootstrap; mailbox.send, file.write and guardrail.gate new_text bodies are stored up to 64 KiB.
findings.impact: Any agent of any role and project can call audit.list {op_prefix:"guardrail.gate"} or {op_prefix:"session.create"} and read other sessions' frozen actions, file contents being written in other projects, private mail between other sessions, and every agent's launch assignment - exactly what the UserOnly gates were meant to withhold.
findings.fix: Make audit.list/audit.get UserOnly, or for agent actors restrict rows to the caller's own session and redact payload/result_summary otherwise, consistent with guardrail.hold.get and task.activity.

v1.reason: ops/audit.rs:13 and :16 declare audit.list / audit.get as OpMeta::query with no .actors(), so Actors::All. Their payloads have no `session` name or `task_id` field (only `session_id: Option<Id>`), so the own-session and own-task checks in guardrail::authorize (guardrail.rs:328-349) never fire, and `if entry.meta.kind == OpKind::Query { return Ok(()) }` (guardrail.rs:350) lets them through. handlers/audit.rs:29-47 call log::list/log::get with no actor-based filtering, and row_to_audit (audit.rs:164-193) returns the stored `payload` and `result_summary`. engine.rs stores req.payload (the token is kept separately in req.token, so it is not exposed). A frozen guardrail.gate's new_text, session.create prompts and mailbox bodies are all in that payload column, up to 64 KiB (audit.rs:14). guardrail.hold.get is UserOnly (ops/guardrail.rs:29-30), and a test asserts that an agent must not inspect another actor's frozen action (tests/guardrails.rs:169). task.activity is UserOnly too (ops/task.rs:34-35). So audit.list {op_prefix:"guardrail.gate"} undoes that intent. The live engine here even offers audit_list as an MCP tool to agent sessions.
v1.correction: The real leak is smaller than claimed. Agents can already file.read and git.diff other projects (see lens-contract#6), so the new exposure is mainly frozen held content, other sessions' launch prompts and private mail. Fix: for agent actors, either make the ops UserOnly or force session_id to the caller's own session and drop payload/result_summary from rows that belong to other sessions. The board's own audit.list call runs as the user, so it is unaffected.

findings.title: ui.pane.* / ui.window.* succeed against an engine-side model the desktop never renders; BUS.md §6.5 forwarding and ui.absent are not implemented
findings.evidence: ui.pane.open pushes a PaneInfo into the in-memory engine.ui (UiRuntime), returns 'pane-N' and emits ui.changed with that model (ui.rs:67-96); `PaneOpenIn.at` is never read; ui.pane.move emits {"move":{...}} instead of state (180); ui.window.popout invents 'popout-N' (262-291). Nothing forwards to a UI: the GTK client's ui.changed handler only switches page/project and focuses a terminal when a focused pane targets a session (shell.rs:438-463). BUS.md §6.5 (361-372): ui.* ops are 'forwarded to the UI client ... If no UI is connected (headless), they return unavailable / ui.absent. This is how an agent opens a diff pane'. Engine::ui_connected is never set (engine.rs:406, 446), so app.status.ui_connected is always false (app.rs:33).
findings.impact: An allow_ui agent calling the documented ui.pane.open {kind:"diff", target:{sha}}, or ui.pane.move/close/ui.window.popout, gets success and ids for panes/windows that never appear; ui.state reports the engine's bookkeeping rather than what the window shows; headless engines never answer ui.absent.
findings.fix: Either implement §6.5 (the native client registers as executor and answers ui.* ops; core returns ui.absent when none is connected and tracks ui_connected), or narrow the contract: refuse pane kinds/ops the desktop does not honour with not_implemented and document the page/terminal-focus subset.

v1.reason: ui.pane.open (ui.rs:67-96) only pushes a PaneInfo into the in-memory engine.ui model, returns `pane-N` and emits ui.changed. The GTK client's handler for that event, apply_ui_event (shell.rs:438-463, dispatched from app.rs:1247), only acts on `page`/`project_id` and on a focused pane whose target is a session. A diff/file/note/run/mirror pane, a pane move (ui.rs:180 emits {move:...}, which the handler ignores) and a popout window are never rendered, yet the op reports success. The op is reachable by agents the user grants 'UI control', a toggle the desktop exposes (agent_menu.rs:498, launch.rs:346). Engine::ui_connected is initialised false (engine.rs:446) and never stored to anywhere, so app.status.ui_connected is always false.
v1.correction: The §6.5 forwarding model is not simply missing. It was deliberately replaced by D40 (DECISIONS.md:146-149): core owns the page, pane and window state spine and the shell mirrors ui.changed. That decision was written for the old Svelte shell. The real defect is that the GTK shell mirrors only page and session focus, so most pane and window ops return success with no visible effect, and BUS.md §6.5 and ui_connected are stale. The better fix is the narrowing option: refuse pane kinds and ops the native shell does not honour with not_implemented, or have the shell render them. Then update BUS.md §6.5 to D40's model and either set ui_connected when the native client subscribes or remove the field.

findings.title: audit.undo records inverses it can never execute (workspace.update, session.update, task.move out of done) and an incomplete one for notify.settings.set
findings.evidence: The staleness check maps only task./module./notes./project.update/skill. ops to a table and returns Ok(None) otherwise (audit.rs:11-23); undo then fails when actual != Some(expected) (59-63). workspace.update records expect {updated_at} (workspace.rs:144-146) and so does session.update (session.rs:1474-1477), so both always fail audit.stale without force. session.update's inverse always carries "branch": s.branch (a string), which the handler refuses after first spawn (session.rs:1435-1436 'if spawned && (p.branch.is_some() || ...) -> session.already_spawned'), so even force fails for any post-spawn edit such as toggling bus_writes. task.move records the inverse task.move {column: before.column} (task.rs:905); for a card moved out of Done that is column "done", which task.move refuses (task.rs:897) - reachable from the board's Ctrl+Z (board_view.rs:875-892). notify.settings.set's inverse is {"patch": before} applied with merge_value (notify.rs:150), so keys the original patch added are never removed.
findings.impact: audit.undo of a workspace rename or a session option change always errors; dragging a card from Done back to In review and pressing Ctrl+Z shows 'move to done through task.approve'; undoing a notification-settings change silently leaves part of it in place.
findings.fix: Add workspaces and sessions to target_updated_at (or keep an op-to-table map next to set_undo), emit session.update inverses with only the fields that changed, record a dedicated inverse for moves out of done, and use guardrail::inverse_patch(before, next) for notify.settings.set.

v1.reason: target_updated_at (handlers/audit.rs:10-25) knows only task.*, module.*, notes.*, project.update and skill.*. For any other op it returns Ok(None), and undo then compares `actual.as_deref() != Some(expected)` (audit.rs:58-63), which always raises audit.stale. workspace.update (workspace.rs:144-146) and session.update (session.rs:1474-1477) both record an `expect: {updated_at}`, so undoing either always fails without force. With force, the session.update inverse always carries `"branch": s.branch` (a String, so p.branch.is_some()), and session.rs:1435 refuses that with session.already_spawned once the session has spawned. task.move records `column: column_str(before.column)` (task.rs:905), and task.move refuses Column::Done (task.rs:897). A user can move a Done card to InReview (task.rs:902 handles that case), and the board's Ctrl+Z (board_view.rs:872-892) picks the latest undoable task.* row, so undo then shows 'move to done through task.approve'. The notify.settings.set inverse is `{"patch": before}` (notify.rs:150), applied with merge_value (settings.rs:104-117). merge_value removes a key only when the patch value is null, so keys added by the original patch survive the undo.
v1.correction: Only the task.move-out-of-Done case is reachable from the UI (board Ctrl+Z, which lists only task.* rows). The workspace, session and notify undos are reachable only through `relay cmd audit.undo`. That keeps this at medium, not high. A task.move inverse for a card that was in Done should restore the column through a direct state restore (or task.approve), not through task.move. Use guardrail::inverse_patch(before, next) for notify.settings.set.

findings.title: settings.set / settings.reset write guardrails.* without guardrail.config.set's validation, so one bad value breaks every agent
findings.evidence: SettingsSet writes any valid dotted path, guardrails included: set(ctx.tx(), &p.path, &p.value, ...) (settings.rs:217-219); SettingsReset deletes the subtree (225-229). guardrail.config.set rejects nested projects/workspaces keys (handlers/guardrail.rs:46) and validates the merged result via config_for -> typed -> validate_config (guardrail.rs:193-198, 292-312). The same rows are read on every agent mutation (authorize: 'let cfg = config(conn, Some(session.project_id))?;' guardrail.rs:358), by every guardrail.gate evaluation (466-467) and by session.bootstrap (awareness.rs:476).
findings.impact: relay cmd settings.set '{"path":"guardrails.caps.files","value":0}' (or a non-array protected_paths, an unknown shape validator) is accepted; afterwards every agent mutation, every guardrail.gate hook call (failing closed, so all Bash/Write/Edit are blocked) and session.bootstrap fail with invalid/guardrail.config until the setting is repaired by hand. settings.reset {path:"guardrails"} also silently drops every workspace and project guardrail layer.
findings.fix: Refuse settings.set/reset under the `guardrails` prefix (pointing at guardrail.config.set), or run the same typed validation on the resulting tree before committing.

v1.reason: SettingsSet writes any valid dotted path (settings.rs:215-222) and SettingsReset deletes any subtree (224-233), with no check on the `guardrails` prefix. guardrail.config.set refuses nested projects/workspaces keys (handlers/guardrail.rs:46) and validates the merged result. config_for -> typed -> validate_config (guardrail.rs:71-75, 193-198, 292-312) rejects caps.files==0, a non-array protected_paths (serde) and unknown validators. That same config() call runs in authorize for every agent mutation not covered by grants::OP (guardrail.rs:358) and in evaluate (guardrail.rs:466), so a bad global value makes those fail with invalid/guardrail.config. Reachability is narrower than claimed: settings.set and settings.reset are Actors::UserOnly (relay-bus ops/notify.rs:24,27), so agents cannot call them. The phone door does not expose them, and the native client never calls settings.reset or settings.set under guardrails.* (its guardrail UI uses guardrail.config.set, guardrail_settings.rs:368). The only trigger is the user hand-typing the op via the CLI, and it can be undone (Undo::Inverse) or overwritten.
v1.correction: Downgraded to low: it is a self-inflicted footgun reachable only from the user's own CLI, with undo available. It is still worth a small fix: refuse `guardrails`/`guardrails.*` paths in settings.set and settings.reset and point to guardrail.config.set, or run guardrail::typed on the resulting effective tree before commit.

findings.title: workspace.remove leaves its guardrail layer behind; the next workspace that reuses the id inherits it
findings.evidence: WsRemove deletes only the row: 'DELETE FROM workspaces WHERE id = ?1' (workspace.rs:178). The layer lives in settings under guardrails.workspaces.{id} (handlers/guardrail.rs:69) and guardrail::layers applies it to every project whose workspace has that id (guardrail.rs:107, 129-130). workspaces.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT (store.rs:46-47), so SQLite reuses the highest id. project.remove does delete its own layer (workspace.rs:378-379); workspace.remove has no counterpart.
findings.impact: Remove the newest workspace and create another: it gets the same id and silently inherits the deleted workspace's caps, protected paths, denied commands and role allowlists (possibly looser than global), shown by guardrail.config.layers as the new workspace's own overrides.
findings.fix: Delete guardrails.workspaces.{id} and guardrails.workspaces.{id}.% (with LIKE escaping) in workspace.remove; consider AUTOINCREMENT for workspaces and projects.

v1.reason: workspace.rs:178: WsRemove ends with only `DELETE FROM workspaces WHERE id = ?1`. The workspace layer is stored as leaf rows under `guardrails.workspaces.{id}` (handlers/guardrail.rs:69, written via settings::set, which flattens into `path.*` leaves). project.remove deletes `guardrails.projects.{id}.%` (workspace.rs:378-379), but nothing in the crate deletes `guardrails.workspaces.*`: rg finds only guardrail.rs:107 and handlers/guardrail.rs:69. store.rs:46 declares `workspaces.id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` without AUTOINCREMENT, unlike the later tables, so SQLite hands out max(rowid)+1 again after the newest workspace is deleted. guardrail::layers (guardrail.rs:107-130) then applies any `guardrails.workspaces.{id}.*` row to the new workspace and to every project in it.
v1.correction: Trigger: remove the workspace with the highest id, then create or onboard another. The new one gets that id and inherits the old caps, protected paths, denied commands and allowlists. If the old layer was looser than global, guardrails are silently weaker. This needs a user action (removal, then re-creation), so medium is right. Fix: in WsRemove, delete `path = 'guardrails.workspaces.{id}' OR path LIKE 'guardrails.workspaces.{id}.%' ESCAPE '\'`; handlers/guardrail.rs:30 already has delete_settings_under, which can be reused. Even without id reuse, the orphaned rows pile up.

findings.title: Agent menu Save sends model:""/effort:"" for unspawned sessions, which session.update rejects
findings.evidence: The Model/Effort entries show the current value with placeholders 'Provider default'/'Default' (agent_menu.rs:478-479); for a not-yet-spawned session the save always adds payload["model"] = model.text() and payload["effort"] = effort.text() (545-548). session.update turns a present model into Some(...) and calls validate_options (session.rs:1438-1441), which refuses an empty model ('invalid session.model: model cannot be empty', providers.rs:253-254) and any effort outside the provider's list (256-266). UpdateIn.model/effort are plain Option<String> (ops/session.rs:143-146), so the bus cannot express 'back to provider default'.
findings.impact: For a session still in `created` (an interrupted launch, or one staged by the phone with start:false) whose model was left at provider default, any Save in the agent menu - even just toggling 'Agent bus writes' - fails with 'model cannot be empty'; a model, once set, can never be cleared back to the default.
findings.fix: Send model/effort only when changed and non-empty; make UpdateIn.model/effort nullable (Option<Option<String>> with relay_bus::nullable) so null clears to the provider default.

v1.reason: When the session has no spawned_at (agent_menu.rs:476), the Save handler always sets payload["model"]=model.text() and payload["effort"]=effort.text() (agent_menu.rs:545-548), even when both entries are empty because the session uses the provider default. UpdateIn.model/effort are plain Option<String> (relay-bus ops/session.rs:138-139), so "" arrives as Some(""). The Update handler (session.rs:1440-1442) does p.model.clone().map(Some) and then validate_options, which rejects an empty model with invalid session.model "model cannot be empty" (providers.rs:253-254). An empty effort would also fail the allowed-list check (providers.rs:260-266). So for any unspawned session (created with start:false, a launch that stopped before session.spawn, or one staged via task.dispatch start:false) whose model is the default, every Save fails, including one that only flips 'Agent bus writes' or 'UI control'. The bus also has no way to clear a model back to the provider default.
v1.correction: Wrong line numbers: the UpdateIn struct is at crates/relay-bus/src/ops/session.rs:137-140, and the handler's model/effort merge is at session.rs:1440-1442. Fix: add model/effort to the payload only when they changed from the original and are non-empty after trim, and make UpdateIn.model/effort nullable via crate::nullable (as task_id/module_id already are) so that null clears them.

findings.title: Ops registered as implemented that do not do what their contract says: app.log.tail, app.reconcile, git.log graph
findings.evidence: app.log.tail is declared .stream("log") 'Attach the log stream' (ops/app.rs:39; BUS.md:383, 628) but its handler only emits a system app.log.attached event echoing level/filter and returns {} (app.rs:133-136); the socket door has no app.log.tail branch, so no log frame is ever sent. app.reconcile, 'Run the 60s trust-but-verify pass now' (ops/app.rs:59-60), always returns {actions: []} (app.rs:137-141) and no 60 s pass exists anywhere, although BUS.md §1.3 relies on it for resource.sample. GitLogIn.graph (ops/git.rs:29) is never read by the git.log handler (git.rs:256-274).
findings.impact: relay cmd app.log.tail reports success and then streams nothing; bus.ops marks these ops implemented, so agents and scripts cannot tell they are stubs.
findings.fix: Implement them (forward tracing records as log frames; run real reconcile checks; honour graph) or answer bus.not_implemented and correct the summaries.

v1.reason: handlers/app.rs:133-136: the LogTail handler only emits `app.log.attached` and returns Empty. No door code handles a "log" stream: socket.rs builds stream frames only for pty, mirror and logcat. Yet ops/app.rs:39 declares `.stream("log")` with "Attach the log stream". Reconcile (app.rs:137-141) always returns an empty actions list; its comment admits "Phase 1 has nothing to verify yet", and BUS.md:1143 calls it a "no-op list" for phase 1. Even so, BUS.md:127 and :633 describe a real 60 s pass, and nothing schedules one. GitLogIn.graph (ops/git.rs:29) is never read by the git.log handler (git.rs:256-274). The ops report success and do nothing, so callers cannot tell they are stubs.
v1.correction: Line numbers are right. There is one more consequence of the missing reconcile pass: BUS.md §5.4 (line 290) says soft-deleted tasks, modules, notes, files and sessions are "hard-deleted by the reconcile pass" after undo.grace_days, but no hard-delete or purge code exists in relay-core, so soft-deleted rows and .relay/trash entries accumulate forever. It is still low impact: a single-user store grows slowly. Fix: answer bus.not_implemented, or implement the pass, and correct the docs.

findings.title: Socket door answers bus.subscribe / bus.wait / bus.unsubscribe without the envelope, actor or token checks
findings.evidence: The door intercepts these three ops right after Engine::parse (socket.rs:362-453) and never calls dispatch, so the v check (engine.rs:808-812), actor resolution (engine.rs:1347-1374: system rejected, agent:<name> requires a matching token) and door rules are skipped. The Actor schema says "system" is internal and rejected at every door (envelope.rs:89).
findings.impact: A request with actor "system", an unknown agent:x or a wrong token, or v:2, can subscribe to every event across projects or block in bus.wait. Same-uid only, so the exposure is limited.
findings.fix: Run these ops through the same envelope/actor validation as dispatch (e.g. an Engine::validate step) before the door handles them.

v1.reason: It is true that socket.rs:362-453 handles bus.subscribe, bus.wait and bus.unsubscribe without dispatch, so the envelope v and actor are not checked. But this gives a caller nothing new. On the socket door, resolve_actor (engine.rs:1347-1374) accepts `Actor::User` with no token at all. Any process that can open the 0600 socket in its 0700 directory (same uid, socket.rs:56/102) can simply send actor "user" and is entitled to subscribe to every event anyway. Nothing on this path filters events by actor or project, so a check that rejects "system" or a bad agent token gates nothing. The phone door filters actors before forwarding (relay-remote wire.rs:95-116, which allows only user or test). Claiming "system" or v:2 here gains no privilege.
v1.correction: At most a consistency nit: validate the envelope for symmetry. It is not a security finding. A more significant question, outside this finding, is that tokenless `user` on the socket means any same-uid agent process could claim user; that belongs to the guardrail threat model, not to these three ops.

findings.title: noun.changed events carry partial payloads, contrary to BUS.md §3.3's full-entity contract
findings.evidence: BUS.md:182: '`noun.changed` (entity upserted; payload is the full entity)'. task.changed is also emitted as {"task_id","state":"failed"} (session.rs:666), {"task_id","state":"blocked"} (1182), {"task_id","state":task_state} (1398) and {"project_id","bulk":true} from the v3 import (import_v3.rs:333); integration.changed as {"integration_id","state":"discarded"} (integration.rs:67); ui.changed as {"move":{...}} (ui.rs:180); avd.changed as {"name","state"} (device.rs:352).
findings.impact: A bus.wait consumer matching {"id": N} on task.changed misses exactly the failed/blocked transitions (which carry task_id, not id), and one matching task_id misses the full-entity events; any client applying the payload in place gets partial rows.
findings.fix: Re-read and emit the full entity, or give partial notifications their own domain event names; update BUS.md if partial payloads are intended.

v1.reason: BUS.md:182 says `noun.changed` payload 'is the full entity'. The cited emitters do send partial payloads: session.rs:666/1182/1398 {task_id,state}, import_v3.rs:333 {project_id,bulk}, integration.rs:67 {integration_id,state}, ui.rs:180 {move:{...}}, device.rs:352/359 {name,state}. The drift is much wider than listed. About 30 json! emit sites send partial `*.changed` payloads, including module.rs:205-206 task.changed {module_id,unlinked/restored}, session.rs:109, worktree.changed {project_id}, settings.changed {path,value}, overlap.changed, notify.changed, layout.changed and device.signing.changed. The native client subscribes to these events and mostly treats them as re-query hints, so in practice they are invalidation signals. The claimed bus.wait {id:N} miss is speculative: no consumer doing that was shown.
v1.correction: Partial payloads are the de facto convention across the codebase, so the right fix is to change BUS.md §3.3 rather than the code. Define `*.changed` as an invalidation hint that carries at least the scope id plus whatever changed. Alternatively, standardise the id key, e.g. always `task_id` and never `id`, so bus.wait filters can work. Rewriting about 30 emitters to send full entities would cost a re-read inside the transaction for no consumer benefit.

findings.title: Native client matches error code device.sdk_missing that the engine never produces (it emits avd.sdk_missing)
findings.evidence: phone_error maps Some("device.sdk_missing") | Some("device.adb_missing") => format!("Android SDK not found: {error}") (agent_menu.rs:91), but device.run's SDK failure comes from android_sdk_root: BusError::unavailable("avd.sdk_missing", ...) (device.rs:435, returned at 163-166). Similarly client.rs:69 gives a 180 s timeout to "git.worktree.create", which is not an op (the op is worktree.create).
findings.impact: The SDK-missing case falls through to the generic message; the timeout entry is dead.
findings.fix: Match avd.sdk_missing (or rename the engine code for device.run) and fix or drop the timeout key.

v1.reason: agent_menu.rs:91 matches Some("device.sdk_missing"), but no code in crates/ produces that code. device.run calls android_sdk_root (device.rs:163-166), and when the default gradle command is in use it returns that function's error, which is BusError::unavailable("avd.sdk_missing", ...) (device.rs:435). phone_error (used at agent_menu.rs:745) therefore falls through to the generic error.to_string(). The "device.adb_missing" half of the arm does work: adb_path at device.rs:151 emits it (device.rs:565/570). client.rs:69 gives "git.worktree.create" a 180 s timeout, but no op has that name (the engine op is worktree.create), and the native client never calls worktree.create at all (rg finds no call), so that entry is dead.
v1.correction: Only the sdk_missing half of the match is wrong; device.adb_missing is real and reachable. The impact is cosmetic: the user still sees "Android SDK root could not be detected" with its hint, just without the "Android SDK not found:" prefix. Fix: match "avd.sdk_missing", and drop the "git.worktree.create" key (or rename it to worktree.create if the client ever calls it).

findings.title: integration.request's deploy installs on a device without checking or taking the device lease
findings.evidence: Deploy runs shell(&path, command, Some(&device)) - fish -lc run_cmd with RELAY_DEVICE (integration.rs:207, 228-234) - and integration.rs never touches device_lease, while device.run checks and holds the lease (device.rs:150, 177) and the Device contract says 'A conflicting run, install or claim from anyone else is refused with device.busy' (types.rs:733-735). integration.request is in the builder baseline (settings.rs:36).
findings.impact: A builder (or the user) can deploy an integration build onto a phone another session has claimed or is running on, interleaving installs the lease system exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Check/acquire a run-kind lease for `deploy` before starting and release it when the integration finishes, as device.run does.

v1.reason: integration.rs has no reference to device_lease anywhere. When `deploy` is set, run() (background thread spawned after commit, integration.rs:39-41) calls shell(&path, command, Some(&device)) at integration.rs:207. That runs `fish -lc run_cmd` with RELAY_DEVICE set (integration.rs:228-234) and never checks or takes a lease. device.run checks the lease before any adb work (device.rs:150, `device_lease::check(ctx, &p.device, &holder)`) and acquires a Kind::Run lease (device.rs:177). The Device type documents that 'A conflicting run, install or claim from anyone else is refused with device.busy' (types.rs:731-732). integration.request is in the builder and docs role baselines (settings.rs:36), so an agent can deploy onto a device another session has claimed or is running a build on.
v1.correction: The Device doc comment is at types.rs:731-732, not 733-735. The deploy device string is also never checked: there is no require_device or state check, unlike device.run. The deploy shell uses a bare cmd.output() with no timeout. That runs on a background thread rather than in a handler, so it breaks no invariant, but a hung run_cmd leaves the integration stuck in Deploying forever. Fix: at request time, check the lease for `deploy` with an integration holder. In run(), acquire a Run-kind lease around the deploy step and release it on every exit path.

findings.title: BUS.md §9.3/§10.8 still say Codex has no tool hooks and guarded=false; the code installs .codex/hooks.json and reports guarded=true
findings.evidence: BUS.md:524-533 'Codex (no tool hooks): ProviderInfo.guarded is false and the settings surface labels its sessions unguarded' and BUS.md:744 'Codex, having no hooks, degrades to PTY-derived idle/busy'; providers.rs:212 fn guarded(&self) -> bool { true } for Codex; hooks.rs:495-545 installs PreToolUse/SessionStart/PostToolUse/Stop for Codex (D132); the Codex adapter maps Edit/Write/apply_patch to kind exec (relay-cli main.rs:508), so write policies bind only at the pre-commit gate.
findings.impact: Readers of the bus contract, and agents reading it, get the wrong enforcement model for Codex.
findings.fix: Update BUS.md §9.3 and §10.8 to D132, including that Codex patches are judged as exec and write-set enforcement happens at commit.

v1.reason: BUS.md:524-533 still says 'Codex (no tool hooks): ProviderInfo.guarded is false ... labels its sessions unguarded', with post-hoc write detection only. BUS.md:744 says 'Codex, having no hooks, degrades to PTY-derived idle/busy'. The code disagrees: providers.rs:212 has `fn guarded(&self) -> bool { true }` for Codex, hooks.rs:495+ merges Relay handlers into `.codex/hooks.json`, and relay-cli main.rs:508-512 maps Bash/apply_patch/Edit/Write to a guardrail.gate `kind: exec`. DECISIONS.md:650 (D132) records the change: shell and patch go through guardrail.gate, and the pre-commit gate remains the final write-set boundary.
v1.correction: Update BUS.md §9.3 and the session.report row in §10.8 to D132. Say that Codex edits and patches are judged as exec commands, so path-based write policies bind only at the pre-commit gate.

findings.title: Desktop event subscription omits workspace.deleted, so a workspace removed elsewhere stays in the sidebar
findings.evidence: The bus.subscribe list includes workspace.changed and project.* but not workspace.deleted (app.rs:1154), although the loop refreshes the registry on any workspace.* event (1223). workspace.remove emits workspace.deleted (plus project.deleted per removed project) (workspace.rs:179).
findings.impact: Removing a workspace with no projects from the CLI or phone leaves it listed in the desktop sidebar until an unrelated refresh.
findings.fix: Subscribe to workspace.deleted (or workspace.*).

v1.reason: The desktop's bus.subscribe list (app.rs:1154) includes workspace.changed but not workspace.deleted. The event loop would mark the registry dirty and refresh on any workspace.* event (app.rs:1223-1225), but workspace.deleted never arrives. workspace.remove emits only workspace.deleted for the workspace row (workspace.rs:179), plus project.deleted events through the nested project.remove calls. A workspace with no projects that is removed from the CLI or another door therefore stays in the sidebar until something else sets registry_dirty. When the desktop itself removes the workspace (shell/registry.rs:622/677), it sets registry_dirty locally, so only removals from elsewhere are affected.
v1.correction: If the removed workspace still had projects, the project.deleted events trigger a registry refresh, so only an empty workspace is affected, as the finding says. Fix: add "workspace.deleted" to the list, or subscribe to "workspace.*" (the socket filter supports prefix.*, socket.rs:207).

findings.title: Editor file.* saves treat a held (user_bypass) response as a plain error; only the Git panel offers the inline confirm
findings.evidence: Editor save calls file.write and on any Err shows err.to_string() and re-enables Save (editor.rs:704-721); git ops go through guarded(), which recognises kind Held with confirm guardrail.confirm and offers 'Allow this held action once?' (code_git.rs:1722-1762). For the user, protected paths and large rewrites are holds (guardrail.rs:1028-1034 user_bypass).
findings.impact: Saving a protected file from the editor shows 'Held guardrail.user_bypass ... confirm to bypass this policy' with no way to confirm in place; confirming on the Guardrails page writes the file while the editor keeps its old baseline, so the next save fails with file.edit_conflict.
findings.fix: Use the same guarded() flow for file.write/create/rename/move/delete in the editor and project-files views.

v1.reason: The editor's save (editor.rs:704-721) calls ui.call("file.write", ...) and on any Err only runs show_error(err.to_string()) and re-enables Save. code_git.rs guarded() (1722-1762) recognises ErrorKind::Held with a guardrail.confirm confirmation and offers 'Allow this held action once?'; the editor does not use it. For the User actor, protected-path writes and failed shape gates become holds (guardrail.rs:513-520, 1021-1034 refuse_or_user_hold -> guardrail.user_bypass). Destructive rewrites of tracked files are usually allowed because they are recoverable (guardrail.rs:725-729). So saving a protected file from the editor shows the hold message as a transient error toast, with no way to confirm it there. If the user confirms on the Guardrails page, the file is written while editor.original keeps the old baseline. The next Save then sends the stale expected_sha256 and gets file.edit_conflict (file.rs:77-89). The file.changed event does show 'Files changed on disk... discard reloads the file' (editor.rs:530-532), so the user can recover.
v1.correction: The realistic triggers are protected_paths and shape_gates. A large rewrite of a tracked file is usually not held (allow_if_recoverable). The user can recover by discarding and reloading, so this is a UX gap rather than a stuck state. Fix: reuse guarded() for the editor's file.write and the other file.* mutations. On success it returns the outcome result, so the baseline can then be updated.

findings.title: Native UI re-runs the whole Code workspace refresh (≥3 full git statuses + gh API + worktree list) on every file/git event from any project, even with the panels hidden
findings.evidence: invalidate() only checks `matches!(ui.page.borrow().as_str(), "code" | "agents")` (the page is "agents" for both the terminal wall and the code view: app.rs navigate maps code→agents) and after a 1 s one-shot runs `e.load_tree(..)` (or `e.run_search(..)` when the search box has text), `e.refresh_git(&ui)` and `e.refresh_scopes(&ui)` (editor.rs:514-526). The file sidebar and git panel are hidden by default (`file_sidebar.set_visible(false); git.set_visible(false);` editor.rs:299-300) and invalidate never checks visibility. The event loop skips other projects only via `e.project_id.is_some_and(|id| id != ui.project.get())` (app.rs:1213), but the watcher emits `engine.emit_system("file.changed", payload)` (watch.rs:128) and emit_system builds `Event::new(..)` with `project_id: None` (engine.rs:567-570, envelope.rs:235-245), so watcher events from every project pass; the payload's `worktree` is ignored. One cycle = file.tree with git_badges (file.rs:30-31: `status_badges(&root)` = a full `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`) + one more file.tree per expanded folder (`if self.expanded.borrow().contains(&path) { toggle(true); }` editor.rs:866-867) + git.status (code_git.rs:159, another full status) + `tokio::join!(git.branches, git.log, integration.list, git.pr.list)` (code_git.rs:578-583) + worktree.list (editor.rs:922-926). refresh_git re-runs immediately if events arrived meanwhile (GitRefreshGuard, code_git.rs:4-11); run_search has no in-flight guard at all (editor.rs:1100-1114), so each event queues another full-tree file.search.
findings.impact: Trigger: the user sits on the default Agents page while agents edit files (agents' own file_read/git_status MCP calls register a watcher on their worktree; edits in any project then emit file.changed). Every ~1 s the client spawns 2+K `git status -uall` runs, a paginated `gh api` call (finding on git.pr.list) and a gix worktree enumeration, rebuilds the whole git panel widget tree, and keeps the single UI connection busy (see the per-connection serialization finding) — for panels nobody can see and often for a different project/worktree than the one changed. Violates SPEC §15 ("Idle, app open, unfocused: 0 subprocess spawns/min"; "git panel open: event-driven").
findings.fix: Gate invalidate on `file_sidebar.is_visible() || git.is_visible()` and refresh lazily when a panel is shown; set the envelope project on watcher events (`Event::new(..).in_project(project_id)` instead of emit_system) and drop events whose payload worktree is not the editor's scope; give run_search the same pending/dirty coalescing as refresh_git; compute badges once per cycle (one status) and reuse it for every expanded folder instead of one status per file.tree call.

v1.reason: Editor::invalidate (editor.rs:508-533) checks only that ui.page is "code" or "agents". navigate maps code to agents (app.rs:1314-1315), and agents is the main page. It never checks whether file_sidebar or git is visible; both start hidden (editor.rs:299-300). After 1 s it runs load_tree or run_search, refresh_git and refresh_scopes. The watcher emits file.changed through engine.emit_system (watch.rs:128), which builds Event::new with project_id None (envelope.rs:235-245, engine.rs:567-569). The other-project filter at app.rs:1213 (`e.project_id.is_some_and(..)`) therefore lets these events through, and invalidate runs for them (app.rs:1232-1240). The payload's worktree is ignored. Watchers are registered on any root that file.tree, file.read or git.status touches (file.rs:21/41/301, git.rs:164), including agents' worktrees when agents call the relay MCP file/git tools. Each cycle costs: file.tree with git_badges, a full `git status -uall` (file.rs:30-31), repeated for every expanded folder (editor.rs:866-867); git.status (code_git.rs:159); the branches/log/integration/PR fan-out, where git.pr.list is a paginated `gh api` call to github.com (git.rs:1083-1090); and worktree.list. All handlers are register_unlocked or use output_with_timeout, so this neither holds the store mutex nor freezes the bus. The cost is wasted subprocesses, GitHub API quota and UI-connection traffic for hidden panels and unrelated projects. That is real and contradicts SPEC §15, but it is not a freeze or a user-visible failure, so medium rather than high. The watcher's .relay exclusion (watch.rs:169-173) means that agents editing under .relay/worktrees do not trigger the editor's own primary-root watcher. The trigger needs a watcher registered on those worktrees, for example by an agent's relay file/git MCP call.
v1.correction: Severity: medium, not high. There is no bus or UI freeze, because the handlers are unlocked and subprocesses are bounded. The gh api call on every refresh is the costliest part (network and rate limit) and should be cached or done only when the panel is shown. The fix stands: gate on panel visibility, tag watcher events with in_project(project_id), and drop events whose worktree is not the editor's.

findings.title: Socket door processes one request at a time per connection while the native client multiplexes all UI traffic on one connection (head-of-line blocking; D149's 'genuinely parallel' claim does not hold)
findings.evidence: `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? { ... tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || e.dispatch(req, Door::Socket)).await? ...; let _ = out_tx.send(serde_json::to_string(&resp)?).await; }` (socket.rs:335-744): the next request line is not read until the previous dispatch returns; `bus.wait` holds the loop up to 1 h (socket.rs:400-449). The native client is written as a concurrent multiplexer (client.rs:1 'Bounded, concurrent socket transport', pending map, out-of-order test) and `Ui::call` sends every non-lifecycle op over the single `ui.client` (app.rs:1111-1117); its 30 s timeouts (client.rs:65-72) do not cancel engine work. Only lifecycle ops get their own connection (`lifecycle_request`, client.rs:131-141: 'must not sit behind slow reads on the UI socket'). DECISIONS.md D149 (lines 814-815) states unlocked queries 'now genuinely run in parallel' because doors use spawn_blocking — true across connections only.
findings.impact: Any slow request on the UI connection — git.pr.list (≤10 s network), each `git status` (≤10 s timeout), file.search (unbounded walk), git.diff.file / git.show (unbounded Myers diff), git.push and the user's pre-commit hook (no timeout) — delays every other UI request queued behind it (board task.list, file.read when opening a file, project.list/session.list refreshes). With the editor refresh cascade issuing 6-8 requests per file event, user actions routinely wait seconds; after a client-side timeout the already-sent requests still run serially, so the backlog persists. The phone bridge (one engine connection per phone) has the same behaviour.
findings.fix: In handle_conn spawn each request as its own task and write responses as they complete (ids already correlate), keeping only per-session `session.input`/`session.resize` and attach/detach bookkeeping ordered; or have the native client open a small pool of connections and route slow ops (git.*, file.search, worktree.*) away from the control connection. Update D149.

v1.reason: socket.rs:335-741 is a strict read, dispatch, await, respond loop. Every branch awaits its spawn_blocking (or the bus.wait timeout, which can be up to 1 h) before the next `lines.next_line()`, so requests on one connection never overlap. In the native client, Ui::call (app.rs:1111-1117) sends every non-lifecycle op over the single shared `self.client`. The only things with their own connections are lifecycle ops (client.rs:50-62, 133-141), image_read, terminals (terminal.rs:476), mirrors, devices and status. That leaves git.push and git.commit (code_git.rs:533, 280/392; pre-commit hooks and network), git.pr.list (code_git.rs:582), git.status (code_git.rs:159) and file.search (editor.rs:1114) sharing one serial pipe with every board, file.read and list refresh. D149 (DECISIONS.md:814-815) says these queries 'now genuinely run in parallel', but that only holds across connections. The client-side pending map and 30 s timeouts (client.rs:64-71) cannot cancel requests already queued at the engine, so after a timeout the backlog keeps running and later calls can time out too.
v1.correction: Keystrokes and terminal output are not affected, because each terminal has its own connection. Event delivery is not affected either, because the forwarder is a separate task. The stall hits the UI control plane: during a push, a commit with hooks, or a slow PR listing, every panel load and file open on that connection waits. Fix: in handle_conn, spawn the generic spawn_blocking dispatch per request and respond as each completes (ids already correlate), keeping attach/detach/subscribe bookkeeping ordered. Alternatively, route git.*/file.search through a separate client connection the same way lifecycle ops are. Update D149.

v2.reason:
(a) The claimed code does exist. handle_conn (socket.rs:335-745) is a strict read → dispatch → await → respond loop, run once per connection (accept loop, socket.rs:108-114). The generic path awaits spawn_blocking (socket.rs:741-742) before writing the response (socket.rs:744) and reading the next line. Ui::call (app.rs:1111-1117) sends every op except the lifecycle ones over the single `ui.client`. Nothing hidden serializes unlocked ops (dispatch_unlocked, engine.rs:906-908 and 1175-1210, takes the store only for short reads), so this connection really is the bottleneck. BUS.md §6.2 promises only "pipelining allowed; correlation by id", not in-order processing. D149 (DECISIONS.md:800, 815) says the Code page's seven ops, once "serialized end to end", now "genuinely run in parallel". No Tauri client remains (apps/ holds only relay-native and relay-mobile), so for the only UI client that claim is false.

(b) The user hits this in normal use. The default page is "agents" (app.rs:747). On the Agents and Code pages, every file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed or integration.* event (app.rs:1230-1240) triggers Editor::invalidate (editor.rs:508-526). At most once a second, that sends file.tree or file.search, then refresh_git: git.status (code_git.rs:159) followed by a tokio::join! of git.branches, git.log, integration.list and git.pr.list (code_git.rs:578-583), plus worktree.list. All of these go through ui.call on the one connection. git.pr.list runs `gh api --paginate ... state=all` on every refresh, with a 10 s cap (git.rs:1083-1101). So while agents are editing, a GitHub round trip sits ahead of user requests such as file.read when opening a file (editor.rs:634-638), task.list (task_pages.rs:431) and project.list/workspace.list (app.rs:1373-1376). Push (code_git.rs:533) and Commit (code_git.rs:280/392) also go through guarded → ui.call (code_git.rs:1722-1723). git push runs through worktree::git(), which calls a plain .output() with no timeout (worktree.rs:26-36). The user's pre-commit hook also runs with a plain .output() (hooks.rs:210-213). For the full length of either, every panel request waits. The author has already hit this: d849b98, "keep session controls responsive", moved only lifecycle ops to their own connections (client.rs:131-141, plus a test modelling a stalled git.status).

(c) What happens: the GTK main loop stays responsive. Terminals use their own connections (terminal.rs:476, input at 229-243), and events reach the client through a separate forwarder task (socket.rs:373), so neither is affected. Every other UI request stalls: file opens, board and sidebar loads, settings writes. The stall lasts as long as whatever slow op is in flight. During agent activity that is typically up to one gh round trip; during a push or hook it is the whole duration. Anything queued longer than 30 s (client.rs:65-72 and 326-332) fails with "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown; refresh before retrying." The engine still runs it later, so a retried mutation can apply twice. The refresh the message suggests is itself queued behind the same slow op.

(d) High fits the rubric. During normal flows (agent activity, push, commit) the whole UI control plane is functionally frozen, and the user sees spurious timeout errors. It is not critical: keystrokes and other connections (agents' MCP servers, the CLI) keep working, and no data is lost.

(e) The proposed server-side fix is incomplete and would introduce a bug. The native client pipelines fire-and-forget mutations on this connection. For example, save_collapsed (shell/registry.rs:244-258) spawns an independent settings.set carrying the whole folded set on each toggle. Today these apply in arrival order; with unordered concurrent dispatch, the stale set could be written last.
v2.correction:
Impact wording:
- The 6-8 requests come per debounced cascade (at most one a second; refresh_git is coalesced through git_refresh_pending/git_refresh_dirty), not per file event.
- The typical wait is one gh round trip on a small repo: sub-second to about 2 s. It reaches about 10 s when the state=all PR listing paginates many pages or the network is slow, and has no upper bound during git push or the user's pre-commit hook. "Routinely wait seconds" overstates the common case.
- The bus.wait one-hour hold does not matter here. The native client never sends bus.wait, and the MCP server (relay-cli mcp.rs) is a sequential stdio loop, so it is already serial.
- project.clone (onboarding.rs:527) is a different root cause. It runs an unbounded `git clone` inside a locked `register` handler (workspace.rs:228-235), and no connection-level change helps it.
- The phone bridge (bridge.rs:156-187) does share one engine connection per phone. What the phone actually sends is out of scope.

Fix:
- Server side, if chosen: dispatch only unlocked queries concurrently, under a per-connection semaphore so one client cannot flood the blocking pool. Keep mutations and staged ops in order per connection, acting as barriers for the requests after them on that connection. Keep subscribe, attach/detach, watch and run/mirror bookkeeping inline, as today.
- Lower-risk option, mirroring the existing lifecycle pattern: in relay-native, send git.*, git.pr.list, file.search, file.tree and worktree.list over a second dedicated connection or a small pool, leaving mutations and the subscription on the control connection.
- Either way, correct D149 (DECISIONS.md:815) to say the parallelism holds across connections only.
- Separately, wrap worktree::git (used by push) and run_user_pre_commit in proc::output_with_timeout.

findings.title: project.clone and git.pr.open run network subprocesses inside the store transaction with no timeout
findings.evidence: `e.register::<ProjectClone>(...)` runs `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()` (workspace.rs:228-238) and `e.register::<PrOpen>(...)` runs `gh pr create ... cmd.output()` (git.rs:666-692). Both use Engine::register, so they execute between `let mut conn = self.store.lock()` and commit (engine.rs:953-1024). Neither goes through proc::output_with_timeout nor sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0/GH_PROMPT_DISABLED. The client allows `"project.clone" => Duration::from_secs(1800)` (client.rs:67), i.e. clones are expected to take minutes. run.sh starts the engine with `nohup ... &` (no setsid), so it keeps the launching terminal as its controlling tty.
findings.impact: While a clone runs (minutes for a large or LFS repository; it is the onboarding 'clone from GitHub' path) or `gh pr create` waits on GitHub (seconds), every request that needs the store blocks: every agent's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook (guardrail.gate, session.report), MCP calls, session.list/task.list — all sessions stall; only in-memory keystrokes pass. If git/ssh needs credentials or a host-key confirmation and the run.sh terminal is still open, they prompt on /dev/tty and the global lock is held indefinitely. Breaks CLAUDE.md invariants (slow work under the mutex; every handler subprocess through output_with_timeout).
findings.fix: register_staged: do the clone / `gh pr create` in prepare via proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1 and null stdin; finish only inserts the project (invoke project.add) / emits git.changed. Remove the partial clone on timeout.

v1.reason: ProjectClone (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:228-247) is plain `e.register` and runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()` inside the transaction (line 234), with no timeout, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and stdin inherited. PrOpen (git.rs:666-692) is plain register and runs `gh pr create ... cmd.output()` with no timeout. The client allows 1800 s for project.clone (apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:67), so clones are expected to take minutes. For that whole time the store mutex is held, and every locked op stalls (agents' guardrail.gate / session.report hooks, the UI's locked queries). The CLAUDE.md/D144 rules require output_with_timeout for handler subprocesses and slow work off the mutex. run.sh starts the engine with `nohup ... </dev/null &`, which nulls stdin but does not detach the controlling tty, so a git/ssh credential or host-key prompt on /dev/tty can hold the lock indefinitely. That last part is plausible rather than demonstrated: it depends on how the engine was launched.
v1.correction: Same root cause as lens-perf#5 (locked handlers running slow subprocesses with no timeout); merge it there, keeping clone as the worst instance. Fix: register_staged. Do the clone / `gh pr create` in prepare through proc::output_with_timeout, with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1 and null stdin (proc.rs already nulls stdin), and remove the partial destination on timeout. Finish then invokes project.add / emits git.changed.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding claims. In workspace.rs:228 `ProjectClone` is registered with plain `e.register`, and line 234 runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()`. It has no timeout and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. In git.rs:666 `PrOpen` is also plain `register` and runs `gh pr create ... .output()` (line 680) with no timeout. Every plain-register handler runs between `let mut conn = self.store.lock()` (engine.rs:954) and the commit. `Store::lock` is a blocking std Mutex (store.rs:474), and `LockSpan` only logs. The sibling network ops `git.fetch` and `git.push` were moved to `register_staged` with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and output_with_timeout (git.rs:580-622, 937-959). The `git.pr.list` comment (git.rs:1091) names exactly this hazard ("an unbounded wait on a flaky network used to be an unbounded wait for every other bus op"). D144 and D149 forbid it, and nothing in DECISIONS exempts clone or pr.open. So these two ops were missed in the conversion, not kept deliberately.

(b) Reachability: the user triggers both. Clone runs from first-run onboarding, and also from the sidebar "Add project…" (registry.rs:472 → open_repository_in → onboarding.rs:527 `ui.call("project.clone")`), a normal flow while agents are working. It can also be called with `relay cmd`. It is UserOnly. `git.pr.open` runs from the Code page "Publish a pull request" action. It is Actors::All but appears in no default role allowlist (settings.rs:36-38), so agents cannot normally call it. Frequency: occasional, once per cloned project.

(c) Effect: for the whole clone the global lock is held. That is seconds for a small repo, minutes for a large or LFS one (the client allows 1800 s, client.rs:67), and unbounded if the network stalls, because git sets no low-speed timeout by default. Every agent socket request blocks at its first store access, `check_session_token` (engine.rs:1378), so the following all wait:
- PreToolUse `guardrail.gate` hooks. Claude abandons them at the 30 s hook timeout (hooks.rs:349).
- Lifecycle `session.report` hooks, abandoned at 10 s.
- Agent MCP calls. The CLI `Client::call` has no timeout.
- Agents' git pre-commit `relay cmd guardrail.gate`.

The UI's own main connection is also stuck. `project.clone` goes over it (`Ui::call`; it is not in `is_lifecycle_request`), and `handle_conn` runs a connection's requests strictly one at a time (`spawn_blocking(..).await` inside the read loop, socket.rs:741). So every other UI request queued behind the clone hits its 30 s client timeout ("outcome unknown"), while queued mutations still run later.

Keystrokes and PTY output keep working: each pane has its own connection (terminal.rs:476) and input goes through the in-memory fast path. No data is lost.

Unverified: what Claude Code does with a timed-out PreToolUse hook is outside this repo. If it treats the timeout as a non-blocking error, guarded tool calls run unchecked during a long clone.

(d) High fits the rubric: a freeze of the bus in a normal flow, unbounded in the stall case. Critical is not justified, because sessions, PTYs and data survive.

(e) The proposed fix is correct in direction but incomplete. See the correction.
v2.correction:
1. The tty claim needs narrowing. Rust's `Command::output()` already gives the child a null stdin, so "stdin inherited" (first verifier) is wrong. The prompt risk comes from git and ssh opening /dev/tty directly. That only happens when the engine was started by run.sh from a terminal that is still open. The .desktop launcher (install-native-desktop.py → run.sh) gives the engine no controlling tty, so prompts fail fast there. The general unbounded case is a stalled network.

2. Missing impact: the UI's main connection is head-of-line blocked, as described in (c).

3. Changes the fix needs:
   - **Free the UI connection too.** register_staged alone frees the store but not the UI's main connection. Also send project.clone on its own connection, the way `Client::lifecycle_request` does, or make it genuinely async. BUS.md §5 and the op summary already promise this: "(async; project.changed when done)" with a `project.clone.completed` audit row. The code is currently synchronous, which is docs drift.
   - **Use a long clone timeout.** Use a deadline of at least the client's 1800 s, not the 20 s fetch bound, and add stall detection with `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=… -c http.lowSpeedTime=…`.
   - **Claim the destination atomically.** Once the clone runs outside the lock, two requests can race on the same destination. Claim it with `fs::create_dir` and clone into that empty directory. Remove only a directory this request created.
   - **Cover ssh prompts.** `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` does not stop ssh prompts. The CLI accepts any URL, so also set `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes'`.
   - **gh prompts are not the issue.** `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED` is only belt-and-braces: gh with piped stdout cannot prompt. For PrOpen, the real fixes are staging with `resolve_root_unlocked` (as `git.push` does) and a timeout.

4. Keep the clone as the lead instance. PrOpen is a seconds-long freeze that only the user can trigger. If lens-perf#5 is the same root cause, merge this into it.

findings.title: A single response/event line over 2 MiB kills the native UI's control connection, and engine responses such as git.diff.file are unbounded
findings.evidence: `if line.len() + n > max_line { return Err(Error::Protocol(format!("frame exceeds {} MiB", ...))) }` (client.rs:200-205) ends the reader: every pending request fails and `Notice::Disconnected` is sent; the app then drops the client and stops its event loop (app.rs:1267-1275). Reconnect runs connect(), which calls `p.stop()` on every pane and clears them (app.rs:1137-1142), so terminals are rebuilt with only the ≤256 KiB attach catch-up. Engine side, git.diff.file returns the whole HEAD blob, the whole working file and a full unified diff with no cap (git.rs:235-254); the client's guard `if old.len() + new.len() > 1048576 { ui.show_error("Diff exceeds the 1 MiB editor limit.") }` (code_git.rs:1350) only runs after the response was received. git.status lists every untracked file (`--untracked-files=all`, worktree.rs:89); file.tree depth 1 lists every entry of a directory.
findings.impact: Clicking a modified file in Source Control whose old+new+diff JSON exceeds 2 MiB — e.g. this repo's docs/perf/runs/2026-09-19/profiles.json (556 KB of quote-heavy JSON, escaped again) after a perf rerun, or apps/relay-mobile/package-lock.json (480 KB) after a large npm update — disconnects the whole UI; recovering wipes the VTE history of every terminal pane. A worktree with roughly 25k+ untracked files makes every git.status exceed the limit, so each reconnect's refresh disconnects again.
findings.fix: Client: on an oversized line, consume it without buffering, parse the id from the prefix and fail only that request (or raise MAX_LINE for responses while keeping the cap for frames). Engine: cap git.diff.file (return sizes + `truncated`, skip NUL-containing blobs), use `--untracked-files=normal` for status/badges or cap the entry count, cap file.tree entries per directory.

v1.reason: client.rs:200-205: when `line.len() + n > max_line` the reader returns Err(Protocol). The outcome handler (client.rs:254-260) fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected. The UI connection is opened through Client::connect -> open(), which uses MAX_LINE = 2 MiB (client.rs:48, 166). Only image_read (24 MiB) and the mirror get a larger limit. app.rs:1267-1275 handles Disconnected by dropping ui.client and breaking out of the event loop. Reconnecting goes through connect() (app.rs:1131-1144), which calls p.stop() on every pane and clears panes/ordered. Engine side, the DiffFileOp handler (git.rs:235-254) is register_unlocked and returns the whole HEAD blob (revision_text), the whole working file (working_text reads the whole file with from_utf8_lossy, git.rs:842-848) and a full unified diff, with no size cap. The client's 1 MiB check (code_git.rs:1350) runs only after the response has arrived, so it cannot prevent the disconnect. Trigger: in Source Control, click a modified file larger than about 1 MB, or a smaller one that was rewritten heavily, so that old + new + diff in JSON exceeds 2 MiB. Images go to open_image and avoid this. A modified non-image binary (for example an Unreal .uasset, which this user works with) goes through lossy UTF-8, and every U+FFFD replacement character costs 3 bytes in the JSON, so a binary of roughly 700 KB is already enough. Consequence: the UI control connection is lost and reconnecting rebuilds every terminal pane. The 25k-untracked-file git.status case is mechanically possible but less likely; it is a secondary point.
v1.correction: Main trigger: git.diff.file on a large or binary modified file (the related git.diff op computes `binary` from NUL bytes, but diff.file does not). Fix on the engine side first: cap old/new (or return `truncated` plus sizes) and skip NUL-containing blobs in DiffFileOp. On the client side, drain an oversized response line and fail only that request instead of tearing down the connection.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says, and I checked each step myself.
- **Client cap.** client.rs:200-205 returns `Err(Protocol("frame exceeds 2 MiB"))` once a line passes `max_line`. The UI connection uses MAX_LINE = 2 MiB (client.rs:48, 166). Only `image_read` and the mirror get a larger cap.
- **Teardown.** client.rs:259-265 fails every pending request and sends `Notice::Disconnected`. app.rs:1267-1275 then drops `ui.client` and breaks out of the event loop.
- **No auto-reconnect.** Recovery waits until the user clicks the Reconnect button (app.rs:970-972), which runs `connect()`. That stops and clears every pane (app.rs:1139-1142). New `Pane`s and VTEs are created at app.rs:1488, fed only `ATTACH_CATCHUP_BYTES` = 256 KiB (pty.rs:19).
- **Engine side.** `DiffFileOp` (git.rs:235-254, `register_unlocked`) returns the whole HEAD blob, the whole working file and a full unified diff. `revision_text` and `working_text` read everything through `from_utf8_lossy` (git.rs:802-848). socket.rs:744 writes the response as one line. Nothing in dispatch caps it; the audit truncation applies only to the stored summary.
- **Client call site.** A Source Control row click (code_git.rs:898) reaches `open_diff`, which calls `ui.call("git.diff.file")` on the control connection (code_git.rs:1338). Only image extensions are sent elsewhere (image_preview.rs:7-17). The 1 MiB check at code_git.rs:1350 runs only after the response has arrived.

(b) Reachable by the user, through a normal action: clicking a changed file in Source Control. I estimated response sizes with a simulation using serde_json-equivalent escaping and lossy UTF-8:
- Compressed or random binary grows about 2.36x (an ELF binary about 3.3x).
- So any added, deleted or LFS-modified non-image binary over about 445 KiB crosses 2 MiB, and so does a fully changed tracked binary over about 220 KiB.
- Example: apps/relay-native/resources/scrcpy-server-v4.1 (733 KB) gives a response of about 3.4 MB on any change.
- Text files cross at about 0.9 MB after a small edit or when added, and at about 0.45 MB when fully rewritten.
- The app is built for LFS asset repos (client.rs:67 comment, worktree.rs:83-85) and ships Unreal and Blender tooling. Changed .uasset, .umap, .blend and .fbx files, fonts, PDFs and audio are therefore routine in Source Control for this user.
- With LFS, HEAD holds only a pointer while `working_text` reads the whole asset.

(c) What the user sees and loses:
- The diff never opens. The UI shows "Invalid engine response: frame exceeds 2 MiB" and the status "Engine disconnected".
- Every other in-flight control request fails.
- The UI stops receiving all events (guardrail.held approval prompts, notifications, session state), and every non-terminal action fails until the user clicks Reconnect.
- Terminals keep streaming and accepting input on their own connections until then.
- Reconnect rebuilds every pane with a fresh VTE holding only the last 256 KiB or less of output. Engine data and the agents are unaffected.
- Clicking the same file again repeats the whole failure.
- similar 2.7's `TextDiffConfig` has no default deadline, so a very large binary can take longer than the 30 s client timeout. The oversized line still kills the connection when it finally arrives, because the size check runs before the request-id lookup.
