(d) High is right, at the low edge of high. A normal action on a routine class of files hard-fails the UI's whole control connection. Recovery is manual and costs every pane's scrollback. The failure also cuts in ahead of the client's own graceful 1 MiB guard. It stays at the low edge because no engine data is lost and terminals keep working until Reconnect.

(e) The engine-side cap is the right primary fix. The `--untracked-files=normal` part of the proposed fix is not drop-in; see the correction.
v2.correction:
**Impact wording**
- The terminals are not cut off by the disconnect. They have their own connections and keep working until the user clicks Reconnect, and there is no automatic reconnect.
- "Wipes VTE history" should read: every pane is recreated with a new VTE fed only the last 256 KiB or less of output (pty.rs:19).

**Examples**
- package-lock.json is borderline. Only a near-total rewrite crosses the limit (about 2.16 MB against 2.097 MB), and the file belongs to the out-of-scope mobile app.
- profiles.json after a small edit gives a response of about 1.26 MB, so no disconnect (the client's 1 MiB guard fires instead). It crosses only when a rerun rewrites most of its 29k lines.
- Lead with non-image binaries instead: apps/relay-native/resources/scrcpy-server-v4.1 (about 3.4 MB response on any change), or LFS .uasset and .blend files (anything over about 445 KiB).
- The file.tree example is weak. `list_dir` filters node_modules, target, build, dist, Intermediate, Saved and similar names (watch.rs:169-183), so it needs a single directory with roughly 20k or more direct entries under some other name.

**git.status path: worse than stated when it fires**
- `refresh_git` runs on every file.changed and git.changed event on both the agents page and the code page (editor.rs:508-524).
- So a git.status response over 2 MiB (about 20-25k untracked, non-ignored files) disconnects the UI again within about a second of the next file event after each Reconnect.
- It still needs a missing .gitignore.

**Fix**
- **Primary (engine):** in `DiffFileOp`, check sizes before reading anything (`fs::metadata`, blob size). Return a typed refusal (for example `git.diff_too_large` or `git.binary`) when old plus new exceeds 1 MiB, or when either side contains NUL or is not valid UTF-8. No schema change is needed, because `open_diff` already shows `err.to_string()`. This also avoids reading very large assets and running a diff with no deadline over them.
- **Client, defence in depth:** when a line is oversized, keep consuming up to the newline without buffering it. If its prefix is `{"v":1,"id":"<uuid>"` (the field order is documented in `shape()`), fail only that request; otherwise drop the line.
- **Do not switch `status_files` to `--untracked-files=normal`.** It also feeds the git.diff op, which calls `working_text` on every status path (git.rs:203-210). An untracked directory reported as "dir/" makes `fs::read` fail with an error other than NotFound, so the whole git.diff fails with `git.read_failed`. It would also change per-file rows and badges. Cap the number of git.status entries instead.

findings.title: Locked handlers still run local subprocesses, tree deletions and gix rev-walks under the store mutex (git_mutate has no timeout)
findings.evidence: Engine::register (transaction + store mutex) handlers doing external work: git.stage `git add` (git.rs:490-506), git.unstage (507-530), git.branch.create `git check-ref-format` + `git switch -c` (345-383, 1269-1274), git.branch.delete (445-489: branches_for + list_with_dirty + `git branch -d`), git.branch.clean_merged (693-720: N × `git branch -d`), git.commit's finish `git commit --no-verify` (571-572, post-commit hooks still run), file.restore_head `git checkout --` (file.rs:253-261), file.import recursive copy (file.rs:262-298), worktree.remove → purge_build (dir_size + remove_dir_all of target/), dir_size, `git worktree remove` (git.rs:129-144 → worktree.rs:339-370), device.run → `adb devices -l` (device.rs:140-158), session.update → rename_branch (session.rs:1458-1461), session.brief → awareness::brief → git::briefing_state (session.rs:1124-1129, awareness.rs:211: gix open + upstream_metrics ×2 + divergence rev-walks, no object cache). session.spawn/wake/resume call plan_launch inside `ctx.read(|conn| { ... plan_launch(conn, engine, row, kind) })` (session.rs:604-609), which runs the same briefing_state (451) and loads up to 8 MiB of scrollback (456-458) with the lock held. `worktree::git()` behind git_mutate is `Command::new("git")...output()` with no deadline (worktree.rs:26-33).
findings.impact: Each of these holds the global lock for the whole subprocess/walk: `git add` of LFS/Unreal assets runs the clean filter over GB-size files (seconds+), worktree.remove deletes a Rust target/ (GBs, 100k+ files) under the lock, and a session branch or local base far behind its upstream makes every spawn/brief walk thousands of commits. Meanwhile every bus request except in-memory keystrokes waits (agents' hooks, UI refreshes). D144/D149 state slow work never runs with the mutex held; CLAUDE.md requires output_with_timeout for handler subprocesses.
findings.fix: Convert these to register_staged (prepare: subprocess/walk/rev-walk with nothing locked; finish: row writes + events), route git_mutate through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, register session.brief as unlocked, and in stage_launch read the rows under ctx.read but compute awareness::brief's git lines (and decode scrollback) after the lock is released.

v1.reason: All of these use plain `Engine::register` (git.rs:129 WorktreeRemove, 345 BranchCreate, 445 BranchDelete, 490 Stage, 507 Unstage, 693 CleanMerged; file.rs:253 RestoreHead, 262 Import; device.rs:140 RunOp; session.rs Brief). Plain register runs between `let mut conn = self.store.lock()` and commit (engine.rs:954ff). They call `worktree::git_mutate` → `git()`, which is `Command::new("git")...output()` with no deadline (worktree.rs:26-36), so it breaks the CLAUDE.md/D144 rule that handler subprocesses go through proc::output_with_timeout. WorktreeRemove calls `worktree::remove` → `purge_build` (dir_size + remove_dir_all of build dirs) → `dir_size` → `git worktree remove --force` (worktree.rs:339-370), all under the lock. session.brief calls awareness::brief → git::briefing_state (git.rs:1018-1058: gix open, upstream_metrics twice, divergence walk) inside the transaction. stage_launch (session.rs:604-609) is the unlocked phase of a staged handler, but it calls plan_launch inside `ctx.read(|conn| ...)`, so briefing_state and the resume scrollback load (session.rs:451-458) run with the lock held. D149 lists the handlers that were converted, and none of these are among them. Triggers: removing a worktree with a large target/ (GBs), `git add` on LFS assets, or a pre-commit-free but slow git operation. Each holds the global lock for its whole run, so every agent's hook (guardrail.gate, session.report) and the UI's locked ops stall; keystrokes (D148) are unaffected.
v1.correction: Lines verified: WorktreeRemove git.rs:129-144, Stage 490-506, Unstage 507-530, BranchCreate 345, BranchDelete 445, CleanMerged 693-720, RestoreHead file.rs:253-261, Import file.rs:262-298, Brief session.rs:1124-1129, stage_launch session.rs:604-609, session.update's rename_branch session.rs:1458-1461. require_device in device.run probably already goes through a timeout helper (D144), so that part is lock time with a bound, not the missing-timeout breach. The git.commit item is wrong: CommitOp is register_staged (git.rs:535), and the subprocesses sit in its prepare phase per the comment at 531-534. Leave it out unless finish itself forks. lens-perf#3 (project.clone / git.pr.open) has the same root cause and should be merged into this finding. Fix as proposed: register_staged / register_unlocked; route git_mutate through proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; in stage_launch, read the rows under ctx.read and compute briefing_state and decode the scrollback after the lock is released.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. A handler registered with plain `register` runs between `self.store.lock()` and commit (engine.rs:954-956). These locked handlers fork git or walk/delete trees inside the transaction:
- git.stage (git.rs:490-506, `git add --`)
- git.unstage (507-530)
- git.branch.create (345-383): bare `.output()` `git check-ref-format` at 1269-1274, then `git switch -c <name> [<start>]`
- git.branch.delete (445-489): the merged_tips walk in branches_for, upstream_metrics for every branch, list_with_dirty, `git branch -d`
- git.branch.clean_merged (693-720)
- file.restore_head (file.rs:253-261)
- file.import (262-298)
- worktree.remove (git.rs:129-144 → worktree.rs:352-370)
- session.update's rename_branch (session.rs:1458-1461)

git_mutate → git() is `Command::output()` with no deadline and no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (worktree.rs:26-36). session.brief (session.rs:1124-1129) and the ctx.read in stage_launch (604-609 → plan_launch:451) run git::briefing_state (gix, up to six paint walks) with the lock held. The authors' own rule says this should not happen: session.rs:854-856 says checkout and LFS filters "None of it belongs under the global store mutex". The sibling git.branch.switch was made staged and bounded (run_switch, git.rs:1347-1352, 120 s, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0) for the same `git switch` that git.branch.create runs with the lock held. docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md says "Every subprocess goes through proc::output_with_timeout"; that is false for git_mutate.

(b) Who reaches it:
- The native UI sends git.stage/unstage (code_git.rs:470-474, 904-908), git.branch.create (always checkout:true, start point optional, code_git.rs:1033-1037), git.branch.delete and git.commit. It also sends session.brief/update (agent_menu.rs:457, 553) and spawn/wake/resume on every launch.
- worktree.remove, file.restore_head, file.import and clean_merged are UserOnly and the native client never sends them; only the CLI (`relay cmd`) does. The shell's close and discard paths remove worktrees unlocked, in a staged prepare (session.rs:1505-1525, 1547-1590). So "deletes a Rust target/ under the lock" only happens on a CLI-only path.
- "Every spawn walks thousands of commits" is overstated. The gix-traverse 0.60 hidden-frontier paint is bounded by how far the branches diverge, which costs milliseconds. The baseline measured session.brief at 0.7 ms and spawn at 22.7 ms in total.

(c) What happens when it fires: while one of these runs, every locked op and every Unlocked::read waits. That stalls every agent's hooks (resolve_actor takes the lock, engine.rs:1377-1385) and every UI query. Keystrokes are spared (D148). There is no data loss. In code repos the holds are milliseconds (baseline: stage 4.1 ms, unstage 5.8 ms, branch.create 7.6 ms, commit 29 ms). They reach seconds or more in two cases:
- Large-binary or LFS content: clean filters on `git add`/`git reset`; checkout plus smudge filters (which may download) on `git switch -c <name> <start>`. The app expects such content (client.rs:67-68, worktree.rs:83-85). git-lfs is installed on this machine but no global filter is configured.
- A git child that blocks, since nothing bounds it.

I could not establish what Claude Code does when its 30 s PreToolUse hook timeout (hooks.rs:351) fires during such a stall.

(d) Severity: the invariant breach is real. As scoped, though, the long holds need LFS/large content, a distant start point, or CLI-only ops, and the common UI case costs milliseconds. That fits medium ("real bug in a less common path"), not high. The certain freezes from this root cause are in lens-perf#3:
- project.clone runs a full network `git clone` with the lock held and no deadline (workspace.rs:228-247). The client allows 1800 s. It is reached from Add project → clone (onboarding.rs:527).
- git.pr.open runs `gh pr create` with the lock held (git.rs:666-692; button at code_git.rs:662).

Merged with those, the finding is high.

(e) The fix direction is correct: staged ops, as BranchSwitch and Close already do. Caveats are listed in the correction.
v2.correction:
1) The first verifier was wrong about git.commit. Its finish (git.rs:560-576) forks `git commit --no-verify` at 571 inside the transaction. Running the gate and the commit together inside the transaction is deliberate (comment 531-534), so the fix there is a deadline, not moving the call. "post-commit hooks still run" only applies outside session worktrees: install_git points core.hooksPath at a directory that holds only pre-commit (hooks.rs:103, 153).

2) Re-anchor the impact on two cases:
- git.branch.create: a checkout plus LFS smudge, with the lock held, unbounded. The identical switch in git.branch.switch is staged and bounded.
- git.stage/unstage: LFS or large-binary clean filters.

Demote the rest:
- worktree.remove, file.restore_head, file.import and clean_merged are CLI-only.
- device.run's adb probe is bounded at 2 s (device.rs:577-590). That is lock time, not a missing timeout.
- session.update's rename and the briefing_state walks cost milliseconds: cleanup, not causes of a freeze.
- The scrollback load is a SQLite read that needs the connection anyway. Only the lossy UTF-8 copy could move out (sessions.rs:194-203).

3) Remove app.rs:47 from related: backup is SQLite work through the one connection and needs the lock by nature. Keep workspace.rs:114: workspace.discover is a query that does a depth-4 directory walk under plain register.

4) Merge lens-perf#3 (workspace.rs:228 project.clone, git.rs:666 git.pr.open) into this finding. The merged finding should be high and lead with those two.

5) Fix caveats:
- proc::output_with_timeout sends SIGKILL to the process group (proc.rs:53-58). If it kills a mutating git, it can leave .git/index.lock or ref locks behind, which blocks that checkout until someone deletes them. Send SIGTERM first (git cleans up its lock files on SIGTERM), then SIGKILL.
- Use a deadline per op. git_mutate also runs `git push` in Push's prepare (git.rs:617), where a short shared deadline would kill large pushes.
- Keep file.import's guard_path_mutation and the worktree-owner check in finish, or re-check them there.
- Moving briefing_state out of the lock first needs awareness::brief split into a store part and a git part.

findings.title: Line counts use an unbounded Myers diff (no deadline, binary checked afterwards), including inside the locked file.write
findings.evidence: file.write is `e.register::<Write>` (file.rs:72) and calls `let (removed, added) = line_counts(&old, &p.text);` (103) → `TextDiff::from_lines(old, new).iter_all_changes()` (599-610), right after guardrail::enforce computed counts for the same pair with `changed_line_counts`, whose doc says it is a 'Linear multiset line comparison ... This deliberately avoids quadratic LCS work on large generated files (SPEC §15's performance doctrine)' (guardrail.rs:1096-1099, used at 575). similar 2.7's TextDiff::from_lines uses Myers with no deadline (TextDiffConfig::default: `deadline: None`); its docs: time O((N+M)D), 'two large and completely distinct sequences ... spin'. The same unguarded diff runs per changed file in git.diff (git.rs:203-213 → counts 850-860), in git.commit's prepare via staged_numstat (861-873), in git.show/tree_diff_files (1239), and as the unified diff of git.diff.file (248-251); `binary: old.contains('\0') || new.contains('\0')` is computed after diffing (224, 1246).
findings.impact: Saving (editor) or file_write-ing (agents via MCP) a large file whose content changed substantially — a reformatted or regenerated 20k-line file — costs on the order of (N+M)·D ≈ 10^9 line comparisons: seconds with the store mutex held, stalling every session. In the unlocked git paths, a regenerated lockfile or a binary asset kept in git (.blend/.uasset without LFS) pins a core and the requesting connection (UI head-of-line) for seconds to minutes.
findings.fix: file.write: return the counts guardrail::enforce already computed (or call the linear changed_line_counts); everywhere else build diffs with `TextDiff::configure().timeout(Duration::from_millis(200))`, and skip blobs that contain NUL or exceed a size cap before reading them into strings.

v1.reason: similar 2.7.0's TextDiff::from_lines uses Myers with no deadline by default. Its own docs say two large, completely distinct inputs 'will make it spin', and find_middle_snake iterates k over -d..=d unclamped up to max_d=(n+m)/2. Lines are interned to u32 above 100 lines, but the work is still about (n+m)^2/4 loop iterations when D is about n+m. Callers: (1) file.write is `e.register::<Write>` (file.rs:72, store mutex held) and calls `line_counts(&old, &p.text)` (file.rs:103 -> 599-610). That is right after guardrail::enforce, whose own comment (guardrail.rs:1096-1098) says it uses a linear multiset comparison deliberately to avoid this. (2) git.diff's `counts` (git.rs:212, 850-860) runs per changed file on text built with from_utf8_lossy (working_text/revision_text, 838-847), and `binary: old.contains('\0')...` is computed only after counts (224). The same applies to tree_diff_files for git.diff and git.show (1239, 1246), to git.commit's prepare phase via staged_numstat (557, 861-873; the UI's Code panel commit at code_git.rs:280/392), and to git.diff.file's unified diff (248). The socket loop awaits each request before reading the next on a connection (socket.rs:740-743), so a long unlocked diff also blocks every later request on that client connection.
v1.correction: The strongest trigger is binary files, not text rewrites. A modified binary asset in git (a .uasset, .umap or PNG without LFS) is split on '\n' into tens to hundreds of thousands of mostly distinct pseudo-lines. With LFS, HEAD holds a 3-line pointer while the working file is the real binary, which is the worst case: d runs to about m/2 with about d iterations each. Either way, committing or viewing such a file in the Code panel can pin a core for seconds to minutes, and the whole asset is read into a String first. Under the lock in file.write, the trigger needs a near-total rewrite of a large file: about 1-3 s at 20k lines, about 0.1 s at 5k. That is real but less common. Fixes: file.write should reuse the linear changed_line_counts, since only counts are needed. Elsewhere, detect binary (NUL in the first 8 KiB of the raw bytes) and cap size before converting or diffing, and build diffs with `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says, at commit 361c6f9:
- file.write is `e.register::<Write>` (file.rs:72), so it runs with the store mutex held. At line 103 it calls `line_counts`, which is `TextDiff::from_lines(old,new).iter_all_changes()` (file.rs:599-610).
- This runs right after guardrail::enforce → evaluate_write has already counted the same pair with the linear `changed_line_counts` (guardrail.rs:575, 1096-1099). D25 in DECISIONS.md says that counting is linear precisely to avoid "an LCS's quadratic worst case on generated files".
- similar 2.7.0's `from_lines` uses `TextDiffConfig::default()`: Myers, `deadline: None` (text/mod.rs:41-46, 378-383). myers.rs has no cost heuristic, and its own module doc says distinct inputs "make it spin".
- The k-loop in find_middle_snake is unclamped: -d..=d for each d up to (n+m)/2.
- I ported conquer/find_middle_snake faithfully to Python and counted iterations:
  - Fully distinct n=m: about n² iterations.
  - A 3-line old side against m lines: about 1.34·m²/4.
- `tokenize_lines` splits on a lone '\r' as well as '\n', so a binary has roughly 1 "line" per 128 bytes.
- The git callers are all `register_unlocked`, or the prepare phase of `register_staged` for commit:
  - git.diff (lines 181-233, counts at 213)
  - git.diff.file (248, which has no binary check at all)
  - git.show / tree_diff_files (1239)
  - git.commit's staged_numstat (557, 861-873)
  - In each, `binary` is computed only after counting (224, 1246).
- socket.rs:740-744 awaits each dispatch before it reads the next line on that connection.
- The native UI sends every non-lifecycle call over one control connection (app.rs:1111-1116), with a 30 s client timeout (client.rs:65-72).

(b) Reachability:
- **Strongest trigger: binary assets in the unlocked git paths.** This app ships Unreal and Blender tooling and expects LFS (client.rs:68).
  - For a modified LFS asset, `revision_text` returns the 3-line pointer while `working_text` returns the real binary. D is then about m, and the cost is quadratic in the asset's size.
  - `status_files` runs real `git status` (worktree.rs:86-97), so only modified assets are diffed. In UE/Blender work, modified assets are routine.
  - Clicking a modified non-image asset in the Code panel calls git.diff.file. open_diff only diverts images (code_git.rs:1319-1338).
  - An agent's MCP git_diff pays the cost summed over every modified asset.
  - Non-LFS binaries also hit git.show (commit dialog) and the Code-panel commit.
- Estimates for an LFS asset: about 20 MB → ~8e9 iterations, roughly 10-25 s; 50 MB+ → minutes.
- **file.write under the lock is the weaker path.** Agents' normal writes go through guardrail hooks, which count linearly, and nothing steers agents toward file_write. So the trigger is mostly editor saves, which open at most 1 MiB, or occasional MCP use.
  - A total rewrite of a 20k-line file is about 4e8 iterations, roughly 0.5-1.5 s.
  - It is worse when a small file is overwritten with large, distinct content. destructive_write lets that through: removed ≤ 50, and old_lines < min_file_lines turns off the percentage rule. 100k new lines costs several seconds with the mutex held.

(c) Consequences:
- **Git paths:** one core is pinned for seconds to minutes, and the requesting connection is blocked behind it. For the native UI, every later engine call queues behind the diff and times out at 30 s with "outcome unknown". Calls that timed out still run later. The store mutex is not involved.
- **file.write:** every store-backed request stalls, including agents' PreToolUse guardrail.gate and MCP calls, and UI queries. Typing and PTY output are not affected: small session.input and session.resize requests are answered from memory with no store lock (D148, engine.rs:885-897, 1261-1300). "Stalling every session" overstates it.

(d) Severity: high is justified by the binary/LFS path. One click in a normal flow for this app's target projects can make the UI's engine channel unresponsive for tens of seconds or more. On its own, the locked file.write part would be medium.

(e) The fix is right in direction:
- **file.write:** use the linear counts, which is safe because no gate reads WriteOut's counts.
- **Git paths:**
  - detect binary on the raw bytes before diffing;
  - apply a size cap;
  - add `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`, which similar checks once per d, so it is honored at a fine grain.

It needs the caveats listed in the correction.
v2.correction:
Corrections to the finding:
1. **Lead with the binary/LFS trigger in the unlocked git paths, not the store-mutex stall.**
   - LFS makes working-tree diffs (git.diff, git.diff.file) the worst case: 3-line pointer vs the full smudged binary.
   - Staged and commit numstat compare pointer to pointer, so they are fast with LFS. They are slow only for non-LFS binaries.
   - '\r' also splits lines in similar, which doubles a binary's pseudo-line count and makes it about 4x slower.
   - Regenerated lockfiles rarely hit the bad case, because most of their lines are unchanged.
2. **The cost figures are overstated.** A fully rewritten 20k-line file is about 4e8 Myers iterations (about n² for distinct n=m), roughly 0.5-1.5 s, not about 1e9 and "seconds". The file.write case is also not limited to near-total rewrites: a small file overwritten with large distinct content costs about 0.34·m², and the destructive_write gate allows it.
3. **"Stalling every session" is wrong for keystrokes.** User session.input and session.resize skip the store (D148). What stalls is store-backed requests: agents' hook and MCP calls, and UI queries.
4. **The git cost blocks only the requesting connection,** but the native UI uses one control connection, so all its engine calls queue behind it with 30 s timeouts.

Related, but a separate root cause: git.diff.file returns the whole lossy-decoded binary as `new`, and again in `hunks`. The native client caps the control channel at 2 MiB (client.rs:47, 192-197). Opening the diff of almost any non-image binary therefore tears down the UI's engine connection ("frame exceeds 2 MiB"; app.rs:1267-1275). The binary/size guard fixes both problems.

Fix caveats:
- **file.write:** call `changed_line_counts` (make it `pub(crate)`). Getting the counts back out of `enforce` would need plumbing, because enforce returns `()` and `evaluate_granted` may evaluate twice. Multiset semantics stop counting moved lines as changed, so document that for `WriteOut`.
- **Binary detection:** test raw bytes (a NUL in the first 8 KiB) before `from_utf8_lossy`.
- **LFS:** treat an LFS pointer on the old side, or an oversized blob, as binary.
- **git.diff.file:** give DiffFileOut a binary/too-large flag and send no content for those files.
- **Time budget:** a 200 ms per-file deadline still adds up across many files in git.diff, so use a total budget too.

findings.title: git.pr.list paginates every PR the repository ever had through `gh api`, uncached, on every git-panel refresh
findings.evidence: `command.current_dir(root).args(["api", "--paginate", "--slurp", "repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100&sort=updated&direction=desc"])` with PR_LIST_TIMEOUT = 10 s (git.rs:83, 1083-1094); the PrList handler keeps no cache (625-644). The native client calls it from every refresh_git (`ui.call("git.pr.list", ...)`, code_git.rs:582) only to find the PR whose head is the current branch (code_git.rs:592-604).
findings.impact: Each refresh spawns gh and issues ceil(all PRs/100) sequential GitHub REST requests (closed and merged PRs included, so the page count only grows). With the editor refreshing about once per file event while agents work, that is up to ~3,600 gh invocations per hour (× pages) against GitHub's 5,000 requests/hour per-user limit, which agents' own `gh` usage shares — once exhausted, every `gh` command fails for up to an hour. Each call also holds the UI connection for up to 10 s (head-of-line finding).
findings.fix: Ask only for what is shown: `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --limit 5 --json number,state,isDraft,title,url,headRepository` (one request), cache the answer per (repo, branch) with a TTL, and invalidate it on git.push / git.pr.open.

v1.reason: list_pull_requests (git.rs:1083-1112) runs `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100...`, so it fetches every PR the repository ever had, open, closed and merged, and nothing caches the result. The PrList handler (git.rs:625-644) calls it on every request. The native client's refresh_git calls git.pr.list (code_git.rs:582) only to find the PR for the current branch (592-604). refresh_git is driven by Editor::invalidate on every file.changed / git.changed / worktree.changed event (app.rs:1232-1240), and the engine's watcher emits file.changed (watch.rs). Invalidate is debounced to one run per second while the Code or Agents page is shown, and refresh_git coalesces overlapping runs (GitRefreshGuard). With agents editing steadily, that comes to about 3,600 refreshes an hour, each costing ceil(total PRs / 100) REST requests. That exhausts the 5,000/hour authenticated limit once a repository passes about 100 PRs, and agents' own `gh` calls share that limit. The call is register_unlocked with a 10 s timeout, so it does not hold the store mutex.
v1.correction: The '~3,600 per hour' figure is a ceiling: it needs file events at least once a second with the Code or Agents page open, which is common while agents work. The proposed fix as written would lose behaviour. The handler also uses the full list to find merged PRs whose leftover branches it cleans up (git.rs:629-641, branch_cleanup::after_merged_prs). Fix: keep the per-branch lookup for the panel (`gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` or a `head=` filter), cache results per (repo, branch) with a TTL that git.push / git.pr.open invalidate, and run the full merged-PR sweep rarely (on its own timer, or with a conditional/ETag request or `gh api --cache`).

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. list_pull_requests (git.rs:1083-1112) runs `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100...`. Nothing caches the result anywhere: there is no cache in the handler (625-644), in engine dispatch (engine.rs:1175-1211) or in OpMeta. The `8` in OpMeta::query is a roadmap phase, not a rate limit. refresh_git (code_git.rs:142-583) calls git.pr.list every time, with no check that the Git panel is visible. It uses the result only to find the current branch's PR (592-604). This contradicts a recorded decision: D130 (DECISIONS.md:635-640) says the Code surface asks git.pr.list once when the project opens, and "File-watch refreshes do not repeat the network request."

(b) The trigger is reachable in normal use.
- Any file.changed, git.changed, worktree.changed or integration.* event for the current project calls Editor::invalidate (app.rs:1232-1240). Events are filtered by project (1213-1222), not by worktree.
- invalidate refreshes after a 1 s debounce whenever the page is `agents` or `code` (editor.rs:508-529). `agents` is the startup page (app.rs:747), the editor root is that page (618), and `code` maps onto it (1314-1315).
- The project-root watcher ignores `.relay/` (watch.rs:169-187). Agents' commits, fetches and pushes still count, because they write the shared `.git/refs/*` and `.git/config` (163-167).
- An agent's edits in its pooled worktree count once that worktree has a watcher. One is registered the first time anyone calls git.status, file.tree, file.read or file.search on it (git.rs:164; file.rs:21, 41, 301), and it is never removed. That happens when the person picks the checkout in the scope picker (project_files.rs:87-105), or when the agent calls those ops through Relay MCP: root_choice defaults to the caller's own worktree (file.rs:463-465).
- refresh_git merges overlapping runs (GitRefreshGuard, code_git.rs:4-12, 146-149). So under steady file activity, about one gh request is in flight all the time, or one per second for a single fast page. That is roughly 2,000-3,600 REST requests an hour during active multi-agent work.

(c) What happens when it fires:
- Each refresh spawns gh and downloads the project's whole PR history. Every item embeds the full head and base repository objects, so a page of 100 runs to about a megabyte.
- The call occupies the main UI connection while it runs, because one connection is served in order (socket.rs:335-745). Terminal input is not affected, since each pane has its own connection (terminal.rs:476). That head-of-line effect is a separate finding.
- Repositories with more than about 100 PRs can use up the 5,000/hour REST quota from this panel alone. Smaller ones reach up to about 72% of it.
- Once the quota runs out, `gh api user` fails and github.status reports GitHub as not connected (github.rs:45-53). github.repo.list (69-76), this panel, and the user's other REST clients also fail for up to an hour.
- The cost grows with PR history forever. Once a full listing takes more than 10 s, every call times out and the panel shows "GitHub unavailable · status unknown" permanently.
- Each call also spawns a cleanup thread (see the correction).

(d) High is right for the rubric: the work is repeated during the normal flow, it contradicts D130, and it grows without bound with the repository's PR history. Quota exhaustion is plausible rather than certain. It needs sustained activity, and with 100 or fewer PRs it also needs other REST traffic.

(e) The proposed fix is directionally right, but as written it changes the bus op's contract and drops the merged-PR cleanup trigger.
v2.correction:
Impact corrections:
- "Every gh command fails" is too broad. GitHub's REST and GraphQL quotas are separate, and most `gh pr` subcommands, including branch_cleanup's `gh pr list` (branch_cleanup.rs:167-178), use GraphQL. What breaks is REST callers: `gh api`, `gh run`/`gh workflow`, Relay's github.status (which shows GitHub as not connected) and github.repo.list, this panel, and the user's other GitHub apps.
- The rate is not "3,600 × pages" an hour. Overlapping refreshes are merged while one is in flight, so the ceiling is about one page request in flight continuously: roughly 3,600 an hour at 1 s per page. With 100 or fewer PRs it peaks around 3,600 an hour and cannot exhaust the quota on its own.
- "About once per file event" is really "about once per 1 s debounce window, while the agents/code page is shown".
- Add: for large repositories, once a listing takes more than 10 s every call times out, the panel stays "GitHub unavailable", and the requests already spent are wasted.

Related amplifier (separate root cause, worth its own finding):
- On every call, `leftover` (git.rs:631-641) matches merged PR branch names against all closed sessions (branch_cleanup.rs:74-80). It never checks that the branch still exists.
- Closed rows keep their branch (session.rs:1533, 1608) and are deleted only with their project (workspace.rs:360), so matches accumulate forever.
- Each call therefore spawns a branch-cleanup thread through after_merged_prs (use_gh_cache false, 416-425). That thread runs at least one `git rev-parse` per such session, waits on the global SWEEPING lock, and makes a GraphQL `gh pr list` for every pushed branch it keeps.
- Fix: filter `leftover` to refs/heads that still exist, and skip spawning while a cleanup for the project is already queued.

Fix corrections:
1. Do not change git.pr.list's contract ("All pull request states ... across every page", `complete`). MCP agents call it too. Add a `branch` parameter, or a separate op that uses REST `pulls?state=all&head=<owner>:<branch>`: one request, and the owner qualifier keeps same_repository correct.
2. If `gh pr list --head` is used instead, `headRepository` has no owner. Use `isCrossRepository`, and map the uppercase OPEN/CLOSED/MERGED states.
3. Do what D130 says in the client: fetch on project or checkout open, branch switch, push, PR open and the Refresh button, and reuse the last answer on file-watch invalidations. Add an engine-side TTL cache, or `gh api --cache`.
4. Leave merged-branch cleanup to the existing 20-minute sweep (SWEEP_EVERY, branch_cleanup.rs:42), or run it on a slow timer.

findings.title: file.search reads every file whole and skips only four directory names (diverged from watch::is_generated_path)
findings.evidence: The walk descends into every directory except `".git" | ".relay" | "node_modules" | "target"` (skip_dir, file.rs:629-636) and does `fs::File::open(&path).and_then(|mut file| std::io::Read::read_to_end(&mut file, &mut buffer))` for each file with no size cap before testing UTF-8 (334-343); the reused buffer keeps the largest capacity seen. watch::is_generated_path already lists build, dist, .gradle, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache, Binaries, coverage, .next, .svelte-kit (watch.rs:169-187) and list_dir uses it (file.rs:519), but search does not. No time budget; hits stop the walk only at the hit limit.
findings.impact: On an Unreal project (Content/*.uasset, DerivedDataCache, Intermediate, Saved, Binaries) or an Android one (build/, .gradle/), a search with few hits reads gigabytes and grows the buffer to the largest file — tens of seconds to minutes on a blocking thread, holding the UI connection (head-of-line) past the 30 s client timeout; with a query left in the Code panel's search box it is re-run on every file event (cascade finding).
findings.fix: Prune with watch::is_generated_path (better: the `ignore` crate honouring .gitignore), skip files above a few MiB or whose first 8 KiB contain NUL before reading the rest, and add a wall-time budget that returns partial hits. Keep one shared 'generated directory' list (watch.rs, file.rs skip_dir, worktree::BUILD_DIRS, app.rs dir_usage, workspace discover all differ).

v1.reason: file.search (file.rs:299-375, register_unlocked) walks the whole tree and prunes only components matching skip_dir's `".git" | ".relay" | "node_modules" | "target"` (file.rs:629-636). For every file it calls `read_to_end` into a reused buffer (334-336) with no size cap, and only afterwards rejects non-UTF-8 (340). There is no time budget, and the walk stops early only at the hit limit. watch::is_generated_path (watch.rs:158-187) already lists build, .gradle, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache, Binaries, dist and others, so the two lists have diverged. In the UI, editor.rs:1100-1114 calls file.search, and invalidate() (editor.rs:508-528) re-runs it on every debounced file event (1 s) whenever a query is left in the search box. The server reads the next request on a connection only after the previous one completes (socket.rs:740-743), and the UI uses a single client (app.rs:1111-1116), so a long search delays the UI's later requests.
v1.correction: Pruning with is_generated_path alone would not fix the Unreal case. Content/ (GBs of .uasset) is source and not in any skip list, so the decisive fix is to sniff the first 8 KiB for NUL or invalid UTF-8 and apply a per-file size cap before reading the rest. Add a wall-time budget that returns partial hits as well. The buffer keeping the largest capacity seen lasts only for the duration of the request. Whether the cost is seconds (page cache) or minutes (cold disk) depends on project size and could not be measured here.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. The walk at file.rs:316-328 prunes only skip_dir's ".git" | ".relay" | "node_modules" | "target" (file.rs:629-636). Every file is read whole with read_to_end (file.rs:334-336) before the UTF-8 check (file.rs:341). There is no size cap and no time budget. list_dir (file.rs:517-519) hides watch::is_generated_path dirs (watch.rs:158-188), but search does not.

(b) Reachability. Every Code-panel search on Enter (editor.rs:952-955) sends limit 100 with no glob (editor.rs:1110) and, with no worktree selected, searches the project root (file.rs:398-408). invalidate() re-runs it (editor.rs:508-528), and agents can call it through MCP. I could not run cargo, so I measured the user's own Relay-managed projects read-only with a Python emulation of the handler: same readdir order, same skip rule, same UTF-8 check, one hit per line, same limit.
- Game4 (UE5): a full walk reads 12,650 files and 5.53 GB. It takes 3.1 s cold (fincore showed 0 bytes cached) and 2.2 s warm on this Samsung 990 PRO with btrfs zstd. The reused buffer peaks at 380 MB (the Intermediate .gch file).
- So "tens of seconds to minutes, past the 30 s timeout" is not what happens on this machine. The cost scales linearly, so a project with tens of GB of Content, or a slower disk, would reach it.
- The stall lands only on the UI control connection, which is served one request at a time (socket.rs:335, 742-744). Terminals have their own connections (client.rs:1-2, terminal.rs:476). The handler is register_unlocked, so the store and the bus are not frozen.

(c) The decisive consequence is wrong results, from the same root cause. On btrfs, readdir returns entries in creation order. Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache and Binaries are created after Source, so they are pushed later and the DFS pops them first. Intermediate holds UHT-generated copies of every class name.
- Searching "Game4Character" on Game4 returns 100 of 100 hits from Intermediate/Build/.../UHT/*.gen.cpp and *.generated.h, shown as "(limit reached)". It returns 0 hits from Source, so the real .h and .cpp files never appear.
- "ForestWind" returns 99 of 100 hits from Intermediate and Saved/Logs, and none from Source/Game4/ForestWind.*.
- On Android projects, files the tree hides are 951 of 1,283 searched text files in Tally and 2,100 of 4,427 in Avex (build/ output).
- No data is lost. Each search also churns 5.5 GB through the page cache on a machine already 23 GB into zram swap.

(d) High stands, but because this is likely user-visible wrong behavior in a normal flow (searching a class name in a built Unreal C++ project). The performance cost alone (a stall of about 3 s per search on the UI connection) would be medium.

(e) The fix direction is right. Emulating "prune generated dirs + sniff the first 8 KiB for NUL" on Game4 reads 89 MB instead of 5.53 GB and takes 0.2-0.6 s. "Game4Character" then returns 24 real hits from Source and Config. Caveats are in the correction.
v2.correction:
Reframe this as a correctness bug with a performance cost. Replace "tens of seconds to minutes / past the 30 s timeout" with the measured figures: Game4, 12,650 files, 5.53 GB, 3.1 s cold / 2.2 s warm, buffer peak 380 MB. The headline impact is that the 100-hit limit fills with UHT-generated hits before Source is reached.

Fix details:
1. Prune with `skip_dir(relp) || crate::watch::is_generated_path(&root, &path)`, the same union list_dir uses (file.rs:518-519). Do not use is_generated_path alone: it treats only a root-level `.git` as generated (watch.rs:162), so nested `.git` dirs such as vendored plugin repos would start being walked.
2. A cap of "a few MiB" would drop tracked data such as Game4's Art/ForestExpansion/*.json (5.5-7.4 MB). Once binaries are sniffed, a cap is optional, or it can be high (about 32 MiB).
3. A wall-time budget needs a `truncated` flag in SearchOut, which today carries only `hits` (relay-bus/src/ops/file.rs:40), and matching text in the UI. Without it, partial results look complete.
4. Skip non-regular files. Opening a FIFO blocks forever, and a symlink to /dev/zero reads forever. Their metadata length is 0, so a size cap misses them.
5. Do not fold worktree::BUILD_DIRS into a shared list. It is the purge-before-remove list (worktree.rs:10-12), so adding view-filter names like Saved would delete Unreal autosaves and config. Share one predicate between file.tree and file.search only. editor.rs:1100 is the UI caller, not a list.

Separate root causes found while verifying; file them on their own:
(1) Hit.text is the whole matched line, with no bound (file.rs:358-364). Searching "SM_fern_02_02" on Game4 hits the tracked 7.4 MB single-line Art/ForestExpansion/original-foliage-transforms.json. The response is about 7.9 MB, over the native client's 2 MiB MAX_LINE (client.rs:48, 198-203). The client returns Error::Protocol, the main UI connection drops, and the UI shows "Engine disconnected" (app.rs:1267-1275). Pruning does not fix this, because Art/ is source.
(2) `fs::read_dir(&dir).map_err(..)?` (file.rs:317-318) fails the whole search if any directory is unreadable, or is deleted between being pushed and popped. A Gradle or UBT build cleaning build/ or Intermediate/ can do that, and the walk currently enters both.

findings.title: git.branches never received the §1.3 single-walk/object-cache fix that FIXES-2026-09-20 credits it with
findings.evidence: The bus op's handler (git.rs:290-344) still computes `let merged = head.as_ref().and_then(|h| repo.merge_base(*h, id.detach()).ok())...` and `upstream_metrics(&repo, &name)` per branch on a fresh `gix::open(&root)` with no `object_cache_size_if_unset`. The single walk (`merged_tips`, 1289-1308) and the 16 MiB cache exist only in `branches_for` (1445-1512), used by git.branch.delete and git.branch.clean_merged. The handler was identical at f2789df (`git show f2789df:crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs`), yet FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24 reports 'git.branches 10.0 ms → 899 µs ... one walk decides merged for every branch; object cache on' and lines 51-53 describe the change as if git.branches used it.
findings.impact: git.branches still costs branches × distance-to-base commit inflations, the pattern the baseline measured at 520 ms / 545 MB for ~150 branches (§1.3); Relay creates a relay/<session> branch per session, so it grows with use. It runs on every refresh_git (code_git.rs:579, i.e. per file event) and every scope-picker open (project_files.rs:194).
findings.fix: Make the handler use merged_tips with `repo.object_cache_size_if_unset(16 MiB)` (share the code with branches_for, adding remote_branches), and correct the FIXES table.

v1.reason: The bus handler `e.register_unlocked::<Branches>` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:290-344) still opens a plain `gix::open(&root)` with no object cache and computes `merged` per branch with `repo.merge_base(*h, id.detach())` (lines 324-328), plus `upstream_metrics` per branch. `merged_tips` (1289-1308) and `object_cache_size_if_unset(16 MiB)` exist only in `branches_for` (1445-1512), whose only callers are BranchDelete (455) and CleanMerged (695). `git show f2789d^` and `git show f2789df` show the Branches handler is the same before and after the perf commit; f2789df changed only `branches_for`. Yet docs/perf/FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24 credits `git.branches` with 10.0 ms → 899 µs ('one walk decides merged for every branch'). The native client calls git.branches from every refresh_git (code_git.rs:579). That refresh is debounced to at most about once a second by Editor::invalidate (editor.rs:508-528) and runs only while the Code or Agents page is shown.
v1.correction: The handler is register_unlocked, so this costs CPU and memory on a worker thread and does not hold the store mutex. The 520 ms / 545 MB baseline was clean_merged's, so git.branches' own cost is lower, and merged session branches get cleaned up (branch_cleanup), which limits how far it grows. This is also docs drift: the FIXES table and commit f2789df credit a change the handler never got. Fix: build the bus handler on the same tip collection plus merged_tips with the 16 MiB cache (shared with branches_for, keeping the owners-by-worktree lookup and remote_branches), and correct the FIXES row.

findings.title: Worktree watchers are never removed: one thread + inotify instance leaked per worktree, and a recreated worktree at the same path is never watched again
findings.evidence: `watchers.insert(key.clone(), watcher)` (watch.rs:132-146) is the only write to `engine.watchers: Mutex<HashMap<String, RecommendedWatcher>>` (engine.rs:420); nothing ever removes an entry. Each notify 8.2 INotifyWatcher owns an inotify fd and spawns a 'notify-rs inotify loop' thread. When the worktree directory is deleted notify drops its watch (DELETE_SELF → remove_watch) but the map entry stays, and ensure_after_commit returns early on `if engine.watchers.lock().unwrap().contains_key(&key) { return; }` (watch.rs:53). Session worktrees live at `.relay/worktrees/<session name>` and a name is accepted again once that path no longer exists (session.rs:839-842).
findings.impact: Every worktree that ever received a file.tree/file.read/file.search/git.status (agents' own MCP file tools do this) keeps a thread and an inotify instance until the engine restarts — fs.inotify.max_user_instances is 128 on many distros and exhaustion also breaks other applications' watchers. When a later session reuses a name, its worktree is never watched, so the tree/git panels for it never refresh on change.
findings.fix: Remove the entry when a worktree is removed or its session closes (and when the root's Remove(Folder) event arrives), or keep one watcher per project root and route by path.

v1.reason: The only reads or writes of `engine.watchers` (engine.rs:420, initialised at :457) are in watch.rs: the `contains_key` early return at :53, and the check-then-insert at :134-138. Nothing in the crate removes an entry. Removing a worktree (worktree.rs:352 `remove`, which runs `git worktree remove --force` and falls back to `remove_dir_all`) and closing a session never touch the map. Four handlers call `ensure_after_commit`: file.tree, file.read and file.search (file.rs:21/41/301) and git.status (git.rs:164). They do so for whatever worktree they resolve, so every session worktree that the UI or an agent's MCP file/git tools touch gets a watcher. In notify 8.2.0, each INotifyWatcher calls `Inotify::init()` (inotify.rs:539) and spawns a "notify-rs inotify loop" thread (inotify.rs:123-124). Both live until the watcher is dropped, which happens only at engine shutdown. When the worktree is deleted, the kernel releases the per-directory watches, but the inotify instance and the thread stay, so each session ever opened and then closed leaks one inotify instance (counted against fs.inotify.max_user_instances, which defaults to 128 in the kernel and is shared with every other app of the same user) and one idle thread. Name reuse is real but rare: `sessions::new_name` (sessions.rs:74-89) excludes only names whose session is not closed, and there are 36x36 = 1296 names, so a closed session's name (and its pooled path) can come back. When it does, `ensure_after_commit` returns early because of the stale key, and the new worktree is never watched, so its tree and git panels stop auto-refreshing.
v1.correction: The stale-key problem on a recreated worktree is real but rare (1296-name space). The main impact is the steady leak of one inotify instance and one thread per closed session in a long-running engine. On a heavy day with many agent sessions this can reach the 128-instance limit (on distros that keep the kernel default), after which new watchers fail silently: `ensure` returns without registering, and the next request retries the registration and fails again. Other applications' file watchers also break. Fix: remove `engine.watchers[canonical path]` (dropping the watcher closes its fd and stops its thread) wherever a worktree is removed (worktree::remove and its callers, session close and purge), and optionally on a DELETE_SELF/Remove event for the root itself.

findings.title: Launch-time recovery VACUUMs the entire store whenever any audit row aged out, i.e. on nearly every start once the store is older than the retention window
findings.evidence: Step 7 deletes audit rows older than `audit.retention_days` (default 180, recovery.rs:183-206) and then `if pruned > 0 { conn.execute_batch("VACUUM") }` (217-221). serve::start runs recovery synchronously before `SocketServer::start` (serve.rs:23, 36). D151 says it 'compacts the store only when a prune actually removed something', which at steady state is every launch.
findings.impact: After the first 180 days every launch removes the rows that crossed the window since the previous launch and rewrites the whole database before any client can connect. The dev store on this machine is already 179 MB (~/.local/share/relay-v4/dev/store.db, data dir dated Sep 4), which extrapolates to ~1 GB at 180 days: seconds to tens of seconds per engine start during which the UI shows 'Connecting' and agents' hooks fail.
findings.fix: VACUUM only when `PRAGMA freelist_count` is a large share of `page_count` (e.g. >25%), or enable auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL and run `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(N)` on a worker after the door is open; run the prune itself on that worker too.

v1.reason: recovery.rs:183-206 deletes audit rows older than audit.retention_days (default 180). recovery.rs:217-221 then runs `conn.execute_batch("VACUUM")` whenever pruned > 0. serve.rs:23 runs recovery::run_with synchronously, before SocketServer::start at serve.rs:36, so no client can connect until the VACUUM finishes. In normal daily use, once the store is older than the window, every launch has rows that crossed the cutoff since the previous launch, so every launch rewrites the whole database. D151 (DECISIONS.md:839-841) says it compacts 'only when a prune actually removed something' and treats that as rare, but at steady state it is the common case. The dev store is already 190 MB after about a month (store.db, dir dated Sep 4).
v1.correction: The cost is a full rewrite of the database on every launch, proportional to total store size rather than to how many rows were pruned. Expect seconds at a few hundred MB, during which the UI shows Connecting. Fix: VACUUM only when `PRAGMA freelist_count` is a large fraction of page_count (or use auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL with incremental_vacuum on a worker), and do it after the socket is open.

findings.title: Audit log keeps the whole post-edit file for every agent Edit/Write gate, and undo_op is stored with no size cap (wallpaper rotation writes an image per rotation)
findings.evidence: store_limit gives the 2 KB cap only to `"session.report" | "usage.report"`; everything else keeps 64 KB (audit.rs:22-27, 88-93). The Claude PreToolUse hook turns every Edit/MultiEdit into guardrail.gate with `"new_text": next` — the entire file after the edit (relay-cli/src/main.rs:419-432), and guardrail.gate is an always-audited mutation (relay-bus/src/ops/guardrail.rs:16-17), so each edit of a file ≤64 KB stores the whole file. undo_op is written as `e.undo_op.map(|u| serde_json::to_string(u).unwrap_or_default())` with no limit (audit.rs:123); settings.set records the entire previous value as its undo (settings.rs:220), and wallpaper rotation calls settings.set on appearance.wallpaper (a data: URI image) every interval, default 15 min (wallpaper_rotation.rs:122-128, 168-171).
findings.impact: Two PreToolUse/PostToolUse audit rows per agent tool use, the Edit/Write ones carrying whole files, plus ~100-400 KB per rotation with custom wallpapers (≈96 rotations/day) — tens of MB per day retained for 180 days. The store here is already 179 MB after about a month; this growth feeds the launch VACUUM finding and every audit scan (task.activity, dashboard).
findings.fix: Put guardrail.gate under the chatty limit (or record path + sha256 + line counts instead of new_text); apply the same size policy to undo_op (store oversized inverse values by reference or mark the row non-undoable).

v1.reason: Every hook-driven gate is audited at full size. hooks.rs:350 installs the Claude PreToolUse hook with matcher "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash". main.rs:417-431 turns each Edit into guardrail.gate with `"new_text": next`, the whole file after the edit. guardrail.gate is `OpMeta::mutation` (guardrail.rs:16), and mutation() defaults to `audit: Audit::Always` (registry.rs:117); should_audit (engine.rs:1394) returns true. store_limit (audit.rs:22-27) gives the 2 KB cap only to session.report and usage.report, so any payload up to 64 KB is stored verbatim. undo_op is written with no limit at all (audit.rs:123). settings.set (UserOnly, Undo::Inverse) records the whole previous subtree as its undo (settings.rs:217-220). Wallpaper rotation calls settings.set on appearance.wallpaper, whose value is a data:image URI, on every interval (wallpaper_rotation.rs:122-171, default 15 min). Custom wallpapers are JPEG 1280x900 at quality 80, base64-encoded (tools_settings.rs:1003-1009), so each is roughly 100-500 KB. The built-in presets are about 12 KB of base64 each. Each rotation stores the previous image uncapped in undo_op, plus up to 64 KB each in payload and result_summary. Retention is 180 days by default (recovery.rs:18).
v1.correction: Rotation is opt-in (it returns early unless `config["enabled"] == true`), so the wallpaper growth applies only to users who turn it on. Even the built-in presets add about 36 KB per rotation, about 3.5 MB a day. With custom images it is 10-40 MB a day, mostly from the uncapped undo_op. The 179 MB store figure could not be checked from the repo. Fix: put guardrail.gate under CHATTY_STORE_LIMIT, or store path, sha256 and length instead of new_text. Apply store_limit to undo_op too; an oversized inverse should make the row non-undoable rather than be kept whole. The wallpaper could also be referenced by library id instead of being stored inline.

findings.title: session.attach takes the store mutex on a tokio worker thread
findings.evidence: After the attach is validated on the blocking pool, the async handler calls `crate::handlers::session::pty_by_name(&engine, &p.session)` inline (socket.rs:469), which does `let conn = engine.store.lock(); let row = sessions::by_name(&conn, name)?;` (session.rs:1732-1736) — a blocking std::sync::Mutex wait on a runtime worker.
findings.impact: If a long locked handler (clone, git add, file.write diff, see the other findings) is queued for the mutex when panes re-attach (window restore, gap reconnect, page switch), each attach parks a runtime worker; with as many attaching panes as worker threads the whole socket door stalls, including D148's in-memory keystroke path.
findings.fix: Use `engine.pty_named(&p.session)` (in-memory map) or move the lookup into the spawn_blocking closure that already validated the attach.

v1.reason: socket.rs:469 calls `crate::handlers::session::pty_by_name(&engine, &p.session)` directly in the async connection task. That function (session.rs:1731-1739) does `engine.store.lock()` plus a sessions::by_name query, a blocking mutex wait on a tokio worker. Every other store access in handle_conn goes through spawn_blocking (for example socket.rs:417-420 for bus.wait). Engine::pty_named (engine.rs:600-608) already resolves name to PTY from in-memory maps without the store.
v1.correction: The engine runs under relay-cli's `#[tokio::main]` (main.rs:106), which uses the default worker count (one per core), not the 2-worker native runtime. D149 also moved slow work off the lock and warns past 16 ms. So stalling every worker would need as many simultaneous attaches as cores, all queued behind a long locked handler. The realistic effect is a brief worker park on re-attach bursts. Fix: use `engine.pty_named(&p.session)`, or do the lookup inside the preceding spawn_blocking closure.

findings.title: Recursive watchers cover every session worktree and all build output; IN_OPEN floods and queue overflow become file.changed
findings.evidence: `watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive)` on the project root (watch.rs:133); the worktree pool lives inside it (`repo.join(".relay").join("worktrees")`, worktree.rs:14-16). Generated paths are dropped only after the event (watch.rs:98-111). notify 8.2's inotify backend adds a watch for every directory (WalkDir) and its mask includes WatchMask::OPEN, so every open() is delivered; an IN_Q_OVERFLOW becomes `Flag::Rescan`, and `need_rescan()` bypasses both filters here (watch.rs:95-115) → file.changed. A write to .git/index re-opens the repo and hashes every index entry on the notify thread (watch.rs:13-25, 103-107), and status_files sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1 so Relay's own statuses rewrite the index.
findings.impact: On the user's project root the watcher holds ~24.6k directory watches, ~21k of them under target/ or node_modules (find), so every cargo/npm build in any session worktree is processed event by event on the notify thread; overflow bursts emit file.changed and start the editor refresh cascade.
findings.fix: Walk with is_generated_path/.gitignore pruning (skipping .relay) and add NonRecursive watches per kept directory (adding new ones on Create(Folder)); treat Access events at the mask level if notify allows, and debounce Rescan.

v1.reason: watch.rs:133 calls `watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive)`. file.tree, file.read and git.status (file.rs:21/41, git.rs:164) call ensure_after_commit on the resolved root, which is the project root when no worktree is given, and that root contains .relay/worktrees (worktree.rs:14-16). notify 8.2's inotify backend uses a mask that includes WatchMask::OPEN (inotify.rs:425-432) and turns IN_Q_OVERFLOW into Flag::Rescan (inotify.rs:212-213). The callback drops Access and generated paths only after the event arrives, and `need_rescan()` skips both filters (watch.rs:95-115), so an overflow emits file.changed. I measured the RelayV4 root at 24,634 directories, 21,177 of them under target/ or node_modules/. max_queued_events is 16384, so a cargo build in any session worktree can plausibly overflow the queue.
v1.correction: Impact is CPU on the notify thread during builds, plus occasional spurious file.changed refreshes; these are coalesced by the 125 ms pending flag, so this is not a storm. Session worktrees can also be watched again under their own roots, which doubles the coverage. On a system with a low max_user_watches, the recursive registration can fail outright and leave no watcher. Fix: register per-directory NonRecursive watches pruned by is_generated_path (including .relay), adding new directories on Create(Folder), and debounce Rescan.

findings.title: session.scrollback defaults to the whole 8 MiB ring and builds it inside the store transaction
findings.evidence: `e.register::<Scrollback>` (session.rs:1701) with `p.lines` None calls `pty.scrollback(None)` → `ring.bytes_from(0)` + `String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()` (pty.rs:323-339) while the handler's transaction holds the store mutex; the result is then JSON-escaped (ESC → \u001b).
findings.impact: An agent calling session_scrollback without `lines` receives up to ~8 MiB (plus escaping) of raw terminal bytes into its context, and the copy/conversion holds the global lock (baseline: 3.4 ms and 10 MB allocated for a 1.8 MB ring).
findings.fix: Default `lines` (e.g. 200) and cap bytes; register it unlocked (a query whose live path needs no store).

v1.reason: Scrollback is `e.register::<Scrollback>` (session.rs:1701), so it runs inside the transaction with the store mutex held. When `p.lines` is None, `pty.scrollback(None)` calls `ring.bytes_from(0)` and `String::from_utf8_lossy(..).into_owned()` over the whole ring, up to SCROLLBACK_BYTES = 8 MiB (pty.rs:16, 323-339). The payload makes `lines` optional (relay-bus ops/session.rs:161). No native, CLI or remote caller uses session.scrollback, so it is reached through MCP/agents. The lock hold is a few milliseconds of memcpy and UTF-8 conversion, and the oversized result mostly floods an agent's context.
v1.correction: The live-PTY path needs no SQLite, but the fallback (`sessions::load_scrollback`) and the ownership check do. Registering it unlocked means doing by_name/assert_own through ctx.read and then reading the ring with nothing held. Default `lines` (e.g. 200) and cap the bytes.

findings.title: Devices page requests worktree dirty flags it never reads (one full git status per checkout)
findings.evidence: `ui.call("worktree.list", json!({"project_id":project}))` (tools_devices.rs:38 and 630) omits include_dirty; the handler defaults it to true (`p.include_dirty.unwrap_or(true)`, git.rs:96), so list_with_dirty runs `is_dirty` → `git status --untracked-files=all` for the primary and every linked worktree in sequence (worktree.rs:139-150). tools_devices.rs never reads `dirty` (rg finds no use).
findings.impact: Opening Device control or the device panel costs one status per session worktree on the UI connection before the form appears.
findings.fix: Pass `"include_dirty": false` as editor.rs:925 does (or default it to false and opt in).

v1.reason: tools_devices.rs:38 and :630 call worktree.list with only project_id. The handler defaults include_dirty to true (git.rs:96). list_with_dirty then runs is_dirty, which calls status_files, a `git status --untracked-files=all` subprocess (worktree.rs:78-92, 139-150), once for the primary and once for each linked worktree, in sequence. The only consumer is WorktreePicker::new (tools_devices.rs:231-237), which reads only branch and path. `dirty` is never read in tools_devices.rs. editor.rs:925 already passes include_dirty:false for the same purpose.

findings.title: Board rebuilds every card on every task/session event with per-card linear scans (O(n²))
findings.evidence: board_view::show stores the new list and calls `board.render()` (497-503), which `clear(&self.content)` and rebuilds all lanes and cards (1181-1190, 1642-1650) on each refresh_page (task events; session.changed on the board page, agent_menu.rs:133-135). Per card: `all.iter().find(|t| t["id"] == task["duplicate_of"])` (1796) and in list rows `rows(task, "blocked_by").iter().any(|other| all.iter().any(|t| t["id"] == *other ...))` (1937-1939); pages.rs:69-75 also scans modules per task.
findings.impact: With hundreds of tasks and agents moving them, every event rebuilds hundreds of card widgets plus O(n²) serde_json Value comparisons on the GTK main thread (client could not be built here to measure).
findings.fix: Build an id→task HashMap once per render and update only changed cards (or reuse card widgets keyed by id).

v1.reason: board_view::show stores the tasks and calls board.render() (board_view.rs:502-503). render() does clear(&self.content) and rebuilds every lane and card (1181-1190). apply_session_event calls refresh_page while the board is showing (agent_menu.rs:133-135), which re-runs task.list plus module.list (pages.rs:66-75) and a full rebuild on every session.changed. The per-card linear scans are real (`all.iter().find(|t| t["id"] == task["duplicate_of"])` at 1796, and the nested any at 1937-1939). The O(n²) Value comparisons are negligible at realistic task counts. The real cost is rebuilding every card widget on each session/task event. The GTK client cannot be built here, so this is not measured.
v1.correction: The dominant cost is the full widget rebuild, plus the task.list and module.list round trips, on every session.changed while the board is open, not the O(n²) scans. Skip the board refresh for session events that do not change task-visible fields, or diff cards by id. An id-to-task HashMap is a minor addition.

findings.title: Each keystroke waits for the previous keystroke's response, which is queued behind the pane's PTY output
findings.evidence: The input future handles one key at a time: `client.request(&p.rt, "session.input", ...).await` (terminal.rs:229-248). The engine answers it through the same `out_tx` mpsc (capacity 1024 lines, socket.rs:295, 744) that carries the pane's frames (488-489); the client reader handles lines in order and blocks on the 64-slot notices channel while GTK feeds VTE (client.rs:179, 232-255).
findings.impact: While an agent prints heavily, each further keystroke is delayed by the whole output backlog ahead of the previous response (up to ~1024 frames + socket buffers + VTE feeding), so typed characters arrive in proportion to output volume rather than at keystroke latency.
findings.fix: Pipeline input: enqueue requests without awaiting each response (the engine processes a connection's input in order) and surface errors asynchronously, or send input on its own connection.

v1.reason: Each pane opens its own connection (terminal.rs:476-487). The input future awaits each session.input response before sending the next one (terminal.rs:229-248). On the engine, handle_conn sends a request's response through the same out_tx (capacity 1024, socket.rs:295) that the attach task feeds PTY frames into (socket.rs:488-489). The response is pushed after session.input is answered inline (socket.rs:737-744). The client reader processes lines in order and blocks on the 64-slot notices channel (client.rs:179, 232-237) while GTK feeds VTE. So the mechanism holds: under heavy output, each keystroke's response sits behind the queued frames, and the next keystroke waits for it. The engine processes a connection's requests in order, so pipelining would be safe. The impact is bounded: keystrokes are buffered (64 slots), not lost, and VTE drains quickly. This affects only typing into a pane that is printing heavily, and the magnitude was not measured.

findings.title: Branch sweeper polls every second for the engine's lifetime and re-checks every kept branch with ~10 subprocesses per sweep
findings.evidence: `while Instant::now() < deadline { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); match weak.upgrade() {...} }` (branch_cleanup.rs:436-441), sweeping every 20 min (42, 451-453) over every closed session's branch that still exists (candidates, 74-94); `evaluate` runs rev-parse, `worktree list --porcelain`, `config --get` ×1-2, rev-parse ×2-3, `merge-base --is-ancestor`, `cherry` per base, plus `gh pr list` (cached 1 h) per branch (200-280). Added 2026-10-05 (2d38f75), after the baseline.
findings.impact: Breaks the baseline's '0 wakeups at rest' (now ≥1/s) and SPEC's 'no polling timers'; the sweep's cost grows with every abandoned session branch (100 kept branches ≈ 1,000 git spawns every 20 min and ~100 GitHub calls/hour).
findings.fix: Wait on a quit Condvar/channel with a timeout instead of 1 s sleeps, and remember 'kept, tip and base unchanged' verdicts so unchanged branches are skipped.

v1.reason: branch_cleanup.rs:435-442 loops `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1))` and calls weak.upgrade() for the engine's whole lifetime, only to notice quit or drop. That is one wakeup per second at rest, against SPEC.md:34 ("NO polling timers anywhere in v4") and the perf baseline's 0 wakeups/s at rest (docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:39). Every 20 min (SWEEP_EVERY, line 42) run() evaluates every closed session's branch that still exists (candidates, lines 74-94). For an unmerged branch, evaluate (200-280) spawns rev-parse, worktree list, 1-2 config gets, 2-3 rev-parse for the bases, merge-base --is-ancestor and cherry per base, and rev-list --count. gh pr list is skipped only while the tip is unchanged within GH_RECHECK (1 h).
v1.correction: The cost is small. The thread runs at background priority, a 1 Hz wakeup is negligible CPU, and about 10 short git spawns per kept branch every 20 min cost a few seconds of CPU at most, even with 100 abandoned branches. The main point is the broken idle and no-polling contract. Fix: wait on a Condvar or channel signalled at quit, with a SWEEP_EVERY timeout. Optionally cache the 'kept' verdict keyed on (tip, base tip) so unchanged branches are skipped.

findings.title: PTY scrollback ring grows to as much as twice its 8 MiB budget
findings.evidence: `self.buf.extend(data);` runs before `if self.buf.len() > SCROLLBACK_BYTES { ... drain(..excess) }` (pty.rs:65-70), so the VecDeque must hold SCROLLBACK_BYTES + one read; amortized growth doubles the capacity past 8 MiB (to ~12-16 MiB depending on the first chunk), and as the ring wraps it touches the whole allocation. A resume pushes up to 8 MiB at once (192), forcing the next growth to 16 MiB.
findings.impact: Each busy session settles at ~12-16 MiB of RSS for its ring instead of 8 MiB; with an 11-pane wall that is ~50-90 MB above budget.
findings.fix: Trim before extending (drain the bytes the new chunk will push out), or allocate with `VecDeque::with_capacity(SCROLLBACK_BYTES + 64 * 1024)` once the ring first fills.

v1.reason: pty.rs:58-71 Ring::push does `self.buf.extend(data)` and only then drains back to SCROLLBACK_BYTES (8 MiB, pty.rs:16). The ring starts as `VecDeque::new()` (pty.rs:190), so once len first reaches 8 MiB + one read the deque must reallocate, and amortized doubling takes the capacity to about 16 MiB. A resume seeds the ring with up to 8 MiB at once (pty.rs:191-192), which reaches that point sooner. At steady state the head keeps advancing, so the written region cycles through the whole allocation and every page ends up resident. Nothing ever shrinks the buffer.
v1.correction: The realistic figure is about 16 MiB of capacity per session that has produced more than 8 MiB of output, not 12-16 MiB. That is roughly 8 MiB over budget per busy session. This is memory overhead, not a leak: it is bounded and freed when the PTY drops. Category performance rather than resource-leak. Simplest fix: allocate `VecDeque::with_capacity(SCROLLBACK_BYTES + max read size)` once, or trim before extending.

findings.title: ue_log reads, filters and re-joins the entire Unreal log on every call to return a 200-line tail
findings.evidence: `let bytes = std::fs::read(&path)?; let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes);` then `let kept: Vec<&str> = text.lines().filter(..).collect();` and `tail(&kept.join("\n"), lines)` (unreal.rs:1611-1623), where tail splits into lines and joins again (1590-1600). unreal_process.rs:126 likewise reads the whole log to inspect its first 400 lines.
findings.impact: Editor logs reach tens to hundreds of MB; every agent ue_log call reads the whole file and holds roughly three copies in memory to return 200 lines, adding seconds and hundreds of MB per call during Unreal work.
findings.fix: Read backwards from the end in blocks until enough (matching) lines are collected, or cap the read to the last few MiB; for the 400-line header probe read only the first block.

v1.reason: unreal.rs:1611 `std::fs::read(&path)` then from_utf8_lossy, then `text.lines().filter(..).collect()` and `tail(&kept.join("\n"), lines)` (1619-1623); tail (1590-1601) collects every line again and joins the last N. So the whole log is read and an almost full-size joined copy is built to return at most 5000 lines. unreal_process.rs:126 `read_to_string(log)` then `.lines().take(400)` reads the whole log for a header probe. Nothing upstream caps the size. This runs in the CLI/MCP process, not under the engine's store mutex, so the cost lands only on the calling agent.
v1.correction: The impact is overstated. from_utf8_lossy borrows when the log is valid UTF-8, so the real cost is the byte buffer plus one joined copy, about 2x the file size, not 3x. UE rotates its log on each editor start, so a log is typically a few to tens of MB and a call takes tens to hundreds of ms, not seconds. The unreal_process.rs:126 probe runs only in the engine-root discovery fallback, after UE_ROOT and a running editor have both failed. The fix still stands: seek to the end and read blocks backwards (or read the last few MiB), and use a BufReader with take(400) for the header probe.

results.coverage:
Scope: the resource-lifecycle lens, followed across crates/relay-core, relay-bus, relay-cli, relay-remote and the parts of apps/relay-native that handle connections and attachments. apps/relay-mobile was excluded.

Search patterns (rg):
- Engine maps: `\.(mirrors|device_runs|watchers|provider_updates|creating_sessions|watcher_registrations|resource_cpu|resource_disk)`
- Threads and tasks: `thread::spawn|thread::Builder::new\(\)|spawn_blocking|tokio::spawn`
- Subprocesses: `\.output\(\)|\.status\(\)|\.spawn\(\)|wait_with_output|output_with_timeout`
- Kills and reaping: `libc::kill|\.kill\(\)`, `setsid|process.group|orphan|reap`
- Table growth: `INSERT (OR ..)? INTO <table>` counted per table, `DELETE FROM`, `grace_days|purge|reconcile`
- Global caches: `static .*Mutex|thread_local|LazyLock`
- Broadcast subscribers: `\.subscribe\(\)`
- Connection limits: `RLIMIT|keepalive|ping`
- Temp files and logs: `tempfile|temp_dir|json.tmp|relay-tmp`, `log_dir|tracing_appender`
- Result limits: LIMIT in list handlers
- Native client: `"mailbox.list"`, `ui.pane.open`, `session.scrollback`

Code read closely:
- Engine core: engine.rs, socket.rs, pty.rs, proc.rs, store.rs, recovery.rs, serve.rs, watch.rs, device.rs, branch_cleanup.rs, worktree.rs, provider_updates.rs, github.rs.
- Handlers: session, device (run, build, mirror, avd), integration, workspace, file, git, notes (mailbox), app, ui.
- relay-remote: bridge, direct, tunnel, rendezvous, registry.
- relay-cli: mcp.rs, remote.rs, the hook paths in main.rs, unreal_process.rs, the Unreal lock and image cleanup, and blender.rs temp dirs.
- Native: client.rs, terminal.rs, app.rs connect and event loop, pages.rs, mirror decode, sounds, image_preview and notification_center caches.
- Library internals: notify 8.2's inotify backend and tungstenite 0.30's default limits, read in ~/.cargo/registry.

Two scratchpad experiments ran under exp/: race.py reproduced the remote.json corruption, and unix_reset.py confirmed that closing an AF_UNIX socket with unread data gives the peer ECONNRESET.

Checked and not reported:
- Bounded by design: the PTY ring (8 MiB) and frame index, broadcast capacities, the device-run log buffer (512 lines), the mirror buffer (2 MiB), backups (KEEP_BACKUPS=5), the native thumbnail cache (64) and timers, notify.list, holds.list, integration.list and device.run.list limits, provider-update and Blender temp-dir cleanup, gradle-init NamedTempFile lifetimes, device lease expiry, and the creating_sessions Drop guard.
- Exited sessions keep their PTY (ring plus master fd) until close. This looks intentional (their scrollback stays readable) and is bounded by the sessions visible on the wall.
- resource_cpu (keyed by pid) and branch_cleanup's GH_CACHE never evict, but only grow by KBs.
- engine.ui panes grow only through agent or CLI ui.pane.open; the native client never calls it.
- Closing a session with remove_worktree:false keeps its worktree and branch. This is a documented choice, and branch_cleanup removes merged ones.
- A session.create failure after checkout preserves the worktree, as documented.
- No events, usage or activity tables exist. Audit is pruned only at launch, which is noted under the VACUUM finding.

Not finished:
- I could not verify how Claude Code and Codex group their tool subprocesses, so I cannot say whether a session's descendants escape the `kill(-pid)` in Pty::kill on close.
- A failed multi-skill install may leave skill folders orphaned; not traced.
- The remaining native UI files and guardrail.rs were only skimmed.
- Possible thread starvation from the inline `session.input` PTY write on tokio workers when a child stops reading was noted but not developed.

findings.title: Worktree file watchers are never dropped: one inotify instance, one thread and a recursive watch set per worktree ever opened, for the engine's whole lifetime
findings.evidence: file.tree, file.read and file.search (handlers/file.rs:21,41,301) and git.status (handlers/git.rs:164) all call ensure_after_commit for the worktree the caller names. Agents default to their own session worktree. ensure() builds notify::recommended_watcher, calls watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive) (watch.rs:133) and keeps it with `watchers.insert(key.clone(), watcher)` (watch.rs:138). Engine::watchers is a Mutex<HashMap<String, RecommendedWatcher>> (engine.rs:420). A grep finds only contains_key and insert on it, never a remove: not in session.close (session.rs:1547-1638), git.worktree.remove, integration.discard or project.remove. In notify 8.2 each INotifyWatcher owns an inotify fd, a mio epoll fd and an eventfd waker, plus a 'notify-rs inotify loop' thread that exits only on the Shutdown message sent from Drop (notify inotify.rs:128-150, 177-182, 606-611). Recursive mode walks the tree with WalkDir and adds one inotify watch for every directory, including target/, node_modules/ and .git/objects. The project-root watcher also covers every nested .relay/worktrees/<name>/ checkout. is_generated_path (watch.rs:158) only filters events inside the callback; it does not stop the watches that D57 says are ignored.
findings.impact: Each session worktree that an agent (via MCP file_read/git_status) or the Code view touches adds a permanent watcher. When a session closes and its checkout is removed, the watcher's thread and 3 fds stay. When the checkout is kept, all of its directory watches stay too; the shell's discard action passes remove_worktree:false (shell.rs:734). Kept watchers go on emitting file.changed for dead sessions. On this machine the project root alone has 24,634 directories and one worktree has 15,075, so a few dozen kept worktrees approach fs.inotify.max_user_watches (524,288 here). Each watch costs roughly 1 KiB of unswappable kernel memory. With the kernel-default max_user_instances of 128, a long-running engine can use up inotify instances for the whole user session.
