v1.reason: In crates/relay-cli/src/mcp.rs:20-31, serve() iterates over stdin.lock().lines() and awaits handle(...) for each line before it reads the next one. handle() returns None for any message without an id (36-40), so notifications/cancelled is silently dropped. call_tool (138-149) awaits client.call with no timeout. In crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs (Wait branch, about lines 405-449), bus.wait clamps timeout_ms to 1 s-3,600,000 ms and simply loops on rx.recv() under tokio::time::timeout. Nothing races the wait against the connection's read half, so a client that has gone away does not end it. grants.rs BOOTSTRAP_HINT tells agents to bus.wait on guardrail.request_resolved after a guardrail.request, so long waits are a designed, normal flow. While one wait is pending, every other tools/call from that agent (parallel calls, or the next turn after the user interrupts) and every MCP ping sits unread in the pipe until the wait returns.
v1.correction: The default wait is 60 s (unwrap_or(60_000)), so the 1 h stall only happens when the agent passes a long timeout_ms. Severity stays medium: one agent's Relay tools stall, not the engine or other sessions. The engine-side leak is minor: a broadcast receiver and a tokio task per abandoned wait, bounded by the timeout.

findings.title: The socket connection handler skips its cleanup on any read error or handler panic, including a client that closes with unread frames (ECONNRESET)
findings.evidence: `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? {` (socket.rs:335) and the `spawn_blocking(...).await?` calls (361, 419, 459, 511, 524, 652, 726, 742) return from handle_conn before the cleanup block that aborts `forwarder`, `attached` and `attached_runs` and awaits the writer (746-759). Dropping a tokio JoinHandle detaches the task rather than aborting it. On Linux, closing an AF_UNIX stream socket with unread data in its receive queue makes the peer's next read fail with ECONNRESET; a scratchpad experiment (exp/unix_reset.py) confirmed this. That is the normal case when a GUI terminal attachment (terminal.rs:446-451) or a device-run log client disconnects mid-stream.
findings.impact: The per-attachment PTY forwarder, the writer task and the socket's fd survive until that session next produces output, or until the next event for subscriptions. A handler panic also drops the client's response silently. The leak is bounded by the next output, but it builds up for idle sessions while the GUI switches projects.
findings.fix: Treat a read error like EOF: replace the `?` on next_line with a match that breaks on Err or None. Convert JoinErrors into an internal-error response. Put the aborts in a guard type with a Drop impl so every exit path runs them.

v1.reason: socket.rs:335 `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? {` and the `spawn_blocking(...).await?` calls (around 361, 419, 459, 511, 524, 652, 726, 742) return from handle_conn before the cleanup at 746-759, which aborts forwarder/attached/attached_runs and awaits the writer. Dropping a JoinHandle detaches the task. Linux sets ECONNRESET on the peer when a unix stream socket closes with unread data, which is the normal case when a GUI attached to a busy PTY disconnects. No catch_unwind exists in relay-core, so a handler panic takes the same path. The impact is bounded, though. attached_mirrors and the WatchLease Arcs are locals whose Drop impls (socket.rs:231-263) still run on early return. The detached forwarders exit on their next failed send, after the detached writer fails its write_all and drops out_rx. Until the next frame or event arrives, they hold only a few tasks and the write-half fd.
v1.correction: Severity stays low: the only leak is idle tasks and one fd per connection, released by that session's next PTY frame or broadcast event, and mirrors and watch leases are cleaned up by Drop regardless. A panic makes the client see EOF, or keeps it waiting while a detached forwarder holds out_tx, rather than getting an internal-error response. The fix is as proposed: treat Err from next_line like EOF, map JoinError to BusError::internal, and move the aborts into a Drop guard.

findings.title: Children that are spawned and then forgotten are never reaped, so zombie processes accumulate under the long-lived engine
findings.evidence: os.reveal and os.open_url run `std::process::Command::new("xdg-open").arg(target).spawn()` and drop the Child (ui.rs:343-345, 356-359). avd.boot runs `command.spawn().is_ok()` for the emulator (device.rs:353-358). A stopped run's killed shell or logcat child is never waited on (device.rs:1776-1777, 1843-1845). relay-cli's editor launch returns `child.id()` and drops the Child (unreal_process.rs:306-307). std::process::Child does not reap the process when dropped.
findings.impact: Each link or reveal click, each emulator session and each stopped run leaves a <defunct> process, holding a PID and an RLIMIT_NPROC slot, under the engine (or under the Unreal MCP server) until that parent exits.
findings.fix: Reap the children: hand each to a thread that calls wait(), or use tokio::process and spawn a task that awaits child.wait(). Detached launches can instead double-fork and call setsid. In the run worker, wait() after killing.

v1.reason: ui.rs:343-345 and 356-359 spawn xdg-open and drop the Child. xdg-open normally exits quickly, so each click leaves a defunct child under the engine. No SIGCHLD handler or SIG_IGN exists anywhere in crates/ (no 'SIGCHLD' or 'waitpid' matches). device.rs:353-358 (avd.boot) drops the emulator Child, so it becomes a zombie once the emulator exits. On RunStop (device.rs:263-267), RunRuntime::stop (device.rs:403-408) only kills the child. The run and logcat workers then return early on `runtime.stopped()` (device.rs:1776-1777, 1843-1845) without take_child()+wait(), so the killed child is never reaped. Compare the mirror path (device.rs:884-887), which does wait. unreal_process.rs:306-307 returns child.id() and drops the Child, so the editor becomes a zombie under the MCP server only after it exits.
v1.correction: The impact is only PID-table slots, until the engine exits. A fix: in the run and logcat workers, call take_child() and wait() on the stopped path. For fire-and-forget launches (xdg-open, emulator), spawn a thread that calls child.wait().

findings.title: The engine log is appended to forever with no rotation; the rotating log in the data dir that SPEC §14 describes was never wired up
findings.evidence: run.sh starts the engine with `nohup "$relay" ... serve --remote >>"$log" 2>&1`, where log is target/engine-$RELAY_INSTANCE.log (run.sh:29-32). The subscriber writes to stderr at info level by default (main.rs:210). Instance::log_dir() (paths.rs:63) is never used. SPEC §14 promises a 'rotating structured log (tracing crate) in ~/.local/share/relay/logs'.
findings.impact: Steady-state output keeps growing the file without bound: the branch sweep's per-branch lines every 20 minutes, 'store lock over budget' warnings, 'rendezvous unreachable' every 30 s or less while offline, and 'accept failed' every 50 ms under fd exhaustion. The file lives under target/, so `cargo clean` silently deletes the only diagnostics.
findings.fix: Use tracing-appender's rolling file writer into Instance::log_dir() with a retention count or size cap, keep stderr for interactive runs, and point run.sh at the new log.

v1.reason: run.sh:32 starts the engine with `nohup "$relay" --instance "$RELAY_INSTANCE" serve --remote >>"$log" 2>&1`, where log=$PWD/target/engine-$RELAY_INSTANCE.log (run.sh:29). That append-only file is never rotated. main.rs:209-211 sets up tracing_subscriber::fmt() at info level, writing to stderr, with no file writer. Instance::log_dir() (crates/relay-core/src/paths.rs:63) has no callers anywhere in crates/ or apps/, and the workspace has no tracing-appender dependency. SPEC.md lines 363-365 promise a 'rotating structured log (tracing crate) in ~/.local/share/relay/logs'. Because the file lives under target/, `cargo clean` deletes it.
v1.correction: The real path is data_dir()/logs (relay-v4/<instance>/logs), not ~/.local/share/relay/logs as SPEC says. That is a second small drift. The finding's growth-rate examples are illustrative and I did not measure them. At info level in normal use this is probably megabytes a month, not a disk-filling problem. The exception is the 50 ms 'accept failed' loop in direct.rs:49-51, which only runs under fd exhaustion. Low severity is right.

findings.title: Codex receives the whole session brief as a single argv string, so a standing note or task body that keeps growing eventually makes Codex sessions fail to spawn (E2BIG)
findings.evidence: codex_developer_instructions appends the full compact brief and returns `format!("developer_instructions={value}")` as one --config argument (providers.rs:81-93, used at 220 and 227). The compact brief contains the task body and changelog (awareness.rs:236-241), the full standing note (286-298) and every adjacent task in the module. None of these is capped. notes.append adds to the standing note with no size limit and is in every agent role's allowlist (notes.rs:412-487; settings.rs:36-38). Linux limits a single argv string to MAX_ARG_STRLEN, 128 KiB.
findings.impact: Once the JSON-escaped brief passes 128 KiB (for example a spec pasted into a task body, or months of standing-note appends), every Codex spawn or resume in that project fails with session.spawn_failed: 'Argument list too long'. Claude reads its prompt from a file and does not fail, but the prompt keeps growing in tokens.
findings.fix: Pass the brief to Codex through a file, as Claude already does with --append-system-prompt-file, or cap the injected sections: truncate the standing note and task body and point to the full brief file.

v1.reason: providers.rs:81-93 builds one `developer_instructions=<json>` argv string that contains the full compact brief, used for both Fresh and Resume (providers.rs:220, 227; session.rs:528-539). awareness.rs:236-241 adds every assigned task's body and changelog to state, and state_public, which goes into compact, is cloned after them (awareness.rs:249). It also includes the full standing note (awareness.rs:286-298, 389-391). notes.append (notes.rs:412-486) appends without a length cap for the standing target; only suggestions are capped at 500 characters. Task bodies are uncapped. Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN is 32 pages (128 KiB) per argv string, so exec fails with E2BIG once the JSON-escaped text exceeds that, for every Codex spawn or resume in the project.
v1.correction: The trigger needs more than about 128 KiB across the standing note, assigned task bodies and changelogs, and the adjacent task list. That is reachable but uncommon. The argv also exposes this text through world-readable /proc/<pid>/cmdline, a privacy concern that the comment at awareness.rs:246-248 already partly acknowledges. Fix: write the brief to a file and point Codex at it, or truncate the injected sections and reference RELAY_BRIEF.

results.coverage: Read in full: CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/engine/BUS.md, docs/engine/SPEC.md, docs/PARITY.md, docs/VERIFICATION.md, docs/MOBILE.md (PC-side claims), docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/SOURCES.md, DECISIONS.md D1-D38 and D104-D162, plugin README/plugin.json/docs for unreal-engine and blender, deploy/*, .github/workflows/*. Not finished or not possible: per-field verification of every BUS.md §10 payload/result shape (spot-checked only); SPEC.md treated as Relay-2/Tauri history except V4-relevant claims; DECISIONS D39-D103 only checked where cited; docs/upstream-v3, docs/perf, outputs/, PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, plugin SKILL.md bodies and argument-level claims in the Unreal/Blender mcp-tools.md not reviewed; native-client claims in ARCHITECTURE.md/PARITY.md only spot-checked (GTK client cannot be built here); Codex's real PreToolUse payload shape and hook-trust semantics could not be exercised offline, which is why the two Codex findings state that uncertainty; nothing was run (no cargo, no engine).

findings.title: Codex apply_patch/Edit/Write are gated as kind=exec, so no write guardrail ever runs for Codex while the UI labels it Guarded
findings.evidence: main.rs:506-512 builds `{session, kind: 'exec', command}` for `"Bash" | "apply_patch" | "Edit" | "Write"`. evaluate_exec (crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:811-848) checks only self_approval and denied_commands; protected paths, destructive-write holds, shape gates and write roots live in evaluate_write (guardrail.rs:503), reached only for kind=write. Yet D132 (docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:650-655) says 'Shell and patch invocations reach the same guardrail.gate bus path as Claude', BUS.md §9.2 (494-498) lists those policies for `gate {kind: write}`, and the Codex driver's `fn guarded(&self) -> bool { true }` (providers.rs:212) makes the launch sheet print 'Guarded' (apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:651-654) and Settings 'Guardrail adapter available' (tools_settings.rs:388-392).
findings.impact: A Codex builder whose apply_patch truncates a large data file, overwrites a protected path or corrupts a shape-gated JSON is never held or refused at write time: the SPEC §5 'data.ts truncation made impossible to do silently' case lands silently on disk. The pre-commit hook later checks only caps and protected paths (never destructive-write or shape gates), after the damage exists. Separately, until the user trusts the generated hook in Codex's /hooks (D132) no gate runs at all, but `guarded` is a constant true and the only 'surfacing' of the trust requirement is a description string in .codex/hooks.json (hooks.rs:500-502). Not verifiable offline: the exact tool_input Codex sends for Edit/Write; if it lacks a `command` string the adapter fails closed and blocks those tools outright. Either way no write policy is ever evaluated for Codex.
findings.fix: In codex_pre_tool, route apply_patch/Edit/Write to kind 'write': parse the patch's `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` sections (or Edit/Write path+content) into one gate call per file with new_text or diff, as claude_pre_tool does; keep kind 'exec' only for Bash. Make ProviderInfo.guarded report what actually binds (exec-only, hook trust unknown) and correct D132 and BUS.md §9.3.

v1.reason: codex_pre_tool (crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:499-531) builds `{session, kind:"exec", command}` for all of Bash, apply_patch, Edit and Write (line 508), using tool_input.command. evaluate_exec (crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:811-848) checks only self_approval and denied_commands. Protected paths, destructive-write holds, shape gates and write roots are applied only by evaluate_write (guardrail.rs:503), which this path never reaches. The hook config (hooks.rs:517, matcher 'Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write') sends every Codex file edit through this exec-only path. Meanwhile D132 (DECISIONS.md:650-655) says patch invocations reach 'the same guardrail.gate bus path as Claude', BUS.md §9.2 attaches the write policies to `gate {kind: write}`, and Codex's driver hard-codes `fn guarded(&self) -> bool { true }` (providers.rs:212). As a result, a Codex edit that truncates a large file or breaks a shape-gated file is never held. Protected paths and caps are checked only later, by the pre-commit gate, after the file is already on disk. No other code path applies write policy to Codex edits: rg finds apply_patch only at these two sites.
v1.correction: I could not verify offline what tool_input Codex sends for Edit/Write. If `command` is absent, required_string fails, codex_pre_tool returns Err and the CLI exits 5, not 2. Whether Codex then blocks or proceeds is unknown, so 'fails closed' is unestablished. Context: any agent, Claude included, can write files through its shell tool without a write gate, so write guardrails are best-effort for every provider. That is a separate root cause. This finding is that Codex's primary edit tool is unguarded while the docs and UI say it is guarded. Fix as proposed: parse the apply_patch `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` sections into one kind:write gate call per file. Also make the trust state and `guarded` reflect reality, and correct D132 and BUS.md §9.3.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says.
- crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:506 reads `tool_input.command`. Line 508 then builds `{session, kind:"exec", command}` for all of Bash, apply_patch, Edit and Write.
- guardrail.rs:466-472 sends exec to evaluate_exec (811-848). That function runs only self_approval and denied_commands.
- Protected paths, write roots, shape gates and destructive-write holds exist only in evaluate_write (503).
- evaluate_commit (757-809) checks only protected paths and caps.
- No other detection exists. No code emits `guardrail.violation`; the only hit is the op description at relay-bus/src/ops/file.rs:33. So the post-hoc watcher promised in BUS.md §9.3 and D5 was never built.

(b) Reachable on every Codex launch, with one caveat about hook trust.
- session.rs:485-486 calls install_codex on every Codex launch, with matcher `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write` (hooks.rs:517).
- Codex's published hook docs (developers.openai.com/codex/hooks, now learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) say "Bash and apply_patch use tool_input.command". They also say Edit and Write are matcher aliases only: "hook input still reports tool_name: 'apply_patch'". The installed Codex 0.154 binary agrees: the strings `apply_patch` and `command` sit together in its hook code.
- So the open question is settled. `command` is present, and every Codex edit reaches evaluate_exec with the whole patch as its "command".
- Codex's own prompt makes apply_patch its edit tool ("Use apply_patch for local file edits. Do not create or edit files with cat..."). This therefore covers essentially every Codex file edit.
- Caveat: per the same docs, untrusted project hooks do not run, and trust is keyed by the absolute hooks.json path. Relay writes a fresh `<worktree>/.codex/hooks.json` per session, so each session needs its own /hooks review. Until then, not even the exec gate runs. On this machine ~/.codex/config.toml holds 15 hook trust entries and none for a RelayV4 worktree.

(c) What happens to the user's data.
- No write policy ever binds a Codex edit at write time.
- With defaults (handlers/settings.rs:28-33), protected_paths and shape_gates are empty, so the check actually lost is the destructive-write hold. Under D114 (allow_if_recoverable) that hold fires only for untracked or uncommitted files, which are exactly the files whose bytes exist nowhere else.
- So a Codex patch that removes more than 50 lines, or more than 40% of a file of 30+ lines, from a file holding uncommitted work destroys that work silently. The identical Claude Edit would be held.
- Any protected paths, shape gates or write roots the user configures are also skipped at write time. The commit gate only refuses the later commit; the file on disk is already changed. Codex's own workspace-write sandbox is what remains for writes outside the worktree.
- Meanwhile the UI reports "Guarded" (apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:651-654) and "Guardrail adapter available" (tools_settings.rs:388-392). That reverses D107's deliberate "unguarded" label, and BUS.md §9.3 still says Codex has no hooks and guarded=false.
- Side effect of the same root cause: the whole patch text, context and removed lines included, is parsed as a shell line. A patched file containing an unquoted denied pattern (e.g. `git push --force` in a markdown line) is refused as guardrail.command. A word starting with `RELAY_SESSION=`, as at tests/guardrails.rs:766, is refused as self_approval, which no grant can lift; self_approval inspects quoted words too (guardrail.rs:857-878). I saw this parser refuse my own read-only rg live, through the Claude Bash hook, because its quoted regex began with that prefix.

(d) High is right: a safety check is silently skipped on every Codex edit while the UI says Guarded. It is not critical:
- it requires choosing Codex;
- the default config narrows the loss to unrecoverable files;
- the commit gate and Codex's sandbox still apply;
- no agent has to subvert anything adversarially;
- shell-tool writes skip write gates for every provider anyway.

(e) The fix direction is right but needs the corrections listed below.
v2.correction:
1. The first verifier is wrong about exit 5. main.rs:367-374 maps every codex_pre_tool error to Ok(2), so a missing `command` would block (fail closed). The point is moot: Codex always sends `tool_input.command` (the patch) for apply_patch.
2. Codex never sends tool_name Edit or Write; they are matcher-only aliases. The Edit/Write match arms are dead, and the fix should parse apply_patch only. Its "Edit/Write path+content" part has nothing to act on.
3. Impact wording: protected_paths and shape_gates are empty by default, and destructive-write holds fire only for untracked or modified files (D114). The default-config loss is therefore uncommitted work in a file a Codex patch truncates, and the silent "data.ts" case applies only to such files.
4. Fix details:
   - `*** Add File:` → new_text (strip the leading `+`).
   - `*** Delete File:` → new_text "", so the protected-path and destructive checks run.
   - `*** Update File:` → apply the hunks to the on-disk file to get new_text, as claude_pre_tool does for Edit. A diff alone works for destructive counts, but shape-gated paths are then always held (guardrail.rs:524-534).
   - Gate the destination of `*** Move to:` as well, and tolerate `*** Environment ID:` lines.
   - Block the whole tool call if any file is refused or held.
   - Stop running exec checks on patch text; this also removes the false self_approval and denied-command refusals.
5. `guarded` cannot simply be true, because hooks run only after a per-worktree /hooks trust. Label it accordingly, and correct D132 and BUS.md §9.3. §9.3 also documents a `guardrail.violation` notify watcher that was never implemented.

findings.title: Codex reviewers are told to reach the bus through the shell, but the exec gate refuses every shell call a reviewer makes, so a Codex reviewer can never bootstrap, mail or finish
findings.evidence: providers.rs:84-86 tells Codex 'Relay tools are not registered with this provider: reach the bus by running `$RELAY_BIN q <op> '<json>'` in a shell'; Codex gets only plugin MCP servers (handlers/session.rs:546-547), never the relay server. Every Codex session, whatever its role, gets the Bash PreToolUse hook (session.rs:485-486, hooks.rs:516-525) which calls guardrail.gate; the reviewer allowlist (handlers/settings.rs:37) has no guardrail.gate, so authorize() refuses with actor.allowlist (guardrail.rs:356-383) - tests/guardrails.rs:298-304 asserts exactly this for a Codex reviewer running `cargo test` - and the adapter exits 2 (relay-cli/src/main.rs:521-530). Group advancement waits until every non-closed reviewer has called session.done (handlers/session.rs:116-119).
findings.impact: The headline cross-vendor pair (SPEC.md:120-122 'Claude builds / Codex reviews') cannot work once the Codex hook is trusted: `$RELAY_BIN q session.bootstrap`, `mailbox.send` of fixes, `session.done` and even `guardrail.request` are shell calls and are all blocked, so `reviewers_left` never reaches 0 and the review group's next queued task is never assigned until the user closes the reviewer by hand. D154's 'role instructions are an executable authorization contract' test (DECISIONS.md:868) checks op names only, not the shell channel Codex depends on. If the hook is not trusted, the reviewer's shell is instead unguarded and can write files. The same refusal stops Claude reviewers running any check although their instruction says 'verify its correction' (providers.rs:73). Confidence is medium only because Codex's runtime hook behaviour could not be exercised here; the Relay-side refusal is certain and tested.
findings.fix: Register the relay MCP server for Codex the way plugin servers already are (`--config mcp_servers.relay.*`, providers.rs:103-126), or exempt validated `$RELAY_BIN q|cmd` argv (and read-only commands) from the reviewer's exec refusal; add an agent-surface test that a Codex reviewer can reach session.done through the channel its prompt names.

v1.reason: providers.rs:81-87 tells every Codex session that Relay tools are not registered and to run `$RELAY_BIN q <op> '<json>'` in a shell. session.rs:541-548 adds only codex_notify_config and plugin MCP servers, never a relay MCP server. Every Codex session gets install_codex (session.rs:485-486), which adds a PreToolUse hook matching `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write` (hooks.rs:516-525). codex_pre_tool (relay-cli main.rs:499-530) sends every Bash command, whatever it is, as guardrail.gate {kind: exec} and returns exit code 2 on any error. The default reviewer allowlist (settings.rs:37) has no guardrail.gate, and guardrail::authorize lets queries and guardrail.request through but refuses other mutations with actor.allowlist (guardrail.rs:350-383). tests/guardrails.rs:298-304 asserts exactly this refusal for a codex reviewer running `cargo test`. The hook adapter has no carve-out for `$RELAY_BIN q`, so once the hook is trusted (D132), a Codex reviewer's bootstrap, mailbox.send and session.done (all shell calls) are blocked. session.rs:116-119 then never sees reviewers_left reach 0, and the review group's next queued task is never assigned. SPEC.md:120-122 names 'Claude builds / Codex reviews' as the point of the pair preset.
v1.correction: The secondary claim about Claude reviewers is weaker. They keep the relay MCP tools (bootstrap, mailbox, session.done, git.diff, file.read), so only their shell is refused, and that looks like the intended 'do not modify files' policy rather than a bug. The core defect is the Codex reviewer, whose only bus channel is the shell. The one runtime assumption is that Codex PreToolUse treats exit 2 as a block, which is what D132 relies on for every Codex guardrail. Fix: register the relay MCP server for Codex through the existing codex_mcp_config path, or have the codex adapter/gate allow validated `$RELAY_BIN q|ops|schema` argv for roles without guardrail.gate. Add a test that a Codex reviewer can reach session.done through the channel its prompt names.
