So once trusted, Codex runs the hook for shell commands, including `relay q` calls, and exit 2 blocks them.

(b) Reachable by the user. The native Review-group launch lets the reviewer slot pick Codex (apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:783). SPEC §4 names "Claude builds / Codex reviews". The trigger also needs the user to approve Relay's hooks in Codex's startup hook review for that worktree, which D132 and the hooks.json description ("Review once with /hooks") ask for. Once both hold it fires every time. On this machine it is latent today. The RelayV4 store has 0 reviewer sessions (58 Claude and 16 Codex builders). No RelayV4 worktree has a Codex trust entry, because trust is keyed by absolute hooks.json path. That matches 0 Codex exec gates. Untrusted, a Codex reviewer works through the shell but is unguarded.

(c) Once fired, every reviewer command fails with "RELAY blocked Bash: ... (actor.allowlist)": cat, rg, git diff, and `relay q` session.bootstrap, mailbox.send, session.done and guardrail.request. The reviewer can neither read the code nor report. complete_group_assignment returns while reviewers_left != 0 (session.rs:116-119), and only session.done calls it (session.rs:1166). The next queued task is never assigned. Nothing is lost, and the failure is loud.

(d) High is right. This is a deterministic hard failure of a documented flow the UI offers, in its intended guarded setup. It is latent here only because a separate gap leaves Codex hooks untrusted, and fixing that gap would make it fire. It is not critical: it is not frequent or engine-wide and loses no data.

(e) The direction of the fix is right, but it is incomplete (see correction). The secondary Claude-reviewer claim is not a defect. Claude reviewers keep the relay MCP tools and Read/Grep/Glob. Note: the evidence came from read-only copies of both stores in this session's scratchpad (exp/db and exp/db2, under the 0700 /tmp/claude-1000). Relay's guardrail refused `rm -rf` on them, so they are still there for the user to delete.
v2.correction: 1) The title should be conditional: "When Relay's Codex hooks are trusted (the D132 state), the exec gate refuses every shell call a Codex reviewer makes...". Untrusted, which is the state of every RelayV4 worktree here, the reviewer reaches the bus through its shell but runs unguarded. 2) Confidence can rise from medium to high. Relay-2's audit has 1131 Codex exec gates, and Codex rollouts show `relay q` calls blocked by the Relay PreToolUse hook on exit 2. 3) Closing the reviewer by hand does not unstick the group. session.close (session.rs:1547-1633) never calls complete_group_assignment, and the builders were told not to repeat session.done. The next queued task waits until a builder repeats done or the user dispatches it. 4) Fix caveats. codex_mcp_config puts env values into argv (`--config mcp_servers.<n>.env={...}`). Putting RELAY_TOKEN there exposes it to `ps`, which session.rs:497-498 deliberately avoids. Forward RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_INSTANCE, RELAY_PROJECT and RELAY_WORKTREE through Codex's env forwarding (`env_vars`) instead. Also change the "Relay tools are not registered" text (providers.rs:84). The reviewer's shell would still be refused, so it would read code through file.read, file.search and git.diff. The adapter-side alternative is to skip the gate when the whole line is a single argv-parsed `$RELAY_BIN q|cmd|ops|schema` call with no chaining. That is safe because the bus authorizes each op, but it leaves file reads only through `relay q file.read`. D154's test (tests/agent_surface.rs:133-160) checks op names only, for Claude sessions. Add a test that takes a Codex reviewer through its shell channel to session.done.

findings.title: Handlers registered with Engine::register run slow external work under the store lock with no timeout: project.clone (git clone), git.pr.open (gh), avd.create/avd.boot, worktree.remove, workspace.discover
findings.evidence: workspace.rs:228-247 is `e.register::<ProjectClone>` (transaction and store mutex held) and runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()` with no deadline; git.rs:666-691 `e.register::<PrOpen>` runs `gh pr create` via `cmd.output()`; device.rs:321-342 avd.create spawns avdmanager and `wait_with_output()`, then list_avds; avd.boot (device.rs:346) also calls list_avds, which runs `emulator -list-avds` and `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` with plain `.output()` (device.rs:478, 505) - while the comment on list_avds_with (device.rs:475-476) claims these calls 'happen with nothing locked (D144)'; worktree.remove (git.rs:129-144) calls worktree::remove, which walks and deletes build dirs (dir_size, worktree.rs:360-361) and runs an unbounded `git worktree remove --force`; workspace.discover (workspace.rs:114-131) walks 4 levels of directories inside the lock. CLAUDE.md:48-55 and D144 (DECISIONS.md:729-738) promise every handler subprocess goes through proc::output_with_timeout and that slow work is registered unlocked/staged; BUS.md:246-250 even lists project.clone as a handle-returning async op. The native client gives project.clone an 1800 s deadline (apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:67).
findings.impact: Cloning a large repository from onboarding (LFS-heavy Unreal projects are the plugin's target) or a stalled network during `gh pr create` holds the one store connection for the whole run: every other request queues - every agent's guardrail.gate hook (Codex's hook times out at 30 s and fails closed), task moves, session.list after each session.changed - and the native client's 30 s requests report 'outcome unknown'. A hung clone/gh/adb (credential prompt on an inherited TTY, network stall, unresponsive emulator console) freezes the bus indefinitely. avd.boot is a routine Devices-page action.
findings.fix: Convert these handlers to register_staged (or register_unlocked for discover): do the clone/gh/avdmanager/emulator/adb calls and the tree walks in the prepare phase through proc::output_with_timeout with generous deadlines, keep only the row writes/emits in finish; fix the device.rs comment and BUS.md §5.1's async list.

v1.reason: Verified. workspace.rs:228 `e.register::<ProjectClone>` runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()` (line 234) with no deadline. Plain `register` handlers run in dispatch_inner after `self.store.lock()` + `conn.transaction()` (engine.rs:954-956); only ops in `self.unlocked` or `self.prepares` escape the lock. git.rs:666 `e.register::<PrOpen>` runs `gh pr create` via `cmd.output()` (line 680), while its neighbours BranchCleanup/Fetch/Push/PrList were deliberately moved to register_staged/unlocked with comments citing D144. device.rs:321 AvdCreate spawns avdmanager and `wait_with_output()`, then calls list_avds(ctx.tx()), which runs `emulator -list-avds` with plain `.output()` (device.rs:477) and `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` with plain `.output()` (device.rs:504); device.rs:346 AvdBoot calls list_avds under the lock too, and the comment at device.rs:475-476 saying these calls run 'with nothing locked (D144)' does not hold on these paths. git.rs:129 WorktreeRemove (register) calls worktree::remove, which walks/deletes build dirs (purge_build/dir_size) and runs `git worktree remove --force` without a timeout (worktree.rs:351-366). workspace.rs:114 WsDiscover is a plain register doing a directory walk. D144 (DECISIONS.md:729-738) and CLAUDE.md state the opposite rule. BUS.md:246-247 lists project.clone as a handle-returning async op, which it isn't. The native client gives project.clone an 1800 s deadline (client.rs:67), so the author knows it takes a long time.
v1.correction: One correction to the impact: user keystrokes are not blocked. session.input/resize take a lock-free fast path (engine.rs ~885-893) before any transaction. Agent requests are blocked, though: guardrail.gate, which every hooked agent tool call makes, task ops, session.list and so on. The real offenders are project.clone (minutes), git.pr.open (network), worktree.remove (walking and deleting multi-GB Unreal Intermediate/build dirs) and workspace.discover. `emulator -list-avds` in avd.boot is normally fast, and list_with_adb is already bounded by output_with_timeout (device.rs:582). Only the per-device `adb emu avd name` call has no bound. Fix as proposed: register_staged or register_unlocked with output_with_timeout, then fix the device.rs comment and BUS.md §5.1.

v2.reason:
(a) The code does what the finding says. Plain `register` handlers run after `self.store.lock()` and `conn.transaction()` (engine.rs:954-956); only ops in `unlocked` or `prepares` escape (engine.rs:906, 920). workspace.rs:228/234: ProjectClone runs `Command::new("git")...arg("clone")...output()` with no deadline and, unlike fetch_remote (git.rs:943), run_switch (git.rs:1349), branch_cleanup.rs:114 and worktree.rs:213, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. git.rs:666/680: PrOpen runs `gh pr create` via `cmd.output()`. It is `Actors::All` (registry.rs:121), so agents can call it as well as the user. device.rs:321/335: AvdCreate waits on avdmanager via `wait_with_output()`, then calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())`. device.rs:344/346: AvdBoot calls `list_avds(ctx.tx())`. Both therefore run `emulator -list-avds` (device.rs:478) and the per-device `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` (device.rs:505) with plain `.output()` under the lock. The comment at device.rs:475-476 ("nothing locked (D144)") is true only for the unlocked AvdList. git.rs:129 WorktreeRemove runs worktree::remove under the lock: purge_build/dir_size walks and deletes, and `git worktree remove --force` goes through worktree::git with a bare `.output()` (worktree.rs:26-27, 351-366). workspace.rs:114 WsDiscover is an OpMeta::query registered with plain `register` and walks four levels. D144/D149 (DECISIONS.md:729, 797) and CLAUDE.md state the opposite rule, and none of these ops is in D149's converted list or in any documented exception. The leftovers are inconsistent with their neighbours: session.close and discard_restorable already do worktree::remove in a staged prepare phase (session.rs:1503-1580), project.remove defers it to after_commit "instead of holding the bus through all of it" (workspace.rs ~323-345), and git.fetch/push/branch.cleanup are staged.

(b) Reachability. The sidebar "Open repository" (+) button opens the onboarding panel at any time (app.rs:523, 976, 1695 → onboarding.rs:527 `ui.call("project.clone")`), so a clone can run while agent sessions in other projects are working. The client's 1800 s deadline for project.clone (client.rs:67) shows clones of many minutes are expected. git.pr.open is a Code-page action (code_git.rs:662) that agents can also call. avd.boot is a routine Devices-page action (tools_devices.rs:110/117).

(c) What happens when it fires. For the whole clone, every request that needs the store queues on the one mutex: the user's, every agent's and the phone's. That includes guardrail.gate, a plain `register` (guardrail.rs:304) that runs on every hooked Bash/Edit/Write tool call, plus session.report, task ops and UI reads. The provider hooks are installed with a 30 s timeout (hooks.rs:351, 521) and then killed. The socket door also handles each connection sequentially (socket.rs:335-745 awaits each spawn_blocking before reading the next line). project.clone travels on the UI's main connection (app.rs:1111), so every other main-connection request queues behind it and fails at 30 s with "outcome unknown". An unbounded hang is also plausible but conditional. Relay's `gh auth login` runs with stdin null (github.rs:55-62), which probably does not configure a git credential helper. A private HTTPS clone_url with no helper, while `relay serve` runs from a terminal, would make git prompt on /dev/tty (or be SIGTTIN-stopped as a background job), and the mutex would never be released.

(d) Severity high fits "a freeze of the bus or the UI" in a normal flow. The rating rests on project.clone (minutes) and git.pr.open (network, agent-callable).

(e) The fix direction is right, but see the correction: as written it is incomplete for project.clone.
v2.correction:
Impact corrections:
- **Keystrokes are not blocked.** Each terminal pane has its own connection (terminal.rs:476). A small session.input from the user is answered from memory (socket.rs `answers_from_memory`, engine.rs:885-893), with no store lock in resolve_actor or fill_identity for the user actor.
- **Hook timeout semantics are outside the repo.** The finding's "Codex fails closed" is unverified. The adapter's own comment (relay-cli main.rs:352-353) says Claude Code treats only exit 2 as blocking, so a PreToolUse hook killed at its 30 s timeout may let the tool run unguarded. That is not established here.
- **Two of the six ops have no client caller.** worktree.remove and integration.discard are UserOnly and called by neither the native client, the phone door nor the CLI's MCP. They are reachable only through raw `relay cmd`.
- **The device ops hold the lock briefly.** avd.boot's locked work is normally sub-second: `emulator -list-avds`, `adb devices` (already bounded at 2 s via output_with_timeout, device.rs:582) and an unbounded per-emulator `adb emu avd name` (device.rs:505). avd.create holds the lock for avdmanager's JVM run, a few seconds.
- **workspace.discover is small.** It is a depth-4 walk that skips build directories.

Related locations to add: integration.rs:58 IntegrationDiscard (worktree::remove under the lock) and git.rs:693 CleanMerged (an unbounded `git branch -d` loop via worktree::git under the lock). The docs drift also covers the op summary at relay-bus/src/ops/workspace.rs:38, "(async; project.changed when done)": project.clone is synchronous and writes no project.clone.completed audit row.

Fix corrections:
1. **project.clone still blocks the UI connection.** `register_staged` alone frees the global lock but not the UI's main connection, which the socket door serves one request at a time. Either send project.clone on its own connection (add it to `is_lifecycle_request`, client.rs:50), or make it truly async: return at once, clone on a worker after commit, then call project.add via system_write, emit project.changed and append the .completed audit row. Either way, set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and stdin null on the clone, and run it through output_with_timeout. Its `process_group(0)` means a tty read would stop git, so the deadline is what saves it.
2. **git.pr.open.** Use register_staged with `resolve_root_unlocked` (git.rs:768), output_with_timeout (60-120 s) and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, since gh may run git. The finish step is just `changed()`. A guardrail-held agent call that is replayed through guardrail.confirm still runs its prepare under the lock (D149's accepted cost).
3. **worktree.remove and integration.discard.** Stage them as session.close does.
4. **workspace.discover.** Switch to `register_unlocked`; the closure ignores ctx.
5. **avd.create and avd.boot.** Read the tool paths with ctx.read, then run avdmanager and list_avds_with in prepare under deadlines. Then fix the comment at device.rs:475-476 and BUS.md §5.1's list of async ops.

findings.title: worktree::git_mutate, the shared git-mutation helper, has no timeout and is called inside locked handlers
findings.evidence: worktree.rs:26-36: `Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output()` with no deadline, and `pub fn git_mutate(...) { git(repo, args) }`. Called under the store lock by git.branch.create (`git switch -c`, git.rs:374), git.branch.delete (git.rs:485), git.stage (`git add`, git.rs:503), git.unstage (git.rs:527), git.commit's locked finish phase (`git commit --no-verify`, git.rs:571), git.branch.clean_merged (git.rs:712), file.restore_head (`git checkout --`, file.rs:256), integration.discard (integration.rs:64), session.update branch rename (session.rs:1460 -> worktree.rs:377-378) and worktree.remove (worktree.rs:362). branch_cleanup.rs:20-21 says its git calls are bounded by output_with_timeout, but it removes worktrees through worktree::remove (branch_cleanup.rs:307). hooks.rs:210-213 runs the user's pre-commit with raw `.output()`; that is unlocked normally, but guardrail.confirm replays a held git.commit's prepare inside its transaction (engine.rs invoke_registered, D149).
findings.impact: `git add` of large binaries runs the LFS clean filter, `git checkout -- path` the smudge filter (possibly a download), `git commit` the post-commit hooks, a confirmed held commit the user's whole pre-commit suite - all while every other request waits; a filter or hook that blocks (credential prompt, network) hangs the bus with no deadline, contrary to CLAUDE.md:53-55.
findings.fix: Route worktree::git/git_mutate through proc::output_with_timeout (as hooks::git already does with GIT_TIMEOUT) and return a typed timeout error; move stage/checkout/branch work into register_staged prepare phases where the op allows it; bound run_user_pre_commit too.

v1.reason: worktree.rs:26-36: `fn git` uses `Command::new("git")...output()` with no deadline, and `git_mutate` is a thin wrapper around it. Plain `register` handlers (store lock and transaction held) call it: BranchCreate (git.rs:345→374), BranchDelete (445→485), Stage (490→503), Unstage (507→527), CleanMerged (693→712), RestoreHead (file.rs:253→256) and IntegrationDiscard (integration.rs:58→62-64, which also calls worktree::remove). CommitOp's finish phase runs `git commit --no-verify` inside the transaction (git.rs:571), and --no-verify still runs post-commit hooks and LFS/filters. engine.rs:325-345 confirms that invoke_registered runs a staged op's prepare against the open transaction, so a guardrail.confirm replay of a held git.commit runs `git add -A` and run_user_pre_commit (hooks.rs:210-213, raw `.output()`) under the lock. A hook or filter that blocks, for example an LFS smudge waiting on the network or a credential prompt, freezes every agent request with no deadline.
v1.correction: This overlaps lens-docs#3 for worktree.remove. The distinct root cause is the shared helper having no timeout. Most of these git calls finish in milliseconds, so a hang needs a filter or hook that blocks, which is why medium fits. Unlocked callers (git.push prepare at git.rs:617, the device.rs:1575 fetch) are also unbounded, but they only hang their own request, not the bus. Fix: route `fn git` through proc::output_with_timeout with a GIT_TIMEOUT-style bound and a typed timeout error, and bound run_user_pre_commit too.

findings.title: Plugin MCP servers (ue_python, blender_python save/save_as, ue_property writes...) are handed to every role, giving a 'write nothing' reviewer an ungated write path
findings.evidence: session.rs:437-438: 'A plugin that is on brings its MCP servers to every agent of the project (D159)' - plugins::mcp_servers(conn, project_id, ...) with no role filter, added for Claude (session.rs:484 -> hooks.rs:417-441) and Codex (session.rs:546-547). Relay's PreToolUse matchers cover only `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash` (hooks.rs:350) and `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write` (hooks.rs:517), so MCP tool calls never reach guardrail.gate. BUS.md:465 says a reviewer gets 'nothing that writes files, commits, or moves the task'; SPEC.md:144-145 'Pair's reviewer can read everything and write nothing'.
findings.impact: In a project with the Unreal or Blender plugin on, a reviewer (and any builder) can save .blend files (blender_python save/save_as, blender_export), run arbitrary editor Python that saves assets (ue_python), import Data Tables and write properties - in the primary checkout the builder also uses (Unreal sets default_checkout primary) - with no protected-path, destructive-write, denied-command or role check; arbitrary Python also sidesteps the denied-command list for builders. Not established: whether the provider's own permission prompt intervenes (Claude asks for MCP tools unless pre-approved; Codex runs with --approve-for-me, D135, delegating approvals to its automatic reviewer).
findings.fix: Filter plugin MCP servers by role (no write-capable servers, or a manifest-declared read-only tool subset, for reviewers), or add the plugin tool names to the PreToolUse matchers and gate them like Bash; document the gap in BUS.md §9.3.

v1.reason: plan_launch (handlers/session.rs:437-438) passes plugins::mcp_servers to every session with no role filter. Claude gets them through add_claude_mcp_servers (hooks.rs:417) and Codex through codex_mcp_config (session.rs:546-547). The PreToolUse matchers are 'Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash' (hooks.rs:350) and 'Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write' (hooks.rs:517), so plugin MCP calls (blender_python, ue_python, ue_property...) never reach guardrail.gate. The relay-cli blender/unreal MCP servers do no role or guardrail checks.
v1.correction: The plugin MCP path is not the root cause. guardrail.gate (handlers/guardrail.rs:501-525) and guardrail::evaluate (guardrail.rs:466-473) never look at the session's role. The layer-3 role allowlist (role_allowlist, guardrail.rs:441) is applied only to bus ops in authorize. So a reviewer's native Edit/Write/MultiEdit or Bash (`sed -i`, `git commit`) is judged exactly like a builder's and passes whenever no protected-path, cap, shape or denied-command policy fires. The reviewer's 'write nothing' (BUS.md:465, SPEC.md:144-145) rests only on the prompt text in providers.rs:73. Plugin MCP tools are one more instance, and they additionally skip protected-path and destructive-write policies for builders. Claude is launched without a permission bypass, so its own permission prompt still applies unless the user pre-approved tools. Codex runs with --approve-for-me (providers.rs:218,225). Fix: in gate(), refuse kind=write/commit for sessions whose role allowlist admits no file or git write. Refuse Exec too, or restrict it to a read-only command set. Then filter plugin MCP servers or tools by role, or add them to the PreToolUse matchers.

findings.title: D106's 'an agent sees nothing outside its project' is not enforced: dashboard.get, audit.list/get, task.list and holds.list return every project's data to any agent
findings.evidence: D106 (DECISIONS.md:491-497) and BUS.md §9.1 layer 2 (453-456) state one boundary: an agent sees the metadata of any session in its own project and nothing outside it. authorize() (guardrail.rs:328-353) only checks payload `session`/`task_id` fields, then returns Ok for every query. dashboard.get (notify.rs:157-189) iterates `SELECT id FROM projects` and returns all projects' live peers (name, branch, claimed files, task title, intent), every in_review task with its body and every open hold with details; audit.list/audit.get (handlers/audit.rs:30-47) are unscoped and return stored payloads (up to 64 KiB) of any request; task.list without project_id (task.rs:831-839), guardrail.holds.list (handlers/guardrail.rs:306-331) and notify.list are likewise global. All roles get 'all queries'.
findings.impact: An agent in project A can read project B's session metadata, task bodies, guardrail holds and, via audit.get, the full payloads other actors sent (mailbox texts, file.write contents, task bodies) - the cross-project probing D106 was written to stop. The live store is opened EXCLUSIVE, so the bus is the normal read path to this data.
findings.fix: Scope agent queries centrally: force project_id to the agent's project for project-filterable queries (task.list, audit.list, holds.list, notify.list), restrict audit.get to the agent's project, and filter dashboard.get to the agent's project or make it user_only.

v1.reason: guardrail::authorize (guardrail.rs:322-353) checks only a payload `session` string and a `task_id`, then returns Ok for every Query. Nothing pins `project_id`, and fill_identity (engine.rs:1139) only fills it when it is missing. dashboard.get (notify.rs:157-189) loops over every project's peers via awareness::peers and returns their live session metadata, every in_review task and every open hold. That directly contradicts D106's rule that an agent sees session metadata in its own project 'and nothing outside it' (DECISIONS.md:491-497). audit.list/get (handlers/audit.rs:30-47), guardrail.holds.list (handlers/guardrail.rs:306) and task.list without project_id are unscoped too. The registry marks them Scope::Global (ops/audit.rs:13,16; ops/notify.rs:39).
v1.correction: The impact is overstated for this threat model. Every project belongs to the same single user. Agents already read any project's files with their provider-native Read/Bash tools, which no guardrail gates for reads. D106's stated purpose is consistent boundaries so agents do not learn to probe, not secrecy. The only data reachable solely through the bus is store-only content: task bodies, mailbox texts and request payloads in audit.get, and hold details. Hold rows do not carry the frozen envelope or token (hold_row, guardrail.rs:1305-1318). Rated low. The fix stands: scope agent queries to the caller's project centrally in authorize, or make dashboard.get and audit.get user_only.

findings.title: device.signing.create carries the keystore password on every door, contradicting D157/BUS.md §10.14 'TauriOnly, the socket/CLI door never receives the secret'
findings.evidence: ops/device.rs:37-39 registers SigningCreate with `.audit(Audit::Never).actors(Actors::UserOnly)` and no `.doors(...)`; schema/bus.v1.json shows doors=all. Commit e4a60fc removed `.doors(Doors::TauriOnly)` when the GTK client replaced Tauri, and the native client now sends it over the socket (apps/relay-native/src/tools_devices.rs:529). D157 (DECISIONS.md:894-897) still says it is TauriOnly and 'agents, the socket/CLI door, run rows, logs, and SQLite never receive the secret'; BUS.md:867 says 'unavailable over the socket so its secret never reaches audit, CLI arguments, or agents'. The phone door forwards any actor:user line to the socket (relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:202-206), including over plain ws:// on the LAN.
findings.impact: The documented secret-handling guarantee no longer holds: `relay cmd device.signing.create '{..."password":...}'` is accepted and puts the upload-key password in argv (readable by other local users through /proc/<pid>/cmdline), and a paired phone or any remote-door client can send it over an unencrypted LAN WebSocket or through the rendezvous operator. Audit stays off, so the store itself is still clean.
findings.fix: Refuse device.signing.create in the remote door's gate and require the CLI to read the password from stdin (`-`), or introduce a local-native-only door flag; at minimum rewrite D157/BUS.md §10.14 to the real guarantee.

v1.reason: Commit e4a60fc removed `.doors(Doors::TauriOnly)` from SigningCreate at crates/relay-bus/src/ops/device.rs:37-39; the op is now audit Never, UserOnly, doors All. D157 (DECISIONS.md:894-897) and BUS.md:867 still say it is TauriOnly, that the socket/CLI door never receives the secret, and that the op is 'unavailable over the socket'. Those statements are now false. The real exposure is smaller than the finding says. The native client sends the password over the user's own local socket to the user's own engine. A password lands in argv only if the user types it into `relay cmd` themselves. The remote door forwards any actor:user op (bridge.rs gate), but that peer is the user's own paired phone. Plain-ws LAN exposure applies to every user op the door carries, session.input keystrokes included, so it is a property of the door and not specific to this op. Audit stays Never, so the secret never reaches the store.
v1.correction: Recategorise as docs-drift, severity low. The documented guarantee is stale, and no new attacker gains a path through this op. Fix: rewrite D157 and BUS.md §10.14 to the real guarantee (never audited or logged, user-only, and the socket door accepts it). Optionally have the remote door refuse device.signing.create and the CLI read the password only from stdin. Doors::TauriOnly cannot simply be restored, because the GTK client talks over the socket.

findings.title: `relay remote revoke` does not cut off a phone that is connected: admitted bridges never re-check remote.json
findings.evidence: admit() reads the registry once per connection (bridge.rs:93-121); after the welcome, the loop at bridge.rs:197-213 forwards every inbound line until the phone disconnects, with no re-validation; tunnel lanes are the same (tunnel.rs:139-145). Revoke only rewrites the file (registry.rs:239-243; relay-cli/src/remote.rs:252-259). docs/MOBILE.md:193-194 presents revoke as the way 'To cut a phone off from the PC side'.
findings.impact: A lost or stolen phone with the app open (MOBILE.md:133-134 even offers 'keep the screen on in a terminal') keeps full user rights - typing into agent terminals, confirming guardrail holds, dispatching tasks - after revocation, for as long as its WebSocket or rendezvous lane stays up; the only way to drop it is restarting the engine/door, which the docs never mention.
findings.fix: Re-check the device on each inbound line (cheap: compare remote.json mtime/device presence) or add an in-process revocation signal that closes the device's bridges; document the restart until then.

v1.reason: bridge.rs:111-195: run() loads the registry and admits the device once. After the welcome, the loop at lines 175-191 forwards every inbound line to the engine socket until the phone disconnects, and never checks the registry again. tunnel.rs:131 runs the same bridge::run per lane, with no revocation path. registry.rs:239-243 revoke() only drops the device from the in-memory list, and the CLI (relay-cli/src/remote.rs:252-259) saves the file and prints 'revoked {id}; its next connection will be refused'. Nothing signals or closes live bridges, and I found no other revoke mechanism in relay-remote or relay-core. docs/MOBILE.md:193-194 presents revoke as the way 'To cut a phone off from the PC side'. A connected phone therefore keeps full user rights after revocation, for as long as its WebSocket or rendezvous lane stays up.
v1.correction: The CLI message is accurate ('next connection'), so the gap is between the docs' promise and the live-connection behaviour, not a lying CLI. Exposure is limited by how long a phone's socket stays up, since mobile OSes often drop backgrounded sockets, so medium is right. Fix: re-check device presence in remote.json cheaply (mtime) on each inbound line, or add an in-process revocation signal that ends that device's bridges. Until then, document that the door or engine must be restarted.

findings.title: Soft-deleted rows and .relay/trash payloads are never purged: the reconcile pass and undo.grace_days that BUS.md §5.4 promises do not exist
findings.evidence: BUS.md:288-292: restorable 'for the grace window (settings: undo.grace_days, default 7), then hard-deleted by the reconcile pass'; SPEC.md:169 and 357 repeat it. `undo.grace_days` exists only as a default (handlers/settings.rs:42) and is read nowhere; app.reconcile returns an empty action list (handlers/app.rs:137-141) and there is no 60 s pass; recovery.rs prunes audit rows only. file.delete moves the target, file or whole directory, to `<worktree>/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` (file.rs:221-236) and nothing deletes it; project.remove deletes the file_trash rows (workspace.rs:369) but leaves the payloads on disk.
findings.impact: Deleting a large folder (build output, assets) from the Project Files tree frees no disk space, ever, in the primary checkout; after project.remove those payloads become unreachable orphans. Users and agents reading the docs and the Settings tree believe deletes expire after 7 days.
findings.fix: Purge soft-deleted rows and trash payloads older than undo.grace_days during launch recovery and delete payloads on project.remove; or document that deletes are kept indefinitely and drop the dead setting.

v1.reason: file.delete (handlers/file.rs:221-236) renames the target, a file or a whole directory, into `<root>/.relay/trash/<id>/payload` and records a file_trash row. Nothing ever deletes these payloads. The only references to file_trash are file.rs and `DELETE FROM file_trash WHERE project_id=?1` in project.remove (workspace.rs:369), which drops the rows but leaves the payloads on disk. app.reconcile (app.rs:137-141) returns an empty action list. `undo.grace_days` has no readers outside settings defaults and tests (tests/bus.rs:729). Soft-deleted tasks, notes and modules are likewise never hard-deleted. BUS.md §5.4 (lines 288-292) promises a hard delete after the grace window.
v1.correction: The leak is mainly in the primary checkout and long-lived worktrees. A pooled worktree's .relay/trash goes away when that worktree is removed. The leaked payloads are files the user explicitly deleted through Relay's file tree or an agent's file.delete. Disk is never reclaimed, and after project.remove they cannot be restored through Relay. The fix is a purge of file_trash rows and payloads older than undo.grace_days, plus a hard delete of other soft-deleted rows. Run it off the store mutex: collect paths under a short lock, then remove_dir_all unlocked, per CLAUDE.md. project.remove should also delete payloads. Alternatively, rewrite §5.4 and drop the dead setting.

findings.title: BUS.md §9.3/§14 promise a post-hoc `guardrail.violation` watcher with one-click restore for Codex writes; no such detection exists
findings.evidence: BUS.md:524-533: 'writes are detected post-hoc by the notify watcher - a destructive write that already landed raises a guardrail.violation notification with a one-click git checkout -- <path> restore (file.restore_head)'; BUS.md:852 and crates/relay-bus/src/ops/file.rs:33 describe file.restore_head as 'the one-click answer to a post-hoc violation'; BUS.md:1130-1131 and D5 (DECISIONS.md:19-21) repeat 'Codex writes are post-hoc'; BUS.md:524-526 and 1056-1057 also say ProviderInfo.guarded is false for Codex. `guardrail.violation` occurs nowhere in the code; the watcher (watch.rs:115-129) only debounces and emits file.changed; providers.rs:212 returns guarded=true for Codex.
findings.impact: A reader trusting the API document believes destructive Codex writes are at least flagged after the fact with a restore button; combined with the exec-only Codex gating, a Codex truncation produces no hold, no refusal and no notification. Developers may also skip real enforcement believing the net exists.
findings.fix: Rewrite §9.3, §14 and the §11.4 guarded comment to D132's hook model and the actual exec-only coverage, or implement the watcher-based violation notification the doc describes.

v1.reason: The code contradicts the doc in three places. (1) BUS.md:524-533 says Codex `ProviderInfo.guarded` is false and that destructive writes raise a post-hoc `guardrail.violation` notification from the notify watcher. `guardrail.violation` appears nowhere in crates/ or apps/relay-native, so no such watcher exists. (2) providers.rs:212 `fn guarded(&self) -> bool { true }` for Codex. (3) D132 (DECISIONS.md:650-655) replaced the hookless model with `.codex/hooks.json` PreToolUse hooks (hooks.rs:494-540, matcher `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write`). D5 (DECISIONS.md:19-21), BUS.md:1056-1057, BUS.md:1130-1131 and the file.restore_head descriptions (BUS.md:852, relay-bus/src/ops/file.rs:33) still describe the old post-hoc model. The API document describes a safety net that was never built.
v1.correction: The finding's 'exec-only Codex gating' needs a correction. Codex write tools are hooked (hooks.rs:517). However, codex_pre_tool (relay-cli/src/main.rs:507-512) maps Bash, apply_patch, Edit and Write all to `kind: "exec"`, passing the patch or command text as `command`. guardrail.rs:469-471 then sends them to evaluate_exec, not evaluate_write. As a result, write-path rules (protected paths, destructive-write shape gates) never apply to Codex edits, and the git pre-commit gate is the only write-set enforcement. That is the concrete reason the stale doc matters, and it may deserve its own security or invariant finding. Doc fix: rewrite §9.3, §11.4 and §14, and D5's Codex clause, to match D132. State that Codex edits are gated as exec commands, not as writes, and either remove the 'post-hoc guardrail.violation' wording from the file.restore_head descriptions or build the watcher.

findings.title: BUS.md §6-§7 and §14 still describe the Tauri app: wrong socket path, UI-executor and door semantics, and 'no RPC over the network'
findings.evidence: BUS.md:323-325 gives the socket as `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay/<instance>.sock` with bundle ids com.quietsoftware.relay; the code uses `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay-v4/` (paths.rs:66-81, whose own doc cites §6.2), and README.md:26-29 notes the old location belongs to the separate Relay-2/V3 engine. §6.1 (311-319) documents a Tauri invoke door; §6.5 (361-372) says ui.* are forwarded to the UI and return unavailable/ui.absent when headless, but handlers/ui.rs:41-66 and 320-363 answer them in core from an in-memory UiRuntime and succeed with no UI; §7 (381) says mirror is 'Tauri Channel only; socket door returns unavailable' while socket.rs streams it; §7 (383) promises a `log` stream from app.log.tail, whose handler only emits `app.log.attached` (handlers/app.rs:133-136); §14 (1121) 'No RPC over the network. Unix socket only' and §4.2 (207-208) 'user needs no token (same uid, same trust)' predate the phone door that forwards user-actor lines from LAN/rendezvous (ARCHITECTURE.md:57-64). SOURCES.md:48 calls docs/engine a preserved Relay-2 reference, yet CLAUDE.md and code comments cite it as current.
findings.impact: A client or script written from §6.2 connects to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay/dev.sock` - the Relay-2/V3 engine's socket if one is running - and silently operates on the wrong store; agents calling ui.toast/ui.page.switch headless get success instead of ui.absent; anyone adding a user-only op reasons from a 'local, same uid' threat model the phone door has invalidated.
findings.fix: Update §6/§7/§14 to the V4 doors (relay-v4 socket path, native client over the socket, core-held UI state, the remote door as a networked user door), or mark them historical and point to ARCHITECTURE.md/MOBILE.md.

v1.reason: BUS.md:323-325 gives `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay/<instance>.sock` and com.quietsoftware bundle ids. The code uses `relay-v4/` (paths.rs:66-81, whose doc cites §6.2), and README.md:26-29 says the old path belongs to Relay-2/V3. §6.1 describes a Tauri invoke door that does not exist in V4. §6.5 says ui.* is forwarded to the UI and returns unavailable/ui.absent when headless, but handlers/ui.rs:41-66 mutates an in-memory `engine.ui` and returns Ok, and `ui.absent` appears nowhere in crates/relay-core. §7's mirror row says 'socket door returns unavailable', yet socket.rs:224-241 manages native mirrors per connection. §7's `log` stream is not produced: LogTail only emits `app.log.attached` (handlers/app.rs:133-136). §14 ('No RPC over the network. Unix socket only') and §4.2 ('user needs no token (same uid, same trust)') predate the remote door, which forwards LAN or rendezvous lines as actor user. SOURCES.md (line ~19, not 48, since the file has 23 lines) calls docs/engine 'Relay-2's bus/spec/decision reference', while BUS.md:7-8 claims it wins disagreements and code comments and CLAUDE.md cite it as current. The risk to everyday function is small for a single author, but the stale threat model ('same uid, same trust', 'no network RPC') is what agents and future changes will reason from when deciding which ops a phone may call.
v1.correction: The SOURCES.md reference is line 19 ('`docs/engine/` preserves Relay-2's bus/spec/decision reference'), not 48. The wrong-store scenario needs a Relay-2/V3 engine to be running, so it is less likely than the stale-threat-model cost. Fix: update §4.2/§6/§7/§14 for the V4 doors and the networked user door (BUS.md:207-208 especially), or mark those sections historical and point to ARCHITECTURE.md and MOBILE.md.

findings.title: A default-on branch sweeper wakes every second and deletes branches (local and on GitHub) every 20 minutes, contradicting the docs' 'no timers' and 'no silent deletion' guarantees
findings.evidence: serve.rs:34-35 starts branch_cleanup::spawn_sweeper on every engine start; branch_cleanup.rs:429-456 loops forever sleeping 1 s at a time (437) and every SWEEP_EVERY = 20 min (42) runs git/gh, deleting merged session branches, clean unowned pooled worktrees (307) and the remote branch via `git push <remote> --delete` (329). README.md:82-86 'The application has no engine refresh timers by default'; VERIFICATION.md:202-205 'the only recurring timers in the application are the opt-in wallpaper rotation and one-shot debounces'; SPEC.md:33-35 'NO polling timers anywhere'; SPEC.md:375 idle '0 subprocess spawns/min'; D140 (DECISIONS.md:706-708) cites a 'no-idle-process rule'; ARCHITECTURE.md:40-41 'No cleanup path silently deletes a worktree, branch or repository'.
findings.impact: Users and agents tuning idle cost, or reasoning about what Relay may delete, are misled: a merged session branch kept for reference disappears locally and on GitHub with only a system audit row, and the engine is never idle (a thread wake per second plus periodic git/gh processes).
findings.fix: Make the sweep trigger-driven (session close, git.pr.list, explicit git.branch.cleanup) or opt-in, replace the 1 s sleep loop with a condvar/park_timeout signalled on quit, and document the behaviour in README, VERIFICATION and ARCHITECTURE.

v1.reason: serve.rs:35 calls branch_cleanup::spawn_sweeper on every engine start. branch_cleanup.rs:429-456 loops forever: it sleeps 1 s at a time, runs the first sweep after 90 s (SWEEP_FIRST, line 41) and then one every 20 minutes (SWEEP_EVERY, line 42). Each sweep runs git, and gh where available, on every closed session's branch. When a merged PR proves it, it deletes the local branch (update-ref -d, line 312) and the remote branch (`git push <remote> --delete`, line 326). That contradicts README.md:82 ('no engine refresh timers by default') and VERIFICATION.md:202-205 ('the only recurring timers ... are the opt-in wallpaper rotation and one-shot debounces'). Neither `git.branch.cleanup` nor the sweep appears in BUS.md, while git.branch.delete and clean_merged do (BUS.md:823, 830).
v1.correction: Several parts of the claim are overstated. (1) The deletion is not silent. Each one writes a system audit row, emits git.changed and is logged (record(), branch_cleanup.rs:375-403). (2) It is conservative. It uses compare-and-delete on the judged tip, keeps any branch checked out in the primary checkout or outside the pool, and deletes the remote only while it still points at the merged PR head. (3) It matches SPEC §8's 'branch kept until merged' and the module's own doc comment. So the ARCHITECTURE.md:41 'silently deletes' contradiction is weak. The real drift is the undocumented recurring timer and remote deletion. One ongoing cost is small but real: candidates() (line 74) returns every closed session's branch forever, so each sweep runs at least one `git rev-parse` per branch that ever existed, including ones already 'gone'. The fix is to document the sweep and git.branch.cleanup in BUS.md, README and VERIFICATION. Optionally, wait with park_timeout/condvar instead of a 1 s loop. Making the sweep trigger-only would drop squash-merged PRs merged after close that git.pr.list never sees.

findings.title: deploy/relay-remote.service starts a stable engine while ./run.sh and the desktop app use dev, so its 'the desktop app reuses a running engine' claim is false
findings.evidence: relay-remote.service:4 'The desktop app reuses a running engine, so it keeps working as before'; :9 `ExecStart=%h/.cargo/bin/relay serve --remote` with no RELAY_INSTANCE, so the CLI default stable applies (relay-cli/src/main.rs:24). run.sh:5 defaults to dev and only reuses an engine that answers `--instance dev ping` (run.sh:26-28); relay-native defaults to dev (apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:304). The dev engine's `serve --remote` then cannot bind 0.0.0.0:7420 held by the stable door and runs without it (relay-cli/src/remote.rs:105-113); `relay remote pair` resolves to the requested stable engine when it is alive (remote.rs:155-158). Nothing in README installs relay into ~/.cargo/bin.
findings.impact: Following the unit yields two engines with two stores: the phone pairs with and controls the stable store while the desktop shows the dev store, and agents started from either side are invisible to the other.
findings.fix: Add `Environment=RELAY_INSTANCE=dev` (or document --instance), add the install step, and fix the comment and MOBILE.md:46.

v1.reason: deploy/relay-remote.service:9 runs `%h/.cargo/bin/relay serve --remote` with no RELAY_INSTANCE, and the CLI default is `stable` (relay-cli/src/main.rs:24). run.sh:5 defaults to dev and starts its own dev engine unless `--instance dev ping` answers (run.sh:26-31). install-native-desktop.py:9/22 makes the desktop entry launch dev. relay-native app.rs:304 defaults to dev. The dev engine started by run.sh tries the default 0.0.0.0:7420, which the stable door already holds, so it logs 'phone door not opened' and runs without it (remote.rs:105-113). `relay remote pair` resolves to stable when stable is alive (remote.rs:155-158). The result is two engines and two stores, and the phone talks to a different store from the desktop. The comment on line 4, 'The desktop app reuses a running engine', is false. Nothing in the repo installs relay into ~/.cargo/bin.
v1.correction: This is a misconfigured deploy unit as much as doc drift, so the category is bug. Fix: add `Environment=RELAY_INSTANCE=dev` (or `--instance dev`), document how to install the binary (or point ExecStart at the checkout's target), and correct the comment and MOBILE.md §2.

findings.title: BUS.md §5.1 says queries read concurrently through WAL under a tokio Mutex and that async ops write `<op>.completed` rows; neither is true
findings.evidence: BUS.md:225-227 'a single tokio::sync::Mutex around the engine's write side; queries may read concurrently through the WAL' - the store is one rusqlite Connection in a std::sync::Mutex (store.rs:376-378, 473-476) and every handler registered with Engine::register, query or not, runs inside that lock (engine.rs:7-8); CLAUDE.md:56 says 'Reads serialize with writes', while BUS.md:7-8 says BUS.md wins disagreements. BUS.md:246-250 says integration.request, project.clone, device.run, device.build and session.spawn write a `<op>.completed` system row; the real ops are integration.advance (integration.rs:283), device.build.finish / device.run.advance / device.run.crash (device.rs:2170-2211) and session.spawn.completed, and project.clone is synchronous.
findings.impact: A developer trusting the self-declared authoritative API doc registers a slow query with Engine::register expecting it not to block writes, and freezes the bus; `audit.list {op_prefix: 'device.run.completed'}` finds nothing.
findings.fix: Rewrite §5.1's first bullet to the one-connection/one-mutex model with the three handler shapes, and list the real completion op names.

v1.reason: BUS.md:225-227 describes a tokio::sync::Mutex on the write side with concurrent WAL reads. The store is `conn: Mutex<Connection>` (std, store.rs:376-378), locked for each request (store.rs:473-476), so reads serialize with writes, as CLAUDE.md says. BUS.md:246-250 lists `<op>.completed` system rows for integration.request, project.clone, device.run, device.build and session.spawn. The real system_write ops are integration.advance (integration.rs:283), device.build.finish / device.run.advance / device.run.crash (device.rs ~2170-2211) and session.spawn.completed (session.rs:649). project.clone is synchronous (workspace.rs:228-245). The bus-freeze impact is overstated: the same §5.1 (BUS.md:234-241) already describes the unlocked and staged handler shapes, and CLAUDE.md states the real model, so a developer is unlikely to be misled into a freeze by this bullet alone.
v1.correction: While checking: project.clone (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:234) runs `git clone` via `Command::output()` inside a handler registered with `Engine::register`. That is a network subprocess run with the store mutex held and without proc::output_with_timeout. It is a real CLAUDE.md invariant violation that can freeze the bus for the whole clone, and it deserves its own finding if no other auditor reported it.

findings.title: MOBILE.md's rendezvous and restart steps fail against the documented ./run.sh engine
findings.evidence: MOBILE.md:104-109 says run `relay remote via wss://...` then `relay remote serve --pair`; with the run.sh engine (`serve --remote`, MOBILE.md:21-22) already bound to 0.0.0.0:7420, `remote serve`'s DirectServer::bind fails (relay-cli/src/remote.rs:191) and exits; the in-process tunnel is spawned only at engine start (remote.rs:119-122) and run.sh reuses a running engine (run.sh:26-28), so `via` takes effect only after an engine restart, which §4 never says (`via` itself prints 'restart `relay remote serve`', remote.rs:289). MOBILE.md:31's restart command `relay --instance dev cmd app.quit '{}'` is refused with conflict app.sessions_live whenever an agent is live (handlers/app.rs:39-41).
findings.impact: A user following §4 gets 'address already in use' and a rendezvous that is never dialed; the §1 restart fails exactly when agents are running.
findings.fix: Document: after `relay remote via`, restart the engine (`app.quit {"force":true}` then ./run.sh) instead of `remote serve`, noting that live sessions become restorable.

v1.reason: MOBILE.md:21-22 says the run.sh engine already carries the door (`serve --remote`, which binds 0.0.0.0:7420 by default, main.rs:68 and registry.rs:60). §4 (MOBILE.md:106-109) then says to run `relay remote via ...` followed by `relay remote serve --pair`. `remote serve` resolves to the running dev engine and calls `DirectServer::bind(ctx, 0.0.0.0:7420)` (remote.rs:191, a plain TcpListener::bind at direct.rs:32), which fails with address in use. The engine's own tunnel is spawned only at startup from the registry (remote.rs:119-122), so a rendezvous set later is not dialed until the engine restarts, and `via` prints 'restart `relay remote serve`' (remote.rs:289). The restart at MOBILE.md:31, `cmd app.quit '{}'`, is refused with conflict app.sessions_live whenever a PTY is live (handlers/app.rs:39-41). The error message does name `force`, which softens this.
v1.correction: Document the restart path: `app.quit {"force":true}` (live sessions become restorable), then ./run.sh. Alternatively, make `relay remote via` tell the person to restart the engine when the engine itself carries the door.

findings.title: The remote door's actor gate checks a whole WebSocket frame, so a frame with an embedded newline delivers un-gated envelopes to the engine
findings.evidence: wire.rs:95-98 forwards any frame that does not parse as a single JSON value ('Anything that is not a request object is forwarded untouched'); bridge.rs:202-206 writes the frame plus a newline to the Unix socket, which the engine reads line by line (direct.rs:107-116 passes text and binary frames through as-is). A frame `{..."actor":"user"...}\n{..."actor":"agent:x","token":"..."...}` fails serde_json::from_str (trailing characters), is forwarded, and becomes two engine requests, the second never gated. MOBILE.md:180-182 and wire.rs:1-2 and 91-93 claim every line a phone sends goes through this check before the engine sees it.
findings.impact: Today the engine's own checks (token for agent:*, system refused, test refused on stable) still hold, so the practical effect is unthrottled agent-token guessing by a paired client; but any phone-specific restriction added to gate() later (its natural home, e.g. refusing device.signing.create) is bypassable.
findings.fix: Reject frames containing CR/LF (or split them and gate each line), and refuse rather than forward lines that do not parse.

v1.reason: wire.rs:94-97: `gate` returns Gate::Forward when `serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line)` fails, and a frame holding two JSON objects separated by '\n' fails with trailing characters. bridge.rs:171-180 skips only blank frames, calls gate on the whole frame, and on Forward writes `line` plus b"\n" to the engine socket. direct.rs:107-117 passes Text and Binary frames through unsplit. The engine's socket reader is line-based (`BufReader::lines`, socket.rs:323/335), so the second line reaches the engine without passing the gate. The engine still enforces the actor rules on its own (engine.rs:1349 refuses System, 1352 refuses Test on stable, and agent:* needs the session token), and a paired phone already has full `user` rights. What is lost today is defense in depth plus the doc promise (wire.rs:1-2, MOBILE.md:180-182). Guessing tokens is not a realistic gain, so the claim that this enables 'unthrottled agent-token guessing' has no practical weight. The real exposure is that any phone-only restriction added to gate() later can be bypassed.
v1.correction: Practical impact today is nil beyond breaking the documented invariant. The real risk is a future phone-specific rule in gate() being bypassed. Fix: split the frame on '\n' and gate each line, or refuse frames that contain CR/LF. Also refuse lines that do not parse instead of forwarding them, or forward only after confirming the frame is a single line.

findings.title: BUS.md §7 promises PTY frames are 'coalesce, never drop', but the socket door drops frames on lag and `relay attach` ignores sequence gaps
findings.evidence: BUS.md:380 'Backpressure: coalesce, never drop'. socket.rs:489-493 handles broadcast RecvError::Lagged by logging 'frames dropped - client should re-attach from its last seq' and continuing, with no gap marker sent; the PTY broadcast holds 1024 frames (pty.rs:189). `relay attach` (relay-cli/src/main.rs:243-268) decodes and prints every frame without checking seq or epoch.
findings.impact: A client written to the documented contract (the CLI's attach, scripts, a phone on a slow rendezvous behind a 256-line outbound queue) shows terminal output with silently missing chunks during output bursts.
findings.fix: Correct §7 (gaps are possible; detect seq jumps and re-attach with from_seq) and make `relay attach` re-attach on a gap, or emit an explicit gap frame on Lagged.

v1.reason: BUS.md:380 (§7 pty row) says 'Backpressure: coalesce, never drop'. Each PTY has one broadcast channel of 1024 frames (pty.rs:189 `broadcast::channel(1024)`). The socket door's per-attach task (socket.rs:476-497) awaits `tx.send(line)` on the outbound queue. A slow client therefore stalls that task, and the broadcast receiver falls behind. On `RecvError::Lagged(n)` (socket.rs:491-493) the door only logs 'frames dropped — client should re-attach from its last seq' and keeps looping. The client gets no gap frame or error. `relay attach` (relay-cli/src/main.rs:243-266) writes every decoded frame to stdout without checking seq or epoch, so it cannot notice a gap. The contract in the doc is false, and the reference client shows output with chunks missing and no sign that anything was lost.
v1.correction: The trigger is a socket client that reads more slowly than the PTY produces, until it falls more than 1024 frames behind. The door does not drop frames itself. It applies backpressure to the outbound queue, and the drop happens when the broadcast receiver lags. The real fix should be in the code: send an explicit gap or resync line on Lagged (or re-run pty.attach from the last seq that was sent), and update §7 to match. Fixing the doc alone would leave `relay attach` silently losing output.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md says relay-remote's integration tests exercise every bus payload the phone sends; they cover about ten ops
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:30-31. crates/relay-remote/tests/remote.rs exercises bus.ping, bus.subscribe, workspace.create, project.add, session.list, session.attach, task.create, task.dispatch, session.create and mailbox.send (116-147, 277-330). MOBILE.md:146-167 lists further phone ops never sent in those tests: session.spawn, session.scrollback, session.input, session.park/wake/resume, guardrail.confirm/reject, task.list, task.approve, git.status, git.diff, git.diff.file and notification acknowledgement.
findings.impact: An engine-side payload change to, say, guardrail.confirm or session.input passes CI while breaking the phone - the regression agents were told these tests catch.
findings.fix: Extend the remote tests with the remaining phone payloads, or narrow the CLAUDE.md sentence to what is covered.

v1.reason: CLAUDE.md:30-31 says relay-remote's integration tests 'exercise every bus payload the phone sends'. The only test file, crates/relay-remote/tests/remote.rs, sends just bus.ping, bus.subscribe, workspace.create, session.attach, session.list, task.create, task.dispatch, session.create (plus project.add/mailbox.send in setup) via call() at lines 117-330. The phone ops MOBILE.md lists (session.input, guardrail.confirm/reject, git.diff, etc.) never appear. The bridge forwards payloads unchanged, so CI checks the door's framing and gating. It does not check that each phone payload still matches the engine's schema.
v1.correction: This is mostly docs drift: the CLAUDE.md sentence overstates the coverage. The cheapest fix is to narrow the sentence. Adding the missing ops to the tests (S effort) is the more useful fix. Low severity: CI coverage is overstated, but nothing breaks at runtime.

findings.title: README's native verification step `cargo fmt -p relay-native --check` no longer passes (about 500 hunks in 37 files)
findings.evidence: README.md:61-66 lists it among the checks; .github/workflows/ci.yml:81-82 recommends wiring it into CI; VERIFICATION.md:30 records it as Passed (2026-09-04). rustfmt 1.9.0 --check (default config, edition 2021; the repo has no rustfmt.toml) on a scratch copy of apps/relay-native/src reports 500 diffs across 37 files (board_view.rs 60, shell/registry.rs 49, mirror.rs 48, e.g. let-else formatting at app.rs:118). Medium confidence only because the local rustfmt is not the CI-pinned 1.94 toolchain.
findings.impact: A developer verifying a native change sees the documented gate fail on untouched files and either ignores the verification list or reformats the crate wholesale - the noise CLAUDE.md asks to avoid; adding it to CI as ci.yml suggests would go red at once.
findings.fix: Drop the fmt check from README and the ci.yml note (consistent with the workspace's deliberate non-rustfmt policy), or reformat relay-native once in a dedicated commit.

v1.reason: README.md:61-66 lists `cargo fmt -p relay-native --check` as a verification step, and docs/VERIFICATION.md:30 records it as Passed. ci.yml:81-82 suggests adding it to CI later. The repo has no rustfmt.toml. I copied apps/relay-native/src to the scratchpad and ran `rustfmt 1.9.0 --edition 2021 --check main.rs`: it reported 500 'Diff in' hunks, which matches the finding. The same ci.yml comment says the workspace is deliberately not rustfmt-clean, so this README step contradicts the project's own policy.
v1.correction: The local rustfmt may differ slightly from the pinned toolchain, but with 500 hunks the result is clearly a fail. Fix: remove the fmt step from README.md and from the ci.yml suggestion, and mark the VERIFICATION.md row as historical.

findings.title: CLI exits 5 ('engine unreachable' per BUS.md §8.2) for local argument errors such as bad JSON or a missing project_id
findings.evidence: main.rs:109-114 maps every anyhow error from run() to EXIT_UNREACHABLE (5): a bad --instance (201), a payload that is not JSON (138-140), a bad envelope (593) and fill_project's `bus.project_required` bail (185). BUS.md:421-422 defines 5 as 'engine unreachable' and BUS.md:412 documents bus.project_required as an error code.
findings.impact: Scripts and agents that treat exit 5 as 'engine down, (re)start it' restart or wait on a healthy engine when the real problem is their own payload.
findings.fix: Return 1 (invalid) for client-side argument/payload errors and reserve 5 for connection failures.

v1.reason: main() at crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:107-115 maps every Err from run() to EXIT_UNREACHABLE (5). Client-side errors therefore also exit 5. Examples: read_payload's 'payload is not JSON' (137-140), do_cmd's 'payload must be a JSON object', 'envelope is not JSON' and 'bad envelope', and fill_project's bail containing bus.project_required (185). BUS.md:421-422 reserves 5 for 'engine unreachable', and BUS.md §8.2 describes bus.project_required as an error code. The CLI emits it as an anyhow string on stderr instead of a typed Response on stdout, despite the documented 'always a Response JSON on stdout' contract.
v1.correction: Also affected: hook adapters such as codex_pre_tool and claude_pre_tool return Err for malformed hook input or a missing RELAY_SESSION, and those also exit 5. How a provider treats exit 5, as opposed to 2, is a separate fail-open question worth checking. Fix: return 1 for local validation errors, keep 5 for connect() failures, and print a typed Response for bus.project_required.

findings.title: workspace.discover/create with a blank path resolve against the engine's cwd ($HOME), not the caller's checkout as BUS.md §10.4 says
findings.evidence: BUS.md:651-652: a blank path 'resolves ... to the current Git checkout's parent (or the current directory outside a checkout)'. suggested_workspace() (workspace.rs:72-87) uses the engine's std::env::current_dir(), and `relay serve` changes directory to $HOME before starting (relay-cli/src/main.rs:204-208). The discovery walk (workspace.rs:393-410) also aborts entirely on the first unreadable directory (`fs::read_dir(path)?`).
findings.impact: `relay q workspace.discover '{}'` or a blank workspace.create run from inside a repository scans or creates $HOME (or /home when $HOME is itself a dotfiles repository) instead of the repository's parent; onboarding's blank discovery fails outright if any root-owned directory sits within four levels of $HOME.
findings.fix: Have the CLI fill its own cwd when path is blank (the engine cannot know the caller's), document the engine-cwd fallback, and skip unreadable directories instead of failing the walk.

v1.reason: suggested_workspace (workspace.rs:72-78) uses the engine's own std::env::current_dir(). `relay serve` does set_current_dir($HOME) before starting (relay-cli/src/main.rs:207-208, added in c97284f). So a blank path in workspace.discover (workspace.rs:115-116) or workspace.create (canon_workspace, line 54-55) always resolves to $HOME, or to $HOME's parent if $HOME is a repository. The caller's checkout plays no part, contrary to BUS.md:651-652. discover_repositories' walk (workspace.rs:393-405) uses `fs::read_dir(path)?` and `entry?`, so one unreadable directory down to depth 3 fails the whole discovery with workspace.discover_failed.
v1.correction: The trigger is narrower than claimed. The native onboarding prefills the path field with its own process cwd (apps/relay-native/src/onboarding.rs:73-78) and sends that, so blank reaches the engine only from the CLI or when the user clears the field. The doc comment on suggested_workspace ('a desktop app may inherit a deep build directory') has also been stale since the chdir. Fix: document that blank means the engine's home, or have the CLI send its cwd. Skip unreadable entries in walk instead of aborting.

findings.title: Without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR the socket directory falls back to a predictable /tmp path whose parent is never ownership-checked
findings.evidence: paths.rs:66-75 falls back to `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("relay-v4-{uid}"))` and then joins `relay-v4`; socket.rs:54-56 runs create_dir_all and chmods only the leaf to 0700; nothing verifies that /tmp/relay-v4-<uid> is owned by the user and not writable by others. BUS.md:207-208 and §0.6 rest the user actor's trust on the socket being reachable only by the same uid.
findings.impact: When the engine and clients run without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (cron, some SSH or container sessions), another local user who pre-creates /tmp/relay-v4-<uid> can rename the engine's leaf directory and plant their own <instance>.sock; the user's CLI, MCP servers and guardrail hook adapters then talk to that socket, handing over agent RELAY_TOKENs and accepting forged 'allow' verdicts from guardrail.gate.
findings.fix: Create the fallback parent with mode 0700 and refuse to use it unless owner == uid and it is not group/world-writable, or fall back under the user's data directory; have clients check the socket owner before connecting.

v1.reason: paths.rs:66-75: when directories::BaseDirs gives no runtime dir (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset), the base is `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("relay-v4-{uid}"))` and then `relay-v4`. socket.rs:54-55 runs `create_dir_all(&dir)` and then `let _ = set_permissions(&dir, 0o700)`, which ignores the error and touches only the leaf. Nothing checks who owns the parent or the leaf. I found no peer-credential or owner check anywhere (searched for SO_PEERCRED, peer_cred and st_uid in crates/ and apps/relay-native: none). So if another local user pre-creates /tmp/relay-v4-<uid> (or the leaf as well) as their own world-writable dir, the chmod fails silently. They can then rename or unlink the engine's socket and bind their own, and the user's CLI, MCP servers and hook adapters, which send RELAY_TOKEN, connect to it. A forged guardrail.gate 'ok' makes the hook adapters exit 0 (allow).
v1.correction: This needs both a missing XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and a hostile local account on a single-user desktop, so low is right. Another weakness: if the attacker pre-creates the leaf, the `let _ =` on set_permissions hides the failure. Fix: create the fallback with mode 0700 and verify owner==uid and no group/other write bits on both levels, refusing to start otherwise. Optionally, clients can check the socket owner.
